units.tr: Proof of the major premise from the authority of Ambrose, On Duties, book 2, chapter 28, and of Augustine, Epistle 154, saying that they are to be turned either to common uses or to the honour of the true God.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia alioqui non pietate sed avari-tia destrui videtur idololatria.
units.tr: Reason: (1) Because otherwise idolatry seems to be destroyed not by piety but by avarice.

units.la: 11. Quia Deus aurum Hierichuntinum ana-thematizatum non diripi, sed in suos thesauros inferri voluit.
units.tr: (2) Because God wished the gold of Jericho, devoted to destruction, not to be plundered but carried into his own treasuries.

units.la: Argumentum III. à pari: Quia non licet vesci Idolothytis. 1.Cor.8.
units.tr: Argument III, from parity: Because it is not lawful to eat things sacrificed to idols. 1 Cor. 8.

units.la: Argumentum IV. ab adiuncto: Quia hoc est communicare rapinis. Amplificetur minor ex eo quod viliter vendunt.
units.tr: Argument IV, from the accompanying circumstance: Because this is to share in plunder. The minor premise is amplified by the fact that they sell cheaply.

units.la: Conclusio: Petere igitur te amici judicium.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore I ask your friend's judgment.

units.la: Responsio ad quæstionem Amici.
units.tr: Answer to a Friend's Question.

units.la: PARS AFFIRMANS.
units.tr: THE AFFIRMATIVE PART.

units.la: EXordium habeat collaudationem amici de quæstione mota.
units.tr: The exordium should contain praise of the friend for the question raised.

units.la: Ratio 1. quod intelligas, cum conscientiæ rationem habere in re dubia.
units.tr: Reason 1: that you understand that one must take account of conscience in a doubtful matter.

units.la: I I. Quod tuo judicio tantum tribuat.
units.tr: II. That you attribute so much to your own judgment.

units.la: ἀνϑυποφορὰς: Non ita facile esse respondere.
units.tr: ἀνθυποφορὰς: That it is not so easy to respond.

units.la: 1. Quia judicium magna ex parte pendeat ex circumstantiis, quas ipse omiserit.
units.tr: 1. Because the judgment depends for the most part on circumstances which you yourself have left out.

units.la: I I. Quia videri possis velle patrocinari sacrilegis, si ab ipso dissentias.
units.tr: II. Because you might seem to wish to defend sacrilegious persons, if you dissent from him.

units.la: Amplif. à thesi: Improbos facile arripere pretextus scelerum, ex factis ambiguis.
units.tr: Amplification from the thesis: The wicked easily seize upon pretexts for their crimes from ambiguous deeds.

units.la: Conclusio per adversat: Sed tamen te responsurum, quantum per judicii imbecillitatem possis.
units.tr: Conclusion by way of opposition: Yet I will respond, as far as the weakness of my judgment allows.

units.la: Propositio bipartita: Excusari posse vendentes & ementes ejusmodi spolia: positis his conditionibus: si milites ea jussu vel permissu Ducum hostibus eripuerint: si non vendat ad idololatriam: si ementes eandem non intendant: si denique periculum idololatriæ apud alios atque scandalum absit:
units.tr: Two-part proposition: Those who sell and those who buy such spoils may be excused, provided these conditions are met: if the soldiers seized them from the enemy by the command or permission of the commanders; if they are not sold for idolatry; if the buyers do not intend the same; and finally, if there is no danger of idolatry or scandal among others.

units.la: Non positis vero, utrosque peccare.
units.tr: But if these conditions are not met, both parties sin.

units.la: In antithesi conditiones contrariæ expriman-tur.
units.tr: In the antithesis the contrary conditions are to be stated.

units.la: Argumentum I. primæ partis. Quia stipen-diis legitimè partis uti liceat militi.
units.tr: Argument 1 of the first part: because a soldier may lawfully use the wages he has legitimately earned.

units.la: Probetur & amplif. dicto Johannis: Estote contenti stipendiis vestris. Luc.3.14.
units.tr: Let it be proved and amplified by the saying of John: "Be content with your wages." Luke 3:14.

units.la: Subjiciatur minor: Hæc militi obtigisse pro stipendio diu non soluto.
units.tr: Let the minor premise be added: that this fell to the soldier as pay, which had long not been paid.

units.la: Ratio: quia voluntate Victoris, in cujus potestatem res hostium legitimè venerant.
units.tr: Reason: because it came by the will of the victor, into whose power the enemy's goods had lawfully passed.

units.la: Amplificetur ex loco communi de jure Victoris in victos, de quo Deut. 20. v. 14: Omnia spolia depradaberis tibi.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the common topic of the right of the victor over the vanquished, concerning which Deut. 20:14: "All the spoil you shall take for yourselves."

units.la: Item à veteri consuetudine Romanorum, antequam militi solverentur stipendia. Livius lib.4. in expug. Anxuris.
units.tr: Likewise from the ancient custom of the Romans, before wages were paid to the soldier. Livy, book 4, on the storming of Anxur.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Luc.3.14: Neminem diripite.
units.tr: Objection 1. Luke 3:14: "Plunder no one."

units.la: Ergo improbari talia stipendia.
units.tr: Therefore such wages are disapproved.

units.la: Resp.ad antecedens. 1 Contra jus belli, seu disciplinam militarem.
units.tr: Response to the antecedent: 1. Against the law of war, or military discipline.

units.la: II.[?] Pacis tempore.
units.tr: II. [?] In time of peace.

units.la: Illustretur thesi, desumta[?] ex responso Camilli ad perfidum ludimagistrum Faliscorum: Sunt & belli sicut pacis jura. Liv.lib.5.
units.tr: Let the thesis be illustrated from Camillus's reply to the treacherous schoolmaster of the Falerii: "There are laws of war as well as of peace." Livy, book 5.

units.la: Obiect. 11. Abstinendum tamen à sacris in expugnationibus. Hæc potest exaggerari exemplis contrariis illaudatis Pyrrhi, & Pleminii diri-pientium thesauros Proserpinę, apud Locrenses: Romanorum eosdem restituentium. Livius lib. 29. Valer. Max. lib. 1. 2.
units.tr: Objection 2. Nevertheless one must abstain from sacred things in the storming of cities. This may be enlarged by contrary examples, not praised: Pyrrhus, and Pleminius, who plundered the treasures of Proserpina among the Locrians; and the Romans, who restored them. Livy, book 29; Valerius Maximus, book 1, chapter 2.

units.la: Respond.per distinct. Maioris: Abstinendũ esse. 1. militi privato. 2. à sacris vere sic dictis: non idololatricis: & de quibus non est dictum magi-stratui: igni comburetis. 3. non cogete necessitate: Antithesis: Hæc Idololatrica, voluntate ducum directa esse: alia satisfactione tunc non suppetente.
units.tr: Response, by distinction of the major premise: One must abstain (1) from a private soldier; (2) from things truly sacred, not idolatrous, and concerning which no command has been given to the magistrate: "you shall burn them with fire"; (3) one is not to be compelled by necessity. Antithesis: these are idolatrous, directed by the will of the commanders, while no other satisfaction is then at hand.

units.la: Ad exempla: Esse dissimilia: quia direptio partim bello injusto, partim expilatione sit facta: restitutionis autem finis fuerit idololatria.
units.tr: As to the examples: they are dissimilar, because the plundering was done partly in an unjust war, partly by pillage; but the purpose of the restitution was idolatry.

units.la: Instantia: Etiam victoribus abstinendum, quia magistratui bona Ecclesiæ conflare non licet.
units.tr: Instance: Even victors must abstain, because it is not lawful for the magistrate to melt down the goods of the Church.

units.la: Respon. 1. Negatione conseq. ex thesi: Alia belli, alia pacis jura esse.
units.tr: Response 1: by denying the consequence from the thesis: "There are other laws of war, other laws of peace."

units.la: II. ad antecedens: non cogente necessitate, quæ excusat: Ambros.lib.2.offic.c.28.
units.tr: II. As to the antecedent: not under compulsion of necessity, which excuses. Ambrose, book 2 of the Duties, chapter 28.

units.la: Probetur exemplo Davidis edentis panes pro-positionis.
units.tr: Let it be proved by the example of David eating the bread of the presentation.

units.la: Et ex thesi: Misericordiam volo nō sacrificiū.
units.tr: And from the thesis: "I desire mercy, not sacrifice."

units.la: Conclusio primi argumenti: Non igitur accu-sandos milites, stipendia sua distrahentes.
units.tr: Conclusion of the first argument: Therefore the soldiers who sell their pay are not to be accused.

units.la: Potest amplificari exemplo militum opsonia merentium apud Romanos.
units.tr: It may be amplified by the example of soldiers among the Romans who earned their provisions.

units.la: Argumentum II. Quia quæ recte vendun-tur, etiam recte emuntur.
units.tr: Argument II: because what is rightly sold may also be rightly bought.

units.la: Argumentum III. Quia conflando ea præ-cidunt victores & milites occasiones idololatriæ instaurandæ.
units.tr: Argument III: because by melting them down the victors and soldiers cut off the occasions of reviving idolatry.

units.la: Occupatiuncula: Abesse scandalum.
units.tr: Small objection: the scandal is absent.

units.la: Ratio: quia clam sint conflata, non inter in-firmos.
units.tr: Reason: because they are melted down secretly, not among the weak.

units.la: Argumentum secundæ partis sit unicum: Quia tunc sint rapinæ, quibus non liceat com-municare. Jer.1.23.[?] Psal.50.17.
units.tr: The one argument of the second part: because then there are robberies, in which it is not lawful to take part. Jer. 1:23 [?]; Ps. 50:17.

units.la: Transitio ad confutationem.
units.tr: Transition to the refutation.

units.la: Cum aliquatenus excusari factum possit: non simpliciter amicum id debere improbare.
units.tr: Since the deed can in some measure be excused, your friend ought not to condemn it outright.

units.la: Ratio sit argumentorum amici dilutio, sed modesta: quod videlicet non plus probent, quam tu etiam concedas.
units.tr: The aim is a refutation of the friend's arguments, but a moderate one: namely, that they do not prove more than you yourself also concede.

units.la: Ad I. argumentum de interdicto Dei. Fuisse illud politicum & temporarium illius gentis.
units.tr: To the first argument, concerning the prohibition of God: that prohibition was political and temporary, belonging to that nation.

units.la: Ratio: quia pollutio ex usu & contactu materiae conflatae fuerit tantum legalis.
units.tr: Reason: because the pollution arising from the use and contact of the melted material was only legal.

units.la: Illustretur simili de immunditie animalium: Sic his non licuisse vesci propter Dei interdictum.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated by a similar case concerning the uncleanness of animals: thus they were not permitted to eat them because of God's prohibition.

units.la: Ad solutionem obiectionis: Christianis idololatriam prohiberi, non usum rerum bonarum per se, aut mediarum extra scandalum: propter aliorum abusum.
units.tr: To the solution of the objection: idolatry is forbidden to Christians, not the use of good things in themselves, or of indifferent things, outside of scandal, on account of others' abuse of them.

units.la: Probetur absurdo: alioqui Solis & Lunae conspectus illicitus foret propter abusum: sic aeris, vini, &c.
units.tr: Let it be proved by an absurdity: otherwise the sight of the sun and moon would be unlawful on account of abuse; so too bronze, wine, etc.

units.la: Et a thesi: Mundis omnia munda. Tit.1.15.
units.tr: And from the thesis: "To the pure all things are pure." Titus 1:15.

units.la: Ad II. argumentum responsum jam esse in obiectione 11.
units.tr: To the second argument the answer has already been given in objection 2.

units.la: Ad sententiam Augustini, per concessionem, quia publicum sit munus, dare militi stipendia.
units.tr: To the opinion of Augustine, by concession, because it is a public duty to give wages to a soldier.

units.la: Ad exemplum Hierichuntinum: fuisse id speciale.
units.tr: To the example of Jericho: that was a special case.

units.la: Opponatur: Madianiticum Num.31.27: in quo Deus praedam distribui jubet populo & militib. & duces offerunt spolia, quasi res suas. Ibidem vers.50.
units.tr: Let it be opposed: the Midianite spoil, Num. 31:27, in which God orders the booty to be distributed to the people and the soldiers, and the commanders offer the spoils as if they were their own things. Ibid., verse 50.

units.la: Ad III. Vefciidolothytis peccatum suis-se propter accedens scandalum: non per se.
units.tr: To the third: the eating of things sacrificed to idols was a sin on account of the accompanying scandal, not in itself.

units.la: Probetur ex 1.Cor.10.v.27.
units.tr: Let it be proved from 1 Cor. 10:27.

units.la: Ad IV. negatione majoris.
units.tr: To the fourth: by denying the major premise.

units.la: Ratio petatur ex 1. argumento, 1. partis.
units.tr: The reason is to be sought from the first argument of the first part.

units.la: Conclusio brevis constet mitigatione sententiæ tuæ per ἀνθυποφορεῖν[?]: Etsi mitius judices propter circumstantias: tamen facta ejusmodi vix peccato carere.
units.tr: The brief conclusion stands with the softening of your sentence, by way of ἀνθυποφορεῖν[?]: even if you judge more leniently on account of the circumstances, yet deeds of this kind hardly lack sin.

units.la: Et consilio: Rectius facere, qui ab his mercibus abstinent. Ratio ex 1. Cor. 6. 12. & cap. 8. 9. Omnia mihi licent, sed non omnia conducunt.
units.tr: And by counsel: those who abstain from such goods act more rightly. Reason from 1 Cor. 6:12 and chapter 8:9: "All things are lawful for me, but not all things are expedient."

units.la: Exercitatio II.
units.tr: Exercitatio II.

units.la: Paraphrasis orationis Mosis, qua populum ad obedientiam legis hortatur. Deut. 8. Scribatur latine sine Hebraismis.
units.tr: Paraphrase of Moses' speech, in which he exhorts the people to obedience to the law. Deut. 8. To be written in Latin without Hebraisms.

units.la: Propositio: Hortor vos, ut Legi divinæ obtemperetis.
units.tr: Proposition: I exhort you to obey the divine Law.

units.la: Potest præmitti brevis ὑποφορὴ[?] ex loco benevolentiæ à persona Mosis & ipsorum.
units.tr: A brief hypophora[?] may be prefixed, drawn from a locus of goodwill, in the person of Moses and of the people themselves.

units.la: Ratio 1. ab utili: ut vivatis, ver.1.
units.tr: First reason, from what is useful: that you may live, ver. 1.

units.la: Ratio II. ab honesto: Recordare totius viæ i-stius, ver.2.
units.tr: Second reason, from what is honourable: Remember the whole of this way, ver. 2.

units.la: Hæc ratio constet narratione. 1. periculorum populi in deserto. 2. Causarum efficientis nimirum & finalis. 3 præcipuorum beneficiorum.
units.tr: This reason should consist of a narrative: (1) of the dangers of the people in the wilderness; (2) of the causes, namely both efficient and final; (3) of the chief benefits.

units.la: Ratio III. ab honesto & utili, ver. 7: Jehova mox te, &c.
units.tr: Third reason, from what is honourable and useful, ver. 7: For the LORD your God shortly brings you, etc.

units.la: Hæc 1. recitet promissionem terræ jam occupandæ. 2. Vbertatem terræ promissæ exag-geret. 3. Habeat πάθ[?]ος seu omen ex thesi. Luxuriant animi rebus plerunque secundis. 4. Dehortetur à securitate carnali & ingratitudine.
units.tr: This reason should (1) recite the promise of the land now to be taken possession of; (2) magnify the fertility of the promised land; (3) have a pathos or omen drawn from the thesis: Minds grow proud, for the most part, on prosperity. (4) It should dissuade from carnal security and ingratitude.

units.la: Ratio IV[?] à pernicioso, ver. 19. Si oblitus, &c. Habeat contestationem à veritate & iustitia Dei.
units.tr: Fourth reason, from the harmful consequences, ver. 19, If you forget, etc. It should have a solemn attestation drawn from the truth and justice of God.

units.la: Exercitatio III.
units.tr: Exercitatio III.

units.la: Progymnasma: Quod Deus non tantum corporalia promittat: Levit. 26. & Deut. 28.
units.tr: Progymnasma: That God does not promise only corporal things: Lev. 26 and Deut. 28.

units.la: EXordium: multos sic discernere veterem & novam Ecclesiam, quòd illa tantum terrenas: hæc spirituales promissiones habeat.
units.tr: Introduction: many thus distinguish the old and the new Church, in that the former has only earthly promises, the latter spiritual promises.

units.la: Propositio: per adverf. Impium errorem esse, tantum corporalia populo Dei tribuere.
units.tr: Proposition: by way of contrast, it is an impious error to attribute only corporal things to the people of God.

units.la: Ratio I. à specie ad proprium: Quia unica tantum Ecclesia, & sanctorum communio. Declaretur & probetur ex Rom. 14. 1.Cor. 5. & 10. & 12, Col. 2.
units.tr: Reason I, from the species to the proper: because there is only one Church and one communion of the saints. This is to be declared and proved from Rom. 14:1, 1 Cor. 5, 10 and 12, and Col. 2.

units.la: Ratio II. Quia lex tam æterna quam temporalia promittit obedientibus: & minatur transgressoribus: Ex definitione legis. Et ex dictis. Levit. 18.5: Vivet in eis: Deut. 27.26. Gal. 3.10. Maledictus omnis, &c.
units.tr: Reason II: because the law promises both eternal and temporal things to the obedient and threatens transgressors, from the definition of law. And from the sayings in Lev. 18:5, He shall live in them; Deut. 27:26; Gal. 3:10, Cursed is everyone, etc.

units.la: Obiectio: Conditionem promissionis esse impossibilem.
units.tr: Objection: the condition of the promise is impossible.

units.la: Ergo frustra legem promittere spiritualia.
units.tr: Therefore it is in vain for the law to promise spiritual things.

units.la: Respond. 1. per βλάσφημον[?]: sic etiam corporalia frustra promitteret. 2. Est possibilis Evange-licè, Declaretur & probetur, non excludi obedientiam Evangelicam ex Deut.30 11. & Rom.8.6.
units.tr: Answer 1: by a blasphemous [?] claim; in that case it would also promise corporal things in vain. 2: it is possible in the Gospel sense; that Evangelical obedience is not excluded is to be declared and proved from Deut. 30:11 and Rom. 8:6.

units.la: Ratio III. Quia corporalia fuerunt typi & tesserae spiritualium. Ratio a natura Dei, nihil promittentis & dantis nisi reconciliatis, 2. Cor. 1:In Christo omnes, &c.
units.tr: Reason III: because corporal things were types and tokens of spiritual things. The reason is drawn from the nature of God, who promises and gives nothing except to the reconciled, 2 Cor. 1: In Christ all, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur a causa obscuritatis promissionum, quae petatur ex discrimine utriusque Testamenti.
units.tr: This is to be amplified from the cause of the obscurity of the promises, which is to be sought in the difference between the two Testaments.

units.la: Ratio IV. Quia expresse spirituales promissiones adduntur hic & alibi. Probetur ex Levit. 26.v.11.12.13. & Deut.28.v.9.10.
units.tr: Reason IV: because spiritual promises are expressly added here and elsewhere. This is to be proved from Lev. 26:11, 12, 13 and Deut. 28:9, 10.

units.la: Ratio v. Quia sine spiritualibus servari non potuerunt. Minor applicetur ex Act.15. 11. & 4. 12:Non est datum, &c. Rom.4.13. Joh.8.v.58.
units.tr: Reason V: because they could not have been kept without spiritual things. The minor premise is to be applied from Acts 15:11 and 4:12, There is no other given, etc.; Rom. 4:13; John 8:58.

units.la: Conclusio: Explodendam igitur ex Ecclesia ef-fe opinionem de patribus in terra promissa tanquam porcis in hara saginatis.
units.tr: Conclusion: therefore the opinion about the fathers in the promised land, as pigs fattened in a sty, is to be driven out of the Church.

units.la: Exercitatio IV.
units.tr: Exercitatio IV.

units.la: An Gibeonitarum dolus quo Josuam circumvenerunt ob vitae conservationem excusari possit. Jos.9.9. PARS AFFIRMANS.
units.tr: Whether the trick by which the Gibeonites deceived Joshua may be excused for the sake of preserving their lives. Josh. 9.9. THE AFFIRMATIVE SIDE.

units.la: EXordium à thesi. Recitationes historiæ sacræ publicas in scholis, præter delectationem, utilitatis plurimum habere.
units.tr: Introduction from the thesis. Public recitations of sacred history in the schools, apart from the pleasure they give, are of great use.

units.la: Ratio, quia de variis rebus, ad judicium formandum pertinentibus cogitandi materiam of-ferant.
units.tr: Reason: because they offer material for thinking about various matters that pertain to forming judgment.

units.la: Amplificatio à minori. Multò rectius sacram quàm profanam historiā Prudentiæ ac vitæ Ma-gistram nominari.
units.tr: Amplification from the lesser: Sacred history is much more rightly called the teacher of prudence and of life than profane history.

units.la: Transferatur ad hypothesin, ac breviter narre-tur res gesta: Dolum Gibeonitarum cum nuper in schola recitaretur, præbuisse materiam disputationi, tuo judicio non inutili, de jure facti: quod breviter exponatur.
units.tr: Let it be transferred to the hypothesis, and the event be briefly narrated: when the deceit of the Gibeonites was recently being recited in school, it provided material for a disputation, not useless in your judgment, on the right of the deed; let this be briefly set out.

units.la: Propositio: Tibi videri eos non peccasse.
units.tr: Proposition: It seems to you that they did not sin.

units.la: Ratio I. Quia servaverint hoc modo vitam.
units.tr: Reason I. Because they preserved their lives in this way.

units.la: Illustretur major ex thesi: Omnia naturaliter ferri ad conservationem sui: Et præcepto Dei: Non occides.
units.tr: Let the major be illustrated from the thesis: all things naturally tend to self-preservation; and by the precept of God: Thou shalt not kill.

units.la: Ratio II. Quia dolus bonus & simulatio salutaris excusetur.
units.tr: Reason II. Because a good deceit and a salutary pretence are excused.

units.la: Obiectio: Fuisse mendacium.
units.tr: Objection: it was a lie.

units.la: Resp. sed officiosum, quod non sit peccatum.
units.tr: Answer: but a dutiful one, which is not a sin.

units.la: Illustretur exemplo Josuę simulantis fugam in oppugnatione urbis Ai, sine peccato. Jos.8.15.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated by the example of Joshua feigning flight in the assault on the city of Ai, without sin. Josh. 8.15.

units.la: Amplificetur thesi a minori: In bellis stratagemata licere ad hostes opprimendos: multò magis ad placandos.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by the thesis from the lesser: in wars, stratagems are lawful for overcoming enemies; much more so for appeasing them.

units.la: Ratio III. Quia vindicando sese templi servitio, veram religionem amplexi sint.
units.tr: Reason III. Because by claiming for themselves the service of the temple, they embraced the true religion.

units.la: Amplif. ab eventu: Divinitus servati sunt. nec legitur factum Deo displicuisse, sed potius contrarium, 2.Sam.21.2.
units.tr: Amplification from the outcome: they were preserved by divine providence, nor is it read that the deed displeased God, but rather the contrary: 2 Sam. 21.2.

units.la: Ratio IV. ab edicto Dei. Deut.20.11. Petentes pacem non esse opprimendos. Petere igitur pacem Gibeonitis licuit. Ratio v. Ab exemplis laudatis: Obstetricum in Ægypto mendacio officioso servantium infantes, Exod. 1. 20. Michalis servantis maritum Davidem: 1. Sam. 19. 17. Jehu tollentis Baalitas, 2. Reg. 10. 18.
units.tr: Reason IV. From God's edict: Deut. 20.11, those who seek peace are not to be attacked. It was therefore lawful for the Gibeonites to seek peace. Reason V. From the examples cited: the midwives in Egypt who saved the infants by a dutiful lie, Exod. 1.20; Michal who saved her husband David, 1 Sam. 19.17; Jehu who removed the Baalites, 2 Kings 10.18.

units.la: Conclusio: Non igitur peccasse Gibeonitas.
units.tr: Conclusion: therefore the Gibeonites did not sin.

units.la: Habeat translationem.Si quid peccatum sit, Jo-suam potius peccasse negligentiâ inquisitionis.
units.tr: Let it also have a counter-proposition: if anything was sinned, Joshua rather sinned through negligence in inquiry.

units.la: Et adversativam: Te tamen paratum esse au-dire amici rationes, si diversum sentiat.
units.tr: And an adversative: nevertheless, you are ready to hear the reasons of a friend, if he thinks otherwise.

units.la: Pars negans.
units.tr: The denying part.

units.la: Refutatur defensio doli Gibeonitarum.
units.tr: The defence of the Gibeonites' deceit is refuted.

units.la: EXordium breve sumatur à thesi: Multa pec-cata videri hominibus rectè facta.
units.tr: The introduction is taken briefly from the thesis: many sins seem to men to have been done rightly.

units.la: Applicetur ad hypothesin de dolo Gibeonitarum: Ideo excusari eum à nonnullis, quia ingeniose inventus sit, & utiliter cesserit.
units.tr: Applied to the hypothesis concerning the deceit of the Gibeonites: some excuse him because he was ingeniously devised and turned out to be useful.

units.la: Propositio per adversat. Te vero ostensurum, quòd excusari non possit.
units.tr: The proposition, by way of contrast: but I will show you that he cannot be excused.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia lex Dei simpliciter vetet, sal-sum dicere voluntate fallendi: Non dices falsum testimonium, &c. Non eris testis mendax, &c.
units.tr: Reason 1: because the law of God simply forbids speaking falsehood with the will to deceive: "You shall not bear false witness," etc.; "You shall not be a lying witness," etc.

units.la: Minor confirmetur ex historiæ circumstantiis: Dicunt, quæ sciunt non esse vera: simulant falsa, ut fallant Josuam.
units.tr: The minor premise is confirmed from the circumstances of the story: they say things they know not to be true, and they pretend falsehoods in order to deceive Joshua.

units.la: Ratio II. Quia turpe & injustum sit, in pactis & conventis mendacem esse.
units.tr: Reason 2: because it is base and unjust to be a liar in agreements and covenants.

units.la: Confutatio.
units.tr: Refutation.

units.la: Rationis 1. per distinct. majoris: vitam esse ser-vandam, sed secundum legem & honestatem.
units.tr: Against the first reason, by distinguishing the major premise: life is to be preserved, but in accordance with the law and honesty.

units.la: Confirmetur thesi: Non esse facienda mala, ut eveniant bona, Rom. 3. 8.
units.tr: The thesis is confirmed: evil things are not to be done so that good may come of them, Rom. 3:8.

units.la: Applicatio ad minorem : Gibeonitas dolo & mendacio vitam redemisse.
units.tr: Application to the minor premise: the Gibeonites redeemed their lives by deceit and lying.

units.la: Rationis I I. per negationem minoris: Quia dolus nocuerit Israelitis.
units.tr: Against the second reason, by denying the minor premise: because the deceit harmed the Israelites.

units.la: Probatio 1. Quia inducti hac fraude violarint Dei mandatum de exstirpandis gentibus.
units.tr: Proof 1: because, led on by this fraud, they violated God's command to root out the nations.

units.la: I I. Quia sic fraudati sint portione terræ pro-missæ.
units.tr: 2: because they were thus defrauded of a portion of the promised land.

units.la: Digressiuncula de mendacio officioso. Etiam illud esse peccatum.
units.tr: A short digression on the dutiful lie: that this too is a sin.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia Augustinus ad Consentium, quem citârit distinctionis peccati authorem, non excuset: sed deformitatem ac defectum habere concedat, etiam cum pro gloria Dei, & pro ani-mæ salute admittitur. Multò magis cum pro vitæ conservatione.
units.tr: Reason 1: because Augustine, in his letter to Consentius, whom they cite as the author of the distinction of sin, does not excuse it, but concedes that it has deformity and defect, even when it is admitted for the glory of God and the salvation of the soul. Much more so when it is admitted for the preservation of life.

units.la: Ratio I I. Quia veritas tantum est bonum, ut nullius rei causa sit[?] violandum.
units.tr: Reason 2: because truth is so great a good that it must not be violated for the sake of anything at all.

units.la: Amplif. testimonio Aristotelis Eth. l 4. c. 7. π[?] ψευδ[?] [illegible, ~6 letters]
units.tr: Amplification from the testimony of Aristotle, Eth. bk. 4, ch. 7: π[?] ψευδ[?] [illegible, about six letters]

units.la: Ratio I I I. Quia verbum Dei simpliciter præ-cipit loqui veritatem. Eph. 4. 25. Coloss. 3. 9. nec jubet aut permittit mendaciis juvare nos vel a-lios.
units.tr: Reason 3: because the word of God simply commands us to speak the truth (Eph. 4:25; Col. 3:9), and neither orders nor permits us to help ourselves or others by lies.

units.la: Adinstantiam, de fuga Iosuæ. Respond. fuisse stratagema bellicum, quo hostem armatum circum-venire sit licitum: quia armis liceat.
units.tr: As to the objection concerning Joshua's flight: the answer is that it was a military stratagem, by which it is lawful to outwit an armed enemy, since arms are lawful.

units.la: Adinstantiam de stratagematibus. Resp. Ne-gatione majoris: quia hæc implicent contradi-ctionem: Placare hostem, & eundem stratage-mate circumvenire.
units.tr: As to the objection concerning stratagems: the answer is by denying the major premise, because these would involve a contradiction: to placate an enemy and at the same time outwit him by the same stratagem.

units.la: Amplificetur ex thesi: Alia belli, alia pacis jura esse: Livius lib. 5.
units.tr: Amplified from the thesis: there are one set of laws of war and another of peace; Livy, bk. 5.

units.la: Rationis III. 1. Conversionem Gibeonita-rum esse incertam. 2. Non excusare dolum, sed losuæ facilitatem, quod resipiscentibus pepper-cerit.
units.tr: Reason 3: (1) the conversion of the Gibeonites is uncertain; (2) the deceit is not excused, but Joshua's easy-going nature, in that he spared those who repented.

units.la: Adinstantiam de eventu. Respon. Careat suc-cessib. opto, &c. Et a thesi: Non omnia facta Deo probari, quæ indulsit.
units.tr: As to the objection from the outcome: the answer is, "May it be without success," etc. And from the thesis: not all deeds that God has permitted are approved by God.

units.la: Rationis IV. Præceptum Deut. 20. loqui de hostibus externis, non de possessoribus terræ promissæ, quos Deus simpliciter devoverat exitio, Deut.7.24.
units.tr: Reason 4: the precept in Deut. 20 speaks of external enemies, not of the possessors of the promised land, whom God had simply devoted to destruction (Deut. 7:24).

units.la: Rationis V. Exempla nihil probare, quia sint vel dissimilia, vel ambigua.
units.tr: Reason 5: examples prove nothing, because they are either dissimilar or ambiguous.

units.la: In obstetricib. laudari misericordiam, non mendacium.
units.tr: In the case of the midwives, mercy is praised, not lying.

units.la: Michalis figmentum esse ambiguum: plerisque tamen improbari.
units.tr: Michal's pretence is ambiguous, though most condemn it.

units.la: Ratio, quia etiam sine mendacio poterat non prodere maritum.
units.tr: Reason: because even without a lie she could have refrained from betraying her husband.

units.la: Amplificetur ab ejus persona: quod alibi etiā non laudetur Michal, tanquam contemtrix religionis & mariti.
units.tr: Amplified from her person: Michal is not praised elsewhere either, as a despiser of religion and of her husband.

units.la: In Iehu laudari factum, non modum: quia fuit hypocrita.
units.tr: In the case of Jehu, the deed is praised, not the manner, because he was a hypocrite.

units.la: Conclusio: Non esse excusatione Gibeonitarum fenestram aperiendam mendaciis.
units.tr: Conclusion: the excuse of the Gibeonites should not open a window for lies.

units.la: A maiori: Ne sanctorum quidem facta omnia excusari posse.
units.tr: From the greater to the lesser: not even all the deeds of the saints can be excused.

units.la: Hortatio: potius deprecanda esse peccata, quā excusanda.
units.tr: Exhortation: sins should rather be deprecated than excused.

units.la: Exercitatio V.
units.tr: Exercitatio V.

units.la: Collatio sententiæ Peripateticæ & Ecclesiasticæ de summo bono seu felicitate hominis, ex Aristotelis Ethic. lib. 1.
units.tr: Comparison of the Peripatetic and Ecclesiastical teaching on the highest good, or the happiness of man, from Aristotle's Ethics, book 1.

units.la: EXordii propositio: Peripateticos de fine seu fe-licitate hominis commodius sentire, quàm Philosophos alios.
units.tr: Proposition of the introduction: The Peripatetics think more soundly about the end or happiness of man than other philosophers.

units.la: Ratio: quia in proprio & perfectissimo hominis bono eam collocare videantur.
units.tr: Reason: because they seem to place it in what is man's own and most perfect good.

units.la: Ostendatur antithesi, quòd non, & quare non collocent in voluptate, in honore, in virtute, in divitiis, ex cap. 5. lib. 1. Eth.
units.tr: Let it be shown by antithesis that they do not place it in pleasure, honour, virtue or riches, and why not, from Ethics book 1, chapter 5.

units.la: Addatur [illegible, ~8 letters] sententiæ Platonicæ de Ideis: quia nec πρακτὸν ἢ [?], nec κτητὸν ἀνθρώπῳ cap. 6.
units.tr: Let there be added [illegible, ~8 letters] the Platonic doctrine of the Ideas, because it is neither practicable [?] nor attainable by man, chapter 6.

units.la: Adversativa [illegible, ~8 letters]: Etsi multis de causis utile sit, peripateticam doctrinam cognoscere: non posse tamen citra salutis æternæ jacturam in ea acquiesci.
units.tr: Adversative [illegible, ~8 letters]: Although for many reasons it is useful to know the Peripatetic doctrine, yet one cannot rest in it without the loss of eternal salvation.

units.la: Ratio: qui subsistat in hujus vitæ Bono.
units.tr: Reason: because it rests in the good of this life.

units.la: Conclusio Exordii: Discendum igitur esse dis-crimen.
units.tr: Conclusion of the introduction: It must therefore be learned what the difference is.

units.la: Propositio: In multis convenire & discrepare sentensententiam Aristotelis & Ecclesiæ de felicitate.
units.tr: Proposition: That the opinion of Aristotle and of the Church about happiness agrees in many points and differs in others.

units.la: CONVENIENTIA I Esse aliquem finem ultimum hominis: Aristot.cap.1.lib.1.
units.tr: AGREEMENT I. That there is some ultimate end of man: Aristotle, chapter 1, book 1.

units.la: Sic: Proverb.16.4. Omnia propter seipsum fecit Deus, &c. 1.Cor.15.19. Si tantum in hac vita speramus, &c.
units.tr: So: Proverbs 16:4. The LORD has made all things for himself, etc. 1 Corinthians 15:19. If in this life only we have hope, etc.

units.la: Convenient. II. Vltimum finem hominis esse summum ejus bonum seu felicitatem: Aristot.cap.2.
units.tr: They agree. II. That the ultimate end of man is his highest good or happiness: Aristotle, chapter 2.

units.la: Sic Psal.144.15. Beatus populus, cuius Iehova est Deus, &c.
units.tr: So Psalm 144:15. Blessed is the people whose God is the LORD, etc.

units.la: Convenient. III. Summi boni considerationem pertinere ad Architectonicam, hoc est, dominam omnium scientiarum practicarum: Aristoteles cap.2.
units.tr: They agree. III. That the consideration of the highest good belongs to the architectonic science, that is, the mistress of all practical sciences: Aristotle, chapter 2.

units.la: Sic Iohan.5.39: Scrutamini scripturas quia, &c.
units.tr: So John 5:39: Search the Scriptures, for, etc.

units.la: Convenient: IV. Felicitatem hominis esse perfectissimum & αὐτάρκες bonum: Aristoteles cap.7.
units.tr: They agree: IV. That the happiness of man is the most perfect and self-sufficient [αὐτάρκες] good: Aristotle, chapter 7.

units.la: Sic Psal.34.10. Timentibus Deum non deerit ullum bonum. 1. Tim.5.6. Pietas magnus quæstus, &c.
units.tr: So Psalm 34:10. To those who fear God no good thing will be lacking. 1 Timothy 6:6. Godliness is great gain, etc.

units.la: Convenient. V. Esse ἐνέργειαν animi: Aristoteles cap. 7. & quandam ἀζωίαν καὶ ἀπραξίαν μετὰ ἡδονῆς cap.8.
units.tr: They agree. V. That it is an activity [ἐνέργεια] of the soul: Aristotle, chapter 7, and a certain [ἀζωία and ἀπραξία] with pleasure, chapter 8.

units.la: Sic Psal.1.2: Et in lege Domini voluptas eius, &c. Roman.2.13. Non auditores sed factores legis iusti sunt apud Deum: Ioh.17.3. Hæc est vita æterna, &c.
units.tr: So Psalm 1:2: And in the law of the LORD is his delight, etc. Romans 2:13. It is not the hearers but the doers of the law who are righteous before God. John 17:3. This is eternal life, etc.

units.la: Convenient. VI. Non fortuito contingere: sed esse Dei donum: Aristoteles cap.8.
units.tr: They agree. VI. That it does not come by chance, but is a gift of God: Aristotle, chapter 8.

units.la: Sic Rom.6.23: Dei donum vita æterna.
units.tr: So Romans 6:23: The gift of God is eternal life.

units.la: Convenient. VII. Exercitia, assuetudinem & doctrinam pertinere ad acquirendam felicitatem: Aristot.cap. 9.
units.tr: They agree. VII. That exercises, habit and teaching pertain to the acquiring of happiness: Aristotle, chapter 9.

units.la: Sic Rom.1.16: Evangelium potentia Dei. Et 10. 17. Fides ex auditu: Matt.7.7: Petite & dabitur vobis.
units.tr: So Romans 1:16: The gospel is the power of God. And 10:17: Faith comes from hearing. Matthew 7:7: Ask, and it will be given to you.

units.la: Convenient. VIII. Esse stabile & immutabile quiddam, μονιμόν[?], καὶ μηδαμῶς ἀμετάβολον: Aristoteles cap.10.
units.tr: They agree. VIII. That it is something stable and unchangeable, [μόνιμον and μηδαμῶς ἀμετάβολον]: Aristotle, chapter 10.

units.la: Sic Ioh.10.28. Nemo rapiet oves meas, &c. 2. Ti-moth.2.19: Solidum stat fundamentum Dei, &c.
units.tr: So John 10:28. No one will snatch my sheep, etc. 2 Timothy 2:19: The firm foundation of God stands, etc.

units.la: TRANSITIO ad discrepantias, in quibus doctrina Ecclesiæ approbetur: & defectus philosophiæ ostendantur.
units.tr: TRANSITION to the differences, in which the teaching of the Church is approved and the defects of philosophy are shown.

units.la: Discrepantia I. In scientia Architectonica, quæ philosophis est politica: Ecclesiæ Scriptura Sacra seu Theologia.
units.tr: Difference I. In the architectonic science, which for the philosophers is politics, for the Church is Holy Scripture or theology.

units.la: Approbetur sententia Ecclesiæ per antithesin, ostenso philosophiæ defectu.
units.tr: Let the opinion of the Church be approved by antithesis, with the defect of philosophy shown.

units.la: I. Quia non Politica, sed sola Scriptura sacra tradat veram cognitionem Dei, perfectissimi boni: Deut.4.6.Ioh.1.18: Deum nemo vidit unquam, &c.
units.tr: I. Because it is not politics but Holy Scripture alone that hands down the true knowledge of God, the most perfect good: Deuteronomy 4:6. John 1:18: No one has ever seen God, etc.

units.la: II. Quia ipsa Politica subserviat Scripturæ tanquam nobiliori.
units.tr: II. Because politics itself serves Scripture as the nobler science.

units.la: Ostendatur applicatione duorum argumentorum Aristotelis, quibus primatum vendicat politicæ, ad Scripturam.
units.tr: Let it be shown by applying to Scripture two arguments of Aristotle, by which he claims the primacy for politics.

units.la: I. Quod hæc accuratissime docent, quæ artes & scientiæ discendæ, & in Republ. admittendæ sint, vel non sint. Rom.12. v.3.6.&c. Deut.8.10. 1.Cor.7.10.1.Thess.4.11.
units.tr: I. Because Scripture teaches most accurately which arts and sciences are to be learned, and which are to be admitted or not admitted in the commonwealth: Romans 12:3, 6, etc.; Deuteronomy 8:10; 1 Corinthians 7:10; 1 Thessalonians 4:11.

units.la: II. Quod hæc imperet functionibus nobilissimis Ecclesiasticę, Politicæ, Oeconomicæ, militari, oratoriæ, &c.
units.tr: II. Because Scripture commands the most noble functions: ecclesiastical, political, domestic, military, oratorical, etc.

units.la: Discrepantia II. In felicitatis differentia essentiali, quæ Peripateticis est Actio animi secundum rectum rationis judicium, & virtutem moralem: Ecclesiæ est veri Dei agnitio, cum obedientia fidei conjuncta.
units.tr: Difference II. In the essential difference of happiness, which for the Peripatetics is an action of the soul according to the right judgement of reason, and moral virtue; for the Church it is the knowledge of the true God, joined with obedience of faith.

units.la: Explicetur doctrina Ecclesiæ ex dictis. Ioh.17, 17. Hæc est vita æterna: Eph.4.24. Homo secundum Deum conditus in vera, &c. Rom.1.17. Justus fide sua vivet.
units.tr: Let the teaching of the Church be explained from what has been said. John 17:3: This is eternal life. Ephesians 4:24: Man created according to God in true, etc. Romans 1:17: The just shall live by his faith.

units.la: Et ostendatur antithesi, quod in hac sit totum δικαιώματος[?] legis: illi tantum externæ disciplinæ legis partem docent.
units.tr: And let it be shown by antithesis that the whole [δικαίωμα?] of the law lies in this; they teach only the external discipline of the law as a part.

units.la: Amplificetur defectus ex dictis: Diliges Dominum, &c. Maledictus omnis, &c.
units.tr: Let the defect be amplified from what has been said: You shall love the Lord, etc. Cursed is everyone, etc.

units.la: Discrepantia III. In ejusdem differentia accidentali: Aristoteles in vitam perfectam rejicit felicitatem: eaque terminat. cap. 7.9.
units.tr: Difference III. In its accidental difference: Aristotle rejects happiness for the perfect life and ends it there, chapters 7 and 9.

units.la: Scriptura nullam ætatem excludit: & æternam esse docet: Ab utero matris in te proiectus sum: In veritate cognosco. Sinite pueros venire ad me: Qui credit in me, habet vitam æternam.
units.tr: Scripture excludes no age and teaches that it is eternal: I was cast upon you from my mother's womb; in truth I know. Suffer the children to come to me. He who believes in me has eternal life.

units.la: Amplificetur ex dicto: Eph. 1.3. Dilexit nos ante iacta mundi fundamenta.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the saying: Ephesians 1:3. He chose us before the foundation of the world.

units.la: Discrepantia IV. In causa efficiente principali. Felicitas Aristotelica paratur disciplina & exercitio: μάθησιν καὶ ἄσκησιν[?].
units.tr: Difference IV. In the principal efficient cause. Aristotelian happiness is acquired by teaching and exercise: [μάθησις and ἄσκησις?].

units.la: Occupat: Etsi fatetur, esse θεόπνευστον καὶ θεόδοτον ἢ[?]: tamen plus tribuit studio humano, quàm Deo. Ecclesiastica fontem habet æternam & gratuitam Electionem. Eph. 1. Elegit nos, &c. Rom. 9. 11. Antequam pueri, &c. & 11. 7. Electio obtinuit. Eph. 2. 8. Gratia Dei servati estis.
units.tr: It is objected: Although it confesses that it is divinely inspired and divinely given [θεόπνευστον and θεόδοτον?], it nonetheless ascribes more to human study than to God. The Church has as its source the eternal and gratuitous election. Ephesians 1: He chose us, etc. Romans 9:11: Before the children, etc. and 11:7: The election obtained it. Ephesians 2:8: By the grace of God you are saved.

units.la: Approbetur 1. ab honesto: quia merito ad Deum refertur summum bonum præstantissimæ creaturæ: Ex dicto: Fecit hominem ad imaginem suam: Præstantissimæ causæ debetur præstantissimus effectus.
units.tr: It is approved 1. from what is honourable: because the highest good of the most excellent creature is rightly referred to God; from the saying: He made man in his own image. The most excellent effect is owed to the most excellent cause.

units.la: II. à necessario: Quia corruptio naturæ humanæ Philosophis ignota cogit extra nos salutem quærere.
units.tr: II. From what is necessary: because the corruption of human nature, unknown to the philosophers, compels us to seek salvation outside ourselves.

units.la: Occupat: Fidem & pietatis exercitia media esse σωτηρίαν [?] non αἵρεσιν [?]: Marc. 16. 16: Qui crediderit. Heb. 11. 6. Sine fide Deo placere, &c. 1. Tim. 4. 8. Pietas ad omnia utilis.
units.tr: It is objected: Faith and the exercises of piety are the means of salvation [σωτηρία], not of choice [αἵρεσις?]: Mark 16:16: He who believes. Hebrews 11:6: Without faith it is impossible to please God, etc. 1 Timothy 4:8: Godliness is profitable for all things.

units.la: Discrepantia v. In causa adjuvante. Felicitas Aristotelica augetur affluentia: minuitur carentia bonorum fortunæ: evertitur calamitatibus Priamicis: eoque non est vere αὐτάρκης [?] bonum. cap. 8. 9. 10.
units.tr: Difference V. In the helping cause. Aristotelian happiness is increased by abundance, diminished by lack of the goods of fortune, and overthrown by Priamic calamities; therefore it is not truly self-sufficient [αὐτάρκης] good: chapters 8, 9 and 10.

units.la: Christiana vere est αὐ τέχνης [?], & cum & sine illis, Rom. 8. 28. Omnia cooperantur in bonum diligentib. Deum. Et ver. 35. Quis nos separabit: Matt. 5. 3. Beati pauperes spiritu, &c.
units.tr: The Christian good is truly [αὐτάρκης] and both with and without those things: Romans 8:28: All things work together for good for those who love God. And verse 35: Who shall separate us? Matthew 5:3: Blessed are the poor in spirit, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur a contrario: Citius minuunt ea, quam augent divitiæ, potentia, &c. 1. Cor. 1. 26. Non multi nobiles, &c. Matt. 19. 23: Quam difficile est divitem ingredi, &c.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the contrary: riches and power, etc., diminish more quickly than they increase. 1 Corinthians 1:26: Not many noble, etc. Matthew 19:23: How hard it is for a rich man to enter, etc.

units.la: Ratio petatur ex facilitate abusus rerum externarum.
units.tr: The reason is to be sought from the ease with which external things are abused.

units.la: Conclusio: per ὑπόθεσιν [?]: Discrepantias exilio-res te res te consulto præterire, & finem collationis facere.
units.tr: Conclusion: by hypothesis: that the lesser differences are deliberately passed over, and the comparison brought to an end.

units.la: Ratio à gemina utilitate. 1. Quia hæc sufficiát ad commendandam philosophiam moralem: cum in tam multis cum Theologia congruat.
units.tr: Reason from a twofold usefulness. 1. Because these points suffice to commend moral philosophy, since in so many matters it agrees with theology.

units.la: Amplificetur per πρόσλημμα[?]. Magnum esse adminiculum Theologiæ in explicatione doctrinæ de disciplina & virtutum officiis secundæ tabulæ.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by [πρόσλημμα?]: that it is a great aid to theology in explaining the doctrine of discipline and the duties of virtues of the second table.

units.la: II. Quia satis demonstrent philosophiæ defectus: & scripturæ perfectionem.
units.tr: II. Because they sufficiently demonstrate the defects of philosophy and the perfection of Scripture.

units.la: Amplificetur ab utili; ne cum monachis Ethicam Aristotelis existimemus ad salutem sufficere.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from usefulness: lest we think, with the monks, that Aristotle's Ethics is sufficient for salvation.

units.la: Et à definitione philosophiæ Platonica in Phæd. quòd sit ὁμοίωσις θεῷ κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ.
units.tr: And from Plato's definition in the Phaedo, that it is [ὁμοίωσις θεῷ κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ], likeness to God so far as is possible for man.

units.la: Exercitatio VI.
units.tr: Exercitatio VI.

units.la: Censura postulationis Israëlitarum de rege creando. 1. Sam. 8. 5.
units.tr: Censure of the Israelites' demand for a king to be created. 1 Sam. 8. 5.

units.la: EXordium à thesi: Multa per se bona vitio hominum fieri peccata.
units.tr: Opening from the thesis: Many things good in themselves become sins through the vice of men.

units.la: Hypothesis, continens propositionem: Sic postulando Regem Israëlitas peccare.
units.tr: Hypothesis, containing the proposition: In thus demanding a king, the Israelites sinned.

units.la: Ratio: quia Deus factum graviter improbet propter multa peccata concurrentia.
units.tr: Reason: because God severely disapproves of the deed, on account of the many sins that concur in it.

units.la: Subiciantur ordine peccata, quæ sint causæ improbationis.
units.tr: The sins that are the causes of this disapproval are to be set out in order.

units.la: I. Ἀποστασία[?] à Deo. Ratio: quia petentes mutari statum Reip. Deo inconsulto, abrogant ei jus excitandi Iudices. Exaggeretur ab ingratitudine pro variis beneficiis.cap.12.
units.tr: I. Apostasy from God. Reason: because those who ask that the state of the commonwealth be changed, without consulting God, take away from him the right of raising up judges. It is amplified from their ingratitude for various benefits. Chapter 12.

units.la: II. Diffidentia: quasi Deus non posset Ecclesiam diutius servare sine Rege.
units.tr: II. Distrust, as if God could not preserve the Church any longer without a king.

units.la: Amplif. ex causis, quas praetexunt, ver.5.
units.tr: Amplification from the causes which they put forward, verse 5.

units.la: III. Ingratitudo & iniuria erga Samuelem bene meritum, quem jam senem abjiciunt.
units.tr: III. Ingratitude and injury toward Samuel, who had deserved well, whom they cast off now that he is old.

units.la: IV. Ambitio & curiositas, ne videantur inferiores aliis gentibus, ver.5.
units.tr: IV. Ambition and curiosity, that they might not seem inferior to other nations, verse 5.

units.la: Obiectio: Deus jubet Samuelem assentiri: Ergo non improbat:
units.tr: Objection: God bids Samuel to consent; therefore he does not disapprove.

units.la: Resp. Respectu finis volebat, non respectu modi in agendo vitiosi:
units.tr: Answer: He wished it with respect to the end, not with respect to the vicious manner of acting.

units.la: Amplificetur ab ipsorum confessione cap. 12. 10.peccavimus, quia dereliquimus Jehovam.
units.tr: It is amplified from their own confession, chapter 12, verse 10: "We have sinned, because we have forsaken Jehovah."

units.la: Conclusio repetat propositionem additA Thesi: Non affectus nostros: sed verbum Dei consiliorum nostrorum regulam esse debere.
units.tr: The conclusion repeats the proposition with the added thesis: that our affections, not, but the Word of God, ought to be the rule of our counsels.

units.la: Exercitatio VII.
units.tr: Exercitatio VII.

units.la: Progymnasma, de recta quadragesimalis jejunii in nostris Ecclesiis abrogatione.
units.tr: Progymnasma, on the proper abolition of the Lenten fast in our Churches.

units.la: EXordium: Indignas esse superstitiones Pontificias, quae in Ecclesia vel nominentur.
units.tr: Exordium: The Papist superstitions are unworthy to be even named in the Church.

units.la: Adversat. Necessariam tamen esse taxationem.
units.tr: Objection. Nevertheless, an assessment is necessary.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia vulgo sint plausibiles.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because they are commonly applauded.

units.la: Amplif. etiam multis doctis, propter antiquitatem.
units.tr: Amplification: even by many learned men, on account of their antiquity.

units.la: II. Quia monstratione causarum abrogationis nis magis confirmentur conscientiæ piorum.
units.tr: II. Because the demonstration of the causes of their abolition confirms the consciences of the godly more firmly.

units.la: Narretur per hypothesin, consuetudo ieiunii quadragesimalis ante Pascha. 1. vetus: & ostendatur ejus varietas in numero dierum & ciborum abstinentia ex Socrat. lib.5.cap.21. Et Sozom. lib. 7.cap.19. II. Nostri temporis: & in hoc 1. Initium à Bacchanalium festo.
units.tr: Let the custom of the Lenten fast before Easter be set out by way of hypothesis. 1. The ancient custom, and let its variety be shown in the number of days and in the abstinence from foods, from Socrates, book 5, chapter 21, and Sozomen, book 7, chapter 19. II. The custom of our own time, and in this: 1. its beginning from the feast of the Bacchanalia.

units.la: 2. Duratio dierum 42.
units.tr: 2. Its duration of 42 days.

units.la: 3. Modus: abstinentia à cibis pontificia lege prohibiti.
units.tr: 3. Its manner: abstinence from foods forbidden by papal law.

units.la: 4. Finis: satisfactio pro furore Bacchanaliū, & expiatio aliorum peccatorum.
units.tr: 4. Its purpose: satisfaction for the frenzy of the Bacchanalia, and expiation of other sins.

units.la: Propositio: Recte abrogatum esse.
units.tr: Proposition: That it has been rightly abolished.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia non sit à Deo præceptum, sed inventum merè humanum.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because it was not commanded by God, but is a purely human invention.

units.la: Probetur testimonio Pontificiorum, quorum alii Telesphorum, alii Melchiaden, alii Montanum, alii alios authores faciunt.
units.tr: Let it be proved by the testimony of the Papists, some of whom make Telesphorus its author, others Melchiades, others Montanus, others other authors.

units.la: Ratio II. Quia prohibitio certorum ciborum sine expresso Dei mandato pugnat cum doctrina & libertate Evangelica. Col.2.16: Ne quis vos iudicet. 1.Cor.7.23. Ne fiatis servi hominum. Tit.1.15. Omnia munda mundis. 1.Tim.4.1. Doctrina dæmoniorum.
units.tr: Reason II. Because the prohibition of certain foods without an express command of God conflicts with Evangelical doctrine and liberty. Col. 2.16: Let no one judge you. 1 Cor. 7.23: Do not become slaves of men. Tit. 1.15: To the pure all things are pure. 1 Tim. 4.1: Doctrines of demons.

units.la: Ratio III. Quia fictitii cultus & conscientiarum torturæ non sunt feredæ in Ecclesia Christiana. Matth.15.9: Frustra me colunt. Col.2.16: Ne quis vos iudicet ob cibum, &c.
units.tr: Reason III. Because invented worship and the torture of consciences are not to be endured in the Christian Church. Matt. 15.9: In vain do they worship me. Col. 2.16: Let no one judge you concerning food, etc.

units.la: Minoris probatio sumatur ex definitione cultus Dei: & experientia: quæ probetur Hymno: Vt expiati annuis Jejuniorum victimis Tendamus ad Paschalia Digne colenda gaudia.
units.tr: The proof of the minor premise is to be taken from the definition of the worship of God, and from experience, which is proved by the hymn: That, cleansed by the yearly sacrifices of fasts, we may press on to celebrate the Paschal joys worthily.

units.la: Confutatio.
units.tr: Confutatio.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Christus jejunavit 40.dies. Ergo ecclesia recte imitatur: Ex Hymno Jesu quadragenaria Dicator abstinentia Qui ob salutem mentium Hoc sanxeras jejunium.
units.tr: Objection 1. Christ fasted forty days. Therefore the Church rightly imitates him, as in the hymn: Jesu, quadragenaria dicator abstinentia, Qui ob salutem mentium hoc sanxeras jejunium.

units.la: Resp. multiplex dissimilitudo.
units.tr: Answer. There is a manifold dissimilarity.

units.la: 1. Christus semel, isti quotannis.
units.tr: 1. Christ fasted once; they fast every year.

units.la: 2. Christus absque omni cibo: isti abstinentia tantum a carnibus: &c.
units.tr: 2. Christ fasted without any food; they abstain only from meat, etc.

units.la: 3. Christus absque fame, ideoque miraculose: isti expleta gula piscium lautitiis non esuriunt.
units.tr: 3. Christ was not hungry, and so fasted miraculously; they, having gorged themselves on luxuries of fish, are not hungry.

units.la: 4. Christus ex vocatione: isti ex superstitione. Accommodetur major & distinguatur: Exempla Christi esse imitanda.
units.tr: 4. Christ fasted by a calling; they fast from superstition. Let the major premise be granted and distinguished: that the examples of Christ are to be imitated.

units.la: 1. Quae sunt praecepta aut causam universalem habent. 2. Quae sunt possibilia. 3. Et absque superstitione.
units.tr: 1. Those which are commands or have a universal cause. 2. Those which are possible. 3. And those which are free from superstition.

units.la: Addatur negatio sanctionis jejunii: &c.
units.tr: Add the denial that the fast was ever sanctioned, etc.

units.la: Obiectio 11. Patres plerosque approbasse ut traditionem Apostolicam. Respond. Ex Socrate lib.5.cap.21. liquet diversum. Quandoquidem nemo de quadragesima praeceptum literarum monimetis proditum potest offendere, perspicuum est, Apostolos liberam potestatem in eadem cuiusq; menti & arbitrio permisisse, &c.
units.tr: Objection 11. Most of the Fathers approved it as an apostolic tradition. Answer. From Socrates, book 5, chapter 21, it is clear otherwise: Since no one can take offence at the precept of the forty days, handed down by the monuments of the letters, it is evident that the Apostles left the free power in this matter to each one's mind and judgement, etc.

units.la: Conclusio : Verum jejunium Christianorum non consistere in delectu ciborum, neque esse paucorum dierum abstinentiam: sed esse perpe-tuam vitæ sobrietatem ac temperantiam.
units.tr: Conclusion: The true fasting of Christians does not consist in the choice of foods, nor in abstaining for a few days, but in a perpetual sobriety and temperance of life.

units.la: Exercitatio VIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio VIII.

units.la: Censura affinitatis & expeditionis Iosaphati cum impio Achabo.2.Chron.18.&19.
units.tr: Censure of the alliance and expedition of Jehoshaphat with the impious Ahab, 2 Chron. 18 and 19.

units.la: EXordium habeat γνώμῳ : Luxuriant animi, &c.
units.tr: Let the exordium be γνώμῳ: Luxuriant animi, &c.

units.la: Hypothesis de Iosaphati fortuna, affinitate & expeditione contra Syros cum impio Achabo.
units.tr: Hypothesis: concerning Jehoshaphat's fortune, his marriage alliance and his expedition against the Syrians with the impious Ahab.

units.la: Propositio: Eum hauddubiè graviter peccasse.
units.tr: Proposition: that he undoubtedly sinned gravely.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia affinitas & societas militaris cũ impiis sit quædam conspiratio in Deum.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because an alliance and military fellowship with the impious is a kind of conspiracy against God.

units.la: Probetur ex verbis Prophetæ reprehendentis eum,cap.19,ver.2.
units.tr: Let it be proved from the words of the prophet rebuking him, chap. 19, vers. 2.

units.la: Amplificetur ex thesi de fœderibus cum impiis per occupationem: Etsi quædam aliquando sint licita & necessaria de finibus, commerciis, pace: tamen alia verbo Dei damnari,
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the thesis concerning covenants with the impious made for the sake of occupation: although some things are at times lawful and necessary concerning boundaries, commerce and peace, yet others are condemned by the Word of God.

units.la: Ratio II. à causa impulsiva: partim externa: amicitia regis potentis sed impii: partim interna: diffidentia auxilii divini.
units.tr: Reason II. From the impelling cause: partly external, the friendship of a powerful king who is nevertheless impious; partly internal, distrust of divine help.

units.la: Ratio III. Quia scandalum dedit subditis, quasi foris non improbaret Idololatriam, quam domi abrogaverat.
units.tr: Reason III. Because he gave an offence to his subjects, as if he did not disapprove abroad of the idolatry which he had abolished at home.

units.la: Amplificetur à circumstantiis: Michæ oraculo non obtemperat: connivet ad colaphos & carcerem Michæ in gratiam Achabi.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the circumstances: he does not obey the oracle of Micaiah; he connives at the blows and the prison of Micaiah for the sake of favour with Ahab.

units.la: Addatur locus communis de vi & poenis scan-dalorum.
units.tr: Let a commonplace be added concerning the force and penalties of offences.

units.la: Ratio I v. Quia ex foedere cogitur lacessere hostes Ecclesiae sine necessitate.
units.tr: Reason IV. Because by the covenant he was compelled to attack the enemies of the Church without necessity.

units.la: Amplificetur 1. quod contra pactum Asę patris cum Syris de non laedendo.
units.tr: Let it be amplified 1. because it was contrary to the pact of Asa, his father, with the Syrians, not to harm them.

units.la: 11. ab eventu: qui utrique fuit exitialis.
units.tr: 2. from the outcome, which proved fatal to both.

units.la: Ratio .v Quia impiis nuptiis perdidit Filium & Regnum.
units.tr: Reason V. Because by an impious marriage he lost his son and his kingdom.

units.la: Conclusio: Sic etiam pios Magistratus non raro graviter peccare, & poenas sibi attrahere, quoties affectus suos potius, quam verbum Dei normam consiliorum suorum faciunt.
units.tr: Conclusion: So also pious magistrates not infrequently sin gravely and draw penalties upon themselves, whenever they make their own affections, rather than the Word of God, the rule of their counsels.

units.la: Exercitatio IX.
units.tr: Exercitatio IX.

units.la: Progymnasma: de dogmate Lombardi lib. 3. d. 18. Christum sibi primo, deinde no-bis meritum esse.
units.tr: Progymnasma: on the dogma of Lombard, book 3, distinction 18, that Christ merited first for himself and then for us.

units.la: EXponatur dogma Lombardi: Christum meruisse quidem membris suis redemptionem a peccato & morte: sed meruisse etiam sibi.
units.tr: Let the dogma of Lombard be set out: that Christ indeed merited for his members redemption from sin and death, but also merited for himself:

units.la: 1. Corporis immortalitatem.
units.tr: 1. The immortality of his body.

units.la: 2. Animę impassibilitatem:
units.tr: 2. The impassibility of his soul.

units.la: 3. Nominis gloriam, h.e, Deitatis manifestationem, ut vocetur Deus.
units.tr: 3. The glory of the name, that is, the manifestation of his Deity, so that he is called God.

units.la: 4. Meruisse haec omnia tum plenitudine virtutum, quibus inde ab utero plenissimè fuerit in anima ornatus, ut meritis proficere non potuerit, tum in passione per humilitatis obedientiam.
units.tr: 4. That he merited all these things both by the fullness of virtues, with which he was most fully adorned in soul from the womb, so that he could not advance by merit, and in the passion by the obedience of humility.

units.la: Transitio: Hoc dogma non tantum à Scho-lasticis & Jesuitis hodiè defendi: sed etiam Doctoribus quibusdam Orthodoxis defendendum videri.
units.tr: Transition: This dogma is defended today not only by the Scholastics and Jesuits, but also appears to be defended by certain orthodox teachers.

units.la: Propositio per adversat: sed esse falsum.
units.tr: Proposition, by way of opposition: but it is false.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia nusquam traditur in Scriptura.
units.tr: Reason 1: because it is nowhere taught in Scripture.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Tradi à Paulo Phil. 2: Patri obedi-ens factus usq; ad mortem crucis, propterea exalta-vit eum Deus, &c. Ergo humilitatis obedientia fuit exaltationis meritum.
units.tr: Objection 1: Paul teaches in Philippians 2: "Becoming obedient to the Father unto the death of the cross, therefore God exalted him, etc." Therefore the obedience of humility was the merit of exaltation.

units.la: Respond. Est fallacia non causæ: quia non de meriti effectu, sed de humilitatis consequente præmio gratuito apostolus loquitur.
units.tr: Reply: This is a fallacy of non-cause, because the apostle speaks not of the effect of merit but of the free reward that follows humility.

units.la: 1. Probatio Ex verbis: ἐχαρίσατο αὐτῷ ὄνομα: Gratis dedit ei nomen: Ergo non meruit.
units.tr: 1. Proof from the words "ἐχαρίσατο αὐτῷ ὄνομα" [he gave him a name freely]: "Freely gave him the name": therefore he did not merit it.

units.la: II. Ex scopo Apostoli, qui exemplo Christi ad modestiam hortari, non fiduciam meriti afferre.
units.tr: II. From the purpose of the apostle, who by Christ's example exhorts to modesty, and does not offer a ground of confidence in merit.

units.la: Amplificetur à repugnantia effectorum gratiæ & meriti.
units.tr: It is further enlarged from the incompatibility of the effects of grace and merit.

units.la: Instantia 1. Particula διὸ notat causam exaltationis.
units.tr: Instance 1: The particle "διὸ" [therefore] denotes the cause of the exaltation.

units.la: Respond. non causam, sed ordinem seu consequentiam passionis & gloriæ: Vt alibi Luc.24.26.
units.tr: Reply: not the cause, but the order or sequence of the passion and the glory: as elsewhere, Luke 24:26.

units.la: Probetur ex 1.Pet.1.v.11. παθήματα καὶ τὰς μετὰ ταῦτα δόξας.
units.tr: Let it be proved from 1 Peter 1:11: "τὰ παθήματα καὶ τὰς μετὰ ταῦτα δόξας" [the sufferings and the glories that would follow].

units.la: Ostendatur locis similibus: Gen.22.16. Et 26.5. Luc.7.47.Heb.1.9.
units.tr: Let it be shown by similar passages: Genesis 22:16; 26:5; Luke 7:47; Hebrews 1:9.

units.la: Instantia II. Augustinum & Ambrosium de merito interpretari.
units.tr: Instance II: Augustine and Ambrose interpret it of merit.

units.la: Resp. I. Interpretationem repugnantem textui & scopo Apostoli non admitti.
units.tr: Reply I: An interpretation that contradicts the text and the purpose of the apostle is not admitted.

units.la: 11. Apud Ambrosium esse κατὰ χρῆσιν[?] vocabuli Mereri: omnibus patribus Latinis familiarem, pro posse vel obtinere: Quid humilitas meretur, id est, possit, hic ostendit, &c.
units.tr: II. In Ambrose the word "mereri" [to merit] is used in the sense of "κατὰ χρῆσιν" [by common usage]; it is familiar to all the Latin Fathers in the sense of "to be able or to obtain": "What humility merits, that is, what it is able to do, he shows here," etc.

units.la: Obiectio 11. Ex Heb.2.9. Videmus Iesum propter passionem mortis gloria & honore coronatum.
units.tr: Objection II: From Hebrews 2:9: "We see Jesus, because of the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour."

units.la: Resp. Fallacia compositionis & divisionis: quia ἀλλὰ τὸ πάθημα[?] cum ἡλαττωμένον[?], non cum ἐστεφανωμένον[?] est construendum.
units.tr: Reply: A fallacy of composition and division, because "ἀλλὰ τὸ πάθημα" [but on account of the suffering] must be construed with "ἡλαττωμένον" [made a little lower], not with "ἐστεφανωμένον" [crowned].

units.la: Conclusio 1. argumenti: Labefactatis hisce Lombardi & aliorum argumentis, liquere in scriptura non tradi.
units.tr: Conclusion 1 of the argument: With the arguments of Lombard and others thus overthrown, it is clear that this is not taught in Scripture.

units.la: Ratio 11. Quia repugnat Scripturae.
units.tr: Reason II: Because it is contrary to Scripture.

units.la: Probatio minoris sumatur ex dictis de fine incarnationis & passionis Christi. Jes.9. Matth.1.21. Luc.2.v.10.11. Ioh.3.16. Rom.8.31. 1.Cor.1.30. 2 Corint.8.9. Tit.2.14: quae loca non singula recitentur, sed ex iis collectim eliciatur argumentum repugnantiae: Tantum nobis est natus & passus, id est, nascendo & patiendo meruit. Ergo non sibi.
units.tr: The proof of the minor premise is taken from what is said about the purpose of Christ's incarnation and passion: Isaiah 9; Matthew 1:21; Luke 2:10-11; John 3:16; Romans 8:31; 1 Corinthians 1:30; 2 Corinthians 8:9; Titus 2:14. These passages are not recited one by one, but from them together the argument of incompatibility is drawn: He was born and suffered for us alone, that is, he merited by being born and by suffering. Therefore not for himself.

units.la: Confirmetur exclusiva antecedentis. 1. ab αὐτοχεία[?] Filii Dei, cui accommodetur dictu Ambrosii: Si nobis non resurrexit, utique non resurrexit, qui cur sibi resurgeret rationem non habebat.
units.tr: The exclusive form of the antecedent is confirmed: 1. from the "αὐτοχεία" [self-sufficiency] of the Son of God, to which Ambrose's saying applies: "If he did not rise for us, surely he did not rise, since he had no reason to rise for himself."

units.la: 11. A forma passionis: tantum fuit sacrificiu pro peccatis nostris Hebr.7.27: Talis enim nos decebat Pontifex, qui non pro se, sed pro populo sacrificaret.
units.tr: II. From the form of the passion: the sacrifice was only for our sins, Hebrews 7:27: "For such a high priest became us, who would not sacrifice for himself, but for the people."

units.la: Amplificetur ex argumentis consolatoriis & hortatoriis scripturae a nativitate & morte Christi, Luc.2.&c. itemque ab amore Dei erga nos ductis: Rom.5.& 8:quorum vim & consecutionem per dogma Lombardi enervari breviter oste-datur: Si sibi debuit aliquid mereri: non totum meritum cjus est nostrum.
units.tr: It is enlarged from the arguments of Scripture that comfort and exhort, drawn from the birth and death of Christ, Luke 2, etc., and likewise from the love of God toward us, Romans 5 and 8; the force and consequence of which is briefly shown to be weakened by Lombard's dogma: If he was bound to merit anything for himself, then his whole merit is not ours.

units.la: Ratio III. Quia repugnat sibi.
units.tr: Reason III: Because it contradicts itself.

units.la: Probatio minoris 1. Quia mereri impassibilitatem per justitiam: & eandem mereri per passionem, sunt repugnantia. Si habuit immortalitate & impassibilitatem per virtutes à conceptione: non demum meruit per crucem: mereri enim est acquirere, quod non habes. Aut dupliciter meruit, contra regulam justitię[?].
units.tr: Proof of the minor premise, 1: Because to merit impassibility by righteousness and to merit the same by passion are incompatible. If he had immortality and impassibility through virtues from his conception, he did not at last merit them by the cross; for to merit is to acquire what you do not have. Otherwise he merited the same thing twice, against the rule of justice.

units.la: II. Quia justitia Dei non requirit ejusdem rei duplex meritum perfectum.
units.tr: II. Because the justice of God does not require a double perfect merit of the same thing.

units.la: Ratio IV. Ex definitione meriti, quod secundum Lombardum est opus indebitum facions pramium ex indebito debitum, vel de minus debito magis debitum.
units.tr: Reason IV: From the definition of merit, which according to Lombard is "a work done that is not owed, producing a reward from what is not owed as something owed, or from less owed to more owed."

units.la: In minore ostendatur, non fuisse Christo indebitam.
units.tr: In the minor premise it is shown that these were not owed to Christ.

units.la: I. Incorruptibilitatem & impassibilitatem: quia homo ἀναμάρτητος.
units.tr: I. Incorruptibility and impassibility: because he was a man without sin.

units.la: II. Gloriam Deitatis: quia natura Deus.
units.tr: II. The glory of the Deity: because by nature he is God.

units.la: Conclusio: Retinendam ergo esse Scripturae perpetuam doctrinam: Christum non sibi sed nobis omnia meritum esse. 1. propter gloriam Dei, 2. propter consolationem nostram.
units.tr: Conclusion: The perpetual doctrine of Scripture must therefore be retained: that Christ merited all things not for himself but for us, 1. for the glory of God, 2. for our consolation.

units.la: Exercitatio X.
units.tr: Exercitatio X.

units.la: De Contentione Pauli & Petri, Galat. 2. an fuerit simulata. PARS AFFIRMANS.
units.tr: On the Dispute between Paul and Peter, Galatians 2, whether it was feigned. AFFIRMATIVE PART.

units.la: Initio breviter narretur Antiochena controversia per partes:
units.tr: At the outset, let the Antiochene controversy be briefly related in its parts:

units.la: 1. Libertas Petri in convictu gentium ante adventum Judæorum.
units.tr: 1. Peter's freedom in table fellowship with the Gentiles before the arrival of the Jews.

units.la: 2. Subductio à gentibus, post eorundem adventum.
units.tr: 2. His withdrawal from the Gentiles after the Jews had arrived.

units.la: 3. Causa separationis: metus offensionis Judæorum infirmorum.
units.tr: 3. The cause of the separation: fear of offending the weak Jews.

units.la: 4. Barnabę & Iudæorum factæ separationis approbatio & imitatio.
units.tr: 4. Barnabas's approval and imitation of the separation made by the Jews.

units.la: 5. Pauli publica objurgatio.
units.tr: 5. Paul's public rebuke.

units.la: Transitio ad propositionem: Multos hoc certamen Apostolorum parum attentè considerantes existimare, Petrum à Paulo de simulatione seriò accusari.
units.tr: Transition to the proposition: Many, not considering this contest between the Apostles carefully enough, think that Peter was seriously accused of hypocrisy by Paul.

units.la: Adversativa: Sed rem magna prudentia sic inter eos gestam esse.
units.tr: Adversative: But the matter was conducted between them with great prudence.

units.la: Propositio habens αἰτιολογίαν: Quia fuerit contentio non seria sed simulata.
units.tr: Proposition, containing an αἰτιολογία: Because the contention was not serious but feigned.

units.la: Declaretur modus agendi & scopus utriusq;: Paulum reprehendendo: Petrum reprehensionem ferendo ac cedendo: infirmos Iudæos à prava opinione abduxisse, & cum gentibus conciliasse.
units.tr: Let the manner of acting and the aim of each be declared: Paul, by rebuking; Peter, by bearing the rebuke and yielding; by these means they drew the weak Jews away from a perverse opinion and reconciled them with the Gentiles.

units.la: Confirmationis argumentum 1. Ex textu: quia κατὰ πρόσωπον[?], hoc est in speciem Paulus Petro restitit: v.11.
units.tr: Argument of confirmation, 1. From the text: because Paul "withstood him to the face," that is, in appearance, Paul resisted Peter: v. 11.

units.la: I. Quia Petri factum neque in convictu gentium, neque in separatione reprehensionem merebatur.
units.tr: I. Because Peter's conduct deserved rebuke neither in his table fellowship with the Gentiles nor in his separation.

units.la: Probetur minor. I. de convictu: Quia ex libertate Christiana, & absque scandalo convixit.
units.tr: Let the minor premise be proved. I. Concerning the table fellowship: because he ate with them from Christian freedom and without offence.

units.la: II. de separatione: Quia scandalum infirmorum Iudaeorum cavit juxta regulam: Si esca offendat fratrem meum, in aeternum non vescar carnibus: Item: Bonum est non vesci carnibus, aut facere aliquid, in quo infirmus offendatur.
units.tr: II. Concerning the separation: because he avoided offending the weak Jews, according to the rule: If food offends my brother, I will never eat meat again; likewise: It is good not to eat meat, or to do anything by which a weak brother is offended.

units.la: Accommodetur ad hypothesin: Petrum separatione sua utrisque infirmis consuluisse: Iudaeis Iudaizando: gentibus clam id faciendo.
units.tr: Let it be applied to the hypothesis: Peter by his separation provided for both weak groups: for the Jews by Judaizing, for the Gentiles by doing so secretly.

units.la: Obiectio I. Ex textu: Petrus erat reprehensibilis, ver.11.
units.tr: Objection I. From the text: Peter was blameworthy, v. 11.

units.la: Respond. καταγνωστέον[?] significare reprehensum, nempe non a Paulo: sed ab aliis consilii Apostolici ignaris.
units.tr: Response: καταγνωστέον[?] signifies "condemned," namely not by Paul but by others ignorant of the Apostolic counsel.

units.la: Obiectio II. Ex textu: Separavit se, metuens Iudaeos versic. duod. Ergo non scandalum fugiens.
units.tr: Objection II. From the text: He withdrew, fearing the Jews, v. 12. Therefore not avoiding offence.

units.la: Respond. metum fuisse non periculi sed scandali.
units.tr: Response: The fear was not of danger but of offence.

units.la: Amplif. à Petri fiducia ex Act.2.3.&4.
units.tr: Amplification from Peter's confidence, Acts 2, 3 and 4.

units.la: Obiect. III. Simulavit, & Barnabam in simulationem pertraxit, ver 13.
units.tr: Objection III. He dissembled, and drew Barnabas into the dissimulation, v. 13.

units.la: Resp. κατὰ[?] vocari ὑπόκρισιν[?] occultationem prudentis & officiosi consilii: cujus praeter Paulum & Barnabam etiam firmiores Iudaeos fecerit conscios, & approbatores habuerit. Amplificetur à thesi: Officiosam simulationē non semper esse vitiosam.
units.tr: Response: ὑπόκρισις[?] (hypocrisy) is called a concealment of a prudent and dutiful counsel, of which, besides Paul and Barnabas, he also made the firmer Jews aware and had them as approvers. Let it be amplified from the thesis: A dutiful dissimulation is not always sinful.

units.la: Obiectio 1 v. Non incessit recto pede veritatis Evangelii, ver.14.
units.tr: Objection IV. He did not walk uprightly by the truth of the Gospel, v. 14.

units.la: Respond. Opinione gentium, non intelligentium cjus consilium: quod confirmetur argumento sequente.
units.tr: Response: By the opinion of the Gentiles, not by those understanding his counsel; which is confirmed by the following argument.

units.la: Argumentum III. ab impossibili: Quia Petrus non potuerit errare in doctrina.
units.tr: Argument III. from the impossible: because Peter could not have erred in doctrine.

units.la: Probetur 1. in Thesi ex definitione Apostoli: 2. In specie ex oraculo, Act.10.
units.tr: Let it be proved 1. in the thesis from the definition of the Apostle; 2. in particular from the oracle, Acts 10.

units.la: Inde ostendatur Petrum omnium optimē doctrinam de libertate Christiana intellexisse.
units.tr: From this let it be shown that Peter understood the doctrine of Christian freedom best of all.

units.la: Conclusio argumenti per dilemma: aut ergo nō scrio: aut injustè reprehensum fuisse.
units.tr: Conclusion of the argument by a dilemma: either then he was not rebuked seriously, or he was rebuked unjustly.

units.la: Rejiciatur injusta reprehensio.
units.tr: The unjust rebuke is rejected.

units.la: 1. à persona Pauli & ejusdem in Petrum reliquosque apostolos charitate, de qua Galat.2.9.
units.tr: 1. from the person of Paul and his charity toward Peter and the remaining apostles, of which Galatians 2:9.

units.la: 11. ab incommodis inde redundaturis in universam Pauli doctrinam.
units.tr: 2. from the inconveniences that would thence overflow upon the whole doctrine of Paul.

units.la: Argumentum IV. ab effectu seriæ reprehensionis: Paulus fuisset author scandali publici.
units.tr: Argument IV. from the effect of a serious rebuke: Paul would have been the author of public scandal.

units.la: Argumentum V. Ex regula Christi Matth. 18.de correptionibus fratrum clam faciendis.
units.tr: Argument V. From Christ's rule, Matthew 18, concerning correcting brothers privately.

units.la: Amplif.a maiori: ne quidem minimos delinquentes oportere publicè statim taxari: multò minus tantum apostolum.
units.tr: Amplification from the greater: that not even the very smallest offenders ought to be publicly censured at once, much less such an apostle.

units.la: Concludatur ex prudentia Pauli: Potius privatim admoniturum fuisse dissentientem vel errātem, &c.
units.tr: Let it be concluded from Paul's prudence: that he would rather have admonished the dissenting or erring man privately, etc.

units.la: Argumentum VI. ab absurdo, Paulum non damnasse in Petro quod ipse cum laude fecerat, Decla-
units.tr: Argument VI. from the absurd: that Paul would not have condemned in Peter what he himself had done with praise. Let it be declared

units.la: Declaretur simile factum Pauli: ex Act. 16.3.& 18.18.& 21.24.
units.tr: Let a similar act of Paul be declared: from Acts 16:3, 18:18 and 21:24.

units.la: Approbetur factum ex 1.Cor.9.20.
units.tr: Let the act be approved from 1 Corinthians 9:20.

units.la: Argumentum VII. ab authoritate Origenis, Chrysostomi, Didymi, Hieronymi, &c. qui ita senserint de hoc facto.
units.tr: Argument VII. from the authority of Origen, Chrysostom, Didymus, Jerome, etc., who thought this way about this act.

units.la: Conclusio. Hoc judicium optime congruere cum charitate, & refutare blasphemias Porphyrii: quod vel Petrus erraverit, vel Paulus procaciter apostolorum Principem confutaverit.
