units.tr: Conclusion. This judgment agrees very well with charity, and refutes the blasphemies of Porphyry: that either Peter erred, or Paul insolently refuted the Prince of the apostles.

units.la: Pars negans.
units.tr: The negating part.

units.la: Propositio Exordii à Thesi: Saepe ad excusandos sanctorum hominum lapsus confingi multa absurda.
units.tr: Proposition of the Exordium from the Thesis: Often many absurd things are invented to excuse the lapses of holy men.

units.la: Probatio sit hypothesis per narratiunculam: cujus partes sint:
units.tr: Proof shall be the hypothesis, through a short narrative, whose parts are these:

units.la: 1. Hieronymum & alios quosdam veteres defendisse Petri simulationem Antiochenam.
units.tr: 1. That Jerome and some other ancient writers defended Peter's dissimulation at Antioch.

units.la: II. Causa, ut Porphyrii blasphemias refutarent.
units.tr: II. Cause: that they might refute the blasphemies of Porphyry.

units.la: III. Verior causa, ut primatum Petri stabilirent.
units.tr: III. Truer cause: that they might establish the primacy of Peter.

units.la: IV. Absurda inde conficta, quae addantur.
units.tr: IV. The absurdities thence devised, which are added:

units.la: 1. Aliquam simulationem & dispensationem veri, h.e. mendacium, esse honestam. 2. Paulum tali dispensatione de Petro scripsisse, quod in veritate Evangelii claudicaverit. 3. non serio Petrum reprehendisse.
units.tr: (1) that some dissimulation and dispensation of the truth, that is, a lie, is honourable; (2) that Paul wrote of Peter in such a dispensation, that he limped in the truth of the Gospel; (3) that Peter was not seriously rebuked.

units.la: V. Augustini contra Hieronymum acris disceptatio. Adversativa. Sed non ex personis, verum ex causa ipsa judicandum esse, & fugiendum ita, ut ne praeter casam.
units.tr: V. Augustine's sharp dispute against Jerome. Adversative. But judgement must be made not from the persons but from the cause itself, and one must avoid it so as not to go beyond the case.

units.la: Propositio per ἀνθυπ[?]: Etsi sententia Hieronymi speciosis rationibus fucari possit: tamen sine dubio veriorem sententiam ab Augustino defendi: Petrum à Paulo jure & serio reprehensum esse.
units.tr: Proposition through the counter-argument: Although Jerome's opinion can be dressed up with specious reasons, nevertheless without doubt Augustine defends the truer opinion: that Peter was rightly and seriously rebuked by Paul.

units.la: Confirmationis Argumentum fit unicum: Quis Petrus graviter peccaverit: i. In infirmos Iudæos. ii. In Barnabam collegam: iii. In gentiles conversos. iv. In libertatem Christianam:
units.tr: The argument of the confirmation is a single one: How grievously Peter sinned: i. against the weak Jews; ii. against his colleague Barnabas; iii. against the converted Gentiles; iv. against Christian liberty.

units.la: Singula membra brevissime declarentur: & ad-datur conclusio argumenti: non ergo Paulum cum eo colludere voluisse vel potuisse absq; peccato.
units.tr: Let the individual members be declared very briefly, and the conclusion of the argument added: therefore Paul did not wish, or was not able, to collude with him without sin.

units.la: Probatio antecedentis. Ex textu. 1. ὅτι κατηγνωσμέ-νος ἦν[?]: quia reprehensibilis erat.
units.tr: Proof of the antecedent. From the text. 1. that he stood condemned: because he was blameworthy.

units.la: Ostendatur participium pro nomine positum esse, ex absurdo sensu contrario: Ego restitui ei: quia fuit reprehensus.
units.tr: Let it be shown that the participle is used in place of a noun, from the absurd contrary sense: "I resisted him, because he was rebuked."

units.la: Probatio ii. Quia separatio à gentibus sine professione causarum fuit per se scandalosa distractio Ecclesiæ: & injussa coactio gentium ad Iudaizandum, si vellent communionem Petri: textus: Cur cogis gentes, &c.
units.tr: Proof ii. Because separation from the Gentiles, without a profession of reasons, was in itself a scandalous disruption of the Church, and an unordered compulsion of the Gentiles to Judaize, if they wished fellowship with Peter. Text: Why do you compel the Gentiles, etc.

units.la: Clausula per occupationem: Cavendum quidem fuisse scandalum Iudæorum: sed non cum graviore scandalo gentium, & distractione Ecclesiæ. Applicetur ad regulam scandali: atque ostendatur, Petrum utrisq; male consuluisse.
units.tr: Closing clause by way of anticipation: Indeed the scandal of the Jews ought to have been avoided, but not with the greater scandal of the Gentiles and the disruption of the Church. Let it be applied to the rule of scandal, and it be shown that Peter dealt badly with both.

units.la: Probatio III. Ex textu ver.13: Quia simulavit: & alios simulatione seduxit.
units.tr: Proof III. From the text, verse 13: Because he dissembled, and led others astray by his dissimulation.

units.la: Declaretur & ostendatur: simulationem non fuisse occultationem consilii officiosi: sed osten-sionem falsæ opinionis: I. de necessitate Iuda-ismi ad salutem. II. de illicito convictu cum gentibus.
units.tr: Let it be declared and shown that the dissimulation was not a concealment of a dutiful counsel, but a display of a false opinion: I. about the necessity of Judaism for salvation; II. about the unlawful table-fellowship with the Gentiles.

units.la: Amplificetur ab effectu pernicioso in Iudæis & gentibus.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the pernicious effect upon both Jews and Gentiles.

units.la: Subiiciatur maior: Talem simulationem haud dubiè peccatum esse: confirmetur testimonio Ciceronis ex Lælio: Simulatio tum omnium rerum est vitiosa (tollit enim iudicium veri) tum amicitia repugnat maxime.
units.tr: Let the major premise be stated: that such dissimulation is undoubtedly sin; let it be confirmed by the testimony of Cicero from the Laelius: "Dissimulation is faulty in all matters (for it removes the judgement of what is true), and it is especially opposed to friendship."

units.la: Probatio IV. ex ver.14: Quia non incessit recte pede veritatis.
units.tr: Proof IV. From verse 14: Because he did not walk uprightly according to the truth of the Gospel.

units.la: Declaretur, fuisse claudicationem non in do-ctrina ipsa, sed in πράξει[?] doctrinę: & ostendatur, non tantum opinione gentium, sed revera, & Pauli judicio Petrum claudicasse: ex textu: Cum ego vidissem, &c.
units.tr: Let it be declared that the limping was not in the doctrine itself, but in the practice [praxis] of the doctrine; and let it be shown that Peter limped not merely in the opinion of the Gentiles, but in reality and by Paul's judgement, from the text: When I saw, etc.

units.la: Hic inferatur argumentum Augustini contra Hieronymum: aut Petrum revera claudicasse, aut Paulum mentiri.
units.tr: Here the argument of Augustine against Jerome is inferred: either Peter really limped, or Paul lied.

units.la: Minor sit negatio posterioris, & confirmetur: 1. ex ver.20.c.1: In iis quæ scribo vobis, ecce coram Deo non mentior. 2. Ex thesi: quia nullum ne of-ficiosum quidem mendacium scriptoribus sacris est attribuendum.
units.tr: The minor premise is the denial of the latter, and let it be confirmed: 1. from verse 20 of chapter 1: In what I write to you, behold, before God I do not lie. 2. From the thesis: because no lie, not even a dutiful one, is to be attributed to the sacred writers.

units.la: Hæc nonnihil elaboretur ab autho-ritate Scripturæ S: à discrimine Scriptorum Ca-nonicorum & Ecclesiasticorum: & à periculo di-versæ sententiæ. Claudatur verbis Augustini: Satius esse credere Paulum vere omnia scripsisse: quam Petrum non rede aliquid egisse.
units.tr: These matters are to be worked out somewhat more fully from the authority of Holy Scripture, from the distinction between the Canonical and Ecclesiastical writings, and from the danger of a contrary opinion. Let it be concluded with the words of Augustine: "It is better to believe that Paul wrote everything truly, than that Peter did nothing wrongly."

units.la: Confutatio.
units.tr: Confutatio.

units.la: Ad argumentum I. Resp. rejectione glossæ. Probetur ex ratione ὁπ καταγνωσμένος ὧν: & ex scopo totius narrationis, qui est, ostendere, certitudinem Evangelii sui non à Petro & apostolis aliis pendere.
units.tr: To the first argument. Reply: by rejecting the gloss. It is proved from the reason that he was "condemned" (ὁπ καταγνωσμένος ὧν [ὅτι καταγνωσμένος ἦν]), and from the aim of the whole narrative, which is to show that the certainty of his Gospel does not depend on Peter and the other apostles.

units.la: Ad argumentum II. Resp. negatione minoris: quia Petrum in separatione scandalosa peccāsse ostensum sit.
units.tr: To the second argument. Reply: by denying the minor premise, since it has been shown that Peter sinned in a scandalous separation.

units.la: Ad argumentum III. Resp. 1. approbatione ac defensione minoris: quod non errare potuerit in doctrina. 2. negatione majoris: probetur ex inæqualitate causarum certitudinis doctrinæ & actionum seu morum in apostolis, h. e, perfectæ illuminationis, & imperfectæ regenerationis.
units.tr: To the third argument. Reply 1: by approving and defending the minor premise, that he could not err in doctrine. 2: by denying the major premise. It is proved from the inequality of the causes of certainty in doctrine and of the actions or conduct of the apostles, that is, of perfect illumination and imperfect regeneration.

units.la: Breviter addatur thesis contra calumnias Porphyrii: Lapsus morales sanctorum non derogare doctrinæ divinitus ipsis inspiratæ.2.Cor.4.7: Habemus thesaurum in vasis testaceis, &c.
units.tr: The thesis may be briefly added against the calumnies of Porphyry: the moral lapses of the saints do not detract from the doctrine divinely inspired in them. 2 Cor. 4.7: "We have this treasure in earthen vessels," etc.

units.la: Amplif. à causa, cur Deus infirmis inspiraverit doctrinam: ex 1.Cor.1.17. Et cap.2.5.
units.tr: An amplification from the cause, why God inspired doctrine in weak men: from 1 Cor. 1.17, and chapter 2.5.

units.la: Ad argumentum IV. Resp. per distinctionem majoris: Serió reprehendens publicè Doctorem Ecclesiæ author est scandali publici: Si fiat 1. sine officio. 11. sine causa gravi. 111. sine prudentia & tia & charitate. I v. non studio avertendi scan-dalum gravius ab alio datum.
units.tr: To the fourth argument. Reply by distinguishing the major premise: one who rebukes a teacher of the Church publicly and in earnest is the author of public scandal, if this is done (1) without an office, (2) without a serious cause, (3) without prudence and charity, (4) without the aim of averting a greater scandal given by another.

units.la: Fiat applicatio distinctionis ad factum Pauli: & ostendatur, scandalum, si quod fuit, accidentarium seu acceptum fuisse.
units.tr: Let the distinction be applied to the deed of Paul, and let it be shown that the scandal, if there was any, was incidental and was taken up by others.

units.la: Ad argumentum V. Resp. 1. explicatione regulæ Christi, de lapsibus privatis privatim corrigendis. 2. Assertione publicæ reprehensionis publici peccati: ex eadem regula: Dic Ecclesiæ: & ex dicto: 1. Tim. 5.20. Eos qui peccant, coram omnibus argue.
units.tr: To the fifth argument. Reply: (1) by explaining Christ's rule concerning private faults, which are to be corrected privately; (2) by asserting that public rebuke of public sin is required by the same rule, "Tell it to the Church," and by the saying of 1 Tim. 5.20: "Those who sin, rebuke before all."

units.la: Ad argumentum VI. Respond. negatione minoris, quod Paulus idem fecerit.
units.tr: To the sixth argument. Reply: by denying the minor premise, that Paul did the same thing.

units.la: Probatio 1. quia nunquam coëgit gentes Judaizare: ut Petrus.
units.tr: Proof (1): because he never compelled the Gentiles to Judaize, as Peter did.

units.la: II. quia Iudaizaverit cum Iudæis infirmis citra confirmationem eorum in errore: & citra scandalum gentium. Ratio: quia addidit professionem suæ sententiæ de libertate.
units.tr: (2): because he Judaized with the weak Jews without confirming them in their error, and without giving scandal to the Gentiles. The reason: because he added a profession of his own opinion concerning liberty.

units.la: Ostendatur: Petrum dissimulasse doctrinam, ex separatione.
units.tr: It is to be shown that Peter dissembled in his doctrine, from the separation.

units.la: Addatur in Thesi de abusu adiaphorum: Nō accedente doctrina in adiaphoris, nec curari mor-bum infirmorum, nec vitari scandalum: ideoque abusum esse.
units.tr: Let it be added in the thesis concerning the abuse of indifferent things: unless doctrine accompanies the use of indifferent things, neither is the sickness of the weak cured nor is scandal avoided; and therefore it is an abuse.

units.la: Ad argumentum VII. Respond. 1. Autho-ritates humanas cedere divinæ: ideo Augustinū recte provocare ad unum Paulum contra septem Patres ab Hieronymo allegatos.
units.tr: To the seventh argument. Reply: (1) human authorities must yield to divine authority; therefore Augustine rightly appealed to Paul alone against the seven Fathers cited by Jerome.

units.la: II. Tertullianum, Cyprianum, Ambrosium, recte sentire cum Augustino.
units.tr: (2) Tertullian, Cyprian and Ambrose rightly think with Augustine.

units.la: Conclusio repetat breviter propositionem, & ostendeostendat hujus quæstionis non causam: ut lapsus sanctorum exagitentur: veram causam: 1. ne excusetur hypocrisis & simulatio. 11. ne veritas Scripturæ periclitetur.
units.tr: The conclusion should briefly repeat the proposition, and show that the cause of this question is not the following: that the lapses of the saints be censured; the true cause is (1) that hypocrisy and dissimulation should not be excused; (2) that the truth of Scripture should not be endangered.

units.la: Exercitatio XI.
units.tr: Exercitatio XI.

units.la: Paraphrasis orationis Jonathæ pro Davide apud Saulem Patrem intercedentis.
units.tr: Paraphrase of the speech of Jonathan interceding for David before Saul his father.
1 Sam. 19, vers. 4, 5.

units.la: Præmittatur ex historia occasio: de odio Saulis in Davidem: de consilio occidendi: de Jonathæ indicio: & intercessionis pollicitatione.
units.tr: Let the occasion be set out first from the history: Saul's hatred of David, his plan to kill him, Jonathan's warning, and his promise to intercede.

units.la: Propositio: Non debes interficere Davidem.
units.tr: Proposition: You ought not to kill David.

units.la: Argumenta ducantur ex loco honesti.
units.tr: The arguments are drawn from what is honourable.

units.la: Argumentum I. quia est servus tuus, cui de-betur defensio.
units.tr: Argument I. Because he is your servant, to whom defence is owed.

units.la: Deducatur ex jure herili in servos, de quo non inserantur ipsa dicta.
units.tr: This is deduced from the master's right over servants; the words themselves are not to be inserted here.

units.la: Argumentum II. quia innocens.
units.tr: Argument II. Because he is innocent.

units.la: Probatio: nec in te, nec in regnum peccavit.
units.tr: Proof: He has sinned neither against you nor against the kingdom.

units.la: Maior argumenti illustretur à fine gladii regibus à Deo concessi: & amplificetur ex Thesi contraria: Grave esse, fundere sanguinem inno-xium.
units.tr: The major premise of the argument is illustrated from the purpose of the sword, which God has granted to kings, and is amplified from the contrary thesis: that it is a grievous thing to shed innocent blood.

units.la: Argumentum III. Quia optimè de te & regno meritus.
units.tr: Argument III. Because he has deserved very well of you and of the kingdom.

units.la: Probetur ex victoria de Goliatho.
units.tr: Let this be proved from the victory over Goliath.

units.la: Amplificetur ex circunstantiis historiæ.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the circumstances of the history:

units.la: 1. de magnitudine periculi publici & ipsius Davidis.
units.tr: (1) from the greatness of the public danger and of David's own danger;

units.la: II. de commodis publicis victoriâ consecutis. Addatur ἤϑ⊙[?], per provocationem ad testimonium & conscientiam ipsius Saulis.
units.tr: (2) from the public benefits gained by the victory. Let there be added [a reference to] ἤθος [character], by appeal to the testimony and conscience of Saul himself.

units.la: Argum. IV. Quia vir fortis: Posuit vitam, in manu sua: quod referatur ad omnia ejus hacte-nus praeclare gesta.
units.tr: Argument IV. Because he is a brave man: "He put his life in his hand"; this is to be referred to all the splendid deeds he has performed so far.

units.la: Argumentum V. Quia Deo charus. Probatio: Iehova dedit salutem per eum.
units.tr: Argument V. Because he is dear to God. Proof: Jehovah gave salvation through him.

units.la: Conclusio repetat propositionē: & habeat πάν[?] Servetur in tota oratione decorum Filii ad Pa-trem regem.
units.tr: The conclusion should repeat the proposition, and have πάν [everything]. Throughout the whole speech the propriety of a son speaking to his father the king is to be observed.

units.la: Exercitatio XII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XII.

units.la: Διαλλαγὴ locorum Scripturæ in speciem pugnantium. Rom.3.28.
units.tr: Reconciliation of passages of Scripture that seem to contradict each other. Rom. 3.28.

units.la: COlligimus igitur, fide hominem justificari absque operibus legis:
units.tr: We conclude, therefore, that a man is justified by faith without the works of the law.

units.la: Et Iacob.2.24: Videtis igitur, ex operibus justificari hominem, & non ex fide tantum.
units.tr: And James 2.24: You see, then, that a man is justified by works, and not by faith only.

units.la: Seu Conciliatio Pauli & Iacobi: de justifica-tione hominis.
units.tr: Or, the reconciliation of Paul and James on the justification of man.

units.la: EXordium brevissimè exponat.
units.tr: The introduction should be set out very briefly.

units.la: I. Doctrinam Pauli de justificatione fidei absque operibus.
units.tr: I. The doctrine of Paul concerning justification by faith without works.

units.la: II. Præcipua ejusdem argumenta ab exemplo Abrahami: à testimonio Davidis: ab effectu legis: addita eorundem & doctrinæ Paulinæ ap-probatione.
units.tr: II. His principal arguments: from the example of Abraham, from the testimony of David, from the effect of the law; with the approval of Paul's doctrine by these same witnesses added.

units.la: III. Doctrinam Iacobi cap. 2. de justificatione ex operibus non ex fide tantum.
units.tr: III. The doctrine of James, chapter 2, on justification by works, and not by faith only.

units.la: Transitio: Videri repugnantiam: Haec ostendatur oppositione propositionum: Homo iustificatur sola fide, absque operibus. Homo non iustificatur sola fide, absque operibus.
units.tr: Transition: a contradiction seems to appear. This is shown by the opposition of the propositions: A man is justified by faith alone, without works. A man is not justified by faith alone, without works.

units.la: Amplificetur ab effectu apparentis repugnantiae.
units.tr: The apparent contradiction is amplified by its effect.

units.la: I. apud quosdam Orthodoxos, qui & olim & recens, non intellecta mente utriusque, Epistolam Jacobi totam abjecerint:
units.tr: I. Among certain orthodox writers, who, both in former times and recently, not having understood the mind of each, have rejected the whole Epistle of James.

units.la: II. apud Pontificios, qui ex Jacobo justitiam operum defendentes, ita conciliant, ut sententia Pauli depravent.
units.tr: II. Among the Papists, who, defending the righteousness of works from James, reconcile the two in such a way that they corrupt the opinion of Paul.

units.la: Subiungatur conciliatio Pontificia: Paulum loqui de justificatione prima, qua homo ex injusto fit justus, & de operibus, quae fiunt ante fidem & gratiam, solis viribus liberi arbitrii: Iacobum loqui, de justificatione secunda, qua quis ex justo fit justior, & de operibus ex fide & gratia profectis.
units.tr: The Papist reconciliation is added: Paul speaks of the first justification, by which a man becomes righteous from unrighteous, and of works which are done before faith and grace, by the powers of free will alone; James speaks of the second justification, by which one who is righteous becomes more righteous, and of works proceeding from faith and grace.

units.la: PROPOSITIO bimembris per adversativam. Sed nec esse repugnantiam: nec Pontificiorum conciliationem simpliciter veram.
units.tr: A proposition of two parts joined by an adversative. But there is neither a contradiction, nor is the Papists' reconciliation simply true.

units.la: Confirmatio prioris membri sit ratio una: Quia non idem affirmetur & negetur de eodem.
units.tr: The confirmation of the first part is one reason: because the same thing is not affirmed and denied of the same thing.

units.la: Declaretur, quia de alia tum iustificatione tum fide uterque loquatur.
units.tr: Let it be explained: because each speaks of a different justification and of a different faith.

units.la: Ostendatur utrunque, per geminam ἀντίθεσιν, in quibus consistit conciliatio.
units.tr: Let each be shown, by the twofold antithesis in which the reconciliation consists.

units.la: I. Paulus agit de justificatione coram Deo.
units.tr: I. Paul treats of justification before God.

units.la: Probatio brevis sumatur ex serie disputationis. nis.Rom.1.2.3. Item:ex cap.3.ver.23.24.item ex definitione justificationis cap.4.ver.6.
units.tr: A brief proof is to be taken from the sequence of the argument: Rom. 1.2.3. Likewise from chapter 3, verses 23 and 24, and likewise from the definition of justification in chapter 4, verse 6.

units.la: Ἀντίθεσις[?]: Iacobus dejustificationis illius externa ostensione coram hominib. per opera.
units.tr: Antithesis [?]: James treats of that justification in its external manifestation before men, through works.

units.la: Probetur 1. ex verbis. Ostende mihi, nempe homini, fidem tuam ex operibus.
units.tr: Let it be proved (1) from the words: Show me, namely, to a man, your faith by your works.

units.la: II. Ex Abrahami exemplo, qui dicitur justificatus oblatione Filii, hoc est, pro justo declaratus coram hominib. ver.21.
units.tr: II. From the example of Abraham, who is said to have been justified by the offering of his Son, that is, declared righteous before men, verse 21.

units.la: Confirmetur interpretatio ex historia Gen. 22.
units.tr: Let the interpretation be confirmed from the story in Gen. 22.

units.la: 12. Nunc cognovi: quo in loco observetur ἀνθρω-ποπάθεια[?].
units.tr: 12. Now I know: in which place the anthropopathy [?] is to be noted.

units.la: Item, ex justificatione Abrahami per fidem multo ante oblationem hanc facta. Gen. 15. 6. Rom.4.3.
units.tr: Likewise, from the justification of Abraham by faith, made long before this offering. Gen. 15.6. Rom. 4.3.

units.la: Item ex locis similibus. Psal.51: ut justificeris: Matth.11.19.Luc.7.29.Luc.10.29.&c.
units.tr: Likewise from similar passages: Ps. 51: that you may be justified; Matt. 11.19; Luke 7.29; Luke 10.29; etc.

units.la: Clausula colligat primam conciliationis partem. Non pugnare Apostolos, dum justificatio-nem diversam adimunt & tribuunt operibus.
units.tr: The conclusion gathers the first part of the reconciliation: the Apostles do not contradict each other, since they deny one justification and attribute another to works.

units.la: Secunda pars Διδασκαλίας[?].
units.tr: The second part of the Doctrine.

units.la: Transitio ad secundam ἀντίθεσιν per προομολο-γίαν[?]: Etsi justificari idem significaret Apostolis, tamen Fidem non idem eis significare.
units.tr: Transition to the second antithesis, by way of a preliminary statement: although to be justified would mean the same thing to the Apostles, faith would not mean the same thing to them.

units.la: Ostendatur συνωνυμία[?], per alteram ἀντίθεσιν, cujus prior pars sit: Paulum loqui de fide vera seu viva.
units.tr: Let the synonymy be shown through the other antithesis, whose first part is this: Paul speaks of true or living faith.

units.la: Declaratur, quæ & qualis hæc sit.
units.tr: It is explained what this faith is, and of what kind it is.

units.la: I. ἀ[?] forma, quæ est fiducia gratuitæ remissio-nis peccatorum, & acceptationis pro justo, per & propter Christi redemtionem. Rom.3.14. Et cap.4.5.7.
units.tr: I. As to its form, which is the trust in the free forgiveness of sins and acceptance as righteous, through and on account of the redemption of Christ. Rom. 3.14; and chap. 4.5.7.

units.la: I. A proprio: quod est studium novæ obedientiæ. Rom.3.31. per fidem stabilimus legem. Act.15.18: Fide purificans corda; Gal.5.6. Fides per charitatem efficax.
units.tr: I. As to its source, which is the zeal for new obedience. Rom. 3.31: by faith we establish the law. Acts 15.18: cleansing hearts by faith; Gal. 5.6: faith working through love.

units.la: III. Ab effectis: quæ sunt: pax conscientiæ, εὐθυμία ad Deum, spes gloriæ, &c. Rom.5.1.
units.tr: III. As to its effects, which are: peace of conscience, a cheerful confidence toward God, the hope of glory, etc. Rom. 5.1.

units.la: Subiiciatur brevis probatio: hanc fidem solam justificare.
units.tr: Let a brief proof be added: that this faith alone justifies.

units.la: I. Quia sola justificavit Abrahamum, Rom.4
units.tr: I. Because it alone justified Abraham. Rom. 4.

units.la: II. Quia sola amplectitur gratuitam imputationem justitiæ & acceptationem propter Christum, Rom.4.v.5.6.
units.tr: II. Because it alone embraces the free imputation of righteousness and acceptance on account of Christ. Rom. 4.5.6.

units.la: III. Quia sola certas facit conscientias, cum legis conditio sit impossibilis. Rom.4.14.
units.tr: III. Because it alone makes consciences certain, since the condition of the law is impossible. Rom. 4.14.

units.la: Addatur brevis ἐπανόρθωσις: Fidem justificare non habitualiter, sed correlative: Quod quale sit declaretur & probetur ex Rom.5.19: Obedientia unius iusti constituentur multi.
units.tr: Let a brief correction be added: faith justifies not habitually but correlatively. What kind of thing this is shall be explained and proved from Rom. 5.19: By the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.

units.la: Ἀντιθέσεως; pars altera: Jacobum adimere justificationem fidei historicæ & mortuæ:
units.tr: The other part of the antithesis: James removes justification from historical and dead faith.

units.la: Probetur I. Ex textu ver.14: Num potest hæc fides eum servare: Et ver.17. Fides mortua est. II. Ex scopo: Quia refutat hypocritas fidem jactantes, sed nullo opere declarantes. III. Quia vocat fidem Dæmoniorum: v.19.
units.tr: Let it be proved: I. From the text of verse 14: Can this faith save him? And verse 17: Faith is dead. II. From the purpose: because he refutes hypocrites who boast of faith but show it by no work. III. Because he calls it the faith of demons: v. 19.

units.la: Clausula colligat alteram conciliationis partem: Non esse pugnantia: Fides viva iustificat: Et, Fides mortua non iustificat.
units.tr: The conclusion should bind together the second part of the reconciliation: that they are not contradictory: Living faith justifies; and, Dead faith does not justify.

units.la: Addantur συνθέσεις: I. De consensu apostolorum in his duobus: Fidem vivam iustificare co-ram ram Deo: Et: Fidem vivam operibus iustificare coram hominibus.
units.tr: Let the syntheses be added: I. On the agreement of the apostles in these two points: living faith justifies before God; and: living faith justifies by works before men.

units.la: II. Authoritatem Epistolae Iacobi praetextu repugnantiae in dubium vocari non debere.
units.tr: II. The authority of the Epistle of James ought not to be called into doubt on the pretext of contradiction.

units.la: Tertia pars Διαλλαγῆς.
units.tr: The third part of the Reconciliation.

units.la: Transitio fit nexus: & repetat secundum propositionis membrum de falsitate conciliationis Pontificiae.
units.tr: Transition, making the link: and he repeats the second member of the proposition, concerning the falsity of the Papistic reconciliation.

units.la: Confirmatio per ἀνυπονοήτως breviter praemittat limitationis additae rationem: recte quidē intelligi ac dici posse: Paulum de prima, Iacobum de secunda Iustificatione loqui: juxta declarationem primae antithescos
units.tr: Confirmation: by ἀνυπονοήτως he first briefly sets out the reason for the added limitation: that it can rightly be understood and said that Paul speaks of the first justification and James of the second, according to the explanation of the first antithesis.

units.la: Ratio: quia etiam Scriptura aliquando sub justificatione sanctificationē coprehēdat: Rō.8.30.
units.tr: Reason: because Scripture sometimes also comprehends sanctification under justification: Rom. 8.30.

units.la: Deinde per adversat. ostendat vitia, quae sunt totidem argumenta.
units.tr: Then, by way of contrast, he shows the faults, which are as many arguments.

units.la: Primò: depravat doctrinam Pauli de justificatione Evangelica:
units.tr: First: they corrupt Paul's doctrine of evangelical justification.

units.la: Probetur: quia definit justificationem hyperphysica quadam alteratione seu qualitatis infusione (ut cum physice aqua frigida fit calida: politicè egenus fit dives:) cum sit gratuita absolutio à reatu, & justitiae imputatio propter Christi satisfactionem & meritum.
units.tr: Proof: because they define justification as a certain hyperphysical alteration, or infusion of quality (as when cold water is physically made warm, or a needy man is made rich in a political sense), whereas it is a gratuitous absolution from guilt, and the imputation of righteousness on account of Christ's satisfaction and merit.

units.la: Secundò: Confundit fidem justificantem & historicam.
units.tr: Second: they confuse justifying faith and historical faith.

units.la: Ratio: quia fingit, eidem fidei tribui, & adimi justificationem coram Deo.
units.tr: Reason: because they pretend that justification before God is ascribed to and taken away from the same faith.

units.la: Tertiò: Stabilit vires liberi arbitrii ad bona operaante gratiam & fidem: contra Scripturam 2.Cor.3.5.Ioh.15.5.Et Rom. 14: Quicquid non est ex fide peccatum est.
units.tr: Third: they establish the powers of free will to do good works without grace and faith, contrary to Scripture: 2 Cor. 3.5; John 15.5; and Rom. 14: Whatever is not of faith is sin.

units.la: Quarto : Confundit beneficium justificationis & regenerationis.
units.tr: Fourth: they confuse the benefit of justification and regeneration.

units.la: Ratio: quia fingit hanc tantum esse illius [?]σεοπ[?]- [?]νευστιν [?]: & quidem coram Deo.
units.tr: Reason: because they pretend that this alone is that [illegible] ... and indeed before God.

units.la: Explicentur brevissimè discrimina justificationis & regenerationis:
units.tr: Let there be explained very briefly the differences between justification and regeneration:

units.la: I. In genere: quod justificatio sit relationis: regeneratio alterationis.
units.tr: I. In kind: justification is of relation; regeneration is of alteration.

units.la: II. In forma, quòd illa sit imputatio justitiæ Christi'per fidem : hæc instauratio naturæ per Spiritum S.
units.tr: II. In form: that the former is the imputation of Christ's righteousness through faith; the latter is the restoration of nature through the Holy Spirit.

units.la: III. In ordine : quod tempore quidem sint simul: sed illa hanc præcedat naturâ.
units.tr: III. In order: that in time they are indeed simultaneous, but the former precedes the latter in nature.

units.la: IV. Ingradibus : quod illa perfecta sit in hac vita. Rom.8.1. 1.Ioh.1.7. Hæc tantum incoata & semper crescens: quod sensus, querelæ, & preces sanctorum testantur.
units.tr: IV. In degrees: that the former is perfect in this life (Rom. 8.1; 1 John 1.7), whereas the latter is only begun and always growing, as the feelings, complaints and prayers of the saints bear witness.

units.la: Addatur hic [illegible, ~7 letters] de necessitate discrimi-nis: ne obscuretur gratia Christi:& labefactetur consolatio Evangelii in judicio Dei.
units.tr: Here should be added [illegible, about seven letters] on the necessity of the distinction: lest the grace of Christ be obscured and the comfort of the Gospel be weakened in the judgment of God.

units.la: Quinto: Falsò statuit Paulum tantum adimere justificationem operibus ante gratiam.
units.tr: Fifth: they wrongly maintain that Paul took away justification only from works done before grace.

units.la: Probetur: quia adimit eam etiam operibus Abrahami renati. Rom.4.2. Et ex antithesi gratiæ atque operum. Rom.11.6.
units.tr: Proof: because he takes it away also from the works of Abraham after he was born again (Rom. 4.2), and from the antithesis of grace and works (Rom. 11.6).

units.la: Conclusio habeat [?]συλλογισμὸν[?]. Nollete sophisma-tum pontificiorum de Iustificatione operum re-futationem addere.
units.tr: The conclusion should have [a syllogism]. Do not add a refutation of the Papists' sophisms about the justification of works.

units.la: Ratio 1. ne prolixitas materiæ tædium asse-rat.
units.tr: Reason 1. lest the length of the matter produce weariness.

units.la: II. Quia observatis nervis ἀληθείας[?], non sit difficilis.
units.tr: II. Because, once the sinews of the truth are observed, it is not difficult.

units.la: Et repetat usum conciliationis.
units.tr: And he repeats the use of the reconciliation.

units.la: I. Vt ex consensu doctrinae apostolicae authoritas confirmetur.
units.tr: I. That the authority of the apostolic doctrine may be confirmed by the agreement of doctrine.

units.la: II. ut vitentur praepostera judicia de libris sacris.
units.tr: II. That preposterous judgments about the sacred books may be avoided.

units.la: III. Vt doctrina Iustificationis fidei contra Sophistas defendatur ac illustretur.
units.tr: III. That the doctrine of justification by faith may be defended and illustrated against the Sophists.

units.la: Exercitatio XIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XIII.

units.la: Scribatur Narratio instaurationis Templi & cultus post reditum populi ex Babylone: observatis bona narrationis legibus: & expressa praecipue temporis notatione: ex Esdrae cap. 1. 3. 4. 5. 6.
units.tr: Let there be written a narrative of the restoration of the Temple and of worship after the people's return from Babylon, observing the good laws of narration, and expressing above all the note of time, from Ezra chapters 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6.

units.la: MEmbra praecipua haec sint, quae non numerentur, sed aptè contexantur: & vitetur prolixitas.
units.tr: The principal heads are these, which should not be merely enumerated but aptly woven together, and prolixity should be avoided.

units.la: I. Tempus, & causae efficientes atq; adjuvantes reditus: cap. 1.
units.tr: I. The time, and the efficient and helping causes of the return: chapter 1.

units.la: II. Prima cultus instauratio: Vbi de altaris structura: primis sacrificiis, & templi fundamentis jactis, anno secundo reditus populi & monarchiae Cyri: cap. 3.
units.tr: II. The first restoration of worship: where the building of the altar, the first sacrifices, and the laying of the foundations of the Temple are described, in the second year of the people's return and of the monarchy of Cyrus: chapter 3.

units.la: III. Impedimenta structurae Templi: ubi breviter exponantur calumniae Toparcharum ad Consiliarios Cyri absentis in Massagetis, h. e, ad proregem Cambysen. c. 4. v. 5. & ad Ahasverum Darium Histaspis contra aedificantes: ibid. ver. 6.
units.tr: III. Hindrances to the building of the Temple: where the calumnies of the governors (toparchs) against the counsellors of the absent Cyrus, that is, among the Massagetae, i.e. against the viceroy Cambyses, are briefly set out: chapter 4, verse 5; and against Ahasuerus, Darius son of Hystaspes, against those building: ibid., verse 6.

units.la: v: Et interdictum structuræ, Ibid. v.23. Non exscribatur epistola, sed pœnantur tantum propositiones cum præcipuis argumentis.
units.tr: v: And the prohibition of the building: ibid., verse 23. The letter should not be copied out, but only its propositions set down together with the chief arguments.

units.la: Et intermissio structuræ per annos 42. sub Cambyse ac Magis annis penè 6. sub Ahasvero Darío annis 19. sub Artaxerxe annis 16. sub Dario annis penè 2.
units.tr: And the interruption of the building for 42 years: under Cambyses and the Magi for almost 6 years; under Ahasuerus Darius for 19 years; under Artaxerxes for 16 years; under Darius for almost 2 years.

units.la: IV. Continuatio & perfectio structuræ.
units.tr: IV. The continuation and completion of the building.

units.la: Vbi de instauratione operis diu intermissi, hortatu Haggæi Anno 2. Darii Iudæorum Evergetę Esdr. 6.8.
units.tr: Where the resumption of the work, long interrupted, at the urging of Haggai in the second year of Darius, king of the Jews (Ezra 6:8), is described.

units.la: De nova Toparcharum intercessione, & dela-tione ad Darium. cap. 5.
units.tr: Concerning the new intervention of the governors, and their accusation before Darius: chapter 5.

units.la: De edicti Cyri per Darium approbatione.
units.tr: Concerning the approval of Cyrus's edict by Darius.

units.la: Et de Templi intra quadriennium absoluti solenni dedicatione: atque cultus instauratione: anno 6. Darii: post primam fundationem 46. ju-xta illud Ioh. 2.20.
units.tr: And concerning the solemn dedication of the Temple, completed within four years, and the restoration of worship in the sixth year of Darius, forty-six years after the first foundation, in accordance with that saying of John 2:20.

units.la: Claudatur Epiphonemate: Tantæ molis su-isse, propter obstantia Satanæ organa, collapsum cultum instaurare:
units.tr: Let it be closed with an epiphonema: that so great a work, against the obstructing instruments of Satan, was carried out, and that the fallen worship was restored.

units.la: Addatur Thesis allegorica: Sic Ecclesiam varie ab hostibus in hac vita impeti: sed divinitus servari.
units.tr: Let an allegorical thesis be added: thus the Church, in this life, is attacked in various ways by its enemies, but is preserved by divine providence.

units.la: Exercitatio XIV.
units.tr: Exercitatio XIV.

units.la: An Nabothrectè negaverit Achabo vineam suam. 1.Reg.21.
units.tr: Whether Naboth rightly refused Ahab his vineyard. 1 Kings 21.

units.la: PARS NEGANS.
units.tr: THE NEGATIVE PART.

units.la: BReviter narretur historia petitionis Achabi, & recusationis Nabothi & eventus.
units.tr: Let the history of Ahab's request, Naboth's refusal and the outcome be briefly told.

units.la: Moveatur quæstio de responso Nabothi.
units.tr: Let the question about Naboth's answer be raised.

units.la: Propositio. Videri injuria negasse vineam Regi.
units.tr: Proposition: It seems that Naboth wrongly refused the vineyard to the King.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia vinea jure ad Regem spectabat.
units.tr: Reason 1: because the vineyard by right belonged to the King.

units.la: Addatur maior: Suum juste petitur: & injuste negatur.
units.tr: Let the major premise be added: What is justly owed is justly sought, and unjustly denied.

units.la: Probetur minor: ex jure regio. 1. Sam. 8.14. Hoc erit ius regis: Tollet agros vestros.ver.17. Eritis ei servi.
units.tr: Let the minor premise be proved from the royal right: 1 Sam. 8.14: "This will be the right of the king: he will take your fields," verse 17: "You will be his servants."

units.la: Licet autem Domino ad se transferre posses-siones, quibus fruuntur servi.
units.tr: Although the Lord permits the transfer to himself of the possessions which the servants enjoy.

units.la: Ratio II. quia honesto regis desiderio non satisfacere injustum fuit: ex dicto: Cui honorem, honorem.:
units.tr: Reason II: because it was unjust not to satisfy the honourable desire of the king, from the saying: "Honour to whom honour is due."

units.la: Probetur honestas. 1. à forma petitionis: non vi sed honesta permutatione vel emtione eam habere cupit:
units.tr: Let the honesty be proved. First, from the form of the request: he desires to have it not by force but by an honest exchange or purchase.

units.la: II. à fine: Ad honestam recreationem.
units.tr: Second, from the end: for honest recreation.

units.la: Amplificetur ex officio subditorum erga magistratus à Thesi[?]: Partem gratitudinis & honoris Magistratibus debiti esse, illorum commodis & recreationib. honestis privatam utilitatem post-ponere.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the duty of subjects toward magistrates, from the thesis: that part of the gratitude and honour owed to magistrates is to place private advantage after their benefits and honest recreations.

units.la: Ratio III. Quia duriore responso conciliavit sibi necem contra præceptum: non occides.
units.tr: Reason III: because by a harsher answer he brought upon himself death, contrary to the precept: "You shall not kill."

units.la: Obiectio: Lex vetabat vendere.
units.tr: Objection: The law forbade selling.

units.la: Resp. 1. Salvo jure regio. Ostendatur ex regu-la: Lex posterior derogat priori: specialis gene-rali:
units.tr: Answer 1: Saving the royal right. Let it be shown from the rule: a later law repeals an earlier one; the special overrides the general.

units.la: II. Extra casum periculi vitæ quod hic erat.
units.tr: II. Outside the case of danger to life, which was the case here.

units.la: Probetur distinctio ex regula: Ceremonialia & Forensia cedunt moralibus: Et: misericordiam volo non sacrificium. Amplificetur à minori per exemplum: Licet exemplo Augustini, Ambrosii, &c. in periculo tradere bona Ecclesiæ publica & aliena: multò magis privata & propria.
units.tr: Let the distinction be proved from the rule: ceremonial and forensic laws yield to moral ones; and: "I desire mercy and not sacrifice." Let it be amplified from the less to the greater by the example that, as Augustine, Ambrose, etc., allowed the public and others' goods to be surrendered in time of danger, much more may private and one's own goods be given up.

units.la: Conclusio: Nabothum ergo cedere petitioni Regis debuisse.
units.tr: Conclusion: Naboth therefore ought to have yielded to the King's request.

units.la: Pars affirmans.
units.tr: The affirmative part.

units.la: Defensio Nabothi, quod iure negaverit vineam Achabo.
units.tr: The defence of Naboth, that he rightly refused to give his vineyard to Ahab.

units.la: Propositio: Nabothum jure negasse vineam Achabo.
units.tr: Proposition: Naboth rightly refused to give his vineyard to Ahab.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia tradedo peccasset in Legem Dei.
units.tr: Reason 1: because by handing it over he would have sinned against the Law of God.

units.la: Probetur expositione Legis Levit. 25.23: & collatione petitionis Achabi cum ea: quod Deus vetuerit agros vendere, nisi cum conditione redimendi aut recipiendi eos anno lubilæo: Achabus contra voluerit vineam sibi vendi vel permutari mancipio: absque conditione.
units.tr: Proof from the exposition of the Law, Leviticus 25:23, and from comparing Ahab's request with it: God forbade the sale of fields except on the condition that they be redeemed or recovered in the year of Jubilee; Ahab, on the other hand, wanted the vineyard sold or transferred to him by conveyance without any such condition.

units.la: Amplif. à maiori ex causa legis: Quia terra mea est: Colonis non licere fundos alienare nolentibus Dominis, multò minus Israelitis licuisse, prohibente Deo, cujus erant coloni.
units.tr: Amplification from the greater case, by the reason of the law: "For the land is mine." Tenants may not alienate their holdings when the landlords are unwilling; much less may the Israelites have done so, since God, whose tenants they were, forbade it.

units.la: Respondeatur hic ad solutionem objectionis:
units.tr: Here an answer is to be given to the solution of the objection:

units.la: 1. non excipi jus Regium in lege.
units.tr: 1. The royal right is not excepted in the law.

units.la: Ratio: quia non fuerit jus, sed Tyrannis, cujus ostensio rejiciatur in confutationem primi argumenti.
units.tr: Reason: because it was not a right but tyranny, and the showing of it is to be rejected in refutation of the first argument.

units.la: 2. Neque casum periculi.
units.tr: 2. Nor is it an exception for the case of danger.

units.la: Ratio:quia obedientia legis etiam vitæ fuerit anteferenda : Diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde.
units.tr: Reason: because obedience to the law is to be preferred even to life: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart."

units.la: Ad Regulam : Ceremonialia & Forensia cedunt moralibus : negatione maioris: quia etsi lex erat forensis: tamen voluntaria ejus violatio fuerit contemtus Dei,& peccatum morale.
units.tr: To the rule: Ceremonial and judicial laws yield to moral ones. Denying the major premise: because, even if the law was judicial, its deliberate violation was contempt of God and a moral sin.

units.la: Ad amplificationem à minori: 1. antecedens de licita traditione bonorum Ecclesiasticorum valdè controversum esse, propter rationes & exempla in utramque partem probabilia, quæ per ἀντι-[illegible, ~6 letters] rejiciantur alio : 2. Negatione consequentiæ ob dissimilitudinem exemplorum: quia lex hodie non vetet tradere, ut olim.
units.tr: To the amplification from the lesser case: (1) the antecedent, concerning the lawful surrender of ecclesiastical goods, is very much disputed, on account of reasons and examples that are plausible on both sides, and these are refuted by the opposite side (antithesis [illegible]); (2) by denying the consequence, on account of the dissimilarity of the examples: because today the law does not forbid such surrender as it did formerly.

units.la: Claudatur prima ratio.
units.tr: Let the first reason be concluded.

units.la: Ratio 1 1. quia Deus per Eliam factum Nabothi probarit,& necem ultus sit.
units.tr: Reason 1.1: because God, through Elijah, avenged the deed done to Naboth and punished his death.

units.la: Ratio 1 1 1. Quia postulatio Achabi injusta.
units.tr: Reason 1.1.1: because Ahab's demand was unjust.

units.la: Probatio 1. Quia prohibita in Decalogo:non concupisces.
units.tr: Proof 1: because it is forbidden in the Decalogue: "You shall not covet."

units.la: 1 1. Quia pugnet cum jure Regio. Deut.17. Rex ne efferat se supra fratres.
units.tr: 1.1: because it conflicts with the royal right. Deuteronomy 17: "The king shall not lift himself up above his brethren."

units.la: 1 1 1. Quia incitet Nabothum ad violandam legem Levit.25.prius expositam.
units.tr: 1.1.1: because it would have incited Naboth to violate the law of Leviticus 25, explained above.

units.la: Amplificetur ab inhonesto: Turpe esse, magistratus instigare subditos ad violationem Legum, quarum esse debent custodes.
units.tr: Amplified from dishonour: It is shameful for the magistrate to urge his subjects to violate the laws, whose guardians they ought to be.

units.la: Conclusio confirmationis: Injustæ igitur petitioni recte non obtemperasse Nabothum.
units.tr: Conclusion of the confirmation: Naboth therefore rightly did not comply with an unjust request.

units.la: Ex thesi: Quæ injuste & contra legem Dei petuntur, recte negantur.
units.tr: From the thesis: What is asked unjustly and against the law of God is rightly refused.

units.la: Confutatio.
units.tr: Refutation.

units.la: Transitio ad confutationem: Primi argumenti negetur Minor cum probatione.
units.tr: Transition to the refutation: The minor premise of the first argument is denied, with proof.

units.la: Ratio: quia Samuel καταχρηστικῶς Tyrannidé appellat jus Regis, nempe usurpatum: non datum a Deo & legibus.
units.tr: Reason: because Samuel calls the king's right "tyranny" by an abuse of the word, namely a usurped right, not one given by God and the laws.

units.la: Probatio 1. quia nihil constituit, sed tantum minatur mala & injurias a Rege inferendas.
units.tr: Proof 1: because he did not establish anything, but only threatened the evils and injuries that the king would inflict.

units.la: Ostendatur ex scopo dehortantis populum ab instituto: enumeratione malorum.
units.tr: It is shown from the purpose of his dissuading the people from the institution: by the enumeration of the evils.

units.la: Exponatur per ἀντίθεσιν. Verum jus Regis Deut.17. praecipere defensionem libri Legis: prohibere oppressionem subditorum.
units.tr: It is set out by antithesis: the true right of the king, Deuteronomy 17, is to command the defence of the book of the Law, and to forbid the oppression of subjects.

units.la: Probatio 11. Quia non voluit populum Dei subjicere servituti, contra legem: quae deducatur ex jure primitiarum & primogenitorum: Exod. 13. Deut.15.26.
units.tr: Proof 2: because he did not wish the people of God to be subjected to slavery, contrary to the law; this is to be deduced from the right of the firstfruits and the firstborn: Exodus 13; Deuteronomy 15, 26.

units.la: Probatio 111. Quia noluit tollere distinctionem dominiorum & proprietatem, jure gentium & Decalogo sancitam.
units.tr: Proof 3: because he did not wish to abolish the distinction of dominions and property, which is sanctioned by the law of nations and by the Decalogue.

units.la: Instantia 1. Omnia sunt Regum. Resp. Iure defensionis, non usurpationis aut proprietatis.
units.tr: Instance 1: "All things are the kings'." Answer: by the right of defence, not by usurpation or ownership.

units.la: Instantia 11. Etiam usurpatione, quia exactiones sunt juris divini. Rom.13. Resp. Moderatae & necessariae ad splendorem convenientem & defensionem regni: non ad luxum & oppressionem: qualis haec fuit.
units.tr: Instance 2: Even by usurpation, because exactions are of divine right. Romans 13. Answer: they are moderate and necessary for the fitting splendour and defence of the kingdom, not for luxury and oppression, such as this one was.

units.la: Ad secundum Argumentum: negatione minoris ex tertia ratione.
units.tr: To the second argument: the minor is denied by the third reason.

units.la: Ad probationem: Petitionem & finem pugnas-se cum lege.
units.tr: To the proof: the petition and its purpose were in conflict with the law.

units.la: Ad amplificationem: Gratificandum esse magistratuum commodis & recreationibus honestis: citra offensionem Dei: & læsionem conscientiæ, quam incurrisset Naboth.
units.tr: To the amplification: magistrates are to be gratified in their honest conveniences and recreations, without offence to God and without injury to the conscience, which Naboth would have incurred.

units.la: Ad III. Argumentum per fallaciam non causæ: Causam necis fuisse non justam negationem: sed avaritiam & sævitiam Tyranni.
units.tr: To the third argument, by the fallacy of a non-cause: the cause of his death was not the unjust refusal but the greed and cruelty of the tyrant.

units.la: Instantia: Irritavit regem immodestia: Absit mihi ut dem, &c.
units.tr: Instance: The king was provoked by immodesty: "Far be it from me that I should give," etc.

units.la: Resp. 1. responsum non totum sed summam tantum recitari. 2. Reverentiam Legis Dei, quā postulatoRegis opponit, esse summam modestiā: Absit à Jehova ut dem, &c.
units.tr: Answer 1: the reply is not quoted in full but only in summary. 2: the reverence for the Law of God, which Naboth sets against the king's request, is the highest modesty: "Far be it from Jehovah that I should give," etc.

units.la: Conclusio: Laudandam igitur esse Nabothi constantiam.
units.tr: Conclusion: Naboth's constancy is therefore to be praised.

units.la: Exercitatio XV.
units.tr: Exercise XV.

units.la: Scribatur in genere Demonstrativo: Approbatio Chriæ Apostolorum : Oportet Deo magis obedire quam hominibus. Act.4.19.& 5.29.
units.tr: To be written in the demonstrative genre: approval of the saying of the Apostles: "We ought to obey God rather than men." Acts 4:19; 5:29.

units.la: Narretur occasio: Impium edictum Pharisaeorum, de Christo non prædicando: Apostolorum recusatio & ratio: Deo magis obtemperandum esse quam hominibus.
units.tr: The occasion is to be narrated: the impious edict of the Pharisees, forbidding the preaching of Christ; the refusal of the Apostles and its reason: that God must be obeyed rather than men.

units.la: Subiiciatur approbatio facti: cum αἰλολογία[?] quæ sit ipsa.
units.tr: The approval of the deed is to be added, with [?] which is itself.

units.la: PROPOSITIO: Quia rectè ac piè judicant: Oportere Deo magis quam hominibus obtemperare, quoties diversa vel pugnantia præcipiunt. Confirmationis Ratio I. a necessario, seu a Dei mandato, cui oportet obedire: Diliges Dominum Deum ex toto corde, &c. Ezech.20.18. Non in statutis patrum: sed in meis, &c.
units.tr: PROPOSITION: Because they judge rightly and piously that, whenever men command things that differ or conflict, one ought to obey God rather than men. Reason of the confirmation I: from what is necessary, or from the command of God, whom one ought to obey: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart," etc. Ezekiel 20:18: "Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, but in my statutes," etc.

units.la: Ratio II. ab honesto. Quia major erga Deum obligatio quam erga homines.
units.tr: Reason II: from the honourable. Because our obligation to God is greater than our obligation to men.

units.la: Probatur: quia illa absoluta: Pf.24. Domini est terra & plenitudo eius: Haec conditionalis; si nihil vel impium vel injustum praecipiant.
units.tr: It is proved: because the one is absolute: Psalm 24: "The earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof"; the other is conditional: if they command nothing either impious or unjust.

units.la: Ratio discriminis sumitur a personis: Deus suprema majestas: quia creator & gubernator mundi: Homines legati, ministri, Rom.13.
units.tr: The reason for the distinction is taken from the persons: God is the supreme majesty, because he is the creator and governor of the world; men are envoys and ministers, Romans 13.

units.la: Amplificetur ex Thesibus: Supremae majestati debetur major reverentia: Domino quam servo major obedientia.
units.tr: Amplified from the theses: Greater reverence is owed to the supreme majesty; greater obedience is owed by the servant to the Lord.

units.la: Item: Praevaricatio legati nulla est potestas.
units.tr: Likewise: the transgression of an envoy is no authority.

units.la: Ratio III. ab utili & inutili ex dicto Christi: Nolite metuere eos, qui corpus solum interficere possunt: sed eum qui corpus & animam abducere potest in gehennam.
units.tr: Reason III: from the useful and the useless, from the saying of Christ: "Do not fear those who can kill only the body; but fear him who can cast body and soul into hell."

units.la: Amplificetur comparatione praemiorum Dei & hominum ex Psal.49.ver.7.8.15.
units.tr: To be amplified by comparing the rewards of God and of men, from Psalm 49:7, 8, 15.

units.la: Ratio IV. ab exemplis laudatis eorum, qui injustis mandatis hominum non obtemperarunt.
units.tr: Reason IV: from the praised examples of those who did not obey unjust commands of men.

units.la: Obstetricum Aegyptiarum. Exod.1.21.
units.tr: The Egyptian midwives. Exodus 1:21.

units.la: Sociorum Danielis. Dan.3.
units.tr: The companions of Daniel. Daniel 3.

units.la: Abdia 1.Reg.18.13.
units.tr: Obadiah. 1 Kings 18:13.

units.la: Maccabaeorum. 1.Macch.1.2.
units.tr: The Maccabees. 1 Maccabees 1:2.

units.la: Antigona apud Sophoclem sepelientis fratre contra edictum Creontis: Videatur locus in Antigone: οὐδὲ ὀφέιλειν τοσοῦτον, &c.
units.tr: Antigone in Sophocles, burying her brother against the edict of Creon. Let the passage in the Antigone be consulted: "nor did I think that your decree was of such force," etc.

units.la: Conclusio: Soli igitur Deo sine exceptione parendum rendum : Humanæ obedientiæ tàm in Ecclesia quam in Politia pietatem & justitiam metas esse.
units.tr: Therefore to God alone, without exception, obedience is to be rendered; the piety and justice of human obedience, both in the Church and in the State, have God as their limit.

units.la: Exercitatio XVI.
units.tr: Exercitatio XVI.

units.la: Exemplo Rechabitarum non confirmari regulas monasticas & traditionum observantiam, Ier.25.
units.tr: That the rules of the monks and the observance of traditions are not confirmed by the example of the Rechabites, Jer. 35.

units.la: Exordium: Narrentur I. Ionadabi instituta posteris tradita: II. Rechabitarum obedientia. III. Obedientiæ laudatio, & benedictionis promissio, ver.35.
units.tr: Introduction: Let there be related (I.) the precepts of Jonadab handed down to posterity; (II.) the obedience of the Rechabites; (III.) the praise of obedience and the promise of blessing, ver. 19.

units.la: Propositio exordii quæ narrationi præmitti vel subjici potest: Videri hoc exemplo comprobari Regulas monasticas, & traditiones Papisticas.
units.tr: A proposition of the introduction, which may be placed before or after the narrative: it seems that by this example the monastic rules and the Papistical traditions are confirmed.

units.la: Αἰτιολογία[?] prioris à pari: Si laudantur observates regulam Ionadabi, cur non etiam Dominici, Francisci, Augustini?
units.tr: Argument from the like (a pari) for the former: if those who observe the rule of Jonadab are praised, why not also those of Dominic, Francis, and Augustine?

units.la: Posterioris à minori: Si obligarunt traditiones hominis privati: quanto magis totius Ecclesiæ?
units.tr: Argument from the lesser for the latter: if the traditions of a private man bound, how much more those of the whole Church?

units.la: PROPOSITIO per adversat: Sed neutras confirmari.
units.tr: PROPOSITION by way of opposition: but neither is confirmed.

units.la: Ratio: quia fit dissimilitudo.
units.tr: Reason: because there is a dissimilarity.

units.la: Probatio minoris fit ἐκ τῶν[?] dissimilitudinis.
units.tr: Proof of the minor is drawn from the dissimilarity.

units.la: I. In materia. Rechabitæ observant licita, nec lege prohibita abstinentes à vino, agricultura, urbibus.
units.tr: I. In the matter. The Rechabites observed lawful things, abstaining from wine, agriculture, and cities, which was not forbidden by law.

units.la: Ratio per occupat: Usum istorum concessum, non præceptum fuisse à Deo.
units.tr: Reason by anticipation: the use of those things was permitted, not commanded, by God.

units.la: Monachi pugnantia cum lege: ut votum cœlibatus, libatus, desertionem parentum, & humanæ socie-tatis, falsos cultus, multas impias traditiones, &c.
units.tr: The monks, (their practices being) contrary to the law: such as the vow of celibacy, the vow of poverty, the desertion of parents and of human society, false worship, many impious traditions, etc.

units.la: II. Infirma. Rechabitarum conscientiæ non obligantur, retinentes libertatem secus faciendi, propter causas necessarias vel probabiles.
units.tr: II. In the form. The consciences of the Rechabites were not bound, since they retained the liberty of acting otherwise, on account of necessary or probable causes.

units.la: Probetur ex textu: quia mutant institutum patris sine peccato migrantes ex agro in urbem bel-li tempore.
units.tr: Let it be proved from the text: because they changed the institution of their father without sin, migrating from the field into the city in time of war.

units.la: Monachi & traditiones conscientias obstrin-gunt.
units.tr: The monks and the traditions bind consciences.

units.la: III. Infine. Rechabitarum abstinentia non est cultus Dei, ut regulæ monachorum & traditiones esse finguntur.
units.tr: III. In the end. The abstinence of the Rechabites was not a worship of God, as the rules of the monks and the traditions are feigned to be.

units.la: Probetur [illegible, ~9 letters] finium: Instituta fuisse merè politica vel ethica.
units.tr: Let it be proved [illegible, ~9 letters] of the ends: the institutions were purely political or ethical.

units.la: I. Exploratio reverentiæ in patrem.
units.tr: I. A test of reverence toward the father.

units.la: II. Exercitium sobrietatis & humilitatis.
units.tr: II. An exercise of sobriety and humility.

units.la: III. Præparatio ad ferendas olim ærumnas publicas.
units.tr: III. A preparation for bearing public hardships in time to come.

units.la: Amplificetur [illegible, ~10 letters] ab opinione meritorum & perfectionis monasticæ: & opinionis hujus improbatione, ex dicto: Frustra me colunt. &c.
units.tr: Let it be amplified [illegible, ~10 letters] from the opinion of merits and of monastic perfection, and from the rejection of this opinion, by the saying: "In vain do they worship me," etc.

units.la: Addatur thesis: Omnes ἐθελοθρησκείας[?] damna-ri à Deo.
units.tr: Let the thesis be added: that all self-chosen worship is condemned by God.

units.la: Obiectio. Abstinentiam Rechabitarum etiam fuisse cultum: quia à Deo laudatur.
units.tr: Objection: the abstinence of the Rechabites was also a worship, because it is praised by God.

units.la: Resp. Laudari reverentiam mandati paterni non illiciti: & fuisse cultum generalem: Honora patrem, &c. cujusmodi cultus Regulæ monasticæ & Traditiones non sunt.
units.tr: Answer: the reverence of a father's command, which was not unlawful, is praised, and it was a general worship: "Honour thy father," etc. The monastic rules and the traditions are not of this kind of worship.

units.la: Conclusio repetat propositionem addita thesi:
units.tr: The conclusion repeats the proposition with the added thesis:

units.la: Exercitatio XVII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XVII.

units.la: Laudatio facti Ebedmelechi, liberantis Ieremiam ex foveâ. Ier. 38.
units.tr: Lauds of the deed of Ebed-melech, who freed Jeremiah from the pit. Jer. 38.

units.la: Narretur breviter periculum Ieremię[?]: & liberatio per Ebedmelech.
units.tr: The danger to Jeremiah[?] is briefly related, and his deliverance through Ebed-melech.

units.la: Propositio: Esse factum heroicum & laudandū.
units.tr: Proposition: The deed is heroic and worthy of praise.

units.la: Cōfirmatio seu laudatio ab honesto: quia multæ virtutes in eo concurrant.
units.tr: Confirmation, or praise from honourableness, because many virtues concur in it.

units.la: I. Fiducia in Deum: quia fretus Dei auxilio suscepit rem humanitus impossibilem.
units.tr: I. Trust in God: because, relying on the help of God, he undertook a thing humanly impossible.

units.la: Probetur impossibilitas à maiori. Rex non poterat cohibere principes, &c. Fiducia Ebedmelechi, testimonio ipsius Dei. cap.39.18.
units.tr: Let the impossibility be proved from the greater. The king could not restrain the princes, etc. The trust of Ebed-melech is attested by God himself. Chap. 39.18.

units.la: Amplificetur ab ejus persona: quod Æthiops.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from his person: that he was an Ethiopian.

units.la: II. Pietas in Prophetam, cujus calamitate afficitur.
units.tr: II. Piety towards the Prophet, by whose calamity he is moved.

units.la: III. Fortitudo: quia suscipit patrocinium Prophetæ odiosum & periculosum.
units.tr: III. Fortitude: because he takes up the patronage of a hated and dangerous prophet.

units.la: Amplificetur à principum furore, & multitudine.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the fury and the multitude of the princes.

units.la: IV. Magnanimitas: quia libere: publicè: & constanter.
units.tr: IV. Magnanimity: because he acts freely, openly, and constantly.

units.la: Ostendatur ex circumstantiis: ubi & quomodo causam egerit.
units.tr: Let it be shown from the circumstances: where and how he pleaded the cause.

units.la: Amplific. ab occasione crudelitatis collegarum.
units.tr: Amplification from the occasion of the cruelty of his colleagues.

units.la: V. Tolerantia laborum.
units.tr: V. Endurance of labours.

units.la: VI. Prudentia, quod arripit vetustos pannos, ut antevertat rumorem : item, quod relinquit in atrio custodiæ prophetam, etsi malit abducere domum.
units.tr: VI. Prudence, in that he snatches up old rags, so as to forestall the rumour; likewise, that he leaves the prophet in the court of the guard, although he would rather lead him home.

units.la: Occupatio: Non timuit periculum suum, sed prophetæ, qui denuò fuisset à principibus comprehensus.
units.tr: Occupatio: He did not fear for his own danger, but for the prophet's, who would again have been seized by the princes.

units.la: Conclusio: Esse igitur laudandum & imitandum.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore he is to be praised and imitated.

units.la: Amplificetur à præmio, & addatur Epiphonema: Adeo pulcrum & utile esse juvare afflictos.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the reward, and an epiphonema be added: So noble and useful a thing it is to help the afflicted!

units.la: Exercitatio XVIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XVIII.

units.la: Beneficia Messiæ ad omnes & solos credentes pertinere.
units.tr: The benefits of the Messiah belong to all believers and to them alone.

units.la: Ponatur propositio: & subjiciatur confirmatio.
units.tr: Let the proposition be laid down, and then the confirmation be added.

units.la: I. Quod ad OMNES fideles pertineant.
units.tr: I. That they pertain to ALL the faithful.

units.la: Ratio I. quia ad omnes credentes pertinet promissio. Ostendatur ex Scriptura. Ioh.3.16: Ut omnis qui credit. Act.10.43. Remissionem peccatorum accipiat omnis qui credit. Rom.3.22. Justitia Dei per fidem in omnes & super omnes credentes. Ergo etiam beneficia promissa.
units.tr: Reason I. Because the promise pertains to all who believe. Let it be shown from Scripture. John 3:16: that everyone who believes. Acts 10:43: everyone who believes receives remission of sins. Rom. 3:22: the righteousness of God through faith, upon all and over all who believe. Therefore the promised benefits also belong to them.

units.la: Ratio II. quia omnes credentes ea percipiunt.
units.tr: Reason II. Because all who believe receive them.

units.la: Probetur brevi inductione beneficiorum ex Scriptura.
units.tr: Let this be proved by a brief enumeration of the benefits from Scripture.

units.la: Liberantur à peccato & morte, Ioh. 5.24. Ioh. 3.36.
units.tr: They are freed from sin and death: John 5:24; John 3:36.

units.la: Reconciliantur Deo & justificantur, Rom.3.28.30.& 5.1.9.
units.tr: They are reconciled to God and justified: Rom. 3:28, 30; 5:1, 9.

units.la: Regenerantur ad novam vitam per Spiritum Sanctum, Act.15.9. Eph.2.8.10. Ioh.15.2.1. Cor.6. 11.&15.22.
units.tr: They are regenerated to new life through the Holy Spirit: Acts 15:9; Eph. 2:8, 10; John 15:2, 1; 1 Cor. 6:11; 15:22.

units.la: Resurgent à mortuis & glorificabuntur in Christo, Ioh 6:39.40.Ioh.11.26.& 17.24.
units.tr: They will rise from the dead and be glorified in Christ: John 6:39, 40; John 11:26; 17:24.

units.la: Ratio 111. Quia ad omnes electos pertinet Christus cum suis beneficiis, Eph.1.4. Elegit nos in Christo. Ioh.17.24.quos dedisti mihi. Tales autem sunt omnes credentes, Act.13.48.Eph.1.4.
units.tr: Reason III. Because Christ with his benefits belongs to all the elect: Eph. 1:4, He chose us in Christ; John 17:24, whom you have given me. Now all who believe are such: Acts 13:48; Eph. 1:4.

units.la: Ratio iv. Omnes credentes sunt filii & hæ-redes. Rom. 8.16. Ad omnes ergo pertinet hære-ditas.
units.tr: Reason IV. All who believe are sons and heirs: Rom. 8:16. Therefore the inheritance belongs to all.

units.la: II. Quod ad solos fideles pertineant.
units.tr: II. That they pertain to the faithful alone.

units.la: Ratio 1. Ad solos credentes pertinet Christus. Ergo & beneficia.
units.tr: Reason I. Christ belongs to believers alone. Therefore so do the benefits.

units.la: Probetur antecedens:quia soli habent Spiritum Christi, Rom.8.9.Gal.3.14. & 4.6.Rom.8.14.16.
units.tr: The antecedent is proved: because only they have the Spirit of Christ: Rom. 8:9; Gal. 3:14; 4:6; Rom. 8:14, 16.

units.la: Ratio 11. Soli credentes sunt tales, qualibus promittuntur beneficia Messiæ: nempe agentes pœnitentiam, & fide promissionem amplectentes, sequeque gratos Deo exhibentes.
units.tr: Reason II. Only believers are of the kind to whom the benefits of the Messiah are promised, namely those who repent, who embrace the promise by faith, and who show themselves grateful to God.

units.la: Ostendatur, quia omnes promissiones Evangelii annexam habent conditionem pœnitentiæ, fidei, & gratitudinis, Icf.7.9.[?]
units.tr: Let it be shown, because all the promises of the Gospel have annexed to them the condition of repentance, faith and gratitude: Isa. 7:9 [?].

units.la: Ratio 111. Ad solos hæredes, filios, &c. pertinet hæreditas.Gal.4. Eiice ancillam & filium eius,&c.
units.tr: Reason III. The inheritance belongs to heirs and sons alone, etc.: Gal. 4. Cast out the bondwoman and her son, etc.

units.la: Tales sunt soli credentes, habentes Spiritum Christi, Rom.8.
units.tr: Such are only believers, who have the Spirit of Christ: Rom. 8.

units.la: Ratio iv. a contrario: Infideles neque jus ad rem, neque jus in re habent. Probetur prius: quia non sunt hæredes. Po-sterius quia sine fide impossibile placere Deo, Heb.11.6:
units.tr: Reason IV, from the contrary: Unbelievers have neither a right to the thing nor a right in the thing. The former is proved: because they are not heirs. The latter: because without faith it is impossible to please God: Heb. 11:6.

units.la: Item, ex dictis. Ioh. 3: Qui non credit, super eo manet ira Dei: jam condemnatus est.
units.tr: Likewise, from what has been said: John 3: He who does not believe, the wrath of God remains upon him; he is already condemned.

units.la: Objectio 1. Promissio Evangelii est universalis: Venite ad me omnes: Ut omnium misereretur, &c.
units.tr: Objection I. The promise of the Gospel is universal: Come to me, all of you; that he might have mercy on all, etc.

units.la: Resp. Est universalis respectu credentium & agentium pœnitentiam:
units.tr: Answer. It is universal with respect to believers and those who repent.

units.la: Ostenditur: ex τῷ ῥητῷ promissionum. Ut omnis qui credit: In omnes & super omnes credentes. Venite ad me omnes qui laboratis: Dives in omnes invocantes eum. Quisquis invocaverit nomen Domini ser-vabitur.
units.tr: This is shown from the plain sense of the promises: that everyone who believes; upon all and over all who believe; Come to me, all you who labour; rich to all who call upon him; whoever calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

units.la: Objectio 11. Christus est pro omnibus mor-tuus.
units.tr: Objection II. Christ died for all.

units.la: Resp. per distinct. Pro omnibus merito seu sufficientia λύτρον. Pro solis electis credentibus, applicatione seu efficacia λύτρον.
units.tr: Answer, by a distinction. For all, as to the merit or sufficiency of the ransom [λύτρον]. For the elect believers alone, as to the application or efficacy of the ransom.

units.la: Probetur distinctio 1. quia pro his solis oravit. Joh.17.9.
units.tr: The distinction is proved, first, because he prayed for these alone: John 17:9.

units.la: Ostendatur valere argumentum a nexu inter-cessionis & mortis tanquam partium Sacerdotii Christi.
units.tr: Let it be shown that the argument holds from the connection between intercession and death, as parts of Christ's priesthood.

units.la: 11. Quia Scriptura restringit efficaciam mortis Christi ad solos electos. Matth.20.28. & 26.28 Joh.10.15. Gal.3. 22.Isef.53.[?] 11. Servus meus iustus cognitione sui iustificabit multos, quorum iniquitates ipse portavit. Rom. 8.33. Quis intentabit crimina adversus electos Dei, &c.
units.tr: Second, because Scripture restricts the efficacy of Christ's death to the elect alone: Matt. 20:28; 26:28; John 10:15; Gal. 3:22; Isa. 53 [?]. Second, My righteous servant, by his knowledge, shall justify many, and he shall bear their iniquities. Rom. 8:33: Who shall bring any charge against the elect of God?, etc.

units.la: Exercitatio XIX. Epistola Responsoria.
units.tr: Exercitatio XIX. Epistola Responsoria.

units.la: De quaestione: Cur Spiritus sanctus non mox à resurrectione Christi, sed demum die Pentecostes Apostolis missus fuerit.
units.tr: On the question: Why the Holy Spirit was not sent to the Apostles immediately after the resurrection of Christ, but only on the day of Pentecost.

units.la: EXordium sit laudatio petitionis amici.
units.tr: The exordium is a commendation of a friend's request.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia videas, cum cum Ecclesia tem-pore consueto de praecipuis Dei beneficiis cogi-tare.
units.tr: Reason 1: because you see that we are, at the customary time, thinking with the Church about the chief benefits of God.

units.la: II. quia tibi occasionem dederit de Quaestio-ne accuratius cogitandi.
units.tr: II: because it has given you an occasion of thinking more carefully about the question.

units.la: Occupat.per adversat: Etsi citra jacturam salu-tis causae ignorari possint: & praestet fructus mis-sionis Spiritus sancti meditari, quam momenta temporis investigare: tamen tibi etiam videri quaestionem explicatione non indignam.
units.tr: Objection, with its answer: Although these matters could be left unknown without loss to salvation, and it is better to meditate on the fruit of the mission of the Holy Spirit than to investigate the moments of time, nevertheless the question seems to you not unworthy of explanation.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia ad illustrationem beneficii Ec-clesiae exhibiti pertineat.
units.tr: Reason 1: because it pertains to the illustration of the benefit given to the Church.

units.la: II. Quia etiam veteres Theologi eam tracta-rint.
units.tr: II: because the ancient theologians also treated it.

units.la: PROPOSITIO sit partitio quaestionis.
units.tr: PROPOSITION: let there be a division of the question.

units.la: I. Cur non illico à resurrectione Christi.
units.tr: I. Why not at once after the resurrection of Christ.

units.la: II. Cur die Pentecostes venerit Spiritus sanctus..
units.tr: II. Why the Holy Spirit came on the day of Pentecost.

units.la: Ἐξήγησις[?] prima partis sit causarum enumeratio.
units.tr: Explanation of the first part: let there be an enumeration of the causes.

units.la: I. Quia post Christi ascensionem demum promissus fuerat, Ioh.16.
units.tr: I. Because the Spirit had been promised only after Christ's ascension, John 16.

units.la: II. Quia Christo praesente discipuli nondum opus co habebant.
units.tr: II. Because while Christ was present the disciples did not yet have need of it.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia pendebant a corporali ejus præsentia. Matth. 9. 15: Filii thalami non possunt lugere, præsente sponso. Ioh. 16. Hactenus non petivistis, &c.
units.tr: Reason 1: because they depended on his bodily presence. Matt. 9.15: The sons of the bridal chamber cannot mourn while the bridegroom is present. John 16: Hitherto you have not asked, etc.

units.la: Ratio 11. Quia promulgatio Evangelii ab ipsis post ascensionem demum facienda erat.
units.tr: Reason 2: because the proclamation of the Gospel was to be made by them only after the ascension.

units.la: Probetur ex mandato Christi, ne abscederent Hierosolymis, donec, &c. Act. 1. 4.
units.tr: This is proved from the command of Christ, that they should not leave Jerusalem until, etc. Acts 1.4.

units.la: 111. Quia missio reservata erat glorificationi Messiæ. Ioh. 7: Nondum erat Spiritus sanctus, quia Christus nondum erat glorificatus, &c. Act. 2. Christus effudit hoc quod videtis.
units.tr: III. Because the mission was reserved for the glorification of the Messiah. John 7: The Holy Spirit was not yet, because Christ was not yet glorified, etc. Acts 2: Christ has poured out this which you see.

units.la: Ratio ex Chrysost. homil. 1. in Act. Oportebat in cœlo nostram naturam comparere: & intercessione eius perfectam reconciliationem fieri, ac tum venire Spiritum sanctum, ut purum merumq; gaudium fieret. Ioh. 16. Nisi abiero, Paracletus non veniet ad vos.
units.tr: Reason from Chrysostom, homily 1 on Acts: It was necessary that our nature should appear in heaven, and that through his intercession a perfect reconciliation should be made, and then the Holy Spirit should come, so that the joy might be pure and unmixed. John 16: Unless I go away, the Paraclete will not come to you.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Etiam patribus & fidelibus in veteri Testamento erat datus.
units.tr: Objection 1: The Spirit was also given to the fathers and believers in the Old Testament.

units.la: Resp. 1. propter futuram Christi intercessionem & glorificationem.
units.tr: Answer 1: on account of Christ's future intercession and glorification.

units.la: 11. Non miraculose & visibiliter, ut Apostolis.
units.tr: 11. Not miraculously and visibly, as to the Apostles.

units.la: 111. Non copiose, ut tempore Novi Testamenti. Illustretur discrimen ex oraculo Ioelis, & dicto Christi: Multi Reges & Prophetæ, &c.
units.tr: III. Not abundantly, as in the time of the New Testament. The difference is illustrated from the oracle of Joel and the saying of Christ: Many kings and prophets, etc.

units.la: Obiectio 11. Apostoli acceperant Spiritum flatu Christi. Ioh. 20.
units.tr: Objection 2: The Apostles had received the Spirit by the breath of Christ. John 20.

units.la: Resp. Ex Chrysostomo 1. per enallagen temporum dici de eo quod futurum erat, perinde quasi jam factum esset.
units.tr: Answer: From Chrysostom, 1: by an enallage of tenses, what was going to happen is spoken of as though it had already happened.

units.la: 11. per ἐνχόρδωσιν prioris: Rectius dici accepisse. pisse primitias, quibus eos capaces reddidit accipiendo complemento.
units.tr: 11. By the enchordosis of the former: it is more correctly said that they received the firstfruits, by which he made them capable, the fullness being received afterwards.

units.la: Transitio ad [illegible, ~6 letters] secundæ partis.
units.tr: Transition to the second part.

units.la: Figuretur occupatiuncula: Te saltem indicaturum, quid probabile videatur.
units.tr: Let a short preliminary point be stated: that you at least will indicate what seems probable.

units.la: Ratio: Quia certò causas circumstantiæ quinquagesimi diei definire, & defendere velle, sit prohibita curiositas. Act.1.7. Non est vestrum.
units.tr: Reason: because to wish to define and defend with certainty the causes of the circumstance of the fiftieth day is forbidden curiosity. Acts 1.7: It is not yours.

units.la: Subiiciantur causæ, seu conjecturæ duæ.
units.tr: Let the causes, or two conjectures, be set forth.

units.la: I. Causa: Miraculi celebritas & utilitas: quæ in festo major quàm alio tempore esse potuit.
units.tr: I. Cause: the celebrity and usefulness of the miracle, which could be greater at the feast than at another time.

units.la: Ostendatur hoc I. Ex fine festi: quia tunc convenerant Judæi ad considerationem operum divinorum. Magis ergo ad miraculum attenti erat.
units.tr: Let this be shown: I. from the purpose of the feast: because the Jews had then gathered to consider the works of God. They were therefore more attentive to the miracle.

units.la: II. quia tunc magnus erat confluxus hominum ex variis locis, Act. 2. 5: Erant Ierosolymæ Judæi viri pii ex omni gente sub cælo, &c. Tunc igitur miraculi fama latius spargi & pluribus innotescere potuit.
