units.tr: II. because there was then a great concourse of people from various places, Acts 2.5: There were dwelling at Jerusalem devout Jews from every nation under heaven, etc. Then, therefore, the report of the miracle could be spread more widely and become known to more people.

units.la: Amplificetur coniectura I. à fine miraculi, seu missionis visibilis: qui fuit, ne lateret, sed ut mundo innotesceret & prodesset.
units.tr: Let the conjecture be strengthened I. from the purpose of the miracle, or of the visible mission: which was that it should not be hidden, but made known to the world and be of benefit.

units.la: II. Ab exemplis Christi Joh.2.5.7.10.12: Et Pauli, Act.20.16. qui sæpè Ierosolymam profecti sunt ad dies festos frequentiæ causa, ut doctrinæ & miraculorum usus esset uberior.
units.tr: II. from the examples of Christ, John 2.5.7.10.12, and of Paul, Acts 20.16, who often went up to Jerusalem for the festival days, for the sake of the crowd, so that the use of doctrine and of miracles might be more abundant.

units.la: III. Causa. Analogia latæ legis die 50. post Pa-scha: & dati Spiritus Sancti totidem diebus post resurrectionem Christi veri Paschatis.
units.tr: III. Cause. Analogy with the law given on the fiftieth day after the Passover, and with the Holy Spirit given the same number of days after the resurrection of Christ, the true Passover.

units.la: Afferatur[?] authoritate Augustini, existimantis hanc anagogen etiam à Deo spectatam fuisse, Lib. 2. quæst. 16. in Exod. Epistola 119. ad Ianuar. Et ostendatur conjecturæ probabilitas ex 2.Cor.3. ubi Apostolus modum promulgatæ Legis & Evangelii quasi typum & rem inter se comparare videtur.
units.tr: Let it be cited on the authority of Augustine, who thought that this anagogy was also regarded by God, Book 2, question 16 on Exodus; Epistle 119 to Januarius. And let the probability of the conjecture be shown from 2 Corinthians 3, where the Apostle seems to compare, as type and thing, the manner of the promulgation of the Law and of the Gospel.

units.la: Explicetur breviter ratio comparationis ex v.3.
units.tr: Let the reason for the comparison be briefly explained from verse 3.

units.la: Quia corda, in quibus Evangelium à Spiritu S. est scriptum, vocat tabulas carneas: & eas opponit tabulis lapideis legis. Ergo inscriptionem Evangelii in cordibus, quæ in Pentecoste præcipuè est facta: inscriptioni Legis in tabulis lapideis conferre videtur.
units.tr: Because he calls the hearts, in which the Gospel is written by the Holy Spirit, fleshy tablets, and sets them against the stone tablets of the Law. Therefore he seems to compare the inscription of the Gospel in hearts, which was done chiefly at Pentecost, with the inscription of the Law on stone tablets.

units.la: Addatur & alia ratio Augustini: Quia digitus Dei, quo tabulæ legis dicuntur scriptæ, in novo Testamento Spiritus Dei vocatur. Exod.31.18. Matth.12.28. Luc.11.20. Videtur ergo scriptio legis digito Dei facta: promulgationem Evangelii à Spiritu sancto præstandam præfigurasse.
units.tr: Let another reason of Augustine be added: because the finger of God, by which the tablets of the Law are said to have been written, is in the New Testament called the Spirit of God. Exodus 31.18; Matthew 12.28; Luke 11.20. It seems therefore that the writing of the Law was done by the finger of God, and that it foreshadowed the promulgation of the Gospel, which was to be accomplished by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Conclusio sit συμπέρασις[?]. cum thesi, δόξαν[?] Dei esse summam divinorum operum causam: in quâ extra patefactiones & verbum non sit temere inquirendum.
units.tr: Conclusion let there be a summing up. With the thesis that the glory of God is the highest cause of the divine works, in which, apart from revelations and the Word, one should not rashly inquire.

units.la: Exercitatio X X.
units.tr: Exercitatio XX.

units.la: Consultatio ad amicum de universalitate Redemptionis per mortem-Christi.
units.tr: Consultatio ad amicum de universalitate Redemptionis per mortem Christi.

units.la: EXordium ab occasione. Nuper te incidisse in controversiam cum adversario quodam de universalitate redemtionis omnium hominum per mortem Christi: in qua desideraveris amici præsentiam : & nunc cupias audire judicium ejus.
units.tr: Exordium ab occasione. Recently you became involved in a dispute with a certain opponent about the universality of the redemption of all men through the death of Christ; in which you missed the presence of your friend, and now you wish to hear his judgment.

units.la: Ratio ab ejus dexteritate : & à rationum adversarii speciositate, qua multis ille imponat.
units.tr: Ratio from his skill, and from the plausibility of the opponent's arguments, by which that man deceives many.

units.la: Occupatio : Etsi sententiam amici scias congruere cum tua : tamen rectè eum facturum, si brevem quoq; ἀνασκέλλω[?] rationum illarum scriptam ad te mittat.
units.tr: Occupatio: Although you know that your friend's opinion agrees with yours, nevertheless he will do well if he sends you a brief written account of those arguments, which he has overthrown.

units.la: Propositio : Te breviter repetiturum statum controversiæ & adversarii sententiam cum argumentis.
units.tr: Propositio: You will briefly repeat the state of the controversy and the opponent's position, together with his arguments.

units.la: Ponatur status : An Christus pariter pro o-mnibus ac singulis credentibus & incredulis, piis & impiis, non modo quo ad sufficientiam, sed etiam quo ad efficaciam λύτρων[?], sit passus & mortuus.
units.tr: Ponatur status: Whether Christ suffered and died equally for all and each, believers and unbelievers, the pious and the impious, not only as to sufficiency but also as to the efficacy of the ransom.

units.la: Subiiciatur adversarii affirmatio: ac declaratio per partes:
units.tr: Subiiciatur the opponent's affirmation, and its declaration part by part:

units.la: I. Christum pariter pro Abele & Caino: Petro & Iuda mori voluisse, & mortuum esse.
units.tr: I. That Christ equally wished to die for Abel and Cain, for Peter and Judas, and did die.

units.la: II. Morte sua pariter verè & proprie peccata omnium etiam incredulorum expiasse: & omnibus etiam incredulis salutem præstitisse.
units.tr: II. That by his death he truly and properly expiated the sins of all, even of unbelievers, and conferred salvation on all, even on unbelievers.

units.la: III. Totum genus humanum, nulla fidei vel infidelitatis cujusquam ratione habita, Christi mortem in gratiam & sinum Dei repositum esse.
units.tr: III. That the whole human race, without any regard to the faith or unbelief of anyone, has been restored by Christ's death to the favour and bosom of God.

units.la: IV. Incredulos salutem sibi collatam incredulitate rursus excutere : & denuo in æternum perire, non propter peccata: sed propter incredulitatem.
units.tr: IV. That unbelievers, by unbelief, again cast off the salvation conferred on them, and perish again for ever, not on account of sins, but on account of unbelief.

units.la: Argumentorum adversarii tres classes.
units.tr: The three classes of the opponent's arguments.

units.la: Prima classis à testimoniis Scripturæ Universalitatem expressè continentibus: citra cujusquam hominis exceptionem: comprehendatur Syllogismo: Quod tribuitur toti generi universaliter, necesse est etiam tribui omnibus speciebus & individuis.
units.tr: First class, from the testimonies of Scripture expressly containing universality, without the exception of any man; it may be comprehended in a syllogism: What is attributed universally to the whole genus must necessarily be attributed also to all the species and individuals.

units.la: Redemtio per Christi mortem tribuitur toti generi humano universaliter. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Redemption through Christ's death is attributed universally to the whole human race. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Minoris probatio sint dicta Scripturæ Universalia: recitentur quædam præcipua. Gen. 22. Isai. 53. Ioh. 1.1. Ioh. 2.1. Tim. 2.2. Cor. 5. Heb. 5. Ioh. 3. & 12. Ioh. 17. Rom. 3.1. Cor. 15. &c. Huberus in thesibus enumerat testimonia XXVII.
units.tr: Proof of the minor: let the universal sayings of Scripture be cited; certain principal ones are recited: Gen. 22. Isa. 53. John 1.1. John 2.1. Tim. 2.2. Cor. 5. Heb. 5. John 3. and 12. John 17. Rom. 3.1. Cor. 15. etc. Huber in his theses lists twenty-seven testimonies.

units.la: Amplificetur à natura oppositorum: Propositiones de universali corruptione & reatu generis humani sunt illis oppositæ, & non possunt particulariter accipi: Ergo nec illæ. Omnes in Adamo moriuntur. Omnes mendaces, omnes declinaverunt. Omnes sub peccato.
units.tr: Amplified from the nature of the opposites: The propositions about the universal corruption and guilt of the human race are opposed to these, and cannot be taken particularly; therefore neither can those. In Adam all die. All are liars; all have gone astray. All are under sin.

units.la: Secunda classis à testimoniis Scripturæ de reprobis & infidelibus morte Christi redemtis: comprehendatur Syllogismo. Quibus omnibus Christus venit Salvator: ii omnes mortè ejus sunt redemti efficaciter. Venit autem Salvator tam credentibus qui salvantur, quam incredulis qui non salvantur. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Second class, from the testimonies of Scripture concerning the reprobate and unbelievers redeemed by Christ's death; it may be comprehended in a syllogism: All those for whom Christ came as Saviour were effectively redeemed by his death. Now he came as Saviour both for believers who are saved and for unbelievers who are not saved. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Minor probetur dictis Scripturæ de incredulis [?]cos eos fuisse Christo insitos. Ioh.15. Rom. 11. eis remissa fuisse debita: Matt.18. Christum pro eis mortuum esse: Rom.14. 1.Cor.8. eos a Christo fuisse pretio emtos, 2.Pet.2. eos oblivisci purgationis veterum peccatorum. 2.Pet.1. eos excidere gratia. Gal.3. Heb.2. 2.Cor.6. Rom.11. rursus implicari peccatis & redire ad vomitum. 2.Pet.2. denuo sibi ipsis crucifigere Christum. Hebr.6. Sanguine Christi fuisse sanctificatos. Heb.2. 10. Iudam a Patre fuisse datum filio. Ioh.17. &c.
units.tr: The minor is proved by Scripture's sayings about unbelievers: that they were grafted into Christ, John 15; Rom. 11; that their debts were forgiven them, Matt. 18; that Christ died for them, Rom. 14; 1 Cor. 8; that they were bought from Christ with a price, 2 Pet. 2; that they forgot the purging of their former sins, 2 Pet. 1; that they fall from grace, Gal. 3; Heb. 2; 2 Cor. 6; Rom. 11; that they are again entangled in sins and return to their vomit, 2 Pet. 2; that they crucify Christ afresh for themselves, Heb. 6; that they were sanctified by the blood of Christ, Heb. 2 and 10; that Judas was given by the Father to the Son, John 17; etc.

units.la: TERTIA CLASSIS argumentorum ab absurdis contrariae sententiae, quam ideo absurdam esse oporteat.
units.tr: THIRD CLASS of arguments, from the absurdities of the contrary opinion, which must therefore be absurd.

units.la: Probatio minoris sit absurdorum enumeratio.
units.tr: Proof of the minor is an enumeration of the absurdities.

units.la: I. In dubium vocari totam religionem & fidem Christianam.
units.tr: I. That the whole Christian religion and faith is called into doubt.

units.la: II. Scripturam transformari in mendacissimum Alcoranum.
units.tr: II. That Scripture is transformed into the most lying Alcoran.

units.la: III. Damnari sententiam Catholicae Ecclesiae.
units.tr: III. That the opinion of the Catholic Church is condemned.

units.la: IV. Homines adigi ad desperationem.
units.tr: IV. That men are driven to despair.

units.la: V. Deludi puris particularibus: Christus pro aliquibus duntaxat est mortuus. Ergo etiam pro me &c.
units.tr: V. That they are deceived by mere particulars: Christ died only for some. Therefore also for me, etc.

units.la: VI. Abrogari universum Evangelium: quia nemo sciat, quid cui sit praedicandum.
units.tr: VI. That the whole Gospel is abrogated, because no one knows what should be preached to whom.

units.la: VII. Sacramenta tolli.
units.tr: VII. That the sacraments are abolished.

units.la: Ratio I. quia baptizatis nulla certa promittatur gratia & salus.
units.tr: Reason I. Because no certain grace and salvation is promised to the baptized.

units.la: II. quia corpus & sanguis Christi nulli possit certo exhiberi & praecipi.
units.tr: II. Because the body and blood of Christ cannot be certainly offered and presented to anyone.

units.la: VIII. Deum accusari fraudis, quod aliud dicat, & aliud sentiat.
units.tr: VIII. That God is accused of fraud, because he says one thing and thinks another.

units.la: I x. Accusari eundem execrabiles mendacii, quia promittat, quod non det.
units.tr: IX. That the same God is accused of execrable lying, because he promises what he does not give.

units.la: x. Christum accusari, quod Deum & homines deluserit. Ratio, quod Deum: quia fateatur se pro omnibus mortuum, quum mandatum acceperit à Deo moriendi tantum pro paucis. Ratio, quod homines: quia dicat se mortuum pro omnibus, quum tantum sit mortuus pro paucis.
units.tr: X. That Christ is accused of deceiving God and men. The reason as to God: because he confesses that he died for all, when he had received a command from God to die only for a few. The reason as to men: because he says he died for all, when he died only for a few.

units.la: XI. XII. XIII. Deum accusari injustitiæ, crudelitatis, ἀπιστίας, &c.
units.tr: XI. XII. XIII. That God is accused of injustice, cruelty, faithlessness [ἀπιστία], etc.

units.la: Ἀπολογία: reliqua ut à candore nimis remota consulto te praeterire, &c.
units.tr: Apology: the rest, as too remote from candour, I deliberately pass over to you, etc.

units.la: Conclusio sit petitio κατακλησις, cum pollicitatione gratitudinis.
units.tr: Conclusion is a petition [κατάκλησις], with a promise of gratitude.

units.la: Exercitatio XXI.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXI.

units.la: Responsio de universalitate Redemtionis per mortem Christi.
units.tr: Response on the universality of Redemption through the death of Christ.

units.la: EXordium sit brevis querela de furoribus Satanæ turbantis Ecclesiæ pacem litibus novis & periculosis cum offendiculo infirmorum.
units.tr: Let the exordium be a brief complaint about the furies of Satan, who disturbs the peace of the Church with new and dangerous quarrels, to the stumbling of the weak.

units.la: Adversarii. Pios tamen non debere turbari.
units.tr: Objection. Yet the godly ought not to be disturbed.

units.la: Ratio I. Qua Spiritus sanctus prædixerit. 1.Cor.11.Matt.24.
units.tr: Reason I. The Holy Spirit foretold it. 1 Cor. 11; Matt. 24.

units.la: I I. Quia Deus his malis bene utatur ad probationem electorum & veritatis illustrationem.
units.tr: II. Because God makes good use of these evils to prove the elect and to illustrate the truth.

units.la: I I I. Quia fit χειροτονία victoriæ nostræ in controversiis superioribus. Eucharistica & Vbiquitaria taria: quia actores malæ causæ lites novas quæ-runt.
units.tr: III. Because it is a χειροτονία (ordination, a choosing) of our victory in the earlier controversies: the Eucharistic and the Ubiquitarian ones, because the authors of a bad cause seek out new quarrels.

units.la: Transitio per hypothesin ἀπολογητικῶς [?] cum modesta extenuatione iudicii tui: Cum videris amicum adversarii Sophistica nonnihil turbatum: te libenter pro tenuitate tua petitioni eius gratificaturum.
units.tr: Transition by way of hypothesis, ἀπολογητικῶς [?], with a modest qualification of your judgment: when you see your friend, the adversary's sophist, somewhat troubled, you will gladly, as far as your slender ability allows, grant his request.

units.la: Ostendatur amico, ad faciliorem victoriam faciendam esse quæstionis separationem de electis seu fidelibus: & de reprobis seu perseverantibus & perseveraturis in impœnitentia.
units.tr: To be shown to the friend: to make the victory easier, the question must be separated into the elect or believers on the one hand, and the reprobate or those who persist and will persist in impenitence on the other.

units.la: Ratio: quia de illis constet: de his solis quæstio relinquatur, An & quatenus pro eis Christus sit mortuus.
units.tr: Reason: because the former are agreed upon; the question is left only concerning the latter: whether and in what sense Christ died for them.

units.la: Clausula: Hanc igitur solam urgendam esse, ut constet, adversarium tantum reproborum & scelera-torum patronum agere: & de hac prius: postea de universalitate redemtionis te re-sponsurum.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore this alone is to be pressed, so that it is established that the adversary is the patron only of the reprobate and the wicked; and that this is dealt with first, and afterwards you will be answered on the universality of redemption.

units.la: Propositio per distinctionem: Christum esse mortuum, & voluisse mori etiam pro reprobis, dici posse ratione sufficientiæ λύτρων [?]: sed non ratione efficaciæ.
units.tr: Proposition by distinction: that Christ died, and willed to die, also for the reprobate, can be said by reason of the sufficiency of the λύτρων [?] (ransom), but not by reason of its efficacy.

units.la: Confirmatio affirma-tivæ.
units.tr: Confirmation of the affirmative.

units.la: Subjiciatur declaratio & confirmatio utriusq; partis.
units.tr: Let the declaration and confirmation of each part be subjoined.

units.la: I. Affirmativa. Declaretur, quid sit sufficientia λύτρων [?] pro reprobis, &c. & confirmetur per occup. Etsi multis non placeat distinctio: tamen propter contentiosos retinendam esse.
units.tr: I. Affirmative. Let it be declared what the sufficiency of the λύτρων [?] is for the reprobate, etc., and let it be confirmed by an occupation (an argument from the thing itself). Although the distinction does not please many, nevertheless it is to be retained on account of the contentious.

units.la: Argumentum I. Quia scriptura aliquoties dicit, Christum pro omnibus mortuum, quod non potest nisi de sufficientia intelligi. 1. Tim. 2. 2. Cor. 5. Heb. 2. 1. Ioh. 2.
units.tr: Argument I. Because Scripture on several occasions says that Christ died for all, which cannot be understood except of sufficiency. 1 Tim. 2; 2 Cor. 5; Heb. 2; 1 John 2.

units.la: II. Quia etiam infideles & impœnitentes redemti dicuntur, 2. Pet. 2. Heb. 6. & 10.
units.tr: II. Because even unbelievers and the impenitent are said to be redeemed. 2 Pet. 2; Heb. 6 and 10.

units.la: III. Quia Christus <bl>ἀντίλυτρον</bl> præstare voluit infinitæ dignitatis & sufficientiæ: ne ex defectu vel insufficientia <bl>ἀντίλυτρου</bl> quisquam periret.
units.tr: III. Because Christ willed to furnish an ἀντίλυτρον (counter-ransom) of infinite dignity and sufficiency, so that no one might perish through a defect or insufficiency of the ἀντίλυτρον.

units.la: Amplif. à contrar: Cum culpa sit universalis: etiam medicinam rectè dici universalem & immensam sufficientia.
units.tr: Amplification from the contrary: since the guilt is universal, the medicine too is rightly said to be universal and of immense sufficiency.

units.la: IV. Quia patribus & Scholasticis distinctio fit usitata: Augustin. Tom. 7. art. 1. Prosper. Innoc. 3. Lombardus lib. 3. d. 20. Thomas Sum. de veritate: Neque Calvinus improbat Comm. in 1. Ioh. 2. 2.
units.tr: IV. Because the distinction is customary among the Fathers and the Schoolmen: Augustine, Tom. 7, art. 1; Prosper; Innocent 3; Lombard, bk. 3, d. 20; Thomas, Summa, on truth; nor does Calvin disapprove, Comm. on 1 John 2.

units.la: Confirmatio negativæ.
units.tr: Confirmation of the negative.

units.la: II. Præcisio, & Transitio ad confirmationem Negativa: quæ prius rectè circunscribatur: Qui dicantur reprobi: perseverantes & perseveraturi in infidelitate & impœnitentia manifesta vel occulta: damnati & damnandi. Quid, Christum pro his non mortuum ratione efficaciæ: non conferre beneficia mortis sua, utpote infidelibus: Ac ponatur negatio adversarii verbis: non eos redemisse à peccato, morte non purgasse, sanctificasse, Deo reconciliasse: in sinum & gratiam Dei reposuisse, &c.
units.tr: II. Precision, and transition to the confirmation of the negative: which must first be properly circumscribed: who are called the reprobate: those persevering and about to persevere in unbelief and manifest or hidden impenitence: the damned and those to be damned. That is, Christ did not die for these, in respect of the efficacy of his death: he does not confer the benefits of his death on them, inasmuch as they are unbelievers. And the adversary's denial is to be set down in these words: that he has not redeemed them from sin, not cleansed them from death, not sanctified them, not reconciled them to God, not restored them to the bosom and favour of God, etc.

units.la: Confirmationis Argumentum i. ab authori-tate Scripturae hoc negantis.
units.tr: Argument for the confirmation I, from the authority of Scripture denying this.

units.la: Probetur tripliciter : 1. quia promissiones Evangelii perpetuò habent annexam conditionem fidei, pœnitentiæ & gratitudinis, quæ non est in reprobis. Illustretur aliquot dictis de præcipuis beneficiis.
units.tr: Let it be proved in three ways: 1. because the promises of the Gospel always have attached to them the condition of faith, repentance and gratitude, which is not present in the reprobate. Let it be illustrated by several sayings concerning the chief benefits.

units.la: 1. Remissione peccatorum Act.10.43.Rom.3
units.tr: 1. Remission of sins: Acts 10:43; Rom. 3.

units.la: 2. Liberatione à morte, Ioh.5.24. A Diabolo.2. 1 im[?].2.26. Eph.6.16.
units.tr: 2. Deliverance from death: John 5:24; from the Devil: 2 Tim. 2:26; Eph. 6:16.

units.la: 3. Purgatione Ioh.15.2. Act.15.9.
units.tr: 3. Cleansing: John 15:2; Acts 15:9.

units.la: 4. Sanctificatione Ioh.17.19.20.
units.tr: 4. Sanctification: John 17:19, 20.

units.la: 5. Reconciliatione. Rom.5.1.
units.tr: 5. Reconciliation: Rom. 5:1.

units.la: 6. Gratia Dei Heb.11. Absque fide impossibile est placere Deo.
units.tr: 6. The grace of God: Heb. 11: Without faith it is impossible to please God.

units.la: 7. Vita æterna. Ioh.3.&5.&6.
units.tr: 7. Eternal life: John 3, 5 and 6.

units.la: Probatio ii. Quia infideles ab his beneficiis diserte excluduntur in Scriptura: &c. Ioh.3.36. Qui non credit super eum manet ira Dei. 1.Cor.6. Qui talia faciunt, &c. Rom.8.8. Qui in carne sunt, &c. Qui Spiritum Christi non habent, &c. Gal.4.30. Eiice ancillam, &c. Apoc.22.15. Foris sunt canes, &c.
units.tr: Proof II. Because unbelievers are plainly excluded from these benefits in Scripture, etc.: John 3:36, He who does not believe, the wrath of God remains on him. 1 Cor. 6, Those who do such things, etc. Rom. 8:8, Those who are in the flesh, etc.; those who do not have the Spirit of Christ, etc. Gal. 4:30, Cast out the bondwoman, etc. Rev. 22:15, Outside are the dogs, etc.

units.la: Prob. iii. Quia infidelibus Scriptura minatur mala illis bonis contraria. Ioh.3.18: Iam condemnatus est: & 36. Ira Dei manet super eū, Mat.25. Ite maledicti in ignem æternum.
units.tr: Proof III. Because Scripture threatens unbelievers with evils contrary to those goods. John 3:18, Already he is condemned; and v. 36, the wrath of God remains on him. Matt. 25, Depart, accursed, into everlasting fire.

units.la: Obiectio. Excluduntur, & damnabuntur non propter peccata expiata, sed propter incredulitatem Ioh.3.18. Quia non credit, &c.
units.tr: Objection. They are excluded and will be damned not on account of sins atoned for, but on account of unbelief: John 3:18, because he does not believe, etc.

units.la: Respon. i. neg.conseq. quia posito uno peccato tanquam præcipua causa damnationis, non negantur alia.
units.tr: Answer I. I deny the consequence: because, when one sin is posited as the chief cause of damnation, the others are not thereby denied.

units.la: Ratio: quia omnia peccata manent in infideli-bus, & merentur mortem.
units.tr: Reason: because all sins remain in unbelievers, and deserve death.

units.la: Item: Christus & Paulus non solam infidelitatem, sed quævis peccata faciunt causam damnationis. Matth.25.1.Cor.6.
units.tr: Likewise: Christ and Paul make not only unbelief but any sins the cause of damnation: Matt. 25; 1 Cor. 6.

units.la: II. Negatur antithesis peccatorum & incredulitatis, quia[?] hæc est caput omnium peccatorum.
units.tr: II. The antithesis between sins and unbelief is denied, because this is the head of all sins.

units.la: III. Per βλασφημίαν[?]: Si propter incredulitatem, Ergo propter peccata: Ratio quia incredulitas est pater & mater peccatorum.
units.tr: III. By blasphemy: If on account of unbelief, then on account of sins. Reason: because unbelief is the father and mother of sins.

units.la: Instantia. Incredulitas non consideratur ut in se peccatum est, sed quatenus respuit media salutis.
units.tr: Instance. Unbelief is not considered as it is in itself a sin, but insofar as it rejects the means of salvation.

units.la: Resp. per βλασφημίαν quia respuit: ideo peccatum: quia contemtus salutis & mediorum est ἀνομία. Repudietur tam crassa ἀδολεσχία[?].
units.tr: Answer. By blasphemy, because it rejects; therefore it is a sin, because contempt of salvation and of the means is lawlessness. Let such crude babbling be rejected.

units.la: Argumentum II. à testimoniis Scripturæ, quibus beneficia mortis Christi ad credentes & Ecclesiam diserte restringuntur.
units.tr: Argument II. From the testimonies of Scripture, by which the benefits of Christ's death are expressly restricted to believers and the Church.

units.la: Recitentur & applicentur quædam præcipua.
units.tr: Let certain chief passages be recited and applied.

units.la: De credentibus. Ioh.3.16.&5.24.&6.40.47. Act.10.43. Rom.3.22. Gal.3.22. Heb.5.9. Ioh.12.46. ut nullus qui in me credit in tenebris maneat.
units.tr: Concerning believers. John 3:16; 5:24; 6:40, 47. Acts 10:43. Rom. 3:22. Gal. 3:22. Heb. 5:9. John 12:46, that no one who believes in me may remain in darkness.
Concerning the Church. Matt. 1:21; John 10:15; 15:13; 17:9, 19. Eph. 5:25.

units.la: Obiectio. Exclusivam non addi.
units.tr: Objection. The exclusive particle is not added.

units.la: Resp. Imo addi, dum excluduntur infideles & alieni ab Ecclesia. Qui non crediderit, &c. Ergo soli credentes.
units.tr: Answer. Indeed it is added, while unbelievers and those alien from the Church are excluded. He who does not believe, etc. Therefore only believers.

units.la: Instant. In Ecclesia multos esse infideles & hy-pocritas.
units.tr: Instance. That there are many unbelievers and hypocrites in the Church.

units.la: Resp. Non in Ecclesia electorum, pro qua so-la se Christus sanctificavit.
units.tr: Answer. Not in the Church of the elect, for which alone Christ sanctified himself.

units.la: Argumentum III. ex Matth.7. Christus infideles & hypocritas nunquā novit. Ergo nun-quam redemit, ita ut in gratiam & sinum Dei reposuerit.
units.tr: Argument III. From Matt. 7: Christ never knew unbelievers and hypocrites. Therefore he never redeemed them, so as to have restored them to grace and the bosom of God.

units.la: Argumentum IV. A præcepto Christi Matth.7. Vetat sanctum dare canibus, margaritas objicere porcis. Multo minus ipse hoc fecit: sinum & gratiam Dei canibus & porcis aperien-do, vel panem filiorum eis objiciendo.
units.tr: Argument IV. From a precept of Christ, Matt. 7: he forbids giving what is holy to dogs, or casting pearls before swine. Much less would he himself have done this, opening the bosom and grace of God to dogs and swine, or throwing the children's bread to them.

units.la: Argumentum V. Contemtores cœnæ nun-quam gustabunt eam. Luc.14.24. Explicetur al-legoria: & addatur conclusio: aspernantes gra-tiam, licet vocentur, nunquam tamen ejus factos esse vel fieri participes.
units.tr: Argument V. Despisers of the Supper will never taste it. Luke 14:24. Let the allegory be explained, and the conclusion added: those who spurn grace, although they are called, nevertheless never were made, or are made, partakers of it.

units.la: Objectio: Sententiam esse parabolicam.
units.tr: Objection: That the sentence is parabolic.

units.la: Resp. Sed sensum proprium congruere cum voce Evangelij: Qui non crediderit condemnabi-tur.
units.tr: Answer. But the proper sense agrees with the voice of the Gospel: He who does not believe will be condemned.

units.la: Argumentum VI. Hypothesis de omnib. infidelibus in gratiam & sinum Dei morte Chri-sti restitutis, est absurda & impia.
units.tr: Argument VI. The hypothesis that all unbelievers have been restored by the death of Christ to grace and the bosom of God is absurd and impious.

units.la: Ratio: quia multa principia Christianæ fidei evertit.
units.tr: Reason: because it overthrows many principles of the Christian faith.

units.la: Probetur enumeratione principiorum quæ evertit:
units.tr: Let it be proved by enumerating the principles which it overthrows:

units.la: 1. quòd omnes nascimur filii iræ, seu de pec-cato originis. Eph.2. Psal.51. Ratio confeq: Quia omnes nascentur in sinu & gratia Dei, quod filiis irae non competit.
units.tr: 1. That we are all born children of wrath, or concerning original sin: Eph. 2; Ps. 51. Consequent reason: because all would be born in the bosom and grace of God, which does not befit children of wrath.

units.la: II. Quod extra Ecclesiam nō est salus Act.4. Extra eũ nō est salus, Rom.8. Quos vocavit, hos, &c.
units.tr: II. That outside the Church there is no salvation: Acts 4. There is no salvation outside him, Rom. 8: Whom he called, these, etc.

units.la: Ratio: quia omnes Turcarum & Canibalum familiae nascentur in gratia & sinu Dei extra Ecclesiam.
units.tr: Reason: because all the families of the Turks and the Cannibals would be born in the grace and bosom of God outside the Church.

units.la: III. Quod impossibile est sine fide placere Deo. Heb.11.
units.tr: III. That it is impossible to please God without faith: Heb. 11.

units.la: Ratio: quia placere Deo est in sinu & gratiam Dei propter Christum recipi, quod isti etiam infidelibus tribuunt.
units.tr: Reason: because to please God is to be received into the bosom and grace of God on account of Christ, which they also attribute to unbelievers.

units.la: IV. Quod infidelibus post mortem nullus relinquitur gratiae locus. 2. Cor.5. Superinduemur, si non nudi, &c.
units.tr: IV. That for unbelievers after death no place of grace remains: 2 Cor. 5: We shall be clothed, if not naked, etc.

units.la: Ratio: quia ex adversarii opinione omnes infideles ante Christum mortui & damnati per mortem ejus in gratiam & sinum Dei reponentur.
units.tr: Reason: because according to the opinion of the adversary, all unbelievers who died before Christ and were damned will be restored through his death to the grace and bosom of God.

units.la: V. Quod justitia Dei neminem damnat nisi peccantem.
units.tr: V. That the justice of God condemns no one except the sinning.

units.la: Ratio: Quia mortui & damnati ante Christū è sinu Dei rursus excuti finguntur, nullo ipsorum novo peccato interveniente.
units.tr: Reason: because those who died and were damned before Christ are imagined to be cast out again from the bosom of God, no new sin of theirs intervening.

units.la: VI. Quod omnia peccata morte Christi sunt expiata, 1. Ioh.1.
units.tr: VI. That all sins have been atoned for by the death of Christ: 1 John 1.

units.la: Ratio: Quia excipiunt incredulitatem.
units.tr: Reason: because it excepts unbelief.

units.la: VII. Quod nulli electi pereant, Matth.24. Ioh.10.
units.tr: VII. That none of the elect perish: Matt. 24; John 10.

units.la: Ratio: quia juxta adversarium multi vere credentes, Deo reconciliati peribunt.
units.tr: Reason: because according to the adversary, many who truly believe and are reconciled to God will perish.

units.la: Syllogismi harum rationum δι’ ἀλλωάτα[?].
units.tr: Syllogisms of these arguments, δι’ ἀλλωάτα [?].

units.la: Nulli nascentes in sinu & gratia Dei nascuntur filii irae.
units.tr: No one born in the bosom and grace of God is born a child of wrath.

units.la: Omnes homines (ex hypothesi) nascuntur in sinu & gratia Dei.
units.tr: All men (by hypothesis) are born in the bosom and grace of God.

units.la: Ergo nulli homines nascuntur filii irae: quod est falsum.
units.tr: Therefore no men are born children of wrath: which is false.

units.la: Maior vera ex natura contrariorum immediatorum.
units.tr: The major is true from the nature of immediate contraries.

units.la: Minor est adversarii falsa: quia conclusionis falsae causa.
units.tr: The minor is false according to the opponent, since it is the cause of a false conclusion.

units.la: Omnes nascentes in sinu & gratia Dei, eo momento sunt salvi.
units.tr: All who are born in the bosom and grace of God are saved at that moment.

units.la: Omnes Turcae & Canibales extra Ecclesiam nascuntur in sinu.&c.
units.tr: All Turks and cannibals, born outside the Church, are in the bosom, etc.

units.la: Ergo eo momento sunt salvi: & morientes ante actualem incredulitatem salvantur extra Ecclesiam: quod est absurdum.
units.tr: Therefore they are saved at that moment, and those who die before actual unbelief are saved outside the Church: which is absurd.

units.la: Maior vera ex dicto Rom.5. Reconciliati mul-to magis servab. &c.
units.tr: The major is true from the saying of Rom. 5: "Being reconciled, much more shall they be saved," etc.

units.la: Minor est adversarii absurda: quia conclusionis absurdae causa.
units.tr: The minor is absurd according to the opponent, since it is the cause of an absurd conclusion.

units.la: Omnes recepti in sinum & gratiam Dei placent Deo.
units.tr: All who are received into the bosom and grace of God are pleasing to God.

units.la: Omnes infideles recepti sunt in sinum, &c.
units.tr: All unbelievers are received into the bosom, etc.

units.la: Ergo omnes infideles placent Deo: falsum. Maior est vera ex terminorum æquipollentia.
units.tr: Therefore all unbelievers are pleasing to God: false. The major is true from the equivalence of the terms.

units.la: Minor adversarii falsa: quia falsæ conclusionis causa.
units.tr: The minor is false according to the opponent, since it is the cause of a false conclusion.

units.la: Omnes ante Christum mortui, morte Christi sunt restituti in sinum & gratiam Dei post mortem.
units.tr: All who died before Christ were restored to the bosom and grace of God after death by the death of Christ.

units.la: Quidam ante Christum mortui fuerunt infi-deles.
units.tr: Some who died before Christ were unbelievers.

units.la: Ergo quidam infideles restituuntur in gratiam Dei post mortem.
units.tr: Therefore some unbelievers are restored to the grace of God after death.

units.la: Maior est adversarii: falsa: quia falsæ conclusionis causa.
units.tr: The major is false according to the opponent, since it is the cause of a false conclusion.

units.la: Minor vera ex Scriptura & historia.
units.tr: The minor is true from Scripture and history.

units.la: Omnes impii mortui ante Christum damnantur.
units.tr: All wicked men who died before Christ are condemned.

units.la: Omnes impii mortui ante Christum non habent peccatum.
units.tr: All wicked men who died before Christ have no sin.

units.la: Ergo quidam non habentes peccatum damnantur, falsum.
units.tr: Therefore some who have no sin are condemned: false.

units.la: Maior vera ex Ioh. 3. qui non credit in filium Dei, &c.
units.tr: The major is plainly true from John 3: "He who does not believe in the Son of God," etc.

units.la: Minor sequitur ex hypothesi adversarii.
units.tr: The minor follows from the opponent's hypothesis.

units.la: Omnes purgati morte Christi ab omni peccato tunc cum amplius peccare non possent, non habuerunt peccatum.
units.tr: All who were cleansed from all sin by the death of Christ, at the time when they could no longer sin, had no sin.

units.la: Omnes impii mortui ante Christum, morte ejus purgati sunt ab omni peccato tunc cum amplius peccare non possent: quia mortui.
units.tr: All wicked men who died before Christ were cleansed from all sin by his death, at the time when they could no longer sin, because they were dead.

units.la: Ergo omnes impii mortui ante Christum nō habent peccatum.
units.tr: Therefore all wicked men who died before Christ have no sin.

units.la: Maior manifeste vera: quia à prioribus peccatis fuerunt purgati, ex hypothesi: nova admittere non potuerunt mortui.
units.tr: The major is manifestly true, since they were cleansed from their earlier sins by hypothesis; the dead could not admit new ones.

units.la: Minor itidem vera ex hypothesi. Et falsa tamen utraque ex Scriptura: Necesse ergo est hypothesin falsam esse.
units.tr: The minor is likewise true by hypothesis. Yet both are false from Scripture. It is necessary therefore that the hypothesis is false.

units.la: Incredulitas non est expiata sanguine Christi.
units.tr: Unbelief is not atoned for by the blood of Christ.

units.la: Incredulitas est peccatum.
units.tr: Unbelief is sin.

units.la: Quoddam ergo peccatum nō est expiatū sanguine Christi: fallum ex dicto.1.Ioh.1.7. Sanguis Iesu Christi filii Dei purgat nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: Therefore some sin is not atoned for by the blood of Christ: false, from the saying of 1 John 1:7: "The blood of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, cleanses us from all sin."

units.la: Minor vera ex lege, & 1.Ioh.3.
units.tr: The minor is true from the law and 1 John 3.

units.la: Maior ex hypothesi adversarii sequitur:
units.tr: The major follows from the opponent's hypothesis:

units.la: Propter quod solum damnantur impii, id nō est expiatum morte Christi.
units.tr: For the reason that the wicked alone are condemned, that is not atoned for by the death of Christ.

units.la: Propter solam incredulitatem damnantur impii ex hypothesi. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: By hypothesis the wicked are condemned for unbelief alone. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Multi vere credentes deficiunt & pereunt.
units.tr: Many who truly believe fall away and perish.

units.la: Omnes vere credentes sunt electi.
units.tr: All who truly believe are elect.

units.la: Ergo multi electi deficiunt & pereunt, contra Scripturam, Matt.24. Ioh.10.
units.tr: Therefore many of the elect fall away and perish, against Scripture, Matt. 24; John 10.

units.la: Minor est vera: Act.13. Crediderunt quotquot erant ord.
units.tr: The minor is true: Acts 13: "As many as were ordained to eternal life believed."

units.la: Maior falsa: quia falsæ conclusionis causa.
units.tr: The major is false, since it is the cause of a false conclusion.

units.la: Confutatio.
units.tr: Refutation.

units.la: Præcisio absurdorum & confirmationis: cum transitione ad confutationem argumentorum adversarii.
units.tr: A cutting off of the absurdities and of the confirmation, with a transition to the refutation of the opponent's arguments.

units.la: Ad syllogismum primæ classis argumentorū.
units.tr: To the syllogism of the first class of arguments.

units.la: Resp. 1. per concessionem totius de sufficientia λύτρῳ [?] Christi: quia satisfactio sufficit pro culpa omnium & singulorum : & medicina æque est universalis atque morbus, modo fiat applicatio per fidem.
units.tr: Answer I: by granting the whole concerning the sufficiency of Christ's ransom: because satisfaction suffices for the guilt of all and of each, and the medicine is as universal as the disease, provided application is made through faith.

units.la: II. per negationem minoris de universali applicatione & effectu redemtionis in singulis: quia major pars reliquit oblatum beneficium. Probetur simul ex primo & secundo argumento confirmationis negativæ partis.
units.tr: II: by denying the minor concerning the universal application and effect of redemption in each individual, because the greater part left the offered benefit. Let it be proved at the same time from the first and second arguments of the confirmation of the negative part.

units.la: Adprobat. minoris. Resp. Esse fallacia consequetis.
units.tr: Proof of the minor. Answer: this is a fallacy of the consequent.

units.la: Ratio: quia dicta universalia non probent universalitatem applicationis & effectus in singulis, sed tantum meriti.
units.tr: Reason: because the said universal statements do not prove the universality of application and effect in each individual, but only of merit.

units.la: Occupatio: Etsi inductione seu examine singulorum id facile esset offendere: tamen te generaliter tantum id facturum.
units.tr: Objection: Although it would be easy to take offence at this by induction or examination of individuals, yet you will do it only in general terms.

units.la: Ratio I. quia inductio foret prolixa & tædiosa repetitionib. II. quia non necessaria: cum pleraque similiter solvantur.
units.tr: Reason I: because the induction would be long and tedious through repetitions. II: because it is not necessary, since most of them are similarly resolved.

units.la: Exponatur solutio tripartita.
units.tr: The threefold solution is set out.

units.la: I. Pleraq; dicta loquuntur vel de sufficientia αὐτάρκεια & meriti pro singulis & omnib. vel certe de universitate credentium, quib. solis effectus redemtionis contingit: quia soli eam fide sibi applicant; Vt Jef.53. Lev.16. Rom.5.&8. 2.Cor.5. Col.1.20. 21.22. Heb.2.
units.tr: I. Most of the sayings speak either of the sufficiency and self-sufficiency of merit for each and all, or certainly of the universality of believers, to whom alone the effect of redemption belongs, because only they apply it to themselves by faith; as Isa. 53; Lev. 16; Rom. 5 and 8; 2 Cor. 5; Col. 1:20, 21, 22; Heb. 2.

units.la: Brevitatis causa remittatur amicus ad diligentem textus inspectionem.
units.tr: For the sake of brevity the friend is referred to a careful inspection of the text.

units.la: II. Quædam loquuntur de universali mandato fidei & invitatione ad salutem, ut 1.Tim.2. 2.Pet.3. Act.17. Col.1.23.28. Tit 2. Hinc vero inferre universalitatem applicationis & effectus, est fallacia non causæ.
units.tr: II. Some speak of the universal command of faith and the invitation to salvation, as 1 Tim. 2; 2 Pet. 3; Acts 17; Col. 1:23, 28; Titus 2. To infer from these universality of application and effect is a fallacy of non-cause.

units.la: III. In multis per universalem particulam extenditur redemtionis beneficium vel copula-tive tam ad gentes quàm ad Judæos fideles: ut Gen.13.&22.Psal.2.1.Ioh.2.Ioh.17. Rom.16.& in dictis similibus, in quibus mundi fit mentio: Vel distributive ad quosvis omnium nationum, con-ditionum, ætatum, sexuum, homines: sed cum conditione fidei & pœnitentiæ expressa vel sub-intellecta, ut 1. Tim.2. Act.10. v.35.43.
units.tr: III. In many passages the benefit of redemption is extended by the universal particle, either conjunctively, to Gentiles as well as to believing Jews, as Gen. 13 and 22; Ps. 2:1; John 2; John 17; Rom. 16; and in similar sayings in which mention is made of the world; or distributively, to any men of all nations, conditions, ages and sexes, but with the condition of faith and repentance expressed or understood, as 1 Tim. 2; Acts 10:35, 43.

units.la: Addatur ratio communis: quia in his manifesta est collatio Veteris & Novi Testamenti, & amplificatio gratiæ Christi pertinentis ad omnes credentes: Illustretur authoritate Augustini Enchir.cap.103.&c.
units.tr: Let the common reason be added: because in these there is a manifest comparison of the Old and New Testaments, and an amplification of the grace of Christ pertaining to all believers. Let it be illustrated by the authority of Augustine, Enchiridion, chap. 103, etc.

units.la: Ad amplificationem à natura oppositorum.
units.tr: To the amplification from the nature of opposites.

units.la: Resp. 1. per concessionem de sufficientia tàm medicinæ quàm morbi, ut supra.
units.tr: Answer I: by granting the sufficiency of both the medicine and the disease, as above.

units.la: II. per negationem consequentiæ propter oppositorum dissimilitudinem.
units.tr: II: by denying the consequence, on account of the dissimilarity of the opposites.

units.la: Ostendatur dissimilitudo duplex.
units.tr: Let the twofold dissimilarity be shown.

units.la: I. quod reatus propagatur per naturam: redemtio datur per gratiam arbitrariam: Miseretur quorum vult:
units.tr: I. That guilt is propagated through nature; redemption is given through arbitrary grace: "He has mercy on whom he wills."

units.la: II. quod reatus propagatur in omnes abso-lutè: Redemtio offertur cum conditione fidei & pœnitentiæ: Ut omnis qui credit, &c.
units.tr: II. That guilt is propagated to all absolutely; redemption is offered with the condition of faith and repentance: "That whoever believes," etc.

units.la: Claudatur, Reatum ergo absolutè: redemtionem ex hypothesi universalem esse.
units.tr: Conclusion: therefore guilt is absolute, and redemption is universal only by hypothesis.

units.la: Responsio ad syllogismum secundæ classis argumentorum.
units.tr: Response to the syllogism of the second class of arguments.

units.la: I. Per concessionem totius de sufficientia λύτρων[?] pro peccatis tam incredulorum quam credentium; ut prius.
units.tr: I. By conceding the whole premise about the sufficiency of the λύτρα[?] for the sins of unbelievers as well as believers, as before.

units.la: II. De efficacia per negationem consequentiae: à non sufficiente causa ad effectum: quia redemtionis causa sufficiens non est salvatoris adventus: sed salutis partae & oblatae acceptio per fidem: seu: quia redemti dicuntur non quibus venit, sed à quibus agnoscitur Redemtor.
units.tr: II. Concerning efficacy, by denying the consequence: from a cause that is not sufficient to the effect. For the sufficient cause of redemption is not the coming of the Savior, but the acceptance through faith of the salvation that has been obtained and offered. Or: those are called redeemed not those to whom the Redeemer came, but those by whom the Redeemer is acknowledged.

units.la: Probetur ex Ioh. i. v. ii. 12. In propria venit & sui eum non receperunt: Quotquot autem acceperunt eum, his dedit potestatem ἐξουσίας[?].
units.tr: Let it be proved from John 1:11–12: He came to his own, and his own did not receive him. But as many as received him, to them he gave the power [ἐξουσία]?

units.la: Illustretur exemplo Mosis, qui missus redemtor populo nil profuit, quamdiu repudiaretur. Act. 7. 25.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated by the example of Moses, who, sent as redeemer, profited the people nothing as long as he was rejected. Acts 7:25.

units.la: III. Negatione minoris de incredulis per occupationem: Etsi & his venerit redemtor, invitatione eorum ad fidem & salutem, ut sint ἀπολύτρωτοι[?]: solis tamen electis credentibus venisse redemtorem praedestinatione & efficacia.
units.tr: III. By denying the minor premise concerning unbelievers, by the counter-assumption: although the Redeemer has also come to them, by inviting them to faith and salvation, so that they may be [ἀπολύτρωτοι]?, yet the Redeemer has come only to the elect who believe, by predestination and efficacy.

units.la: Probatio 1. à testimoniis Scripturae Isai. 9. Filius nobis est datus. Zach. 9. Rex tuus venit tibi. Matth. 1. Servabit populum suum. Rom. 8. Filium suum dedit pro nobis omnibus nempe electis fidelibus: de quibus sequitur. Eph. 5. 14. Surge à mortuis & illucescet tibi Christus. Eph. 1. Electi in Christo, ut essemus sancti.
units.tr: Proof 1, from the testimonies of Scripture: Isaiah 9: A son is given to us. Zechariah 9: Your king comes to you. Matthew 1: He will save his people. Romans 8: He gave his Son for us all, namely the faithful elect, from whom it follows. Ephesians 5:14: Arise from the dead, and Christ will shine upon you. Ephesians 1: The elect in Christ, that we should be holy.

units.la: Probatio II. quia pugnaret cum Sapientia Dei, Christum frustrari fine mortis suae in maxima parte hominum. Ioh. 6. Sciebat à principio, quinam essent, qui non crederent, &c.
units.tr: Proof II, because it would conflict with the wisdom of God, that Christ should frustrate the purpose of his death in the greatest part of mankind. John 6: He knew from the beginning who they were that did not believe, etc.

units.la: Ad probationem Minoris. Resp. 1. generalis: Est fallacia consequentis.
units.tr: In response to the proof of the minor premise. Answer 1, general: it is the fallacy of the consequent.

units.la: Ratio: quia ex dictis tantum sequitur conclusio particularis in prima vel tertia figura: & sic deficit probatio universalis.
units.tr: Reason: because from what has been said only a particular conclusion follows in the first or third figure, and so the universal proof fails.

units.la: Ostendatur exemplo primi loci vel sequentiü.
units.tr: Let it be shown by an example of the first or following forms.

units.la: Omnes Christo insiti sunt morte ejus redēti.
units.tr: All who are grafted into Christ are redeemed by his death.

units.la: Quidam insiti sunt increduli reprobi.
units.tr: Some who are grafted in are unbelieving reprobates.

units.la: Quidam ergo increduli reprobi sunt morte Christi redemti.
units.tr: Some unbelieving reprobates, therefore, are redeemed by the death of Christ.

units.la: Responsio II. generalis. Probationes sumunt vel minorem vel majorem falsam pro vera.
units.tr: Answer II, general. The proofs take either a false minor or a false major for a true one.

units.la: Exempla de minore falsa:
units.tr: Examples of a false minor:

units.la: Ex Joh.15.Rom.11. Quidam vere Christo insiti.
units.tr: From John 15, Romans 11: Some are truly grafted into Christ.

units.la: Ex Matth.18. Quidam vere peccatorum remissionem consecuti.
units.tr: From Matthew 18: Some have truly obtained the remission of sins.

units.la: Ex 1. Pet.2.Quidam lapidi angulari Christo impositi.
units.tr: From 1 Peter 2: Some are placed upon Christ, the cornerstone.

units.la: Ex Rom.14.1.Cor.8: Quidam pro quib. Christus efficaciter mortuus.
units.tr: From Romans 14 and 1 Corinthians 8: Some for whom Christ died effectively.

units.la: Ex 2. Pet.2. Quidam à Christo efficaciter redemti.
units.tr: From 2 Peter 2: Some are effectively redeemed by Christ.

units.la: Ex Heb.10. Quidam sanguine Christi sanctificati.
units.tr: From Hebrews 10: Some are sanctified by the blood of Christ.

units.la: Ex Joh.17. Quidam Christo à patre ab æterno dati, &c. Omnes falsæ.
units.tr: From John 17: Some were given to Christ by the Father from eternity, etc. All are false.

units.la: Ratio falsitatis: quia hæc beneficia sunt propria electorum teste apostolo. Rom.8. Quos prædestinavit, hos vocavit, justificavit, glorificavit, &c. Et ver.33. Quis accusabit electos Dei: Deus est qui justificat: Christus est qui mortuus est, &c. & Chri-sto: sto: Ioh. 10. Ego animam meam pono pro ovibus meis,&c.
units.tr: Reason for the falsity: because these benefits belong peculiarly to the elect, as the apostle testifies. Romans 8: Whom he predestined, these he also called, justified, glorified, etc. And verse 33: Who shall accuse God's elect? It is God who justifies; it is Christ who died, etc. And John 10: I lay down my life for my sheep, etc.

units.la: Exempla de maiore falsa:
units.tr: Examples of a false major:

units.la: Ex 1.Pet.1. Quidam finaliter obliviſcentes purgationis veterum peccatorum.
units.tr: From 1 Peter 1: Some who finally forget the cleansing of their former sins.

units.la: Ex Gal.3.&5.1.Cor.3. 6. quidam finaliter ex-cidentes gratia.
units.tr: From Galatians 3 and 5, 1 Corinthians 3 and 6: Some who finally fall away from grace.

units.la: Ex 2.Pet.2. quidam rursus implicati peccatis: & redeuntes ad vomitum ac volutabrum.
units.tr: From 2 Peter 2: Some who, again entangled in sins, return to the vomit and the wallowing.

units.la: Ex Hebr.6. Quidam denuo sibi Christum cru-cifigentes.
units.tr: From Hebrews 6: Some who crucify Christ afresh for themselves.

units.la: Ex 1.Ioh.5. quidam mendacem Deum facien-tes,&c.
units.tr: From 1 John 5: Some who make God a liar, etc.

units.la: Omnes falsæ, Ratio: quia redemti efficaciter, h.e, vere fideles & conversi talia peccata vel nun-quam vel non finaliter admittunt.
units.tr: All false. Reason: because those who are redeemed effectively, that is, truly faithful and converted, either never commit such sins or do not commit them finally.

units.la: Ioh.10. Ego ovibus meis do vitam aeternam.
units.tr: John 10: I give eternal life to my sheep.

units.la: Matth.24. Impossibile est seduci electos.
units.tr: Matthew 24: It is impossible for the elect to be led astray.

units.la: 1.Ioh.3. Qui natus est ex Deo non peccat, nec po-test peccare.
units.tr: 1 John 3: He who is born of God does not sin, nor can he sin.

units.la: Transitio ad tertiam classem de Absurdis.
units.tr: Transition to the third class, concerning the absurdities.

units.la: Responsio generalis: 1. per negationem minoris, quod ex nostra doctrina haec absurda neces-sario sequantur.
units.tr: General answer: 1. by denying the minor, that these absurdities necessarily follow from our doctrine.

units.la: Ratio: quia vera & Scripturæ consentanea est. Ex vero autem nil nisi verum sequitur.
units.tr: Reason: because our doctrine is true and agrees with Scripture. Nothing but what is true, however, follows from what is true.

units.la: II. per βίαιον[?]: Adversarii hypothesin falsam & absurdam esse.
units.tr: II. By [βίαιον]?: the adversary's hypothesis is false and absurd.

units.la: Ratio I. quia repugnet Scripturæ.
units.tr: Reason I: because it contradicts Scripture.

units.la: II. quia ex ea sequantur absurda, ut patet in
units.tr: II: because absurdities follow from it, as is clear in

units.la: [illegible, ~7 letters] Responsio specialis ad singula: formentur inte-gri syllogismi, ut melius appareat solutionum veritas.
units.tr: [illegible, ~7 letters] Special answer to each point: let complete syllogisms be formed, so that the truth of the solutions may appear more clearly.

units.la: AD PRIMUM absurdum. In dubium vocari totam Christianam religionem & fidem: Pro-batio adversarii Thesi 499. quia falsitatis argua-tur tota Scriptura.
units.tr: TO THE FIRST absurdity: that the whole Christian religion and faith is called into doubt. Proof by the adversary, Thesis 499: because the whole of Scripture is charged with falsehood.

units.la: (Fiat syllogismus: Falsitatis arguere totam Scripturam est totam religionem & fidem in dubium vocare.
units.tr: (Let the syllogism be formed: to charge the whole of Scripture with falsehood is to call the whole religion and faith into doubt.

units.la: Negare absolutam redemtionem omnium etiam infidelium est falsitatis arguere totam Scripturam. Ergo, &c.)
units.tr: To deny the absolute redemption of all, even of unbelievers, is to charge the whole of Scripture with falsehood. Therefore, etc.)

units.la: Respon. i. negatione minoris. Rationes breviter petantur ex confirmatione.
units.tr: Answer: 1. by denying the minor. Reasons are to be sought briefly from the confirmation.

units.la: 1. quia Scriptura beneficia mortis Christi vē-dicat solis credentibus. Ioh.3.
units.tr: 1. because Scripture claims the benefits of Christ's death for believers alone. John 3.

units.la: 2. Infideles canes & porcos diserte excludit, Ioh.3. Matth.7.
units.tr: 2. Scripture expressly excludes unbelievers as dogs and swine, John 3, Matthew 7.

units.la: 3. Vniversalitas promissionum Evangelii ad credentes pertinet. Act.10. vox omnium prophe-tarum, &c. quod conditio fidei & poenitentiae expressa vel subintellecta ostendit.
units.tr: 3. The universality of the promises of the Gospel pertains to believers. Acts 10; the voice of all the prophets, etc., which the condition of faith and repentance, either expressed or understood, shows.

units.la: II. per inversionem. Adversarii hypothesis evertit religionem:
units.tr: II. By inversion. The adversary's hypothesis overturns religion:

units.la: Ratio: quia canes & porcos in sinum & gratiam Dei collocando, atheismo portam aperit.
units.tr: Reason: because by placing dogs and swine in the bosom and grace of God, it opens the door to atheism.

units.la: AD SECUNDUM absurdum. Scripturam transformari in mendacissimum Alcoranum. Probatio adversarii: Thes. 276. 277.&c. quia sit Mahometica doctrina, Deum non velle omnes homines salvos facere & fieri.
units.tr: TO THE SECOND absurdity: that Scripture is transformed into the most lying Koran. Proof by the adversary: Theses 276, 277, etc., because it is the Mohammedan doctrine that God does not will all men to be saved and to become so.

units.la: Fiat Syllogismus: Docere Deum non velle omnes homines salvos facere & fieri, est Scripturam in Alcoranum convertere.
units.tr: Let the syllogism be formed: to teach that God does not will all men to be saved and to become so is to turn Scripture into the Koran.

units.la: Ratio: quia Alcoranus sic docet: Azoara 42. At negantes efficacem impiorum omnium redemtionem, negant Deum velle omnes homines salvos facere& fieri. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Reason: because the Koran teaches thus: Azoara 42. But those who deny the effective redemption of all the impious deny that God wills all men to be saved and to become so. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Respon. 1. per negationem minoris: quia docemus Deum velle omnes credentes & pios salvos facere: tantum negamus in Deo voluntatem servandi omnes infideles & impios, idque cum Scriptura. Psal. 5. ver. 5. 6. 7. Matth. 25. 41.
units.tr: Answer 1, by denying the minor: because we teach that God wills all believers and the pious to be saved; we only deny that there is in God a will to save all unbelievers and the impious, and this with Scripture. Psalm 5:5–7; Matthew 25:41.

units.la: Item[?]: quia non negamus Deum velle omnes homines salvos fieri, si quidem omnes crederent: Seu, quo ad approbationem, invitationem, & affectum erga creaturas, quo non laetatur ullius destructione, quatenus destructio est, Ezech. 18. 1. Tim. 2.
units.tr: Likewise: because we do not deny that God wills all men to be saved, if indeed all were to believe. Or, as regards approval, invitation, and affection toward creatures, by which he does not rejoice in the destruction of anyone, insofar as it is destruction: Ezekiel 18; 1 Timothy 2.

units.la: I I. negatione maioris, de voluntate efficiendi salutem in omnibus simpliciter.
units.tr: II. By denying the major, concerning the will to effect salvation simply in all.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia neque Scriptura neque Alcoranus docet, Deum velle omnes homines salvos facere.
units.tr: Reason 1: because neither Scripture nor the Koran teaches that God wills all men to be saved.

units.la: I I. Quia Deus non esset omnipotens, si vellet omnes salvos facere, nec tamen salvos faceret: idenim non faceret quia facere non posset per hominum malitiam: sic non esset omnipotens.
units.tr: II. Because God would not be omnipotent if he willed to save all and yet did not save them; for he would not do so because he could not do so on account of human malice, and thus he would not be omnipotent.

units.la: Adprobationem Maioris. 1. ne[?]gatione con-sequentiae: quia Scriptura non mox fit Alcora-nus, si hic cum illa in aliquo vero conveniat, ut Deum esse: mortuos resuscitandos, &c.
units.tr: As proof of the major. 1. By denying the consequence: because Scripture does not at once become the Koran if this agrees with it in some truth, such as that there is a God, that the dead are to be raised, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur hypothesi: adversarius non ideo vult esse Mahometanus: quia cum Mahometo credit: hominem esse animal: ter tria esse nove, &c.
units.tr: Let the hypothesis be amplified: the adversary does not for that reason wish to be a Mohammedan, because he believes with Mohammed that man is an animal, that three is a number, etc.

units.la: II. Fallacia accidentis: quia non propter Alcoranum, sed propter Scripturam credimus, Deum non omnes promiscue sed solos credentes velle salvare, sed omnes vero impios damna-re. Rom.9. Miseretur, quorum vult. Psal.2. Con-fringes eos in virga ferrea.
units.tr: II. The fallacy of accident: because we believe, not on account of the Koran but on account of Scripture, that God wills to save not all indiscriminately but only believers, and to condemn all the impious. Romans 9: He has mercy on whom he wills. Psalm 2: You shall break them with a rod of iron.

units.la: III. Negatur Alcoranum idem docere.
units.tr: III. It is denied that the Koran teaches the same.

units.la: 1. quia nihil habet de æterna prædestinatione electorum ad vitam in Christo, de qua Eph.1.
units.tr: 1. because it has nothing about the eternal predestination of the elect to life in Christ, of which Ephesians 1.

units.la: 2. Nec de fide in Christum, quam potius damnat.
units.tr: 2. Nor about faith in Christ, which it rather condemns.

units.la: 3. nec de redemtione fidelium à peccatis & morte per Christum, de qua Ioh.5.&c.
units.tr: 3. Nor about the redemption of the faithful from sins and death through Christ, of which John 5, etc.

units.la: 4. nec de patefactione misericordiæ Dei in servandis electis ex gratia, de qua Rom.9.
units.tr: 4. Nor about the manifestation of God's mercy in saving the elect by grace, of which Romans 9.

units.la: 5. nec de declaratione justitiæ Dei in damnandis impiis propter peccata: de qua ibidem. In hoc ipsum excitavi te ut in te ostendam potentiam meam.
units.tr: 5. Nor about the declaration of God's justice in condemning the impious for their sins, of which in the same place: For this very purpose I have raised you up, that I might show my power in you.

units.la: AD TERTIUM absurdum: Damnari Catholicam & veram Ecclesiam.
units.tr: TO THE THIRD absurdity: that the Catholic and true Church is condemned.

units.la: Probatio adversarii. Thes. 559. & Compend. 29: quia hæc semper uno ore professa sit: Christum pro omnibus hominibus mortuum esse.
units.tr: Proof by the opponent: Thes. 559 and Compend. 29, because the Church has always professed with one voice that Christ died for all men.

units.la: Respond. ad antecedens: Sententiam Ecclesiæ vel de sufficientia λύτρως, vel de omnibus fidelib. intelligendam esse.
units.tr: Reply to the antecedent: the judgment of the Church must be understood either of the sufficiency of the ransom, or of all the faithful.

units.la: Ratio: quia vera Ecclesia non dissentit à scri-ptura: cujus hanc esse sententiam ostensum est supra.
units.tr: Reason: because the true Church does not dissent from Scripture, whose judgment on this point has been shown above.

units.la: Præcisio: Examen authoritatum non esse hu-jus loci.
units.tr: Exclusion: an examination of authorities does not belong to this place.

units.la: Remittatur amicus ad lectionem Cyrilli in Joh.lib.ii.cap.19.
units.tr: Let my friend be referred to Cyril on John, book 2, chapter 19.

units.la: Augustini ad articulos: Ambrosii de vocatio-ne gen. Prosperi, Gregorii: Innocentii, Thomæ, &c.
units.tr: To Augustine on the articles; to Ambrose on the calling of the Gentiles; to Prosper, Gregory, Innocent, Thomas, etc.

units.la: AD QUARTUM absurdum: Homines adi-gi ad desperationem. Probatio adversarii Thes: 366:quia consolationem petere jubeantur ex pro-missionibus pure particularibus, quod declaratur syllogismo.
units.tr: TO THE FOURTH absurdity: that men are driven to despair. Proof by the opponent, Thes. 366: because they are bidden to seek consolation from promises that are purely particular, which is set out in a syllogism.

units.la: Respon. 1: Minor salsissima:
units.tr: Reply 1: the minor premise is most false.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia promissio Evangelii universalis est, non respectu omnium hominum, sed respectu omnium credentium: ut litera ipsa testatur.
units.tr: Reason 1: because the promise of the Gospel is universal, not with respect to all men, but with respect to all believers, as the very letter of the text bears witness.

units.la: II. Quia medium seu nervus consolationis non est; hominem esse, sed fideiem[?] esse.
units.tr: II. Because the means or sinew of consolation is not that a man is a man, but that he is a believer.

units.la: Declaretur: quod syllogismus consolatorius non sit iste: ut vult adversarius:
units.tr: Let it be made clear that the consoling syllogism is not this one, as the opponent maintains:

units.la: Pro omnibus hominibus Christus est mortuus:
units.tr: Christ died for all men.

units.la: Ego sum homo.
units.tr: I am a man.

units.la: Ergo pro me est mortuus. Sic enim Turca et-iam Turca manes cum sit homo, esset redemtus:
units.tr: Therefore he died for me. For in this way a Turk too, even though he remains a Turk, since he is a man, would be redeemed.

units.la: Sediste:
units.tr: Rather, the syllogism is this:

units.la: Pro omnibus credentibus Christus est mortuus efficaciâ: seu omnes credentes morte Christi servantur.
units.tr: Christ died efficaciously for all believers; or, all believers are saved by the death of Christ.

units.la: Ego credo in Christum.
units.tr: I believe in Christ.

units.la: Ergo pro me est mortuus efficaciâ & servabor.
units.tr: Therefore he died efficaciously for me, and I shall be saved.

units.la: II. per inversionem: Adversarius evertit co-solationem mortis Christi sua hypothesi.
units.tr: II. By inversion: the opponent overturns the consolation of Christ's death by his own hypothesis.

units.la: Ratio: quia docet, non omnes servari, pro qui-bus Christus est mortuus.
units.tr: Reason: because he teaches that not all are saved for whom Christ died.

units.la: Fiat syllogismus. Aliqui pro quibus est mortuus Christus servantur:
units.tr: Let the syllogism be made: some for whom Christ died are saved.

units.la: Pro me est mortuus.
units.tr: Christ died for me.

units.la: Ergo ego servabor.
units.tr: Therefore I shall be saved.

units.la: AD QUINTUM absurdum: Abrogari uni-versum Evangelium. Probatio adverf. Thes. 474. Quia docentes Christum pro solis electis mor-tuum, non possint omnibus annunciare gratiam Evangelii, cum non sint omnes electi.
units.tr: TO THE FIFTH absurdity: that the whole Gospel is abolished. Proof against Thes. 474: because those who teach that Christ died only for the elect cannot announce the grace of the Gospel to all, since not all are elect.

units.la: Respond. 1. Negatur minor: quia annun-ciant gratiam omnibus credentibus. Pro creden-tibus autem habere debent, judicio charitatis, o-mnes profitentes fidem & poenitentiam: proin-de etiam pro electis.
units.tr: Reply 1. The minor premise is denied, because they announce the grace to all believers. But for believers, by the judgment of charity, they ought to hold all who profess faith and repentance; therefore also the elect.

units.la: II. negatur major in qua est insufficiens e-numeratio.
units.tr: II. The major premise is denied, in which the enumeration is insufficient.

units.la: Ratio: quia manent nihilominus praecipuę[?] partes Evangelij, licet gratia non promittatur impiis.
units.tr: Reason: because the chief parts of the Gospel nevertheless remain, although grace is not promised to the impious.

units.la: I. Mandatum & invitatio omnium ad fidem. II. Promissio gratiae ad fideles pertinens. III. Comminatio adversus infideles.
units.tr: I. The command and invitation of all to faith. II. The promise of grace, pertaining to the faithful. III. The threat against the unbelieving.

units.la: AD SEXTUM absurdum: Tolli Baptismū:
units.tr: Sixth absurdity: that Baptism is abolished.

units.la: Probatio: quia baptizatis nulla certa possit promitti gratia & salus.
units.tr: Proof: because no certain grace and salvation can be promised to those who are baptized.

units.la: Respons. Negatur minor. Ratio 1. quia Eccle-sia omnes quos baptizat habet pro fidelibus, & his, quo ad se, certò obsignat gratiam: de occultis vero non judicat. 2. Non baptismum, sed tantum opinionem operis operati tolli per nostram doctrinam.
units.tr: Answer. The minor premise is denied. Reason (1): because the Church regards all whom it baptizes as believers, and to these, as far as it is concerned, it certainly seals grace; but it does not judge concerning hidden things. (2): It is not baptism that is abolished by our teaching, but only the opinion of the work done (operis operati).

units.la: AD SEPTIMUM absurdum: Tolli Cœnam. Thes.437.
units.tr: Seventh absurdity: that the Lord's Supper is abolished. Thes. 437.

units.la: Probatio: Quia corpus & sanguis Christi nulli certò possit exhiberi, nec ab ullo certò percipi.
units.tr: Proof: because the body and blood of Christ cannot be certainly offered to anyone, nor certainly received by anyone.

units.la: Resp. Negatur minor: Quia Ecclesia omnes communicantes habet pro fidelibus: quibus pro inde certo exhibet Christum: quantum ad se. Communicantes vero jubet se probare an sint in fide, &c.
units.tr: Answer. The minor premise is denied: because the Church regards all who communicate as believers, and to these it certainly offers Christ, as far as it is concerned. But it commands those who communicate to test themselves whether they are in the faith, etc.

units.la: AD OCTAVUM absurdum: Accusari Deum fraudis. Thes.318.
units.tr: Eighth absurdity: that God is charged with deceit. Thes. 318.

units.la: Probatio: quia aliud dicat, & aliud sentiat, omnes vocans nec tamen omnes venire & servare volens. Syllogismus cum prosyllogismo est manifestus.
units.tr: Reply 1. By denial of the minor premise: because those whom God calls, he wills all to come, and having come, to save. 1 Tim. 2; John 6.

units.la: Respond. 1. negatione minoris: quia quos Deus vocat omnes vult venire, & venientes servare. 1.Tim.2.Ioh.6.
units.tr: Answer. (1) By denying the minor premise: because God wills that all whom he calls should come, and should save those who come. 1 Tim. 2; John 6.

units.la: Ratio: quia omnium salute, nullius perditione delectatur. Nolo mortem, &c.
units.tr: Reason: because he delights in the salvation of all and in the perdition of no one. I do not desire the death, etc.

units.la: II.[?] Distinctione maioris: Si vocet absq; conditione fidei & poenitentiæ, sine qua Deus neminem neque vocat neque vult servare. Resipiscite & credite Evangelio: Qui non credit condemnabitur. Vult omnes ad agnitionem veritatis pervenire.
units.tr: (2) By distinguishing the major premise: if he calls without the condition of faith and repentance, without which God neither calls nor wills to save anyone. Repent and believe the Gospel; he who does not believe shall be condemned. He wills that all come to the knowledge of the truth.

units.la: AD NONUM absurdum: Accusari Deum mendacii. Probatio: quia verbis promittat, quod non det nec[?] dare decreverit.
units.tr: Reply. The minor premise is denied. 1. Because he gives eternal life, and has decreed to give it, to all to whom he also promises it, namely believers. He who believes in me has eternal life.

units.la: Respond. Negatur minor. I. quia vitam aeternam dat & dare decrevit omnibus, quibus etiam promittit, nempe credentibus. Qui credit in me habet vitam aeternam.
units.tr: II. Because he has nowhere promised that he will give faith and repentance even to all the reprobate. He has mercy on whom he wills. It has been given to you to know, etc.; not to the rest.

units.la: II. quia fidem & poenitentiam omnibus etiam reprobis se daturum nusquam promisit. Miseretur quorum vult. Vobis datum est nosse, &c. reliquis non.
units.tr: TO THE TENTH absurdity: that Christ is accused of having deluded God with a false suffering and men with a false Gospel.

units.la: AD DECIMUM absurdum: Christum accusari quod falsa passione Deum, & falso Evangelio homines deluserit.
units.tr: Proof: that as to God: because, contrary to God's decree and command that he should die only for a few, he died for all. That as to men: because he says and promises something other than what he has done and performs, namely that he died for all, when he died only for a few.

units.la: Probatio: quòd Deum: quia contra Dei decretum & mandatum ut moreretur tantum pro paucis, sit mortuus pro omnibus. Quod homines: quia dicat & promittat aliud, quàm fecit & praestat, se videlicet mortuum pro omnibus cum sit mortuus tantum pro paucis.
units.tr: Proof that God [does so]: because, contrary to the decree and command of God that he should die only for a few, he has died for all. [Proof] that men [do so]: because they say and promise something other than what he has done and performs, namely that he died for all, when he died only for a few.

units.la: Responsio figuretur detestatione tam petulantis sophisticae: & ostendat pugnantiam, quod prior probatio sumat, altera neget, Christum mortuum esse pro omnibus.
units.tr: Answer: let it be met with a denunciation of such impudent sophistry, and let it show the contradiction, that the former proof assumes and the other denies that Christ died for all.

units.la: Deinde negetur minor in utraque.
units.tr: Then let the minor premise be denied in both.

units.la: Probetur negatio prioris: quia & factum & doctrina Christi congruit cum decreto & mandato Dei, ut moreretur sufficientia quidem λύτρον[?] pro omnibus: efficacia vero pro solis credentibus. Haec est voluntas eius qui misit me, &c. Ego ovibus meis do vitam aeternam. Non oro pro mundo, sed pro his, &c.
units.tr: Let the denial of the former be proved: because both the deed and the doctrine of Christ agree with the decree and command of God, that he should indeed die as a sufficient ransom (lytron) for all, but as an efficacious one only for believers. This is the will of him who sent me, etc. I give eternal life to my sheep. I do not pray for the world, but for those, etc.

units.la: Posterioris I. quia reprobis & incredulis nihil promittat. ii. quia tàm mortem quàm intercessionem suam vendicet solis electis credentibus. Pro eis me sanctifico.
units.tr: TO THE ELEVENTH absurdity: that God is accused of cruelty. Thef. 299. Proof, scattered throughout: because he has predestined the greater part of mankind to death.

units.la: AD UNDECIMUM absurdum: Accusari Deum crudelitatis. Thef. 299. Probatio passim inspersa: quia majorem partem hominum praedestinavit ad mortem.
units.tr: Eleventh absurdity: that God is charged with cruelty. Thes. 299. Proof, scattered throughout: because he has predestined the greater part of mankind to death.

units.la: Respond. 1. rejectione argumenti alieni ab instituto.
units.tr: Answer. (1) By rejecting an argument foreign to the subject.

units.la: ii. negatione majoris de Deo: Ratio à mero Dei jure in creaturas. Poterat adversarium nō creare hominem, scil. asinum sine injustitia. Fi-guretur exclamatione Paulina: O homo tu quis es? & similitudine: Nonne figulus habet potestatem, &c.
units.tr: (2) By denying the major premise concerning God: the reason is from God's mere right over creatures. He could have not created a man, namely an ass, without injustice to the adversary. Let it be illustrated by the Pauline exclamation: O man, who are you? and by the comparison: Has not the potter power, etc.?

units.la: iii. Per distinctionem majoris: Si destinet exitio sine justa causa: quod Deus non fecit: quia ut neminem damnat: ita neminem damna-re decrevit seu ad damnationem ordinavit nisi propter peccatum.
units.tr: (3) By distinguishing the major premise: if he destined them to destruction without a just cause, which God does not do; because just as he condemns no one, so he has not decreed, or ordained to damnation, anyone except on account of sin.

units.la: Instantia 1. Deus decrevit reproborum non misereri. Ergo crudelis.
units.tr: Instance (1): God has decided not to show mercy to the reprobate. Therefore he is cruel.

units.la: Respon. Addatur major & distinguatur: crude-lem esse, qui non miseretur omnium.
units.tr: 1. if he is bound to have mercy on all.

units.la: 1. si teneatur omnium misereri.
units.tr: (1) If he were bound to show mercy to all.

units.la: ii. nisi gloria summi boni requirat miseri-cordiæ & justitiæ temperamentum.
units.tr: (2) Unless the glory of the supreme good requires a tempering of mercy with justice.

units.la: Utrumque applicetur ad Deum, & ostendatur ex dictis: Quis prior dedit ei? nonne licet mihi de meo facere, &c. Miserer cuius misereor: Volens ostendere iram, & notas facere divitias, &c. Instant 2. Etiam qui suæ tantum gloriæ causa multos reprobat, crudelem videri.
units.tr: Let both be applied to God, and let it be shown from what has been said: Who first gave to him? Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with my own, etc.? I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy. Willing to show wrath and to make known his riches, etc. Instance (2): Even he who reprobates many for the sake of his own glory alone seems cruel.

units.la: Resp. 1. per negationem majoris de Deo.
units.tr: Answer. (1) By denying the major premise concerning God.

units.la: Ratio: quia sit summum bonum, cujus gloriæ omnium creaturarum destructio servire cogitur. Prov. 16. Omnia propter seipsum fecit, &c.
units.tr: Reason: because he is the supreme good, to whose glory the destruction of all creatures is compelled to serve. Prov. 16. The Lord has made all things for himself, etc.

units.la: Item: Si reprobet insontes, At omnes reprobi natura sunt filii iræ, sicut & cæteri.
units.tr: Likewise: if he reprobates the innocent. But all the reprobate are by nature children of wrath, as are the rest.

units.la: AD DUODECIMUM absurdum: Accusari DEUM Θπχαρεκτικίας[?] Thes. 291. Prob. quia prædestinat creaturas suas ad mortem. Resp. per distinctionem majoris: Θπχαρεκτικὸν[?] esse, qui destinat ad mortem. 1. quatenus est mors seu destructio. 2. nulla interveniente reproborum culpa. Sed Deum propter peccata destinasse damnationi quatenus executio est ejus justitiæ, Rom. 9. Volens ostendere.
units.tr: Twelfth absurdity: that God is charged with hypocharectia (tyranny). Thes. 291. Proof: because he predestines his creatures to death. Answer: by distinguishing the major premise: he is hypocharectikon who destines to death, (1) insofar as it is death or destruction; (2) with no intervening fault of the reprobate. But God has destined them to damnation on account of sins, insofar as the execution is an exercise of his justice, Rom. 9. Willing to show.

units.la: AD DECIMUMTERTIUM absurdum: Accusari Deum προσωπολημψίας[?] & injustitiæ Thes. 292. Prob. quia det æqualibus inæqualia.
units.tr: Thirteenth absurdity: that God is charged with partiality (prosopolempsia) and injustice. Thes. 292. Proof: because he gives unequal things to equals.

units.la: Respond. ad maiorem per distinctionem: Injustus est, qui dat æqualibus inæqualia:
units.tr: Reply to the major premise by a distinction: the unjust person is one who gives unequal things to equals.

units.la: 1. propter προσωπ[?], quæ spectant iniqui judices.
units.tr: 1. On account of προσωπ[?] (respect of persons), which concerns unjust judges.

units.la: II. obligatus lege ad dandum æqualia.
units.tr: II. Being bound by law to give equal things.

units.la: Ostendatur neutrum in Deum cadere.
units.tr: Let it be shown that neither of these falls upon God.

units.la: 1. quia in nullis invenit causam favoris: Cum essemus inimici, &c.
units.tr: 1. Because he finds in no one a cause of favour: "When we were enemies, etc."

units.la: II. quia nulli obligatur, Quis prior dedit, ei? An non licet, &c.
units.tr: II. Because he is under obligation to no one: "Who has first given to him? Or is it not lawful, etc."

units.la: Amplificetur simili largientis inæqualem eleemosynam æqualib. mendicis sine injustitia.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by the similar case of one who bestows an unequal alms on equal beggars without injustice.

units.la: Conclusio.
units.tr: Conclusion.
