units.la: Hæc si amicus recte meditetur, sperare te, eum adversarii strophas & calumnias nihil moraturû. Addatur ἐπιδιώξις[?]: quatuor postrema absurda tantum esse convitia responsione indigna.
units.tr: If a friend meditates on these things rightly, you may hope that the adversary's strophes and calumnies will not hold him back. Let the ἐπιδιώξις [?] be added: that the last four absurdities are only insults, unworthy of an answer.

units.la: Excusetur prolixitas 1. quia disputationis amplitudo te breviorem esse non permiserit.
units.tr: Let the length be excused: 1. because the breadth of the disputation would not have allowed it to be shorter;

units.la: II. quia ipse ad singula ἀνασκευαστικῶς[?] postula-verit.
units.tr: II. because he himself demanded a refutation ἀνασκευαστικῶς [?] of each point.

units.la: Petitio: ne moveatur impudentia adversarii:
units.tr: Petition: that the adversary's impudence not be allowed to disturb you.

units.la: Consilium: Clamoribus & calumniis ejus doctrinam fidei & pœnitentiæ Evangelii propriam constanter opponat.
units.tr: Counsel: Let him constantly set against his clamours and calumnies the doctrine of faith and of the repentance of the Gospel, which is proper to it.

units.la: Exercitatio XXI I.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXII.

units.la: Paraphrasis historiæ de Altari exstructo à Rubenitis ad Iordanem Iosuæ 22. scribatur phrasi latina.
units.tr: Paraphrase of the history of the altar erected by the Reubenites beside the Jordan, Joshua 22, to be written in Latin phrase.

units.la: Narretur 1. dimissio duarum & dimidiæ tribuum post occupatam Cananæam: & oratio Iosuæ, primo collaudantis obedientiam & operam fratribus præstitam: secundo permittentis reditum in Gileaditidem: tertio exhortantis ad Legis & cultus divini observantiam. quarto Benedicentis ac munera dantis ex præda discedentibus.
units.tr: Let there be told: (1) the dismissal of two and a half tribes after the conquest of Canaan; and the speech of Joshua, (first) commending the obedience and service rendered by their brothers, (second) permitting their return to Gilead, (third) exhorting them to observe the Law and the worship of God, (fourth) blessing them and giving gifts from the spoil to those who depart.

units.la: II. Exstructio altaris in Gileaditide ad Iordanem: & sinistra fama de Altari ad Israëlitas in Cananæam perlata,& eorum Zelus.
units.tr: II. The erection of the altar in Gilead beside the Jordan, and the ill report about the altar carried to the Israelites in Canaan, and their zeal.

units.la: III. Legatio Israëlitarum ad Rubenitas, & Oratio Pinchæ I. reprehendentis factum duobus argumentis: quia videantur Apostatæ à Deo: & attracturi sint sibi ac toti cœtui novas pœnas, exemplo majorum colentium Peorem. Num.25: & Achanis rapientis quædam ex anathemate. Ios.7. 2. Invitantis eos ad transitum in Cananæam, si displiceat Gileaditis: adhibita obsecratione, ne faciant Schisma.
units.tr: III. The embassy of the Israelites to the Reubenites, and the speech of Phinehas, who first rebukes the deed on two grounds: because they seem to have apostatized from God, and because they will bring upon themselves and the whole assembly new punishments, after the example of their forefathers who worshipped Peor (Num. 25), and of Achan, who took some of the devoted things (Josh. 7). (2) He invites them to cross over into Canaan, if Gilead displeases them, and with entreaty asks them not to create a schism.

units.la: IV. Defensio Rubenitarum & sociorum: qua 1. se purgant interposito gravi jurejurando, à suspicione apostasiæ: ratione ducta à non causa exstructi altaris, ut in eo sacrificarent, relicto altari Jehovæ. 2. Exponunt causam ædificati altaris per inversionem: ut esset symbolum consensus & unionis in religione cum ipsis: addita confirmatione per ἐκθεσιν periculi exclusionis sui ab Ecclesia apud posteros, ob interluentem inter utrosque Jordanem: & evitationis periculi per hoc altare. 3. Protestantur de sua innocentia, consensu, & constantia in vero cultu.
units.tr: IV. The defence of the Reubenites and their companions, in which (1) they clear themselves, under a solemn oath, of the suspicion of apostasy, on the ground that the altar was not built for sacrificing upon it in place of the altar of Jehovah. (2) They set out the cause of the altar's building by inversion: that it might be a symbol of consent and union with them in religion; and they add a confirmation by ekthesis [ἔκθεσις] of the danger that they and their posterity would be cut off from the Church, because of the Jordan flowing between the two sides, and of the means of avoiding that danger through this altar. (3) They protest their innocence, their agreement, and their constancy in the true worship.

units.la: V. Legatorum reditus: populi gratulatio, mutatio consilii de bello: nomen altari inditum: ad cavendum ejus abusum apud posteros.
units.tr: V. The return of the envoys; the people's rejoicing; the change of plan about war; the name given to the altar, to guard against its abuse among posterity.

units.la: Exercitatio XXIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXIII.

units.la: An Rubenita cum sociis recte fecerint exstruentes altare trophæum ad Jordanem. Ios.22.
units.tr: Whether the Reubenites with their companions did rightly in erecting the altar as a trophy at the Jordan. Joshua 22.

units.la: EXordium à thesi: Laudanda modestia eorum, qui non quævis facta etiam piorum simpliciter laudant vel vituperant.
units.tr: The introduction from the thesis: the restraint of those is to be praised who do not simply praise or blame every deed, even of the pious.

units.la: Ratio: quia multa per se bona vel indifferentia circumstantiis fiunt mala.
units.tr: Reason: because many things good in themselves, or indifferent, become evil through their circumstances.

units.la: Hypothesis sit propositio: Tale est factum Rubenitarum exstruentium altare trophæum ad Jordanem.
units.tr: Hypothesis is the proposition: such is the deed of the Reubenites in erecting the altar as a trophy at the Jordan.

units.la: Confirmatio approbationis:
units.tr: Confirmation of approval:

units.la: I. A genere: quia trophæa victoriæ statuere est laudabile.
units.tr: I. From the genus: because to set up a trophy of victory is praiseworthy.

units.la: Amplificetur ab effectu (celebratio Dei: Deus & memoria virtutis) & exemplis laudatis.
units.tr: It is amplified from the effect (the celebration of God: God and the memory of virtue) and from the examples praised.

units.la: II. A fine: quia fuit bonus, ut esset symbolum unionis cum Israelitis in religione & in politia.
units.tr: II. From the end: because it was good, in that it was to be a sign of union with the Israelites in religion and in polity.

units.la: Amplificetur à causa impulsiva, seu periculo posteritatis, quæ aliquando videri poterat excludi ex Canaanea propter interluentem amnem Jordanis.
units.tr: It is amplified from the impulsive cause, namely the danger to posterity, which at some time could seem to be excluded from the land of Canaan on account of the river Jordan flowing between.

units.la: Confirmatio reprehensionis.
units.tr: Confirmation of blame.

units.la: I. A forma: Exstruunt altare contra legem, Exod.20. Deut.12, Lev.17.
units.tr: I. From the form: they erect an altar contrary to the law, Exodus 20, Deuteronomy 12, Leviticus 17.

units.la: Amplif. à caulis unitatis altaris à Deo præcepti: quæ erant: conservatio cultus instituti: Vitatio schismatum & scandalorum: & typus Christi.
units.tr: Amplification from the causes of the unity of the altar, which God commanded: these were the preservation of the instituted worship, the avoiding of schisms and offences, and the type of Christ.

units.la: 2. A modo facti: quia inconsulto summo Pontifice & fratribus rem novam & scandali plenam faciunt.
units.tr: 2. From the manner of the deed: because they do a new thing, full of offence, without consulting the high priest and the brethren.

units.la: 3. fit [illegible, ~7 letters] prioris: ab effectis.
units.tr: 3. [illegible, ~7 letters] of the former: from the effects.

units.la: 1. Reddunt se suspectos de apostasia à Deo & vero cultu: quod ostenditur ex oratione Pinchæ.
units.tr: 1. They make themselves suspect of apostasy from God and the true worship; this is shown from the prayer of Phinehas.

units.la: 1. Relicturi erant posteris scandalum: & materiam idololatriæ. Amplif.ab astutia Satanæ: & vanitate ingenii humani: quibus etiam bona in-stituta, inedum speciem vel occasionem Idolo-latriæ præbentia in abusum rapiuntur.
units.tr: 1. They were going to leave to posterity an offence and matter for idolatry. Amplification from the cunning of Satan and the vanity of the human mind, by which even good institutions, which offer even the appearance or occasion of idolatry, are seized and turned to abuse.

units.la: 3. Accersunt sibi justum & periculosum bel-lum a fratribus justo zelo gloriæ Dei ardentib.
units.tr: 3. They bring upon themselves a just and dangerous war from brethren burning with a just zeal for the glory of God.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Ædificarunt non ad immolan-dum.
units.tr: Objection 1. They built, not in order to sacrifice.

units.la: Resp. 1. Videbantur ideo ædificasse: tacentes institutum suum. Fugite omnem speciem mali.
units.tr: Answer 1. They seemed to have built for that purpose, by keeping silent about their intention. Flee every appearance of evil.

units.la: 2. Periculum erat posteris.
units.tr: 2. There was danger to posterity.

units.la: 3. Tutius alia forma ædificassent.
units.tr: 3. They could have built in some other form more safely.

units.la: Instantia: Cavent abusum inscriptione, Resp. Sibi, sed non posteris.
units.tr: Instance: They guard against abuse by the inscription. Answer: for themselves, but not for posterity.

units.la: Obiect. II. Non jubentur diruere.
units.tr: Objection II. They were not commanded to tear it down.

units.la: Resp. Non factis sed legib. est iudicandum.
units.tr: Answer: Things are to be judged not by deeds but by laws.

units.la: Obiectio III. Etiam Jacobus exstruxit alta-ria. Gen.28.&31.
units.tr: Objection III. Jacob also erected altars. Genesis 28 and 31.

units.la: Resp. 1. Sed ante legem.
units.tr: Answer 1. But before the law.

units.la: II. Instinctu divino seu spiritu prophetico.
units.tr: II. By divine impulse, or by the prophetic Spirit.

units.la: III. Alia fuerunt temporaria, alia μνημόσυνα aut limites,
units.tr: III. Some were temporary, others were memorials or boundary marks.

units.la: Conclusio: Bonam intentionem in causa reli-gionis sine verbo Dei non excusare quævis fa-cta: & plerunque male cedere.
units.tr: Conclusion: A good intention in a matter of religion does not excuse any deed done without the Word of God, and for the most part it turns out badly.

units.la: Exercitatio XXIV.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXIV.

units.la: Ad petitoriam amici De Exorcismo
units.tr: On the Exorcism: Reply to a Friend's Request

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Response.

units.la: Exordium figuratum ἀνθυποφορᾶς[?] à causis, cuĭ de controversia Exorcismi aliena ab Eccle-siis & Scholis nostris ad ipsum scribas. I. quia ipse petierit. II. quia vivat iis locis, ubi nunc propter eam turbantur Ecclesiæ. III. quia etiam huc apportentur libelli va-rii defendentes Exorcismum.
units.tr: A figured exordium, drawn from the causes, in which I write to him about the controversy over exorcism, a matter foreign to our Churches and Schools. I. Because he himself asked for it. II. Because he lives in those places where the Churches are now troubled over it. III. Because various pamphlets defending exorcism are also brought here.

units.la: NARRATIO sit descriptio Exorcismi, quod sit Ceremonia ante baptismum infantum certis verbis & characteribus adiurandi malum daemonem, ut Spiritui sancto cedat sua possessione & iure in baptizandis.
units.tr: NARRATIO: a description of exorcism, which is a ceremony before the baptism of infants, in which the evil demon is adjured with certain words and signs, so that he may yield his possession and his right over those to be baptized to the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Addatur ἐκθεσις[?] totius ritus per partes.
units.tr: The exposition of the whole rite, part by part, is to be added.

units.la: I. Exorcista imperat daemoni, ut exeat, & locum det Spiritui sancto.
units.tr: I. The exorcist commands the demon to depart and to give place to the Holy Spirit.

units.la: II. Frontem & pectus baptizandi signat cruce.
units.tr: II. He marks the forehead and breast of the one to be baptized with the cross.

units.la: III. Gemina precatiuncula Deum orat, ut hunc servum suum suscipiat.
units.tr: III. He prays to God in a twofold little prayer that He would receive this His servant.

units.la: IV. Adjurat Spiritum immundum in nomine Patris Filii & Spiritus sancti, ut exeat ab hoc servo Jesu Christi.
units.tr: IV. He adjures the unclean spirit, in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, to depart from this servant of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Transitio ad partitionem: De hoc ritu, cum sic petat, te breviter explicaturum: I. Quæ sit exorcistarum sententia. II. Quid de ea tibi videatur. III. Ad exorcistarum rationes responsurum.
units.tr: Transition to the division: since he asks it, I shall briefly explain this rite: I. What the opinion of the exorcists is. II. What I think of it. III. I shall answer the exorcists' arguments.

units.la: Sequatur ἐξήγησις[?] partitionis: & primo sententia Exorcistarum ex eorum libellis distributa in propositiones veras & falsas.
units.tr: Let the explanation of the division follow: and first, the opinion of the exorcists, drawn from their pamphlets and divided into true and false propositions.

units.la: Enumerentur propositiones Exorcistarum ve-ræ cum approbatione: I. Quod Exorcismus non sit de substantia Baptismi. Muller.Thes.38.
units.tr: Let the true propositions of the exorcists be listed, with approval: I. That exorcism is not of the substance of baptism. Muller, Thes. 38.

units.la: Approbetur ratione: quia non est à Christo institutus. II. Quod Exorcismus non sit pars baptismi. Muller.Thes.38.
units.tr: Let it be approved by reason: because it was not instituted by Christ. II. That exorcism is not a part of baptism. Muller, Thes. 38.

units.la: Approbatio: quia Ecclesiæ Apostolicæ habuerunt, & nostræ habent Baptismum integrum sine Exorcismo. III. Quod Exorcismus non sit ceremonia necessaria. Muller.ibid.
units.tr: Approval: because the apostolic Churches had, and our Churches have, complete baptism without exorcism. III. That exorcism is not a necessary ceremony. Muller, ibid.

units.la: Approbetur iisdem rationibus: quia & olim non fuit, & hodie passim non est, salvo Baptismo. IV. Quod Exorcismus non debeat instaurari ubi est abrogatus. Muller.Thes.37.
units.tr: Let it be approved by the same reasons: because it was not so in former times either, and today it is commonly not so, with baptism remaining intact. IV. That exorcism ought not to be restored where it has been abolished. Muller, Thes. 37.

units.la: Ratio ipsorum: quia instauratio fieret cum scandalo rudiorum, quasi non essent rite baptizati.
units.tr: Their reason: because a restoration would cause offence to the less instructed, as if they had not been rightly baptized.

units.la: Addatur alia gravior: quia Baptismus non sit denuo polluendus ceremonia superstitiosa & magica, qualem esse exorcismum postea ostendetur.
units.tr: Another, weightier reason is to be added: because baptism must not be polluted again by a superstitious and magical ceremony, which exorcism will afterwards be shown to be.

units.la: v. Quod Exorcismus debeat abrogari, sicubi accesserit vel accedat abusus. Muller. Thef. 39.
units.tr: V. That exorcism ought to be abolished wherever abuse has crept in or is creeping in. Muller, Thef. 39.

units.la: TRANSITIO ad propositiones controversas, quas praecipuè tuentur Exorcistæ in suis libellis:
units.tr: TRANSITION to the controverted propositions, which the exorcists chiefly defend in their pamphlets:

units.la: I. Quod Exorcismus non fit suo genere impius:
units.tr: I. That exorcism is not in its own kind impious:

units.la: Ratio Leyseri: quia neque cum Decalogo, neque cum symbolo, neque cum oratione Dominica, neque cum doctrina Sacramentorum pugnat
units.tr: Reason of Leyser: because it is in conflict neither with the Decalogue, nor with the Creed, nor with the Lord's Prayer, nor with the doctrine of the sacraments.

units.la: II. Quod Exorcismus fit ἀλλοφύλος[?]. Muller. Thef. ss.
units.tr: II. That exorcism is adiaphorous. Muller, Thef. ss.

units.la: Argumentum commune omnib. quia nec præceptus nec prohibitus, sed ab Ecclesia significationis causa institutus est.
units.tr: Argument common to all: because it is neither commanded nor forbidden, but was instituted by the Church for the sake of signification.

units.la: Breviter declaratur significatio: infantes spiritualiter à Diabolo obstrictos esse, & ab ejus potestate liberari per Baptismum.
units.tr: The signification is briefly explained: that infants are spiritually bound by the Devil, and are freed from his power through baptism.

units.la: III. Quod Exorcismus fit utilis & retinendus ubi viget.
units.tr: III. That exorcism is useful and ought to be retained where it flourishes.

units.la: Ratio I. Heshusii: quia formula Exorcismi: Adjuvote, &c. est quædam expositio verborum Baptismi in eis comprehensa. Baptizo te. I. testor te esse impurum Satanæ mancipium, & hoc lavacro purgari in domicilium Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: First reason of Heshusius: because the formula of exorcism, Adjuvote, etc., is a certain exposition of the words of baptism contained in them. I baptize you. I. I testify that you are an unclean slave of Satan, and that by this washing you are purged to become a dwelling of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Ratio II. Heshusii. Est aperta testificatio de usu & efficacia Baptismi, quod infantes liberentur à tyrannide Diaboli, & regenerentur.
units.tr: Second reason of Heshusius: it is a plain testimony concerning the use and efficacy of baptism, that infants are freed from the tyranny of the Devil and are regenerated.

units.la: Addatur maior: Vtile esse, rudibus externa ce[?]a ceremonia commendare vim Sacramenti. Et amplificetur à contrario : Abrogatione exorcismi minui dignitatem ac virtutem Baptismi.
units.tr: Add the major premise: it is useful to commend the power of the sacrament to the unlearned by external ceremonies. And amplify it from the contrary: by the abolition of exorcism the dignity and virtue of baptism are diminished.

units.la: Ratio III. Mulleri Thes. 57. Est confessio de infantum miseria, quod sint obsessi spiritua-liter.
units.tr: Third reason of Muller, Thes. 57. It is a confession of the misery of infants, that they are spiritually possessed.

units.la: Amplificetur, Usurpatione exorcismi exag-gerari: abrogatione minui vim & deformitatem peccati originis.
units.tr: Amplify: by the use of exorcism this is exaggerated; by its abolition the power and the gravity of original sin are diminished.

units.la: Ratio IV. Heshusii & Mulleri Thes. quin-quag.tert. Potestas exorcizandi Ecclesiæ à Chri-sto est concessa & data. Marc. 16. In nomine meo, eucient daemonia. Ergo libere ea uti po-test:
units.tr: Fourth reason of Heshusius and Muller, Thes. 53. The power of exorcizing has been granted and given by Christ to the Church. Mark 16: In my name they shall cast out demons. Therefore it can freely use it.

units.la: Ratio V. quia abrogatio offenderet infirmos, ac dubios redderet, an sint legitime baptizati cū exorcismo.
units.tr: Fifth reason: because abolition would offend the weak and make doubtful whether those baptized with exorcism have been lawfully baptized.

units.la: Ratio VI. Ab authoritate veterum, Tertulliani, Cypriani, Nazianzeni, Augustini, Optati Milevitani, qui exorcismum approbarunt, & usurparunt in Baptismo.
units.tr: Sixth reason: from the authority of the ancients, Tertullian, Cyprian, Nazianzen, Augustine, Optatus of Milevis, who approved exorcism and used it in baptism.

units.la: TRANSITIO ad explicationem tuæ sen-tentiæ.
units.tr: TRANSITION to the explanation of your opinion.

units.la: Propositio: Exorcismus non est conjun-gendus Baptismo, nec ferendus sed abrogandus in Ecclesia Christiana.
units.tr: Proposition: Exorcism is not to be joined to baptism, nor is it to be tolerated, but it is to be abolished in the Christian Church.

units.la: Confirmatio.
units.tr: Confirmation.

units.la: Ratio I. quia non est institutus nec Bapti-smo adjunctus à Christo, cujus solus fuit instiinstituere ritus Sacramentales, qualis fingitur esse Exorcismus; quod probetur. 1. ex Lombar. d.6.l.4. 2. ex eo quod ei significationem Sacramentalem tribuunt.
units.tr: Reason I: because it was not instituted by Christ, nor joined to baptism by Him, whose alone it was to institute sacramental rites, of which kind exorcism is feigned to be; which is to be proved: 1. from Lombard, d. 6, l. 4; 2. from the fact that they ascribe a sacramental signification to it.

units.la: Amplificetur maior ab authoritate & Sapientia Christi: Minor ab eorum confessione, quod non sit pars Baptismi, nec necessarius.
units.tr: Amplify the major premise from the authority and wisdom of Christ; the minor from their own confession, that it is not a part of baptism, nor necessary.

units.la: Ratio II. Quia Apostoli neque conjunxerunt cum Baptismo, neque alias usurparunt, licet pollerent facultate ejiciendi daemonia.
units.tr: Reason II: because the apostles neither joined it to baptism nor otherwise used it, although they had the power of casting out demons.

units.la: Amplific. 1 a religione & simplicitate Ecclesiae primitivae, servantis ritus institutos, sine pompa, superstitione, & addirione, totos 200. annos 2. a maiori: nec quidem χάρισμα a Christo acceptum admiscuit Sacramento.
units.tr: Amplify: 1. from the religion and simplicity of the primitive Church, which kept the rites instituted by Christ without pomp, superstition or addition, for the whole 200 years; 2. from the greater argument: it did not even mingle with the sacrament the gift (charisma) received from Christ.

units.la: Addatur Noema: Haud dubie Ecclesiam tanto esse puriorem, quanto ad formam Apostolicam accedat propius.
units.tr: Add the maxim: Without doubt the Church is so much purer as it comes nearer to the apostolic form.

units.la: Ratio III. Major pars reformatarum Ecclesiarum nostri temporis Baptismum sine exorcismo recte administrat.
units.tr: Reason III: the greater part of the reformed Churches of our time administer baptism rightly without exorcism.

units.la: Probatio 1. exemplo Christi & Apostolorum. 2. Ipsorum confessione.
units.tr: Proof: 1. by the example of Christ and the apostles; 2. by their own confession.

units.la: Recte ergo has aliae imitarentur, propter conformitatem in doctrina & ritibus Sacramentalibus.
units.tr: Therefore these others would rightly imitate them, on account of the agreement in doctrine and sacramental rites.

units.la: Ratio IV. Baptismus Christi sanctissimus non est deformandus nec polluendus Ceremoniis humanis, otiosis & superfluis, vanis, ludicris, mendacibus, Ecclesiam deformantibus, denique superstitiosis, magicis & suo genere impiis.
units.tr: Reason IV: the most holy baptism of Christ is not to be disfigured or polluted by human ceremonies that are idle, superfluous, vain, ludicrous, deceptive, disfiguring the Church, and finally superstitious, magical and impious in their own kind.

units.la: Ordine ostendatur, talem Ceremoniam esse exorcismum. 1. Quod
units.tr: Let it be shown in order that exorcism is such a ceremony. 1. That

units.la: 1. Quod Humana: quia ipsi fateantur esse ritum humanum.
units.tr: 1. That it is human: because they themselves confess it is a human rite.

units.la: Occupatio. Etsi de prima origine & authore Exorcismi non satis constet: tamen videri post tempora Cypriani assutum Baptismo per κακο-ζηλίαν superstitiosorum Episcoporum, arrogantium sibi χάεσμα, quod jam desierat.
units.tr: Occupation. Although the first origin and author of exorcism is not sufficiently certain, yet it appears to have been attached to baptism after the time of Cyprian, through the ill zeal of superstitious bishops who arrogated to themselves a charisma that had already ceased.

units.la: 1. Ne Ecclesia postera videretur Apostolica inferior.
units.tr: 1. So that the later Church might not seem inferior to the apostolic one.

units.la: 2. Vt in admiratione essent vulgo.
units.tr: 2. So that they might be objects of wonder to the common people.

units.la: 3. ut effectum Baptismi efferrent: Vnde tandem opinio de necessitate & opere operato orta est.
units.tr: 3. So that they might magnify the effect of baptism: whence at last the opinion of necessity and of the work wrought (opus operatum) arose.

units.la: II. Quod ociosa & superflua.
units.tr: II. That it is idle and superfluous.

units.la: 1. quia ad Baptismum non pertinet. Ostendatur remotione à partibus: Ceremonia & promissione, quas integras Christus Ecclesiæ tradidit, Apostoli usurparunt sine exorcismo.
units.tr: 1. Because it does not belong to Baptism. This is shown by the removal of its parts: the ceremony and the promise, which Christ handed over to the Church whole, the Apostles used without exorcism.

units.la: 2. quia ad Baptismum nihil facit. Enumerentur & rejiciantur modi, quibus ad eum aliquid facere fingitur.
units.tr: 2. Because it does nothing for Baptism. The modes by which it is imagined to contribute anything to Baptism are listed and rejected.

units.la: Non ad amplificandum: quia non deficit partibus vel partium integritate.
units.tr: Not to enlarge it: because it lacks nothing in its parts or in the integrity of its parts.

units.la: Non ad aliquid significandum, quia significatio ritus à Christo institui, sufficit.
units.tr: Not to signify something, because the signification of the rite, instituted by Christ, is sufficient.

units.la: Non ad illustrandum: quia & ceremonia & promissio Baptismi clara; & declaratio facienda est non ritu humanitus confiato, sed verbo divinitus tradito.
units.tr: Not to clarify it: because both the ceremony and the promise of Baptism are clear; and the declaration to be made must rest not on a rite devised by men but on the word delivered by God.

units.la: Non ad ornandum: quia Sacramenta ornatum alium non requirunt præter nativum à Deo acceptum. Ambrof.
units.tr: Not to adorn it: because the sacraments do not require any other adornment beyond the native one received from God. Ambrose.

units.la: III. Quod vana: quia caret effectu. Probe-tur, quod nec habeat ordinarium, cum destitua-tur mandato & promissione divina, sine quibus neque cedit Satan, neque de ejus cessione homines certi esse possunt: nec extraordinarium, cum miraculorum χαρίσματα[?] desieritin Ecclesia.
units.tr: III. That it is vain: because it lacks effect. It is proved that it has no ordinary power, since it is destitute of the divine command and promise, without which Satan neither yields, nor can men be certain of his yielding; nor has it any extraordinary power, since the gifts of miracles have ceased in the Church.

units.la: IV. Quod ludicra: quia exorcistæ colloquuntur cum dæmone, quem hec vident nec sciunt præsentem esse: & ei imperant sine potestate, quod revera est ludere.
units.tr: IV. That it is mocking: because the exorcists speak with the demon, whom they neither see nor know to be present, and they command him without authority, which is in truth mockery.

units.la: V. Quod mendax. 1. quia arrogant sibi imperium in Dæmonem, quod non habent. 2. quia falso traducunt infantes Ecclesiæ, pro obsessis & arreptitiis. Probatio rejiciatur in confutationem tertiæ rationis exorcistarum. 3. quia fallunt parentes & Ecclesiam inani miraculo.
units.tr: V. That it is lying. 1. Because they arrogate to themselves a power over the demon which they do not have. 2. Because they falsely pass off the infants of the Church as possessed and seized. The proof is to be rejected in the refutation of the third argument of the exorcists. 3. Because they deceive the parents and the Church with an empty miracle.

units.la: VI. Quod Ecclesiam deformans.
units.tr: VI. That it disfigures the Church.

units.la: 1. quia vanitas & temeritas exorcistarum videtur ab Ecclesia approbari & ei imputatur.
units.tr: 1. Because the vanity and rashness of the exorcists seem to be approved by the Church and imputed to it.

units.la: 2. quia deforme est audire Ecclesiam generare infantes arreptitios, cum nec verbum Dei nec experientia id doceat.
units.tr: 2. Because it is a disgrace to hear that the Church begets infants who are possessed, when neither the word of God nor experience teaches this.

units.la: Amplificetur a comparatis: Sic deteriorem conditionem novæ Ecclesiæ statui quam veteris.
units.tr: Let it be enlarged by comparisons: thus the condition of the new Church is made worse than that of the old.

units.la: Ratio: quia hujus infantes non fuerint pro arreptitiis habiti, quod ex circumcisione probetur, quæ exorcismum non requirebat, & Baptismo cessit.
units.tr: The reason: because the infants of the old Church were not held to be possessed, which is proved from circumcision, which did not require exorcism and gave way to Baptism.

units.la: VII. Quod superstitiosa, quia fingitur efferitus applicans gratiam. Muller. Thes. 45. 46. & a multis hodie efficacia & necessitate æquatur Baptismo.
units.tr: VII. That it is superstitious, because a fictitious outward thing is imagined as applying grace. Müller, Thes. 45, 46. And today by many its efficacy and necessity are equated with Baptism.

units.la: VIII. Quod magica: quia magicum est vocibus & characteribus tribuere vim pellendi dæmones: ex definitione magiæ: quod faciunt exorcistæ.
units.tr: VIII. That it is magical: because it is magical to ascribe to words and characters the power of driving out demons; by the definition of magic, this is what the exorcists do.

units.la: Probetur minor: quia ipsorum confessione Papistarum exorcismus sit talis: cum quo ipsorum convenit origine forma & usu.
units.tr: The minor premise is proved: because by the confession of the Papists themselves, such is the exorcism, with which theirs agrees in origin, form and use.

units.la: 1. Origine: quia ex Papatu eum acceperunt.
units.tr: 1. In origin: because they received it from the Papacy.

units.la: 2. Forma: (ex Decret. Grat. d. 4. de conf.) quia 1. similiter exsufflant & exorcizant parvulos verbis conceptis. 2. signant signaculo crucis in corde & fronte. 3. duas precatiunculas dicunt super eos. 4. Iterum exorcizant.
units.tr: 2. In form (from the Decretum Gratiani, dist. 4, de consecratione): because 1. they similarly breathe on and exorcise little children with set words; 2. they sign them with the sign of the cross on the heart and forehead; 3. they say two little prayers over them; 4. they exorcise again.

units.la: Correctio: Castratum tamen nonnihil esse horum exorcismum.
units.tr: Correction: nevertheless, their exorcism is somewhat mutilated.

units.la: 1. quia sal benedictum non imponunt.
units.tr: 1. Because they do not place blessed salt upon them.

units.la: 2. quia nares & aures de salvia non tangunt.
units.tr: 2. Because they do not touch the nostrils and ears with saliva.

units.la: 3. Usu: 1. quia exsufflatione prima fingitur pelli diaboli inimica potestas
units.tr: 3. In use: 1. because by the first breathing it is imagined that the hostile power of the devil is driven out.

units.la: 2. Signaculo crucis cognoscere Diabolus, sibi jam esse alienatum.
units.tr: 2. By the sign of the cross the devil is to recognise that he is now estranged from them.

units.la: 3. Orationes fiunt super eos, ut fiant Catechumeni, & fidei accipiant rudimentum. Can. ante Bapt.
units.tr: 3. Prayers are said over them, so that they become catechumens and receive the rudiments of the faith. Canon ante Baptismum.

units.la: 4. Iterum exorcizantur, ut Diabolus nequitiam suam cognoscens, & judicium Dei timens, totus recedat.
units.tr: 4. They are exorcised again, so that the devil, recognising his wickedness and fearing the judgment of God, may withdraw entirely.

units.la: IX. Quod suo genere impia.
units.tr: IX. That it is impious in its own kind.

units.la: 1. quia est magicus nominis divini abusus cum tertio præcepto pugnans. Amplif. comparatione cum facto filiorum Sceuæ Actor. 19.
units.tr: 1. Because it is a magical abuse of the divine name, clashing with the third commandment. Amplified by comparison with the deed of the sons of Sceva, Acts 19.

units.la: 2. Est falsum testimonium cōtra nonum præceptum ceptum quod ostendatur ex 3. & 5. circunstantia.
units.tr: 2. It is false witness against the ninth commandment, which is shown from the third and fifth circumstances.

units.la: 3. quia ejectionem Dæmonis : quæ est opus digiti seu omnipotentiæ Dei, Luc. 11. tribuit ritui humano.
units.tr: 3. Because it attributes the casting out of demons, which is the work of the finger or omnipotence of God, Luke 11, to a human rite.

units.la: Addatur maior : Opus divinæ omnipotentiæ asscribere ritui humano est impium. lef 4²[?] Gloriam meam, &c.
units.tr: Add the major premise: to ascribe the work of divine omnipotence to a human rite is impious. Isaiah 42:8, My glory, etc.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Christus loquitur de ejectione corporali non spirituali.
units.tr: Objection 1. Christ speaks of bodily casting out, not spiritual.

units.la: Resp. 1. à minori: Si corporalis est opus digiti Dei, multo magis spiritualis: quia difficilius ex anima quam ex corpore Satan pellitur.
units.tr: Answer 1. From the lesser: if bodily casting out is the work of God's finger, much more is spiritual casting out; because Satan is driven out of the soul with more difficulty than out of the body.

units.la: 2. Ejectio spiritualis caret mandato, promissione & exemplis Scripturæ.
units.tr: 2. Spiritual casting out lacks the command, promise and examples of Scripture.

units.la: Instantia: Deus per media ejicit.
units.tr: Instance: God casts out by means.

units.la: Resp. Non humanitus confícta[?], quale est exorcismus.
units.tr: Answer: not devised by men, as exorcism is.

units.la: Obiect. II. Apostoli ejecerunt Dæmones citra impietatem.
units.tr: Objection II. The Apostles cast out demons without impiety.

units.la: Respon. ostensione dissimilitudinis.
units.tr: Answer: by showing the dissimilarity.

units.la: 1. Ejecerunt corporaliter.
units.tr: 1. They cast them out bodily.

units.la: 2. Fide miraculorum.
units.tr: 2. By faith in miracles.

units.la: 3. Christi mandato & promissione.
units.tr: 3. By Christ's command and promise.

units.la: 4. Sine ritu humano & magico.
units.tr: 4. Without a human and magical rite.

units.la: Isti contra spiritualiter, destituti fide, mandato & promissione: per ritum humanum & magicum ejectionem tentant.
units.tr: These men, on the contrary, spiritually, destitute of faith, command and promise, attempt the casting out by a human and magical rite.

units.la: Obiectio III. Ejectio tribuitur exorcismo non effectivè sed ut medio monitorio de effectu Baptismi.
units.tr: Objection III. The casting out is ascribed to exorcism not effectively but as a monitory means concerning the effect of Baptism.

units.la: Respon. 1. negatur distinctio: quia monitorio de effectu Baptismi non est opus alio, quàm verbo.
units.tr: Answer 1. The distinction is denied: because a monitory means concerning the effect of Baptism requires no other work than the word.

units.la: 2. Est medium inane: quia humanus ritus nō potest testari de effectu divini Sacramenti.
units.tr: 2. It is an empty means: because a human rite cannot bear witness concerning the effect of a divine sacrament.

units.la: 3· negatur antecedentis prior pars. 1. quia formula repugnat, qua significant se ejicere Satanam exorcismo, non denunciant, ejiciedum per Baptismum. 2. quia fingunt medium applicatorium gratiæ, quod falsum est & impium. Leise-rus in 1.qu.de Exor. Mull Thef.47.
units.tr: 3. The first part of the antecedent is denied. 1. Because the formula is inconsistent, by which they declare that they drive out Satan by exorcism, rather than announcing that he is to be driven out through Baptism. 2. Because they imagine a means applying grace, which is false and impious. Leiserus, on the first question concerning exorcism; Müller, Thes. 47.

units.la: Ratio V. Exorcismus & merito Christi & efficaciæ Baptismi derogat. Ergo non ferendus in Baptismo.
units.tr: Argument V. Exorcism derogates both from the merit of Christ and from the efficacy of Baptism. Therefore it is not to be tolerated in Baptism.

units.la: Prob. antecedens: quia utriusque proprium ei vendicatur.
units.tr: Proof of the antecedent: because the proper work of each is claimed for it.

units.la: Explicetur utriusque proprium.
units.tr: Let the proper work of each be explained.

units.la: 1. Mortis seu meriti Christi, liberatio à potestate Satanæ. Heb.2.14.
units.tr: 1. Of the death or merit of Christ: deliverance from the power of Satan. Hebrews 2:14.

units.la: 2. Baptismi, testificatio & obsignatio ejusdem ex Rom.6.6.
units.tr: 2. Of Baptism: the attestation and sealing of the same, from Romans 6:6.

units.la: Ostendatur utrunque tribui exorcismo.
units.tr: Let it be shown that both are ascribed to exorcism.

units.la: Obiectio: Tantum applicationem meriti ad singulos ei tribui. Non ergo derogare. Addatur major, cum probatione: Media applicantia gratiam non derogant, &c. cum Deus per verbum & Sacramenta applicet.
units.tr: Objection: Only the application of merit to individuals is ascribed to it. Therefore it does not derogate. Add the major premise, with proof: means applying grace do not derogate, etc., since God applies through the word and the sacraments.

units.la: Respon. 1. negetur minor & probetur: quia caret mandato & promissione divina.
units.tr: Answer 1. The minor is denied, and proved: because it lacks the divine command and promise.

units.la: 2. per [illegible, ~4 letters]: cum applicatio fiat per verbum & Sacramenta; non ergo per exorcismum, qui neutrum est.
units.tr: 2. By [illegible, about four letters]: since application takes place through the word and the sacraments; therefore not through exorcism, which is neither.

units.la: Ratio VI. Nulli baptizandi sunt arreptitii vel obsessi à Cacodæmone. Ergo nulli exorcizandi in baptismo.
units.tr: Argument VI. No one to be baptized is possessed or seized by the evil demon. Therefore no one is to be exorcised in Baptism.

units.la: Prob. antecedens syllogismo disjunctivo; quod baptizandi sint vel adulti vel infantes Ecclesiæ, quorum neutri sint pro arreptitiis habendi, nisi sensus diversum ostendat.
units.tr: Proof of the antecedent by a disjunctive syllogism: those to be baptized are either adults or infants of the Church, and neither of these is to be held as seized, unless the sense shows otherwise.

units.la: Probatio minoris: Adultos baptizandos oportet credere.
units.tr: Proof of the minor: adults to be baptized must believe.

units.la: Act. 10. licet tibi baptizari, si credis toto corde.
units.tr: Acts 10: May you be baptized, if you believe with all your heart.

units.la: Act. 2. Resipiscite, & baptizetur unusquisq; &c. infantes Ecclesiæ sunt filii fœderis non Diaboli, etiam ante baptismum.
units.tr: Acts 2: Repent, and let each one be baptized, etc. The infants of the Church are children of the covenant, not of the devil, even before Baptism.

units.la: Ostendatur 1. ex promissione. Ero Deus tuus & seminis tui. Act. 2. vestra & vestrorum liberorum est promissio. Act. 3. 25. vos estis filii fœderis.
units.tr: Let it be shown 1. from the promise. I will be your God and the God of your seed. Acts 2: The promise is to you and to your children. Acts 3:25: You are the children of the covenant.

units.la: 2. Ex dictis Rom. 11. 16. Si radix sancta etiam Rami. 1. Cor. 7. 14. liberi vestri sancti sunt.
units.tr: 2. From the words of Romans 11:16, If the root is holy, so are the branches. 1 Corinthians 7:14, Your children are holy.

units.la: 3. ex formula exorcismi: quia infantes etiam nondum baptizati vocantur servi Jesu Christi.
units.tr: 3. From the formula of exorcism: because infants not yet baptized are also called servants of Jesus Christ.

units.la: 4. ab absurdo: Omnes ante exorcismum & baptismum morientes necessario damnarentur, & sic perirent multi electi. Ratio: quia manerent sub potestate Cacodæmonis.
units.tr: 4. From the absurd: all who die before exorcism and baptism would necessarily be damned, and thus many elect would perish. Reason: because they would remain under the power of the evil demon.

units.la: Amplif. absurdi: ab effectu: Parentibus & Ecclesiæ nulla esset consolatio & spes salutis suorum infantum sic morientium.
units.tr: Amplification of the absurdity, from its effect: parents and the Church would have no consolation and no hope of salvation for their infants dying in this way.

units.la: Opponatur exemplum Davidis ex 2. Sam. 12. 23. Item: Stabiliretur limbus infantum.
units.tr: Against this is set the example of David, 2 Samuel 12:23. Likewise: the limbo of infants would be established.

units.la: Claudatur probatio minoris: Neutros ergo esse obsessos & adjuratione egere.
units.tr: Therefore the proof of the minor is concluded: neither of them is possessed, and neither needs adjuration.

units.la: Objectio 1. (contra disjunctivam) Omnes sunt baptizandi. Matth. 28. Baptizate omnes gentes. Ergo etiam infantes extra Ecclesiam.
units.tr: Objection 1 (against the disjunctive): all are to be baptized. Matthew 28: Baptize all nations. Therefore also the infants outside the Church.

units.la: Resp. ad antecedens. Mādatum [?] loquitur de omnib.
units.tr: Answer to the antecedent: the command speaks of all.

units.la: 1. Iudæis & gentibus absque discrimine.
units.tr: 1. Of Jews and Gentiles without distinction.

units.la: 2. Habendis pro Christi discipulis, & Eccle-siæ civibus, quales sunt vel adulti fidem professi (ut Eunuchus, Cornelius) vel infantes in Ecclesia nascentes (ut nostri) aut cum parentibus in eam transeuntes (ut infantes familiarum quas baptizarunt apostoli) Infantes autem Turcarum sunt alieni à Christo & ab Ecclesia.
units.tr: 2. They are to be counted as disciples of Christ and citizens of the Church: such as adults who have professed faith (like the eunuch and Cornelius), or infants born in the Church (like our own children), or infants who pass into the Church with their parents (like the infants of the households the apostles baptized). The infants of the Turks, however, are strangers to Christ and to the Church.

units.la: Probetur ex mandato μαθητεύσατε πάντα, &c. Et ex genere ac principali usu Baptismi, quod sit signum fœderis, ad solos fœderatos Dei pertinens.
units.tr: This is proved from the command, "Make disciples of all nations" (μαθητεύσατε πάντα, etc.), and from the nature and principal use of Baptism, which is a sign of the covenant and pertains only to those who are in the covenant of God.

units.la: Item ex argumento Petri, Actor. 2. Baptizetur unusquisque, &c. quia vestra & liberorum vestrorum est promissio.
units.tr: Likewise from Peter's argument in Acts 2: "Let each one be baptized," etc., because the promise is to you and to your children.

units.la: Instantia: Promissio est universalis: In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes, &c.
units.tr: Objection: the promise is universal: "In your seed shall all the nations be blessed," etc.

units.la: Respond. 1. omnes gentes, non soli Judæi.
units.tr: Answer: (1) it says all nations, not only the Jews.

units.la: 2. omnes credentes: pro qualibus habendi sunt soli adulti fidem profitentes: & Ecclesiæ in-fantes, quibus ex fidelibus & in Ecclesia nasci est fidem profiteri.
units.tr: (2) All who believe; and those who must be counted as such are only adults who profess faith, and the infants of the Church, for whom to be born of believers in the Church is to profess faith.

units.la: 3. Promissio fœderis: Ero Deus tuus, &c. est propria familiæ Abrahami, olim carnalis: nunc spiritualis Rom. 9.
units.tr: (3) The promise of the covenant, "I will be your God," etc., belongs properly to the family of Abraham, once carnal, now spiritual (Rom. 9).

units.la: Infantes ergo Ecclesiæ ad hanc pertinentes habent prærogativam.
units.tr: Therefore the infants of the Church who belong to this covenant have the prerogative.

units.la: Obiect. 1 1. (Contra promissionem) Infantes Ecclesiæ sunt caro & filii iræ sicut cæteri; Ephes. 2.
units.tr: Objection 1: (against the promise) The infants of the Church are flesh and children of wrath, like the rest (Eph. 2).

units.la: Ergo non habent prærogativam.
units.tr: Therefore they do not have the prerogative.

units.la: Resp. per concessionem de generatione naturali, non autem de gratia promissionis, qua cum parentib.censentur filii fœderis.
units.tr: Answer: I grant this as regards natural generation, but not as regards the grace of the promise, by which they are counted together with their parents as children of the covenant.

units.la: Instantia: Non ante Baptismum.
units.tr: Objection: Not before Baptism.

units.la: Ratio: quia promissio intelligitur cum conditione applicationis per Sacramentum.
units.tr: Reason: because the promise is understood with the condition that it be applied through the sacrament.

units.la: Respond, negatur antecedens. Ratio 1. quia promissio est rata fidelibus etiam ante baptismum, extra casum contemtus.
units.tr: Answer: the antecedent is denied. Reason 1: because the promise is valid for believers even before baptism, apart from the case of contempt.

units.la: Probatio: quia eadem ratio infantum Ecclesiæ & adultorum fidelium. Illustretur exemplo Abrahami, qui cum familia ante circuncisionem accepit promissionem, & fuit in fœdere: quod probetur ex historia Gen.17.& Rom.4.
units.tr: Proof: because the reason is the same for the infants of the Church and for adult believers. It is illustrated by the example of Abraham, who with his household received the promise before circumcision and was in the covenant; this is proved from the history in Gen. 17 and from Rom. 4.

units.la: Ratio 2. quia applicatio interna fidei antecedit applicationem externam Sacramenti.
units.tr: Reason 2: because the inward application of faith precedes the outward application of the sacrament.

units.la: Probetur absurdo: alioqui damnandi essent infantes Ecclesiæ non baptizati: cum extra fœdus non sit salus: quod astruatur contra Papistarum sententiam: ab exemplo infantum morientium ante circuncisionem in fœdere: & à prærogativa Novi Testamenti, cujus gratia alioqui esset angustior quam veteris.
units.tr: It is proved by absurdity: otherwise the infants of the Church who were not baptized would have to be damned, since there is no salvation outside the covenant. This is confirmed against the opinion of the Papists, from the example of infants who died before circumcision within the covenant, and from the prerogative of the New Testament, whose grace would otherwise be narrower than that of the Old.

units.la: Obiectio III. Si ante baptismum infantes sunt in fœdere & sancti, frustra baptizantur.
units.tr: Objection III: If infants are in the covenant and holy before baptism, they are baptized in vain.

units.la: Resp. 1: est fallacia non causæ: quia nihilo minus sunt causæ Pædobaptismi.
units.tr: Answer 1: it is the fallacy of a non-cause, since they are nonetheless causes of infant baptism.

units.la: 1. Mandatum Christi.
units.tr: 1. The command of Christ.

units.la: 2. Consolatio Ecclesiæ de adoptione infantum.
units.tr: 2. The comfort of the Church concerning the adoption of infants.

units.la: 3. Obsignatio promissionis gratiæ ad infantes & parentes pertinentis.
units.tr: 3. The sealing of the promise of grace which pertains to the infants and the parents.

units.la: 4. Receptio in Ecclesiam.
units.tr: 4. Reception into the Church.

units.la: 5. Discretio à non baptizatis.
units.tr: 5. Distinction from the unbaptized.

units.la: 2. Idem valeret de adultis fidelibus ante baptismum.
units.tr: 2. The same would hold for adult believers before baptism.

units.la: Hieronym. ad Rom. II. Qui mundus accedit, ibi fit mundior & omni habenti ibi amplius datur. Vide Ambrosium ad illud Roman. II. Multum ergo confert baptismus etiam jam per fidem justificato, &c. Item Lombard. l. 4. d. 4. c. Solet.
units.tr: Jerome on Romans 2: "Whoever comes there clean becomes cleaner there, and to everyone who has there more is given." See Ambrose on that passage in Romans 2: "Baptism therefore contributes much even to one who is already justified through faith," etc. Likewise Lombard, book 4, distinction 4, chapter "Solet."

units.la: Obiectio 1 v. Apostolus Rom. II. de Iudæis loquitur.
units.tr: Objection IV: The Apostle in Romans 2 speaks of the Jews.

units.la: Resp. de omnibus fidelibus.
units.tr: Answer: he speaks of all believers.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia hi omnes sunt filii Abrahami. Rom. 4. & 9.
units.tr: Reason 1: because all of these are sons of Abraham (Rom. 4 and 9).

units.la: 2. quia etiam hi sunt rami, licet insititii in radicem sanctam.
units.tr: 2. Because these too are branches, though grafted in, into the holy root.

units.la: Obiectio v. Liberi fidelium vocantur sancti, h.e. legitimi non spurii, 1. Cor. 7.
units.tr: Objection V: The children of believers are called holy, that is, legitimate, not illegitimate (1 Cor. 7).

units.la: Resp. per negationem. Ratio: quia sic nihil consolaretur apostolus fideles conjuges, cum etiam infidelium liberi sint legitimi, non spurii.
units.tr: Answer: by denial. Reason: because in that case the Apostle would offer no comfort to believing spouses, since the children of unbelievers are also legitimate, not illegitimate.

units.la: Addatur declaratio sanctitatis, quod sit comprehensio in fœdere (relativa, non habitualis:) & probetur: alioqui ut alienos à fœdere baptizare eos non liceret.
units.tr: Let a declaration of holiness be added, that it is inclusion in the covenant (relative, not inherent), and let it be proved; otherwise it would not be lawful to baptize them as aliens from the covenant.

units.la: Confutatio.
units.tr: Confutatio.

units.la: TRANSITIO ad confutationem propositionum & rationum pro exorcismo.
units.tr: TRANSITION to the refutation of the propositions and arguments in favour of exorcism.

units.la: Propositio 1. quod exorcismus non sit suo genere impius: Negetur: & ostendatur ex nona circunstantia quarti argumenti confirmationis.
units.tr: Proposition 1: that exorcism is not impious in its own kind. Let it be denied, and it is shown from the ninth circumstance of the fourth argument of confirmation.

units.la: Adrationem: negetur minor.
units.tr: To the argument: the minor premise is denied.

units.la: 1. quia pugnat cum tertio & nono præcepto: de non usurpando Dei nomine temere: & de non dicendo falso testimonio. Item: cum primo articulo symboli: quod declaretur ex eadem circunstantia.
units.tr: 1. Because it conflicts with the third and ninth commandments, on not taking the name of God in vain and on not bearing false witness. Likewise with the first article of the creed, which is made clear from the same circumstance.

units.la: 2. quia deformat baptismum, & derogat ejus efficaciæ quod ostendatur ex ratione 4. & 5.
units.tr: 2. Because it deforms baptism and detracts from its efficacy, which is shown from the fourth and fifth arguments.

units.la: Propositio II. quod exorcismus sit ἀλλ-φος.
units.tr: Proposition II: that exorcism is adiaphoron (indifferent).

units.la: Negetur cum ratione, & probetur:
units.tr: Let it be denied, with the reason, and it is proved:

units.la: 1. quia est ceremonia impia, magica, &c. eoq; prohibita à Deo.
units.tr: 1. Because it is an impious, magical ceremony, etc., and therefore forbidden by God.

units.la: 2. quia ipsi contendunt tanquam pro re necessaria, nolentes cum, etiam publica authoritate magistratus & ministrorum abrogari: & populū de abrogatione erudiri;
units.tr: 2. Because they contend for it as something necessary, unwilling that it be abolished, even by the public authority of the magistrate and the ministers, and that the people be taught about its abolition;

units.la: 3. ex causis, propter quas abrogari nolunt, & abrogationem omnem improbant:
units.tr: 3. From the causes for which they are unwilling to have it abolished, and for which they disapprove of any abolition at all:

units.la: 1. quòd sit de officio ministrorum Novi Testamenti, Dei nomine Satanam exorcizare, &c. ex definitione Leyseri.
units.tr: (1) that it is the office of the ministers of the New Testament to exorcise Satan in the name of God, etc., according to the definition of Leyser;

units.la: II. quòd sit medium applicans baptizato meritum Christi.
units.tr: (2) that it is a means applying to the baptized the merit of Christ;

units.la: III. quod sine eo neque vis peccati originis, neque efficacia Baptismi rectè intelligatur.
units.tr: (3) that without it neither the power of original sin nor the efficacy of Baptism is rightly understood;

units.la: IV. quod abrogatio ejus tollat omnem reverentiam ministerii, verbi & sanctorum in piisEcclefiis, ubi est facta.
units.tr: (4) that its abolition removes all reverence for the ministry, the Word and the sacraments in the pious churches where it has been done;

units.la: V. quia abrogatio sternat viam hæresi Calvinianæ, nianæ, & à solis Calvinistis fit profecta, & facta in Agro Wirtembergico & alibi.
units.tr: (5) that abolition paves the way for the Calvinian heresy, and that it has been proposed only by the Calvinists, and has been carried out in the land of Württemberg and elsewhere.

units.la: Addatur maior per adversativam: Quæ talia sunt, minime pro adiaphoris haberi possunt.
units.tr: The major premise is added by way of contrast: things of such a kind can by no means be regarded as indifferent.

units.la: Ad instantiam tacitam rationis: quod sit significationis causa ab Ecclesia institutus.
units.tr: To the tacit objection of the argument: that it was instituted by the Church for the sake of signification.

units.la: Resp. 1. Sic omnes superstitiones Papatus defendi possent: quia omnibus affingunt Papistæ significationem aliquam.
units.tr: Answer: (1) In this way all the superstitions of Papacy could be defended, since the Papists attach some meaning to all of them.

units.la: 2. Non Ecclesiæ sed solius Dei est ritus testificantes de beneficiis Evangelii instituere.
units.tr: (2) It is not for the Church but for God alone to institute rites that bear witness to the benefits of the Gospel.

units.la: 3. Non opus est hac significatione: cum neque ex Scripturis evinci, neque ratione aliqua probari possit.
units.tr: (3) There is no need for this signification, since it can be proved neither from the Scriptures nor by any reasoning.

units.la: 4. Infantes Ecclesiæ propter peccatum originis non magis imo minus dici possunt arreptitii vel obsessi spiritualiter, quam adulti Judæi, Turcæ, &c. non solo originali sed etiam actuali peccato polluti, quos baptizant absque exorcismo ad Ecclesiam accedentes.
units.tr: (4) Infants of the Church cannot, on account of original sin, be called seized or possessed spiritually any more, or rather any less, than adult Jews, Turks, etc., who are polluted not only by original but also by actual sin, and whom they baptize without exorcism when they come to the Church.

units.la: 5. Ad significationem liberationis à peccato & Satana, non opus est ceremonia humana & ludicra, sed sufficit Baptismus.
units.tr: (5) For the signification of liberation from sin and Satan, no human and childish ceremony is needed; Baptism is sufficient.

units.la: Propositio III. quod exorcismus sit utilis & retinendus, ubi viget: Negetur: quia utile esse non potest, quod polluit Christi ordinem: & derogat efficaciæ baptismi.
units.tr: Proposition III: that exorcism is useful and to be retained where it flourishes. Let it be denied, because that which pollutes the order of Christ cannot be useful, and it detracts from the efficacy of baptism.

units.la: Adrat. 1. Resp. 1. Distinctione majoris: expositionem verborum B. esse utilem & retinendam, quæ non est superstitiosa, qualis hæc est. Probetur ut supra: quia verbis & crucibus tribuitur facultas pellendi dæmones, sine verbo Dei. 2. negatione minoris: ostendatur:
units.tr: To the argument 1. Answer: (1) By distinguishing the major premise: the exposition of the words of Blessed [Paul] is useful and to be retained, but not a superstitious one such as this. Let it be proved as above: because power to drive out demons is attributed to words and crosses without the Word of God. (2) By denying the minor premise, it is shown:

units.la: 1. quia exorcismus praecedit verba, cum expositio debeat sequi verba.
units.tr: (1) because exorcism precedes the words, whereas exposition ought to follow the words;

units.la: 2. qua verba B. sunt ipso exorcismo clariora.
units.tr: (2) because the words of Blessed [Paul] are clearer than the exorcism itself.

units.la: Ostendatur, quod omnes causas gratiae Baptismi efficiētem, materiam, formam, finem clarius exprimant.
units.tr: It is shown that they express the efficient cause, matter, form and end of the grace of Baptism more clearly.

units.la: Ad rationem II. Resp. 1. Negatione majoris: quia Sacramenta non indigent commendatione per ceremonias assututias humanas: sed ipsa vim suam satis commendant: Quod amplificetur à sapientia Authoris, in qua nos decet acquiescere.
units.tr: To the second argument. Answer: (1) By denying the major premise: because sacraments do not need to be commended by human, made-up ceremonies, but commend their power sufficiently by themselves; this is amplified by the wisdom of the Author, in which we ought to rest content. (2) The minor premise is denied: because exorcism does not testify to what Baptism is but to what it itself effects, which is proved from the formula.

units.la: 2. negatione minoris: quia exorcismus nō quid Baptismus sed quid ipse efficiat testatur, quod probetur ex formula.
units.tr: 2. Denial of the minor premise: because exorcism testifies not to what Baptism is but to what it itself effects, which is proved from the formula.

units.la: Negetur quoque minui dignitatem Baptismi abrogatione exorcismi, & revocentur exorcistæ ad primam institutionem & ad Baptismum Apostolorum, cum detestatione eorum arrogantiæ, & impudentiæ, & blasphemiæ in Christum atque apostolos.
units.tr: Let it also be denied that the dignity of Baptism is diminished by the abolition of exorcism, and let the exorcists be recalled to the first institution and to the Baptism of the Apostles, with detestation of their arrogance, impudence and blasphemy against Christ and the apostles.

units.la: Ad rationem III. Resp. Distinctione majoris.
units.tr: To the reason III. Reply: by distinguishing the major premise.

units.la: 1. Si confessio fiat legitimè.
units.tr: 1. If the confession is made lawfully.

units.la: 2. Si non sit falsa.
units.tr: 2. If it is not false.

units.la: Ostende exorcismum esse confessionem illegi-timam, quia fit ritu superstitioso, impio, &c. Et esse falsam: quia infantes Christianorum non sunt arreptitii propter peccatum magis quam a-dulti.
units.tr: Show that exorcism is an unlawful confession, because it is performed with a superstitious, impious rite, etc. And that it is false, because the infants of Christians are not possessed on account of sin any more than adults are.

units.la: Ad rationem VI.[?] Resp. Esse dissimilitudinem.
units.tr: To the reason VI.[?] Reply: there is a dissimilarity.

units.la: 1. quia potestas illa fuit miraculosa: hæc fingitur ordinaria.
units.tr: (2) that one was over bodily possessed persons; this one is over sinners.

units.la: 2. illa in corporaliter obsessos: hæc in peccatores.
units.tr: (3) that one lasted for a time; this one is perpetual.

units.la: 3. illa ad tempus durans: hæc perpetua.
units.tr: (4) that one was outside baptism; this one is in baptism.

units.la: 4. illa extra baptismum: hæc in baptismo.
units.tr: To the fifth answer. (1) That it is an accepted scandal:

units.la: Ad v. Respond. 1. Esse scandalum acceptum:
units.tr: Reason: because the abolition of idolatry and superstitions in itself does not harm the glory of God.

units.la: Ratio: quia abrogatio idololatriæ & superstitionum per se non lædit gloriam Dei.
units.tr: Amplification: under this pretext the whole Papal kingdom could be established.

units.la: Amplific. Hoc prætextu totum Pontificium regnum stabiliri posset.
units.tr: (2) That the weak are to be taught about the causes of abolition from the Word of God.

units.la: 2. Esse docendos infirmos de causis abrogationis ex verbo Dei.
units.tr: To the sixth answer. (1) The institution of Christ is the rule of sacramental rites, not the authority of the Fathers.

units.la: Ad vi. Respond. 1. Institutio Christi est regula rituum Sacramentalium, non authoritas Patrum.
units.tr: (2) The earlier Fathers, Justin Martyr, Dionysius, Irenaeus, etc., were ignorant of exorcisms at Baptism.

units.la: 2. Patres antiquiores, Iustinus Martyr, Dionysius, Irenæus, &c. ignorant exorcismos ad Baptismum.
units.tr: (3) Later Fathers at last exorcised at Baptism those who were truly energumens, adults, with God commending the Christian faith by miracles against the unbelief of the Gentiles.

units.la: 3. Patres sequentes tandem exorcizarunt ad Bapt. verè energumenos, adultos, Deo miraculis commendante Christianam fidem, contra infidelitatem gentilium.
units.tr: (4) Nothing about the form of exorcism for infants can be proved from the Fathers.

units.la: 4. De forma exorcismi infantum nihil ex patribus probari potest.
units.tr: Conclusion: Having considered these things, and having carefully compared the responses of others also, I hope that exorcism will no longer trouble you or those churches.

units.la: Conclusio: His consideratis & cum aliorum quoque responsis diligenter collatis, spero exorcismum neque te, neque Ecclesias illas amplius turbaturam.
units.tr: (end of unit)

units.la: Exercitatio XXV. An Spectra sint animæ defunctorum.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXV. Whether the apparitions are the souls of the dead.

units.la: Exordium exponat opinionem primò gentilium ex Phædone Platonis: omnes defunctorum animas dejici ad inferos, sed inde redire: & sapientes evolare ad sedes beatas: inertes vagari in terris circa sepulcra, & esse spectra. Deinde Papistarum, animas excedentium cum peccato mortali deferri in infernum: cum veniali in purgatorium: inde in cœlum, utrasque aliquando apparere in terris, dispensatione divina, ut vel terreant, vel admoneant viventes vel opem petant.
units.tr: The introduction sets out the opinion, first, of the Gentiles from Plato's Phaedo: all the souls of the dead are carried down to the underworld, but from there return; the wise fly up to the blessed seats, while the idle wander on earth around the tombs and become apparitions. Second, the opinion of the Papists: the souls of those departing with mortal sin are carried down into hell, those with venial sin into purgatory, and from there into heaven; and both sometimes appear on earth, by divine dispensation, either to terrify or to warn the living, or to seek help.

units.la: Propositio: Spectra non sunt animæ defunctorum.
units.tr: Proposition: Apparitions are not the souls of the dead.

units.la: Ratio 1. à conditione immutabili animarum post excessum è corpore.
units.tr: Reason 1, from the unchangeable condition of souls after their departure from the body.

units.la: Pia mox deferuntur in cœlum.
units.tr: The pious are at once carried up into heaven.

units.la: Probetur exemplo Lazari, latronis, & scripturæ dictis.
units.tr: This is proved by the example of Lazarus, the thief, and the words of Scripture.

units.la: Amplificetur: Nolunt ad momentum deserere felicitatem.
units.tr: It is amplified thus: they are unwilling to abandon their happiness even for a moment.

units.la: Impiæ mox dejiciuntur in gehennam.
units.tr: The impious are at once cast down into hell.

units.la: Prob. exemplo epulonis & Scripturæ dictis.
units.tr: Proof: by the example of the rich man and the words of Scripture.

units.la: Amplif. non possunt exire.
units.tr: Amplification: they cannot come out.

units.la: 1. Propter justitiam Dei. Luc.16. Memen-to fili,
units.tr: 1. On account of the justice of God. Luke 16. Remember, son,

units.la: 2. propter χάσμα[?] magnum interjectum.
units.tr: 2. on account of the great chasm placed between.

units.la: 3. Si possent, non errarent, sed redirent ad sua corpora vel alio.
units.tr: 3. If they could, they would not wander, but would return either to their own bodies or elsewhere.

units.la: Ratio II. ab efficiente. Nec Dei, nec Dæmonis, nec sua voluntate & vi errare possunt.
units.tr: Reason II, from the efficient cause. They can wander neither by the will and power of God, nor of the devil, nor of their own will.

units.la: Probatio: Non Dei voluntate: ex fine apparitionum, quem Deus non vult nec permittit: qua per mortuos neq; docere neque terrere vult superstites, sed per concionem Legis & Evangelij. Luc.16. A maiori, multo minus vult stabilire idololatriam vel νεκυομαντίαν[?], quam damnavit, Deut.18.
units.tr: Proof: Not by the will of God, from the purpose of the apparitions, which God neither wills nor permits; for he does not wish to teach or terrify the survivors through the dead, but through the sermon of the Law and the Gospel. Luke 16. A fortiori, he much less wishes to establish idolatry or necromancy, which he condemned, Deut. 18.

units.la: Amplif. argumento Athanasii lib.quæst.q.13. Si Deus permitteret, multi inde apud nos errores nascerentur: quin Diaboli quidvis in specie animarum mentiri & obtrudere nobis possent.
units.tr: Amplification by the argument of Athanasius, in the book of Questions, question 13. If God permitted it, many errors would arise among us from this; indeed the devils could lie about anything in the appearance of souls and foist it upon us.

units.la: Non vi Dæmonis vel magicæ artis: quia à Dæmone nec piæ evocari è felicitate, nec impiæ vel ad momentum liberari à cruciatib. possunt: propter Dei justitiam, Luc.16.
units.tr: Not by the power of the devil or of magical art: because the devil can neither summon the pious away from their happiness, nor free the impious even for a moment from their torments: on account of the justice of God, Luke 16.

units.la: Non sua voluntate: 1. quia piæ nec errare nec stabilire νεκυομαντίαν[?] volunt.
units.tr: Not by their own will: 1. because the pious neither wish to wander nor to establish necromancy.

units.la: II. Impiæ subsunt imperio Dei & dæmonis quorum ille non vult, hic non potest nec vult mutare statum.
units.tr: II. The impious are subject to the command of God and of the devil; the former does not wish, the latter cannot, nor wishes to change their state.

units.la: III. Nec his nec illis patet transitus, Luc. 16.26.
units.tr: III. Neither for these nor for those is there a passage open, Luke 16:26.

units.la: Ratio III. Patres consentiunt, tantùm duos esse animarum status, eosque immutabiles, post excessum.
units.tr: Reason III. The Fathers agree that there are only two states of souls after death, and that these are unchangeable.

units.la: Cyprianus contra Demetr. Hic vita acquiri-tur vel amittitur. August.de verb.Apost.Serm.18. Duo sunt ha-bitacula: unum in igne æterno, alterum in regno a-terno.
units.tr: Cyprian, against Demetrianus: Here life is acquired or lost. Augustine, On the Words of the Apostle, Sermon 18: There are two dwelling places: one in eternal fire, the other in the eternal kingdom.

units.la: Chrysostom.in Matth.8.hom.19. Justorum anima in manu Dei sunt: peccatorum vero post exitum continuo abducuntur, quod è Lazaro & divite planum est, &c.
units.tr: Chrysostom, on Matthew, homily 19: The souls of the just are in the hand of God; but the souls of sinners are at once led away after their departure, which is plain from Lazarus and the rich man, etc.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Deus potest dispensare.
units.tr: Objection 1. God can dispense otherwise.

units.la: Resp. A posse ad esse non valet: non vult. Habent Mosen & prophetas, &c.
units.tr: Answer: The argument from possibility to actuality does not hold: he does not will it. They have Moses and the prophets, etc.

units.la: Obiect. 11. Fatentur se esse animas.
units.tr: Objection 2. They confess that they are souls.

units.la: Resp. Mentiuntur, ut stabiliant νεκυομαντεία[?], & fabulam purgatorii.
units.tr: Answer: They lie, in order to establish necromancy and the fable of purgatory.

units.la: Obiectio 111. Animæ Mosis & Eliæ apparue-runt, Matt.17.
units.tr: Objection 3. The souls of Moses and Elijah appeared, Matt. 17.

units.la: Resp. Exemplum singulare & dissimile non fa-cit regulam.
units.tr: Answer: A singular and dissimilar example does not make a rule.

units.la: Obiectio 1v. Etiam Samuelis anima appa-ruit.
units.tr: Objection 4. The soul of Samuel also appeared.

units.la: Resp. Fuit spectrum diabolicum, specie Sa-muelis indutum, ut stabiliretur magia. 2. Cor. 11. 14. Satan transformans se in angelum lucis.
units.tr: Answer: It was a diabolical apparition, clothed in the likeness of Samuel, so that magic might be confirmed. 2 Cor. 11:14: Satan transforms himself into an angel of light.

units.la: Conclusio: Vana igitur opinio gentilium, ani-mos improborum, vel inhumatorum, vel violenta morte decedentium ad sepulcra mutari in dæmones errantes.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore the opinion of the Gentiles is vain, that the souls of the wicked, or of those unburied, or of those who die a violent death, change at the tombs into wandering demons.

units.la: Et Monachorum: Spectra esse animas defun-ctorum è cœlo, vel inferno, vel purgatorio rede-ntes.
units.tr: And of the monks: that apparitions are the souls of the dead returning from heaven, or from hell, or from purgatory.

units.la: Antithesis: Esse vel inanes umbras, vel ludibria impostorum & Satanæ: vel ipsos dæmones, specie humana vestitos.
units.tr: Antithesis: They are either empty shades, or the illusions of impostors and of Satan; or the devils themselves, clothed in human form.

units.la: Exercitatio XXVI. De dono Perseverantiae
units.tr: Exercitatio XXVI. On the Gift of Perseverance

units.la: Quòd detur omnibus petentibus, seu Electis.
units.tr: That it is given to all who ask, or to the Elect.

units.la: EXordium habeat [illegible, ~3 letters]: mirari te, amicum dubitare de perseverantia sanctorum in fide.
units.tr: Let the exordium be: it is a wonder to you, my friend, that you doubt the perseverance of the saints in the faith.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia quod detur, sit manifestè traditum in Scripturis sacris.
units.tr: Reason 1: because that it is given is clearly taught in the holy Scriptures.

units.la: 2. quia olim ab Augustino & hoc seculo à doctis multis solide sit demonstrata.
units.tr: 2: because it was long ago solidly demonstrated by Augustine, and in this age by many learned men.

units.la: Correctio per adversativam: Sed ignoscere te versanti inter liberi arbitrii patronos, ubi orthodoxorum scripta non feruntur vel contemnantur.
units.tr: Correction by way of adversative: But I pardon you, since you are conversing among the defenders of free will, where the writings of the orthodox are not read or are held in contempt.

units.la: Transitio: Pro amicitia te libenter communicaturum cum eo de veritate.
units.tr: Transition: For the sake of friendship, I will gladly share with you the truth on this matter.

units.la: Addatur amplificatio ab ipsius studio, & à doctrinae necessitate ac usu.
units.tr: Let there be added an amplification from your own zeal, and from the necessity and use of the doctrine.

units.la: Propositio: Te statuere, omnibus electis certò dari à Deo perseverantiam in fide usque ad finem.
units.tr: Proposition: You hold that perseverance in the faith until the end is certainly given by God to all the elect.

units.la: Ratio 1. à fine: quia certò datur salus, quae absque perseverantia in fide nulli contingit.
units.tr: Reason 1, from the end: because salvation is certainly given, and it comes to no one without perseverance in the faith.

units.la: Probetur minor dictis Scripturae Rom. 8. Ioh. 10. Matth. 24.
units.tr: Let the minor premise be proved by the words of Scripture: Romans 8, John 10, Matthew 24.

units.la: Amplif.ab æterno & constanti Amore Dei, quo electos completitur in Christo: Ier.31. & 32. Ioh.13.
units.tr: Amplification from the eternal and constant love of God, by which he perfects the elect in Christ: Jeremiah 31 and 32, John 13.

units.la: II. Fides datur electis: Ergo & perseverantia. Probetur 1. antecedens argumenti ex Eph. 1. & 2. Ioh.6. Tit.1.2. 1 Hess.3. Act.13.
units.tr: II. Faith is given to the elect; therefore perseverance too. Let the antecedent of the argument be proved (1) from Ephesians 1 and 2, John 6, Titus 1 and 2, 1 Thessalonians 3, Acts 13.

units.la: 2. Consequentia ex definitione fidei, quae est notitia & fiducia constans.
units.tr: (2) The consequence follows from the definition of faith, which is a constant knowledge and trust.

units.la: III. Spes datur electis: Ergo & perseverantia. Rursus probetur 1. antecedens ex Scriptura 1.Pet.1. Regeneravit nos in spem vivam, Rom.8. Spe salvi sumus.
units.tr: III. Hope is given to the elect; therefore perseverance too. Let the antecedent be proved again (1) from Scripture: 1 Peter 1, He has begotten us again to a living hope; Romans 8, We are saved by hope.

units.la: 2. Consequentia ex definitione spei, quae est exspectatio certa & constans. Rom.5. Spes non confundit. 2.Cor.1. Spes nostra firma est.
units.tr: (2) The consequence follows from the definition of hope, which is a certain and constant expectation. Romans 5, Hope does not disappoint. 2 Corinthians 1, Our hope is firm.

units.la: Amplificetur utrinque argumentum per contrapositionem: Ergo quicunque non habent fidem & spem constantem seu perseverantem, non habent fidem & spem.
units.tr: Let the argument be amplified on both sides by contraposition: Therefore whoever does not have faith and hope that is constant, or persevering, does not have faith and hope.

units.la: IV. A promissione divina: Deus promisit credentibus perseverantiam. Ergo dat.
units.tr: IV. From the divine promise: God has promised perseverance to those who believe. Therefore he gives it.

units.la: Prob. antecedens inductione promissionum, quae tamen non verbotim describuntur, sed argumento commode aptentur Ies.54.10. Ies.46.4 Ierem.32. Psal.37.24. Matth.12.20. Matth.24.24. Philip.1. Qui coepit, &c.
units.tr: The antecedent is proved by an induction of promises, which are not indeed transcribed word for word, but are fittingly applied to the argument: Isaiah 54:10, Isaiah 46:4, Jeremiah 32, Psalm 37:24, Matthew 12:20, Matthew 24:24, Philippians 1, He who began, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur authoritate Augustini qui hoc argumentum opponit Semipelagianis initio libri de bono perseverantiae ex Ier.32. Dabo eis timorem meum, ut non recedant a me, h.e. inquit Augustinus, ut mihi PERSEVERANTER adhaereant.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by the authority of Augustine, who sets this argument against the Semipelagians at the beginning of his book on the gift of perseverance, from Jeremiah 32: I will put my fear in them, that they may not depart from me; that is, says Augustine, that they may cling to me PERSEVERINGLY.

units.la: V. Ab efficacia intercessionis Christi pro fide & perseverantia Electorum. Deducatur ex Ioh.17. & Luc.22. Oravi pro tene, &c.
units.tr: V. From the efficacy of Christ's intercession for the faith and perseverance of the elect. Let it be deduced from John 17 and Luke 22: I have prayed for you, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur à contrario per absurdum: Si Petri fides defecit vel ad momentum: vana fuit promissio & intercessio.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the contrary, through absurdity: If the faith of Peter failed even for a moment, then the promise and the intercession were in vain.

units.la: Transferatur hypothesis ad thesin: Sic omnium electorum fidem non deficere, vi intercessionis Christi.
units.tr: Let the hypothesis be transferred to the thesis: Thus the faith of all the elect does not fail, by the power of Christ's intercession.

units.la: Ratio: Quia pro omnibus valet intercessio, Ioh.12. Non pro his tantum rogo, &c.
units.tr: Reason: because the intercession is valid for all, John 12: I do not pray for these only, etc.

units.la: VI. A precibus sanctorum, quæ certò exaudiun-tur. Quicquid petieritis: Petunt autem perseverantiam. Marc.9. Opem sir[?], &c. Adauge nobis fidem: Ne inducas nos, &c.
units.tr: VI. From the prayers of the saints, which are certainly heard: Whatever you ask. Now they ask for perseverance. Mark 9: Help [?], etc. Increase our faith; Lead us not [into temptation], etc.

units.la: VII. Spiritus est arrha sanctorum perpetua. Ioh.14.16. Eph.4. Ergo & fides eorum perpetua.
units.tr: VII. The Spirit is the perpetual pledge of the saints. John 14:16, Ephesians 4. Therefore their faith is perpetual too.

units.la: VIII. A similibus Scripturæ comparantis sanctos arbori plantatæ ad rivos & semper viren-ti: Psal.1. monti Sionis immobili Psal.125. 1. Viro prudenti ædificanti super petram. Matt.7. 24.
units.tr: VIII. From the similes of Scripture, which compare the saints to a tree planted by streams and always green, Psalm 1; to Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, Psalm 125; to the wise man building upon the rock, Matthew 7:24.

units.la: Ostendatur hinc sequi certam perseverantiam.
units.tr: Let it be shown that a certain perseverance follows from these.

units.la: IX. Fides electorum non est πρόσκαιρ[?]ος. Ergo perseverans. Probatio antecedentis.
units.tr: IX. The faith of the elect is not temporary [?]. Therefore it persists. Proof of the antecedent.

units.la: 1. quia πρόσκαιρος non est vera: Ex parabola Matth.13. πρόσκαιροι non habent radicem: Ergo est simulata: sicut arbor carens radice est simulacrum arboris, non vera arbor.
units.tr: (1) Because the temporary is not true: from the parable of Matthew 13, the temporary ones have no root; therefore their faith is feigned, just as a tree lacking a root is the image of a tree, not a true tree.

units.la: 2. quia πρόσκαιροι non sunt electi. Ostendatur ex 1.Ioh. 2: quia egredientes ex Ecclesia non sunt de Ecclesia: proinde nec electi.
units.tr: (2) Because the temporary ones are not the elect. It is shown from 1 John 2: because those who go out from the Church are not of the Church, and therefore not the elect either.

units.la: x A fine seu Usu hujus doctrinæ, qui triplex ostendatur.
units.tr: x From the end or use of this doctrine, which is shown to be threefold.

units.la: 1. Vt veritas promissionum divinarum de salute electorum stabiliatur.
units.tr: (1) So that the truth of the divine promises concerning the salvation of the elect may be established.

units.la: 2. Vt efficacia intercessionis Christi sit salva.
units.tr: (2) So that the efficacy of Christ's intercession may be kept safe.

units.la: 3. Vt consolatio piorum in lapsib. contra desperationem confirmet.
units.tr: (3) So that the consolation of the godly in their falls may be confirmed against despair.

units.la: x 1. Sit amplificatio prioris ab incommodis doctrinæ contrariæ de fluxa sanctorum fide & dubia electorum salute:
units.tr: x (1) Let the first point be amplified from the disadvantages of the contrary doctrine, which teaches that the faith of the saints wavers and the salvation of the elect is doubtful:

units.la: Enumerentur quædam, & ex superioribus deducantur.
units.tr: Let some be enumerated, and deduced from what has gone before.
