units.la: 1. Evertit fidem vitæ æternæ.
units.tr: (1) It overthrows the faith of eternal life.

units.la: 2. Stabilit ἐπιχλῳ[?] papisticam.
units.tr: (2) It establishes the Papist [?].

units.la: 3. Labefactat consolationem in lucta[?].
units.tr: (3) It weakens the consolation in the struggle [?].

units.la: 4. Amorem Dei & Deum ipsum facit mutabilem.
units.tr: (4) It makes the love of God, and God himself, changeable.

units.la: 5. Negat vim intercessionis Christi.
units.tr: (5) It denies the power of Christ's intercession.

units.la: 6. Denique promissiones omnes de certa electorum salute in dubium vocat.
units.tr: (6) Finally, it calls into doubt all the promises concerning the certain salvation of the elect.

units.la: Conclusio sit hortatio, ut scrutetur Scripturam, & ex ea potius, quam ex calumniis adversariorum hanc doctrinam æstimet: Et pollicitatio uberioris declarationis, si quid vel non satis assequatur, vel ad objecta sibi responderi velit.
units.tr: The conclusion is an exhortation that people should search the Scripture, and judge this doctrine from it rather than from the slanders of the adversaries; and a promise of fuller explanation, if he does not sufficiently grasp something, or wishes answers to the objections raised against him.

units.la: Exercitatio XXVII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXVII.

units.la: Scribatur Parodia metrica precationis Hizkiæ oranti pro defensione Vrbis & Ecclesiæ contra Assyrios blasphemos. 2. Reg. 19. HOC EST, Precatio Ecclesiæ ad Christum pro defensione sui contra rabiem hostium.
units.tr: A metrical parody of the prayer of Hezekiah, praying for the defence of the city and the Church against the blasphemous Assyrians. 2 Kings 19. THAT IS, The prayer of the Church to Christ for the defence of itself against the fury of its enemies.

units.la: EXordium ex ver. 15. fit Apostrophe ad Christum à descriptione ejus personæ & officii:
units.tr: The exordium, from verse 15, is an apostrophe to Christ, drawn from a description of his person and office:

units.la: 1. quod æterni Patris æterna soboles.
units.tr: (1) that he is the eternal offspring of the eternal Father;

units.la: 2. quod mundus per eum factus, gestetur verbo ejus potente:
units.tr: (2) that the world was made through him and is sustained by his powerful word;

units.la: 3. quod descenderit de cœlo, assumta carne propter nostram salutem.
units.tr: (3) that he came down from heaven, assuming flesh for our salvation;

units.la: 4. quod mortuus & suscitatus pro nobis.
units.tr: (4) that he died and was raised again for us;

units.la: 5. quod ad dextram Dei evectus, rex & caput nostrum dominetur in medio inimicorum.
units.tr: (5) that, exalted to the right hand of God, he reigns as our king and head in the midst of his enemies.

units.la: Propositio ex ver. 16. fit petitio, ut videat angustias audiat preces Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: The propositio, from verse 16, is a petition that he would look upon our distress and hear the prayers of the Church.

units.la: Ratio ex eodem: ab hostium furore, blasphemiis & insolentia in ipsum. ver. 16. Probris afficit Deum viventem.
units.tr: The ratio, from the same verse: the fury, blasphemies and insolence of the enemies against him. Verse 16: They insult the living God with reproaches.

units.la: Explicentur & probentur singula.
units.tr: Let each point be explained and proved.

units.la: 1. Furor ex vastatione Ecclesiarum & Scholarum, sævitia in pios, exiliis, carcere, eversione fortunarum & animarum: conspiratione in oppressionem ac necem nostram.
units.tr: (1) The fury shows itself in the devastation of Churches and schools, cruelty against the godly, exiles, prison, the overthrow of fortunes and lives, and conspiracy for our oppression and destruction.

units.la: 2. Blasphemiæ, ex damnatione fidei Orthodoxæ: quasi sit diabolica hæresis credere, quod vere sis caro nostra, vere mortuus, suscitatus, e-vectus in cœlum,&c.
units.tr: (2) The blasphemies consist in the condemnation of the orthodox faith, as if it were a diabolical heresy to believe that you truly became our flesh, truly died, were raised, and were taken up into heaven, and so on.

units.la: Item ex blasphemis eorum dogmatibus, quod ipsa divinitas sit passa, mortua: quod caro diffusa ubique, etiam in sordibus & gehenna: quod sis numen crustaceum, impuro impiorum ore deglutiendum: quod sis idolum fortunæ, defalvā-dis & damnandis nihil definiti habens: quod sanguine tuo mundaveris etiam damnatos in gehe-na : inque sinum & gratiam Dei reposueris o-mnes impios canes & porcos nunquam salvan-dos, non minus quam Petrum, Paulum, & fideles alios: quod sit dubia piorum fides, perseverantia & salus: quod oves electæ perire possint.
units.tr: Likewise, from their blasphemous doctrines: that the divinity itself suffered and died; that the flesh is spread everywhere, even in filth and in hell; that you are a crustaceous deity, to be swallowed by the impure mouth of the impious; that you are an idol of fortune, having nothing definite to say about the saved and the damned; that by your blood you cleansed even the damned in hell, and restored to the bosom and favour of God all impious dogs and swine who will never be saved, no less than Peter, Paul and the other faithful; that the faith, perseverance and salvation of the godly are doubtful; that the elect sheep can perish.

units.la: 3. Insolentia: ex superbis & virulentis scriptis, quorum argumentum breviter cum oratione Rabsacis[?] comparetur & efformetur oratio superbe dehortantium nos à possessione veritatis: & invitantium ut subscribamus blasphemiis Bergicis.
units.tr: (3) The insolence appears in proud and virulent writings. Their argument should be briefly compared with the speech of Rabshakeh[?], and there should be framed a speech of proud men dissuading us from possessing the truth and inviting us to subscribe to the Belgic blasphemies.

units.la: Exordium sit ἀποστροφῆς[?] sarcastica ad Ecclesias afflictas: Quæ isthæc fiducia vestra? verfic.
units.tr: The exordium is a sarcastic apostrophe to the afflicted Churches: What is this confidence of yours? Verse

units.la: Propositio: ex ver.31. Ne auscultetis Hizkia vestro, transfigite nobiscum.
units.tr: The propositio, from verse 31: Do not listen to your Hezekiah; make peace with us.

units.la: Ratio 1. ex ver.21.22. à necessario: Estis deserti à sociis Helvetiis, Gallis, Anglis, & à Deo.
units.tr: Reason 1, from verses 21–22, from the necessary: You have been deserted by your allies, the Swiss, the French, the English, and by God.

units.la: Prob.quod à sociis, 1. Sunt baculus arundineus.
units.tr: Proof that (you were deserted) by allies: 1. They are a reed staff.

units.la: 2.Sūt remoti. 3. occupati bellis, & sui defensione. Quod à Deo, per occup. Est à vobis offensus de-molitione altarium, statuarum, &c.
units.tr: 2. They are remote. 3. They are occupied with wars and their own defence. That (you were deserted) by God is proved by the occupation: you have offended him by the demolition of altars, statues, etc.

units.la: Ratio II. ex ver.8.9. à necessario: Estis pau-ci & virib. impares potentiae tot principum, magnatum, &c.
units.tr: The ratio (3), from verse 25, from what is honourable, or from God's command, that they should destroy our Churches.

units.la: Ratio III. ex ver.25. ab honesto seu Dei jus-su, ut delcant nostras Ecclesias.
units.tr: Proof (1): from the nature of our doctrine, and from its ... because we deny the omnipotence of God, overturn the Testament of Christ, and so on. They themselves defend the majesty of Christ, and so on.

units.la: Prob. I à genere doctrinae nostrae & su[?] quia nos negemus omnipotentiam Dei, evertamus Testamentum Christi, &c. Ipsi defendant majestatem Christi, &c.
units.tr: (2) from the successes of their doctrine, which everywhere makes great additions.

units.la: 2. à successibus doctrinae ipsorum, quae magnas Vbique faciat accessiones.
units.tr: The ratio (4), from verse 13, from the advantage or benefits of subscription: (1) Each of you shall eat of his own vine; (2) you will gain the favour of the whole Roman empire.

units.la: Ratio IV. ex versic.13. ab utili seu commodis subscriptionis 1. Comedetis unusquisque de vite vestra. 2. Inibitis gratiam totius imperii Romani.
units.tr: The ratio (5), from verses 33, 34 and 35, is a sarcastic reproach of the death of godly princes, heard everywhere: Where now is the God of the Calvinists, Casimir? Where is Christian of Saxony? and so on?

units.la: Ratio V. ex v.33. 34. 35. est farcastica expro-bratio mortis piorum principum passim audita? Vbi nunc Calvinistarum Deus CASIMIRUS? Vbi CHRISTIANUS Saxo? &c.?
units.tr: Let it be closed with a pathetic epiphonema: Alas, by such men now the highest and the lowest insult us.

units.la: Claudatur epiphonemate pathetico: Talibus proh dolor jam summi & infimi nobis insultant.
units.tr: Let there be added, by way of contrast, a fourth part of the prayer, a brief refutation consisting of verse 18.

units.la: Per adversativum subjiciatur quarta pars pre-cationis, brevis confutatio ex ver.18. constans.
units.tr: Next, by way of contrast, a fourth part of the prayer is added, consisting of a brief refutation drawn from verse 18.

units.la: 1. Concessione primae, secundae, quartae & quin-tae rationis, h.e, confessione defectionis, atq; im-becillitatis, quam exprobrant, & commodorum, quae promittunt, & peccatorum, quibus offen-sus Deus, Ecclesiam tantis heroibus & patronis privet.
units.tr: 1. By conceding the first, second, fourth and fifth reasons, that is, by confessing the defection and weakness that they reproach you with, and the advantages they promise, and the sins by which God has been offended, let him deprive the Church of such heroes and patrons.

units.la: II. Negatione, 1. quod Ecclesia nitatur humanis præsidiis, aut confidat principibus.
units.tr: II. By denying: 1. that the Church relies on human protections or trusts in princes.

units.la: 2. quod propter demolitionem altarium & Idololatriæ patiatur.
units.tr: (3) that it denies the omnipotence of God or the testament of Christ;

units.la: 3. quod neget omnipotentiam Dei, vel testamentum Christi.
units.tr: 3. that it denies the omnipotence of God or the testament of Christ.

units.la: 4. quod successus hostium sint approbatio ipsorum doctrinæ.
units.tr: 4. that the successes of the enemies are an approval of their doctrine.

units.la: Epilogus ex ver.19. repetat precationem, ut conservet lucem veritatis, pacem & hospitia Ecclesiæ in his regionibus, avertat tenebras & vastitatem barbaricam, coherceat minas & blasphemias superborum.
units.tr: The epilogue, from verse 19, repeats the prayer that he would preserve the light of truth, the peace and the hospitality of the Church in these regions, turn away the darkness and barbarian devastation, and restrain the threats and blasphemies of the proud.

units.la: Addat breviter rationes.
units.tr: He should add the reasons briefly.

units.la: 1. à fiducia Ecclesiæ cujus ipse sit Rex & servator, Tu Deus noster.
units.tr: 1. From the trust of the Church, whose King and keeper he himself is: "Thou, O God, art our God."

units.la: 2. ab effectu liberationis gemino: ut à nobis celebretur: & ut hostium blasphemiæ refutentur: ver.19. Vt agnoscant omnia regna terræ, &c.
units.tr: 2. From the twofold effect of the deliverance: that it may be celebrated by us, and that the blasphemies of the enemies may be refuted: verse 19, "That all the kingdoms of the earth may know..."

units.la: Exercitat. XXVIII.
units.tr: Exercitation XXVIII.

units.la: Progymnasma de causis malorum in mundo grassantium.
units.tr: Progymnasma on the causes of the evils that rage in the world.

units.la: Exordium sit brevis & pathetica narratio de malis quibus nunc quatitur & urgetur mundus: ut sunt, bella, dissidia, sterilitas, caritas, pestis, &c. & de querela vulgi ac pontificiorum, quod eorum causa sit doctrina Evangelii damnans & tollens Idolorum cultum.
units.tr: Let the exordium be a brief and moving narrative of the evils by which the world is now shaken and oppressed: such as wars, dissensions, barrenness, dearth, plague, and so on; and of the complaint of the common people and of the Papists, that the doctrine of the Gospel, which condemns and removes the worship of idols, is the cause of them.

units.la: Amplificatio: Etiam olim Judæos Jeremiæ & Romanos Christianis hoc objecisse, malorum causam esse, quod ab ipsis Dii non colerentur.
units.tr: By way of amplification: that in former times too the Jews objected to Jeremiah, and the Romans to the Christians, that the cause of evils was that the gods were not worshipped by them.

units.la: Propositio per adversat.Sed esse alias causas.
units.tr: Proposition, by way of opposition: but that there are other causes.

units.la: Subjiciatur causarum ἐνστάσεις[?].
units.tr: Let the objections to the causes be set out [?].

units.la: I. Defectus naturalis mundi senéscentis, & ad interitum vergentis.
units.tr: I. The natural decline of a world that is growing old and tending towards its end.

units.la: Ratio: quia lex Dei est, ut omnia orta occidant & aucta senéscant, ac infirmata tandem deficiant.
units.tr: Reason: because it is the law of God that all things that have arisen should perish, and that things which have grown should grow old, and that what has been weakened should at last fail.

units.la: Ἐξήγησις[?]: Sol in occasu radios minus claros spargit: Item exemplo fontium, arborum, hominum, quorum vires in senecta deficiunt. Applicetur ad ætatem mundi. Vide Cyprianum contra Demetrianum.
units.tr: Explanation [?]: The sun, in setting, sends out rays that are less bright. Likewise, by the example of springs, trees and men, whose strength fails in old age. Let it be applied to the age of the world. See Cyprian, against Demetrianus.

units.la: II. Impletio oraculorum Malachiæ, Christi, &c.
units.tr: II. The fulfilment of the prophecies of Malachi, of Christ, and so on.

units.la: III. Sunt pœnæ idololatriæ & aliorum peccatorum in mundo grassantium. Ratio à providentia, justitia & veritate Dei in comminationibus. Deut. cap. 28. Hagg. 1. Eo quod domus mea deserta est, &c. propterea cœlum abstinebit à rore.
units.tr: III. There are punishments for idolatry and for other sins that rage in the world. The reason is drawn from the providence, justice and truthfulness of God in his threatenings: Deut. ch. 28; Hagg. 1: "Because my house lies desolate, therefore the heaven withholds its dew."

units.la: Applicetur per βλωον[?]: Sic hodie mala accidunt, non quia papistarum idola à nobis non coluntur, sed quia ab ipsis non recte colitur verus Deus.
units.tr: Let it be applied by way of [?]: So today evils befall, not because the idols of the Papists are not worshipped by us, but because the true God is not rightly worshipped by them.

units.la: IV. Sunt pœnæ persecutionum Ecclesiæ & piorum.
units.tr: IV. There are punishments for the persecutions of the Church and of the godly.

units.la: Obiectio. Etiam pii malis implicantur: Non ergo sunt pœnæ eos persequentium. Resp. 1. propter consortium mundi : intra u-nam domum boni & mali versantes communem sortem domus perpetiuntur.
units.tr: Objection: the godly too are caught up in evils; therefore these are not punishments of those who persecute them. Answer: (1) on account of fellowship with the world: good and evil living within one house suffer the common lot of the house;

units.la: 2. Habent interim consolationem ex Christi gratia.
units.tr: (2) meanwhile they have consolation from the grace of Christ;

units.la: 3. Sciunt se probari malis.
units.tr: (3) they know that they are tested by evils;

units.la: 4. Habent spem certam liberationis & salu-taris exitus futurae nimirum gloriae in coelis. Ro-man.5. & 8.
units.tr: (4) they have a certain hope of deliverance and of a safe outcome, namely future glory in heaven. Rom. 5 and 8.

units.la: Exercitatio XXIX.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXIX.

units.la: Ferias Sanctorum esse abolendas in Ec-clesia Christiana.
units.tr: That the feast days of the Saints are to be abolished in the Christian Church.

units.la: NArretur de multitudine feriarum in Papa-tu, quae Sanctis consecratae magna ex parte etiam ab Evangelicis retinentur.
units.tr: Let us speak of the multitude of feast days in the Papacy, which, consecrated to the saints, are to a large extent still retained even by the Evangelicals.

units.la: Propositio: per [illegible, ~10 letters] : Etsi speciose defendi soleant : tamen recte in nostris Ecclesiis abrogatas esse.
units.tr: Proposition: by [illegible, ~10 letters]: Although they are commonly defended with fair-sounding arguments, nevertheless they have rightly been abrogated in our Churches.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia festa soli Deo dicata esse de-beant.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because festivals ought to be dedicated to God alone.

units.la: Prob. 1. a Dei mandato. Exod.20. Erit Sabb. Domino Deo tuo. Lev.23.& 26. Sabbatha mea cu-stodietis.
units.tr: Proof 1. From the command of God. Exod. 20: The Sabbath is to the Lord your God. Lev. 23 and 26: You shall keep my Sabbaths.

units.la: 2. a forma cultus feriarum, ut solennis invo-catio, gratiarum actio, &c. quies a labore, &c. soli Deo debetur, quia solus creator & largitor bo-norum omnipotens & omnipraesens. Deut.6. Matt.4. Ipsi soli servies.
units.tr: 2. From the nature of the worship of feast days, such as solemn invocation, thanksgiving, etc., and rest from labour, etc., which is due to God alone, because he alone is the creator and bountiful giver of good things, almighty and omnipresent. Deut. 6; Matt. 4: Him only shall you serve.

units.la: 3. asme: Usus feriarum est non tantum quies corporum sed præcipuè animarum sanctificatio quæ solius Dei est beneficium. Ego Deus sanctifi-ficans vos. Erò eis in sanctificationem. Christus nobis factus sanctificatio.
units.tr: 3. The purpose of feast days is not merely the rest of bodies but especially the sanctification of souls, which is a benefit of God alone: I am the Lord who sanctifies you. I will be to them for sanctification. Christ is made to us sanctification.

units.la: Claudatur argumentum antithesi: Ergo festa in honorem creaturarum instituta ab hominib. sunt nefasta & abolenda.
units.tr: Let the argument be closed by antithesis: Therefore feast days instituted by men in honour of creatures are unlawful and to be abolished.

units.la: Ratio II. Ab exemplo veteris Ecclesiæ, quæ festa creaturarum vel sanctorum Mosis, Abrahami, Davidis, &c. nulla habuit.
units.tr: Reason II. From the example of the ancient Church, which had no feast days for the creatures or saints such as Moses, Abraham, David, etc.

units.la: Item, Apostolicę, quæ nullas Baptistæ, Stephano, Iacobo, &c. protomartyribus ferias dicavit.
units.tr: Likewise, from the Apostolic Church, which did not dedicate days to John the Baptist, Stephen, James, etc., the first martyrs.

units.la: Ratio III. Cultus sanctorum est idololatria prohibita 1. & 2. præcepto. Sed festa sanctorum cultus causa sunt instituta.
units.tr: Reason III. The cult of saints is the idolatry forbidden in the first and second commandments. But feast days of the saints have been instituted for the sake of this cult.

units.la: Ratio IV. Quia Ecclesiam Christi in paganismum transformant.
units.tr: Reason IV. Because they transform the Church of Christ into paganism.

units.la: Probatio 1. quia gentiles dies festos non Deo sed Divis & creaturis dicabant. Ostendatur breviter aliquot exemplis festorum, quę à quib. gentilib. quibus numinibus, & cur dicata fuerint: A Græcis, Gamelia Iunoni Gameliæ: Lynæa Bac-cho, Elaphebolia Dianæ Venatrici, Chronia Saturno, &c. A Romanis Agonalia Jano, Carmentalia Carmentæ, Ambarvalia Cereri, Paganalia Diis tutelaribus, Bacchanalia Baccho, Saturnalia Saturno, &c.
units.tr: Proof 1. Because the Gentiles dedicated their feast days not to God but to the deified heroes and creatures. Let some examples of festivals be briefly shown, with the Gentiles to whom, the deities, and why they were dedicated: among the Greeks, the Gamelia to Juno Gamelia; the Lynaea to Bacchus; the Elaphebolia to Diana the Huntress; the Chronia to Saturn, etc. Among the Romans, the Agonalia to Janus, the Carmentalia to Carmenta, the Ambarvalia to Ceres, the Paganalia to the tutelary gods, the Bacchanalia to Bacchus, the Saturnalia to Saturn, etc.

units.la: Probatio 2. quia pleraque ex Paganismo in Christianismum sint traducta mutatis nominib.
units.tr: Proof 2. Because most things were carried over from paganism into Christianity with their names changed.

units.la: Ostendatur exemplis Bacchanaliorum, Am-barvaliorum, &c. Et authoritate Gregorii, qui lib. 9. epist. 71. præcipit festa Paganorum sensim in Christiana esse commutanda, & quædam ad eorum similitudinem facienda.
units.tr: Let it be shown by the examples of the Bacchanalia, the Ambarvalia, etc., and by the authority of Gregory, who in book 9, letter 71, directs that the feasts of the pagans are gradually to be changed into Christian ones, and certain things made in their likeness.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Sunt Deo in sanctis dicatæ.
units.tr: Objection 1. They are dedicated to God in the saints.

units.la: Resp. 1. Contra Dei mandatum.
units.tr: Answer 1. This is against the command of God.

units.la: 2. ἐθελοθρησκεία[?] displicent Deo, Matt.15.
units.tr: 2. Self-chosen worship [ἐθελοθρησκεία] displeases God, Matt. 15.

units.la: 3. per βίαιον[?]: quia sanctis: ergo non Deo: nam Deus non vult coli cum sanctis: Gloriam meam alteri non dabo.
units.tr: 3. By forced [βίαιον]: because it is to the saints, therefore not to God; for God does not wish to be worshipped together with the saints: My glory I will not give to another.

units.la: Instantia: Sancti coluntur ἀληθείας[?] Deus λα-τρείας.
units.tr: Instance: The saints are honoured with veneration [ἀληθείας], God with latria [λατρείας].

units.la: Respon. 1. Uterque cultus soli Deo debetur Roman.cap.1.9. Rom.12.11. Rom.16.18. Eph.6.7. 1.Thess.1.9.
units.tr: Answer 1. Both forms of worship are due to God alone: Rom. 1:9; Rom. 12:11; Rom. 16:18; Eph. 6:7; 1 Thess. 1:9.

units.la: 2. Sancti supra Deum honorantur quia ἀληθεία est major quid quam λατρεία.
units.tr: 2. The saints are honoured above God, because veneration [ἀληθεία] is something greater than latria [λατρεία].

units.la: Obiectio 11. Sunt memoriis Sanctorum consecratæ.
units.tr: Objection II. Memorials of the saints have been consecrated.

units.la: Respon. 1. Contra authoritatem Scripturæ.
units.tr: Answer 1. This is against the authority of Scripture.

units.la: 2. Memoriæ etiam sine feriis vigere possunt.
units.tr: 2. Memorials can also flourish without feast days.

units.la: 3. Invexerunt horribiles errores & impios cultus: intercessionem & invocationem mortuorum, cultum reliquiarum, peregrinationes religiosas, &c.
units.tr: 3. They have introduced horrible errors and impious cults: the intercession and invocation of the dead, the cult of relics, religious pilgrimages, etc.

units.la: Obiectio 111. Exempla fidei & constantiæ sanctorum excitant ad imitationem.
units.tr: Objection III. The examples of the faith and constancy of the saints stir us to imitation.

units.la: Respons. 1. Non facienda mala ut eveniant bona: ad excitandam imitationem non opus est feriis, sed doctrinæ meditatione & studio. Hebr. 12.7. Memores estote ducum vestrorum qui locuti sunt vobis sermonem Dei, quorum imitamini fidem, considerantes, &c. Est ergo fallacia non causæ.
units.tr: Answer 1. Evils are not to be done that good may come of them: to stir up imitation there is no need of feast days, but of meditation on and study of doctrine. Heb. 12:7: Remember your leaders, who spoke to you the word of God, whose faith imitate, considering, etc. It is therefore a fallacy of the non-cause.

units.la: 2. à contrario. Ferias sanctorum in toto Papatu servire ocio, crapulæ, profanitati, &c.
units.tr: 2. From the contrary. Throughout the whole Papacy the feast days of the saints serve idleness, drunkenness, profanity, etc.

units.la: Obiectio i v. Sunt longa consuetudine receptæ.
units.tr: Objection IV. They have been received by long custom.

units.la: Resp.ex regula. Non exemplis aut consuetudine sed legibus & verbo Dei judicandum.
units.tr: Answer from the rule. Judgment is to be made not by examples or custom but by laws and the Word of God.

units.la: Obiectio v. Ecclesia habet potestatem instituendi festa. Roman. 14. Qui curat diem Domino curat, &c.
units.tr: Objection V. The Church has the power of instituting feast days. Rom. 14: He who observes the day observes it for the Lord, etc.

units.la: Respond. i. negatione antecedentis, quia festum diem instituere est cultum Dei instituere, quod non est Ecclesiæ sed solius Dei.
units.tr: Answer 1. By denying the antecedent, because to institute a feast day is to institute the worship of God, which belongs not to the Church but to God alone.

units.la: 2. distinctione: Ecclesia potest instituere dies festos ad ordinem pertinentes, ut diem Dominicum, jejunii, precum, &c. sed sine obligatione conscientiarum, aut opinione necessitatis & cultus divini.
units.tr: 2. By distinction: The Church can institute feast days that pertain to order, such as the Lord's day, of fasting, of prayers, etc., but without binding consciences or the opinion of necessity and divine worship.

units.la: 3. Dictum Pauli loquitur de Judaico discrimine dierum, quod in illa mutatione legalis cultus erat ἀδιάφορον[?]: non autem de feriis superstitiosis sanctorum.
units.tr: 3. The saying of Paul speaks of the Jewish distinction of days, which in that change of legal worship was indifferent [ἀδιάφορον]; but not of the superstitious feast days of the saints.

units.la: Conclusio. Etsi pleræque feriæ & memoriæ sanctorum bono zelo antiquitus institutæ fuerint: tamen cum & verbo Dei repugnent, & magnis erroribus in Ecclesia occasionem dederint, recte eas aboleri.
units.tr: Conclusion. Although most feast days and memorials of the saints were instituted in antiquity from a good zeal, nevertheless, since they both conflict with the Word of God and have given occasion for great errors in the Church, they have rightly been abolished.

units.la: Exercitatio XXX.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXX.

units.la: Epistola consolatoria contra scandalum defectionis multorum à fide.
units.tr: Letter of consolation against the scandal of the defection of many from the faith.

units.la: EXordium fit querela de crescente mundi pro-sanitate & levitate multorum ac magnorum deficientium ab Ecclesia Orthodoxa ad Papismum propter compendia mundana: & de piorum scandalo inde nascente.
units.tr: The introduction is a lament over the growing depravity and fickleness of the world, and over the many great men who fall away from the Orthodox Church to Papism for worldly advantages, and over the scandal this brings to the godly.

units.la: Ἀπολογία breviter exponens rationes scandali:
units.tr: A brief statement of the reasons for the scandal:

units.la: 1. quod in animis infirmorum labefactetur certitudo doctrinæ Evangelicæ.
units.tr: (1) that the certainty of Evangelical doctrine is weakened in the minds of the weak;

units.la: 2. quod hostes triumphent & confirmentur in suis erroribus ac superstitionibus,
units.tr: (2) that the enemies triumph and are confirmed in their errors and superstitions;

units.la: 3. quod Ecclesia videatur minui.
units.tr: (3) that the Church seems to be diminished;

units.la: 4. quod videatur everti doctrina de perseverantia sanctorum.
units.tr: (4) that the doctrine of the perseverance of the saints seems to be overthrown;

units.la: 5. quod Ecclesia videatur nudari præsidiis externis si potentes deficiant. (Nota: defecerat eo anno x c i i i. Heinricus IV. Rex Navarræus ab Orthodoxia ad Papatum regni Gallici causa.)
units.tr: (5) that the Church seems to be stripped of external supports if the powerful desert it. (Note: in that year, 1593, Henry IV, King of Navarre, had defected from Orthodoxy to Rome for the sake of the kingdom of France.)

units.la: Propositio per adversat. Sed pios non debere turbari.
units.tr: Proposition by way of objection. But the godly ought not to be disturbed.

units.la: Consolationis Argumentum I. ab oraculis divinis de apostasia multorum à fide. 1. Tim. 4. 2. Tim. 3. &c. quorum eventus nec admirationem nec offensionem habere debet, quod ostendatur ex fine prædictionis. Ioh. 16.
units.tr: First argument of consolation, from the divine oracles concerning the apostasy of many from the faith: 1 Tim. 4; 2 Tim. 3; etc. Their fulfilment ought to cause neither wonder nor offence; this is shown from the purpose of the prediction: John 16.

units.la: Argumentum II. ab exemplis: quod multi jam olim à doctrina ipsius Christi & apostolorû defecerint.Ioh.6.1.Tim.1.20.2.Tim.2.17.
units.tr: Second argument, from examples: that many have already from of old fallen away from the teaching of Christ himself and of the apostles: John 6; 1 Tim. 1:20; 2 Tim. 2:17.

units.la: Amplificetur à persona Judæ, qui fuit apostolus & proditor.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the person of Judas, who was an apostle and a traitor.

units.la: Πόεσμα[?] contra 1. rationem scandali: Apostasiis igitur non labefactari doctrinam Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Conclusion [?] against the first reason for scandal: therefore the doctrine of the Church is not weakened by apostasies.

units.la: Addatur ratio: quia non hominum authoritate, sed verbo Dei nitatur.
units.tr: Let the reason be added: because it rests not on the authority of men but on the Word of God.

units.la: Illustretur noëmate Tertulliani: Ex personis probamus fidem, an ex fide personas? De præscript. hærct.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated by the saying of Tertullian: Do we prove the faith from the persons, or the persons from the faith? On the Prescription against Heretics.

units.la: Argumentum III. à commodo ecclesiæ:
units.tr: Third argument, from the advantage of the Church:

units.la: 1. quod fides ejus probatur: An & vos vultis abire. Ioh.6. Tertullian: Ad hæc sunt hæreses, ut fi-des habendo tentationem etiam haberet probatio-nem:
units.tr: (1) that its faith is thereby tested: Will you also go away? John 6. Tertullian: Heresies exist so that, while faith is being tested, it may also have its proving.

units.la: 2. quod ipsa purgetur à paleis: Tertullianus: Ventilabrum in manu portat ad purgandam aream suam. Volent quantum volent paleæ levis fidei, quocunque afflatu tentationum: & purior massa frumenti in horrea Domini reponetur.
units.tr: (2) that it is itself purged of chaff: Tertullian: He carries the winnowing fan in his hand to cleanse his threshing floor. Let the chaff of light faith be blown away by whatever breath of temptation it likes; and the purer mass of wheat will be stored in the Lord's barn.

units.la: αἰτιολογία[?] à thesi: quod soli hypocritæ deficiant. Ex nobis egressi sunt, &c. 1.Ioh.2. Planta quam non plantavit pater eradicabitur.
units.tr: Argument from the thesis [?]: that only hypocrites fall away. They went out from us, etc. 1 John 2. Every plant which my heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.

units.la: Amplificetur ἀντίθεσις[?]: quod electorum fides non deficiat: quoniam intercessio Christi, pro ea non deficit Luc.22.Ioh.17.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by the antithesis [?]: that the faith of the elect does not fail, since Christ's intercession for it does not fail: Luke 22; John 17.

units.la: Πόεσμα[?] 1. contra rationem III. scandali: Non minui Ecclesiam, cum paleæ non sint de tritico.
units.tr: Conclusion [?] 1, against the third reason for scandal: the Church is not diminished, since the chaff is not of the wheat.

units.la: II. Contra quartam rationem scandali: Non everti perseverantiam sanctorum, cum apostatæ[?] non fuerint veri sancti.
units.tr: II. Against the fourth reason for scandal: the perseverance of the saints is not overthrown, since the apostates were never true saints.

units.la: DIGRESSIO ἀνασκευαστικὴ[?], qua breviter respondeatur ad dicta & exempla Scripturæ in speciem contraria.
units.tr: DIGRESSION (ἀνασκευαστικὴ[?]), in which the statements and examples of Scripture that seem to be contrary are briefly answered.

units.la: 1. Etiam vere sancti dicûtur prolabi. Hebr. 6. & 10.
units.tr: 1. The truly holy are also said to fall away. Heb. 6 and 10.

units.la: Respon. 1. est comminatio conditionalis: Si prolabantur.
units.tr: Answer 1. It is a conditional threat: if they fall away.

units.la: 2. loquitur de temporariis, quorum fides, cum radicem non habeat: non est vera. Probetur ex textu, φωτισθέντας.[illegible, ~12 letters] : terra proferens spinas.
units.tr: 2. It speaks of the temporary, whose faith, since it has no root, is not true. Let this be proved from the text: φωτισθέντας.[illegible, ~12 letters]: the earth bringing forth thorns.

units.la: Amplificetur collatione hujus descriptionis hypocritarum cum illa Matt. 7. Domine, Domine, &c.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by comparing this description of hypocrites with that in Matt. 7: Lord, Lord, etc.

units.la: Item à contrario: quia apostolus ipse comminationem illam à sanctis removet: πεπεισμ[illegible, ~5 letters] δὲ [illegible, ~3 letters] ὑμῶν.
units.tr: Likewise, on the contrary: because the apostle himself removes that threat from the saints: πεπεισμ[illegible, ~5 letters] δὲ [illegible, ~3 letters] ὑμῶν.

units.la: 2. quia spem nostram vocat anchoram tutam ac firmam.
units.tr: 2. Because he calls our hope a sure and firm anchor.

units.la: II. Etiam qui verè effugerant inquinamenta mundi rursus implicati superantur. 2. Pet. 2.
units.tr: II. Those who had truly escaped the defilements of the world are again entangled and overcome. 2 Pet. 2.

units.la: Resp. 1. Etiam est conditionalis comminatio.
units.tr: Answer 1. This too is a conditional threat.

units.la: 2. Loquitur de hypocritis: Probetur ex textu:
units.tr: 2. It speaks of hypocrites. Let this be proved from the text:

units.la: 1. Vocat ψυχὰς ἀστηρίκτους etiam nondum inescatas[?], ver.14.
units.tr: 1. He calls them unstable souls, ψυχὰς ἀστηρίκτους, even those not yet enticed[?], v. 14.

units.la: 2. Tantum historicam fidem eis tribuit, quod ostendatur ex ver.18.20.21.
units.tr: 2. He attributes to them only historical faith, as is shown from vv. 18, 20, 21.

units.la: 3. ex paroemia canis & suis.
units.tr: 3. From the proverb of the dog and the sow.

units.la: Instantia: ὄντως effugerant.
units.tr: Objection: ὄντως they had escaped.

units.la: Resp. 1. Lectio varia: ὀλίγον, ὀλίγως, ὄν-τως pro ὄν-τως.
units.tr: Answer 1. A variant reading: ὀλίγον, ὀλίγως, ὄντως instead of ὄντως.

units.la: 2. ὄντως externè: quo ad professionem & conditionem externam: quia se sociaverant Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: 2. ὄντως outwardly: as regards outward profession and condition, because they had joined themselves to the Church.

units.la: Probetur rursus ex parœmia: Sunt canes & porci: etiam antequam ad vomitum & volutabrum redeant, licet homines lateant.
units.tr: Let it be proved again from the proverb: "They are dogs and swine": even before they return to the vomit and the wallowing-place, although men may not know it.

units.la: Item ex eventu, qui testatur non fuisse de Ecclesia. 1. Ioh. 2.
units.tr: Likewise from the outcome, which testifies that they were not of the Church. 1 John 2.

units.la: 11. Etiam palmites aliqui de vite tolluntur & ejiciuntur. Ioh. 15.
units.tr: 11. Some branches too are taken away from the vine and cast out. John 15.

units.la: Resp. distinctione palmitum: tantùm steriles, fructum non ferentes: qui sunt hypocritæ: Christo non insiti: proinde nec veri palmites.
units.tr: Answer by a distinction of branches: only the barren, those not bearing fruit, who are hypocrites, not ingrafted into Christ; therefore not true branches either.

units.la: Probetur ex versiculo quarto: à contrario: nulli fructum ferentes excidunt, sed omnes purgantur. Fiat conversio.
units.tr: Let it be proved from verse four, by the contrary: none bearing fruit fall away, but all are purged. Let the statement be converted.

units.la: Instantia : ἐν ἐμοὶ[?] : Ergo insiti.
units.tr: Objection: ἐν ἐμοὶ[?]: therefore ingrafted.

units.la: Respon. non vere sed apparenter: vocatione, professione, specie, judicio hominum.
units.tr: Answer: not truly but in appearance: by calling, profession, outward show, and the judgment of men.

units.la: Ratio: quia soli fructum ferentes verè sunt insiti: quod ostendatur ex ver. 5. & 8.
units.tr: Reason: because only those bearing fruit are truly ingrafted, which is shown from vv. 5 and 8.

units.la: Explicetur & urgeatur quid sit esse insitum Christo: à causis & effectis: & concludatur contra hypocritas, in quibus nec causæ nec effecta ea verè exsistunt.
units.tr: Let it be explained and pressed what it is to be ingrafted into Christ, from causes and effects, and let the conclusion be drawn against hypocrites, in whom neither the causes nor the effects truly exist.

units.la: I v. Etiam rami verè insiti exciduntur. Ro-man.11.
units.tr: III. Even truly ingrafted branches are cut off. Rom. 11.

units.la: Respon. Negetur antecedens: 1. quia verè non est in textu.
units.tr: Answer. Let the antecedent be denied: 1. because it is not truly in the text.

units.la: 2. quia apostolus minatur excidii pœnam superbis,& non manentibus in benignitate. ver.20. 22. Tales autem non sunt vere insiti. i. Ioh. 2. Ex nobis non erant. Matth. 7. Nunquam novi vos.
units.tr: 2. because the apostle threatens the penalty of excision to the proud, and to those who do not remain in goodness, v. 20, 22. But such are not truly ingrafted. 1 John 2: They were not of us. Matt. 7: I never knew you.

units.la: Instantia 1. Rami naturales vere fuerunt insiti: & tamen excisi.
units.tr: Objection 1. Natural branches were truly ingrafted, and yet they were cut off.

units.la: Resp. 1. negatur antecedens: quia implicat contradictionem, naturalem & insitum ramum esse.
units.tr: Answer 1. The antecedent is denied, because it involves a contradiction for a natural branch to be also an ingrafted one.

units.la: 2. quia non nisi infideles Iudæi excisi sunt. ver.20.
units.tr: 2. because only unbelieving Jews were cut off, v. 20.

units.la: Explicetur quatenus hi rami naturales dicantur, nempe naturali propagatione ex patribus: successione, & professione fœderis fidelibus juxta & infidelibus Iudæis communi: Minimè vero naturali inexistentia in Christo aut fide.
units.tr: Let it be explained in what sense these branches are called natural: namely, by natural propagation from the fathers, by succession and by profession of the covenant, which was common to believing and unbelieving Jews alike; but certainly not by natural indwelling in Christ or in faith.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia natura erant filii iræ, sicut & cæteri.
units.tr: Reason 1. because by nature they were children of wrath, as were the others.

units.la: 2. quia fides non est naturalis.
units.tr: 2. because faith is not natural.

units.la: Instant. 11. Etiam gentibus vere insitis minatur excidium. v.17. Insitus es pro ipsis, & particeps, &c.
units.tr: Objection 2. Even Gentiles truly ingrafted are threatened with excision. v. 17: You were grafted in among them, and became partakers, etc.

units.la: Respon. 1. Loquitur de insitione gentium in corpus Ecclesiæ per externam vocationem, quæ in multis est sine fide.
units.tr: Answer 1. He speaks of the ingrafting of the Gentiles into the body of the Church through outward calling, which in many is without faith.

units.la: Probetur: quia de toto corpore gentium loquitur: Item de successione gentium in locum & jus commune Iudæorum, quod erat externæ vocationis ad fœdus.
units.tr: Let it be proved: because he speaks of the whole body of the Gentiles; likewise of the succession of the Gentiles into the place and common right of the Jews, which belonged to outward calling to the covenant.

units.la: 2. Comminatio habet conditionem superbæ apostasiæ, quæ in vere credentibus nunquam ponitur.
units.tr: 2. The threat has the condition of proud apostasy, which is never assumed in those truly believing.

units.la: Transitio ad exempla: quod multi gratia & fide penitus exciderint.
units.tr: Transition to examples: that many have altogether fallen away from grace and faith.

units.la: 1. Angelorum & primorum parentum.
units.tr: 1. Of the angels and of our first parents.

units.la: Resp. esse dissimilitudinem in exemplis: quia hi exciderint gratia creationis, non reparationis de qua hic est quæstio.
units.tr: Answer. There is a dissimilarity in the examples: for these fell from the grace of creation, not of restoration, which is the question here.

units.la: Explicetur utraque, & ostendatur dissimilitudo: quod illa fuerit mutabilis, quia pendens a natura & voluntate mutabiliter bona: hæc sit im-mutabilis, quia nitens perpetua intercessione Christi, ne deficiat fides nostra. Rom. 8. Luc. 22.
units.tr: Let each be explained, and the dissimilarity shown: the former was changeable, because it depended on nature and on a will changeably good; the latter is unchangeable, because it rests on the perpetual intercession of Christ, that our faith may not fail. Rom. 8; Luke 22.

units.la: II. Saulis. Resp. Fuisse hypocritam.
units.tr: II. Of Saul. Answer. He was a hypocrite.

units.la: Prob. 1. quia nusquam laudatur a pietate.
units.tr: Proof 1. because he is nowhere praised for piety.

units.la: 2. Exempla hypocriseos extant. 1.Sam.11.13. & 15.
units.tr: 2. Examples of hypocrisy are extant: 1 Sam. 11, 13, and 15.

units.la: 3. Ab eventu.
units.tr: 3. From the outcome.

units.la: Obiect. Habuit Spiritum Domini. Resp. Fortitudinis & prophetiæ non fidei & adoptionis.
units.tr: Objection. He had the Spirit of the Lord. Answer. The Spirit of courage and of prophecy, not of faith and adoption.

units.la: III. Davidis. Resp. Nunquam defecisse penitus, sed semen fidei in eo mansisse licet occultum: quod probetur ex testimonio Dei de ipso. 1.Sam.13.14. Item ex precatione Psal.51.13.
units.tr: III. Of David. Answer. He never utterly fell away, but the seed of faith remained in him, though hidden: which is proved from God's testimony about him, 1 Sam. 13:14, and likewise from his prayer, Ps. 51:13.

units.la: IV. Solomonis. Resp. per occup: Etsi multi eum damnent: tamen esse rationes, quod non penitus defecerit, & ex lapsu resipuerit.
units.tr: IV. Of Solomon. Answer, by way of occupation: Although many condemn him, yet there are reasons why he did not utterly fall away, and why he returned to repentance after his fall.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia habet testimonia veræ regenerationis nunquam plane emorientis. 2.Sam.7.14. Psal.89.27. Ero ei pater: ipse mihi filius. 1.Reg.3.3. Diligebat Deum, & ambulabat in viis patris Davidis. 2.Sam.12.25. Erat Jedidia.
units.tr: Reason 1. because he has the marks of true regeneration, which never wholly perish. 2 Sam. 7:14; Ps. 89:27: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. 1 Kings 3:3: He loved God and walked in the ways of his father David. 2 Sam. 12:25: He was Jedidiah.

units.la: 2. Quia habuit promissionem perpetuæ gratiæ Dei. 2.Sam.7.15.Psal.89.29.34.
units.tr: 2. because he had the promise of God's perpetual grace. 2 Sam. 7:15; Ps. 89:29, 34.

units.la: 3. Quæ sit occupatio obiectionis de promis-sione conditionali nisi deficeret: quia lapsuum pœnam Deus ei minatur non abiectionem sed castigationem. Pf.89.31.
units.tr: 3. The objection about a conditional promise, unless he should fail, is answered: because God threatens him with the penalty of his falls not as rejection but as chastisement. Ps. 89:31.

units.la: Inferatur ex consequenti antecedens: Ergo etiam promisit nunquam ita lapsurum, ut peni-tus abiiciendus esset.
units.tr: Let it be inferred from the consequent to the antecedent: therefore God also promised that he would never so fall that he would have to be utterly cast off.

units.la: 4. Ex Solomonis precatione pro gratia per-severantiæ. 1. Reg. 8.57. &c. quæ haud dubie est exaudita. 1.Reg.9.3.
units.tr: 4. From Solomon's prayer for the grace of perseverance. 1 Kings 8:57, etc., which was undoubtedly heard. 1 Kings 9:3.

units.la: 5. Quia totalis eius defectio à fide & cultu Dei non afstruitur in historia: quod ostendatur ex textu. 1.Reg.11.v.4.6. Cor eius non fuit perfectum sicut, &c. Non ergo penitus defecit, &c.
units.tr: 5. Because his total defection from faith and the worship of God is not asserted in the history: which is shown from the text. 1 Kings 11:4, 6: His heart was not perfect as, etc. Therefore he did not utterly fall away, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur collatione phraseos huius cum aliis, quibus totalis defectio & impietas notatur.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by comparing this phrase with others in which total defection and impiety are noted.

units.la: Item: ex causis impulsivis: Peccavit in senectute amore uxorum, &c. Non ergo malitia aut odio Dei, sed infirmitate, &c.
units.tr: Likewise, from the impelling causes: He sinned in old age through love of his wives, etc. Therefore not from malice or hatred of God, but from weakness, etc.

units.la: 6. Quia Scriptura habet argumenta non ob-scura eius resipiscentiæ.
units.tr: 6. Because Scripture contains clear arguments of his repentance.

units.la: 1. quod Roboam dicitur ambulasse triennio in via Davidis & Solomonis.2.Par.11.17.
units.tr: 1. that Rehoboam is said to have walked for three years in the way of David and Solomon. 2 Chron. 11:17.

units.la: 2. quod Ecclesiastes, de communi Hebræorum sententia, est Solomonis senis publica errorum παλινῳδία [?], peccatorum confessio, detestatio, & pœnitentia: cap.2.v.11.17.18.
units.tr: 2. that Ecclesiastes, according to the common opinion of the Hebrews, is the public palinode of an old Solomon, a confession of his errors and sins, a detestation of them, and repentance: ch. 2, vv. 11, 17, 18.

units.la: v. Simonis magi. Act.8. Hymenæi, & Alexan-dri.1.Tim.1. Phigelli & Hermogenis.2.Tim.1.15. Phileti. 2.Tim.2.17.
units.tr: v. Simon Magus, Acts 8. Hymenaeus and Alexander, 1 Tim. 1. Phygelus and Hermogenes, 2 Tim. 1:15. Philetus, 2 Tim. 2:17.

units.la: Resp. Fuisse hypocritas.
units.tr: Answer. They were hypocrites.

units.la: Obiect. Habuerunt fidem. Resp. Temporariæ: proinde non veram: quia nulla temporaria fides est vera, cum carear radice & fundaméto Matt.13.
units.tr: Objection. They had faith. Answer. Temporary faith, therefore not true faith: because no temporary faith is true, since it lacks root and foundation. Matt. 13.

units.la: Probetur ex textu: Non est tibi pars, &c. Aberraverunt à scopo, &c. Et ex eventu, qui hypocritas detegit. 1. Ioh.2.19.
units.tr: Let it be proved from the text: "You have no part," etc. "They have strayed from the mark," etc. And from the outcome, which discloses the hypocrites. 1 John 2:19.

units.la: Instantia 1. Fecerunt naufragium fidei verae. Ergo habuerunt.
units.tr: Objection 1. They suffered shipwreck of true faith. Therefore they had it.

units.la: Resp. per concessionem de professione verae doctrinae quae etiam dicitur vera fides: & haberi atque abiici potest ab hypocritis.
units.tr: Answer, by concession, concerning the profession of true doctrine, which is also called true faith; and it can be had and cast off by hypocrites.

units.la: Probetur hoc ibi Paulo fidem significare: quia loquitur de abiectione verae doctrinae & professionis, contra conscientiam. 2. Tim.2.17. Aberrarunt à scopo, cum veritatem, &c.
units.tr: Let it be proved that faith here signifies to Paul the profession: because he speaks of the rejection of true doctrine and profession, against conscience. 2 Tim. 2:17, 18: They have strayed from the mark, since they have made the truth, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur ἐπιτάσει[?], quod hypocritae deficientes dupliciter naufragium fidei faciant. 1. internae, cuius larvam prius habuerunt: & per apostasiam abiiciunt. 2. externae professionis, à qua deficiunt.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by ἐπιτάσει[?], that hypocrites who fall away make shipwreck of faith in two ways: 1. of the inward, of which they first had the mask, and which they cast off through apostasy; 2. of the outward profession, from which they fall away.

units.la: Instantia 2. Non larvam sed fidem abiiciunt. Ergo habuerunt: cum quod non habetur, abiici non possit.
units.tr: Objection 2. They cast off not a mask but faith. Therefore they had it: since what is not had cannot be cast off.

units.la: Resp. 1. concessione, quod habuerint δοκήσει seu specie & opinione hominum: & professione.
units.tr: Answer. 1. By concession, that they had it in appearance or outward show and opinion of men, and in profession.

units.la: 2. ad majorem: etiam quod videtur haberi, posse abiici & tolli: applicetur ad φαινόμενα dona hypocritarum ex Luc.8.18.
units.tr: 2. As to the major: even what seems to be had can be cast off and taken away; apply this to the φαινόμενα gifts of hypocrites from Luke 8:18.

units.la: Instantia 3. Apostatae peccant abiiciendo fidem. Ergo habuerunt fidem veram, quia non peccarent abiiciendo hypocriticam.
units.tr: Objection 3. The apostates sin by casting off the faith. Therefore they had true faith, since they would not sin by casting off a feigned one.

units.la: Resp. 1. concessione de vera professione quā habuerunt & abiicientes peccant.
units.tr: Answer 1. I grant the premise concerning the true profession which they had, and that in casting it off they sin.

units.la: 1 Distinctione maioris: non peccant abiicientes hypocrisin per veram conversionem: sed peccant mutantes hypocrisin in apostasiam.
units.tr: 1. Distinction of the major premise: those who cast off hypocrisy through true conversion do not sin; but those who change hypocrisy into apostasy do sin.

units.la: Amplif. Ter peccant apostatae: 1. abiiciendo speciem & opinionem de se bonam. 2. negando professionem veram. 3. degenerando in hostes.
units.tr: Amplification. The apostates sin three times: 1. by casting off the appearance and the good opinion of themselves. 2. by denying the true profession. 3. by degenerating into enemies.

units.la: Transitio per [illegible, ~9 letters] ad 1 v. argumentum propositionis.
units.tr: Transition through [illegible] to the first verse of the argument of the proposition.

units.la: 17. Dec. 93. Argumentum IV. Ecclesia non nititur potentia humana sed Dei: Non in gladio nec arcu, &c. Non multi potentes, &c.
units.tr: 17 Dec. 93. Argument IV. The Church does not rest on human power but on God's: Not by might nor by power, etc. Not many mighty, etc.

units.la: [illegible, ~8 letters] contra 5 rationem scandali: Non ergo nudatur Ecclesia praesidiis apostasia potentum.
units.tr: [illegible] against the fifth reason of offence: therefore the Church is not stripped of its protection by the apostasy of the powerful.

units.la: Amplif. à causis cur Deus aliquando vel morte praematura, vel alia ratione potentes Ecclesiae subtrahat:
units.tr: Amplification from the causes why God sometimes removes the powerful from the Church, either by premature death or in some other way:

units.la: 1. ne in ipsis ponat fiduciam.
units.tr: 1. so that they do not place their trust in them.

units.la: 2. Ne videatur regi consiliis humanis.
units.tr: 2. so that it may not seem to be governed by human counsels.

units.la: 3. Ut eius conservatio tanto sit mirabilior in mundo.
units.tr: 3. so that its preservation may be all the more wonderful in the world.

units.la: Argumentum V. A poenis apostatarum nisi resipiscant.
units.tr: Argument V. From the punishments of apostates, unless they repent.

units.la: Accommodetur locus Petri: Satius fuisset eis non cognovisse.&c. Item. Evomam te ex ore meo, &c. Exemplum Iuliani apostatae.
units.tr: Let the passage of Peter be applied: "It would have been better for them not to have known..." etc. Likewise: "I will spew you out of my mouth," etc. The example of Julian the apostate.

units.la: [illegible, ~8 letters] contra secundam rationem scandali.
units.tr: [illegible] against the second reason of offence.

units.la: 1. per ἀντίτυπον[?]. Etsi hostes triumphent: tamen risum hunc fore Sardonium.
units.tr: 1. by a counter-blow. Even if the enemies triumph, this laughter will be sardonic.

units.la: 2. Etsi errores sic latius serpunt: tamen non parari eis patrocinium multitudine.
units.tr: 2. Even if errors creep more widely in this way, they do not thereby gain patronage through their multitude.

units.la: Conclusio repetat promissionem: & hortetur ad modestiam, ne & nos stantes cadamus: & ad preces, ut Deus ipse in hac hominum perfidia ecclesiam servet: clementer erigat lapsos, & scandala avertat
units.tr: Conclusion repeats the promise, exhorts to moderation lest we too, standing, fall, and to prayer, that God himself would keep the Church in this faithlessness of men, mercifully raise up the fallen, and turn away the offences.

units.la: Exercitatio XXXI.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXXI.

units.la: An Mattathias recte interfecerit Judæum sacrificantem Idolis: & ministrum Antiochi. 1. Maccab. 2. v. 24. 25.
units.tr: Whether Mattathias rightly killed the Jew who was sacrificing to idols, and the minister of Antiochus. 1. Maccab. 2. v. 24. 25.

units.la: Narratio facti Mattathiæ sit brevis. Propositio. Posse defendi.
units.tr: The narrative of Mattathias's deed is brief. Proposition. It can be defended.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia fuit magistratus, cuius est tolerare sceleratos.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because he was a magistrate, and it is the duty of a magistrate to tolerate the wicked.

units.la: Probetur ex textu ver. 17. Tu es princeps, &c.
units.tr: Proof from the text, ver. 17. You are a prince, etc.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Fuit Sacerdos. Resp. Simul princeps populi.
units.tr: Objection 1. He was a priest. Answer. At the same time he was prince of the people.

units.la: Instantia, Lex non armat gladio sacerdotes.
units.tr: Instance: The law does not arm priests with the sword.

units.la: Resp. Ordinarie, & extra casum necessitatis. Tunc vero necessitas eum armabat, & consensus populi.
units.tr: Answer. In the ordinary course, and outside a case of necessity. But in that case necessity armed him, and the consent of the people.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Apostatæ non statim sunt trucidandi, sed convertendi vel devitandi.
units.tr: Objection 2. Apostates are not to be slain at once, but won over or avoided.

units.la: Resp. 1. Etiam erant trucidandi ex lege. Deut. 13. & 18. 2. Non erat simplex apostata, sed blasphemus, proditor libertatis patriæ, & author pessimi exempli in populo.
units.tr: Answer 1. They were in fact to be slain by the law. Deut. 13. and 18. 2. He was not a plain apostate, but a blasphemer, a betrayer of the liberty of the fatherland, and the author of the worst example among the people.

units.la: Ratio 11. Etsi non fuisset magistratus ordinarius: tamen extraordinario motu divino impulsus recte vindicavit gloriam Dei.
units.tr: Reason 2. Even if he had not been the ordinary magistrate, yet, impelled by an extraordinary motion of God, he rightly avenged the glory of God.

units.la: Probetur ex textu: 1. ver. 24. Zelatus est legem.
units.tr: Proof from the text: 1. ver. 24. He was zealous for the law.

units.la: 2. Exemplo Pinchæ laudabili. Num.25.8,
units.tr: 2. From the commendable example of Phinehas. Num. 25. 8.

units.la: Amplificetur thesis: quod Deus sæpe extra ordinem excitet vindices gloriæ suæ, cum ordinarii cessant.
units.tr: Amplification of the thesis: that God often raises up, outside the ordinary order, avengers of his glory when the ordinary ones cease.

units.la: Obiectio. Interficere legatum Regis erat seditiosum. Ergo non instinctu Dei fecit, qui non est author seditionis.
units.tr: Objection. To kill the king's envoy was seditious. Therefore he did not act at the prompting of God, who is not the author of sedition.

units.la: Resp. 1. Non regis sed tyranni minister fuit. Probetur quia impia præcepit, & in non ob-temperantes atrociter sæviit.
units.tr: Answer 1. He was not the minister of a king but of a tyrant. Proof: because he commanded impious things and raged savagely against those who did not obey.

units.la: 2. Etiam inferiori magistratui ordinario vel extraordinario licet vindicare gloriam Dei & servare subditos, contra atroces blasphemias & crudelitatem superiorum.
units.tr: 2. Even an inferior ordinary or extraordinary magistrate may lawfully avenge the glory of God and protect the subjects against the atrocious blasphemies and cruelty of superiors.

units.la: Ostendatur ex causis, cur inferiores sint ad-juncti superioribus & accommodetur.
units.tr: Let it be shown from the causes why inferiors are joined to superiors, and applied.

units.la: Amplificetur dicto Traiani ad Tribunum. Hoc gladio utere pro me, dum iusta: contra me, si iniusta fecero.
units.tr: Amplification by the saying of Trajan to the tribune: Use this sword for me while I act justly; against me, if I act unjustly.

units.la: Conclusio: Facta extraordinaria sine vocatio-ne non sunt imitanda.
units.tr: Conclusion: Extraordinary deeds done without a calling are not to be imitated.

units.la: Exercitatio XXXII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXXII.

units.la: An frequenter sit communicandum mensæ Domini.
units.tr: Whether the Lord's Supper ought to be received frequently.

units.la: EXordium sit improbatio moris communican-di semel tantum quotannis vel rarissimè.
units.tr: The introduction is a condemnation of the custom of communicating only once a year, or very rarely.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia est ingratitudo & neglectus summorum beneficiorum Dei.
units.tr: Reason 1: because it is ingratitude and neglect of God's greatest benefits.

units.la: II. quia fit ex superstitione seu opinione operis operati.
units.tr: II: because it arises from superstition, or from the opinion of the work worked (opus operatum).

units.la: Propositio : Etsi cavendum praecipuè, ut fiat digne:tamen & frequens esse debet communio.
units.tr: Proposition: Although we must above all take care that it is done worthily, yet communion ought also to be frequent.

units.la: ɕArgumentum 1. à mandato Christi: Hoc facite: Et Apostoli, Quotiescunq;, &c.
units.tr: Argument 1, from the command of Christ: "Do this"; and the Apostles: "As often as," etc.

units.la: Ostendatur frequentiam praecipi, ex reipsa: quia recordatio & annunciatio mortis Domini frequens praecipitur.
units.tr: Let it be shown that frequency is commanded from the thing itself, because the remembrance and proclamation of the Lord's death is commanded frequently.

units.la: II. ɕForma: Est communio Christi. Item: Pastus spiritualis cuius tam fastidium quam neglectus est perniciosus.
units.tr: II. Form: It is the communion of Christ. Likewise: it is spiritual food, and neglect of it, as well as distaste for it, is destructive.

units.la: III. A sine principali: ut confirmetur fides piorum.
units.tr: III. From the principal end: that the faith of the godly may be strengthened.

units.la: ɕAmplif. à sapientia Dei: & imbecillitate humana: Utendum ergo adminiculo tàm necessario, quoties Deus dat, ne cum tentemus nostro periculo.
units.tr: Amplification from the wisdom of God and human weakness: therefore we should use so necessary a help as often as God gives it, lest we try without it to our own peril.

units.la: IV. A finib.aliis: ut publicè testemur gratitudinem, &c. alamus charitatem, servemus unitatem, &c. Unus panis unum corpus, &c.
units.tr: IV. From other ends: that we may publicly testify our gratitude, etc.; that we may nourish love, preserve unity, etc. "Because we, being many, are one bread, one body," etc.

units.la: Per occupationem ostendatur ex discrimine Cœnæ & baptisini[?] cur propter tres proximas ratio-nes illa frequenter sit necessaria: iste non item.
units.tr: Let it be shown by the way of occupation, from the difference between the Supper and baptism [?], why that rite is necessary often on account of the three nearer reasons, while baptism is not so.

units.la: v. Ab authoritate apostolicæ Ecclesiæ, in qua nullus fiebat conventus sine verbo, precib.com-munione Cœnæ & eleemosynis. Act.2.42.1.Cor. 11.ver.20.
units.tr: v. From the authority of the apostolic Church, in which no assembly took place without the Word, prayers, communion of the Supper and almsgiving. Acts 2:42; 1 Cor. 11:20.

units.la: vi. A more veteris Ecclesiæ, quæ alibi singu-lis Dominicis, alibi quotidie communicabat.
units.tr: vi. From the custom of the ancient Church, which in some places communicated every Lord's Day and in others daily.

units.la: Ostendatur breviter ex Iustini Apol. 2. Item August. Tract. 26. in Ioh. & Epistola ad Ianuar.
units.tr: Let it be shown briefly from Justin's Apology 2, and likewise from Augustine, Tractate 26 on John, and the letter to Januarius.

units.la: vii. A judicio doctorum:&c. videatur Calvini Instit. l. 4. c.17.d.44 45. 46. Epistola 361. Obiectio I. Canones trinam vel unam tantum communionem in anno sanciunt. Resp.1. Non praejudicant mandato Christi. 2. Loquuntur de communione solenni totius Ecclesiae, non excludentes frequentiorem. Proinde depravantur.
units.tr: vii. From the judgment of the teachers, etc.; see Calvin's Institutes, book 4, chapter 17, sections 44, 45, 46, and Letter 361. Objection 1: The canons decree either three communions or only one in the year. Reply: 1. They do not prejudice Christ's command. 2. They speak of the solemn communion of the whole Church, not excluding a more frequent one. Therefore they are wrongly applied.

units.la: II. Coena vilescet usu. Resp.1. non piis: 2. negetur instantia verbi: item panis quotidiani.
units.tr: II. The Supper is cheapened by use. Reply: 1. Not for the godly. 2. Let the urging of the word be denied; likewise that of daily bread.

units.la: III. Rari communicabunt. Resp. 1. Non multitudo sed dignitas communicantium spectanda. 2. Excitandi omnes: & obiurgandus cessantium torpor.
units.tr: III. Few will communicate. Reply: 1. It is not the number but the worthiness of the communicants that must be considered. 2. All are to be stirred up, and the sloth of the negligent is to be rebuked.

units.la: Conclusio repetat propositionem.
units.tr: Conclusion: let it repeat the proposition.

units.la: Exercitatio XXXIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXXIII.

units.la: Adpetitoriam de loco Zachariæ cap.9.11. Tu quoque,&c. Resp.
units.tr: Objection concerning the passage of Zechariah 9:11, "Tu quoque, &c." Answer.

units.la: EXordium ab adnotatione petitionis amici de significando judicio tuo, an locus Zach.9.11. recte intelligatur de eductione patrum ex limbo inferni per Christum.
units.tr: The introduction takes its start from the remark in your friend's request, that you should state your judgment on whether Zechariah 9:11 is rightly understood as referring to the leading of the fathers out of the limbo of hell by Christ.

units.la: ἀπορία[?] dubitationis: quia vulgo accipiatur in hanc sententiam quam tamen amicus recte non probet.
units.tr: Doubt: because it is commonly taken in this sense, which yet your friend does not rightly prove.

units.la: ἀνθυπόφορος[?]: Etsi sententiæ multorum non libenter te opponas: tamen te gratificaturum amico.
units.tr: Counter-objection: Although you would not willingly set yourself against the opinion of many, yet you will oblige your friend.

units.la: Propositio: Non recte sic intelligitur.
units.tr: Proposition: It is not rightly understood in this way.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia non convenit verbis prophetæ.
units.tr: Reason 1: because it does not agree with the words of the prophet.

units.la: Ostendatur, quod verba prophetæ non sint a-postrophe ad Christum. Et tu Christe emisisti vinctos vinclos tuos sanguine fœderis e lacu, &c.
units.tr: Let it be shown that the words of the prophet are not an apostrophe to Christ: "And thou, Christ, hast sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit by the blood of the covenant, &c."

units.la: 1. Quia pronomen את[?] Tu est fœmininum: non אתה[?] Tu masculinum.
units.tr: 1. Because the pronoun thou (את) is feminine, not thou (אתה) masculine.

units.la: 2. Quia verbum [illegible, ~6 letters] est primæ non secundæ personæ: emisi non emisisti.
units.tr: 2. Because the verb is of the first person, not the second: I have sent forth, not thou hast sent forth.

units.la: Ratio II. fit προθεσμα[?] primæ & ἐκθεσις[?] veræ sententiæ per adversat: Quia sunt verba ipsius Dei vel Christi ad filium Zionis, hoc est, ad Ecclesiam, consolantis & excitantis eam ad fiduciam certæ liberationis à vinculis peccati, mortis & Satanæ per sanguinem fœderis inter ipsam & Deum initi, hoc est, ipsius Christi.
units.tr: Reason II: the proposition and the exposition of the true sense are set out by way of contrast: these are the words of God himself, or of Christ, to the daughter of Zion, that is, to the Church, comforting and stirring her up to confidence in certain deliverance from the chains of sin, death and Satan, through the blood of the covenant made between her and God, that is, of Christ himself.

units.la: Probetur. 1. ex pronomine fœminino: Et tu: nempe filia Zion confide: ellipsis.
units.tr: Let it be proved: 1. from the feminine pronoun: "And thou," namely, daughter of Zion, trust; an ellipsis.

units.la: 2. Ex verbo primæ personæ: Schillachti: emisi: quod ostendit esse rationem, cur debeat confidere, à promissione spiritualis liberationis;
units.tr: 2. From the verb of the first person: shillachti, I have sent forth, which shows that there is a reason why she ought to trust, drawn from the promise of spiritual deliverance;

units.la: 3. Ex sequenti hortatione: Convertimini, &c.
units.tr: 3. From the following exhortation: "Return, &c."

units.la: Ratio III. Non potest probari ex Scriptura talem limbum inferni esse: vel patres ante Christi mortem ibi fuisse.
units.tr: Reason III: It cannot be proved from Scripture that there is such a limbo of hell, or that the fathers were there before Christ's death.

units.la: Probetur 1. quia locus sine aqua hic metaphoricè significat captivitatem peccati sine spe & consolatione, nisi Christus liberet.
units.tr: Let it be proved 1. because the pit without water here metaphorically signifies captivity to sin, without hope or consolation, unless Christ sets free.

units.la: 2. quia credentes etiam ante Christi mortem fuerunt in cœlo: quod ostendatur exemplo Henoch, Heliæ, Abrahami, Lazari.
units.tr: 2. because believers, even before Christ's death, were in heaven; this may be shown by the examples of Enoch, Elijah, Abraham and Lazarus.

units.la: Ratio IV. Modus eductionis non congruit: quia propheta dicit, vinctos liberatos sanguine Christi in cruce fuso: Pontificii descensu Christi ad inferos.
units.tr: Reason IV: The manner of the deliverance does not fit: for the prophet says that the prisoners were freed by the blood of Christ poured out on the cross; the Papists (say) by Christ's descent to the dead.

units.la: Exercitatio XXXIV.
units.tr: Exercise XXXIV.

units.la: Collatio ἐγκωμιαστικὴ[?] castitatis Iosephi & Hippolyti atque aliorum extra Ecclesiam.
units.tr: Encomiastic collation[?] of the chastity of Joseph and Hippolytus and of others outside the Church.

units.la: EXordium ab hypothesi: A poetis celebrari castitatem Hippolyti fugientis incestum cum noverca: Pelei recusantis concubitum cum uxore Acasti: Bellerophontis fastidientis amorem uxoris Proeti, &c.
units.tr: Introduction from the thesis: The poets celebrate the chastity of Hippolytus, who fled incest with his stepmother; of Peleus, who refused intercourse with the wife of Acastus; of Bellerophon, who spurned the love of the wife of Proetus, etc.

units.la: Adverf. Sed in historia Ecclesiae omnibus antecellere castitatis laude Iosephum abstinentem ab hera ad stuprum eum sollicitante.
units.tr: Objection. But in the history of the Church, Joseph, who refrained from his mistress when she solicited him to debauchery, surpasses all others in the praise of chastity.

units.la: Propositio per ἀνθυπόφορον[?]: Etsi videatur in omnibus par virtus, quod sollicitati abstinent: tamen in solo Iosepho est vera & excellens castitas.
units.tr: Proposition through antithesis[?]: Although it may seem that all share an equal virtue, in that the solicited abstain; nevertheless, true and outstanding chastity is found in Joseph alone.

units.la: Confirmatio 1. à causa materiali: Solius Iosephi historia vera: reliquæ fabulosæ.
units.tr: Confirmation 1. from the material cause: The story of Joseph alone is true; the rest are fabulous.

units.la: Ostendatur breviter ex circumstantiis fabularum.
units.tr: Let this be shown briefly from the circumstances of the fables.

units.la: De Hippolyto testimonio Platonis in Cratylo: & quod fingitur loris equorum ruentium discerptus: ab Æsculapio vero ab inferis revocatus, &c.
units.tr: Concerning Hippolytus, the testimony of Plato in the Cratylus, and that he is fabled to have been torn apart by the reins of runaway horses, but was restored from the dead by Aesculapius, etc.

units.la: De Peleo, quod obiectus centauris divinitus accepto gladio eosdem vicerit.
units.tr: Concerning Peleus, that, exposed to the centaurs, he overcame them with a sword received from the gods.

units.la: De Bellerophonte, quod obiectus Chimæræ, Pegasi beneficio, eandem confecerit.
units.tr: Concerning Bellerophon, that, exposed to the Chimaera, he destroyed it with the help of Pegasus.

units.la: Addatur μυθολογία[?] breviter: Significari castitatem esse difficilem, sed Deum adesse, & præmia tribuere eam tuentibus.
units.tr: Let it be added briefly from mythology: that chastity is difficult, but God is present and grants rewards to those who guard it.

units.la: II. A causa efficiente: quæ in Iosepho est Spiritus Sanctus movens volūtatem cogitatione mā- dati divini ad timorem Dei & veram castitatem. ver.9. An peccarem in Deum? In aliis voluntas foris abhorrens à manifesta turpitudine: Sed intus immunditiem retinens, flammis ardens, nec Deum timens,
units.tr: II. From the efficient cause: which in Joseph is the Holy Spirit moving the will, by thought of the divine command, toward the fear of God and true chastity. Ver. 9: How could I sin against God? In others, the will abhors outward manifest filthiness, but inwardly retains uncleanness, burning with flames, and does not fear God,

units.la: iii. à causa finali: Iosephus abstinet ne offendat Deum; alii gloriolam continentiæ captant.
units.tr: III. From the final cause: Joseph abstains so as not to offend God; others seek a little glory from their continence.

units.la: Amplificentur hæ duæ causæ ex Thesi, de dis- crimine virtutum in sanctis & in non renatis.
units.tr: Let these two causes be amplified from the thesis concerning the difference between virtues in the saints and in those not reborn.

units.la: iiii. Ab adiunctis. Iosephi castitatem comitantur præclaræ aliæ virtutes.
units.tr: IV. From the accompanying circumstances. Other excellent virtues accompany the chastity of Joseph.

units.la: i. Pietas, obtemperans Deo: v.9. Quarefacerem malum?
units.tr: i. Piety, obeying God: Ver. 9: How then could I do this great evil?

units.la: 2. Fides rectè agnoscens Deum, & voluntatem eius:&c.
units.tr: 2. Faith, rightly acknowledging God and his will, etc.

units.la: 3. Fidelitas in herum: non abutitur sua potestate, nec vult herum fallere cum possit. ver.8.
units.tr: 3. Faithfulness toward his master: he does not abuse his power, nor wishes to deceive his master though he could. Ver. 8.

units.la: 4. Gratitudo agnoscens & profitens beneficia accepta: nec voles[?] reddere malum pro bono.
units.tr: 4. Gratitude, acknowledging and professing benefits received; nor is he willing to repay good with evil.

units.la: 5. Constantia servans σωφροσύνην[?] rectè faciendi, etsi sæpius tentetur illecebris lascivæ mulieris. ver.10.
units.tr: 5. Constancy, maintaining self-control[?] in doing right, even though he is often tempted by the allurements of a wanton woman. Ver. 10.

units.la: 6. Fortitudo anteferens virtutem & bonam conscientiam certo periculo.
units.tr: 6. Fortitude, preferring virtue and a good conscience to a certain danger.

units.la: Obiectio. Videtur à Deo deseri abiectus in carcerem.
units.tr: Objection. He seems to be forsaken by God, cast into prison.

units.la: Resp. 1. Ex dicto: virtutis comes invidia: Item: Careat successibus opto / Quisquis ab eventu facta notanda putat.
units.tr: Reply. 1. From the saying: envy is the companion of virtue; likewise: May he who thinks deeds are to be judged by their outcome be without success.

units.la: 2. In carcere Deus adest carceri, cumque tandem evehit. Conclusio: In Iosepho vera virtus, in aliis spe-cies tantum fuit.
units.tr: 2. In prison God is present with the prisoner, and at last lifts him up. Conclusion: In Joseph there was true virtue; in the others there was only the appearance of it.

units.la: Exercitatio. XXXV.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXXV.

units.la: Scribatur in genere demonstrativo Detestatio facti Israëlitarum, fabricantium sibi vitulum in deserto: Exod.32.
units.tr: A detestation of the deed of the Israelites who made for themselves a calf in the desert: Exod. 32. This is to be written in the demonstrative genre.

units.la: Propositio sit per comparationem: Etsi plurima exstent peccata Israëlitarum peregrinantium in deserto: tamen hoc maximè detestandum, quod vitulum aureum fabricant & colunt pro Deo.
units.tr: The proposition is to be made by comparison: Although many sins of the Israelites wandering in the desert exist, yet this is to be detested above all, that they made a golden calf and worshipped it as God.

units.la: Confirmationis ratio 1. à turpi: quia est horribilis Idololatria contra secundum præceptum: Non facies tibi sculptile.
units.tr: The reason for confirmation (1) from the shamefulness: because it is horrible idolatry against the second commandment: You shall not make for yourself a graven image.

units.la: Amplif. turpitudo 1. à recenti legis promulgatione.
units.tr: Amplification, the shamefulness (1) from the recent promulgation of the law.

units.la: 2. ab ingratitudine pro plurimis beneficiis.
units.tr: (2) from ingratitude for very many benefits.

units.la: 3. à levi occasione, quod Mose aliquandiu morante in monte mox desperant, putantes Deum cum Mose esse mortuum: ideo quærunt alium Deum & Ducem.
units.tr: (3) from the slight occasion: since Moses delayed for a while on the mountain, they at once despair, thinking that God has died with Moses; therefore they seek another God and Leader.

units.la: 4. à persona Aaronis non opponetis se furori populi ex officio, sed juvantis eum consilio: fundentis vitulum, & addentis blasphemam concionem, qua nomen, honorem & opus Dei proprium tribuit vitulo.
units.tr: (4) from the person of Aaron: he did not oppose the fury of the people as his office required, but helped them with his counsel, by melting the calf and adding a blasphemous proclamation, by which he ascribed the name, honour and work proper to God to the calf.

units.la: Epiphonema: O facinus[?] horrendum sancti viri.
units.tr: Epiphonema: O horrible deed of a holy man!

units.la: Thesis de infirmitate sanctorum, deserente eos Deo. Refutetur opinio Papistarum, quod summus Pontifex non possit errare.
units.tr: Thesis on the weakness of the saints, God forsaking them. Let the opinion of the Papists be refuted, that the supreme Pontiff cannot err.

units.la: Occupatio : Etsi festivitas Iehovæ proclame-tur:tamen non Dei sed vituli imò Cacodæmonis festum fuisse.
units.tr: Occupatio: Although a feast to Jehovah was proclaimed, yet it was not a feast of God but of the calf, or rather of the Evil Demon.

units.la: Ratio:quia sine Dei mandato fingentes cultū fingunt alium Deum: qui nullus est, nisi idolum.
units.tr: Reason: because those who devise a worship without God's command devise another god, who is none, except an idol.

units.la: Item: Dei testimonio,ver.8. Sacrificarūt vitulo: Item Pauli 1.Cor.10. Gentes quæ immolant idolis immolant diabolis.
units.tr: Likewise: by the testimony of God, verse 8: They sacrificed to the calf. Likewise, Paul, 1 Cor. 10: The things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons.

units.la: Translatio ad thesin[?] : Esse hunc prætextum communem Idololatris, ut cultum statuarū Dei nomine pallient: quia honor signi sit ipsius signati juxta versiculos Bonaventuræ:
units.tr: Transition to the thesis: This pretext is common to idolaters, that they cloak the worship of statues in the name of God, because the honour of the image belongs to the thing it represents, according to the verses of Bonaventure:

units.la: Effigiem Christi, dum transis, semper adora: Non tamen effigiem, sed quem designat honora, Et vii Synod. Nicen. Impp. Constant. & Iren.
units.tr: Honour the image of Christ whenever you pass by, always adore it: yet not the image, but honour him whom it designates. And the seventh Council of Nicaea, the emperors Constantine and Irene.

units.la: Nam Deus est q; imago docet, non est Deus ipsa:[?] Hanc videas, sed mente colas, quod cernis in ipsa. Adversativa, Sed est vanus prætextus.
units.tr: For God is the image that teaches, he is not God himself: look upon it, but worship in your mind what you see in it. Adversative: but it is an empty pretext.

units.la: 1. quia non honor sed contumelia est vene-ratio Dei contra eius præceptum.
units.tr: (1) because the veneration of God against his command is not honour but insult.

units.la: 2. quia statuæ non sunt signa Dei Ief.40.[?] Cui assimilabitis me?
units.tr: (2) because statues are not signs of God: Isa. 40: To whom will you liken me?

units.la: Amplificatio v. à forma cultus vana & turpi:
units.tr: Amplification, the fifth point, from the vain and shameful form of the worship:

units.la: 1. quod vitulum fingunt Deum, mutantes gloriam suam in similitudinem bovis comeden-tis fœnum. Psal.106.20.
units.tr: (1) because they make a calf to be God, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox eating hay. Ps. 106.20.

units.la: Fiat comparatio cum Ethnicorum compara-tione: de qua Paulus Rom. 1. 23.[?] mutarunt glo-riam incorruptibilis Dei in efformatam effigiem qua-drupedum, &c.
units.tr: Let a comparison be made with the comparison of the Gentiles, of which Paul speaks, Rom. 1.23: they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed beasts, etc.

units.la: Epiphon. O brutum stuporem: prodigiosum facinus Dei majestatem simulacro bestiæ commutare.
units.tr: Epiphonema: O brutish stupidity! A monstrous deed, to exchange the majesty of God for the image of a beast.

units.la: Addatur probabilis caussa cur bovis potius quam hominis simulacrum effinxerint: quod perversa æmulatione Ægyptios colentes Apim sint imitati.
units.tr: Let a probable cause be added why they fashioned the likeness of an ox rather than of a man: because, by a perverse emulation, they imitated the Egyptians, who worshipped Apis.

units.la: Gnome: Adeo noxia est consuetudo malorum, ut etiam bonos corrumpat.
units.tr: Maxim: So harmful is the custom of the wicked that it corrupts even the good.

units.la: 2. quod epulum Saliare choreis & tripudiis gentium more celebrant. Textus: Seditq; populus ad epulandum: & surrexerunt ad ludendum, juxta illud Ethnici Poëtæ:
units.tr: (2) because they celebrate the Saliar feast with dances and leaping after the manner of the Gentiles. Text: The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play, according to that saying of the heathen poet:

units.la: Nunc est bibendum, nunc pede libero Pulsanda tellus, &c.
units.tr: Now it is time to drink, now with free foot the earth is to be struck, etc.

units.la: Confirmationis ratio 2. à pernicioso: Ad hanc fiat transitio per adversativam: Sed tantum scelus non fuisse impune quia secutæ sunt graves pœnæ.
