units.tr: The reason for confirmation (2) from the destructive outcome: a transition is to be made here by an adversative: but so great a crime was not unpunished, because grievous punishments followed.

units.la: 1. Indignatio Dei adversus totum cœtum: Di-mitte me ut deleam, &c.
units.tr: (1) The indignation of God against the whole assembly: Let me alone, that I may destroy them, etc.

units.la: 2. cædes 3000, qua reatum expiari oportuit.
units.tr: (2) the slaughter of 3000, by which the guilt had to be atoned.

units.la: Conclusio, Cum Idololatria inter alia peccata Deum gravissimè offendat, & ab eo horribiliter puniatur, ideo est fugienda.
units.tr: Conclusion: Since idolatry, among other sins, grievously offends God and is horribly punished by him, therefore it is to be fled from.

units.la: Exercitatio XXXVI.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXXVI.

units.la: Paraphrasis historiæ de bello & victoria Israëlitarum contra Amalekitas Exod. 17. 8.
units.tr: Paraphrase of the history of the battle and victory of the Israelites against the Amalekites, Exod. 17. 8.

units.la: 1. NArretur[?] occasio belli ex Deut. 25. 17.
units.tr: 1. The occasion of the war is related from Deut. 25. 17.

units.la: 2. Expeditio Iosuæ Mosis consilio ad defensionem suscepta.
units.tr: 2. The expedition of Joshua, undertaken for defence at the counsel of Moses.

units.la: 3. Mosis & duorum adjutorum preces in monte: & secundum eas successus prælii: Tollente Mose brachia id est ardenter precante vincebant Israëlitæ, remittente brachia & preces vincebant hostes.
units.tr: 3. The prayers of Moses and of his two helpers on the mountain, and the outcome of the battle according to them: while Moses lifted up his hands, that is, prayed fervently, the Israelites were winning; when he let his hands and prayers fall, the enemy was winning.

units.la: 4. Victoria Iosuæ.
units.tr: 4. The victory of Joshua.

units.la: 5. Trophæum & comminatio Dei de extirpatione Amalekitarum eiusdemque exsecutio 1.Sam.15.2.
units.tr: 5. The trophy, and God's threat concerning the extermination of the Amalekites, and its execution, 1 Sam. 15. 2.

units.la: Claudatur loco communi de necessitate & efficacia precum etiam in præliis, de præcipuis Ecclesiæ armis, & de eiusdem certa victoria atque triumpho contra hostes.
units.tr: Let it be closed with a common-place on the necessity and efficacy of prayer also in battles, on the chief weapons of the Church, and on her sure victory and triumph over her enemies.

units.la: Exercitatio XXXVII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXXVII.

units.la: Approbatio supplicij regum Cananæorum. Iosuæ.10.
units.tr: Approval of the punishment of the Canaanite kings. Joshua 10.

units.la: Narratur breviter historia de supplicio regum Cananæorum devictorum à Iosua. cap. 10.ver.24.25.26.
units.tr: The history of the punishment of the Canaanite kings, defeated by Joshua, is briefly related. Chap. 10, verses 24, 25, 26.

units.la: Obiect. Videtur crudele & barbarum insultare victis: contra illud: Magnanimo satis est, &c. Item iniustum contra illud: Parcere subiectis, &c.
units.tr: Objection. It seems cruel and barbarous to trample on the vanquished; against this is the saying: "It is enough for a magnanimous man, etc." Likewise it seems unjust; against this is the saying: "To spare the subjected, etc."

units.la: Responsio sit propositio per adversativam: Sed non est.
units.tr: Answer. The proposition is to be taken with an adversative clause: but it is not so.

units.la: Ratio: quia sunt causæ graves contumeliæ tam atrocis.
units.tr: Reason: because the causes of so atrocious a contumely are grave.

units.la: Confirmetur ἐκθέσει causarum.
units.tr: Let it be confirmed by an exposition of the causes.

units.la: 1. Quia Deus mandaverat delere omnes. ver. 12 Tradidi eos in manus, &c.
units.tr: 1. Because God had commanded that all be destroyed. Verse 12: I have delivered them into your hands, etc.

units.la: 2. Non insultat eis vindictæ privatæ cupiditate, sed studio vindicandi gloriam Dei.
units.tr: 2. Joshua does not insult them out of a desire for private revenge, but out of zeal to vindicate the glory of God.

units.la: 3. Quia tali exemplo populus fuit armandus ad certam spem victoriæ de aliis. ver. 25. Sic faciet Jehova.
units.tr: 3. Because by such an example the people were to be armed with a certain hope of victory over the others. Verse 25: Thus will the LORD do.

units.la: 4. Statuendum fuit exemplum rigoris in reges, ne perversa clementia populus uti auderet in subditos.
units.tr: 4. An example of severity had to be set against the kings, lest through misplaced clemency the people should dare to use mercy towards their subjects.

units.la: 5. Reges præcipuè erant atroces pœnas meriti tanquam aliis Cananæis male agendi & contra Deum belligerandi caussa existentes.
units.tr: 5. The kings especially deserved the most atrocious punishments, as those who were the cause of the others among the Canaanites acting wickedly and waging war against God.

units.la: 6. Subiectio Regum sub pedes eorum documentum illustre erat amoris Dei erga populum electum.
units.tr: 6. The placing of the kings' necks under the feet of the Israelites was a remarkable proof of God's love towards his chosen people.

units.la: 7. Ut tam gravi animadversione in scelera Regum terror incuteretur populo, ne auderet gentium mores imitari.
units.tr: 7. So that by so grave a punishment of the kings' crimes terror might be struck into the people, lest they should dare to imitate the morals of the nations.

units.la: Conclusio: Propter has caussas nec barbarum nec injustum fuit.
units.tr: Conclusion: For these causes the act was neither barbarous nor unjust.

units.la: Λύσις: [?] Non fuit parcendum, quia non subjecti sed superbi fuerunt.
units.tr: Solution: [?] It was not right to spare them, because they were not subjects but proud men.

units.la: Exercitatio XXXVIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXXVIII.

units.la: Cur Deus sinat grassari & prosperari Turcas contra Christianos.
units.tr: Why God allows the Turks to rage and prosper against Christians.

units.la: EXordium à querela de grassatione & victoriis Turcarum contra Christianos.
units.tr: An introduction from the complaint about the raging and the victories of the Turks against Christians.

units.la: ἀπορία: Videtur hoc promissionibus contra-rium rium de defensione Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: ἀπορία: This seems contrary to the promises concerning the defence of the Church.

units.la: Respon. Non est. Ratio: quia promissiones externæ habent conditionem perseverantiæ Ecclesiæ in fide & pœnitentia, quam nos abjicimus.
units.tr: Answer. It is not. Reason: because the external promises carry the condition that the Church persists in faith and repentance, which we cast off.

units.la: Propositio. Sunt igitur aliæ causæ spectantes ad nostram salutem & ad gloriam Dei.
units.tr: Proposition. There are therefore other causes, bearing on our salvation and on the glory of God.

units.la: Sequatur ἑξῆς[?] causarum:
units.tr: Let the causes follow in order:

units.la: I. Peccata nostra, quæ militant adversus nos, specificentur præcipua profanitas: contemtus Dei & religionis, securitas, luxus, superbia, &c. Ergo juste affligimur.
units.tr: I. Our sins, which fight against us; especially to be specified: profanity, contempt of God and of religion, complacency, pride, etc. Therefore we are justly afflicted.

units.la: Amplific. exemplo Israelitarum, qui cum essent populus Dei, sæpius sibi attraxerunt graves calamitates suis peccatis.
units.tr: Amplification: by the example of the Israelites, who, though they were the people of God, very often drew severe calamities upon themselves by their sins.

units.la: II. Castigatio ad resipiscentiam: ne cum mundo pereamus 1. Cor.11. Domino corripimur.
units.tr: II. Chastisement leading to repentance, lest we perish with the world: 1 Cor. 11. We are corrected by the Lord.

units.la: III. Exercitium patientiæ, fidei, spei pioru. 1.Pet.1. Ut τὸ δοκίμιον fidei vestræ.
units.tr: III. The exercise of the patience, faith and hope of the godly. 1 Pet. 1. That the trial of your faith [τὸ δοκίμιον τῆς πίστεως].

units.la: IV. Humilitas nostra: ut humiliati deponamus cristas, & de nostra petentia desperantes à Deo pendere & victoriam petere discamus.
units.tr: IV. Our humility: so that, humbled, we lay aside our crests, and, despairing of our own strength, learn to depend upon God and to seek victory from him.

units.la: Amplif. a fine: Dei potentiam in liberatione Ecclesiæ esse illustriorem ubi desperatum est de causis secundis: Exemplo Israelitarum ad mare rubrum.
units.tr: Amplification from the end: God's power is more illustrious in the deliverance of the Church when all hope in secondary causes is lost: by the example of the Israelites at the Red Sea.

units.la: V. Declaratio amoris Dei erga Ecclesiam sub cruce contra potentes hostes eam nihilominus servantis.
units.tr: V. A declaration of the love of God towards the Church under the cross, preserving it nonetheless against powerful enemies.

units.la: VI. Declaratio illustrior justitiæ Dei in punitis hostibus, postquam diu eos toleravit & [illegible, ~8 letters]- γίτες reddidit. Confirmetur exēplo Pharaonis : In hocipsum excitavi te,&c.
units.tr: VI. A more illustrious declaration of the justice of God against punished enemies, after he had borne with them for a long time and [illegible, ~8 letters]-gites repaid them. Let it be confirmed by the example of Pharaoh: For this very purpose have I raised you up, etc.

units.la: Item Nebucadnezaris, quem Deus minatur se propter superbiam dejecturum post castigatam Ecclesiam.Jef.10.
units.tr: Likewise Nebuchadnezzar, whom God threatens to cast down on account of his pride, after the Church had been chastised. Isa. 10.

units.la: Conclusio: Nō ergo fremamus nec desperemus: sed resipiscentes patientia fide & precib.ad Deum confugiamus.
units.tr: Conclusion: Let us not therefore rage nor despair, but, returning to our senses, let us take refuge in God through patience, faith and prayers.

units.la: Exercit. XXXVIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XXXVIII.

units.la: An oracula prophetica quæ in N.T.de Christo citantur & impletain eo dicuntur, et-iam ad typos pertineant.
units.tr: Whether the prophetic oracles which are cited in the New Testament concerning Christ and are said to be fulfilled in him also pertain to types.

units.la: PARS NEGANS.
units.tr: THE NEGATIVE PART.

units.la: PRoponatur hæc quæstio amico, & declaretur hypothesi aliqua ex Psal.2. vel.16. vel 22.
units.tr: Let this question be put to a friend, and let it be explained by some hypothesis drawn from Psalm 2, 16 or 22.

units.la: Ratio ἀντίθεσις[?], quia video interpretes dissenti-re: alios de Christo restricte, alios de Christo principaliter & perfecte : & etiam de typis typice in-telligere.
units.tr: Reason (antithesis?), because I see that the interpreters disagree: some understand things of Christ strictly, others of Christ principally and perfectly, and also understand the types typically.

units.la: Propositio : Omnia præcise de solo Christo, nullo autem modo de typis intelligenda esse.
units.tr: Proposition: All things are to be understood solely and strictly of Christ, and in no way of the types.

units.la: Ratio 1. A discrimine typorum & oraculorum: quia typi implicite: sed oracula explicite, & sine involucris figurarum Christum praenunciarunt.
units.tr: Reason 1. From the difference between types and prophecies: because types foreshadow Christ implicitly, but prophecies announce him explicitly and without the veil of figures.

units.la: Ratio 11. Evangelistę & Apostoli, quę de Christo citant, ad eum solum restringunt.
units.tr: Reason 2. The Evangelists and Apostles, when they cite the things about Christ, restrict them to him alone.

units.la: Probatio: quia dicunt, in Christo impleta esse. Ostendatur exemplo Joh.19.24. ut impleretur Scriptura dicens: Partiti sunt vestimenta mea sibi, &c. vel simili.
units.tr: Proof: because they say that they were fulfilled in Christ. Let it be shown by the example of John 19:24, that the Scripture might be fulfilled which says: They divided my garments among them, etc., or by something similar.

units.la: Ratio III. Oracula intellecta etiam de typis, plane enervarentur, & amitterent omnem vim probandi contra Judæos, Christum esse Messiam.
units.tr: Reason 3. Prophecies understood also of types would be utterly weakened and would lose all force of proving, against the Jews, that Christ is the Messiah.

units.la: Probatio : Quia non essent propria quarto modo, à quibus solis ad speciem valet directa consequentia.
units.tr: Proof: because they would not be proper to the fourth mode, from which alone a direct consequence holds good for the point at issue.

units.la: Amplificetur incommodum : Judęi arripe-rent impletionem typicam : abjicerent & Christianis relinquerent anagogicam seu significatam.
units.tr: Let the inconvenience be enlarged upon: the Jews would seize upon the typical fulfilment and would reject it and leave the anagogical or signified fulfilment to the Christians.

units.la: Illustretur exemplo: Si etiam de Davide verum illud: Caro mea requiescet in spe: frustrà inde Petrus probat, Christum esse Messiam, Act. 2. 26.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated by an example: if that saying about David, my flesh shall rest in hope, is also true, then Peter proves in vain from it that Christ is the Messiah, Acts 2:26.

units.la: Ratio IV. Typi Christi non in sua, sed in Christi persona omnia prędixerunt, ut David in persona Messię: Deus meus, Deus meus, quare me dereliquisti, &c.
units.tr: Reason 4. The types did not foretell all things in their own person, but in the person of Christ, as David in the person of the Messiah: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me, etc.

units.la: Ratio V. Orthodoxi Patres omnia interpretantur de solo Christo.
units.tr: Reason 5. The orthodox Fathers interpret all things of Christ alone.

units.la: Conclusio : Cum quæstio sit ardua, ex qua non possis satis te explicare; petere te amici judicium.
units.tr: Conclusion: Since the question is difficult, and you cannot sufficiently explain yourself from it, you ask your friend for his judgment.

units.la: Responsio ad amicum.
units.tr: Reply to the friend.

units.la: PARS AFFIRMANS.
units.tr: THE AFFIRMING PART.

units.la: EXordii Propositio : Difficile ubi esse respon-dere:
units.tr: Proposition of the introduction: It is difficult to know where to answer.

units.la: Causa difficultatis. 1. Iudicii tui tenuitas. 2. Quæstionis gravitas, quam ipse amicus agnoscat. 3. Occupationes, quę non sinant te de re perplexa satis cogitare.
units.tr: Causes of the difficulty. 1. The slightness of your judgment. 2. The weight of the question, which your friend himself acknowledges. 3. The occupations that do not allow you to think enough about a matter so entangled.

units.la: Adversativa. Attamen te conaturum: & amico communicaturum, quod nunc succurrat.
units.tr: Adversative. Nevertheless, you will try, and will share with your friend whatever now occurs to you.

units.la: Propof.per divif. Oracula de Christo in N. T. allegata, alia videri in solo Christo, alia in Christo vere & perfecte, in typis olim per figuram & aliquatenus impleta: & illa simplicia, hæc composita pof-se appellari. Addatur appellationis seu distinctio-nis ratio, quia illa unam tantum, nempe veram in Christo: hæc geminam impletionem habeant, typicam in typis, & significatam in Christo.
units.tr: Proposition by division. The oracles about Christ cited in the New Testament seem, some to be fulfilled in Christ alone, others in Christ truly and perfectly, and formerly in types, through a figure and to some extent. The former may be called simple, the latter composite. Let the reason for this designation or distinction be added: the former have only one fulfilment, namely the true one in Christ, while the latter have a twofold fulfilment, the typical in the types and the signified in Christ.

units.la: Confirmatio primæ partis de simplicib.
units.tr: Confirmation of the first part, concerning the simple oracles.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia multæ sunt expressæ promissiones, item prædictiones de Christo nullis typis adjunctæ. Illustretur exemplis aliquot: Vt Gen. 3. & 22. Ief.7. & 9. & 53. &c.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because there are many express promises, and likewise predictions about Christ, joined to no types. Let this be illustrated by several examples, as Gen. 3 and 22, Isa. 7, 9, 53, etc.

units.la: Clausula: Hæc ergo de typis, cum nullos habeant, non possunt intelligi.
units.tr: Conclusion: These, therefore, since they have no types, cannot be understood in terms of types.

units.la: Ratio 11. Quia multa etiam typica oracula in solo Christo oēm impletione habere res ipsa loqt.[?]
units.tr: Reason 2. Because the thing itself shows that many typical oracles also have their complete fulfilment in Christ alone.

units.la: Declaretur: Primo, quæ typica vocentur: videl. de typis vel à typis Christi personam sustinentib. edita: ut de typo Christi Salomone, 2.Sam.7. Stabiliam thronum regni eius in seculum, &c. à typo Christi Davide, Psal.16: Non sines sanctum tuum videre corruptionem, &c.
units.tr: Let it be explained: first, what things are called typical, namely those uttered about types, or by types who sustained the person of Christ: as of the type of Christ, Solomon, 2 Sam. 7, "I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever," etc.; of the type of Christ, David, Ps. 16, "You will not allow your Holy One to see corruption," etc.

units.la: Deinde, duæ regulæ addantur, unde de simplicib. sit judicandum.
units.tr: Next, two rules should be added by which the simple oracles are to be judged.

units.la: 1. Ex historia, si unicè Christo conveniat: Vt, solus Christus non vidit corruptionem sepulcri.
units.tr: 1. From history, if it applies to Christ alone: as, Christ alone did not see the corruption of the sepulchre.

units.la: 11. Ex Majestate vel excellentia attributorum: ut sunt: regnum universale Psal.2.8. Thronus æternus, 2.Sam.7. Psal.45. &c.
units.tr: 2. From the majesty or excellence of the attributes: as are the universal kingdom, Ps. 2 and 8; the eternal throne, 2 Sam. 7; Ps. 45, etc.

units.la: Clausula: Talia igitur esse simplicia: typis nullo modo applicanda: & de his vera esse argumenta amici, ut postea ostendetur.
units.tr: Conclusion: Such things, therefore, are simple, not to be applied to types in any way; and the arguments of your friend are true concerning these, as will be shown afterwards.

units.la: Transitio ad confirm. sec. partis de Oraculis c̄opo-sitis, habentib. geminam impletionem, &c.
units.tr: Transition to the confirmation of the second part, concerning the composite oracles, having a twofold fulfilment, etc.

units.la: Argum. ab exemplis Scripturae. Proferantur nonnulla manifesta, & in singulis utraq; impletio paucis monstretur, Exod. 12. 48. Ioh. 19. 36. Os non frangetis, &c. Psal. 2. Act. 4: Quare fremuerunt gentes. Ps. 31. 6. Luc. 23. 46: In manus tuas Domine, &c. Psal. 22. & Ioh. 19. Partiti sunt vestimenta mea, &c.
units.tr: Argument from the examples of Scripture. Let some clear ones be set forth, and in each the twofold fulfilment shown briefly: Exod. 12:46; John 19:36, "You shall not break a bone," etc.; Ps. 2; Acts 4, "Why did the nations rage?"; Ps. 31:6; Luke 23:46, "Into your hands, O Lord," etc.; Ps. 22 and John 19, "They divided my garments," etc.

units.la: Obiectio: Non Davidis sed tantum Christi vestimenta sunt divisa.
units.tr: Objection: It was not the garments of David that were divided, but only those of Christ.

units.la: Respond. Christi ad literam, Davidis figurate, cum exutus esset dignitatibus & fortunis omnibus in exilio.
units.tr: Answer. Literally of Christ, figuratively of David, since he had been stripped of all his dignities and fortunes in exile.

units.la: Subiiciantur Regula de quadruplici discrimine, quo oracula composita in typo, & in Christo sunt impleta.
units.tr: Let the rules be added concerning the fourfold distinction by which composite oracles are fulfilled in the type and in Christ.

units.la: Prima. Quaedam literaliter in typo & in Christo: Vt, Exod. 12. 46. Ioh. 19. 36. de ossib. non fractis. Num. 21. 9. Ioh. 3. 14: de serpente suspenso.
units.tr: First. Some things are fulfilled literally both in the type and in Christ: as, Exod. 12:46; John 19:36, concerning the bones not broken; Num. 21:9; John 3:14, concerning the serpent lifted up.

units.la: 2. Sam. 7. Hebr. 1: Ero ipsi Pater, &c. Psal. 35. 19. Ioh. 15. 25: Oderunt me gratis. Hos. 11. 1. Matth. 2. 15: Ex Aegypto vocavi filium meum, &c.
units.tr: 2 Sam. 7; Heb. 1, "I will be his Father," etc.; Ps. 35:19; John 15:25, "They hated me without cause"; Hos. 11:1; Matt. 2:15, "Out of Egypt I called my son," etc.

units.la: Secunda. Quaedam literaliter tantum in Christo: figurate olim in typo: Vt, Psal. 22. Ioh. 19: Partiti sunt vestimenta mea. Psal. 69. 22. Ioh. 19. 29: Posuerunt in escam meam fel. Palm.78.2.Matth.13.35: Aperiam os meum in parabolis, &c.
units.tr: Second. Some things are literally only in Christ, and were formerly figuratively in the type: as, Ps. 22; John 19, "They divided my garments." Ps. 69:22; John 19:29, "They gave me gall for my food." Ps. 78:2; Matt. 13:35, "I will open my mouth in parables," etc.

units.la: Tertia. Alia literaliter in typo, figurate in Christo. Vt,
units.tr: Third. Others are literal in the type and figurative in Christ: as,

units.la: 2.Sam.7.13.Heb.3.6: Ipse ædificabit mihi domum, &c.
units.tr: 2 Sam. 7:13; Heb. 3:6, "He shall build a house for me," etc.

units.la: Psal.2.9.Apoc.2.27.(õteret[?] eos virga ferrea, &c.
units.tr: Ps. 2:9; Rev. 2:27, "He shall break them with a rod of iron," etc.

units.la: Quarta: Alia figurate in utroque: Vt,
units.tr: Fourth: Others are figurative in both: as,

units.la: Psal.41.Joh.13.18: Qui comedit panem mecum, &c.
units.tr: Ps. 41; John 13:18, "He who eats bread with me," etc.

units.la: Psal.118.Matth.21.42. Act.4.11. Lapis reprobatus, &c.
units.tr: Ps. 118; Matt. 21:42; Acts 4:11, "The stone which the builders rejected," etc.

units.la: Claudatur primum argumentum: His discriminibus observatis apparet, quod sint aliqua composita & facilis est applicatio.
units.tr: Let the first argument be concluded: With these distinctions observed, it appears that there are some composite oracles, and their application is easy.

units.la: Argumentum II. à definitione typicorum compositorum: Quia quædam oracula habuerunt analogos eventus in typis & in Christo, sunt ergo typica oracula.
units.tr: Argument II, from the definition of composite typical oracles: Because certain oracles had analogous events in the types and in Christ, there are therefore typical oracles.

units.la: Potest addi major: Oracula analogos eventus habentia in Christo & in typo, recte vocantur typica composita.
units.tr: The major premise may be added: Oracles having analogous events in Christ and in the type are rightly called composite typical oracles.

units.la: Probatio minoris à natura typi: quia typum Christi esse, est similitudine quadam conditionis vel gestorum, vel eventuum Christum præfigurare.
units.tr: Proof of the minor from the nature of a type: because to be a type of Christ is, by a certain similitude of condition or of deeds or events, to foreshadow Christ.

units.la: Illustretur exemplo de fractura prohibita ossium agni & Christi.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated by the example of the forbidden breaking of the bones of the lamb and of Christ.

units.la: Conclusio: Ergo aut est aliqua talis similitudo in typis & in Christo: aut typi non fuerunt typi Christi.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore either there is some such similitude between the types and Christ, or the types were not types of Christ.

units.la: Argumentum III. à veritate historiæ sacræ, quæ typicam impletionem in typis facta esse testatur, quæque negata impletione typica ipsa negaretur.
units.tr: Argument III, from the truth of sacred history, which testifies that the typical fulfilment was accomplished in the types, and which, if the fulfilment were denied, would itself be denied as a type.

units.la: Ostendatur exemplis: negaretur offa agni nō esse fracta: Exod.12. Principes & populos adver-sus Davidem unctum Domini esse tumultuatos. Psal.2.contra historiam, 2.Sam.2.3.5.8.10.&c.Davidem clamasse in angustiis, Psal.22. Confisum esse in Domino.Psal.31.&c.
units.tr: Let it be shown by examples: it would be denied that the bone of the lamb was not broken (Exod. 12); that the princes and peoples raged against David, the anointed of the Lord (Ps. 2), contrary to history (2 Sam. 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, etc.); that David cried out in distress (Ps. 22), and trusted in the Lord (Ps. 31), etc.

units.la: Obiectio:Clamavit in persona Messię.
units.tr: Objection: He cried out in the person of the Messiah.

units.la: Resp.1. Ergo & ipse clamavit: & quidem ex vero cordis affectu & sensu doloris sui: Ratio, Quia & ipse vere fuit a Deo desertus. 2. Angustiis suis & clamore typico præfiguravit angustias & clamorem Messiæ verum.
units.tr: Answer. 1. Therefore he too cried out, and indeed from the true affection of his heart and the feeling of his own grief. Reason: because he too was truly forsaken by God. 2. By his own distress and typical cry he foreshadowed the distress and the true cry of the Messiah.

units.la: Argum. I V.ab incomodo:Quia in multis Iudęi nō possunt convinci, nisi ex analog.typi &Christi.
units.tr: Argument IV, from the inconvenience: because in many matters the Jews cannot be convinced except from the analogy of the type and of Christ.

units.la: Probatio ab enumeratione triū modorū quib. oracula ad Christum pertinere evincitur. 1. Authoritate N.T.2.excellentia attributorum. 3. analogia & nexu necessario typi cum antitypo seu typi substantia, quæ est Christus.
units.tr: Proof, from the enumeration of the three modes by which it is proved that the oracles pertain to Christ: (1) by the authority of the New Testament; (2) by the excellence of the attributes; (3) by the analogy and necessary connection of the type with the antitype, or of the substance of the type, which is Christ.

units.la: Applicatio: Primum modum abjiciunt Judæi. Secundū tantum oracula quędā admittūt. Ergo plurima tertio modo sūt defendeda cōtra Iudęos.
units.tr: Application: The Jews reject the first mode. They admit only certain oracles in the second. Therefore very many must be defended against the Jews by the third mode.

units.la: Ostendatur uno & altero exemplo: Psal.31. In manus tuas Domine, &c. Psal.78. Aperiam os meum in parabolis, &c.
units.tr: Let it be shown by one or two examples: Ps. 31, "Into your hands, O Lord," etc.; Ps. 78, "I will open my mouth in parables," etc.

units.la: Argum. V. Ab authoritate Augustini Psalm. 72. de Solomone typice, de Christo significate interpretantis lib.17.de Civit. Dei, cap. 8. & recentium quorundam, Corneri, Patientis, &c. qui multos Psalmos ut 8. 16.18.22.31.44.45 59.68. 72.89.118.&c.typo & Christo accommodant.De similib.vero est similejudicium.
units.tr: Argument V, from the authority of Augustine, who, in expounding Ps. 72, interprets it typically of Solomon and significantly of Christ (book 17 of The City of God, chapter 8), and of certain recent writers, Cornerus, Pantaleon, etc., who apply many Psalms, such as 8, 16, 18, 22, 31, 44, 45, 59, 68, 72, 89, 118, etc., to the type and to Christ. The judgment on similar passages is indeed similar.

units.la: Claudatur confirmatio: & transfatur ad confutationem diversæ sententiæ.
units.tr: Let the confirmation be concluded, and let us pass to the refutation of the opposing opinion.

units.la: Resp. ad rationes amici.
units.tr: Answer to the arguments of your friend.

units.la: Ad primam de discrimine typorum & oraculorum. Resp. negatione consequentiæ: quia non omnia oracula sine figurarum involucris Christi præfigurarunt; sed tantum quædam: quædam autem habuerunt typos adjunctos. Provocetur ad exempla superiora.
units.tr: To the first, concerning the distinction of types and oracles. Answer: by denying the consequence, because not all oracles foreshadowed Christ without the veils of figures, but only some; and some indeed had types joined to them. Let appeal be made to the examples above.

units.la: Ad secundam, de Evangelistarum & Apostolorum restrictione ad Christum. Resp. I. negatione minoris: nusquam ita restringunt ad Christum, ut impletionem typicam præcessisse negent.
units.tr: To the second, concerning the restriction of the Evangelists and Apostles to Christ. Answer. 1. By denying the minor: they nowhere so restrict these to Christ as to deny that a typical fulfilment preceded.

units.la: Ratio I. quia non negant historiam Propheticam.
units.tr: Reason 1: because they do not deny the prophetic history.

units.la: Ratio II. Quia nusquam addunt exclusivas particulas.
units.tr: Reason 2: because they nowhere add exclusive particles.

units.la: II. Distinctione maioris. Loquitur de impletione significata & perfecta, quam ad solum Christum restringunt.
units.tr: 2. By distinguishing the major. It speaks of the signified and perfect fulfilment, which they restrict to Christ alone.

units.la: Utraq; responsio illustretur exemplo agni. Posterior ex Act. 4. 27: Vere convenerunt Principes, &c. q.d. quod olim in Davide præfiguratum fuit, nunc vere in Christo est impletum.
units.tr: Both answers are illustrated by the example of the lamb. The latter from Acts 4:27, "Truly there were gathered together the princes," etc.; that is to say, what was formerly foreshadowed in David is now truly fulfilled in Christ.

units.la: Ad tertiam, de enervatione oraculorum contra Iudæos: Resp. negatione minoris.
units.tr: To the third, concerning the enervation of the oracles against the Jews: Answer: by denying the minor.

units.la: Ad ejusdem probationem, negatione consequentiæ: quia non quævis impletio sed impletio significata & perfecta oraculorum est proprium Messiæ. Messię quarto modo. Ab hac sola igitur ad Mes-siam valet consequentia necessario.
units.tr: To its proof, by denying the consequence: because it is not every fulfilment but the signified and perfect fulfilment of the oracles that is proper to the Messiah. The Messiah in the fourth mode. From this alone, therefore, the consequence holds necessarily to the Messiah.

units.la: Formetur integra demonstratio: In quo vera & plena est oraculorum propheticorum impletio is est Messias promissus.
units.tr: Let the whole demonstration be formed: He in whom the true and full fulfilment of the prophetic oracles is found is the promised Messiah.

units.la: In Iesu crucifixo Domino nostro vera & plena est eorum impletio: Ergo, &c. Maior patet per se: Minor collatione historiae Evangelicae cum Oraculis.
units.tr: In Jesus crucified, our Lord, their true and full fulfilment is found. Therefore, etc. The major is evident in itself; the minor by comparing the Gospel history with the oracles.

units.la: Ad amplificationem incommodi. Respon. per negationem: quia non videndum, quid Judaei arripiant vel rejiciat, sed quid eis solide possit extorqueri.
units.tr: For amplifying the inconvenience. Reply: by denial, because we must consider not what the Jews seize upon or reject, but what can be solidly wrested from them.

units.la: Ostendatur, quomodo impletio significata seu Anagogica eis extorqueatur de Christo. 1. Ex ma-jestate seu excellentia attributorum. 2. ex ipsa ty-pica impletione; quam non possunt negare propter historiam: per Βίωον[?]: Typica impletio praecessit in typis, teste historia: Ergo impletio vera significata necessario intelligitur sequi in Christo. Valet à necessario nexu typi & substantiae typi.
units.tr: Let it be shown how the signified or anagogical fulfilment is wrested from them concerning Christ. 1. From the majesty or excellence of the attributes. 2. From the typical fulfilment itself, which they cannot deny on account of history: by [?]: the typical fulfilment came first in the types, as history attests. Therefore the true signified fulfilment is necessarily understood to follow in Christ. This holds from the necessary connection between the type and the substance of the type.

units.la: Ad quartam. Respon. 1. per distinctionem: Typi praedixerunt in persona Christi impletionem veram & perfectam 2. non semper praedixerunt nudis verbis, sed saepe facientes aut patientes similia eorum quae de Christo praedicebant. Exemplum: David clamans: Deus meus, Deus meus quare me dereliquisti, &c. ipse etiam Deum suum inclamavit: sentiens se derelictum, vere, non fictitiè, &c. Hęc autè fuit ipsa impleimpletio typica præfigurans significatam evidentiorem futuram in Christo.
units.tr: To the fourth. Reply: 1. by distinction: the types foretold a true and perfect fulfilment in the person of Christ; 2. they did not always foretell it in bare words, but often by doing or suffering things similar to those which were predicted of Christ. Example: David crying out, "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" etc. He himself also called upon his God, feeling himself forsaken, truly and not feignedly, etc. This, moreover, was the typical fulfilment itself, prefiguring the clearer fulfilment to come in Christ.

units.la: Ad quintam, de Authoritatibus, Respondetur per negationem: quia non omnes omnia de solo Christo interpretantur, typis simpliciter negatis: quod ostendatur ex argumento quinto confirmationis.
units.tr: To the fifth, concerning the authorities, it is answered by denial: because not all of them interpret everything solely of Christ, with types simply denied; this is shown from the fifth argument of the confirmation.

units.la: Conclusio sit extenuatio officii præstiti: & hortatio amici, ut ista recte meditetur, expensis ordine oraculis in Novo Testamento allegatis, nec prius abjiciat, quam recte intelligat: audiat & alios, & scopum habeat, non ut in tam gravi argumento a se dissentientes morosè traducat, tanquam Iudaizantes: sed ut fidem Christianam solidis rationibus contra Iudæorum elusiones præmunitam teneat.
units.tr: The conclusion is a lessening of the office rendered, and an exhortation to a friend that he should rightly meditate on these things, weighing in order the oracles alleged in the New Testament, and not reject them before he rightly understands them; let him hear others too, and keep the aim not of censuring with peevish accusations those who dissent from him in so grave a matter, as though they were Judaizers, but of holding the Christian faith fortified with solid reasons against the evasions of the Jews.

units.la: Exercitatio X L.
units.tr: Exercitatio X L.

units.la: An Babylon in Apocalypsi significet Romam. Quæstio ad amicum.
units.tr: Whether Babylon in the Apocalypse signifies Rome. A question for a friend.

units.la: EXordium a thesi de obscuritate Apocalypseos & ejus obscuritatis causa, quia de rebus futuris loquitur per figuras.
units.tr: The introduction: from the thesis concerning the obscurity of the Apocalypse, and the cause of that obscurity, namely that it speaks of future things by means of figures.

units.la: ὑπόθεσις[?]: Sæpè fieri mentionem Babylonis & ejus ruinæ: cap.14.8.&16.19.&17.5.&18.2.10.21. Obscurum autem videri an Roma per eam sit intelligenda.
units.tr: Hypothesis: Mention is often made of Babylon and of its ruin: Rev. 14.8; 16.19; 17.5; 18.2, 10, 21. It seems obscure, however, whether Rome is to be understood by it.

units.la: Propositio: Tibi non videri.
units.tr: Proposition: It does not seem so to you.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia decet Scripturam proprie accipere, ubi non cogit fides ad tropos discedere: ut hic non cogit. Ergo Babylon proprie magna illa urbs Chaldæorum à prophetis toties celebrata videtur intelligenda.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because Scripture ought to be taken literally, where faith does not compel us to depart into tropes, as it does not compel us here. Therefore Babylon seems to be rightly understood as that great city of the Chaldeans, so often celebrated by the prophets.

units.la: eAmplif. à prædictionib. prophetarum de ruina Babylonis. Ier. 21.9. & 48.20. Ier. 50.2. &c.
units.tr: Amplification from the prophets' predictions of the ruin of Babylon: Jer. 21.9; 48.20; Jer. 50.2, etc.

units.la: Ratio II. Non possunt omnia urbi Romę accommodari, quæ de Babylone dicuntur, quod ostendatur.
units.tr: Reason II. Not all the things said of Babylon can be applied to the city of Rome, as may be shown.

units.la: Ratio III. Roma celebratur in scriptis apostolorum & historia Ecclesiastica urbs sancta, sedes apostolica, mater Ecclesiarum, adversus quam portæ inferorum non prævalebunt, Matt. 16. Nō ergo Babylon.
units.tr: Reason III. Rome is celebrated in the writings of the apostles and in ecclesiastical history as the holy city, the apostolic see, the mother of the churches, against which the gates of hell shall not prevail, Matt. 16. Therefore not Babylon.

units.la: Ratio IV. Plurimi interpretes veteres & recentes non de Roma, sed vel de Babylone Chaldæę vel de Bab. Ægyptiorum interpretatur. Lyra de ruina imperii Græcor. propter hęreses, Iesuitæ hodie de Roma quidem sed veteri, sub Impp.
units.tr: Reason IV. Many interpreters, both ancient and recent, explain it not of Rome but either of Babylon of the Chaldeans or of Babylon of the Egyptians. Lyra explains it of the ruin of the Greek empire on account of heresies; the Jesuits today explain it of Rome, indeed, but of ancient Rome, under the emperors.

units.la: Concl. Cum amicus jā publicè audiat in Acad. Apocalypsin explicari, rogetur ejus sententia.
units.tr: Conclusion. Since your friend already hears publicly in the Academy that the Apocalypse is being expounded, let his opinion be asked.

units.la: Resp. ad amicum de Babyl.
units.tr: Reply to a friend concerning Babylon.

units.la: Exord. sit brevis extenuatio tui judicii de re tā obscura & declaratio studii tui erga amicum.
units.tr: The introduction should be a brief statement of your judgment on a matter so obscure, and a declaration of your zeal toward a friend.

units.la: Propositio bipartita habeat rejectionem falsarū sententiarum & assertionem veræ, quod Babylo Apocalypseos non sit Babylon Chaldæorum vel Ægyptiorum: nec totus mundus: qui secundum quosdā est magna illa civitas impiorū, sed Roma, & quidem quam Rom. Papa nunc occupat.
units.tr: The proposition, which has two parts, should contain a rejection of false opinions and an assertion of the true one: that the Babylon of the Apocalypse is not the Babylon of the Chaldeans or of the Egyptians, nor the whole world, which according to some is that great city of the wicked, but Rome, and indeed that Rome which the Roman Pope now occupies.

units.la: 1. Quòd non Babylon Orientis vel Australis, p-betur: quia neutra est vel erit sedes Antichristi.
units.tr: 1. That it is not Babylon of the East or of the South, since neither is nor will be the seat of Antichrist.

units.la: Rejiciatur vetus fabula de ortu & sede Antich. ex tribu Dan in Chaldæa. Ostendatur artificium Satanæ volentis nos ab-ducere à vero Antichristo ad fictitium: ut minus caveamus: ac probetur Antichristum oriturum ac sessurum in ipsa Ecclesia, non extra, 2. Thes.2.
units.tr: The old fable about the origin and seat of Antichrist from the tribe of Dan in Chaldea should be rejected. The craft of Satan should be shown, who wishes to lead us away from the true Antichrist to a fictitious one, so that we take less care; and it should be proved that Antichrist will arise and sit in the Church itself, not outside it (2 Thess. 2).

units.la: Ad rationem 1. respondeatur per negationem regulæ universaliter intellectę. Ratio: quia multa in Scripturis, præsertim in Apocalypsi allegoricè vel alio tropo dicantur: ut Paulus scribit se ereptum ex ore leonis: Iohannes Christum vocat Leonem de tribu Iuda: agnum occisum ab origi-ne, &c. Romam vocat Ægyptum, Sodomam, Hie-rosolymam spiritualem.
units.tr: To the first argument, reply by denying the rule as universally understood. The reason: because many things in the Scriptures, especially in the Apocalypse, are said allegorically or by some other trope: as Paul writes that he was rescued from the mouth of the lion; John calls Christ the Lion of the tribe of Judah; the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world, etc. He calls Rome Egypt, Sodom, and spiritual Jerusalem.

units.la: Ad amplif. ex prophetis: Resp. Illa pertinere ad typum: Iohannem loqui de veritate typi.
units.tr: To the amplification from the prophets: the reply is that those things pertain to the type, and John speaks of the truth of the type.

units.la: Ad rationem II. Resp. Posse omnia Romę ac-commodari melius quam Babyloni: quod postea ostendetur.
units.tr: To the second argument, the reply is that all things can be applied to Rome better than to Babylon; this will be shown afterwards.

units.la: Ad rationem III. Resp. Romam celebrari ab Apostolis & in historia Ecclesiastica, qualis tunc erat: non qualis nunc est & erit sub Antichristo.
units.tr: To the third argument, the reply is that Rome is celebrated by the Apostles and in ecclesiastical history, as it then was, not as it now is and will be under Antichrist.

units.la: Rejiciantur assentatoriæ laudes Romanæ Ec-clesiæ: & ad Ecclesiam Catholicam Christi eas pertinere ostendatur.
units.tr: The fawning praises of the Roman Church should be rejected, and it should be shown that they pertain to the Catholic Church of Christ.

units.la: Ad rationem IV. Resp. Multos ex veteribus deceptos nomine Babylonis & titulis Romanæ Ecclesiæ errasse.
units.tr: To the fourth argument, the reply is that many of the ancients, deceived by the name of Babylon and the titles of the Roman Church, erred.

units.la: 2. Multos etiam de Roma intelligere: Augu-stin. Hieron. Euseb. Orosium Niceph. &c.
units.tr: 2. Many also understood it of Rome: Augustine, Jerome, Eusebius, Orosius, Nicephorus, etc.

units.la: II. Quod non sit ipse mundus.
units.tr: II. That it is not the world itself.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia meretrix magna est Babylon. c. 17.18. non autem est mundus: quia mundum & mundi reges vino scortationis inebriabit. c.17.2.
units.tr: The reason 1: because the great harlot is Babylon (ch. 17–18), but she is not the world, since she will make the world and the kings of the world drunk with the wine of her fornication (ch. 17:2).

units.la: II. Ruina Babylonis non est interitus mundi. Ergo nec Babylon mundus.
units.tr: II. The ruin of Babylon is not the destruction of the world. Therefore neither is Babylon the world.

units.la: Probetur anteced. quia ruina Babylonis & judicium meretricis idem. cap. 17. 1. & 18. 2. At hoc nō est interitus mundi.
units.tr: The antecedent is proved: because the ruin of Babylon and the judgment of the harlot are the same (ch. 17:1 and 18:2). But this is not the destruction of the world.

units.la: Ratio: quia reges, mercatores, nautę plangent super eam cap. 18. 9. Ergo hi erunt post judicium. At non erunt post judicium mundi.
units.tr: The reason: because the kings, merchants, and sailors will lament over her (ch. 18:9). Therefore these will be after the judgment. But they will not be after the judgment of the world.

units.la: III. Iubemur exire è Babylone. c. 18. 4. At nō ex mundo. 1. Cor. 5. 10.
units.tr: III. We are commanded to come out of Babylon (ch. 18:4). But not out of the world (1 Cor. 5:10).

units.la: IV. A communi consensu quod Iohannes vaticinetur de sede Antichristi. Hæc autem no erit totus mundus.
units.tr: IV. By common consensus, John prophesies about the seat of Antichrist. But this will not be the whole world.

units.la: III. TRANSITIO ad veram sententiam. Est Roma, dicta Babylon propter horribiles confusiones civiles & spirituales.
units.tr: III. Transition to the true interpretation. It is Rome, called Babylon on account of the dreadful civil and spiritual confusions.

units.la: Probetur 1. à Πηγαδία septem montium, quibus mulier dicitur insidere, urbs incumbere. c. 17. 9. Ea non legitur competere urbi alicui, nisi ROMÆ: quæ jam olim septicollis, septijuga dicta: Varroni vocatur ἑπτάλοφος. Virgil. Scilicet & rerum facta est pulcherrima Roma Septem quæ una sibi muro circundedit arces.
units.tr: It is proved, first, from the seven mountains on which the woman is said to sit, the city lying upon them (Rev. 17.9). This is not read as applying to any city except ROME, which was long ago called the city of seven hills, the city of seven ridges; by Varro it is called heptalophos [ἑπτάλοφος]. Virgil: Indeed Rome has been made the most beautiful of things, which alone enclosed seven citadels within one wall.

units.la: Propert. Vrbs septem alta jugis toti quæ præsidet orbi.
units.tr: Propertius: The city, high on seven ridges, which presides over the whole world.

units.la: II. A monarchia, quam urbs habebat Iohannis tempore in reges terræ, cap. 17. 18. Ea autem non erat alia quam Roma.
units.tr: II. From the monarchy which the city had over the kings of the earth in John's time (Rev. 17.18). This was none other than Rome.

units.la: III. Ab authoritate veterum: Papiæ discipuli Johannis apud Eusebium hist. Eccl. l. 2. c. 15. Tertul. adv. Iud. Hier. in Isai. 47. Aug. de C. D. l. 18. c. 22. Orosius synchroni ejus l. 2. c. 3. & l. 7. c. 2.
units.tr: III. From the authority of the ancients: Papias, a disciple of John, in Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History, book 2, chapter 15; Tertullian, against the Jews; Jerome on Isaiah 47; Augustine, City of God, book 18, chapter 22; Orosius, his contemporary, book 2, chapter 3, and book 7, chapter 2.

units.la: Obiect. Papistarum occupetur, quod sit Roma quidem, sed vetus Ethnica sub impiis Impp. non Christiana sub sanctis Papis:
units.tr: Objection. The Papists maintain that it is indeed Rome, but the old pagan Rome under the impious emperors, not the Christian Rome under the holy popes.

units.la: Demonstretur contrà, quod nō sit Roma Ethnica sed Papalis.
units.tr: It is shown, on the contrary, that it is not pagan Rome but papal Rome.

units.la: 1. quia Roma Ethnica non fuit sedes Antichristi: de qua communi consensu vaticinatur Iohannes. Probetur anteced: Quia Antichristus nondum fuit Romæ sub impiis Impp.
units.tr: 1. Because pagan Rome was not the seat of Antichrist, of which John prophesies by common consent. The antecedent is proved: because Antichrist was not yet at Rome under the impious emperors.

units.la: II. Non de veteri sed de Papali Roma potest intelligi: Inebriavit incolas terræ vino scortationis suæ: Et:(cum ea scortati sunt reges terræ.
units.tr: II. It can be understood not of old but of papal Rome: She has made the inhabitants of the earth drunk with the wine of her fornication (Rev. 17.2); and: with her the kings of the earth have committed fornication (Rev. 18.3).

units.la: Ratio: quia vetus αὐτονομίαν[?] religionis reliquit gentibus quas subegit: Papalis vero omnib. etiam invitis superstitiones & Idololatriam suam obtrudit.
units.tr: Reason: because the old Rome left the peoples it subdued their own autonomy in religion, whereas papal Rome forces its superstitions and idolatry upon everyone, even the unwilling.

units.la: Ostendatur utrunque ex historiis: & quod scortatio hæc de Idololatria loquatur.
units.tr: Both should be shown from the histories, and that this fornication speaks of idolatry.

units.la: III. Patrum tempore sub Christianis Impp. Roma jam desierat esse Ethnica: & tamen illi vocant eam Babylonem. Ergo non Ethnicam.
units.tr: III. In the time of the Fathers, under Christian emperors, Rome had already ceased to be pagan, and yet they call it Babylon. Therefore it is not pagan.

units.la: IV. Ea Roma est Babylon, cujus ruina post tempora patrum erat futura.
units.tr: IV. That Rome is Babylon, whose ruin was to come after the time of the Fathers.

units.la: Ratio: quia tunc Babylon nondum ceciderat. Nec vero Ethnica erat ruitura: Quia non amplius erat, &c. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Reason: because Babylon had not yet fallen then. Nor indeed was pagan Rome destined to fall, since it no longer existed, etc. Therefore, etc.

units.la: v. Ea Roma est Babylon, quæ nundinatur animas hominum. Apoc. 18.13. At hæc non fecit Ethnica, sed Papalis facit cum suis indulgentiis.
units.tr: V. That Rome is Babylon, which trades in the souls of men (Rev. 18.13). But this was not done by pagan Rome; papal Rome does it with its indulgences.

units.la: VI. A testimonio quorundam Iesuitarum fatentium Romam præsentem intelligi, & futu-
units.tr: VI. From the testimony of certain Jesuits, who admit that the Rome of the present is meant, and that the future seat of Antichrist will be there, namely once the Pope has been cast out.

units.la: ram sedem Antichristi, ejecto scilicet Papa.
units.tr: Objection: John speaks of Babylon, and of Rome as having dominion over the kings of the earth. But that was pagan.

units.la: Obiectio: Iohannes loquitur de Babylone, & Roma habente imperium in reges terrę. Ea autem fuit Ethnica.
units.tr: Answer: Papal Rome also claims this for itself and usurps it from the falsely pretended donation of Constantine (Decretum, distinction 96, Constantinus): by constituting and deposing kings of the earth.

units.la: Respon. Etiam Papalis sibi hanc arrogat & usurpat ex falso prætensa donatione Constantini. Decr.dist.96. C.Constantinus: constituendo & deponendo reges terræ.
units.tr: Response. The Papal party also claims this for itself and arrogates it, from the falsely pretended donation of Constantine (Decr. dist. 96, C. Constantinus): that it is for the Pope to appoint and depose kings of the earth.

units.la: Conclusio: Cum Babylon sit Roma Papalis, nō dubium, quin Romanus Papatus sit regnum Antichristi, Papa ejus caput Antichristus, Spirituo-ris Dei destruendus, &c.
units.tr: Conclusion: Since Babylon is the Papal Rome, there is no doubt that the Roman papacy is the kingdom of Antichrist, and its Pope is the head of Antichrist, who is to be destroyed by the Spirit of God, etc.

units.la: Exercitatio XLI.
units.tr: Exercitatio XLI.

units.la: An recte fecerit Paulus Cæsarem appellans. Act. 25.
units.tr: Whether Paul acted rightly in appealing to Caesar. Acts 25.

units.la: EXordium à concessione Thesis: Non omnia sanctorum facta & exempla excusationem merentur.
units.tr: Introduction, starting from a concession. Thesis: Not all the deeds and examples of the saints deserve excuse.

units.la: Hypothesis per adversat, quę sit propositio: Pau-li tamen provocatio ad Cæsarem culpa vacat.
units.tr: Hypothesis, put in the form of a contrary proposition: Nevertheless, Paul's appeal to Caesar is free from fault.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia Paulus fuit civis Romanus. At licet civi uti legibus suæ civitatis.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because Paul was a Roman citizen. But it is permitted for a citizen to use the laws of his own state.

units.la: I I. à fine ordinis civilis: Magistratus in commodum & laudem bonorum divinitus est ordinatus.
units.tr: II. From the end of civil order: the magistrate has been ordained by God for the good and praise of good men.

units.la: I I I. In necessitate licet uti mediis legitimis. Ergo etiam legum præsidio.
units.tr: III. In necessity it is permitted to use lawful means. Therefore also the protection of the laws.

units.la: Probetur necessitas ex historia: Quia aliter quàm appellatione non potuit declinare forum Iudæorum.
units.tr: The necessity is proved from history: because otherwise he could not avoid the Jewish court except by appeal.

units.la: Amplificetur ex lege: Non occides. Si non appellasset: ipse fuisset causa necis suæ.
units.tr: It is strengthened from the law: "You shall not kill." If he had not appealed, he himself would have been the cause of his own death.

units.la: Obiectio 1. In causa bona non erat declinandum forum.
units.tr: Objection 1. In a good cause one ought not to avoid the court.

units.la: Respon.legitimum: de insidiis & violentia injusta non suspectum quale fuit Iudæorum.
units.tr: Answer: a lawful court, not suspect of ambushes and unjust violence, which the Jews' court was.

units.la: Instantia: Erat certus de conservatione. Ergo non debuit metuere insidias.
units.tr: Instance: He was certain of his preservation. Therefore he ought not to have feared ambushes.

units.la: Amplif.illo Horatii.
units.tr: Amplification: from that line of Horace.

units.la: Iustum & tenacem propositi virum, &c.
units.tr: "The man who is just and firm in his purpose, etc."

units.la: Respon.Negatione majoris omisse, quia certitudo finis non excludit usum mediorum.
units.tr: Answer: by denying the major premise, which was omitted, because certainty of the end does not exclude the use of means.

units.la: Obiectio 11. Non debuit Evangelium subjicere cognitioni Neronis hominis profani.
units.tr: Objection 2. He ought not to have subjected the Gospel to the judgment of Nero, a profane man.

units.la: Respond. Fallacia non causæ. Provocat ad summum tribunal Imperatoris, cum apud inferius nihil juris esset, non ut Evangelii sed ut causæ civilis, quæ in eum agebatur, fieret cognitio.
units.tr: Answer: a fallacy of the non-cause. He appealed to the highest tribunal of the Emperor, since before the lower court there was no right at all; the case was brought before him not as a matter of the Gospel but as a civil cause, which was being pursued against him.

units.la: Obiectio 111. Ipse prohibet litigare Christianos ad tribunal Ethnicorum.
units.tr: Objection 3. He himself forbids Christians to litigate before the tribunal of the heathen.

units.la: Respon. 1. cum Christianis. 2. de rebus le-vibus quas ipsi possent componere. 3. Etiam de gravibus si possit haberi Christianus judex.
units.tr: Answer: 1. This applies to Christians with Christians. 2. It applies to trivial matters which they themselves could settle. 3. It applies even to serious matters, if a Christian judge can be had.

units.la: Ostendatur hic omnia fuisse diversa.
units.tr: Here it should be shown that all these circumstances were different.

units.la: Conclusio: Christianis licet uti legibus & jure civili exemplo Pauli in causa justa, cum postulat necessitas.
units.tr: Conclusion: Christians may use the laws and the civil right, following the example of Paul, in a just cause, when necessity demands it.

units.la: Exercitatio. XLII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XLII.

units.la: De peccato Davidis numerantis populum. 2.Sam.24.
units.tr: On the sin of David in numbering the people. 2 Sam. 24.

units.la: Breviter narretur historia numerationis populi. 2.Sam.24.
units.tr: Let the history of the numbering of the people be briefly related. 2 Sam. 24.

units.la: A' ποεία[?] : videtur David non peccasse.
units.tr: Objection (from the first position): it seems that David did not sin.

units.la: Ratio: quia fecit ex lege Exod.30. & ex officio.
units.tr: Reason: because he acted in accordance with the law of Exodus 30 and from his office.

units.la: Principis est virtus maxima nosse suos.
units.tr: The greatest virtue of a prince is to know his own people.

units.la: Antithesis sit propositio: Sed graviter peccavit.
units.tr: Antithesis, let the proposition be: But he sinned grievously.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia multa gravia peccata in eo facto concurrunt.
units.tr: Reason 1: because many grave sins concur in that deed.

units.la: 1. Superbia & elatio animi, ut possit gloriari de multitudine.
units.tr: 1. Pride and haughtiness of mind, so that he could boast of the multitude.

units.la: Amplif. comparatione cum peccato Hiskiae, ostentantis thesauros 1.Reg.24. Et Nebucadnezaris exclamantis: Haec est illa Babylon.
units.tr: Amplification by comparison with the sin of Hezekiah, who displayed his treasures (1 Kings 24), and with Nebuchadnezzar, who cried out: Is not this great Babylon?

units.la: 2. Confidentia propriae potentiae, qua contra hostes, se tutum putavit magis quam Dei praesidio.
units.tr: 2. Confidence in his own power, by which he thought himself safer against enemies than under the protection of God.

units.la: 3. Curiositas, quod nulla urgente necessitate census instituit.
units.tr: 3. Curiosity, because he undertook the census without any pressing necessity.

units.la: 4. Avaritia, quia simul censu novo, ut fit probabile, fiscum regium explere voluit.
units.tr: 4. Avarice, because at the same time, by the new census, as is probable, he wished to fill the royal treasury.

units.la: Ergo non ex officio: quia Principis virtus est nosse suos non ad ostentandum, vel deglubendum, sed ad tuendum & benefaciendum.
units.tr: Therefore it was not from his office: for the virtue of a prince is to know his own people, not for display or for plundering, but for protecting and doing good.

units.la: Ratio 11. Quia contra legem census instituit.
units.tr: Reason 2: because he instituted the census contrary to the law.

units.la: Ostendatur, quod lex census populi non permisit nisi justa de causa, & cum pensione semisicli in fiscum tabernaculi.
units.tr: Let it be shown that the law did not permit a census of the people except for a just cause, and then only with the payment of a half-shekel into the treasury of the tabernacle.

units.la: Ergo non secundum legem.
units.tr: Therefore not according to the law.

units.la: Ratio III. Deus voluit hunc populum esse innumerabilem ut impleretur promissio: Multiplicabo semen tuum, &c.
units.tr: Reason 3: God willed this people to be innumerable, so that the promise might be fulfilled: I will multiply your seed, etc.

units.la: Ratio IV. A causa impellente: quia Satan eum incitavit. 1. Paral. 21.
units.tr: Reason 4: from the impelling cause: because Satan incited him. 1 Chron. 21.

units.la: Objectio: Atqui Deus dicitur concitasse.
units.tr: Objection: But God is said to have stirred him up.

units.la: Resp. Furor Iehovæ per Satanam: non impel-lendo ad peccandum sed deserendo in tentatio-ne: explorationis & castigationis causa.
units.tr: Answer: The anger of Jehovah was (exercised) through Satan: not by impelling him to sin, but by abandoning him to temptation, for the sake of testing and chastisement.

units.la: Ratio V. Ab effectu gemino: Mala Davidis conscientia: Quia cor eum percussit paulo post: & peste subsequente.
units.tr: Reason 5: from a twofold effect: David's evil conscience, since his heart struck him shortly afterwards; and the pestilence that followed.

units.la: Conclusio sit thesis: Sanctorum lapsus considerandi, ut simus humiles, & timeamus Deum.
units.tr: The conclusion is the thesis: The falls of the saints are to be considered, so that we may be humble and fear God.

units.la: Exercitatio XLIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XLIII.

units.la: De pœnitentia Davidis post numerationem populi. συγγραμματικὸν [?] ὁμιλητικὸν vel ἐξηγητικόν.
units.tr: On David's repentance after the numbering of the people. συγγραμματικὸν [?] ὁμιλητικὸν vel ἐξηγητικόν.

units.la: EXordium a thesi: Scriptura non solum recitat Sanctorum lapsus, ut imbecillitatem naturæ & insidias Satanæ agnoscamus: sed eorundem etiam resipiscentiam & veniam, ut in lapsibus non jacere, sed fiducia misericordiæ Dei eorum exemplis nos erigere discamus.
units.tr: Introduction from the thesis: Scripture does not merely recount the falls of the saints, so that we may recognise the weakness of our nature and the snares of Satan; it also recounts their repentance and pardon, so that we may learn not to lie prostrate in our falls, but by trust in the mercy of God to raise ourselves up by their examples.

units.la: Hypothesis sit exemplum Davidis peccatum & resipiscentia.
units.tr: Hypothesis: Let the example of David be his sin and his repentance.

units.la: Transitio: Proxime peccatum eius demon-stratum.
units.tr: Transition: His sin has been shown just above.

units.la: Propositio. Nunc resipiscentia explicanda ve-nit nit juxta historiæ circumstantias.
units.tr: Proposition: Now his repentance comes to be explained according to the circumstances of the history.

units.la: ἔκθεσις[?] in tribus consistat: Quando, unde & quomodo David resipuerit.
units.tr: Exposition [?] consists in three parts: When, whence and how David repented.

units.la: I. Quando: Text: Postquam numeraverat populum. Numeratio duraverat menses 9. dies 20. Tamdiu securus fuit sine pœnitentia, & Deus pœnas distulit.
units.tr: I. When: Text: After he had numbered the people. The numbering had lasted nine months and twenty days. For so long he was secure without repentance, and God deferred the punishments.

units.la: Transferatur ad thesin: quod pii sæpe diu fascinentur blanditiis carnis & peccati, ut deformitatem eius non videant, donec Deus eis oculos aperiat. Tamdiu autem sunt sub ira Dei.
units.tr: Let it be carried over to the thesis: that the godly are often for a long time bewitched by the flatteries of the flesh and of sin, so that they do not see its deformity, until God opens their eyes. Yet for so long they are under the wrath of God.

units.la: Ostendatur periculum sub ira Dei.
units.tr: Let the danger under the wrath of God be shown.

units.la: Ergo principiis obstandum.
units.tr: Therefore one must resist the beginnings.

units.la: Item: quod Deus non statim pœnas infligat: non quod non videat, sed quod patientia ad pœnitentiam invitet Rom.2.
units.tr: Likewise: that God does not inflict punishments at once: not because he does not see, but because his patience invites to repentance (Rom. 2).

units.la: II. Unde: Text. Percussit Davidem cor. Stimulis conscientiæ excutitur ei veternus peccati, & ad pœnitentiam excitatur. sive id mediate sive immediate factum: divinitus tamen factum:& pœnitentiæ origo à Deo.
units.tr: II. Whence: Text: His heart struck David. By the goads of conscience the lethargy of sin is shaken off from him, and he is roused to repentance. Whether this was done mediately or immediately, it was nonetheless done by divine agency; and the origin of repentance is from God.

units.la: Transferatur ad Thesin: quod peccatum initio blandiatur, tandem afferat conscientiæ cruciatum. Rom.2. Furia, &c. Ergo blanditiæ peccati fugiendæ,&c.
units.tr: Let it be carried over to the thesis: that sin at first flatters, but at last brings torment to the conscience (Rom. 2, Fury, etc.). Therefore the flatteries of sin are to be fled from, etc.

units.la: Item: quod pavores conscientiæ impiis afferant desperationem Ies. 57. Cain,Iudas, &c. Piis salutarem contritionem: Adam, David,Petrus, &c. 2. Cor.7.
units.tr: Likewise: that the terrors of conscience bring despair to the wicked (Isa. 57; Cain, Judas, etc.), but to the godly a saving contrition (Adam, David, Peter, etc.; 2 Cor. 7).

units.la: Addatur causa discriminis:
units.tr: Let the cause of the difference be added:

units.la: III. Quomodo: Tex. Peccavi graviter, Conversus ad Deum non palliat aut extenuat peccatum tum, nec desperat: sed lapsum agnoscit, fatetur, exaggerat, deplorat, deprecatur fiducia miseri-cordiæ Dei erga se servum Dei.
units.tr: III. How: Text: I have sinned grievously. Turning to God, he neither covers nor lessens his sin, nor does he despair; but he acknowledges his fall, confesses it, magnifies it, laments it, and entreats, by trust in the mercy of God towards himself, the servant of God.

units.la: Transferatur ad thesin: Typus veræ pœnitentiæ: quod sit conversio peccatoris ad Deum à peccato, fiducia mediatoris, in contritione salutari & fide consistens.
units.tr: Let it be carried over to the thesis: The type of true repentance: that it is the conversion of a sinner to God away from sin, by trust in the Mediator, consisting in saving contrition and faith.

units.la: Monstrentur singula ex textu:
units.tr: Let the individual points be shown from the text:

units.la: Describatur recte contritio salutaris à causa formali & impulsiva. Item, ab effectu, qui est feria deploratio & confessio peccati ad ipsum Deū.
units.tr: Let saving contrition be rightly described from its formal and impulsive cause. Likewise from its effect, which is the sorrowful lamentation and confession of sin to God himself.

units.la: Tibi soli peccavi, &c.
units.tr: Against you only have I sinned, etc.

units.la: Reiciatur auricularis & hypocritica: Item fides, à forma & ab effectu, qui est implo-ratio & consecutio veniæ propter Christum: Transfer peccatum: Propter Dominum: Quicquid petieritis in nomine meo:
units.tr: Auricular and hypocritical confession is to be rejected. Likewise faith, from its form and from its effect, which is the imploring and obtaining of pardon for Christ's sake: Transfer the sin: For the Lord's sake: Whatsoever you shall ask in my name.

units.la: Obiectio: At secutæ sunt graves pœnæ.
units.tr: Objection: But grave punishments followed.

units.la: Resp. Sed non æternæ. Temporales nō semper transferuntur cū peccato, nec cum Deo ludamus.
units.tr: Reply: Yet not eternal ones. Temporal punishments are not always removed along with the sin, nor should we trifle with God.

units.la: Claudatur hortatiuncula: ut in lapsibus similiter nos erigamus.
units.tr: Let the little exhortation be closed: that in our falls we likewise raise ourselves up.

units.la: Exercitatio XLIV.
units.tr: Exercitatio XLIV.

units.la: De optione pœnæ unius ex tribus Davidi propositæ: ex 2.Sam.24.
units.tr: On the choice of one of three punishments proposed to David: from 2 Samuel 24.

units.la: EXponatur optio pœnæ Davidi post peccatum & pœnitentiam divinitus propositæ: ex ver. 12 & 13. 2.Sam.24.
units.tr: The choice of punishment proposed to David by God after his sin and repentance is to be set out, from verses 12 and 13 of 2 Samuel 24.

units.la: Hinc tria moveantur & explicentur breviter.
units.tr: Three points are to be raised and briefly explained here.

units.la: 1. Cur Davidi pœnitenti denuncietur pœna, peccato iam remisso seu translato.
units.tr: 1. Why is a punishment announced to David, when he is penitent and the sin has already been remitted or removed?

units.la: Ratio ἀντίθεσις[?]: videtur pugnare cum promissione Ier.19. & regula: Sublata causa tollitur effectus.
units.tr: The objection [ἀντίθεσις?]: it seems to conflict with the promise in Jeremiah 19 and with the rule: when the cause is removed, the effect is removed.

units.la: Per adversativam ostendatur non pugnare.
units.tr: By the adversative (the "but"), it is shown that there is no conflict.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia promissio tantum loquitur de remissione culpæ & pœnæ æternæ, q; resipiscētib. semper cōtingit: de venia pœnæ tēporalis nō itē.
units.tr: Reason 1: because the promise speaks only of the remission of guilt and of eternal punishment, which always befalls those who repent; it does not likewise speak of the pardon of temporal punishment.

units.la: Ratio 11. Quia in resipiscentibus non tollitur omnis causa afflictionum cum culpa: Exponantur causæ.
units.tr: Reason 2: because in those who repent, not every cause of afflictions together with guilt is removed. The causes are to be set out.

units.la: 1. Gloria Dei, ne blasphemetur, quasi fautor scelerum 2. Sam.12. 14. Quia blasphemando blasphemare fecisti, &c.
units.tr: 1. The glory of God, lest he be blasphemed as a patron of wickedness: 2 Samuel 12:14, "Because by this deed you have given the enemies of the Lord cause to blaspheme, etc."

units.la: 11. Salus electorum, ne indulgetia fiat securiores.
units.tr: 2. The salvation of the elect, lest indulgence make them more secure.

units.la: 1.Cor.11. A Dno corripimur ne cū mūdo peamus,
units.tr: 1 Corinthians 11: "We are chastened by the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world."

units.la: 111. Terror impiorum. 1.Pet.4. Judicium, &c.
units.tr: 3. The terror of the wicked: 1 Peter 4, "Judgment, etc."

units.la: II. Cur tres simul pestem triduanam, bellum trimestre, famem triennalem & quidem illas non alias denunciet.
units.tr: II. Why does he announce three punishments together: a three days' pestilence, a three months' war, and a three years' famine, and these and no others?

units.la: 1. Quia inter temporales maledictiones legis hæ sunt præcipuæ Deut.27. Amplific. ab antecedentibus & consequentibus singulorum. Item exemplis Ierem.14.&.21.&29. Ezech.5.&6.
units.tr: 1. Because among the temporal curses of the law, these are the chief ones (Deuteronomy 27), amplified from the preceding and following circumstances of each. Likewise by the examples in Jeremiah 14, 21 and 29, and Ezekiel 5 and 6.

units.la: 2. Ut doceat omnes esse promeritum, & magisterreat.
units.tr: 2. So that he may teach that all are deserving, and terrify them.

units.la: 3. Quia singulæ ad minuendum populi numerum faciebant.
units.tr: 3. Because each of them served to diminish the number of the people.

units.la: 4. Ut doceat has pœnas non fortuito aut mūdi tantum malitia evenire, sed esse publica flagella Dei, quibus publica etiam peccata punit.
units.tr: 4. So that he may teach that these punishments do not happen by chance or by the malice of the world alone, but are the public scourges of God, by which he also punishes public sins.

units.la: III. Cur det optionem unius.
units.tr: III. Why does he give the choice of one?

units.la: 1. Ut optione David subscribat justitiæ Dei.
units.tr: 1. So that David may submit to the justice of God by the choice.

units.la: 2. Ut habeat geminum argumentum misericordiæ Dei: tum quod unicam tantum velit infligere, tum quod eam, quam ipse delegisset ut leviorem.
units.tr: 2. So that he may have a twofold argument of the mercy of God: first, that God wishes to inflict only one; second, that it is the one which David himself had chosen as the lighter.

units.la: Conclusio petatur ex dictis: Non irascetur in æternum. Fidelis Deus qui non sinit, &c.
units.tr: The conclusion is to be drawn from what has been said: "He will not be angry for ever. God is faithful, who does not suffer, etc."

units.la: Exercitatio XLV.
units.tr: Exercitatio XLV.

units.la: De electione pestis pro bello & fame. 2.Sam.24. & 1.Chron.21.
units.tr: On the choice of plague over war and famine. 2 Sam. 24 and 1 Chron. 21.

units.la: BReviter & sine ambagibus narretur electio Davidis præferentis pestem triduanam bello trimestri, & fami triennali.
units.tr: The election of David, who preferred a three-day plague to a three-month war and a three-year famine, is to be related briefly and without circumlocution.

units.la: 1. Angor Davidis, eiusque causa.
units.tr: 1. David's anguish, and its cause.

units.la: 2. Electio ipsa, cum ratione.
units.tr: 2. The election itself, with its reasoning.

units.la: Quaestio: an potuerit eligere, & an recte elegerit: cum electio non sit malorum: itern [?] bellum & fames æque sint manus Dei quam pestis: & in illis æque magna possit esse miseratio Dei quam in ista.
units.tr: Question: whether he could choose, and whether he chose rightly, since choosing is not a choice between evils; and whether war and famine are no less the hand of God than plague, and whether God's mercy can be as great in those as in this.

units.la: Propositio sit approbatio optionis.
units.tr: The proposition is the approval of his choice.

units.la: Confirmationis argumentum 1. ab obiecto voluntatis: quia pestis per se mala eligibilis fuit sub specie boni dupliciter. 1. ut castigatio Dei. 2. Ut minus malum: Et inter mala minus habet rationem boni. Fuisse vero pestem minus malum, simul aliquot rationibus sequentibus probatur.
units.tr: The argument for confirmation is, first, from the object of the will: the plague, evil in itself, could be chosen under the appearance of good in two ways. First, as a chastisement from God. Second, as the lesser evil; and among evils the lesser has the character of good. That the plague was in fact the lesser evil is proved at the same time by several following reasons.

units.la: Argumentum II. à causa efficiente, quia pestis manus Dei, in quam præstat incidere quam in manus hominum. Id explicetur & probetur ratione sumta ex verbis: Quia Dei miserationes multæ sunt.
units.tr: Second argument, from the efficient cause: the plague is the hand of God, and it is better to fall into the hand of God than into the hands of men. This is explained and proved by reasoning drawn from the words: "Because the mercies of God are many."

units.la: Hoc argumentum expoliatur trium objectiun-culârum solutione.
units.tr: This argument is polished by the answer to three small objections.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Etiam bellum & fames sunt manus Dei, quod probetur ex comminationibus.
units.tr: Objection 1. War and famine too are the hand of God, as is proved from the threats.

units.la: Resp. Sed mediata, quia hominum manib. infliguntur à Deo: ideo simul sunt manus hominum. Pestis immediata plaga Dei.
units.tr: Answer: yes, but mediately, since they are inflicted by God through the hands of men; so they are at the same time the hands of men. The plague is an immediate blow of God.

units.la: II. Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei Hebr. 10. Et Susanna dicit: Melius est incidere in manus vestras, quam in manus Dei.
units.tr: II. "It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of God," Heb. 10. And Susanna says: "It is better for me to fall into your hands than into the hands of God."

units.la: Responsio ostendat hæc non pugnare, quia dicuntur de manu Dei irati & de incidentibus in eâ per voluntarium peccatum sine pœnitentia: cum David resipiscens loquatur de manu Dei propitij.
units.tr: The answer is that these do not conflict, since the former is said of the hand of an angry God and of those who fall into it through wilful sin without repentance, whereas David, repentant, speaks of the hand of a God who is merciful.

units.la: III. Etiam misericordia Dei est cum liberamur à bello & fame.
units.tr: III. Even when we are delivered from war and famine, God's mercy is present.

units.la: Resp. Sed evidentior, cum liberamur à peste:
units.tr: Answer: yes, but it is more evident when we are delivered from the plague.

units.la: Ostendatur: quia bello, fame, simul ferendæ iniuriæ, contumeliæ hominum: Peste solius Dei ira, & eius aversio est solius misericordiæ Dei opus, cum bellum, fames, hominum opera sæpe avertantur.
units.tr: This is shown: because with war and famine one must also bear the injuries and insults of men; but with the plague, God's anger alone is present, and its turning away is the work of God's mercy alone, since war and famine are often averted by human means.

units.la: Argumentum III. à tempore: quia pestis minus diu erat duratura, quam bellum, fames. Omnia autem brevia tolerabilia esse dicunt, etiamsi magna sint. Cic. in Læl.
units.tr: Argument III, from time: the plague was going to last a shorter time than war and famine. Now, they say that all short things are bearable, however great they may be. Cicero, in Laelius.

units.la: Argumentum IV. à connexis: Bellum & fames plerunque secum trahunt pestem: Hæc sine illis esse potest.
units.tr: Argument IV, from connected things: war and famine for the most part bring the plague with them; the plague can exist without them.

units.la: Argumentum V. Plaga pestis fuit congrua peccato Davidis, juxta legem, qua in censu dandus præcipitur semisiclus, ne fieret plaga in po-pulo.
units.tr: Argument V. The stroke of the plague was fitting to David's sin, according to the law by which a half-shekel was commanded to be given at the census, so that no plague would fall upon the people.

units.la: Argumentum VI. In electione habenda fuit ratio gloriæ Dei: eligenda plaga qua minime hæc læderetur. alis[?] autem pestis: quia bellum & fames coniuncta erant cum opprobrio Dei & ecclesiæ, quod ostendatur.
units.tr: Argument VI. In making the choice, account had to be taken of the glory of God: the plague, by which this glory would be least harmed, was to be chosen. Now the plague alone does this, because war and famine were joined with the reproach of God and of the Church, which is to be shown.

units.la: Argumentum VII. David ipse propter peccatum debuit subesse periculo. Ergo recte pestem elegit: quia bello & fame tantum subditi luissent, quod ipsum quoque ostendatur.
units.tr: Argument VII. David himself, because of his sin, ought to be exposed to danger. Therefore he rightly chose the plague, because the subjects alone would have suffered for war and famine; this too is to be shown.

units.la: Amplificetur à charitate quam testificatur in subditos non modo electione pestis, sed etiam in tercessione[?]: Oues autem ista quid peccarunt?
units.tr: It is amplified from the charity which he showed toward his subjects, not only in choosing the plague, but also in his intercession: "But these sheep, what have they done?"

units.la: Conclusio sit applicatio exempli ad nos: Cum & nos peccatis nostris inciderimus in hanc Dei manum: eam æquius quam hominū manus feramus: & miserationes Dei multas imploremus.
units.tr: The conclusion is the application of the example to us: since we too, by our sins, have fallen into this hand of God, we should bear it more equitably than the hands of men, and implore God's many mercies.

units.la: Exercitatio XLVI.
units.tr: Exercitatio XLVI.

units.la: Paraphrasis exegetica historiæ de pestis cohibi-tione & aversione 1.Par.21. 2.Sam.24.
units.tr: Exegetical paraphrase of the history of the restraining and averting of the plague, 1 Chron. 21, 2 Sam. 24.

units.la: NArrationis sint duæ partes. 1. Inflictio pe-stis populo à Deo per angelum: numerus cæsorum: miseratio Dei & cohibitio angeli, ne perdat Hierosolymam.
units.tr: The narrative has two parts. 1. The infliction of the plague on the people by God through an angel; the number of those slain; the mercy of God and the restraint of the angel, lest he destroy Jerusalem.

units.la: Hinc breviter deducantur hypotheses:
units.tr: From this, the following hypotheses may briefly be drawn:

units.la: 1. Quod pestis infligatur à Deo: Inde manus, gladius, sagittæ Dei, &c.
units.tr: 1. That the plague is inflicted by God. Hence the hand, the sword, the arrows of God, etc.

units.la: 2. Quod per causas fecundas angelos bonos, malos. Ostendatur hunc bonum fuisse, quia postea mittitur ad prophetam: & per naturales alias; astrorum positus, coniunctiones, meteora, ventos, eluviones, putredines, &c.
units.tr: 2. That it comes through secondary causes: good angels and bad. It is to be shown that this one was good, because he is afterwards sent to the prophet; and through natural causes: the positions of the stars, conjunctions, meteors, winds, floods, putrefactions, etc.

units.la: 3. Quod dirigatur manu Dei, ut non sæviat promiscuè, nec diutius quam Deus vult, &c.
units.tr: 3. That it is directed by the hand of God, so that it does not rage indiscriminately, nor longer than God wills, etc.

units.la: 4. Quod Deus non [illegible, ~10 letters], bonus, misericors in pœnis: nec modum excedat: solus etiam cohibere potest. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: 4. That God is not [illegible, about ten letters], good and merciful even in punishments, and does not exceed the measure; He alone can also restrain it. Therefore, etc.

units.la: 11. Quid David fecerit ad avertendam pestem: conspecto percussore consternatus cum senioribus precatur: agnoscit culpam: petit parci populo: jussus exstruit altare in area emta precio, & sacrificia offert.
units.tr: 11. What David did to avert the plague: having seen the destroying angel, he is dismayed and prays with the elders; he acknowledges his guilt, asks that the people be spared; commanded, he builds an altar on ground bought for a price, and offers sacrifices.

units.la: Per occupationem explicetur quæstio, Cur David author mali non fit mortuus: & an non populo innocenti iniuste irrogata plaga.
units.tr: The question is to be explained by way of digression: why David, the author of the evil, did not die, and whether the plague was not unjustly inflicted on the innocent people.

units.la: Postea deducatur hypothesis: quid peste faciendum ut avertatur.
units.tr: Next, the hypothesis is to be drawn: what must be done during a plague so that it may be averted.
