units.la: 1. Agnitio manus Dei: etsi non semper appareat angelus percussor: apparent aliæ causæ, alia signa iræ Dei.
units.tr: 1. Acknowledgement of the hand of God: although the angel who strikes is not always visible, other causes appear, other signs of the wrath of God.

units.la: 2. Agnitio culpæ nostræ, & justitiæ Dei.
units.tr: 2. Acknowledgement of our own guilt and of the justice of God.

units.la: 3. Preces & feria conversio ad Deum.
units.tr: 3. Prayers and a serious conversion to God.

units.la: 4. Exstructio altaris, quæ est fiducia Christi mediatoris: Hic enim altare nostrum. Hebr. 13.
units.tr: 4. The building of an altar, which is trust in Christ the mediator: for He is our altar. Heb. 13.

units.la: 5. Charitas & justitia erga proximum,
units.tr: 5. Charity and justice toward the neighbour.

units.la: 6. Sacrificia laudis. Claudatur applicatione exempli & doctrinæ ad nos: quando Deus etiam nunc videtur inhibere angelum percussorem, ut verè simus grati.
units.tr: 6. Sacrifices of praise. The passage is to be closed by applying the example and the doctrine to ourselves: since God even now seems to restrain the destroying angel, so that we may truly be thankful.

units.la: Exercitatio XLVII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XLVII.

units.la: An etiam pij [?] corripiantur & moriantur peste: ad amicum.
units.tr: Whether the godly too are chastised and die of the plague: to a friend.

units.la: EXordium, [illegible, ~6 letters] mihi visa quæstio tua. Ratio : quia nemo dubitat de communi experientia, & argumenta contraria parum videntur firma.
units.tr: The beginning [illegible, ~6 letters] your question seemed to me worth considering. The reason: because no one doubts the common experience, and the arguments to the contrary seem rather weak.

units.la: Propositio : Pii æque ac impii pesti sunt obnoxii.
units.tr: Proposition: The godly, no less than the ungodly, are liable to the plague.

units.la: Ratio 1. à genere, utrique communia habet omnia carnis commoda & incommoda: quod probetur à communibus causis bonorum & malorum externorum: ut sunt: aëris temperies, caro, cibus, potus, valetudo, peccatum, &c.
units.tr: Reason 1, from the genus: both have in common all the advantages and disadvantages of the flesh. This is proved from the common causes of good and evil external things, such as the temperature of the air, meat, food, drink, health, sin, etc.

units.la: Illustretur exemplis & similibus bonis & malis: communis lux, tenebræ, serenitas, pluviæ, obsidio in civitate: naufragium in mari Testimonio Ecclesiastæ cap.2.14.&8.14.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated by examples and similar goods and evils: common light and darkness, calm and rain, a siege in a city, shipwreck at sea, by the testimony of Ecclesiastes, chapters 2.14 and 8.14.

units.la: Item testimonio Cypriani contra Demetr. Intra unam domum boni & mali interim continemur. Quicquid intra domum evenerit, pari fortuna perpetimur, donec ævi temporalis fine completo ad æternam vel mortis vel mortalitatis hospitia dividamur.
units.tr: Likewise by the testimony of Cyprian against Demetrianus: "Within one house the good and the evil are meanwhile held together. Whatever happens within the house, we suffer with equal fortune, until at the end of temporal life we are divided into the eternal dwellings either of death or of mortality."

units.la: Et de mortalit. Omnium valetudo membrorum cum cæteris communis est nobis quamdiu portatur in sæculo caro ista communis, &c. Amplific. quod pii plerunq; magis infesten-tur malis quam alii: quia magis à Satana oppu-gnantur: & à Deo exercentur, ne cum mundo pereant.
units.tr: And in his treatise On Mortality: "The health of all our members is held in common with the rest, as long as this common flesh is carried in the world, etc." Amplification: the godly are often more troubled by evils than others, because they are assailed more by Satan and are exercised by God, lest they perish with the world.

units.la: Applicetur ad pestem tanquam malorum spe-ciem.
units.tr: Let it be applied to the plague as a species of evils.

units.la: Ratio II. à minori: Sunt obnoxii gravioribus malis bello & fami, quæ probentur esse graviora pestę ex electione Davidis.
units.tr: Reason 2, from the lesser: they are liable to graver evils, war and famine, which are proved to be worse than the plague from David's choice.

units.la: Ratio III. Multi sine dubio fuerunt pii inter 70000.pestę exstinctos 2.Sam.24. Probetur. Oves istæ quid fecerunt?
units.tr: Reason 3: Without doubt many godly people were among the 70,000 killed by the plague, 2 Samuel 24. Let it be proved: "What had these sheep done?"

units.la: Ratio IV. Ab exemplo Hizkiæ pestę lethaliter correpti: pietas eius probetur & morbus.
units.tr: Reason 4: From the example of Hezekiah, who was struck mortally by the plague: let his piety be proved, and his illness.

units.la: Ratio V. à testimonio experientiæ, quod multos quotidie videmus corripi & mori indubitatæ pietatis: (Nota: in his fuit reverendus, & clariss. vir Doctor Iacobus Kimedoncius: extinctus pestę 26.Novemb. An 96.)
units.tr: Reason 5: from the testimony of experience, since we see many daily seized and dying who are of undoubted piety. (Note: among these was the reverend and most distinguished man, Doctor Jacob Kimedoncius, who died of the plague on 26 November, in the year 1596.)

units.la: Obiectio I. Pestis est una ex maledictionibus impiorum Levit.26. Deut.28. Ezech.14,&c. At pii non sunt sub maledictione. Gal.3.13. Ergo.
units.tr: Objection 1: The plague is one of the curses of the ungodly, Leviticus 26, Deuteronomy 28, Ezekiel 14, etc. But the godly are not under the curse, Galatians 3:13. Therefore...

units.la: Resp. I. à compar. Etiam bellum, fames, mors, sunt ex maledictionibus impiorum: & tamen pii eis obnoxii.
units.tr: Answer 1, by comparison: war, famine and death also belong to the curses of the ungodly, and yet the godly are liable to them.

units.la: 2. ad minorem: Non sunt sub maledictione æterna: quia ab hac redemti sunt. Gal.3. Nec sub temporali quatenus maledictio: sed quatenus παιδεία vel δοκιμασία, ut sunt omnes afflictiones piorum.
units.tr: 2. As to the minor premise: they are not under the eternal curse, because they have been redeemed from it, Galatians 3. Nor are they under the temporal curse as such, but as chastisement (παιδεία) or testing (δοκιμασία), as all the afflictions of the godly are.

units.la: Confirmetur I. à thesi: Pios his minime exemtos sed maxime obnoxios. Probetur dictis Heb. 12. 6. Iac.1.2. 1.Pet.4.12.
units.tr: Let it be confirmed, first, from the thesis: the godly are by no means exempt from these, but are very much liable to them. Let it be proved from the sayings: Hebrews 12:6, James 1:2, 1 Peter 4:12.

units.la: Item ex causis impulsivis & finalibus: quia et-iam filii saepe peccant, opus habent & ipsi corre-ptione & exercitiis, ne segnescant, vel cum mun-do pereant.
units.tr: Likewise from the impelling and final causes: because even sons often sin, and they too need correction and exercises, lest they grow slack or perish with the world.

units.la: Hæ causæ singulæ paucis explicentur.
units.tr: Let each of these causes be explained briefly.

units.la: 2. ab alia thesi: Maledictiones piis convertun-tur in benedictiones misericordiæ Dei. Rom.8. Nulla condemnatio iis, &c. Item. Omnia in bo-num cooperantur diligentibus Deum. Hucapplicetur dictum. Gal.3.13. per [illegible, ~9 letters]
units.tr: 2. From another thesis: curses are turned for the godly into blessings of the mercy of God, Romans 8: "There is no condemnation for those who..." etc. Likewise: "All things work together for good for those who love God." Let the saying of Galatians 3:13 be applied here, through [illegible, ~9 letters].

units.la: Transferatur thesis ad hypothesin: Ergo & pestis piis non est pestis: Exponatur quanto discrimine pii & impii corripiantur.
units.tr: Let the thesis be transferred to the hypothesis: therefore the plague too is not a plague to the godly. Let it be set out with how great a difference the godly and the ungodly are seized.

units.la: Obiectio 11. quæ est instantia contra priorem thesin:
units.tr: Objection 2, which is an instance against the former thesis:

units.la: Peccata sunt piis remissa per Christum. Ergo propter ea non sunt obnoxii pesti.
units.tr: The sins of the godly are forgiven through Christ. Therefore on account of them they are not liable to the plague.

units.la: Resp. Sunt remissa quoad reatum æternum: non quoad castigationes temporales. Psal.89. Si deliquerint in virga visitab. iniquitates eorum: sed misericordiam meam, &c.
units.tr: Answer: They are forgiven as to eternal guilt, not as to temporal chastisements. Psalm 89: "If they break my statutes... then I will visit their transgressions with the rod, but my mercy I will not take away," etc.

units.la: Illustretur exemplis Mosis, Aaronis, Mariæ, Iobi, Davidis, Iosiae, &c. qui habentes remissionem peccatorum nihilominus morte, lepra, ulceribus fuerunt castigati. David peste. Ps.38.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated by the examples of Moses, Aaron, Miriam, Job, David, Josiah, etc., who, though they had the forgiveness of sins, were nonetheless chastised by death, leprosy and ulcers. David by the plague, Psalm 38.

units.la: Obiect. 111. Promissiones de piorum defensione à peste videntur repugnare huic sententiæ. Citentur & urgeantur præcipuè ex Ps.91. Adte malum non appropinquabit, &c.
units.tr: Objection 3: The promises concerning the defence of the godly from the plague seem to contradict this opinion. Let them be cited and pressed, chiefly from Psalm 91: "No evil shall come near you," etc.

units.la: Resp. per [illegible, ~8 letters]. Alii intelligunt totum Psalmum de solo Christo, alij de solo Davide, quasi ad hos[?] sit specialis promissio. Sed est promissio generalis de piorum tutela. Negetur vero antecedens, hoc est, ostendatur non repugnare. Ratio: quia est promissio limitata. Declaretur. 1. quod piis nihil adversi accidat temere sine Dei voluntate. Cadent a latere tuo mille, &c. Pilus de capite non cadet, &c. 2. quod adversa non sint mala piis sicut impiis: quia servantur Dei praesidio.
units.tr: Answer through [illegible, ~8 letters]. Some understand the whole Psalm of Christ alone, others of David alone, as if there were a special promise to these. But it is a general promise of the protection of the godly. Yet the antecedent is to be denied, that is, it is to be shown that it does not contradict. Reason: because it is a limited promise. Let it be explained: first, that nothing adverse befalls the godly by chance without the will of God: "A thousand shall fall at your side," etc.; "Not a hair of the head shall fall," etc. Second, that adversities are not evils to the godly as they are to the ungodly, because they are preserved by the protection of God.

units.la: Probetur utrunque ex textu: quod subsint adversis: Cum ipso sum in tribulatione: Invocabit me, &c. Et quod certò liberentur: Eripiam, glorificabo eum, &c.
units.tr: Let both be proved from the text: that they are subject to adversities: "I am with him in trouble," "He shall call upon me," etc.; and that they are certainly delivered: "I will deliver him, I will glorify him," etc.

units.la: Obiectio 1 v. Experientia fallax, habentur pro piis qui forte non sunt, &c.
units.tr: Objection 4: Experience is deceptive; people are taken to be godly who perhaps are not, etc.

units.la: Resp. 1. Exempla Scripturae allata non sunt fallacia.
units.tr: Answer 1: The examples of Scripture alleged are not deceptive.

units.la: 2. Charitas tamen iudicat & sperat, de quib. non habet contraria argumenta.
units.tr: 2. Charity nevertheless judges and hopes concerning those of whom it has no contrary arguments.

units.la: Conclusio: Cum & tu habearis pios, & te pestis periculo non exemtum sentias, tanto minus de hac quaestione dubitare debes.
units.tr: Conclusion: Since you too are held to be godly, and you feel that you are not exempt from the danger of the plague, you ought to doubt this question all the less.

units.la: Concludatur vero: ut & tu & omnes sub Dei praesidio tuti habitemus.
units.tr: Let it be concluded, indeed, that both you and all of us may dwell safe under the protection of God.

units.la: Exercitatio XLVIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio XLVIII.

units.la: An liceat pestem fugere. PARS NEGANS.
units.tr: Whether it is lawful to flee the plague. THE NEGATIVE PART.

units.la: Exordium sit gratiarum actio ad amicum pro explicata superiore quaestione: & petitio ut ad hanc etiam respondeat.
units.tr: Let the introduction be a thanksgiving to a friend for the earlier question having been explained, and a request that he respond to this one as well.

units.la: Ratio: quia hic scrupulus de peste tibi restet: utrum liceat fugere.
units.tr: Reason: because this scruple about the plague remains for you, namely whether it is lawful to flee.

units.la: Occupatio: Non debes mirari, quod huic argumento tamdiu insistam: cum luis periculum nondum hactenus abierit: & inter eruditos tam sint discrepantes sententiæ.
units.tr: Preoccupation: You should not be surprised that I dwell on this argument for so long, since the danger of the plague has not yet passed away, and the opinions of learned men are so divided.

units.la: Propositio: Videtur probabilius quod non liceat.
units.tr: Proposition: It seems more probable that it is not lawful.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia est degenerum liberorum fugere ferulam paternam, qualis est pestis.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because it is the mark of degenerate children to flee from a father's rod, and the plague is such a rod.

units.la: II. Quia est diffidentiæ, quasi non sit providentia, sed pestis temere grassetur: quod ostendatur non fieri, à certa moderatione divina ex Psal. 91. & pestis epithetis, quia est Dei manus, gladius, virga, sagitta, &c. Ostendatur ex Scripturis breviter.
units.tr: II. Because flight shows distrust, as if there were no providence, and as if the plague raged at random; which is shown not to be the case by the certain and measured government of God, from Psalm 91, and from the names given to the plague, since it is the hand of God, a sword, a rod, an arrow, etc. This is to be shown briefly from the Scriptures.

units.la: III. Quia fuga est scandalosa, & minuit fiduciam manentium. Ostendatur & amplif. ex dicto: Væ qui scandalum dat.
units.tr: III. Because flight is a scandal and diminishes the confidence of those who remain. This is to be shown and amplified from the saying: Woe to him who gives offence.

units.la: IV, Quia est desertio proximi in necessitate repugnans dilectioni, qua mutuo sumus obligati.
units.tr: IV. Because it is the abandonment of a neighbour in need, which is contrary to the love by which we are mutually bound.

units.la: Hæc ratio amplific. à natura charitatis, à ἀγγε-ωνία[?] sanctorum.
units.tr: This reason is amplified from the nature of charity, from the ... [?] of the saints.

units.la: V. Quia fuga est inutilis & inanis, cum nemo possit effugere manum & consilium Dei. Probetur & illustretur dictis Psal. 139. Quo ibo à facie tua, &c.
units.tr: V. Because flight is useless and vain, since no one can escape the hand and counsel of God. Let this be proved and illustrated by the words of Psalm 139: Whither shall I go from your face, etc.

units.la: Psal.56. Vanitate sperant se evasuros, &c.
units.tr: Psalm 56: They hope to escape by vanity, etc.

units.la: Item à termino vitæ omnibus fixo. Iob. 14.
units.tr: Likewise, from the end of life, which is fixed for all. Job 14.

units.la: Dies praefinti[?] sunt:
units.tr: The days are appointed:

units.la: Ecclef.3. Est tempus nascendi, moriendi, &c.
units.tr: Eccles. 3: There is a time to be born, and a time to die, etc.

units.la: VI. Ab exemplo Davidis non fugientis 2.Sa. 14: item Christianorum graßante lue manentium & officia gentilibus praestantium. Euseb.l.3. c.8. Videatur locus in hist. Ecclef.
units.tr: VI. From the example of David, who did not flee (2 Sam. 15 [14]); likewise from the Christians who remained during the raging plague and rendered services to the Gentiles. Eusebius, book 3, chapter 8. Let the passage in the Church history be consulted.

units.la: Conclusio: Cum pestis propter peccata infligatur, fuga peccatorum & resipiscentia potius quam secessione avertenda videtur: Et repetatur petitio.
units.tr: Conclusion: Since the plague is inflicted on account of sins, it seems that it is to be averted by flight from sin and by repentance rather than by withdrawal; and the request is to be repeated.

units.la: Exercitatio XLIX. De fuga pestis.
units.tr: Exercitatio XLIX. On the flight from the plague.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: RESPONSE.

units.la: EXordium ab αἰτιολογία[?], cur hactenus non re-sponderis: quia lue Dei gratia depulsa puta-veris sepeliendum hoc argumentum: & cur nunc respondeas: 1. quia ipse urgeat. 2. quia hesternum funus amici in fuga luis defuncti te huius commonefecerit.(D. Johannes Posthius Archiater Palatinus cum augusto Senatu luis causa secesserat Mosbacum: sed ibidem non peste sed podagra & catarrhis exstinctus, Heidelbergam reductus atque humatus fuit 26. Junii.97.)
units.tr: Introduction, from the reason (aitiologia?): why you have not answered until now: because, supposing the plague driven off by the grace of God, you thought this question should be buried; and why you now reply: (1) because it presses upon you; (2) because the funeral of a friend yesterday, who died while fleeing the plague, reminded you of it. (The Court physician Johann Posthius, with the august Senate, had withdrawn to Mosbach because of the plague; but there, not by the plague but by gout and catarrh, he died, and he was brought back to Heidelberg and buried on 26 June 1597.)

units.la: Transitio: Te igitur paucis expositurum tuam de fuga pestis sententiam salvo meliore aliorum judicio.
units.tr: Transition: Therefore, with a few words, I will set out your opinion on fleeing the plague, saving the better judgment of others.

units.la: Partitio: Fugere pestem res est per semedia[?]: ex circumstantiis seu accidenti fit aliis illicita, a-liis licita: Sed nullis admodum expedions.
units.tr: Division: To flee the plague is a thing of the middle kind (per semedia?): by its circumstances or accidents it is made unlawful for some and lawful for others, but expedient for almost none.

units.la: Subiiciatur ἔκθεσις[?] per partes.
units.tr: Let the exposition (ekthesis?) be set out part by part.

units.la: Propositio 1. Est indifferens.
units.tr: Proposition 1. It is indifferent.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia nec praeceptum nec prohibitum Dei verbo.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because it is neither commanded nor forbidden in the Word of God.

units.la: 2. Quia potest recte & non recte fieri: Sicut verbi causa fugere hostem licet gregariis acie disjecta vel duce jubente: non licet ducibus: neque etiam gregariis quo ad stant signa, &c.
units.tr: 2. Because it can be done rightly and not rightly. For example, it is lawful for common soldiers to flee from an enemy when the line has been scattered, or when a commander orders it; it is not lawful for commanders, nor for common soldiers so long as the standards stand, etc.

units.la: Haec ratio illustretur & confirmetur duabus propositionibus sequentibus.
units.tr: This reason is illustrated and confirmed by the two following propositions.

units.la: Propositio 11. Non licet fugere iis, qui officiis publicis etiam pestis tempore necessariis loco sunt alligati: ut magistratus loci, ministri Ecclesiae, medici, &c. sine publico consensu, quo laxatur obligatio.
units.tr: Proposition 2. It is not lawful for those who are bound to place by public offices, which are necessary even in time of plague, such as the magistrates of a place, the ministers of the Church, physicians, etc., to flee without public consent, by which the obligation is relaxed.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia hi vocatione ad manendum obligantur. Fugientes ergo deserunt vocationem, & laedunt conscientias, Mercenarius fugit, &c. Quilibet manet[?] in vocatione sua, &c.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because these are bound to remain by their calling. Those who flee, therefore, desert their calling and wound their consciences: "The hireling flees," etc. Each one remains in his calling, etc.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia hi violant charitatem proximo debitam & necessariam. Contra illud: A carne tua ne subducas te. Dilliges[?] proximum tuum, &c.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because these violate the charity owed and necessary to their neighbour: against that saying, "Do not hide yourself from your own flesh," and "You shall love your neighbour," etc.

units.la: Amplificetur ab incommodis connexis & consequentibus quod destituant aegros ope, consilio, consolatione: egenos eleemosyna: sint causae [illegible, ~6 letters] & mortis multorum.
units.tr: Amplify from the connected and consequent inconveniences: that they abandon the sick in help, counsel and comfort, and the poor in alms; they become causes [illegible, about six letters] and the death of many.

units.la: Obiect. Possunt ista per alios substitutos curari.
units.tr: Objection. These things can be attended to by other substitutes.

units.la: Resp. 1. Minus recte: quia alii plerunque aut non aeque fideles aut minus idonei.
units.tr: Answer. 1. Less rightly, because others are usually either not equally faithful or less fit.

units.la: 2. Quisque tenetur sua vocatione 1. Cor. 9. Necessitas mihi incumbit.
units.tr: 2. Each is bound by his calling: 1 Cor. 9. "Necessity is laid upon me."

units.la: Ratio 3. ab aliis adiunctis: quia horum fuga non potest carere scandalo & offensione manentium, quorum labefactat fiduciam, auget terrorem, parit justas querelas de desertione, derogat authoritati & vocationi fugientium.
units.tr: Reason 3. From other circumstances: because the flight of these men cannot be free from scandal and offence to those who remain, whose confidence it weakens, whose terror it increases, from which it arises that there are just complaints of desertion, and it detracts from the authority and calling of those who flee.

units.la: Clausula: De his igitur te sententiæ & rationibus amici accedere.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore you agree with your friend's opinion and reasons on this point.

units.la: Propositio III. Licet secedere, urgente periculo,
units.tr: Proposition 3. It is permitted to withdraw, when danger presses,

units.la: 1. Magistratui non alligato ad locum: ut sunt superiores, Princeps, curia augusta:
units.tr: 1. For a magistrate not bound to a place, such as superiors, the Prince, the august court;

units.la: Ratio: quia hi foris æque possunt præesse: ut nec vocatio eorum nec charitas periclitetur: cum domi officium faciant delegati.
units.tr: Reason: because these can equally preside abroad, so that neither their calling nor their charity is endangered, since at home the duties are performed by deputies.

units.la: 2. Officiariis loco alligatis, politicis vel ecclesiasticis, accedente ob certas causas & certis conditionibus Reip. vel Ecclesiæ consensu.
units.tr: 2. For officials bound to a place, whether civil or ecclesiastical, when the consent of the Commonwealth or the Church is given, for certain causes and under certain conditions.

units.la: Ratio: quia tali consensu eis laxatur obligatio, & sic secessio potest fieri absque scandalo & desertione vocationis vel charitatis.
units.tr: Reason: because by such consent their obligation is relaxed, and so withdrawal can take place without scandal and without desertion of calling or charity.

units.la: 3. Privatis, maxime iis, quorum mansio habet plus periculi aut jacturæ, minus necessitatis vel commodi: ut sunt valde meticulosi, gravidæ, juventus præsertim scholastica, &c.
units.tr: 3. For private persons, especially those whose staying carries more danger or loss and less necessity or advantage: such as the very timid, pregnant women, and youth, especially scholars, etc.

units.la: Subjiciantur rationes:
units.tr: Let the reasons be added:

units.la: 1. ab æquo & bono: Suam & suorum vitam tueri absque alterius detrimento est licitum.
units.tr: 1. From the fair and good: It is lawful to protect one's own life and that of one's family without harm to another.

units.la: Addatur minor & ostendatur secessionem horum fieri sine læsione aliorum, non minus quam peregrinantium.
units.tr: Add the minor premise and show that the withdrawal of these people takes place without injury to others, no less than that of travellers.

units.la: 2. A simili: licet fugere insidias, bellum, famem, incendia, eluviones, &c. Ergo etiam contagium. Antecedens illustretur exemplis patriarcharū. Abrahami, Isaaci, Iacobi, Ruth, Sunamitidis, Davidis, Christi, apostolorum.
units.tr: 2. From a like case: It is lawful to flee ambushes, war, famine, fires, floods, etc. Therefore also contagion. The antecedent is illustrated by examples from the patriarchs: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Ruth, the Shunammite, David, Christ, the apostles.

units.la: 3. à pari: Contagium lepræ licet vitare separatione leprosorum. Lev.13. Ergo & contagium pestis mutatione loci infecti. Item: morbos à Deo immissos licet medicamentis pellere. Ergo etiam pestem fugere.
units.tr: 3. From a parity: It is lawful to avoid the contagion of leprosy by separation from lepers (Lev. 13). Therefore also the contagion of plague by changing the place that is infected. Likewise: it is lawful to drive away diseases sent by God with medicines. Therefore also to flee the plague.

units.la: 4. ab utili: Secessione horum consulitur manentib. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: 4. From the useful: By the withdrawal of these people, provision is made for those who remain. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Probatur antecedens, quia imminuta multitudine hominum minuitur periculum.
units.tr: The antecedent is proved, because when the number of people is diminished, the danger is diminished.

units.la: Amplif. simili: incendium minuitur vel crescit paucitate vel copia materiæ, Sic morbi epidemii frequentia vel paucitate hominum, &c.
units.tr: Amplify by a like case: a fire is diminished or grows according to the scarcity or abundance of its fuel; so with epidemic diseases, according to the frequency or scarcity of people, etc.

units.la: Clausula: His igitur licet fugere: Sic tamen, ut 1. fugiant peccata. 2. non fugiant à Deo: sed huic se committant.
units.tr: Conclusion: To these, therefore, it is lawful to flee; yet in such a way that 1. they flee from sins; 2. they do not flee from God, but commit themselves to him.

units.la: Transitio à thesi de indifferentibus: Omnia li-cent: sed non omnia conducunt.
units.tr: Transition from the thesis on indifferent things: All things are lawful, but not all things are expedient.

units.la: Illustretur hypothesi Corinthiorum, quibus licebat vesci idolothytis, sed non conducebat propter scandala. 1.Cor.6.& 8.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated by the case of the Corinthians, to whom it was lawful to eat meats offered to idols, but it was not expedient because of scandals (1 Cor. 6 and 8).

units.la: Subjiciatur alia hypothesis de fuga, quæ fit
units.tr: Let another hypothesis about flight be added, which is made

units.la: Propositio I v. Licet quidem aliquibus pestem fugere, sed nullis admodum expedit.
units.tr: Proposition 4. Although it is lawful for some to flee the plague, yet it is expedient for almost none.

units.la: Ratio: quia fugientes variis incommodis se implicant, quod facere sane non expedit.
units.tr: Reason: because those who flee entangle themselves in various inconveniences, which surely it is not expedient to do.

units.la: Probatio minoris sit ἐξ ἕξεως[?] præcipuorum in-commodorum, quibus vel per se vel per accidens fugientes implicantur.
units.tr: Proof of the minor premise is from the state (ex hexeos?) of the chief inconveniences in which those who flee are entangled, either directly or by accident.

units.la: 1. Subducunt se exercitiis efficacioribus pœ-nitentiæ, ñitentiæ[?], invocationis, pietatis, fiduciæ, & timoris Dei, patientiæ, fortitudinis & charitatis, &c. ad quæ manentes quotidianis exemplis & concionibus magno suo bono excitantur.
units.tr: 1. They withdraw from the more effective exercises of repentance, invocation, piety, trust, and the fear of God, patience, fortitude and charity, etc., by which those who remain are stirred up, to their great good, by daily examples and sermons.

units.la: Obiectio: Etiam foris his potest vacari. Resp. Sed multò remissius quam domi.
units.tr: Objection: These exercises can be pursued abroad too. Answer: But much more slackly than at home.

units.la: Ratio: quia domi obiecta magis movent sensus: vexatio dat intellectum, &c.
units.tr: Reason: because at home objects move the senses more; affliction gives understanding, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur à fine, quod Deus ideo immit-tat luem, &c.
units.tr: Amplify from the end, that God therefore sends the plague, etc.

units.la: II. Turbantur & vexantur perpetuo metu ac diffidentia.
units.tr: II. They are troubled and vexed by perpetual fear and distrust.

units.la: Probetur, quia trepide abeunt (metus enim causa fugæ) trepide foris agunt (metu à se arcent quosvis etiam suos domo venientes, solicite rimas obstruunt contagio, rumoribus domesticis percelluntur) trepide redeunt (omnia suspecta habent) ideo magis periclitantur. Ista amplificen-tur à causis & experientia.
units.tr: Let it be proved, because they leave in alarm (for fear is the cause of flight), act in alarm abroad (through fear they keep off from themselves all who come from home, even their own people; they anxiously stop up the chinks against contagion; they are struck with terror by domestic rumours), and return in alarm (they regard everything as suspect); therefore they are in greater danger. These things are amplified from causes and experience.

units.la: Obiectio: Etiam manentes metuunt. Resp. 1. Sed minus & minori diffidentia. Ratio petatur ex Roman.5.3. Oppressio facit patientiam.
units.tr: Objection: Those who remain also fear. Answer: 1. But less, and with less distrust. Reason is taken from Romans 5:3: "Affliction produces patience."

units.la: III. Foris plerunque incommode & majori sumtu habitant: aliis sunt oneri vel terrori: correpti morbo sæpe destituuntur necessariis, medicis, pharmacis, amicis, consiliis, ministeriis suorū, quibus domi frui poterant.
units.tr: III. Abroad they usually live inconveniently and at greater expense; they are a burden or terror to others; when seized by the disease, they are often deprived of necessities, of physicians, medicines, friends, counsel, and the ministry of their own people, which they could enjoy at home.

units.la: Obiectio: Sed servant vitam. Resp. 1. Nono-mnes, quia aliqui fugiendo mutant locum peri-culi non periculum: effugiunt pestem non mor-tem: quod docuerunt jam aliquot exempla.
units.tr: Objection: But they preserve their life. Answer: 1. Not always, because some by fleeing change the place of danger, not the danger itself: they escape the plague, not death; as several examples have already taught.

units.la: 2. Etiam manentes servantur, quam diu Deus vult: Amplific. ex dictis Domini est terra: Capilli nostri sunt numerati. Ad te non accedet malum.
units.tr: 2. Those who remain are also preserved, as long as God wills: amplify from the words "The earth is the Lord's" and "The hairs of your head are all numbered," and "No evil shall come near you."

units.la: (Clausula[?]: Praestat igitur non fugere etiam quibus licet, & se Deo committere.
units.tr: (Conclusion: It is better, therefore, not to flee, even where it is lawful, and to commit oneself to God.

units.la: Ad argumenta partis negantis de fuga pestis.
units.tr: Against the arguments of the party denying flight from plague.

units.la: RESPONSIO.
units.tr: REPLY.

units.la: Transfeatur à dictis ad sententiam & argumentum amici: & primo approbentur secundum qd: quod aliquibus non liceat: ut facit propositione secunda: Non autem simpliciter, quod nullis.
units.tr: Let us turn from the statements to the opinion and argument of our friend. First, let us approve the qualified claim: that flight is not lawful for some people. He makes this claim in his second proposition: not, however, that it is unlawful for absolutely no one.

units.la: Deinde respondeatur ad singula.
units.tr: Next, let us reply to each point.

units.la: Ad 1. Resp. distinctione majoris: Degeneres sunt qui fugiunt patris ferulam. 1. qua ipsi petuntur. 11. Si contra voluntatem patris fugiat. At fugientes pestem citra vocationis desertionem non fugiunt contra vol. Dei.
units.tr: To the first: I reply by distinguishing the major premise. Those who flee their father's rod are degenerate: (1) if they are called back by it; (2) if they flee against their father's will. But those who flee the plague without deserting their calling do not flee against the will of God.

units.la: Ratio: quia Deus permittit periculum vitare, cum honeste possumus: Imo praecipit: Non occides.
units.tr: The reason: because God permits us to avoid danger whenever we can do so honourably; indeed he commands it: "You shall not kill."

units.la: Amplif. à contrario: Degeneres sunt qui ferulam patris non caventaut contemnunt.
units.tr: By way of amplification, from the contrary: those are degenerate who do not heed or who despise their father's rod.

units.la: Ad 11. Resp. Fallacia accidentis. Diffidentia accedit hominum vitio. Pii fugiunt, ut Deo obtemperent, periculum legitime vitando. Ergo nec Deo diffidunt, nec fugae confidunt.
units.tr: To the second: a fallacy of accident. Distrust comes from human vice. The godly flee so that they may obey God, by lawfully avoiding danger. Therefore they neither distrust God nor place their confidence in flight.

units.la: Ad III. Resp. Scandalum ex fuga licita non est datum sed acceptum.
units.tr: To the third: scandal does not arise from lawful flight; it is taken, not given.

units.la: Ad IV. Respon. Non est desertio. 1. quia satis est infectis adesse aliquos vel proximos vel à proximis aut à magistratu constitutos. 2. Dilectio est mutua. Ergo infecti, dummodo ab aliquibus curentur, non debent cupere multos secum periclitari.
units.tr: To the fourth: there is no desertion. (1) For it is enough that some are present to those infected, either neighbours or those appointed by neighbours or by the magistrate. (2) Love is mutual. Therefore the infected, provided that they are cared for by some, ought not to desire that many should be endangered along with them.

units.la: Ad V. Resp. 1. Per concessionem, quod fugere sit inutile. 2. Negatione consequentiæ: quia non sequitur ideo illicitum omnib.
units.tr: To the fifth: I reply (1) by granting that flight is useless; (2) by denying the consequence, for it does not follow that flight is therefore unlawful for everyone.

units.la: Ad dicta de providentia & consilio Dei: Resp. Providentia non tantum est finis sed & mediorū. Non igitur usum istorum tollit.
units.tr: As to what is said about the providence and counsel of God: I reply that providence is not only the end but also the means. Therefore it does not abolish the use of these means.

units.la: Ad VI. David non fugit. 1. quia non voluit, sciens sua culpa pestem attractam, nec diu, nec in se grassaturam. 2. nec potuit: quia erat subitanea & in toto regno.
units.tr: To the sixth: David did not flee. (1) Because he was unwilling to, knowing that the plague had been drawn down by his own fault, and that it would not rage for long nor against him in particular. (2) Nor was he able to, because it was sudden and throughout the whole kingdom.

units.la: Christiani apud Euseb.l.9.c.8. manserunt voluntate non lege.
units.tr: The Christians in Eusebius (book 9, chapter 8) remained by their will, not by law.

units.la: Conclusio sit declaratio studii tui, quod volueris amico gratificari: & approbatio judicii ejus: resipiscentia potius quam fuga pestem declinandam: cum limitatione sententiæ, modo fugam non in omnibus damnandam esse tencat[?].
units.tr: The conclusion is a statement of your zeal, that you were willing to oblige your friend, and an approval of his judgement: that repentance rather than flight should be used to avert the plague, with the qualification that flight is not to be condemned in every case.

units.la: Exercitatio L.
units.tr: Exercise L.

units.la: ΧΑΡΙΣΤΗΡΙΟΝ.
units.tr: ΧΑΡΙΣΤΗΡΙΟΝ [Charistērion].

units.la: Pro defensione collegii nostri a peste. Scribatur oratione metrica.
units.tr: In defence of our college against the plague. It is to be written in metrical form.

units.la: DEploretur miseranda vastitas, quam pestis fecit in Palatinatu, quem incolis nudavit: & in urbe, quam civibus spoliavit, & in Academia quam professoribus orbavit, studiosis etiam partim sublatis partim dissipatis: & in ipsa Ecclesia, quam pastoribus privavit.
units.tr: Let the miserable devastation be lamented which the plague has wrought in the Palatinate, which it stripped of its inhabitants; in the city, which it despoiled of its citizens; in the Academy, which it bereft of its professors, while the students were partly carried off and partly scattered; and in the Church itself, which it deprived of its ministers.

units.la: Addatur causa efficiens peccata nostra, quibus tantam pœnam attraximus.
units.tr: Let the efficient cause be added: our sins, by which we have drawn upon ourselves so great a punishment.

units.la: II. Subjiciatur gratiarū actio, quod inter tot funera Deus tam clementer nobis pepercit: & collegium integrum servavit.
units.tr: II. Let thanksgiving follow, that God has spared us so mercifully amid so many deaths, and has preserved the whole college.

units.la: Hoc beneficium ingens agnoscatur & celebretur tanquam admirandum.
units.tr: This great benefit is to be acknowledged and celebrated as something wonderful.

units.la: Amplificetur a causis: formali: quod ne unus quidem est periclitatus, quodque prophylacticis clementer benedixerit: Et ab efficientib. 1. non veris. quasi fortuito factum; aut quasi aliis fuerimus meliores. 2. Veris: misericordia Dei, preces piorū pro hoc collegio pietatis & literarum seminario, quas Deus exaudivit. Et a finalib. Vt essent semina aliqua instaurandæ Academiæ & scholis: & ut possemus nos præparare ad serviendum ipsi in Ecclesiis & Scholis, quæ passim orbatæ suis pastoribus & præceptoribus jacent desertæ.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from its causes. The formal cause: that not even one of us was endangered, and that He graciously blessed us with preventive measures. The efficient causes: first, the non-true ones, as if it happened by chance, or as if we were better than others; second, the true ones: the mercy of God, and the prayers of the godly for this college, a seminary of piety and learning, which God heard. And from the final causes: that there might be some seeds for restoring the Academy and the schools, and that we might prepare ourselves to serve Him in the Churches and schools, which, bereft of their ministers and teachers everywhere, lie deserted.

units.la: Repetatur gratiarum actio & addatur votum, ut porro Deus nos servet, ex hoc carcere quo pene biennium clausi simus, liberet: Academiam instauinstauret: studiosam juventutem recolligat: Serenissimum Electorem & Senatum Augustum in pace reducat: Studiis denique nostris benedicat, ad laudem gloriosi sui nominis, & Ecclesiæ salutem. Amen.
units.tr: Let thanksgiving be repeated, and let a prayer be added, that God would further keep us and deliver us from this prison in which we have been shut up for nearly two years; that He would restore the Academy, gather together the studious youth, bring the most serene Elector and the august Senate back to peace, and finally bless our studies, to the praise of His glorious name and the salvation of the Church. Amen.

units.la: Exercitatio LI.
units.tr: Exercitatio LI.

units.la: Collatio Gnomarum sacrarum & gentilium.
units.tr: Comparison of sacred and gentile maxims.

units.la: GNomas Isocratis, Theognidis & aliorum γνωμολόγων Ethnicorum magnam habere jucunditatem & utilitatem, constat.
units.tr: It is clear that the maxims of Isocrates, Theognis and the other Gentile gnomic writers (γνωμολόγων) have great pleasantness and usefulness.

units.la: Αἰτιολογία ex definitione: item ex vario argumento seu distinctione in Theologicas, politicas, ethicas, œconomicas, &c.
units.tr: The reasoning from definition (αἰτιολογία); likewise from the different subject matter, or the division into theological, political, ethical, economic, etc.

units.la: Ἀπορία, Videntur sacris gnomis Solomonis, Siracidæ, &c. æquandæ [?], imo hæ esse supervacuæ, quib. non sit opus.
units.tr: Objection (ἀπορία): the sacred maxims of Solomon, of Sirach, etc., seem to be on a par (?) with these; indeed these are superfluous, since they are not needed.

units.la: Propositio per adversa: Sed ingens est discrimen istarum & illarum.
units.tr: Proposition by contrast: But the difference between those and these is enormous.

units.la: Confirmatio ostendat discrimina, quæ petantur ex causis:
units.tr: Confirmation: let the differences be shown, which are to be sought from their causes:

units.la: I. Ethnicæ tantum sunt sententiæ rationis, & natura notæ: Sacræ sunt sententiæ Spiritus Dei: & plerèque natura ignotæ: Vt: Initium Sapientiæ timor Iehovæ: Quærite primum regnum Dei, &c.
units.tr: I. The Gentile sayings are only sentences of reason, and known by nature; the sacred sayings are sentences of the Spirit of God, and for the most part unknown by nature. For example: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Jehovah; Seek first the kingdom of God, etc.

units.la: II. Ethnicæ tantum sunt præcepta de officiis secundæ tabulæ: Sacræ eadem tradunt melius: & simul de præcipuis virtutib. primæ tabulæ: de vera Dei agnitione, invocatione, fide, spe, dilectione Dei, patientia, consolatione in cruce, &c. ut Initium sapientiæ, &c. Hæc est vita æterna, &c.
units.tr: II. The Gentile writers give only precepts about the duties of the second table; the sacred writings deliver the same more fully, and at the same time the chief virtues of the first table: the true knowledge of God, invocation, faith, hope, love of God, patience, consolation in the cross, etc., as in The beginning of wisdom, etc., and This is eternal life, etc.

units.la: Obiectio: Etiam Ethnicæ multæ sunt de Deo, & ejus cultu: ut πέων τιν ϑεὸν τιμᾶν, &c.
units.tr: Objection: The Gentiles also have many sayings about God and his worship, such as πέων τιν ϑεὸν τιμᾶν [honour the god], etc.

units.la: Resp. 1. Sed sine luce verbi, extra quod non est salutaris Dei patefactio & agnitio, &c.
units.tr: Answer. 1. But they lack the light of the Word, outside which there is no saving revelation and knowledge of God, etc.

units.la: 2. Admiscent multa falsa: tetros defendunt errores de πλάνῃ, de Dei essentia, voluntate & cultu. Vere igitur non sunt Theologicæ.
units.tr: 2. They mix in many falsehoods: they defend foul errors about error (πλάνῃ), about the essence, will and worship of God. Truly, therefore, they are not theological.

units.la: 3. Sacræ præclaras habent doctrinas de Christo & ejus beneficiis, remissione peccatorum, justitia & vita æterna: Ut Christus finis legis: Sic Deus dilexit mundum: Qui audit sermonem meum, &c. Ethnicæ de Evangelio nihil habent.
units.tr: 3. The sacred writings have excellent doctrines about Christ and his benefits, the forgiveness of sins, righteousness and eternal life: as Christ is the end of the law; God so loved the world; He who hears my word, etc. The Gentiles have nothing about the Gospel.

units.la: 4. Sacræ præcipiunt de vera pietate, & mundicie cordis: de integra legis obedientia interna & externa: & de fide huic placente, ut placeat Deo. Ethnicæ tantum de externa disciplina, & honestate civili inter homines: quædam etiam fœdæ, obscœnæ, honestati & charitati adversæ.
units.tr: 4. The sacred writings teach true piety and purity of heart, the entire inner and outer obedience to the law, and the faith that pleases God, so that he may be pleased. The Gentiles teach only outward discipline and civil decency among men; some of their teaching is even foul, obscene, and opposed to decency and charity.

units.la: 5. Ethnicæ monstrant finem gloriam & utilitatem propriam, aut saltem evitationem malorum hujus vitæ. Sacræ gloriam Dei & præmia æterna. Luceat lux vestra, &c. Qui credit in filium Dei, &c.
units.tr: 5. The Gentiles point to their own glory and advantage as the end, or at least to avoiding the evils of this life. The sacred writings point to the glory of God and eternal rewards: Let your light shine, etc.; He who believes in the Son of God, etc.

units.la: Conclusio: Sacræ igitur gnomologiæ Ethnicis longè anteferendæ & magis discendæ sunt.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore the sacred collections of maxims are to be placed far above the Gentile ones and are to be learned more eagerly.

units.la: Exercitatio LII.
units.tr: Exercise LII.

units.la: Encomium Dilectionis ex 1 Cor. 13.
units.tr: Encomium of Love, from 1 Cor. 13.

units.la: Exordium petatur ex thesi Apostoli, Dona potiora potius ambienda. Hypothesis sit propositio: Dilectio donum præstantissimum.
units.tr: The introduction may be taken from the thesis of the Apostle, that the greater gifts are rather to be sought after. The hypothesis is the proposition: love is the most excellent gift.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia sine eo nihil sunt alia, linguæ, prophetiæ, fides, &c.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because without it, the other things, tongues, prophecy, faith, etc., are nothing.

units.la: Ratio II. ab effectis: est multarum virtutum mater.
units.tr: Reason II, from its effects: it is the mother of many virtues.

units.la: Probatur enumeratione.
units.tr: This is proved by enumeration.

units.la: 1. Efficit Patientiam: hæc describatur paucis, quod sit 1. propter nullam aut levem causam non irasci. 2. propter gravem non nimium. 3. nō persona: sed vitio: 1 ext. μακροθυμέω. Item: οὐκ ἀγρη-μονεῖ[?]. Item παντὸς [?]ζητεῖ, ἐπιζητεῖ, &c. Declaratio. quod effectus sequatur. 1. Quem diligis ei nihil mali facis. Ergo nec irascéris. 2. ab ἀνλήτω[?] impatientiæ. 3. ab exemplo Christi.
units.tr: 1. It produces patience. This may be described briefly: (1) because one is not angry at all, or only slightly, for no cause or a slight one; (2) because one is not excessively angry at a serious cause; (3) not with the person, but with the vice. Cf. the Greek verb makrothymeō (to be long-suffering). Likewise: "it does not act unseemly" [?]. Likewise "it seeks all things, seeks after," etc. Explanation: that the effect follows. (1) Whom you love, you do no evil to; therefore you will not be angry either. (2) From the impatience of [?]. (3) From the example of Christ.

units.la: 2. Comitatem. 1. facilem ad congressum, collocutionem: χρηστεύεται[?].
units.tr: 2. Kindness. (1) Being easy to approach for company and conversation: "it is kind" [?].

units.la: 3. Modestiam servantem convenientiam, nec efferentem se supra alios: ἀ ζηλοῖ[?], ἀ περιπερ-ευ[?], ἀ φυσῆ[?].
units.tr: 3. Modesty, keeping due proportion and not exalting oneself above others: "it does not envy" [?], "it does not boast" [?], "it is not puffed up" [?].

units.la: 4. Liberalitatem largientem secundum rectam rationem. Non quærit sua.
units.tr: 4. Liberality, giving generously according to right reason. "It does not seek its own."

units.la: 5. Candorem & simplicitatem recte dicta & facta interpretantem, & alienam a suspicacitate temeraria. Prob. omnia credit.
units.tr: 5. Candour and simplicity, interpreting rightly said and done things, and far from rash suspicion. "It believes all things."

units.la: 6. Iustitiam particularem & universalem. Probatio: Non gaudet injustitia: Congaudet autem veritati.
units.tr: 6. Particular and universal justice. Proof: "It does not rejoice in injustice; but rejoices with the truth."

units.la: Ratio III. a duratione, quia ipsa non excidet: reliquis abolitis.
units.tr: Reason III, from its duration: because it will not fall away, all the rest being abolished.

units.la: Ostendatur ex textu: Nunc ergo manet fides, spes, charitas: maxima vero harum, charitas.
units.tr: Let it be shown from the text: "Now therefore abide faith, hope, love; but the greatest of these is love."

units.la: Obiect. Magis ergo justificat. Resp. 1. Si ulla virtus justificaret sane charitas justificaret: At nulla justificat ne fides quidem ut virtus, quia omnis imperfecta. 2. Coram hominibus quidem, sed non coram Deo.
units.tr: Objection: therefore it justifies more. Answer: 1. If any virtue justified, certainly love would justify; but no virtue justifies, not even faith as a virtue, because every one is imperfect. 2. Indeed before men, but not before God.

units.la: Ostendatur breviter ex Rom. 4. & Iac. 2. & quo sensu fides justificet.
units.tr: Let it be shown briefly from Rom. 4 and Jas. 2, and in what sense faith justifies.

units.la: Conclusio: Charitas igitur maxima virtus: maximeque necessaria.
units.tr: Conclusion: Love, therefore, is the greatest virtue and the most necessary of all.

units.la: Exercitatio LIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio LIII.

units.la: An Deus mutet consilium, ex Exod. 32. 14.
units.tr: Whether God changes his purpose, from Exod. 32. 14.

units.la: Breviter narretur Mosis mora in monte: populi apostasia: Dei indignatio & comminatio: Mosis intercessio: & veniae impetratio.
units.tr: Let the delay of Moses on the mountain be briefly related: the apostasy of the people; the indignation and threat of God; the intercession of Moses; and the obtaining of pardon.

units.la: Transitio ad quaestionem: Multae hic sunt quaestiones: praecipue: An Deus mutet consilium. Ratio dubitationis ex comminatione deletionis populi & contrario eventu.
units.tr: Transition to the question: There are many questions here, chiefly this: whether God changes his purpose. The reason for doubt is drawn from the threat of destroying the people and from the contrary outcome.

units.la: Propositio sit responsio: Quod non mutet.
units.tr: The proposition, which is the answer: that he does not change it.

units.la: Ratio 1. a variis testimoniis scripturae de Dei immutabilitate. Num. 23. 1. Sam. 15. Psal. 102. Malach. 3. Iac. 1.
units.tr: Reason 1, from various testimonies of Scripture concerning the immutability of God: Num. 23. 1 Sam. 15. Ps. 102. Mal. 3. Jas. 1.

units.la: Ratio 2. a causis mutationis consiliorum, quae in Deum non cadunt.
units.tr: Reason 2, from the causes of changes of purpose, which do not fall upon God.

units.la: Has ostendatur esse vel ignorantiam, vel errorem, vel impotentiam persequendi consilia.
units.tr: It is shown that these are either ignorance, or error, or inability to carry out one's purposes.

units.la: Probetur in Deum nihil horum cadere: ex immensa ejus sapientia & potentia; Scripturae dicti[?]s: ētis[?] vel gnomis: πάντα ἰδὼν Διὸς ὀφθαλμὸς ἡ πάν-τα νοήσας[?], &c.
units.tr: Let it be proved that none of these falls upon God, from his immense wisdom and power; and from the sayings of Scripture, and from proverbs: "The eye of Zeus sees all things, or understands all things," etc. [πάντα ἰδὼν Διὸς ὀφθαλμὸς ἡ πάντα νοήσας]

units.la: Obiectio 1. Eventus fuit contrarius commi-natio[?]ni. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Objection 1. The outcome was contrary to the threat. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Respon. Negetur antecedens: 1. quia commi-natio fuit conditionalis: Delebo : nisi tu inter-cesseris. 2. Fuit in determinata tempore. Precibus igitur Mosis pœna fuit dilata non sublata. Textus v. 34. In die visitationis meæ tunc visitabo, &c.
units.tr: Answer. The antecedent is denied: (1) because the threat was conditional: "I will destroy, unless you intercede." (2) It was fixed for a time. The punishment was therefore postponed, not removed, by the prayers of Moses. The text, v. 34: "In the day of my visitation I will then visit, etc."

units.la: Obiectio 2. Deum pœnituit: afferantur quæ-dam similia loca Gen.6.1. Sam.15. Ionæ 3.Ier. 19.
units.tr: Objection 2. God repented: let certain similar passages be cited: Gen. 6. 1 Sam. 15. Jonah 3. Jer. 19.

units.la: Resp. ἀνθρωποπαθῶς non mutatione consilii, sed mutatione aut dilatione eventus: quæ certa fuit in mente Dei, & subintellecta in commina-tione ad tacitam conditionem precum, Ostenda-tur idem in similibus locis.
units.tr: Answer. These are spoken in a human manner (anthropopathically): not by a change of purpose, but by a change or postponement of the outcome, which was certain in the mind of God and understood in the threat, as a tacit condition attached to prayers. Let the same be shown in similar passages.

units.la: Conclusio 1. Precibus non mutatur quidem Deus, sed pœnæ tamen vel mitigantur vel differuntur vel avertuntur. 2. Ad comminationes igitur divinas non oportet desperare, sed ardeter[?] orare & agere pœnitentiam.
units.tr: Conclusion 1. By prayers God is indeed not changed, but the punishments are nevertheless either lessened, or deferred, or averted. 2. Therefore one ought not to despair at the divine threats, but to pray earnestly and to practise repentance.

units.la: Exercitat. LIV.
units.tr: Exercitat. LIV.

units.la: RESPONSORIA.
units.tr: RESPONSORIA.

units.la: An amico recte sentienti in Repub. Pontificia liceat funus ad templum prosequi.
units.tr: Whether a friend who holds sound doctrine may lawfully accompany a funeral to the church in the Papist commonwealth.

units.la: EXordium à thesi: Difficile est judicare, quando
units.tr: THE EXORDIUM from the thesis: It is difficult to judge when goods things, or things indifferent, become unlawful,

units.la: res bonæ vel mediæ fiant illicitæ, circumstantiis omnibus non probe cognitis.
units.tr: when all the circumstances are not properly known.

units.la: Ratio: Quia circumstantiæ sæpè variant judicium.
units.tr: Reason: because circumstances often alter the judgment.

units.la: Hypothesis sit quæstio amici, an liceat ipsi comitari funera vicinorum vel magistratus ad templum papisticum: quando præcipitur.
units.tr: The hypothesis is the friend's question: whether it is lawful for him to accompany the funerals of his neighbours, or of the magistrate, to the Papist church, when it is ordered.

units.la: Propositio per ἀπὸ τῆς ὑπάρξεως: Etsi præstaret exire ex Babylone, tamen cum clandestina Ecclesia orthodoxa, in qua sit, ibi maneat, & ipse habeat graves manendi causas: videri tibi licere funus prosequi usque ad templum his positis conditionibus:
units.tr: Proposition, from the existence (ἀπὸ τῆς ὑπάρξεως): Although it would be better to come out of Babylon, yet, since he remains in a secret orthodox Church, where he is, and since he has grave reasons for staying, it seems to you lawful to follow the funeral as far as the church, on these conditions:

units.la: 1. Si magistratus vel lex jubeat.
units.tr: 1. If the magistrate or the law commands it.

units.la: 2. Si professione, & discessione ad templum sacra ipsorum exsequialia improbare se ostendat.
units.tr: 2. If by profession and by withdrawing he shows that he disapproves of their funeral rites performed in the church.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia magistratui in civilibus, per se licitis est obtemperandum, etiam cum aliqua mo lestia. Rom. 13.5.1. Pet. 2.18.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because in civil matters that are lawful in themselves, obedience is owed to the magistrate, even when there is some inconvenience. Rom. 13.5; 1 Pet. 2.18.

units.la: Addatur ratio: quia in talia cives jurant. Recte autem jurata recte præstantur.
units.tr: Let a reason be added: because citizens swear to such things. Things rightly sworn are rightly performed.

units.la: Amplificetur ab incommodis. 1. ne possint accusari perjurii.
units.tr: Let it be amplified from the disadvantages. 1. Lest they be accused of perjury.

units.la: 2. Ne nomen Dei & doctrina blasphemetur 1. Tim. 6.1.
units.tr: 2. Lest the name of God and the doctrine be blasphemed, 1 Tim. 6.1.

units.la: Item a paribus: Possunt sine suo peccato, lege vel magistratu jubete, juvare structuram templi, pendere reditus sacros; servare stationes urbis, dum fit pompa publica: Ratio, quia hæc sunt onera civilia suo genere non impia.
units.tr: Likewise from equals: they may, without their own sin, when ordered by law or magistrate, help in the building of the church, pay the sacred revenues, and keep the city's watches while the public procession takes place. Reason: because these are civil burdens, not impious in their kind.

units.la: Minor subjiciatur, quod deductiones funebres sint officia civilia quatenus lege jubentur: & licitæ per se: quia charitatis, &c.
units.tr: Let the minor premise be added: that funeral processions are civil duties, insofar as they are commanded by law, and lawful in themselves, because they belong to charity, etc.

units.la: Ratio II. Quia peccatum accidit deductioni vel ex approbatione superstitionum, vel ex scandalo aliorum. At professione & discessione à sacris papisticis satis se purgat, quod impios aut superstitiosos ritus non approbet: ideoque scandalum non prabet.
units.tr: Reason II. Because sin attaches to taking part in the procession either through approval of superstitions or through scandal to others. But by profession and by withdrawal from the Papist rites, he sufficiently clears himself, since he does not approve of impious or superstitious rites; and so he gives no scandal.

units.la: Ratio III. à majori. Licet recte sentientib. (cum aliter non possunt) uti ministerio errantium, & ceremonias humanas servare, dummodo fidem suam aperte profiteantur, errores differte improbent, & nihil per se impium verbis vel factis committant. Multo magis licet comitari funus cum improbatione superstitionum.
units.tr: Reason III, from the greater. It is lawful for those who hold sound doctrine (since they cannot do otherwise) to make use of the ministry of those who err, and to observe human ceremonies, provided they openly profess their faith, reprove the errors, and commit nothing impious in themselves by word or deed. Much more, then, is it lawful to accompany a funeral while disapproving of the superstitions.

units.la: Antecedens probetur exemplis prophetarum, Christi & apostolorum, qui sæpe sunt usi ministerio sacerdotum errantium: cum taxatione corruptelarum.
units.tr: The antecedent is proved by the examples of the prophets, of Christ and of the apostles, who often made use of the ministry of erring priests, while censuring their corruptions.

units.la: Obiectio I. Præfertur crux lignea: cantantur nænię [?] impiæ.
units.tr: Objection I. The wooden cross is carried before, and impious dirges are sung.

units.la: Resp. I. Professione improbatur si quid impium ab aliis fiat, 2. Non crux, quæ olim fuit Christianorum symbolum, sed veneratio crucis, est peccatum. 3. Næniæ funerales ferè sunt psalmi pœnitentiales latinè decantati. Si quid corruptelæ admiscetur, id non polluit non intelligentes nec succinentes.
units.tr: Answer I. By profession, whatever impious thing is done by others is disapproved. 2. It is not the cross, which was once the symbol of Christians, but the veneration of the cross, that is sin. 3. Funeral dirges are for the most part penitential psalms sung in Latin. If some corruption is mixed in, it does not defile those who do not understand it or who do not join in the singing.

units.la: Obiectio II. Non fit deductio sine scandalo. Resp. Accepto, in casu professionis, &c.
units.tr: Objection II. A procession cannot take place without scandal. Answer It is accepted, in the case of profession, etc.

units.la: Obiectio III. Sine ut mortui sepeliant mortuos: Resp. Valet in casu abnegationis veritatis, vel desertionis officii, de quo casu loquitur Christus. Aspiciatur locus.
units.tr: Objection III. "Let the dead bury their dead." Answer It holds in the case of denying the truth or deserting one's office, which is the case Christ speaks of. Let the passage be consulted.

units.la: Conclusio: Si per leges & charitatem possit, potius abstineat à tali officio. Si non possit, tibi videri eum sic facientem, absque peccato servitute eam ferre posse.
units.tr: Conclusion: If he can do it consistently with the laws and with charity, he should rather abstain from such an office. If he cannot, it seems to you that he, doing so, can bear the servitude without sin.

units.la: Exercitatio LV.
units.tr: Exercitatio LV.

units.la: NARRATIO ἐγκωμιαστικὴ[?]
units.tr: NARRATIO encomiastica[?]

units.la: De Iohanne Baptista.
units.tr: On John the Baptist.

units.la: EXordium à thesi: Magnorum virorum virtutes esse celebrandas.
units.tr: Exordium from the thesis: The virtues of great men are to be celebrated.

units.la: 1. Ut Dei bonitas & dona agnoscantur & celebrentur.
units.tr: 1. So that God's goodness and gifts may be acknowledged and celebrated.

units.la: 2. Ut imitemur exempla.
units.tr: 2. So that we may imitate their examples.

units.la: Addatur [illegible, ~8 letters]; de Iohanne Baptista, cujus laudatio instituatur.
units.tr: Let there be added [illegible, ~8 letters]; concerning John the Baptist, whose praise is to be undertaken.

units.la: 1. ∝[?] natalibus ex Luc.1. Vbi de parentum familia, conditione, sanctitate, conceptu pleno miraculis: mater sterilis, effœta, angeli nuncius & oraculum, Zacharias mutus, fœtus repletus Spiritu sancto, exultans in utero matris, nativitas: nomen: pater iterum loquens, prophetans de puero, &c. Hæc breviter latina oratione narrentur.
units.tr: 1. Concerning his birth, from Luke 1. Here we narrate briefly, in Latin oratory, the family of his parents, their condition and holiness, the conception full of miracles: a mother barren and worn out with age, the angel's message and oracle, Zacharias made mute, the fetus filled with the Holy Spirit, leaping in the mother's womb, the birth, the name, the father speaking again and prophesying concerning the boy, etc.

units.la: II. ∝[?] vocatione divina. Luc.3.2. Matth.21.25. Vbi paucis de tempore, loco vocationis & officio prophetico.
units.tr: II. Concerning his divine calling. Luke 3:2; Matt. 21:25. Here, briefly, the time, place and office of his prophetic calling.

units.la: 1. est nuncius Iehovæ, præcursor Messiæ Mal. 3.1. Marc.1.2. 2.Elias.Mal.4.5.Luc.1.17.Matt.11.14.
units.tr: 1. He is the messenger of Jehovah, the forerunner of the Messiah: Mal. 3:1; Mark 1:2; 2 Elijah, Mal. 4:5; Luke 1:17; Matt. 11:14.

units.la: Concilietur cum Ioh.1.22.
units.tr: Let it be reconciled with John 1:22.

units.la: 3.Propheta, major propheta: maximus natorum ex mulieribus.Matth.11.9.11.
units.tr: 3. A prophet, and more than a prophet: the greatest of those born of women. Matt. 11:9, 11.

units.la: Declaretur & concilietur cum Ioh.1.22.
units.tr: Let it be explained and reconciled with John 1:22.

units.la: III. Aministerio: Vbi i.de doctrinae genere, summa, usu & efficacia.Matt.3.v.2.3.9.
units.tr: III. Concerning his ministry. Here, first, concerning the kind of teaching, its substance, use and efficacy. Matt. 3:2, 3, 9.

units.la: Accommodetur ad oracula de ipso & ostenda-tur praestantia doctrinae ejus & aliorum prophetarum Ioh.1.29.
units.tr: Let it be adapted to the oracles concerning him, and the excellence of his teaching and of the other prophets is to be shown. John 1:29.

units.la: 2. De baptismo, unde baptista, ubi, quomodo, & qua authoritate, quos ad quid baptizaverit. Matth.3. Marc.1.Luc.3.
units.tr: 2. Concerning baptism: whence he was called the Baptist, where, how, and by what authority, and whom he baptized and for what purpose. Matt. 3; Mark 1; Luke 3.

units.la: IV. A virtutibus. 1. Iustitia & sanctitate. Marc.6.20. 2. Temperantia. Matth.3.4. 3. Modestia. Matth.11.8. 4. Authoritate. Matth.3.7. Marc.6.20. 5. Fidelitate & candore Ioh.1.20. & 3.28.29. 6. προφητεία[?] prophetica. Matth.3.7. Mar.6.18. 7. Constantia. Matth.11.7. 8. Martyrio. Matth.14.
units.tr: IV. From his virtues. 1. By righteousness and holiness. Mark 6:20. 2. Temperance. Matt. 3:4. 3. Modesty. Matt. 11:8. 4. Authority. Matt. 3:7; Mark 6:20. 5. Faithfulness and candour, John 1:20; 3:28, 29. 6. Prophetic [προφητεία?]. Matt. 3:7; Mark 6:18. 7. Constancy. Matt. 11:7. 8. Martyrdom. Matt. 14.

units.la: Exercitatio LVI.
units.tr: Exercitatio LVI.

units.la: Collatio Adami & Christi.
units.tr: Comparison of Adam and Christ.

units.la: Exordium continens propositionem: Cum appareat Paulum collatione primi & secundi Adami esse delectatum: Roman.5.& 1.Corinth.15:operaepretium est considerare, quid simile habeant, & quid dissimile.
units.tr: The introduction sets out the proposition: since it appears that Paul delighted in comparing the first and second Adam (Rom. 5; 1 Cor. 15), it is worth considering what they have in common and how they differ.

units.la: Ostendatur similitudo in tribus: natura, fami-lia & merito.
units.tr: The similarity is shown in three respects: nature, family and merit.

units.la: I. Uterque est verus homo corpore terreno, anima rationali confians.
units.tr: I. Each is a true man, consisting of an earthly body and a rational soul.

units.la: De ADAMO probetur ex creatione: Formavit hominem de limo: Inspiravit spiraculum vitæ. Faciamus hominem ad imaginem nostram, &c.
units.tr: Of Adam this is proved from the creation: "He formed man of the dust; he breathed into him the breath of life"; "Let us make man in our image," etc.

units.la: De CHRISTO I. ex Paulo, qui hominem appellat Rom.5.15.1.Cor.15.v.21.47.1.Tim.2.5.
units.tr: Of Christ: first from Paul, who calls him a man (Rom. 5:15; 1 Cor. 15:21, 47; 1 Tim. 2:5).

units.la: Amplif. Et quidem verum hominem ex Adamo propagatum, quia semen, filius Abrahami, Davidis. Matth.1.1. Rom.1.3. & 9.5. Fructus ventris Mariæ. Luc.1.42. Filius hominis. Matth.9. Ioh.6.
units.tr: Amplification: indeed he is a true man, propagated from Adam, since he is the seed, the son of Abraham and of David (Matt. 1:1; Rom. 1:3; 9:5); the fruit of Mary's womb (Luke 1:42); the Son of Man (Matt. 9; John 6).

units.la: 2. quia oportebat fratrem nostrum esse & manere, ut pro nobis victima fieri, & nos sibi ta-quam membra capiti insitos gestare ac vivificare posset, Hebr.2. Ioh.15.
units.tr: 2. Because it was fitting that he should be and remain our brother, so that he might become a victim for us, and might bear and quicken us, joined to him as members to the head (Heb. 2; John 15).

units.la: Rejiciantur breviter errores Marcionis, Apollinaris, Eutychetis, &c.
units.tr: The errors of Marcion, Apollinaris, Eutyches, etc., are briefly rejected.

units.la: II. Uterque habet familiam & posteros.
units.tr: II. Each has a family and posterity.

units.la: Adam totum genus humanum. Act.17.26.
units.tr: Adam has the whole human race (Acts 17:26).

units.la: Christus omnes fideles electos. Ioh.7.6. Heb. 2.13.
units.tr: Christ has all the faithful elect (John 7:6; Heb. 2:13).

units.la: III. Uterque meretur & communicat posteris suis, quod ipse habet.
units.tr: III. Each merits for his posterity, and communicates to them, what he himself has.

units.la: Declaratur & probetur 1.Rom.5.14. Qui est typus futuri, &c. 1.Cor.15.v.48.49. Qualis terre-nus, &c.
units.tr: This is declared and proved from 1 Rom. 5:14, "who is a type of the one to come," etc.; 1 Cor. 15:48, 49, "as is the earthly, such are the earthly," etc.

units.la: 2. quia uterque gignit posteros. Genitum autem habet naturam gignentis.
units.tr: 2. Because each begets posterity, and what is begotten has the nature of the one who begets it.

units.la: 3. quia uterque accepit a Deo suis communi-canda. De Adamo probetur: quia omnes eramus in Adamo stante & labente Rom.5.12.
units.tr: 3. Because each has received from God things to be communicated to his own. Of Adam it is proved: because all of us were in Adam when he stood and when he fell (Rom. 5:12).

units.la: De Christo: quia frater primogenitus distribuens fratribus haereditatem: Item. Expleni-tudine eius omnes accepimus. Dedit dona hominibus, &c.
units.tr: Of Christ: because he is the firstborn brother who distributes the inheritance to his brothers; likewise, "Of his fullness we have all received"; "He gave gifts to men," etc.

units.la: Dissimilitudo primi & secundi Adami.
units.tr: The difference between the first and second Adam.

units.la: I. Primus Adam homo tantum formatus de terra. Secundus homo & Deus:filius Dei ante se-cula ex patre genitus, coæternus, consubstantialis patri secundum Deitatem: natus ex virgine Maria, nobis similis secundum carnem. Probe-tur Christi Deitas præcipuè ex dictis I. Cor. 15. ver.47. Ioh.1 14.Ioh.6.51. 1.Tim.3.16. Ioh.5.20.
units.tr: I. The first Adam was a man only, formed of the earth. The second is man and God: the Son of God, begotten of the Father before all ages, co-eternal and consubstantial with the Father according to his Deity; born of the virgin Mary, like us according to the flesh. The deity of Christ is proved especially from 1 Cor. 15:47; John 1:14; John 6:51; 1 Tim. 3:16; John 5:20.

units.la: II. Adam justus quidem creatus: sed seductio ne Diaboli peccator & hostis Dei factus. Gen.3. Rom.5.12.19. Unius transgressione & inobedientia, &c. Rom.8.7. Inimicitia est adversus Deum.
units.tr: II. Adam was created indeed righteous, but by the seduction of the devil he became a sinner and an enemy of God (Gen. 3; Rom. 5:12, 19): "by one man's transgression and disobedience," etc.; Rom. 8:7, "the mind of the flesh is enmity against God."

units.la: Christus justus: 1. quia Deus ipsa justitia Ier. 23.6.
units.tr: Christ is righteous: 1. because God himself is righteousness (Jer. 23:6).

units.la: 2. Natura humana sanctificata in utero Luc. 1 ver.35.
units.tr: 2. The human nature was sanctified in the womb (Luke 1:35).

units.la: 3. Talis requirebatur mediator. Heb.7. Talis nobis conveniebat pontifex, &c. Servus meus justus. Ief.53.[?] Non est inventus dolus, &c. Qui peccatum non novit, &c. Quis ex vobis arguet me, &c.
units.tr: 3. Such a mediator was required (Heb. 7): "such a high priest was fitting for us," etc.; "my servant, the righteous one" (Isa. 53); "no guile was found in him"; "who knew no sin," etc.; "which of you convicts me," etc.

units.la: III. Adam per peccatum factus obnoxius morti temporali & æternæ perierat perpetuo, nisi servaretur aliunde: juxta comminationem.
units.tr: III. Adam, made liable to temporal and eternal death through sin, would have perished forever, unless he had been saved from elsewhere, according to the threat.

units.la: Morte morieris: Per peccatum mors, &c. Stipen-dium peccati mors, &c.
units.tr: "In the day you eat of it you shall die" (Gen. 2:17); "through sin, death," etc.; "the wages of sin is death," etc.

units.la: Christus immortalis: 1. Deitate ipsa vita, fons vitæ: Ego sum resurrectio & vita, &c. Filio dedit vitam habere in seipso, &c. Hic est verus Deus & vita æterna. 2. Etiam carne justa sancta per se ex ordine justitiæ: Anima quæ peccaverit ea morietur. Ergo quæ non peccaverit non morietur.
units.tr: Christ is immortal: 1. by his Deity, which is life itself, the fountain of life: "I am the resurrection and the life," etc.; "to the Son he has given to have life in himself," etc.; "This is the true God and eternal life" (John 11:25; 5:26; 1 John 5:20). 2. Also, in his flesh, which is righteous and holy in itself, by the order of righteousness: "The soul that sins shall die" (Ezek. 18:4). Therefore the one who has not sinned shall not die.

units.la: Obiectio: Atqui mortuus. Resp. 1. Non divinitate. 2. Ex carnis infirmitate propter nos suscepta 2. Cor. 13. 3. Devicta morte revixit, potentia Deitatis suæ. Act. 2. Non erat possibile eum detineri, &c. Habeo potestatem ponendi & sumendi animam: Apoc.1.8. Fui mortuus sed ecce vivo.
units.tr: Objection: but he died. Answer: 1. not in his deity. 2. by the weakness of the flesh, which he took up on account of us (2 Cor. 13:4). 3. Having overcome death, he rose again by the power of his Deity (Acts 2:24): "It was not possible for him to be held," etc.; "I have power to lay down and to take up my life" (John 10:18); "I was dead, but behold, I am alive" (Rev. 1:18).

units.la: Ergo idem vivificatus & vivificans.
units.tr: Therefore the same one is made alive and gives life.

units.la: Transitio a dictis[?], qualis uterque sit, ad dicenda, quales uterque suos efficiat posteros, hoc est, quid illis mereatur & communicet, & quomodo.
units.tr: Transition: from what each is, to what each makes his posterity, that is, what he merits for them and communicates to them, and how.

units.la: IV. Adam corruptionem suam propagat in omnes posteros.
units.tr: IV. Adam propagates his corruption into all his posterity.

units.la: Prob. 1. testimonio apostoli Rom. 5. v. 12. 15. 18. 19. Unius peccato peccatores constituti multi.
units.tr: Proved, 1. by the testimony of the apostle (Rom. 5:12, 15, 18, 19): "through one man's sin many were made sinners."

units.la: II. à fine collatæ in eum imaginis Dei, ut nimirum sibi, & posteris eam retineret vel amitteret. Rom. 5. 12. In quo omnes peccaverunt.
units.tr: II. From the end for which the image of God was conferred upon him, namely that he might keep it for himself and his posterity, or lose it. Rom. 5:12: "in whom all have sinned."

units.la: III. A natura eadem gignentis & geniti. Iob. 14. 4. Gen. 5. 3. Genuit ad imaginem suam. Ioh. 3. 6. Natum ex carne caro est.
units.tr: III. From the same nature of the begetter and the begotten (Job 14:4; Gen. 5:3, "he begot a son in his own image"; John 3:6, "what is born of the flesh is flesh").

units.la: CHRISTUS justus suam justitiam communicat in omnes suos.
units.tr: Christ, being righteous, communicates his righteousness to all his own.

units.la: I. Justificando nos: quia sua humiliatione obedientia usque ad mortem crucis, dum passus est justus pro injustis, nobis meritus est remissionem peccatorum, justitiam, Spiritum Sanctum & vitam æternam. Rom.5.19. Per unius obedientiam. Factus obediens usque ad mortem, &c. Sanguis Iesu Christi mundat nos, &c. Servabit populum suum à peccatis suis.
units.tr: I. By justifying us: because by his humiliation, obedient even to the death of the cross, while the righteous one suffered for the unrighteous, he merited for us the forgiveness of sins, righteousness, the Holy Spirit and eternal life (Rom. 5:19): "through the obedience of one"; "became obedient unto death," etc.; "the blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us," etc.; "he will save his people from their sins."

units.la: II. Regenerando nos per Spiritum Sanctum & restituendo in nobis justitiam & conformitatem cum Deo per peccatum amissam. Rom.5.15. Donum per gratiam redundavit in multos. Hebr. 2. II. Qui sanctificat & sanctificantur. Ioh.1. Baptizat Spiritu Sancto. 1. Cor.1. Factus nobis justitia, sanctificatio.
units.tr: II. By regenerating us through the Holy Spirit, and restoring in us the righteousness and conformity with God that was lost through sin (Rom. 5:15): "the gift of grace abounded to many." Heb. 2:11: "for both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified." John 1: "he baptizes with the Holy Spirit." 1 Cor. 1:30: "made to us righteousness and sanctification."

units.la: v. Adam quia peccatum propagat in suos, ideo & mortem: & quidem utramque.
units.tr: v. Because Adam propagates sin into his own, so also death, and indeed both.

units.la: Prob. 1. Testimonium Apostoli: Et per peccatum mors, &c. Mors pervasit in omnes, &c. Unius peccato multi mortui, &c.
units.tr: Proved, 1. by the testimony of the apostle: "and through sin, death," etc.; "death spread to all men," etc.; "through one man's sin many died," etc.

units.la: 2. quia stipendium peccati mors. Rom.6. Ideo omnes natura filii iræ. Eph.2.
units.tr: 2. Because the wages of sin is death (Rom. 6). Therefore all, by nature, are children of wrath (Eph. 2).

units.la: Amplific. Hinc exclusio ex paradiso, à ligno vitæ, tot morbi, pestis, fames, inopia, bella, cædes, &c.
units.tr: Amplification: hence the exclusion from paradise, from the tree of life; so many diseases, plague, famine, want, wars, slaughters, etc.

units.la: CHRISTUS, quia justitiæ ideo & vitæ author est suis. Rom.5.17. Qui redundant gratiam & donum justitiæ accipiunt, &c.
units.tr: Christ, because he is the author of righteousness and therefore of life to his own (Rom. 5:17): "those who receive abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness," etc.

units.la: Probetur 1. Quia morte sua mortem sustulit. Hebr.2.14.15. Ut per mortem, &c. 1.Cor.15. Absorpta mors in victoriam.
units.tr: Proved: 1. because by his own death he destroyed death (Heb. 2:14, 15): "that through death," etc.; 1 Cor. 15: "death is swallowed up in victory."

units.la: 2. quia ex morte resurrexit, ut nos à morte liberatos vivificaret. Rom.6.8. Mortui cum Christo etiam vivemus cum eo. 1.Cor.15. Per hominem resurrectio. Col.3. Si resurrexistis cum Christo.&c.
units.tr: 2. because he rose from the dead, so that he might quicken us, freed from death (Rom. 6:8): "if we have died with Christ, we shall also live with him"; 1 Cor. 15: "through a man came the resurrection"; Col. 3: "If you have been raised with Christ," etc.

units.la: 3. Quia Deus est qui est fons vitæ,&c.i.Ioh.5. Hic verus Deus & vita æterna. Ego vitam æternam do ovibus meis.
units.tr: 3. Because God is the one who is the fountain of life, etc. (1 John 5): "This is the true God and eternal life"; "I give eternal life to my sheep" (John 10:28).

units.la: Transitio, dictum, quid uterque Adam nobis communicet: restat quomodo communicet.
units.tr: Transition: the point made was what each Adam communicates to us; what remains is how he communicates it.

units.la: VI. Adam sua in suos propagat naturâ: Quod natum est ex carne caro est. Qualis terrenus tales terreni.
units.tr: VI. Adam propagates his own into his posterity by nature: "What is born of the flesh is flesh"; "as is the earthly, such are the earthly" (1 Cor. 15:48).

units.la: Amplif. Ideo omnibus communicat peccatum & mortem: quia omnibus naturam. Eramus omnes filij ira natura, sicut & reliqui. In omnes pervasit mors eo quod omnes peccaverunt.
units.tr: Amplification: therefore he communicates sin and death to all, because he communicates nature to all: "We were all by nature children of wrath, as the rest also were"; "death spread to all, because all sinned."

units.la: Christus suos filios iustificat & regenerat ex gratia, id est, gratuita Dei misericordia per sanguinem & Spiritum suum. Rom.5.16. Non ut il-lud quod introut[?] per unum qui peccavit: ita est beneficium,&c. Nam reatus quidem ex una offensa in-troit ad condemnationem: quod autem gratificatur Deus datur ex multis offensis ad iustificatione. Ioh.1. Qui non ex sanguinibus, &c. Ex plenitudine eius omnes accepimus,&c.
units.tr: Christ justifies and regenerates his sons by grace, that is, by God's free mercy, through his blood and his Spirit (Rom. 5:16): "not as with the one who sinned, so is the gift; for the judgment from one offense led to condemnation, but the free gift proceeds from many offenses to justification." John 1: "who were born not of blood," etc.; "of his fullness we have all received," etc.

units.la: Amplif. Ideo non omnes sed soli electi servantur.
units.tr: Amplification: therefore not all, but only the elect, are saved.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia miseretur quorum vult. 2. quia reliqui gratiam repudiant.
units.tr: Reason: 1. because he has mercy on whom he wills; 2. because the rest reject grace.

units.la: Obiect. Non servat absque merito. Non igitur gratis.
units.tr: Objection: he does not save without merit; therefore not freely.

units.la: Resp. Imo gratis. 1. quia non merito nostro sed alieno.
units.tr: Answer: indeed freely. 1. because it is not by our merit but by another's.

units.la: 2. quia Deus & Filium & meritum eius gratis nobis donat : Vt filium suum daret, ut omnis, &c. Qui filio suo non pepercit, &c. Factus nobis à Deo sapientia justitia, &c.
