units.tr: 2. because God gives us both the Son and his merit freely: "that he gave his Son, that everyone..." (John 3:16); "who did not spare his own Son" (Rom. 8:32); "Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, righteousness," etc. (1 Cor. 1:30).

units.la: 3. Etiam fidem donat qua accipiamus. Dei donum est non ex nobis. Domine auge nobis fidem.
units.tr: 3. He also gives the faith by which we receive it: "it is the gift of God, not from ourselves" (Eph. 2:8); "Lord, increase our faith" (Luke 17:5).

units.la: Amplific. à necessario, quia propter naturæ pravitatem non possemus accipere donum, nisi ipse mutaret corda; daret & extenderet nobis ma-num, id est, fidem: Sine me nihil potestis facere.
units.tr: Amplified from the necessary point: because of the corruption of nature we could not receive the gift unless he himself changed our hearts, and gave and extended to us his hand, that is, faith: "Without me you can do nothing."

units.la: VII. Christus potentior ad servandum, quam Adam ad perdendum.
units.tr: VII. Christ is more powerful to save than Adam was to destroy.

units.la: 1. quia Deus magis propensus ad misericordiam quam ad iram. Exod 34.
units.tr: 1. Because God is more inclined to mercy than to wrath. Exod. 34.

units.la: 2. quia meritum unius Christi præponderat omnibus omnium hominum peccatis.
units.tr: 2. Because the merit of Christ alone outweighs the sins of all men together.

units.la: 3. quia Adam merito suo nobis attraxit privationem justitiæ & vitæ: Christus non tantum merito, sed etiam divina efficacia sua nos justifi-cat, regenerat, vivificat. Rom. 5. Etenim si per u-nam offensam, &c. multo magis, &c. Item: Ubi ab-undat peccatum, ibi superabundavit gratia.
units.tr: 3. Because Adam by his merit drew upon us the privation of righteousness and life; Christ justifies, regenerates and quickens us not only by his merit but also by his divine efficacy. Rom. 5. "For if through the one offence, etc., much more, etc." Likewise: "Where sin abounded, grace did much more abound."

units.la: Obiectio. At plures Adam perdidit, quā Christus servat, &c.
units.tr: Objection. But Adam destroyed more people than Christ saves, etc.

units.la: Resp. Potentia utriusq; non spectanda in mul-titudine eorum qui pereunt vel servantur, sed in modo quo fit perditio & servatio, & in magnitu-dine bonorum amissorum & reparatorum.
units.tr: Answer. The power of each is not to be judged by the multitude of those who perish or are saved, but by the manner in which destruction and salvation take place, and by the greatness of the goods lost and restored.

units.la: Declaratur. 1. Facilius est multos perdere, quam unum perditum restituere, quod ostenda-tur exemplis. Facilius est decem de ponte deiicce-re, occidere: quam unum submersum servare, occisum vivificare,&c.
units.tr: Explanation. 1. It is easier to destroy many than to restore one who has been lost, as is shown by examples. It is easier to throw ten men off a bridge and kill them than to save one who has drowned, or to make alive one who has been killed, etc.

units.la: 2. Bona reparata à Christo multo maiora quā in Adamo amissa: quia Adam nos eiecit ex terre-no paradiso: Christus in coelestè collocavit. Hodie mecum eris in paradiso. Vado paraturus vobis locum. Volo ut ubi ego sum ibi etiam sint quos dedisti mihi.
units.tr: 2. The goods restored by Christ are far greater than those lost in Adam: because Adam cast us out of the earthly paradise, but Christ has placed us in the heavenly one. "Today you will be with me in paradise." "I go to prepare a place for you." "Father, I desire that where I am, there also may be those whom you have given me."

units.la: Exercitatio LVII.
units.tr: Exercitatio LVII.

units.la: An liceat Christianis per nomen Dei jurare.
units.tr: Whether Christians may swear by the name of God.

units.la: EXordium à causa quæstionis: quod Anabaptistæ negant licere, prætextu interdicti Christi. Ne omnino juretis.Matth.5.
units.tr: The exordium is taken from the cause of the question: the Anabaptists deny that it is lawful, under the pretext of Christ's prohibition. Swear not at all. Matt. 5.

units.la: Adversativa: Sed id perperam ab eis torquetur: ut pleraque alia eius concionis.
units.tr: Adversative: But this passage is wrongly twisted by them, as are many other things in that sermon.

units.la: Propositio: Licitum est Christianis jurare: Addantur limitationes:
units.tr: Proposition: It is lawful for Christians to swear. Limitations are to be added:

units.la: 1. cum vel magistratus vel alioqui necessitas postulat.
units.tr: (1) when either the magistrate or some other necessity demands it;

units.la: 2. de rebus veris, certis, licitis, possibilibus, gravibus, de aliis vel contrariis non item.
units.tr: (2) about things that are true, certain, lawful, possible and weighty, but not about other or contrary things.

units.la: Ratio 1. à Dei mandato. de deferendo & præstando jurejurando in controversiis Exod. 22.11. Deut.6.10.&10.20,&c.
units.tr: Reason 1: from the command of God, concerning the bringing and performing of an oath in controversies: Exod. 22.11; Deut. 6.10 and 10.20, etc.

units.la: Ratio 11. a genere. Iusjurandum est cultus Dei tertio præcepto sancitus.
units.tr: Reason 2: from the genus. An oath is a worship of God, enjoined by the third commandment.

units.la: Prob. 1. ex definitione: quia est invocatio Dei & recta fides de Deo, quod sit καρδιογνώστης[?], omnipotens, justus, &c. quæ breviter ex definitione monstrentur: 2. quia temeraria & illegitima juramenta & perjuria tanquam profanatio nominis Dei prohibentur. Ergo horum contrariū jusiurandum legitimum tanquam recta usurpatio nominis Dei sancitur.
units.tr: Proof 1: from the definition, because it is an invocation of God and a right faith concerning God, that he is the searcher of hearts [καρδιογνώστης], almighty, just, etc., which are briefly shown from the definition; (2) because rash and unlawful oaths and perjuries are forbidden as a profanation of the name of God. Therefore the contrary, a lawful oath, is enjoined as the right use of the name of God.

units.la: Ratio III. ab Oraculis: Quod juratio per nomen Iehovæ sit cultus Dei etiam in N. T. Ief.19. ver.17. & 65.16.
units.tr: Reason 3: from the oracles: that swearing by the name of Jehovah is a worship of God also in the New Testament. Isa. 19.17 and 65.16.

units.la: Ratio IV. ex fine seu usu: quia juramentum est finis omnis controversiæ inter homines Heb. 6.ver.16.
units.tr: Reason 4: from the end or use: because an oath is the end of every controversy among men. Heb. 6.16.

units.la: Amplific. à necessario: quod alioqui veritas & salus proximi sæpe periclitaretur: & lites in infinitum abirent.
units.tr: Amplification from necessity: because otherwise the truth and the safety of a neighbour would often be endangered, and lawsuits would go on without end.

units.la: Ratio V. ab exemplis Dei, Christi, Angelorum & Sanctorum in utroque Testamento:
units.tr: Reason 5: from the examples of God, Christ, the angels and the saints in both Testaments.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Christus Matth.5. & Iacobus cap.5. ver.12. prohibent omnia juramenta.
units.tr: Objection 1: Christ, Matt. 5, and James, chap. 5, verse 12, forbid all oaths.

units.la: Resp. 1. Negatur: quia non prohibet jurare per nomen Dei. 2. prohibet tantum temeraria & Sophistica: quod ostendatur ex scopo Christi, & ex verbis: Sermo vester sit est est, non non. Sermo noster non dicitur cōstare meris juramentis, sed veris verbis: Eadem sententia Iacobi.
units.tr: Answer 1: Denied: for he does not forbid swearing by the name of God. (2) He forbids only rash and sophistical oaths; this is shown from the aim of Christ and from his words: Let your speech be yea, yea, no, no. Our speech is not said to consist of mere oaths but of true words. The same is the sense of James.

units.la: Obiectio II. Futura non sunt ἐφ᾽ ἡμῖν. Ergo de his saltem non est jurandum: & sic illicita sunt homagia, omniaque juramenta promissoria & obligatoria.
units.tr: Objection 2: Future things are not in our power. Therefore at least concerning these it is not lawful to swear; and so homages, and all promissory and obligatory oaths, are unlawful.

units.la: Resp. 1. Iuratio fit de περιστάσει[?] & voluntate præsente obediendi, quæ est ἐφ᾽ ἡμῖν: Ideo juramentum definitur confirmatio voluntatis testimonio Dei facta: Cic.3.offic.
units.tr: Answer 1: An oath is made concerning the circumstance and the present will to obey, which is in our power. Therefore an oath is defined as a confirmation of the will made by the testimony of God: Cic., De officiis 3.

units.la: II. Omnis obligatio fit disiunctive, aut ad obedientiam præstandam ad pœnam luendam. Hæc autem est Φ᾽ ἡμῖν[?], si deficiat obedientia.
units.tr: (2) Every obligation is made disjunctively, either to perform obedience or to pay the penalty. The latter, however, is not in our power if obedience fails.

units.la: Conclusio: Licita igitur sunt Christianis juramenta.
units.tr: Conclusion: Oaths are therefore lawful for Christians.

units.la: Verum eis utendum, non ut esca, sed ut medicina: quæ male sumta, vel temerè iterata fit venenum.
units.tr: Yet they are to be used not as food but as medicine, which, taken badly or repeated rashly, becomes poison.

units.la: Exercitatio LVIII.
units.tr: Exercise 58.

units.la: Collatio Davidis vincentis Goliathum: & Christi vincentis Diabolum & mortè tanquam typi & antitypi: ex 1. Sam. 17.
units.tr: Comparison of David conquering Goliath and Christ conquering the Devil and death, as type and antitype: from 1 Sam. 17.

units.la: I. David mittitur à patre in castra. Sic Filius mittitur à patre in hunc mû-dum.
units.tr: I. David is sent by his father to the camp. So the Son is sent by the Father into this world.

units.la: II. David mittitur ad visendos & juvandos fratres. Christus mittitur ad liberandum genus huma-num.
units.tr: II. David is sent to visit and help his brothers. Christ is sent to free the human race.

units.la: III. David à fratribus suis impeditur: ob-jurgatur.
units.tr: III. David is hindered and rebuked by his brothers.

units.la: Christus reiicitur à suis. Ioh. 1. Et sui eum non receperunt, &c.
units.tr: Christ is rejected by his own. John 1. And his own did not receive him, etc.

units.la: IV. David sponte se offert ad duellum.
units.tr: IV. David voluntarily offers himself for single combat.

units.la: Christus voluntaria obedientia suscipit partes liberatoris, & cum Satana congreditur.
units.tr: Christ, by voluntary obedience, takes up the part of deliverer and engages with Satan.

units.la: V. David solus prodit contra Goliathum, hostem immanem, maledicentem exercitui Is-raëlis.
units.tr: V. David alone comes forward against Goliath, a huge enemy who reviles the army of Israel.

units.la: Sic Christus solus prodit contra diabolum, in-fernum, fernum, legem, hostes generis humani, &c.
units.tr: So Christ alone comes forward against the devil, hell, the law, the enemies of the human race, etc.

units.la: VI. David non induitur πανοπλίαν[?], sed armis levissimis, funda & lapillis prosternit Goliathum.
units.tr: VI. David does not put on armour [panoply?], but with the lightest weapons, a sling and pebbles, strikes down Goliath.

units.la: Ita Christus exinanivit se divina potētia in forma servi, cruce, ignominia vincit Satanam.
units.tr: So Christ, emptying himself of his divine power in the form of a servant, conquers Satan by the cross and by shame.

units.la: VII. David non vincit sibi sed populo.
units.tr: VII. David does not conquer for himself but for the people.

units.la: Sic Christus non sibi sed nobis. 1. Cor. 15. Vi-ctoriam dedit nobis.
units.tr: So Christ does not conquer for himself but for us. 1 Cor. 15. He gave us the victory.

units.la: VIII. David post victoriam tandem & post multos ἀγῶνας regnat.
units.tr: VIII. David reigns only after the victory, and after many contests [agōnas].

units.la: Sic Christus per passionem & mortē ingres-sus in gloriam sedit ad dextram Dei:
units.tr: So Christ, having entered into glory through suffering and death, sat down at the right hand of God:

units.la: Bibet de torrente in via, exaltavit caput. Psal.110.
units.tr: He shall drink of the brook in the way; therefore he lifted up the head. Ps. 110.

units.la: S V.
units.tr: S V.

units.la: DAVIDIS PAREI Exercitationum Philosophicarum & Theologicarum LIBER III. Exercitationes prolixiores Declamationum Theologicarum continens.
units.tr: DAVIDIS PAREI Exercitationum Philosophicarum & Theologicarum BOOK III, containing the longer exercises of theological declamations.

units.la: Exercitatio I.
units.tr: Exercise I.

units.la: Orationis demonstrativæ Oeconomia de semine[?] mulieris promisso in Paradiso Gen.3.15.
units.tr: The structure of a demonstrative oration on the seed[?] of the woman promised in Paradise, Gen. 3.15.

units.la: EXORDIUM à tempore figuratū gratulatione: Rediit augustissimum anni tempus, quo Ecclesia incarnationem Filii Dei celebrare solet.
units.tr: INTRODUCTION, a congratulation drawn from the season: The most august time of the year has returned, in which the Church is accustomed to celebrate the incarnation of the Son of God.

units.la: Hypothesis: Ergo & nos tanti mysterii memoriam recolamus.
units.tr: Hypothesis: Therefore let us also call to mind the memory of so great a mystery.

units.la: Ratio: Quia nuncius angelorū de nato Chri-sto Sersto Servatore nobis quoque solidum gaudium afferre debet, hoc tristi tempore, &c.
units.tr: Reason: Because the message of the angels concerning the birth of Christ the Saviour ought to bring us also a solid joy, in this sad time, etc.

units.la: Amplif. ab officio Scholasticorum, quos maxi-me decet hæc meditatio.
units.tr: Amplification from the office of the scholars, for whom this meditation is especially fitting.

units.la: Occupatio : Cum unus dicendo ex hoc loco soleat præire aliis: ego id nunc faciam:non inge-nii fiducia vel dicendi vi aliqua, sed vestra bene-volentia fretus:& Præceptorum jussu.
units.tr: Occupatio: Since one usually goes first from this place for the others, I shall now do so: relying not on confidence in my wit or on any power of speech, but on your goodwill, and at the command of my teachers.

units.la: Ἀ[?] Ἀποδίωξις[?]. Non igitur laborabo prolixe de venia.
units.tr: Ἀ[?] Ἀποδίωξις[?]. I shall therefore not labour at length to ask pardon.

units.la: Transitio habens attentionem: Potius transibo ad argumentum, quod, cum & tempori conveniat, & rarius tractetur, spero vos libenter au-dituros: nempe Promissionem primam & antiquissimam Evangelii de semine mulieris post ipsum datam Parentibus à Deo in Paradiso.
units.tr: Transition gaining attention: Rather I shall pass on to the subject which, since it both suits the time and is rarely treated, I hope you will gladly hear: namely, the first and most ancient promise of the Gospel, the promise of the seed of the woman, given by God to our first parents in Paradise after the fall.

units.la: Amplif. à causis. 1. quia confirmat nos de antiquitate & certitudine nostræ fidei.
units.tr: Amplification from causes. (1) Because it confirms us concerning the antiquity and certainty of our faith.

units.la: II. Quia omnibus temporibus ab hæreticis variè fuit obscurata.
units.tr: (2) Because in every age it has been variously obscured by heretics.

units.la: Narratio brevis: cuius membra sint: creatio hominis in Paradiso ad imaginem Dei: Prohibitio arboris sub comminatione mortis. Tentatio hominis à Satana in forma serpentis: Hominis lapsus: agnitio nuditatis: trepidatio, fuga: Denique consolatio de semine mulieris contrituro caput serpentis, &c.
units.tr: Brief narrative: its parts are these: the creation of man in Paradise in the image of God; the prohibition of the tree under threat of death; the temptation of man by Satan in the form of a serpent; the fall of man; the recognition of nakedness; the trembling and flight; and finally the consolation concerning the seed of the woman who will crush the head of the serpent, etc.

units.la: Propositio: de hac breviter explicabo.
units.tr: Proposition: I shall briefly explain these points.

units.la: I. Quodnam & quale sit illud semen promis-sum.
units.tr: (1) What and of what kind is that promised seed.

units.la: II. An sit exhibitum.
units.tr: (2) Whether it has been exhibited.

units.la: III. Ad quid sit promissum atq; exhibitum.
units.tr: (3) To what end it was promised and exhibited.

units.la: 1. Quodnam & quale sit semen promissum.
units.tr: 1. What and of what kind is the promised seed.

units.la: Non rei vulgaris sed maximæ promissionem esse: Ostende 1. ex verbis: Semen mulieris, quasi dicat, non viri, non hominis tantum. 2. ex scopo, Deus vult erigere hac consolatione parentes, & posteros eorum contra comminationem & sensum mortis. Ponam inimicitias, &c. conteret caput, &c. quasi dicat, puniam Diabolum per semen mulieris.
units.tr: That the promise is not of a common thing but of the greatest. Show (1) from the words, the seed of the woman, as if to say: not of a man, not merely of a human being. (2) From the aim: God wishes by this consolation to raise up the parents and their posterity against the threat and the sense of death. I will put enmity, etc.; it shall crush the head, etc., as if to say: I will punish the Devil through the seed of the woman.

units.la: Propositio. Est ergo promissio de Christo liberatore à peccato morte & tyrannide serpentis, moriturq [?] pro genere humano, & reconciliaturo illud Deo, &c. Semen mulieris Christus.
units.tr: Proposition. The promise, therefore, is concerning Christ the deliverer from sin, death and the tyranny of the serpent, who will die for the human race and reconcile it to God, etc. The seed of the woman is Christ.

units.la: Confirmatio 1. Quia contritio ista capitis serpentis est destructio regni ac potentiæ Satanæ, & generis humani liberatio. Qui regnum Satanæ destruxit, est illud semen promissum. Christus hoc fecit. Ergo, &c. Explicetur ratio metaphoræ: Robur serpentis est in capite. Hæc autem fieri debuit per eum, per quem facta est, nempe Christum. Hebr. 2. Vt per mortem, &c. 1. Ioh. 3. Ad hoc patefactus est Filius Dei, &c.
units.tr: Confirmation (1). Because that crushing of the serpent's head is the destruction of the kingdom and power of Satan and the liberation of the human race. He who destroyed the kingdom of Satan is that promised seed. Christ did this. Therefore, etc. Let the reason of the metaphor be explained: the strength of the serpent lies in its head. Now this had to be done through him through whom it was done, namely Christ. Heb. 2: That through death, etc. 1 John 3: For this purpose the Son of God was made manifest, etc.

units.la: 11. Semen promissum Abrahamo & Davidi est Christus: Recitentur promissiones: & exponantur de Christo ex Gal. 3. Hoc idem est semen mulieris.
units.tr: (2) The seed promised to Abraham and David is Christ. Let the promises be recited, and expounded concerning Christ from Gal. 3. This is the same as the seed of the woman.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia eadem est promissio, declarata & restricta, &c.
units.tr: Reason (1): because it is the same promise, declared and restricted, etc.

units.la: 2. quia conterere caput serpentis, & benedicere omnes gentes est eiusdem feminis.
units.tr: (2) because to crush the head of the serpent and to bless all nations belongs to the same seed.

units.la: 111. Mediator fuit & agnitus est in Ecclesia ab initio.
units.tr: (3) The Mediator was and was acknowledged in the Church from the beginning.

units.la: Ratio: quia Ecclesia non est sine fide Media-toris. Ideo Christus heri, & hodie: Agnus macta-tus ab origine.
units.tr: Reason: because the Church is not without faith in the Mediator. Therefore "Christ yesterday and today," "the Lamb slain from the beginning."

units.la: At nulla est antiquior promissio gratiæ. Ergo hæc promittit Christum.
units.tr: But there is no older promise of grace. Therefore this promises Christ.

units.la: IV. Iudæi veteres interpretantur promissio-nem de Christo. Recitentur verba Thargum Hierosolymitani: Quandiu ô [?] serpens, filii mulieris observant legem, inferunt illi tibi mortem: contrà, ubi illam derelinquunt, tu pungis calcaneum, & valde nocere potes: Sed cum tuo vulneri nullum adsit remedium: remedium certe illi certum & paratum est, quia in fine dierum conterent te calce per Chri-stum seu Messiam Regem suum. Docent ergo, promitti liberationem a spirituali morsu & veneno serpentis, hoc est, a peccato & morte æter-na per Christum.
units.tr: (4) The ancient Jews interpret the promise of Christ. Let the words of the Jerusalem Targum be recited: As long as, O serpent, the sons of the woman keep the law, they inflict death upon you; on the contrary, when they abandon it, you sting the heel and can do great harm: but since there is no remedy for your wound, there is certainly a remedy for them, sure and ready, because at the end of days they will crush you with the heel through Christ or the Messiah, their King. They teach, therefore, that deliverance is promised from the spiritual bite and poison of the serpent, that is, from sin and eternal death through Christ.

units.la: Obiect. Ergo falsa & impia interpretatio Chry-sostomi homil. 17. in Genes. Item Calvini: Semen mulieris esse posteritatem mulieris:
units.tr: Objection. Therefore the interpretation of Chrysostom, homily 17 on Genesis, is false and impious; likewise that of Calvin: that the seed of the woman is the posterity of the woman.

units.la: Resp. Non falsa: quia etiam analoga verbis: cū semen mulieris collective intelligitur sicut semē serpentis, de progenie. Inter semen tuum, & semen mulieris, &c. Nec impia: quia Christus minimè excluditur cum victoria de Satana tribui-tur toti Ecclesiæ per caput Christum.
units.tr: Answer. Not false, because it is also analogous to the words: when the seed of the woman is understood collectively, just as the seed of the serpent, of the progeny. Between your seed and the seed of the woman, etc. Nor is it impious, because Christ is in no way excluded, since the victory over Satan is attributed to the whole Church through Christ the Head.

units.la: Digressiuncula: Iniuriâ proscindi à malevolis Calvinum, quod esse promissionem de Christo neget, inimicitias ad homines & serpentes exter-nos restringat.
units.tr: Digression: Calvin is unjustly torn apart by malicious men, because they say he denies that it is a promise concerning Christ, and restricts the enmity to external men and serpents.

units.la: Ratio: Truncant eius sententias per manife-stam calumniam.
units.tr: Reason: They mangle his opinions through a manifest calumny.

units.la: Ostende seriem interpretationis eius.
units.tr: Ostende seriem interpretationis eius.

units.la: 1. Inimicitias à Deo positas simpliciter inter-pretatur, hostile semper fore dissidium humano generi cum serpentibus, quale hodie cernitur.
units.tr: 1. He interprets the enmities set by God simply: there will always be a hostile division between the human race and the serpents, such as is seen today.

units.la: 2. Transit à serpente ad ipsum maleficii authorem Satanam: quia, inquit, non ita evomuit iram suam Deus in externum organum, ut Diabolo parceret, penes quem residebat tota culpa. Nec ser-pentis, sed hominum causa locutus est Dominus. Et mox: Quare ut collapsos hominum animos erigeret Deus, necesse fuit victoriam de Satana, cuius insidiis perierant, in posterum illis promitti. Constituo itaq; Deum sub nomine serpentis Satanam maxime hic petere, & in eum stringere judicii sui fulmen: quod facit duplici de causa 1. ut sibi cavere homines à Satana discant, tanquam ab hoste mortifero. 2. ut certa vincendi fiducia cum eo præliantur [?].
units.tr: 2. He passes from the serpent to Satan himself, the author of the mischief: "because," he says, "God did not so pour out his wrath upon the external instrument as to spare the Devil, in whom all the guilt resided. Nor did the Lord speak for the sake of the serpent, but for the sake of men." And soon after: "Therefore, in order to raise up the fallen minds of men, God had to promise them victory over Satan, by whose snares they had perished. I hold, then, that God here chiefly aims at Satan under the name of the serpent, and hurls the thunderbolt of his judgment against him, which he does for two reasons: (1) that men may learn to beware of Satan as of a deadly enemy; (2) that they may fight against him with a certain confidence of victory [?]."

units.la: 3. De sensu verborum sequentium: Ipsum-vulnerabit, &c. ait sibi non convenire cum aliis. Recitetur eius verba: In verbis quidem Mosis, &c. usque: Interpretor de posteris: Hic blasphemias clamant. Sed addant quæso [?] rationes sententiæ, quas addit. Sequentia enim truncant: Sed cum-experientia, &c. recita usque: Sub pedibus vestris.
units.tr: 3. On the sense of the following words, "Ipsum-vulnerabit, etc.", he says they do not agree with the others. Let his words be quoted: "In the words of Moses, etc., down to: I interpret of the descendants." Here they cry out blasphemies! But let them please add the reasons for the opinion which he adds. For they cut off what follows: "But when-experience, etc.," quote down to: "under your feet."

units.la: Instantia: Eludit evidentissima oracula de Christo: pro Judæis, Arianis, contra Ecclesiam, Patres, &c. Resp. Negatur quod eludat, quod e-videtissima, &c. Adde duo exempla [illegible, ~8 letters] significare unitatem essentiæ, & Trinitatem personarum: dicit parum solidam hanc tantæ rei sibi videri probationem. Item. Gen. 4. Possedi virum Jehovam: reddit, à Jehova, &c. Quid ergo? Hæc
units.tr: Objection: He mocks the most evident oracles about Christ, in favour of the Jews and Arians, against the Church, the Fathers, etc. Reply: It is denied that he mocks them; that they are most evident, etc. Add two examples [illegible, ~8 letters] to signify the unity of essence and the Trinity of persons. He says this proof seems to him not very solid for so great a matter. Likewise, on Genesis 4: "I have gotten a man, the LORD": he renders it "from the LORD, etc." What then? These things

units.la: & alia nonnulla à Patribus contra hæreticos ad-hibita non simpliciter approbans, an erit hæreti-cus, Arianus, Iudæus? Calumnia gravis. 1. quia constat acerrimum fuisse Trinitatis & æternæ Christi Deitatis assertorem. 11. Possunt infini-ta oraculorum exempla proferri, quæ de Christo firmiter interpretantur. 111. Expertus in con-gressibus cum hæreticis, Servetó, Gentile, &c, quæ valida, quæ secus essent, pondere non nume-ro certandum docet contra hæreticos, multo, quam veteres illi fuerint, argutiores. 1v. Spiri-tus Prophetarum sunt subiecti Prophetis. Scri-psit ergo non præscripsit suas sententias Ecclesiæ eximius ille Dei servus:
units.tr: and some other things brought forward against the heretics from the Fathers, not simply approving them, will he be a heretic, an Arian, a Jew? A grave calumny. 1. Because it is established that he was a most fierce defender of the Trinity and of the eternal Deity of Christ. 2. Countless examples of oracles can be brought forward which firmly interpret him concerning Christ. 3. Having experience in encounters with heretics, Servetus, Gentile, etc., he teaches that what is strong and what would be otherwise must be contended with by weight, not by number, against heretics, being much sharper than those ancient writers were. 4. The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets. That eminent servant of God, therefore, wrote his opinions and did not prescribe them to the Church:

units.la: Præcisio. Sed longius excurri: nunc dicam: Quale sit semen, &c.
units.tr: Precision. But I have run on too long: now I will say: "What sort of seed, etc."

units.la: 1. Homo verus, quia semen mulieris de substantia mulieris.
units.tr: 1. A true man, because the seed of the woman is of the substance of the woman.

units.la: Item: Semen Abrahami: Davidis: fructus lumborum Davidis.
units.tr: Likewise: the seed of Abraham; of David; the fruit of David's loins.

units.la: Sic angelus: Benedictus fructus ventris tui.
units.tr: So the angel: "Blessed is the fruit of your womb."

units.la: Confirma ratione: quia verum hominem oportuit lucere culpam generis humani. Sicut per unius hominis inobedientiam: Per hominem mors, & per hominem resurrectio.
units.tr: Confirmation by reason: because it was necessary that a true man should atone for the guilt of the human race. "As by the disobedience of one man ... By a man came death, and by a man the resurrection."

units.la: Reiciantur Marcionitæ, Manichæi, Apollinaris, Eutyches, &c.
units.tr: Let there be rejected the Marcionites, the Manichaeans, Apollinaris, Eutyches, etc.

units.la: Refutentur Anabaptistæ, facientes Christum illud μεταξὺ[?] inter serpentem & mulierem, hoc est, nec serpentis nec mulieris semen, sed tertiam naturam, &c.
units.tr: Let there be refuted the Anabaptists, who make Christ that intermediate [?] between the serpent and the woman, that is, neither the seed of the serpent nor of the woman, but a third nature, etc.

units.la: Resp. 1. ab absurdo: Sic Christus esset ipsa ini-micitia. micitia inter utrunque posita.
units.tr: Answer. (1) From the absurdity: thus Christ would be enmity itself, placed between both.

units.la: 2. Relativum הוּא ipsum non nisi ad semen referri potest.
units.tr: (2) The relative הוּא, he himself, can only be referred to the seed.

units.la: 3. Scriptura veram humanitatem Christo tribuit. Hebr. 2. Factus est carnis & sanguinis particeps μετέσχηκεν[?]: Assumsit semen Abrahæ, &c.
units.tr: (3) Scripture ascribes true humanity to Christ. Heb. 2: "He was made a partaker of flesh and blood" [μετέσχηκεν]; "He took on the seed of Abraham," etc.

units.la: ii. Non modo verus homo, sed & perfecte justus.
units.tr: ii. He is not only a true man, but also perfectly just.

units.la: Ratio. Semen mulieris, hoc est, Virginis Is.7. Virgo concipiet: Gal.4. Factum ex muliere. Luc.1. Conceptus de Spiritu Sancto. Miraculosa ergo conceptio, & semen virginis purum promittitur.
units.tr: Reason. The seed of the woman, that is, of the Virgin: Is. 7: "A virgin shall conceive." Gal. 4: "Made of a woman." Luke 1: "Conceived of the Holy Spirit." A miraculous conception and a pure seed of a virgin are therefore promised.

units.la: Addatur ratio: ex Hebr.7. Talis nobis conveniebat pontifex.
units.tr: Add the reason: from Heb. 7: "Such a high priest was fitting for us."

units.la: iii. Idem verus Deus. Ratio: Conteret caput serpentis antiqui, quod est solius Dei. Rom. 16. ver.20.
units.tr: iii. Likewise true God. Reason: "He shall crush the head of the ancient serpent," which belongs to God alone. Rom. 16, verse 20.

units.la: Subiiciantur alia Testimonia Deitatis Messiæ ex vetere Testamento.
units.tr: Let other testimonies to the Deity of the Messiah from the Old Testament be added.

units.la: 1. Is.7. Erit Immanuel: Deus nobiscum, seu inter nos: Explica per illud: Verbum caro factum habitavit in nobis. Et. Deus manifestatus in carne.
units.tr: 1. Is. 7: "Immanuel shall be": God with us, or among us. Explain it by that passage: "The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us." And: "God manifested in the flesh."

units.la: 2. Iesa.9. Deus fortis, Pater æternitatis.
units.tr: 2. Isa. 9: "Mighty God, Father of eternity."

units.la: 3. Ierem.23. Germen justum Davidis, hoc est, Messias (Chaldæus interpres sic reddit Is.4. & hoc loco) Vocabitur Jehova justitia nostra.
units.tr: 3. Jer. 23: "The righteous Branch of David," that is, the Messiah (the Chaldee interpreter renders it thus in Is. 4 and in this place): "Jehovah shall be called our righteousness."

units.la: 4. Psal.110. Messias Dominus Davidis Regis. Ergo Deus: quia David præter Deum non habuit Dominum: interprete Christo Matth.22.
units.tr: 4. Ps. 110: the Messiah is the Lord of King David. Therefore God: because David had no Lord besides God; Christ is the interpreter, Matt. 22.

units.la: 5. Dan.9. Exaudi propter Dominum למען אדני[?]
units.tr: 5. Dan. 9: "Hear for the sake of the Lord" [למען אדני].

units.la: 6. Galatinus ex Is.53.4. probat Messiæ Deitatem: Vidimus Messiam ut percussum à Deo & humihumiliatum. Ipse: Vidimus ut percussum Deum: Quia Hebraei legūt מכה אלהים per Segol. Percussum Deum: absolutè: non construct̀ per tseri מכה אלהים Percussum Dei: neq; מכה מאלהים Percussum à Deo. Absolutè etiam legit editio Regia.
units.tr: 6. Galatinus, from Is. 53:4, proves the Deity of the Messiah: "We saw the Messiah as smitten by God and humbled." He himself: "We saw God as smitten": because the Hebrews read מכה אלהים with a segol, God smitten, absolutely; not in the construct with a tsere, מכה אלהים, smitten of God, nor מכה מאלהים, smitten by God. The Royal edition also reads it absolutely.

units.la: Praecisio: Longiore recitatione supersedeo, qa haec ludaeis & haereticis convincendis sufficiunt.
units.tr: Restriction: I forgo a longer recitation, since these things are sufficient for convincing the Jews and heretics.

units.la: Colligē breviter quid dixeris: & adde μεσι[?]α- τα duo.
units.tr: Gather briefly what you have said, and add two intermediate points [μεσι[?]α-].

units.la: 1. Cum hæc promissio de Christo Vero Deo & homine sit data parentibus in Paradiso: ergo jam inde fuit Ecclesia aliqua, amplectens fidem de Christo venturo θεανθρώπῳ[?], liberaturo ipsam à tyrannide Satanæ: & hac fide servati sunt Patres Heb.13. Christus heri & hodie: Act.15. Credimus nos servari gratia Christi, sicut & Patres.
units.tr: 1. Since this promise about Christ, true God and man, was given to our parents in Paradise, therefore from that time there was already some Church, embracing faith in the coming God-man [θεανθρώπῳ], who would deliver it from the tyranny of Satan; and by this faith the Fathers were saved. Heb. 13: "Christ, yesterday and today." Acts 15: "We believe that we are saved by the grace of Christ, just as the Fathers were."

units.la: II. Deducatur ex priore: Cum hæc promissio sit ipsissima vox Evangelii de Christi victoria contra Satanam, peccatum, mortem, &c. Ergo Evangelium nostrum est doctrina antiquissima: eoque verissima. Rom.1. Tertullianus: Illud dominicum & verum, quod prius traditum. Contra calumnias de novitate Evangelii.
units.tr: II. Deduce from the former: since this promise is the very voice of the Gospel concerning Christ's victory over Satan, sin, death, etc., therefore our Gospel is the most ancient doctrine, and thereby the most true. Rom. 1. Tertullian: "That which is Lord's and true is that which was handed down first." Against the calumnies about the novelty of the Gospel.

units.la: II. An sit exhibitum.
units.tr: II. Whether it was delivered (exhibitum).

units.la: Fiat connexio: Dic duo hic quæri: an semen mulieris venerit & contriverit caput serpentis? Et an hoc semen sit Iesus ille Dei ac Mariæ filius, crucifixus pro nobis ac resuscitatus.
units.tr: Connection: Let me state that two things are asked here: whether the seed of the woman has come and crushed the head of the serpent; and whether this seed is that Jesus, son of God and Mary, crucified for us and raised again.

units.la: Utrumque contra Iudæos, Mahumedanos, &c. recte nos Christianos credere demonstrabo.
units.tr: I will show that we Christians rightly believe both, against the Jews, the Mahometans, etc.

units.la: Quod sit exhibitum: Ratio una: Tempus exhibitionis a Deo destinatum, & oraculis prophetarum definitum praeteriit: Ergo necesse est fateantur Messiam venisse: aut vanitatis accusent Deum & prophetas. Antecedens probetur.
units.tr: That it has been delivered: Reason one: the time of delivery appointed by God and defined by the oracles of the prophets has passed. Therefore they must either admit that the Messiah has come, or accuse God and the prophets of falsehood. The antecedent is to be proved.

units.la: 1. Gen. 49: Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, donec veniat Silo. Sensus oraculi: Sub idem tempus concidet regnum Judaicum, & veniet Messias: qui dicitur שילה [?] h.e, Filius eius nempe, Judæ κατ' ἐξοχὴν [?].
units.tr: 1. Gen. 49: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, until Shiloh come. The sense of the oracle: at about the same time the Jewish kingdom will fall, and the Messiah will come, who is called שילה [?], that is, his son namely, of Judah, par excellence [?].

units.la: Obiectio Judæorum, שילה [?] faciunt nomen urbis in tribu Ephraim Jud. 21. hoc sensu: Non veniet finis Siloh, donec Saul eligatur in regem in Siloh. Alii igitur de Saule, alii de Jeroboamo rege eligendo in Siloh dictum volunt. Alii etiam de Nebucadnezare misso ad delendum templum & urbem: quasi sit שילה [?] missus & mittendus, ut habet vetus latina:
units.tr: Objection of the Jews: שילה [?] makes the name of a town in the tribe of Ephraim (Judg. 21), in this sense: the end of Shiloh will not come until Saul is chosen king in Shiloh. Others therefore want it said of Saul, others of Jeroboam being chosen king in Shiloh. Others again of Nebuchadnezzar, sent to destroy the temple and the city, as if שילה [?] meant sent and to be sent, as the Old Latin has it:

units.la: Resp. corrumpunt textum & historias.
units.tr: Reply: they corrupt the text and the histories.

units.la: 1. quia in electione Saulis Juda nondum habuerat sceptrum:
units.tr: 1. because at the election of Saul Judah had not yet had the sceptre;

units.la: 2. per Jeroboamum sceptrum non est plane ablatum à Juda.
units.tr: 2. under Jeroboam the sceptre was not clearly taken away from Judah.

units.la: 3. quia in captivitate, & postea mansit aliquod ἀξίωμα [?] sceptri in Juda, h.e. posteris Davidis: Duces: Sanhedrin magnum: etsi sine titulo regio: quem tamen resumsit Iohannes Hyrcanus filius Simonis Machabæi: iterum vero perdidit nepos ejus Hyrcanus ultimus ab Herode trucidatus.
units.tr: 3. because during the captivity and afterwards some semblance (ἀξίωμα [?]) of the sceptre remained in Judah, that is, among the posterity of David: leaders, the Great Sanhedrin, though without the royal title; which John Hyrcanus, son of Simon the Maccabee, did indeed resume, but which his grandson Hyrcanus the last lost again, being put to death by Herod.

units.la: 4. Chaldæus Paraphrastes & veteres Thalmudistæ sic vertunt: Donec veniat Messias Rex: & exponunt: Principatum non defuturum in Ju-da, donec veniat Christus.
units.tr: 4. The Chaldee paraphrast and the ancient Talmudists render it thus: Until the King Messiah come, and explain: the principate will not fail in Judah until Christ comes.

units.la: Minor: At sceptrum dudum est ablatum à Juda per Herodem Idumaeum & Romanos.
units.tr: Minor premise: But the sceptre was taken away from Judah long ago, by Herod the Idumaean and the Romans.

units.la: Amplific. Ipsa tribus Juda cum aliis confusa est per dispersionem à Tito factam.
units.tr: Amplification: The tribe of Judah itself has been mixed up with the others through the dispersion made by Titus.

units.la: Conclus. Ergo necesse est Siloh jam venisse.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore Shiloh must already have come.

units.la: II. Hagg. 2. Messias debuit venire stante secundo templo. Recitetur oraculum: probetur antecedens tribus rationib.
units.tr: II. Haggai 2. The Messiah had to come while the second temple was standing. Let the oracle be recited; the antecedent is proved by three reasons.

units.la: I. Veniet desiderium gentium, h.e, Christus: sic vocatur etiam in oraculo Jacobi.
units.tr: I. The desire of all nations will come, that is, Christ: he is so called also in the oracle of Jacob.

units.la: 2. Secunda domus gloria major erit quam prio-ris. At externa ne par quidem fuit: Ergo major erit spiritualis, propter Messiam.
units.tr: 2. The glory of the second house will be greater than that of the first. But the external glory was not even equal. Therefore it will be greater in spiritual respects, on account of the Messiah.

units.la: 3. In loco isto dabo pacem. Christus autem pax nostra. Eph.2.
units.tr: 3. In this place I will give peace. But Christ is our peace (Eph. 2).

units.la: Conclus. Eversa templo secundo, patet tempus Messiæ præteriisse. Amplif. à consensu Malach.3: Statim veniet Dominator.
units.tr: Conclusion: With the second temple overthrown, it is plain that the time of the Messiah has passed. Amplification: from the agreement of Malachi 3: The Ruler will come suddenly.

units.la: III. Dan.9. Ab exitu sermonis usque ad Chri-stum Ducem, &c. undecunque numerentur LXX septimanæ, h.e, anni 490. ab exitu sermonis (h.e, sive à primo anno Cyri, ut oportet, sive à secundo vel septimo Longimani) finis incidit in tempora Augusti vel Tyberii. Ergo tempus venturi, & passuri Messiæ pro peccatis nostris, (testante Daniele) elapsum est.
units.tr: III. Dan. 9: From the going forth of the word until Christ the Prince, etc. Whatever point the seventy weeks are counted from, that is, 490 years, from the going forth of the word (that is, either from the first year of Cyrus, as is proper, or from the second or seventh of Artaxerxes Longimanus), the end falls in the times of Augustus or Tiberius. Therefore the time of the Messiah who is to come and suffer for our sins (as Daniel attests) has elapsed.

units.la: Pracisio: Hæc oracula sufficiant, &c.
units.tr: Pause: Let these oracles suffice, etc.

units.la: Transitio: Deploranda cæcitas Judæorum ora-cula tam manifesta depravantium. Sed nūc etiam demonstremus alterum.
units.tr: Transition: Deplorable is the blindness of the Jews, who distort oracles so clear. But now let us also demonstrate the second point.

units.la: II. Quod Iesus sit[?] semen mulieris promissum.
units.tr: II. That Jesus is the seed of the woman promised.

units.la: Probatio sit unicum argumentum cum prosyl-log. Quia in Iesu nostro, Dei ac Mariæ filio, omnia prophetarum oracula, de Messiæ persona, familia: parentibus: tempore: loco natali: do-ctrina, miraculis, morte resurrectione & benefi-ciis impleta sunt. [?]Addatur major: & subjiciatur minoris probatio per partes singulas: ac ponantur primo oracula: deinde ostendatur impletio.
units.tr: Proof shall be a single argument with a prosyllogism. Because in our Jesus, son of God and Mary, all the oracles of the prophets concerning the person of the Messiah, his family, parents, time, birthplace, teaching, miracles, death, resurrection and benefits, have been fulfilled. Let the major premise be added, and the proof of the minor premise be set out part by part: let the oracles be placed first, then the fulfilment shown.

units.la: 1. Persona. Debuit esse verus Deus: Gen.3. Conteret caput serp. Ief.7. Emmanuel. Ief.9. Deus fortis. Ier.23. Iehova iustitia nostra.
units.tr: 1. Person. He had to be true God: Gen. 3: He shall crush the head of the serpent. Isa. 7: Immanuel. Isa. 9: Mighty God. Jer. 23: Jehovah our righteousness.

units.la: Et verus atque iustus homo ex virgine semen mulieris. Ecce virgo, servus meus iustus.
units.tr: And a true and righteous man, born of a virgin, the seed of the woman. Behold the virgin, my righteous servant.

units.la: Talis vero solus Christus Iesus, Roman.cap. 9. Deus benedictus. 1.Iohan.cap.5. Hic est verus Deus: Fructus ventris tui: Hebr. 2. Particeps carnis & sanguinis. Assumsit semen Abrahæ. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: Such a one indeed is Christ Jesus alone: Rom. 9: God blessed. 1 John 5: This is the true God. Luke 1: The fruit of your womb. Heb. 2: Partaker of flesh and blood. He took on the seed of Abraham. Therefore, etc.

units.la: II. Familia: Tribus Iuda: stirps Davidis. Gen.49. Donec venerit Schilo, filius eius. Ief.11. Stirps Iesse virgam produxit.
units.tr: II. Family: the tribe of Judah, the stock of David. Gen. 49: Until Shiloh come, his son. Isa. 11: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse.

units.la: Hinc Messias passim David: filius Davidis, &c.
units.tr: Hence the Messiah is everywhere called David, son of David, etc.

units.la: Impletio: Iesus filius Mariæ filiæ Davidis, Luc.2: Ex semine Davidis secundum carnem. Rom.1. Vicit leo Iuda. Apoc.5.
units.tr: Fulfilment: Jesus, son of Mary, daughter of David: Luke 2: According to the flesh, of the seed of David. Rom. 1. The Lion of the tribe of Judah has prevailed. Rev. 5.

units.la: III. Parentes. Mater virgo, ignara viri: quia Messias tantum mulieris non etiam viri semen. Ief.7. virgo concipiet.
units.tr: III. Parents. A virgin mother, not knowing a man: because the Messiah was to be the seed of a woman alone, not also of a man. Isa. 7: A virgin shall conceive.

units.la: Obiectio: Non virgo: sed juvencula nova nupta. Respon. העלמה[?] significat virginem a latendo. Item:
units.tr: Objection: not a virgin, but a young woman newly married. Reply: העלמה [?] means a virgin, from concealing (latendo). Likewise:

units.la: Item:Partus virginis datur in signum. Ergo miraculosus.
units.tr: Likewise: the birth of a virgin is given as a sign. Therefore it is miraculous.

units.la: Impletio: Iosephus pater Iesu putatitius: Maria mater virgo nupta quidem, sed viro non cognita, gravida ex Spiritu sancto, Matth. 1. Luc. 1.
units.tr: Fulfilment: Joseph was the supposed father of Jesus; Mary his mother was a virgin, indeed married, but not known by a man, pregnant by the Holy Spirit (Matt. 1; Luke 1).

units.la: IV. Tempus: Excidium regni Iudaici totale: dissipatio tribuum. Gen. 49. Ezech. 21. Obliquam obliquam, &c.
units.tr: IV. Time: the total destruction of the Jewish kingdom and the dispersion of the tribes. Gen. 49; Ezek. 21: Overturn, overturn, etc.

units.la: Impletio: Iesus natus anno Herodis Idumæi XXXII. quo Iudæi imperio ejus sponte submiserunt: Item Augusti Imp. Romani XLII. cui Iudæa tum erat tributaria. Luc. 2. Exiit edictum: Item elapsis inde ab exitu edicti Cyri LXX. septimanis Danielis. Annis 490.
units.tr: Fulfilment: Jesus was born in the thirty-second year of Herod the Idumaean, when the Jews had of their own accord submitted to his rule; likewise in the forty-second year of Augustus, the Roman emperor, to whom Judea was then tributary (Luke 2: A decree went out). Likewise, with the seventy weeks of Daniel counted from the going out of the decree of Cyrus: 490 years.

units.la: V. Locus: Bethlehem: Mich. 5: Ex te egredietur: Et Matth. 2. Scribę oraculum approbant Herodi. Et Ioh. 7. Ex vico Bethlehem, &c.
units.tr: V. Place: Bethlehem: Mic. 5: Out of you shall come forth; and Matt. 2: the scribes approve the oracle to Herod; and John 7: From the village of Bethlehem, etc.

units.la: Impletio. Iesus nascitur in Bethlehem civitate Davidis. Luc. 2.
units.tr: Fulfilment: Jesus is born in Bethlehem, the city of David (Luke 2).

units.la: Doctrina: Isai. 6. Jehova unxit me ad evangelizandum, &c. Et Isai. 42. Servus meus non vociferabitur: judicium annunciabit gentibus, &c.
units.tr: Teaching: Isa. 61 (6 in the text): The Lord has anointed me to preach the gospel, etc. And Isa. 42: My servant will not cry out; he will announce judgment to the nations, etc.

units.la: Impletio: Matth. 12: 17. Item: Venite ad me omnes: veni ad quaerendas oves perditas Israelis: Credite Evangelio, agite poenitentiam.
units.tr: Fulfilment: Matt. 12:17. Likewise: Come to me all of you; I came to seek the lost sheep of Israel. Believe the gospel, repent.

units.la: VI. Miracula. Isai 35. Tunc aperient oculi caecorum, &c.
units.tr: VI. Miracles. Isa. 35: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, etc.

units.la: Impletio: Iesus sanavit omnes morbos Matt. 8. & 11. Ite annunciate Iohanni quae videtis. Item confessio turbae Ioh. 7. Christus cum venerit.
units.tr: Fulfilment: Jesus healed all diseases (Matt. 8 and 11: Go and report to John what you see). Likewise the confession of the crowd (John 7: When the Christ comes).

units.la: VII. Mors. Gen. 3. Serpens mordebit ei calcaneum. Isai. 53. pingitur Messię[?] humilitas, passio & mors propter peccata nostra, quasi propheta coram intuitus esset singula: Excerpantur evidentiora. Item mactatio victimarum: & Agni Paschalis, &c. Ps.22. Diviserunt vestimenta.
units.tr: VII. Death. Gen. 3: The serpent will bite his heel. Isa. 53 portrays the humility, passion and death of the Messiah for our sins, as if the prophet had looked on each detail: let the more evident passages be excerpted. Likewise the slaughter of the victims and of the Paschal Lamb, etc. Ps. 22: They divided my garments.

units.la: Impletio: Iesus in summa humilitate natus: à Iudæis militibus dirissima passus, à Pilato innocës damnatus: crucifixus mortuus ac sepultus est, propter peccata nostra. Rom.4.
units.tr: Fulfilment: Jesus, born in the utmost humility, suffered the most cruel treatment from the Jewish soldiers, was condemned innocent by Pilate, was crucified, died and was buried, for our sins (Rom. 4).

units.la: VIII. Resurrectio: Gen. 3: Conteret caput serpentis. Ps.16. Non permittes sanctum tuum videre corruptionem. Is.9. Pater æternitatis, Regni ejus non erit finis. Et 53. Ex judicio ereptus est: semen eius quis enarrabit, &c.
units.tr: VIII. Resurrection: Gen. 3: He shall crush the head of the serpent. Ps. 16: You will not allow your holy one to see corruption. Isa. 9: Father of eternity; of his kingdom there will be no end. And Isa. 53: He was taken away from judgment; who will declare his seed, etc.

units.la: Impletio: Matt.20. Filius hominis trucidabitur & resurget. Matth.28. Surrexit: non est hic. Heb.8. Eph.1. Ascendit: sedet in throno majestatis in cælo.
units.tr: Fulfilment: Matt. 20: the Son of Man will be put to death and will rise. Matt. 28: He is risen; he is not here. Heb. 8; Eph. 1: He ascended; he sits on the throne of majesty in heaven.

units.la: IX. Gen.3. Conteret caput serpentis. Gen.22. In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes. Dan.9. Obsignabit peccata: adducet æternam justitiam. Is.53: Livore ejus sanati sumus.
units.tr: IX. Gen. 3: He shall crush the head of the serpent. Gen. 22: In your seed all the nations will be blessed. Dan. 9: He will seal up sins, he will bring everlasting righteousness. Isa. 53: By his stripes we are healed.

units.la: Impletio: 1.Ioh.3. Vt destruat opera Diaboli. Gal.4: Factus est exsecratio: ut nos, &c. 1.Ioh.1. Sanguis I.C. mundat nos. 1.Cor.1. Factus est nobis, &c. Rom.4. Mortuus propter peccata, &c.
units.tr: Fulfilment: 1 John 3: That he might destroy the works of the devil. Gal. 3 (4 in the text): He was made a curse, that we, etc. 1 John 1: The blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us. 1 Cor. 1: He was made to us, etc. Rom. 4: He was put to death for our sins, etc.

units.la: Concludatur demonstratio tota: Cum omnia congruant: certa igitur fides Christiana: exhibitum jam esse semen mulieris promissum in Iesu Christo Dei & Mariæ Filio:
units.tr: Let the whole demonstration be concluded: since all things agree, the Christian faith is certain: that the promised seed of the woman has now indeed been delivered in Jesus Christ, son of God and Mary.

units.la: III. Ad
units.tr: III. Whether (Ad)

units.la: III. Ad quid sit promissum & exhibitum.
units.tr: III. On what end the promise was given and fulfilled.

units.la: Propositio i. Promissio Evangelica de semine parentib. data est ut eos, eorumq; posteros erigeret à desperatione: confirmaret de venia: de reconciliatione cum Deo propter Messiam.
units.tr: Proposition 1. The evangelical promise concerning the Seed was given to our parents so as to raise them up from despair, to confirm them regarding pardon and reconciliation with God on account of the Messiah.

units.la: Probetur, ab effectu: Ideo fide sacrificarunt & placuerunt patres. Heb.11. ob.8. Abraham cupi-vit videre diem meum: & gavisus est, &c.
units.tr: Proof from the effect: Therefore by faith the fathers offered sacrifices and pleased God. Heb. 11. Verse 8: Abraham desired to see my day, and he rejoiced, etc.

units.la: II. Exhibitum vero est semen: ut caput serpentis contereret, & fidem atque spem Patrum expleret: Textus: Ipsum conteret, &c.
units.tr: II. The Seed was indeed exhibited, that he might bruise the head of the serpent and fulfil the faith and hope of the Fathers. Text: He shall bruise him, etc.

units.la: Subjiciatur ἔκθεσις[?]; distincte ostendens: quod sit illud caput serpentis, & quomodo Christus cō-triverit.
units.tr: Let an exposition be added, showing distinctly what that head of the serpent is, and how Christ bruised it.

units.la: Caput serpentis, h. e, potentia & tyrannis Dia-boli: est
units.tr: The head of the serpent, that is, the power and tyranny of the Devil, is:

units.la: I. Servitus peccati, in quam humanum genus subegit per lapsum, Rom.6. Cum effetis servi peccati. 2.Tim.2. Infideles tenentur captivi laqueo Satanae. Eph.2. Agit in filiis contumacia.
units.tr: I. The servitude of sin, into which the human race was brought by the fall. Rom. 6. When you were servants of sin. 2 Tim. 2. Unbelievers are held captive in the snare of Satan. Eph. 2. He works in the sons of disobedience.

units.la: II. Mors corporalis & aeterna. Heb.2. Diabolus habet imperium mortis. Rom.6. Stipendium peccati mors. Rom.5. Per peccatum mors, &c.
units.tr: II. Bodily and eternal death. Heb. 2. The Devil holds the power of death. Rom. 6. The wages of sin is death. Rom. 5. By sin, death, etc.

units.la: III. Ira Dei & maledictio aeterna. Eph.5. Propter hac venit ira Dei in filios contumacia. Matt.25. Ite maledicti, &c.
units.tr: III. The wrath of God and eternal curse. Eph. 5. On account of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Matt. 25. Depart, you cursed, etc.

units.la: Hoc caput Christus contrivit dupliciter:
units.tr: Christ bruised this head in two ways:

units.la: 1. Merito mortis: qua peccata expiavit: mortem abolevit: maledictionem sustulit: ac nos Deo perfectè reconciliavit. Ostendatur dictis[?]. Sangnis Jesu Christi, &c. Mortuus est propter, &c. Heb. 2. 2. Ut per mortem, &c. Rom. 8. Nulla condemnatio iis, &c. Gal. 3. Factus maledictio, &c.
units.tr: 1. By the merit of his death, by which he expiated sins, abolished death, removed the curse, and fully reconciled us to God. Let it be shown from the words: The blood of Jesus Christ, etc. He died for, etc. Heb. 2. Verse 2: That through death, etc. Rom. 8. There is no condemnation for those who, etc. Gal. 3. Made a curse, etc.

units.la: I 1. Efficacia resurrectionis & Spiritus sui: quo nqs[?] sanꝛa[?] à morsu serpentis, naturam instaurat, regenerat, vivificat, sanctificat & glorificat. Osten datur ex Rom. 6. & aliis locis.
units.tr: 1. By the efficacy of his resurrection and of his Spirit, by which he heals from the bite of the serpent, restores nature, regenerates, quickens, sanctifies and glorifies. It is shown from Rom. 6 and other passages.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Textus habet. Ipsa nempe mulier: h.e, Maria: conteret caput serpentis. Ergo nō Christus : semen mulieris.
units.tr: Objection 1. The text has: She, namely the woman, that is, Mary, shall bruise the head of the serpent. Therefore not Christ, the seed of the woman.

units.la: Resp. Negatur antecéd. quia latina versio corrupta: Textus Hebr. habet הוא[?] ipse, non הוא[?] vel ut vult Bellarmin. הוא[?] ipsa.
units.tr: Answer. The antecedent is denied, because the Latin version is corrupt. The Hebrew text has הוא he, not הוא or, as Bellarmine wishes, היא she.

units.la: Probetur masculinum relativum ex verbo & affixo masculino תשופנו[?] conteret ei, quod non potest cum masculino זרע[?] semen construi: non cum fœm. היא[?] &c.
units.tr: The masculine relative is proved from the verb and the masculine suffix תשופנו he shall bruise him, which cannot be construed with the masculine זרע seed, nor with the feminine היא, etc.

units.la: Instantia I Hebraei sæpe confundunt genera.
units.tr: Instance 1. The Hebrews often confuse the genders.

units.la: Resp. Hæc factum esse probari non potest: & obstat affixum verbi masculinum.
units.tr: Answer. That this happened here cannot be proved, and the masculine suffix of the verb stands in the way.

units.la: Instantia II. Augustinus, Ambros. Chrysost. &c. legunt: ipsa: & intelligunt de Ecclesia. Resp. 1. Ergo non de Maria, ut Papistæ. I 1. Opponimus vetustiores: Thargum Onkelos habet masculinum: inter filium tuum: & filium mulieris. ipse conteret, &c. Sic Thalmudistæ omnes, &c. Sic versio LXX. αὐτὸς σου τηρήσει κεφαλὴν, &c. Sic Irenæus lib. 3. c. 88. & Hieron. in Hebr. quest. super Gen. Sic denique Scriptura: Christus ademit Diabolo imperium. Heb. 2. Ergo non mulier.
units.tr: Instance 2. Augustine, Ambrose, Chrysostom, etc. read she and understand it of the Church. Answer 1. Therefore not of Mary, as the Papists hold. Answer 2. We oppose the older witnesses: the Targum of Onkelos has the masculine: between your seed and the seed of the woman; he shall bruise, etc. So all the Talmudists, etc. So the version of the Seventy: αὐτὸς σου τηρήσει κεφαλήν, etc. So Irenaeus, book 3, chapter 88, and Jerome in the Hebrew questions on Genesis. Finally Scripture itself: Christ took away from the Devil his dominion. Heb. 2. Therefore not the woman.

units.la: Obiectio I 1. Diabolus circumit, ut leo rugiens.1.Pet.5.Agit in filiis contumacia. Eph.2.2. Tim. 2.Ergo non est contritus.
units.tr: Objection 1. The Devil goes about like a roaring lion. 1 Pet. 5. He works in the sons of disobedience. Eph. 2. 2 Tim. 2. Therefore he has not been bruised.

units.la: Resp. Contritio non est facta sine morsu calcanei, in capite & membris. Itaq; 1. qui non sunt membra, iis non est contritus, &c. Ioh. 3. Qui non credit super eo manet ira Dei. 2. Membris est contritus, quo ad condemnationem. Rom. 8. 1. non quo ad luctam, Eph. 6. quæ est morsus calcanei.
units.tr: Answer. The bruising was not done without a bite on the heel, in the head and in the members. Therefore, first, those who are not members, on them he has not been bruised, etc. John 3. He who does not believe, the wrath of God remains upon him. Second, he has been bruised in the members as regards condemnation. Rom. 8. First, not as regards the struggle, Eph. 6, which is the bite on the heel.

units.la: CONCLUSIO colligat πρῆσματα hortatoria.
units.tr: CONCLUSION, drawing exhortatory consequences.

units.la: 1. Cum Deus mox à lapsu promiserit Servatorem: cogitemus de immenso Dei amore & misericordia erga nos, &c.
units.tr: 1. Since God promised a Saviour immediately after the fall, let us consider the immense love and mercy of God towards us, etc.

units.la: II. Cum Patribus promiserit, nobis exhibuerit semen mulieris: agnoscamus præstantiam nostræ conditionis, &c. & grati simus.
units.tr: II. Since he promised the seed of the woman to the Fathers and has exhibited him to us, let us acknowledge the excellence of our condition, etc., and be thankful.

units.la: III. Cum angeli nuncient, nobis esse natum Servatorem: Scriptura clamet, caput Satanæ contritum esse: lætemur, & beneficia fide accipiamus: Captivitas erat miserrima: Liberatio ergo maxima.
units.tr: III. Since the angels announce that a Saviour has been born for us, and Scripture proclaims that the head of Satan has been bruised, let us rejoice and receive the benefits by faith. The captivity was most miserable; the deliverance is therefore most great.

units.la: IV. Cum serpens ita contritus sit, ut calcaneū nostrum petere nondum desinat: vigilemus: & oremus, ad pugnam accincti: ne in tentationibus succumbamus exemplo parentum: Vitemus commercium Satanæ & organorum ejus: foveamus inimicitias positas: Sic tandem & ipsi caput ejus conteremus, &c. Subjiciatur brevis gratiarum actio, pro more.
units.tr: IV. Since the serpent has been so bruised that it does not yet cease to strike at our heel, let us be watchful and pray, girded for battle, lest we succumb in temptations, as our parents did. Let us avoid fellowship with Satan and his instruments; let us cherish the enmities laid down. Thus at last we too shall bruise his head, etc. A brief thanksgiving is to be added, as is customary.

units.la: T V. Exer-
units.tr: T V. Exer-

units.la: Exercitatio II. De Nativitate Christi: & de celebratione huius beneficii Dei, quod Messiam exhibuerit; desumta ex nuncio & Cantico Angelorum, Luc. 2.
units.tr: Exercitatio II. On the Nativity of Christ, and on the celebration of this benefit of God, that He has given the Messiah; taken from the message and the song of the Angels, Luke 2.

units.la: EXordium à tempore. Redit crastina die festum Natalis Messiæ[?], quod Ecclesia merito quotannis celebrat.
units.tr: The introduction is taken from the time. Tomorrow the feast of the Messiah's Birth returns, which the Church rightly celebrates every year.

units.la: Ratio: Quia est solennis recordatio incarnationis Filii Dei quæ est opus Dei ipsa omnium rerum creatione admirabilius.
units.tr: The reason: because it is a solemn remembrance of the incarnation of the Son of God, which is a work of God more admirable than the very creation of all things.

units.la: Ostend. brevi collatione: In creatione rerum lucet quidem Dei omnipotentia & sapientia in rebus ex nihilo condendis & ordinandis, quæ nondum fuerant. Sed in hoc mirabili fœdere divinæ & humanæ naturæ omnes virtutes suas ad miserũ humanũ genus redimendum Deus exeruit. Ambr. in Luc. 2. Plus debeo D. Iesu tuis incuriis, quod sum redemtus, quã operibus, quod sum creatus. Fiat. brevis inductio: Omnipotentia est, quod virgo peperit: Ineffabilis misericordiæ & amoris, quod Pater Filium unigenitum donavit redemtorem: Summæ iustitiæ, quod Filio non pepercit: Immensæ Sapientiæ, quod admirando fœdere Filium in carnem misit, & tale temperamentum misericordiæ ac iustitiæ exserendæ invenit, &c.
units.tr: Shown by a brief comparison: In the creation of things the omnipotence and wisdom of God indeed shine forth, in founding and ordering things out of nothing, which had not yet existed. But in this wonderful union of the divine and the human nature, God has put forth all his powers to redeem the wretched human race. Ambrose on Luke 2: "I owe more to your carelessness, O Lord Jesus, that I have been redeemed, than to your works, that I have been created. So be it." A brief induction: It is omnipotence that the virgin bore a child; it is of ineffable mercy and love that the Father gave his only-begotten Son as Redeemer; it is of supreme justice that he did not spare his Son; it is of immense wisdom that by a wonderful covenant he sent the Son into the flesh, and found such a balance for displaying mercy and justice, etc.

units.la: Amplif. Angeli admirantur, gratulantur, & celebrant hoc opus lætissima voce: Annuncio vobis gaudium, &c. Vobis natus est, &c. Gloria in excelsis, &c.
units.tr: Amplification: The angels marvel at, rejoice in, and celebrate this work with the most joyful voice: "I bring you good news of great joy, etc. To you is born, etc. Glory to God in the highest, etc."

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] à minori: Cum hoc beneficium ve-rius ad nos homines quam ad angelos pertineat, magis ergo nobis est celebrandum & lætandum.
units.tr: [illegible, ~6 letters] from the lesser: Since this benefit pertains more truly to us men than to the angels, it ought therefore to be celebrated and rejoiced in all the more by us.

units.la: Hypothesis: Præsertim in Ecclesiis & Scholis, quæ sunt imago agminum cœlestium, celebratio fieri debet.
units.tr: Hypothesis: Especially in the Churches and the Schools, which are an image of the heavenly hosts, the celebration ought to take place.

units.la: Ratio: quia angeli amant cœtus docentium, iisque succinunt. Item: quia aliis voce præire debemus.
units.tr: The reason: because the angels love the assemblies of teachers and sing along with them. Likewise: because we ought to go before others with our voices.

units.la: Conclus. Vt igitur ad meditationem & celebrationem tam admirandi operis Dei mentes nostræ excitentur, instituta est hæc dicendi consuetudo.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore, that our minds may be stirred up to meditate upon and celebrate so admirable a work of God, this custom of speaking has been instituted.

units.la: Adversativa. Etsi conscius mihi meæ infantiæ trepidè huc affcendi: & malim audire quam dicere: tamen veniam & benevolentiam à vobis spero.
units.tr: Adversative: Although, aware of my own youth, I have approached here with trembling, and would rather listen than speak, nevertheless I hope for pardon and goodwill from you.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia obtempero præceptoribus. 2. quia si facultas dicentis spectanda, nullæ nec angelorum nec hominum eloquentissimorum linguæ huic rei explicandæ sufficiunt. 3. quia Deus etiam infantium & lactentium ore vult perficere laudem suam.
units.tr: The reasons: (1) because I obey my teachers; (2) because, if the ability of the speaker is to be considered, no tongues of angels or of the most eloquent men are sufficient to explain this matter; (3) because God wills to perfect his praise even by the mouths of infants and sucklings.

units.la: Transitio: Ipsi Angeli exemplo & voce nobis præeunt.
units.tr: Transition: The angels themselves go before us by example and by voice.

units.la: Propositio: Ergo vestigiis eorum insistentes consideremus.
units.tr: Proposition: Therefore, following in their footsteps, let us consider:

units.la: 1. Quid de nato Messia generi humano, cœlitus nuncient.
units.tr: 1. What the angels announced from heaven to the human race concerning the born Messiah.

units.la: 2. Quo carmine summum hoc Dei opus celebrent angeli.
units.tr: 2. With what song the angels celebrate this highest work of God.

units.la: I. Quid nuncient angeli de nato Messia.
units.tr: I. What the angels announced concerning the birth of the Messiah.

units.la: Recitetur textus de Pastoribus, apparitione, nuncio, & cantico angelorum.
units.tr: Let the text about the Shepherds be read: the appearance, the announcement, and the song of the angels.

units.la: ἐκφρασις[?] partium historiae subjiciatur per excla-mationem. O immensum amorem Dei, non solum donantis Filium in carnem sed & mittentis coelitus angelos nuncios, qui patefaciant mundo ne incognitus Thesaurus mundo non prodesset.
units.tr: A description of the parts of the history is to be added by way of exclamation. O immense love of God, who not only gave his Son in the flesh but also sent angels from heaven as messengers, to make known to the world that the treasure, if unknown, would not benefit the world.

units.la: Amplificetur a necessario propter caecitatem & tenebras mundi, in quibus jacuisset ignotus si-ne patefactione divina.
units.tr: It is to be amplified from necessity, on account of the blindness and darkness of the world, in which it would have lain unknown without divine revelation.

units.la: 1. Sed cur pastoribus & non magnatibus? Respon. per collationem. Cur ex pauper matre, in stabulo, in præsepi natus? Nempe ut non solum pro nobis miser esset, sed etiam doceret, regnum suum non fore mundanum, &c. Idem hic spectatur, &c. Item: ut facilius lateret antequam crucifixus glorificaretur. Item: ut pudefaceret sapientes & potentes, ideo humilia elegit: Item: quia prædictum: Ecce rex tuus venit pauper, &c. Item, ut exemplo esset nobis suis fratri-bus.
units.tr: 1. But why to shepherds and not to great men? Answer: by comparison. Why was he born of a poor mother, in a stable, in a manger? Surely so that he would not only be wretched for our sake, but also teach that his kingdom would not be of this world, etc. The same is seen here, etc. Likewise: so that he might lie hidden more easily until, crucified, he was glorified. Likewise: so that he might shame the wise and the powerful, therefore he chose the lowly. Likewise: because it had been foretold: "Behold, your king comes, poor, etc." Likewise: so that he might be an example to us, his brothers.

units.la: 2. (Cur per Angelos? 1. ut Ecclesia esset magis certa per eosdem nunciata est nativitas per quos & conceptio. 2. propter analogiam pro-mulgatae legis & Evangelii. Gal.3: Lex per manum angelorum lata. Ergo & Evangelium per angelos annunciari debuit, ut non esset minor gloria, sed major Corinth. 3. Ostendatur collatione utriusque historiae: Ibi omnia horrenda & formidabilia: Hic læta & consolationis plena.
units.tr: 2. (Why through angels? 1. So that the Church might be more certain, since the birth was announced through the same messengers through whom the conception was also announced. 2. On account of the analogy of the promulgated law and the Gospel. Gal. 3: "The law was given through the hand of angels." Therefore the Gospel too ought to be announced through angels, so that it would not be of less glory, but of greater. 2 Cor. 3. Let it be shown by comparing the two histories: there everything is dreadful and fearful; here everything is joyful and full of consolation.)

units.la: Ratio per occupationem: Terror pastorum non ex nuncio angelorum sed ex infirmitate naturae non ferentis majestatem coelestem. Item, non ad desperationem afferendam pastoribus: sed ad reverentiam & authoritatem conciliadam coelestibus legatis.
units.tr: The reason by a preoccupation: the terror of the shepherds did not arise from the message of the angels but from the weakness of nature, which could not bear the heavenly majesty. Likewise, it was not to bring despair to the shepherds, but to win reverence and authority for the heavenly envoys.

units.la: 3. Quid nunciant? Gaudium magnum & perpetuum: Erit toti populo. Quare? Quia natus servator. Et quis ille? Christus Dominus? Qualis? Ostende ex verbis angeli, Luc. 1.32. Magnus, Filius altissimi, Rex domus Davidis: habens regnū æternum, &c. Ergo verus Deus. Nullus enim alius est talis Dominus.
units.tr: 3. What do they announce? A great and perpetual joy: "It shall be for all the people." Why? Because a Saviour is born. And who is he? "Christ the Lord." What kind? Show from the words of the angel, Luke 1:32: great, the Son of the Most High, the King of the house of David, having an eternal kingdom, etc. Therefore true God. For there is no other Lord such as this.

units.la: At quomodo Deus, cum hodie natus? Quia Deus existēs assumta carne factus est homo. Ioh. 1. in tempore definito. Gal. 4.
units.tr: But how can he be God, since he is born today? Because being God, he, having assumed flesh, was made man, John 1, at a defined time. Gal. 4.

units.la: Hodie cur dicant? Ut opponant tempus impletionis temporis promissionis & exspectationis: Semen mulieris conteret, &c. Virgo concipiet, pariet, &c. Nunc vero, Hodie natus est: Deus manifestatus est in carne: venit Filius Dei destruere, &c.
units.tr: Why do they say "today"? To set against the time of the fulfilment of the time of the promise and expectation: "The seed of the woman shall crush, etc.; a virgin shall conceive and bear, etc." But now: "Today is born: God has been made manifest in the flesh: the Son of God has come to destroy, etc."

units.la: Epiphonema cum August. Serm. 1. de Temp. O diem exspectatum, festum, faustum, &c. quem Servator natus de Patre sine die, per quem factus est omnis dies, natalem hunc diem habere voluit ex virgine. Si miramur in die, miremur potius æternū Servatorem ante omnem diem permanentem, omnemque diem creantem, in die nascentem, à malitia diei liberantem, &c.
units.tr: An exclamation with Augustine, Sermon 1 on the Time: "O longed-for, festal, happy day, etc., which the Saviour, born of the Father without day, through whom every day was made, willed to have this birthday from the virgin. If we marvel at the day, let us rather marvel at the eternal Saviour, existing before every day, creating every day, born in the day, freeing from the evil of the day, etc."

units.la: In urbe David? Vt ostendant, hunc esse Messiam promissum juxta oracula. Mich.5. Matth.2.
units.tr: "In the city of David"? So that they may show that this is the Messiah promised according to the oracles. Micah 5; Matthew 2.

units.la: Cur latandum nativitate Messiæ[?]? Quia Ser-vator.
units.tr: Why must we rejoice at the birth of the Messiah? Because he is the Saviour.

units.la: Qualem salutem afferens? Non temporalem, ut alii servatores: Sed æternam à peccato, morte, Diabolo liberationem. Matth.1. Heb.2. justi-tiam & vitam æternam. Ief.53[?] Servus meus iustus, &c. Dan.9. Reducet iustitiam æternam. Ego do eis vitam æternam.
units.tr: What kind of salvation does he bring? Not temporal, like other saviours, but eternal liberation from sin, death and the Devil. Matt. 1; Heb. 2; "righteousness and eternal life." Isa. 53: "My servant, righteous, etc." Dan. 9: "He will bring in everlasting righteousness." "I give them eternal life."

units.la: Quomodo? r[?], Quia est Christus Propheta, Sacerdos & Rex Ecclesiæ. 11. Merito & efficacia. Explicentur singula breviter.
units.tr: How? Because Christ is the Prophet, Priest and King of the Church. 11. By merit and efficacy. Let each of these be explained briefly.

units.la: Epiphonema. Hinc nimirum apparet, cur dicat Angeli Gaudium magnum.
units.tr: Summary exclamation: From this, indeed, it appears why the angels say "great joy."

units.la: Sed quibus? Annuncio vobis.
units.tr: But to whom? "I announce to you."

units.la: An solis pastoribus? Erit toti populo. Pax homi-nib.in terra: omnibus offertur.
units.tr: Is it only to the shepherds? "It shall be for all the people. Peace among men on earth": it is offered to all.

units.la: Cur ergo non omnes servantur? Non culpa servatoris, sed sua: quia salutem non accipiunt. Ioh.1. Dedit potestatem, &c. iis qui credunt.
units.tr: Why then are not all saved? Not through the fault of the Saviour, but through their own: because they do not receive salvation. John 1: "He gave power, etc., to those who believe."

units.la: Quomodo accipitur? Fide. Infidelibus non venit servator, sed judex. Ioh.3.
units.tr: How is it received? By faith. The Saviour does not come to unbelievers, but as judge. John 3.

units.la: Breviter refutetur error de liberatione & salu-te etiam infidelium: & ostende, quod repugnet Evangelio, sit Christo contumeliosus, minuat consolationem piorum: sit fenestra Epicureismi, &c.
units.tr: Briefly the error about the deliverance and salvation even of unbelievers is to be refuted, and it is to be shown that it conflicts with the Gospel, is insulting to Christ, diminishes the comfort of the pious, and is a window for Epicureanism, etc.

units.la: Conclusio: Vt igitur salute, quam affert, frua-mur, accipiamus eum fide, & simus grati.
units.tr: Conclusion: Therefore, that we may enjoy the salvation he brings, let us receive him by faith and be thankful.

units.la: Transitio ad secundam partem habens ἀπο-λογίαν[?] à minori: Cum angeli lætentur, & cele-brent. brent Deum:multo magis nos debemus,quibus natus est:Item à facili: Prasertim cum etiam vo-ce & verbis nobis pręeant.
units.tr: Transition to the second part, having an apology from the less: since the angels rejoice and celebrate God, how much more ought we to, to whom he is born. Likewise from the easier: especially since they go before us even with voice and words.

units.la: II. De cantico Angelorum.
units.tr: II. On the song of the angels.

units.la: Recitetur textus: Et subito affuit cum Angelo multitudo exercituum coelestium, &c. Gloria in excelsis,&c.
units.tr: Let the text be read: "And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host, etc. Glory to God in the highest, etc."

units.la: Non unus angelus, sed exercitus angelorum una voce testimonium dant Filio Dei, celebrant Dei donum: natalem Messiæ condecorant, homi-nib. gratulantur. O dulcissimam harmoniam. Conjungunt Deum & homines:coelum & terrā: quia hoc opus Dei gloriosissimum, in coelo & in terra celebrandum. Bruti stuporis erit non succi-nere, pari lætitia Deum non celebrare. ¡Sed audiamus canticum.
units.tr: Not one angel, but a host of angels with one voice bear witness to the Son of God and celebrate the gift of God; they adorn the birth of the Messiah and congratulate men. O sweetest harmony! They join God and men, heaven and earth, because this most glorious work of God is to be celebrated in heaven and on earth. It would be the mark of brutish stupidity not to join in singing, and with equal joy not to celebrate God. But let us hear the song.

units.la: 1. Gloria in excelsis,&c. Gloria Dei est tribuere Deo proprietates & opera ejus propria. Enu-mera quędam pręcipua: & Amplifica à gradibus eorum: in quibus tanto est illustrior Dei gloria, quanto ipsa sunt mirabiliora,&c.
units.tr: 1. "Glory to God in the highest, etc." The glory of God is to ascribe to God his own properties and works. List some of the chief ones, and amplify from their degrees: in which the glory of God is the more illustrious the more wonderful they are, etc.

units.la: Applicatio ad hypothesin: Angelorum testimonio opus Dei gloriosissimum est missio Filii in carnem. Ratio, quia in hac plene elucet gloria Dei, h.e, immensa ejus bonitas, justitia, sapientia, potentia,&c. Hagg.2. Adhuc modicum & commovebo cœlum & terram,&c.
units.tr: Application to the hypothesis: by the testimony of the angels, the most glorious work of God is the sending of the Son in the flesh. Reason: because in this the glory of God shines forth fully, that is, his immense goodness, justice, wisdom, power, etc. Hag. 2: "Yet a little while, and I will shake heaven and earth, etc."

units.la: πόρισμα.[?] Ergo ut hanc gloriam integram Deo tribuamus, agnoscamus ex Evangelio, & osculemur Filium,&c.
units.tr: Corollary: Therefore, that we may ascribe this whole glory to God, let us acknowledge it from the Gospel, and kiss the Son, etc.

units.la: Amplif. à contrario. Turcę Iudęi Diaboli & omnes mnes impii non tribuunt gloriam Deo: Ratio, quia non honorant Filium, &c. Item : quia nec justitiam nec misericordiam Dei agnoscunt, aut si agnoscunt, laudem ejus ei non tribuunt, nec sibi applicant, &c.
units.tr: Amplification from the contrary: Turks, Jews, devils and all the impious do not ascribe glory to God. Reason: because they do not honour the Son, etc. Likewise: because they acknowledge neither the justice nor the mercy of God, or if they acknowledge them, they do not ascribe praise to him nor apply it to themselves, etc.

units.la: Digressio brevis : Hanc gloriam non tantum obscurant haeretici, qui divinitatem veram Filii negant, sed etiam qui humanitatem veram tollunt, aut in aliam naturam transformant.
units.tr: Brief digression: this glory is obscured not only by heretics who deny the true divinity of the Son, but also by those who take away his true humanity or transform it into another nature.

units.la: Occupatio : Dicunt angeli: In altissimis. Ergo ne tantum in coelo est laudandus Deus, & non etiam in terra?
units.tr: Preoccupation: The angels say "in the highest." Therefore is God to be praised only in heaven, and not also on earth?

units.la: Responsio. 1. à minori. Si in coelo, magis in terra, quia ad nos pertinet beneficium : qui in terra fumus. Sed laus erit plenior in coelo, propter completionem beneficii, &c.
units.tr: Answer. 1. From the less: if in heaven, much more on earth, because the benefit pertains to us, who are on earth. But the praise will be fuller in heaven, on account of the completion of the benefit, etc.

units.la: 2. Addunt angeli: Et in terra pax: Ergo praecipue homines ad celebrationem hortantur.
units.tr: 2. The angels add: "And on earth peace." Therefore they especially exhort men to the celebration.

units.la: Obiectio : Quomodo pax? cum sequantur turbae & nativitatem & praedicationem Christi: Offendantur exemplis. Quomodo pax in terra ubi bella quotidie? Quomodo pacem affert, qui dicit. Non veni pacem mittere sed gladium?
units.tr: Objection: How is there peace? For wars and disputes follow both the birth and the preaching of Christ. Let them be shown by examples. How is there peace on earth where there are wars every day? How does he bring peace who says, "I came not to send peace but a sword"?

units.la: Responsio. Affert pacem coelestem conscientiis nostris, hoc est, reconciliationem cum Deo. 2. Corinth. 5. Roman. 5. Iohan. 16. &c.
