Ideo ad-dunt In hominibus benevolentia nempe Dei erit: In filio enim Pater acquiescit reconciliatus, &c. Adde interpretationem Chrysost. & Augustin. Pax in terra, in hominibus bonae voluntatis, h. e. iis qui suscipiunt Christum. Per antithesin offende cau[?]las bellorum & dissidiorum cum impiis: itè cru-cis Ecclesiae, &c. Conclusio breviter repetat summam praecipuorum capitum, & hortationes inde sumtas.
units.tr: Answer: He brings heavenly peace to our consciences, that is, reconciliation with God. 2 Cor. 5; Rom. 5; John 16, etc. Therefore they add, "Good will among men," namely, that of God will be: for in the Son the Father, reconciled, is well pleased, etc. Add the interpretation of Chrysostom and Augustine: "Peace on earth, among men of good will," that is, among those who receive Christ. By antithesis, set against this the causes of wars and dissensions with the impious; likewise the cross of the Church, etc. The conclusion briefly repeats the sum of the chief heads and the exhortations drawn from them.

units.la: 1. {ad}Ad fidem: Cum sit nobis natus Servator, Ergo eum reverenter fide suscipiamus: osculemur filium, &c.
units.tr: 1. To faith: since a Saviour is born to us, let us therefore receive him reverently in faith: let us kiss the Son, etc.

units.la: 2. Ad sanctitatem: Ideo enim Deus noster (inquit Chrysostomus) virgineum sibi requisivit hospitium habitandi, ut nobis ostenderet in casto corpore Deum portari debere, &c.
units.tr: 2. To holiness: for this reason our God (says Chrysostom) sought for himself a virginal dwelling-place to inhabit, so that he might show us that God ought to be borne in a chaste body, etc.

units.la: 3. Ad humilitatem: Cum nostra causa in stabulum inter stercora se demiserit: Simus igitur modesti: & ad humilia eius membra libenter nos demittamus.
units.tr: 3. On humility: Since he humbled himself for our sake, lying among the dung in a stable, let us therefore be modest, and gladly lower ourselves to his lowly members.

units.la: 4. Ad patientiam: ne pudeat nos praesepis, stabuli, exilii & malorum cum ipso ferendorum: Ipse enim cum esset dives propter nos factus est pauper, &c.
units.tr: 4. On patience: Let us not be ashamed of the manger, the stable, and the exile and evils which we must bear along with him. For though he was rich, he became poor for our sake, etc.

units.la: 5. Ad gratitudinem. Cum nobis sit datus, factus a Patre sapientia, justitia, &c. nos servet a peccato & morte, colligat, servet inter nos & glorificaturus sit Ecclesiam, voce Evangelii per Spiritum Sanctum: Ergo simus grati, celebremus eum in hac vita, ut possimus cum celebrare in aeternitate cum angelis, &c.
units.tr: 5. On gratitude. Since he has been given to us, made by the Father our wisdom, righteousness, etc., to keep us from sin and death, to gather us, to preserve us among ourselves, and to glorify the Church through the voice of the Gospel by the Holy Spirit: therefore let us be thankful, and let us celebrate him in this life, so that we may also celebrate him together with the angels in eternity, etc.

units.la: Huius rei causa cum nunc etiam convenerimus, gratiarum actionem & vota coniungamus.
units.tr: Since we have now gathered for this reason, let us join thanksgiving and prayers together.

units.la: 1. Pro Filio servatore nobis nato & dato.
units.tr: 1. For the Son given and born to us as our Saviour.

units.la: 2. Pro electione & defensione Ecclesiae.
units.tr: 2. For the election and defence of the Church.

units.la: 3. Pro puritate doctrinae Evangelicae nobis concessa.
units.tr: 3. For the purity of the Evangelical doctrine granted to us.

units.la: 4. Pro conservatione Scholarum, studiorum, politiarum, & piorum Magistratuum, qui Eccle-sis fiis & studiis literarum dant hospitia.
units.tr: 4. For the preservation of the schools, studies, governments, and pious magistrates, who give shelter to the churches and to the pursuits of letters.

units.la: Petitio: ut porro nobis hæc bona servet, augeat, hostium consilia & conatus frangat, impediat, tribuat pacem & nascenti in nobis Christo & cœtib: docentium atq; discentium, fortunet pios Principes & gubernatores: & hunc annum omnibus nobis faxit salutarem. Amen.
units.tr: Petition: that he would further preserve and increase these good things for us, break and hinder the counsels and attempts of our enemies, grant peace, and prosper Christ, who is being born in us, and the assemblies of teachers and learners; that he would bless the pious princes and rulers, and make this year healthful for all of us. Amen.

units.la: Exercitatio III.
units.tr: Exercitatio III.

units.la: De persona & beneficiis Christi: ex 2. Cor.8.9. Qui cum esset dives, &c.
units.tr: On the person and benefits of Christ, from 2 Cor. 8:9, "Who, though he was rich, &c."

units.la: EXordium à circumstantia temporis seu consuetudine repetendi dictum de Christi persona, officio & beneficiis Ecclesiæ collatis, publica oratione, pridie festi Natalitii: & à tua persona: vel sit liberum, & breve.
units.tr: The exordium is taken from the circumstance of time, or from the custom of repeating in public discourse, on the day before the Nativity festival, what has been said about the person, office and benefits of Christ conferred on the Church; and from your own person. It may be free and brief.

units.la: Transitio ad propositionem: Sæpe antehac ex historia dictum de modo & causis nativitatis Filii Dei ex virgine: Ideo te nunc dicturum pauca de loco Apostoli 1.Cor.8.9. Scitis gratiam, &c.
units.tr: Transition to the proposition: Often before this, from history, we have spoken of the manner and causes of the birth of the Son of God from the virgin. Therefore I shall now say a few things about the passage of the Apostle, 1 Cor. 8:9, "You know the grace, &c."

units.la: Ratio ab argumento: quia breviter complecti-tur doctrinam de Christi persona & beneficii, quod fuerit dives antequam fieret pauper: quod factus sit pauper propter nos, quodque pauper-tate sua nos divites fecerit.
units.tr: Reason from the subject: because it briefly sums up the doctrine concerning the person of Christ and the benefit, namely that he was rich before he became poor; that he became poor on our account; and that by his poverty he made us rich.

units.la: Illustretur à scopo Apostoli ad Corinthios, quos hortatur, ne ad eleemosynam sanctis conferen-dam sint segnes, proposito Christi exemplo: cuius summa: Christi est ingens beneficetia[?] in vos: Ergo & vos benefici sitis in fratres.
units.tr: It is illustrated from the aim of the Apostle to the Corinthians, whom he urges not to be slow in contributing alms to the saints, the example of Christ being set before them. The sum of it is this: Christ's benefaction toward you is immense; therefore you too should be beneficent toward the brethren.

units.la: Vt
units.tr: So that

units.la: Vis exempli explicetur à minori:
units.tr: The force of the example is explained from the lesser:

units.la: Christus dives ex se, nulli obstrictus. Nos divi-tes ex ipso, fratribus obstricti.
units.tr: Christ was rich in himself, bound to no one. We are rich from him, bound to our brethren.

units.la: Christus depauperatus extreme propter nos. Nos tantillum dare gravabimur propter ipsum?
units.tr: Christ was reduced to extreme poverty on our account. Will we be reluctant to give the smallest thing on his account?

units.la: Christus sua paupertate nos ditavit cœlestibus thesauris: Nos gravabimur sublevare inopiam fratrum bonis caducis? Propositio. Dicam. I. Quomodo Christus dives antequam pauper. II. Quomodo factus pauper. III Quare:& quas divitias paupertate sua nobis conferat.
units.tr: Christ by his poverty enriched us with heavenly treasures; will we be reluctant to relieve the want of the brethren with perishable goods? Proposition. I shall speak of: I. How Christ was rich before he was poor. II. How he became poor. III. Why, and what riches he confers on us by his poverty.

units.la: I. Quomodo Christus fuerit dives, antequam fieret pauper.
units.tr: I. How Christ was rich before he became poor.

units.la: Factus est pauper πτωχὸς ὤν. Quomodo & quibus divitiis dives fuerit ante paupertatem, cō-siderandum.
units.tr: "He became poor, being rich" [πτωχὸς ὤν]. It must be considered how, and with what riches, he was rich before his poverty.

units.la: Reiice mundi opinionem, cum divitias vel divitem audit somniantis magnos thesauros & talenta auri, argenti, possessiones fundorum, servorum, &c. vel aliquem Midam, Croesum aut Crassum,&c. quorum historiolas paucis asperge: & ostende eos fuisse divitiarum pauperes servos: quoniam etiam Philosophis pauperes sunt, non qui modicum habent, sed qui plura appetunt. Horum namque fuit insatiabilis cupiditas.
units.tr: Reject the opinion of the world, which, when it hears of riches or a rich man, dreams of great treasures and talents of gold and silver, estates of lands, slaves, &c., or of some Midas, Croesus or Crassus, &c. Touch briefly on their little stories, and show that they were poor slaves of riches; for even to the philosophers those are poor not who have a little, but who desire more. For theirs was an insatiable greed.

units.la: Per [illegible, ~8 letters] subiiciatur Apostoli sententia seu propositio: Christum antequam fieret homo, fuisse Deum verum & aeternum rerum omnium conditorem ac Dominum.
units.tr: [illegible] Let there be added the statement or proposition of the Apostle: that Christ, before he became man, was true God and eternal Creator and Lord of all things.

units.la: Prob. 1. πλούσιος ὢν[?]. Solus Deus vere Dives: quia solus αὐτάρκης[?] sufficiens sibi & rebus omnibus Gen.17. Deus Schadai: Psal. 50. mea sunt pecora campi, &c. Hagg.2. Meum est aurum & argentum. Item. Eph.2. πλούσιος ὢν ἐν ἐλέει[?]. Iacob.1. Ab eo omne munus bonum, &c.
units.tr: Proof: 1. "Being rich" [πλούσιος ὢν]. Only God is truly rich, because only he is self-sufficient [αὐτάρκης] and sufficient to himself and to all things: Gen. 17, God Almighty [Schadai]; Ps. 50, "the cattle on a thousand hills are mine, &c."; Hag. 2, "The silver is mine and the gold is mine." Likewise Eph. 2, "rich in mercy" [πλούσιος ὢν ἐν ἐλέει]; James 1, "Every good gift comes from him, &c."

units.la: Potest illustrari quibusdam locis celebranti-bus abundantes & investigabiles divitias gratiae, bonitatis, misericordiae, & gloriae Dei Rom.2.9. 10.11. Eph.1.2.3.&c.
units.tr: It can be illustrated by certain passages celebrating the abundant and unsearchable riches of the grace, goodness, mercy and glory of God: Rom. 2:9–11; Eph. 1:2–3, &c.

units.la: Minor fit applicatio ad Christum. πλούσιος ὢν cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto. Ioh.16. Omnia quae Pater habet mea sunt: Et: De meo accipiet, & annunciabit vobis.
units.tr: The minor premise is applied to Christ: "being rich" together with the Father and the Holy Spirit. John 16, "All that the Father has is mine"; and, "He will take of what is mine and declare it to you."

units.la: Est filius Divitis habentis dispensatores. Luc. 16.
units.tr: He is the son of a rich man who has stewards. Luke 16.

units.la: Filius regis, cui Pater nuptias parat. Matth.22.
units.tr: The son of a king, for whom the Father prepares a wedding. Matt. 22.

units.la: Sepultus ut dives. Ief.53.
units.tr: Buried as a rich man. Isa. 53.

units.la: Totam Ecclesiam ditans. Ioh.1. Illuminat omnem hominem: Item: Ex plenitudine eius omnes accepimus.
units.tr: Enriching the whole Church. John 1, "He enlightens every man"; likewise, "From his fullness we have all received."

units.la: Obiectio. Etiam Abraham, Loth, &c. fuerunt divites. Divites sapientes. Cicero in Paradox. Epulo dives Luc.16. Divites huius mundi. 1.Tim.6.
units.tr: Objection: Abraham, Lot, &c. were also rich. The rich are wise. Cicero in the Paradoxes. Dives Epulo, Luke 16. "The rich of this world," 1 Tim. 6.

units.la: Resp. 1. non vere sed hominum sermone, aut sua opinione. Prob. ex definitione Ciceronis: Divitem intelligimus eum, qui nihil quaerat, nihil appetat[?], nihil optet amplius. Talis nemo illorum: sed Christus.
units.tr: Answer: 1. Not truly, but in the language of men, or in their own opinion. Proof from Cicero's definition: "We understand a rich man to be one who seeks nothing, desires nothing, wants nothing more." No one of those men was such; but Christ was.

units.la: 2. Opes non sunt veræ divitiæ, quia non faciunt bonos: communes sunt bonis & malis: irritamenta malorum: patiuntur stultitiam: parantur, habentur, amittuntur cum molestia, &c.
units.tr: 2. Wealth is not true riches, because it does not make men good; it is common to good and bad; it is an incitement to the wicked; it suffers folly; it is acquired, held, and lost with trouble, &c.

units.la: Prob. II. Authoritate Ambrosii, Hieronymi, Theoph. & aliorum Patrum sic interpretantiũ Christi divitias.
units.tr: Proof II: by the authority of Ambrose, Jerome, Theophylact and other Fathers who so interpret the riches of Christ.

units.la: Prob. III. Testimoniis Scripturæ, quod fuerit Deus unus cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto ante carnem assumtam.
units.tr: Proof III: by the testimonies of Scripture, that he was one God with the Father and the Holy Spirit before the assumption of flesh.

units.la: Producatur locus usus & alter.
units.tr: Let a passage be produced, and another.

units.la: 1. Locus Gen. 48.16. Exod. 3.2. &c. de Angelo Domini qui locutus est patribus. Fuit ipse Deus: quia vocatur Iehova & tribuuntur ei Iehovæ propria. vide Act. 7.v.31.32.34.
units.tr: 1. Passage: Gen. 48:16; Exod. 3:2, &c., concerning the Angel of the Lord who spoke to the fathers. He himself was God, because he is called Jehovah and the proper attributes of Jehovah are ascribed to him; see Acts 7:31–32, 34.

units.la: Is autem fuit Christus ante carnem: Proba ex consensu totius Ecclesiæ: quia Filius semper fuit legatus Patris ad Ecclesiam Mal. 3.1. Mox veniet ad templum suum Dominus, Angelus fœderis, id est, Christus.
units.tr: But this was Christ before the flesh. Prove it from the consent of the whole Church, because the Son was always the Father's envoy to the Church: Mal. 3:1, "The Lord, the Angel of the covenant, will soon come to his temple," that is, Christ.

units.la: II Locus. Psal. 45.7. Thronus tuus Deus, &c. Hic Deus fuit Filius ante carnem Heb. 1.8.
units.tr: II. Passage: Ps. 45:7, "Your throne, O God, &c." Here God was the Son before the flesh; Heb. 1:8.

units.la: III Locus. Prov. 30.3. Quod nomen eius, & quod nomen Filii eius? Erat igitur tunc Filius cum Patre, omnia gubernans. Hic autem Christus. Heb. 1.3. Omnia sustentat verbo suo potenti. Matth. 8.27. Quis ipse cui obediunt venti, &c.
units.tr: III. Passage: Prov. 30:3, "What is his name, and what is his Son's name?" Therefore the Son was then with the Father, governing all things. Here, however, is Christ. Heb. 1:3, "He upholds all things by his powerful word." Matt. 8:27, "Who is this, whom the winds obey, &c."

units.la: IV. Ioh. 1. λόγῳ[?] est Deus: quia erat in principio, ante res creatas, apud Deum, Deus omnia creans: illuminans omnem hominem, in propria veniens, carnem assumens, habitans in nobis, habens gloriam unigeniti à Patre, &c. Fuit autem Filius Dei Christus : quia σάρξ ἐγένετο: Filius in sinu patris revelavit nobis: Ioh. 16. Exivit a patre & venit in mundum. Heb. 2. ἐπιλαμβάνεται[?] semen Abrahae, &c. venit in carnem. 1. Ioh. 4. Ergo fuit ante carnem.
units.tr: IV. John 1: "the Word" [λόγῳ] is God, because he was in the beginning, before created things, with God, God creating all things, enlightening every man, coming into his own, assuming flesh, dwelling among us, having glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, &c. He was, moreover, the Son of God, Christ, because "the Word became flesh" [σάρξ ἐγένετο]: "The Son who is in the bosom of the Father has revealed him to us"; John 16, "He came out from the Father and came into the world." Heb. 2, "he takes hold of the seed of Abraham, &c., he came into the flesh." 1 John 4. Therefore he was before the flesh.

units.la: v Locus Phil. 2. Qui cum esset, &c. Locus nostro huic similis. Confer membra: ὁ πλούσιος[?] ὤν & ὁ ἐν μορφῇ θεοῦ ὤν[?]. Item: factus pauper, &: Exinanivit seipsum, assumta forma servi, &c.
units.tr: V. Passage: Phil. 2, "Who, being, &c." A passage similar to our own. Compare the members: "being rich" [ὁ πλούσιος ὤν] and "being in the form of God" [ὁ ἐν μορφῇ θεοῦ ὤν]. Likewise: "became poor, &c."; "he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, &c."

units.la: Ostende in forma Dei esse, & æqualem Deo esse, idem esse, quod Deum esse: quia Deo nihil æquale nisi Deus. Ief.40. Et patrum authoritate sic interpretantium Ambrof. lib. 7. Ep. 47. Hilar. 12. de Trinit. Basil. adv. Eunom. lib. 1. Augustin. de fide ad Petil. cap. 2. & de Trin. lib. 1. cap. 1. & 4. Lomb. lib. 3. d. 5.
units.tr: Show that to be in the form of God, and to be equal to God, is the same as to be God, because nothing is equal to God except God; Isa. 40. And by the authority of the Fathers who so interpret it: Ambrose, Letter 47, Book 7; Hilary, On the Trinity, Book 12; Basil, Against Eunomius, Book 1; Augustine, On Faith to Peter, chap. 2, and On the Trinity, Book 1, chaps. 1 and 4; Lombard, Sentences, Book 3, dist. 5.

units.la: Claude χωλωσει[?] locorum. Ex his satis demonstratas Christi divitias, quae & quantae fuerint ante te paupertatem, non nummorum, fundorum, mancipiorum, &c. sed verae divinitatis cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto.
units.tr: Let the passages be closed. From these it is sufficiently demonstrated what and how great the riches of Christ were before his poverty: not money, estates, slaves, &c., but the true divinity with the Father and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: βλασφημία[?] 1. Detestanda igitur blasphemia Photini, Samosateni, Servcti, Socini, &c. quod Christus ante carnem ne fuerit quidem: Sed coeperit ex matre merus homo esse. Ostende quod hoc sit divitias Christi negare: quoniam sic non fuisset dives antequam pauper fieret, cum quatenus homo pauper sit natus ex matre virgine, &c.
units.tr: Blasphemy: 1. Therefore the blasphemy of Photinus, Samosatenus, Servetus, Socinus, &c. is to be detested, who hold that Christ was not even before the flesh, but began to be a mere man from his mother. Show that to deny this is to deny the riches of Christ; for thus he would not have been rich before he became poor, since insofar as he is man he was born poor of the virgin mother, &c.

units.la: 11. Refutentur quoque Ubiquitarii, similiter hunc locum (ut & Phil. 2.) non de divitiis verae Divinitatis, sed de communicata Maiestate & fictitia ubiquitate carnis interpretantes.
units.tr: 2. The Ubiquitarians are also to be refuted, who likewise interpret this passage (as also Phil. 2) not of the riches of true Divinity, but of a communicated majesty and a fictitious ubiquity of the flesh.

units.la: Respond. 1. Historia nativitatis testatur, Christum humanitate statim ab utero pauperem fuisse. Aut ergo divinitate, aut nullo modo fuit dives, antequam fieret pauper.
units.tr: Answer: 1. The history of the nativity testifies that Christ in his humanity was poor from the very womb. Therefore either by his divinity or in no way was he rich before he became poor.

units.la: 2. Est ipsissima glossa Photini, &c. evertens argumentum Deitatis Christi inde ductum.
units.tr: 2. This is the very gloss of Photinus, &c., overturning the argument for the Deity of Christ drawn from it.

units.la: Obiect. 1. Non evertit, quia (inquiunt) dicimus Christum non sola humanitate (ut Photinus) sed & Divinitate divitem fuisse. Resp. Petitio principii, quia si divitiæ hæ etiam fuerunt humanitatis, sive solius sive non; non sequitur hinc necessario, Christum fuisse Deum: sed tantum fuisse hominem divitem, antequam fieret pauper, quæ est Photini blasphemia.
units.tr: Objection 1: It does not overturn it, because (they say) we say that Christ was rich not by his humanity alone (as Photinus says) but also by his divinity. Answer: A petitio principii; for if these riches were also of the humanity, whether alone or not, it does not follow necessarily from this that Christ was God, but only that he was a rich man before he became poor; which is the blasphemy of Photinus.

units.la: Obiect. II. Etiam humanitate ab utero fuit dives: quia hæres omnium. Hebr.1 Resp. 1. Habuit quidem, ius hæreditatis ab utero, sed cum paupertate, quia sine usurpatione, donec hæreditatem adiens verè factus est dives etiam humanitate per exaltationem. Matth. 12. Filius hominis non habet, &c. 2. Apostolus cum prædicat divitem, antequam fieret pauper. Ergo non humanitate divitem dicit. Ratio, quia eodem modo est pauper & homo factus.
units.tr: Objection 2: He was rich even by his humanity from the womb, because he is heir of all things; Heb. 1. Answer: 1. He indeed had the right of inheritance from the womb, but with poverty, since without possession, until by entering upon the inheritance he truly became rich even in his humanity through exaltation. Matt. 12, "The Son of man has not, &c." 2. When the Apostle proclaims him rich before he became poor, he does not therefore call him rich by his humanity. The reason: because in the same way he became poor and man.

units.la: Hinc jam transeatur ad secundam partem: Ad huius argumenti pleniorem confirmationem & illustrationem facere, quod sequitur dicendum: Quomodo dives exsistens factus sit pauper.
units.tr: Now let us pass on to the second part. To make a fuller confirmation and illustration of this argument, what follows is to be said: how, being rich, he became poor.

units.la: II. Quomodo Christus factus sit pauper.
units.tr: II. How Christ Became Poor.

units.la: Primò generatim doceatur modus: quod Filius Dei sit factus pauper, quando est factus homo: Ambrof. Factus pauper, quia Deus nasci dignatus est homo.
units.tr: First, let the manner be taught in general: that the Son of God became poor when he became man. Ambrose: "He became poor, because God deigned to be born a man."

units.la: Illustretur breviter locis similibus, quibus hic modus indicatur. Ioh.1. Verbum caro factum est. Phil.2. Cum esset, &c. assumsit formam servi.
units.tr: Let it be briefly illustrated by similar passages in which this manner is indicated. John 1: "The Word was made flesh." Phil. 2: "Although he was [in the form of God]... he took the form of a servant."

units.la: 1. Tim.3. Deus manifestatus in carne. Hebr.2. Assumsit semen Abrahæ, &c.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 3: "God was manifested in the flesh." Heb. 2: "He took hold of the seed of Abraham," etc.

units.la: Deinde speciatim explicentur partes seu gradus huius paupertatis.
units.tr: Then the parts or degrees of this poverty are to be explained in particular.

units.la: 1. Ipsa incarnatio seu assumtio naturæ huma-næ, facta in utero matris per conceptionem é Spiritu Sancto.
units.tr: 1. The incarnation itself, or the assumption of human nature, made in the mother's womb through conception by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Quid fuerit conceptio paucis indica: Miracu-losa formatio massæ humanæ de substantia matris, virtute Spiritus Sancti: Item: sanctificatio: Item unio eiusdem cum Filio Dei in unam ἕνωσιν[?] Matth.1. Luc.1.
units.tr: Let what the conception was be indicated in a few words: a miraculous formation of human matter from the substance of the mother, by the power of the Holy Spirit. Likewise: its sanctification; likewise the union of this same with the Son of God into one [union]. Matt. 1; Luke 1.

units.la: Prob. quod tunc factus pauper. 1. quia tunc factus homo, quo nihil pauperius, miserius, &c. Iob.14.2. quia factus caro, qua voce Scriptura infirmitates humanas appellat: Ief.40.[?] Omnis caro fœnum. Has Christus cum humana natura suscepit omnes excepto peccato. Heb.2.&4.
units.tr: It is proved that he then became poor: 1. because he then became man, than whom nothing is poorer or more wretched, etc. Job 14:2. Because he became flesh, a word by which Scripture names human infirmities: Isa. 40: "All flesh is grass." Christ took all these with human nature, except sin. Heb. 2 and 4.

units.la: Amplif. Hinc dicitur, verbum caro factum, potius quam homo. Ioh.1. Assumsit formam servi, potius quam hominis. Phil. 2. Et hîc : ἐπτωχεύσεν[?]: mendicus factus.
units.tr: By amplification: hence it is said "the Word was made flesh" rather than "man" (John 1); "he took the form of a servant" rather than "of a man" (Phil. 2). And here: he became a beggar [ἐπτώχευσεν: he became poor, as a beggar].

units.la: II. Nativitas ex matre pauperculayin[?] in stabulo &c. Breviter ostende ex historia. Luc. 2.
units.tr: II. The birth of a mother of little means, in a stable, etc. Briefly show this from the history. Luke 2.

units.la: III. Totius vitæ conditio, plena miseriarum, egestatis, dolorum, contemtus, &c. usque ad mortem crucis: qui ex Jef.53. & ex historia Evang. declaretur. Matth. 8. Vulpes habent, &c.
units.tr: III. The condition of his whole life, full of miseries, want, sorrows, contempt, etc., down to the death of the cross; this is to be declared from Isa. 53 and from the history of the Gospels. Matt. 8: "Foxes have holes," etc.

units.la: Per occupationem ostendatur Christum pau-pertate non amisisse divitias:
units.tr: Through an objection, let it be shown that Christ did not lose his riches through poverty.

units.la: Obiectio: Ex divite est factus pauper. Ergo de-siit esse dives, & Deus: manens tantum homo pauper.
units.tr: Objection: he became poor from being rich. Therefore he ceased to be rich, and God, remaining only a poor man.

units.la: Resp. Neg. antecedens: non factus est ex divi-te pauper sicut Crassus ex divite factus egens, ut ab occurrentibus per jocum tandem salutaretur dives, cuius hæreditas neque creditoribus satis-facere posset: Valer. Max. lib. 6. cap.11.
units.tr: Answer: I deny the antecedent. He did not become poor from being rich in the way that Crassus, from being rich, became needy, so that, when met by those who jokingly greeted him as rich, his inheritance could scarcely satisfy his creditors. Valerius Maximus, book 6, chapter 11.

units.la: Urge phrasin Apostoli: πλούσιος ὢν ἐπτώχευσεν, dives existens & manens factus est mendicus: non amittendo divitias, sed assumendo spontaneam paupertatem, ut idem dives simul & pauper esset.
units.tr: Press the Apostle's phrase: "being rich, he became a beggar" [πλούσιος ὢν ἐπτώχευσεν]: he who was and remained rich became poor, not by losing his riches, but by taking on voluntary poverty, so that the same person was at once rich and poor.

units.la: Prob. 1. quia Deus est factus homo non amis-sione, mutatione vel conversione Deitatis in hominem, sed assumtione hominis in Deum: Manens quod erat, & factus quod non erat. Idem dives Divinitate: pauper humanitate.
units.tr: It is proved: 1. because God became man not by the loss, change or conversion of the Deity into man, but by the assumption of man into God: remaining what he was, and becoming what he was not. The same is rich in his Divinity, poor in his humanity.

units.la: Proba ex dictis: Zach.9. Rex tuus pauper. Joh.1. Verbum caro factum: habens nihilominus gratiam unigeniti à Patre. Act.20. Deus suo sanguine acquisivit Ecclesiam. 1.Cor.2. Dominum gloriæ non crucifixissent, &c.
units.tr: Proved from the sayings: Zech. 9: "Your king is poor." John 1: "The Word was made flesh," nevertheless having the grace of the only-begotten from the Father. Acts 20: "God acquired the Church with his own blood." 1 Cor. 2: "Had they not crucified the Lord of glory," etc.

units.la: Reiiciatur commentum Vbiquit: quod simul dives & pauper humanitate. Sic non fuisset verè pauper. Ratio: quia contraria non consistunt simul in eadem natura. Ergo non ditasset nos sua paupertate, &c.
units.tr: The fiction of the Ubiquitarians is to be rejected: that he is at once rich and poor in his humanity. For so he would not have been truly poor. The reason: because contraries cannot exist together in the same nature. Therefore he would not have enriched us by his poverty, etc.

units.la: [illegible, ~7 letters]. Ergo vere est promissus Messias.
units.tr: [illegible, about seven letters]. Therefore the Messiah was truly promised.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia vere Deus & homo, qualis à prophetis prædictus. Applicentur breviter quædam oracula & utraque natura inde ostendatur.
units.tr: Reason 1: because he is truly God and man, such as was foretold by the prophets. Let some oracles be briefly applied, and from them let both natures be shown.

units.la: Gen. 3. Semen mulieris conteret caput serpentis. Ex contritione capitis serpentis Deitas: ex eo quod semen mulieris, Humanitas.
units.tr: Gen. 3: "The seed of the woman shall bruise the head of the serpent." From the bruising of the serpent's head, the Deity; from the fact that he is the seed of the woman, the humanity.

units.la: Ies.7. Vocabis nomen eius Immanuel. Deus quia Immanuel: Homo, quia puer comedens butyrum & mel, &c.
units.tr: Isa. 7: "You shall call his name Immanuel." God, because Immanuel; man, because a boy eating butter and honey, etc.

units.la: Ies.9. Puer natus, &c. Deus, quia Filius absolute, nempe Dei, habens principatum & regnū æternum. Deus fortis, &c. Homo, quia puer na-tus, &c.
units.tr: Isa. 9: "A child is born," etc. God, because the Son absolutely, namely of God, having dominion and an eternal kingdom: "Mighty God," etc. Man, because "a child is born," etc.

units.la: Ier.23. Suscitabo Davidi justum germen: Deus, quia rex spiritualis: Item servabit Israelem. Item: Iuda in eo sperabit. Item: vocabitur Iehova ju-stitia nostra. Homo, quia germen Davidis.
units.tr: Jer. 23: "I will raise up to David a righteous branch": God, because a spiritual king; likewise "he will save Israel"; likewise "in him Judah will hope"; likewise "he shall be called Jehovah our righteousness." Man, because the branch of David.

units.la: Ratio 11. quia natus est homo plane secundum proph. oracula. Subiiciantur breviter præcipuæ circumstantiæ, quomodo prædictæ & impletæ.
units.tr: Reason 2: because he was born a man in plain accordance with the prophetic oracles. The principal circumstances, how they were foretold and fulfilled, are to be set out briefly.

units.la: 1. Tempus: Natus est sceptro ablato Gen.49. & Luc.2.
units.tr: 1. Time: "He was born when the sceptre was taken away," Gen. 49; and Luke 2.

units.la: 2. Locus: In Bethlehem Mich. 5. & Matth. 2. Luc. 2.
units.tr: 2. Place: "In Bethlehem," Mic. 5; and Matt. 2; Luke 2.

units.la: 3. Familia: Exposteritate Davidis. Ier.23. Suscitabo Davidi: & Luc.1. 27. Angelus mittitur ad virginem è domo David.
units.tr: 3. Family: "from the posterity of David," Jer. 23: "I will raise up to David"; and Luke 1:27: "The angel is sent to a virgin from the house of David."

units.la: 4. Parentes: Ex virgine. Gen.3. Semen mulie-ris. Ief.7. Ecce virgo: & Matth.1.
units.tr: 4. Parents: "from a virgin," Gen. 3: "the seed of the woman"; Isa. 7: "Behold, a virgin"; and Matt. 1.

units.la: 5. De Spiritu Sancto. Ief.7. Iehova dabit signum & Luc.1.
units.tr: 5. "Of the Holy Spirit," Isa. 7: "Jehovah will give a sign"; and Luke 1.

units.la: 6. Pauper & contemtus Zach.9.Ief.53. & Luc. 2. in stabulo: agnitus a paucis iisque contemtis, Maria, Ioseph, Zacharia, Elisabeth, Pastoribus, Anna, Simeone, piscatoribus, &c. Ioh.7.48. Nū quis ex primoribus, &c.
units.tr: 6. Poor and despised: Zech. 9; Isa. 53; and Luke 2: in a stable; known to few, and those despised: Mary, Joseph, Zechariah, Elizabeth, the shepherds, Anna, Simeon, fishermen, etc. John 7:48: "Has any one of the rulers believed in him?" etc.

units.la: 7. Sed habens tamen testimonia divina, quis & quantus sit.
units.tr: 7. But nevertheless having the divine testimonies of who and how great he is.

units.la: In Veteri Testamento prophetarum, quæ non necesse est repetere.
units.tr: In the Old Testament, the prophecies of the prophets, which need not be repeated.

units.la: In Novo 1. Angelorum. Gabriel nunciat conceptionem virgini, prædicat filium Dei, chorus Angelorum nativitatem nunciat pastoribus. Evangelizo vobis gaudium magnum, &c. Natus est vobis Servator, Christus Dominus, &c. Hymno gratulantur Deo & Ecclesiæ. Gloria in excelsis, &c.
units.tr: In the New: 1. of the angels. Gabriel announces the conception to the virgin and proclaims the Son of God; a host of angels announces the birth to the shepherds: "I bring you good tidings of great joy," etc. "To you is born a Saviour, Christ the Lord," etc. They congratulate God and the Church with a hymn: "Glory to God in the highest," etc.

units.la: 2. Spiritus Sancti prophetantis in Zacharia, Anna, Simeone de nato puero.
units.tr: 2. Of the Holy Spirit prophesying in Zechariah, Anna and Simeon concerning the child who was born.

units.la: 3. Doctrinæ & Miraculorum quibus se Filiu[?] Dei Deum demonstravit: Ioh.5. Opera quæ fa-cio testantur de me.
units.tr: 3. Of the teaching and miracles by which he showed himself to be the Son of God and God: John 5: "The works that I do bear witness of me."

units.la: III. Cur factus pauper, & quas divitias nobis conferat.
units.tr: III. Why he was made poor, and what riches he confers on us.

units.la: Propter vos, ut vos eius paupertate ditescere-tis: Transferad thefin: non solis Corinthiis sed omnibus Christi membris hoc dictum.
units.tr: For your sakes, that you through his poverty might be enriched: Transfer the thesis: this saying applies not only to the Corinthians but to all members of Christ.

units.la: Præmitte non causas.
units.tr: Premise the causes not.

units.la: 1. Pauper factus est, non vi, non infortunio, aut casu, aut culpa, &c. ut multi divites depauperantur, sed voluntarie: quia sponte Deus factus homo, Dominus omnium servus egens, passus, mortuus, &c. Matth.20.28. Filius hominis venit, &c.
units.tr: 1. He became poor not by force, not by misfortune, chance or fault, etc., as many rich men are impoverished, but voluntarily: because God, made man of his own accord, the Lord of all, became a needy servant, suffered, died, etc. Matt. 20.28. The Son of man came, etc.

units.la: 2. Non propter se: quia ipse αὐτὸς πλούσιος: Deus benedictus super omnia: Filius unigenitus & hæres omnium.
units.tr: 2. Not on his own account: for he himself is autos plousios [αὐτὸς πλούσιος]: God blessed above all things; the only-begotten Son and heir of all.

units.la: Reiiciatur opinio scholasticorum, quod sibi sit meritus pauperta-te divitias, humilitate exaltationem, &c. Lomb.l.3.d.18.
units.tr: Let the opinion of the Schoolmen be rejected, that he merited for himself riches by poverty and exaltation by humility, etc. Lombard, bk. 3, dist. 18.

units.la: Per ἀνθρώπων subiiciatur vera causa: Propter Nos. Nostra salus: ut nos ditaret, &c. Zach.9. Ecce rex tuus venit tibi. Isef. 9. Puer natus est nobis, &c. Luc.2. Vobis hodie natus est Servator, &c. Athanasius in symbolo: Propter nos homines & propter nostram salutem descendit de cœlo.
units.tr: Let the true cause be set down in place of per anthrōpōn [διὰ ἀνθρώπων]: On account of us. Our salvation: that he might enrich us, etc. Zech. 9. Behold, your king comes to you. Isa. 9. A child is born to us, etc. Luke 2. To you is born today a Saviour, etc. Athanasius in the creed: For us men and for our salvation he came down from heaven.

units.la: Illustretur a causis impellentibus. 1. nostra egestas, miseria: Eramus filij iræ: Eph.2.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated from the moving causes. 1. Our need and misery: We were children of wrath: Eph. 2.

units.la: 2. Immensus amor Dei Patris, mittentis Filium Servatorem: Ioh.3. 1. Ioh.4.9.
units.tr: 2. The immense love of God the Father, who sent the Son as Saviour: John 3. 1 John 4.9.

units.la: 3. Dilectio Filii erga nos. 1. Ioh.3.16. Eph.5. ver.2. πάθος per exclamationem: O ineffabilem bonitatem, dilectionem, &c.
units.tr: 3. The love of the Son toward us. 1 John 3.16. Eph. 5.2. The emotion expressed by exclamation: O ineffable goodness, love, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur comparatione quorundam, qui forte pro amicis, pro patria, &c, occubuerunt: ut Curtius, Cleombrotus, &c. quorum laus inges: sed nihil ad Christi gloriam. quia 1. isti pro amicis, patria, &c. Christus pro nobis peccatoribus, hostibus. Rom.5.10.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by comparison with certain men who perhaps died for friends, for country, etc., such as Curtius, Cleombrotus, etc., whose praise is great: but nothing compared with the glory of Christ. For, 1. those men died for friends, country, etc.; Christ for us sinners, enemies. Rom. 5.10.

units.la: 2. isti spe inanis gloriolae vel ostentatione, &c. Christus misericordia & amore nostrae salutis.
units.tr: 2. Those men did so from the hope of a vain little glory, or from display, etc.; Christ from mercy and love for our salvation.

units.la: 3. Isti suo interitu commoda quaedam externa suis pepererunt, quae qualia fuerint breviter indica. Christus sua paupertate nobis coelestes divitias contulit.
units.tr: 3. Those men by their death procured for their own people certain external advantages, which we briefly indicate, of whatever kind they were. Christ by his poverty conferred on us heavenly riches.

units.la: Refutentur qui terrenas opes in Christo quaerunt, sicut Papa cum suis praetextu Christi regna & opes mundi ad se rapuit.
units.tr: Let those be refuted who seek earthly wealth in Christ, as the Pope with his followers, under the pretext of Christ, has seized kingdoms and the wealth of the world for himself.

units.la: Ostendatur regnum & divitias Christi non esse de hoc mundo, sed spirituales coelestes & aeternas quas fures non rapiunt Matth.6.20.
units.tr: Let it be shown that the kingdom and riches of Christ are not of this world, but spiritual, heavenly and eternal, which thieves do not steal. Matt. 6.20.

units.la: Enumerentur praecipua Christi beneficia: gratia Dei, reconciliatio, adoptio, remissio peccatorum, justificatio, sanctificatio, fides, resipiscentia, pax, dilectio, spes, timor Dei, patientia, constantia, vita & salus aeterna.
units.tr: Let the chief benefits of Christ be enumerated: the grace of God, reconciliation, adoption, forgiveness of sins, justification, sanctification, faith, repentance, peace, love, hope, the fear of God, patience, constancy, eternal life and salvation.

units.la: Proba brevissime ex Ioh.3. & 5. Rom.4. Mortuus propter, &c. 1.Cor.1. Factus est nobis &c.
units.tr: Let it be proved very briefly from John 3 and 5, Rom. 4. He was dead on account of, etc. 1 Cor. 1. He was made for us, etc.

units.la: Exaggeretur horum bonorum praestantia, quod non auro non omnibus mundi thesauris emuntur, sine istis opes aliae nihil prosunt: sine opibus aliis haec ad salutem sufficiunt. Psal. 49. Matth. 16. Luc.12. & Psal.144.15. Psal.146.5.
units.tr: Let the excellence of these goods be magnified: that they are not bought with gold or with all the treasures of the world; without them other riches profit nothing; without other riches these suffice for salvation. Ps. 49. Matt. 16. Luke 12. and Ps. 144.15. Ps. 146.5.

units.la: Posthac dicatur, quomodo & quos Christus ditarit & ditet sua paupertate: Figuretur interrogatione occupatoria: An non ἀπροσδόξον[?], paupertate Christi nos ditari? an Irus dabit opes? an non poterat aliter quam paupertate ditare?
units.tr: Next let it be said how and whom Christ has enriched and enriches by his poverty. Let it be presented by an occupying question: Are we not enriched by the poverty of Christ, unexpectedly? Will Irus give wealth? Could he not enrich us otherwise than by poverty?

units.la: Resp. 1. Fuit Irus in mundo, sed Croesso opulentior & potetior in cœlo quia Deus. Dominus de cœlo, &c. Ergo potest dare bona quæ habuit & simul etiam quibus sponte caruit, &c.
units.tr: Answer: 1. Irus was in the world, but more opulent and powerful than Croesus in heaven, because he is God. The Lord from heaven, etc. Therefore he can give the goods which he had and also those which he willingly lacked, etc.

units.la: 2. Poterat quidem aliter nos ditare, quam per suam paupertatem: in quantum Deus absolutæ potentiæ. Matth. 19. 26.
units.tr: 2. Indeed he could enrich us otherwise than through his poverty, insofar as he is God of absolute power. Matt. 19.26.

units.la: 3. Non poterat aliter, propter obstantem justitiam & veritatem divinam, cui satisfieri oportuit paupertate Mediatoris.
units.tr: 3. He could not otherwise, on account of the opposing justice and truth of God, which had to be satisfied by the poverty of the Mediator.

units.la: 4. Quomodo ditati? Merito & efficacia: declaretur breviter ex dictis 1. Ioh. 1. Sanguis Iesu Christi, &c. 1. Cor. 6. Justificati estis, &c. Eph. 2. Deus dives misericordia vivificavit, &c. Ioh. 10. Ego ovibus meis do vitam aeternam, &c.
units.tr: 4. How were we enriched? By merit and efficacy: let it be declared briefly from what has been said: 1 John 1. The blood of Jesus Christ, etc. 1 Cor. 6. You were justified, etc. Eph. 2. God, rich in mercy, quickened us, etc. John 10. I give to my sheep eternal life, etc.

units.la: 5. Quos? Non solos Corinthios, sed omnes credentes: Luc. 2. Quod erit toti populo. Matth. 1. Salvum faciet populum suum. Populus autem eius sunt omnes credentes Psal. 110. Populus tuus sponta-neus, &c. Ioh. 1. Quotquot eum receperunt, his dedit, &c. Ioh. 3. Qui credit, &c. Qui non credit, &c.
units.tr: 5. Whom? Not the Corinthians only, but all believers: Luke 2. Which shall be to all the people. Matt. 1. He shall save his people. Now his people are all believers. Ps. 110. Your people are willing, etc. John 1. As many as received him, to them he gave, etc. John 3. He who believes, etc. He who does not believe, etc.

units.la: Claudatur reiectione opinionis contrariæ: quod etiam infideles ditet, &c.
units.tr: Let it be closed by rejecting the contrary opinion: that he enriches even unbelievers, etc.

units.la: πενίασμα[?] 1. Cum propter nos ditandos Christus fit factus pauper: sumus igitur omnes natura egeni, miseri, &c. spiritualiter, quia omnes veris divitiis destituti. Hæc vera & extrema pauper-tas, quam non sentientes verè sunt miseri, licet auro plenas possideant. Luc. 12. 21. Hanc agnoscere est felicitatis principium. Matth. 5. Beati pauperes spiritu. Ratio quia saturantur à Christo æternis bonis. Luc. 1. 53. Hortare ad horum bonorum desiderium quia hæc avaritia sola ho[?]ecta & salutaris: Quaerite regnum Dei, &c. Parate vobis thesauros, &c.
units.tr: penias-ma [πενίασμα]? 1. Since Christ was made poor to enrich us, we are therefore all by nature needy, wretched, etc., spiritually, because all are destitute of true riches. This is the true and extreme poverty, which those who do not feel it truly are wretched, although they possess coffers full of gold. Luke 12.21. To acknowledge this is the beginning of happiness. Matt. 5. Blessed are the poor in spirit. Reason: because they are satisfied by Christ with eternal goods. Luke 1.53. Exhort to the desire of these goods, because this is the only and saving avarice: Seek the kingdom of God, etc. Make for yourselves treasures, etc.

units.la: II. Cum sola Christi paupertate ditescamus: non ergo quaerendae opes in nostra arca, hoc est, justitia & salus in nostris meritis. Reiciatur Papistarum doctrina de lib.arbit. de operib.praeparatoriis, meritoriis, supererogatoriis, &c. tanquam impia, derogans gloriae Christi, & stulta, ostendens miseris mendicis carbones pro thesauris. Ief.64. Omnes justitiae nostrae. 1. Cor. 1. Qui gloriatur in Domino glorietur, &c.
units.tr: II. Since we are enriched by the poverty of Christ alone, riches are not therefore to be sought in our own chest, that is, righteousness and salvation in our own merits. Let the doctrine of the Papists concerning free will, preparatory, meritorious and supererogatory works, etc., be rejected as impious, derogating from the glory of Christ, and foolish, showing miserable beggars coals for treasures. Isa. 64. All our righteousnesses. 1 Cor. 1. He who glories, let him glory in the Lord, etc.

units.la: III. Cum propter nos susceperit terrenam paupertatem, non pudeat nos paupertatis ignominiae crucis Christi.
units.tr: III. Since for our sake he took on earthly poverty, let us not be ashamed of the disgrace of poverty of the cross of Christ.

units.la: Ratio ab utili. [?]Est salus Ecclesiae: & a contrario inutilis: Accommodetur huc dictum Hieronymi: 'Postquam Ecclesia ad Christianos principes venit, potentia quidem & divitiis maior, sed virtutibus minor est facta.'
units.tr: Reason from usefulness. It is the salvation of the Church: and from the contrary, it is unprofitable. Let the saying of Jerome be applied here: 'After the Church came to Christian princes, it became greater in power and riches, but less in virtues.'

units.la: IV. Cum nos Christus sua paupertate ditarit, &c. merito hortatur Apostolus, ut & nos pauperum egestati succurramus. Gal.6.v.9.10.&c.
units.tr: IV. Since Christ has enriched us by his poverty, etc., the Apostle rightly exhorts us also to succour the needs of the poor. Gal. 6.9-10, etc.

units.la: Conclusio breviter repetat summam partium, & praecipuae doctrinae de persona & beneficiis Christi: & hortetur ad gratitudinem: Cum propter nos sit factus pauper: & nos tantis bonis ditarit, simus igitur grati, &c. & celebremus misericordiam aeterni Patris, & amorem Filii nobis dati & nati, &c.
units.tr: Conclusion: let it briefly repeat the sum of the parts and of the chief doctrine concerning the person and benefits of Christ, and exhort to gratitude: since he was made poor for us, and has enriched us with so great goods, let us therefore be thankful, etc., and let us celebrate the mercy of the eternal Father and the love of the Son given and born for us, etc.

units.la: Claudatur gratiarum actione ad Filium Dei, quod propter nos, cum esset dives, dignatus est nasci pauper, &c. quod nos famelicos explet bonis, nis,donat remissionem peccatorum,justitia,Spi-ritu Sancto, &c. accendit inter nos lucem verae doctrinae,& colligit Ecclesiam,&c. & dum mundus ubique crepitat ruinis,&c. confervat pacem & politiam: dat pios magistratus qui Ecclesiam afflictam curent,defendant, alant egena Christi membra. Et precatione: ut hæc tanta bona porro servet,augeat, tueatur Ecclesiam, fulciat ruinas imperii contra Turcas,Tyrannos, ne deleatur in vocatio nominis Dei in his terris: Servet Electo rem pium Ecclesiæ nutritium, roboret Spiritu fortitudinis & sapientiæ, &c. ut pax & veritas floreat:& Deus celebretur. AMEN.
units.tr: Let it be closed with thanksgiving to the Son of God, that for our sake, though he was rich, he deigned to be born poor, etc.; that he fills us who are hungry with good things, grants us forgiveness of sins, righteousness, the Holy Spirit, etc.; kindles among us the light of true doctrine and gathers the Church, etc.; and while the world everywhere cracks with ruins, etc., preserves peace and government; gives pious magistrates who care for the afflicted Church, defend it, and feed the needy members of Christ. And with a prayer: that he would keep, increase and guard these so great goods and the Church, prop up the ruins of the empire against the Turks and tyrants, lest the calling upon the name of God be destroyed in these lands; keep the pious Elector, nurse of the Church, strengthen him with the Spirit of fortitude and wisdom, etc., so that peace and truth may flourish and God be celebrated. AMEN.

units.la: Exercitatio IV.
units.tr: Exercitatio IV.

units.la: De fructibus resurrectionis Christi.
units.tr: On the Fruits of Christ's Resurrection.

units.la: EXordium sit approbatio consuetudinis Scho-lasticæ, quod hoc tempore ex hoc loco quot-annis repeti soleat memoria resurrectionis Chri-sti a mortuis.
units.tr: The exordium is the approval of scholastic custom, namely that at this season the memory of Christ's resurrection from the dead is customarily repeated from this text every year.

units.la: Ratio approbat: ab honesto: quia ordinem scholasticum præcipuè decet celebrare benefi-cia Christi hoc tempore Ecclesiæ parta.
units.tr: The reason for approval is drawn from what is honourable: it is fitting that the scholastic order especially celebrate, at this season, the benefits of Christ won for the Church.

units.la: Occupatio: Etsi tibi sis conscius tuæ infantiæ, & pro more utendum esset excusatione: tamen etiam sine hac te polliceri tibi veniam.. 1. Quia nulla ingenii fiducia, sed jussu præceptorum, dicendi partes in te susceperis. II. Quia in his exercitiis juventutis vel conatus laudari soleat. III. Quia speres in argumenti dignitatem potius quâ in dicentis facultatem intentos fore.
units.tr: Occupatio: Although you are aware of your own youth, and by custom an excuse ought to be used, nevertheless you may promise yourself pardon even without this excuse. (1) Because you have taken on the parts of speaking not from any confidence in your talent but at the command of your teachers; (2) because in these exercises the efforts of young people are customarily praised; (3) because you hope that the audience will be attentive to the dignity of the subject rather than to the speaker's ability.

units.la: Transitio per ἀποσιώπησιν[?]. Itaque te omissa pro-lixiore excusatione ad rem ipsam transiturum, atque dicturum de gloriosa servatoris nostri re-surrectione ex mortuis:
units.tr: Transition by aposiopesis[?]. Therefore, leaving aside a lengthier excuse, you will pass to the matter itself and speak of the glorious resurrection of our Saviour from the dead:

units.la: Adde votum: Invoco te fili Dei mortue pro nobis ac resuscitate,ut spiritu tuo mentes nostras illumines,&c.
units.tr: Add a prayer: I call upon you, O Son of God, who died and were raised again for us, that by your Spirit you would enlighten our minds, etc.

units.la: Propositio 1. Repetam praecipuas quasdam hi-storiae partes ad fidei confirmationem.
units.tr: Proposition: (1) I will recall certain principal parts of the history, for the confirmation of faith.

units.la: II. Qui sint fructus resurrectionis Domini ad consolationem.
units.tr: (2) What the fruits of the Lord's resurrection are, for consolation.

units.la: III. Ad quos hi fructus pertineant ad com-monefactionem nostram.
units.tr: (3) To whom these fruits pertain, for our admonition.

units.la: I. De resurrectionis historia.
units.tr: I. On the history of the resurrection.

units.la: Historia petenda ex Evangelistis, quorum ordinem sequar. circumstantiae praecipue tres: Tempus, modus, putefactio:
units.tr: The history is to be taken from the Evangelists, whose order I will follow. There are chiefly three circumstances: time, manner, and manifestation.

units.la: I. Tertio die resurrexit Ioh. 20. primo die he-bdomadis.
units.tr: I. He rose on the third day, John 20, on the first day of the week.

units.la: Ostende triduum: sexto die, qui erat parasceve Judaeorum exspiraverat. Ἐπίδειξις[?]. Verus ergo Messias.
units.tr: Show that it was three days: on the sixth day, which was the Preparation of the Jews, he had expired. Demonstration[?]. Therefore he is the true Messiah.

units.la: Ratio: Quia ipse solus & nullus alius resurrexit tertio die secundum Scripturas, 1. Cor. 15.4. Matt.17.23.juxta typum Jonae. Matt.12.40.
units.tr: Reason: because he alone, and no one else, rose on the third day according to the Scriptures, 1 Cor. 15:4; Matt. 17:23, in accordance with the type of Jonah, Matt. 12:40.

units.la: Amplifica ab effectu hujus circumstantiae: quod inde primum diem hebdomadis Christiani sacrum celebremus.
units.tr: Amplify from the effect of this circumstance: that from then on we celebrate the first day of the Christian week as holy.

units.la: 1. Resurrexit vere a mortuis, h.e:anima vere ad corpus rediit, à quo per mortem fuerat avulsa: & corpus non aliud, sed idem quod ceciderat resurrexit.
units.tr: 1. He truly rose from the dead, that is, his soul truly returned to the body from which it had been torn away by death, and the body that rose was not another but the same that had fallen.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia quod λόγῳ[?] semel assumfit, in æternum non deponit. 2. nostra natura debuit ut mori, ita etiam resurgere, 1. Cor. 15: Per hominem mors & resurrectio. 3. Christus prædixerat eúdem filium hominis moriturum & resurrecturum: Et angelus: Surrexit: non est hic. Amplific.à notatione vocis Resurgere.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because what the Word once assumed, it does not put off for eternity. 2. Our nature had to die and so also rise again, 1 Cor. 15: Through man came death and resurrection. 3. Christ had foretold that the Son of Man would die and rise again; and the angel: He has risen, he is not here. Amplify from the wording of the term to rise again.

units.la: Πόρισμα[?] Ergo nec anima nec corpus Christi fuerunt ubique.
units.tr: Corollary[?]. Therefore neither the soul nor the body of Christ was everywhere.

units.la: 11. Resurrexit idem corpus, sed glorificatum, h.e, incorruptibile, immortale, spirituale, expers infirmitatum, ornatum gloria ac donis cœlestibus, &c. non deificatum, immensum[?], ubiquitarium, absq; proprietatib.essentialib.naturæ humanæ.
units.tr: 2. The same body rose, but glorified, that is, incorruptible, immortal, spiritual, free from infirmities, adorned with glory and heavenly gifts, etc.; not deified, immense, ubiquitous, and without the essential properties of human nature.

units.la: Probetur: Præcedet vos in Galilæam: Seminatur corpus corruptibile, &c. (conformabit mortalia corpora nostra gloriosō corpori suo. Manebunt tamen vera corpora. 2. Cor. 5. Non cupimus exui, sed superindui, ut absorbeatur mortalitas à vita. Augustin[?] ad Dard: Gloria carni immortalitatem dedit, naturam non abstulit.
units.tr: Let it be proved: "He will go before you into Galilee"; "The corruptible body is sown," etc.; "He will conform our mortal bodies to his glorious body." Nevertheless true bodies will remain. 2 Cor. 5: "We do not wish to be unclothed, but to be further clothed, so that mortality may be swallowed up by life." Augustine to Dardanus: Glory gave immortality to the flesh; it did not take away its nature.

units.la: 111. Resurrexit propria potentia : non carnis (quia hæc mortua erat) sed divinitatis suæ.
units.tr: 3. He rose by his own power, not by the power of the flesh (since this was dead), but by his divinity.

units.la: Probetur 1. Ex terræmotu, in quo haud dubie Dominus resurrexit.
units.tr: Let it be proved (1) from the earthquake, in which without doubt the Lord rose.

units.la: Ratio à fine, qui fuit, non modo ut hostes terreret, sed ut divinam potentiam resurgens Christus mundo declararet.
units.tr: Reason from the end, which was not only to terrify the enemies, but that Christ, rising by his divine power, might declare it to the world.

units.la: Occupatio : descendit angelus de coelo ac devolvit lapidem : sed non ut liberaret Christum occlusum. Vera causa : ut esset praeco divinæ potentiæ, & resurrectionis Christi. Item, ut serviret gloriæ resurgentis & quasi gratularetur victori.
units.tr: Objection: an angel descended from heaven and rolled away the stone; but not to free Christ, who was shut in. True cause: that he might be the herald of the divine power and of Christ's resurrection. Likewise that he might serve the glory of the risen one and, as it were, congratulate the victor.

units.la: II. Ex verbis angeli: Surrexit sicut dixit. Dixerat autem: Habeo potestatem ponendi & sumendi animam meam: Ego readificabo templum hoc, &c.
units.tr: II. From the words of the angel: He has risen as he said. Now he had said: I have power to lay down and take up my soul; I will rebuild this temple, etc.

units.la: Obiectio : Pater excitavit filium, Actor.2. & 3. Eph.1.
units.tr: Objection: the Father raised up the Son, Acts 2 and 3; Eph. 1.

units.la: Respond. Sed per ipsum filium, Ioh.5: Pater o-peratur & ego operor. Item, qua pater facit, filius si-militer facit. Item, mortificatus carne vivificatus spiritu.
units.tr: Answer: but through the Son himself, John 5: My Father works and I work. Likewise, whatever the Father does, the Son does in like manner. Likewise, put to death in the flesh, made alive in the Spirit.

units.la: πνεῦμα[?]. Ergo verus Deus, Rom.1. 4: Declaratus, &c.
units.tr: Spirit[?]. Therefore the true God, Rom. 1:4: declared, etc.

units.la: Ratio : quia propria potentia mortem a se depulit.
units.tr: Reason: because by his own power he drove death away from himself.

units.la: Consolatio : Ergo & nos membra sua vivificare poterit. Ego suscitabo eum, &c.
units.tr: Consolation: therefore he will also be able to quicken his members. I will raise him up, etc.

units.la: Patefactio fuit necessaria: propter fidem & consolationem nostram: Thesaurus defossus nulli prodest. Facta est autem. 1. Testimonio angeli. 2. apparitionibus Christi.
units.tr: The manifestation was necessary, on account of our faith and consolation: a buried treasure profits no one. It was made, however: (1) by the testimony of the angel; (2) by the appearances of Christ.

units.la: 1. Testimonium angeli ad mulieres: Quid quæritis viventem cum mortuis? Surrexit: præcedet vos in Galilæam sicut dixit.
units.tr: (1) The angel's testimony to the women: Why do you seek the living among the dead? He has risen; he will go before you into Galilee, as he said.

units.la: Cur ad mulieres ? 1. ut primæ nuncium vitæ accipiant, quæ primæ mortem in mundum invexerant. 2. ut primæ gaudeant, quæ maxime doluerant. 3. Quia primæ Christum quæsiverant:
units.tr: Why to the women? (1) so that the first to receive the news of life should be those who had first brought death into the world; (2) so that those who had grieved most should be the first to rejoice; (3) because they had been the first to seek Christ.

units.la: II. Apparitiones Christi redivivi plures per totos dies 40.
units.tr: II. Apparitions of the risen Christ, several, over the whole course of 40 days.

units.la: 1. Mariae Magdalenae in horto, ipso mane resurrectionis, Ioh.20.Mar.16.
units.tr: 1. To Mary Magdalene in the garden, early on the morning of the resurrection, John 20; Mark 16.

units.la: 2. Duobus Emaunta proficiscentibus eodem die, Marc.16.12.Luc.24.
units.tr: 2. To two men going to Emmaus on the same day, Mark 16:12; Luke 24.

units.la: 3. Discipulis congregatis metu Judaeorum, eadem vespera, Luc24.Ioh.20.
units.tr: 3. To the disciples gathered together for fear of the Jews, the same evening, Luke 24; John 20.

units.la: 4. Iisdem eodem loco congregatis cum Thomaincredulo post dies 8.
units.tr: 4. To the same men, gathered in the same place with Thomas the unbeliever, after eight days.

units.la: 5. Petro & sociis piscantibus ad mare Tyberiadis, Ioh.21.
units.tr: 5. To Peter and his companions fishing by the sea of Tiberias, John 21.

units.la: 6. Amplius quam quingentis fratribus, 1.Cor.15. Recita ordinem apparitionum ex Paulo ibid.
units.tr: 6. To more than five hundred brethren, 1 Cor. 15. Recite the order of the appearances from Paul, ibid.

units.la: Subjice utilitates ex causis: cur non mox ascē-derit, sed toties se patefecerit.
units.tr: Add the uses, from the causes: why he did not ascend at once, but showed himself so many times.

units.la: 1. ut fides nostra esset certa de resurrectione ejus: basis omnis consolationis, 1.Cor.15. Probaid-eo apparuisse. Discipuli non credunt: Maria plorat: Sustulerunt Dominum, &c. Ipse ergo redivivus apparet, & jubet nunciare fratrib. suis, ut credat. Ioh.20. Et Luc.24. O stulti, nonne oportuit Christum haec pati & resurgere.
units.tr: 1. So that our faith might be certain concerning his resurrection, the basis of all consolation, 1 Cor. 15. Prove that he therefore appeared. The disciples do not believe; Mary weeps: They have taken away the Lord, etc. He therefore appears risen again and bids them announce to his brethren that they should believe, John 20; and Luke 24: O foolish ones, was it not necessary for Christ to suffer these things and to rise?

units.la: Occupatio: Frustra Judæi eludunt apparitiones ob testium vilitatem.
units.tr: Objection: The Jews vainly deride the appearances on account of the worthlessness of the witnesses.

units.la: 1. Quia non solæ mulieres & discipuli: sed & angeli.
units.tr: 1. Because they were not only women and disciples, but also angels.

units.la: 2. apparitiones multæ & multis factæ.
units.tr: 2. The appearances were many and made to many.

units.la: 3. à quatuor Evangelistis tùm descriptæ, cum historia publicè nota esset. In ore trium, &c.
units.tr: 3. They were described by all four evangelists, at a time when the history was publicly known. In the mouth of three witnesses, etc.

units.la: Amplific.à causa, cur non Pilato, Herodi ap-paruerit: ne hominum authoritate, sed divinis testitestimoniis niteretur fides nostra, Joh. 20: Beati qui credunt 1.Cor.1.Ne evacuetur crux (Christi, &c.
units.tr: Amplification from the cause: why he did not appear to Pilate or Herod: so that our faith might rest not on the authority of men but on divine testimonies, John 20: Blessed are those who believe; 1 Cor. 1: Lest the cross (of Christ, etc.) be made void.

units.la: II. ut de veritate resurrectionis constaret: contra somnia Marcionis, Eutychis: & aliorum: de spectro deificato, ubiquitario, &c.
units.tr: II. So that it might be established concerning the truth of the resurrection, against the dreams of Marcion, Eutyches, and others: concerning a deified, ubiquitous specter, etc.

units.la: Proba ideo toties apparuisse ex Luc. 24: ubi negat se spectrum: Probat verum corpus palpabile, finitum, locale a propriis. Et Ioh. 20. Mitte manum tuam in latus meum & ne sis incredulus.
units.tr: Prove that he therefore appeared so often, from Luke 24, where he denies that he is a specter, and proves a true body, palpable, finite, local, and distinct from its own. And John 20: Put your hand into my side, and do not be unbelieving.

units.la: Obiectio I. Non agnoscitur a Maria & discipulis.
units.tr: Objection I. He is not recognized by Mary and the disciples.

units.la: Ergo non erat idem.
units.tr: Therefore it was not the same.

units.la: Resp. Reteri[?] sunt oculi ne agnosceret. Luc. 24.
units.tr: Response. Their eyes were restrained so that they would not recognize him. Luke 24.

units.la: Obiectio II. Repente evanuit: Ergo habet corpus invisibile, aërium, spirituale.
units.tr: Objection II. He suddenly vanished. Therefore he has an invisible, aerial, spiritual body.

units.la: Respond. 1. Rursus retenti sunt oculi ne viderent. ἀφαντος[?] ἀπ' αὐτῶν.
units.tr: Response 1. Again, their eyes were restrained so that they would not see. [He was] invisible [or: vanished] from them.

units.la: 2. Fuit corpus spirituale, sed non spiritus: h. est, dotib. non essentia seu μετοχὴ[?].
units.tr: 2. It was a spiritual body, but not a spirit; that is, spiritual in its endowments, not in its essence or participation.

units.la: Obiectio III. Penetravit saxum & fores clausas. Ergo corpus illocale, ubique existens.
units.tr: Objection III. He penetrated the stone and the closed doors. Therefore a body not local, existing everywhere.

units.la: Respond. 1. antecedens non est in textu. 2. nulla consequentia a penetratione ad ubiquitatem. Ratio: etiam spiritus creati penetrant corpora, nec sunt ubique. 3. penetratio evertit scopum apparitionis: pugnat cum verbis Christi: non sum Spiritus, &c. & in utroque miraculo corpus Christi fuit in suo u B I[?], mutavit locum, non simul fuit intus & foris 4. Hieronymus ad Pammachium: creatura nonne cederet creatori?
units.tr: Response. 1. The antecedent is not in the text. 2. There is no consequence from penetration to ubiquity. Reason: even created spirits penetrate bodies, and they are not everywhere. 3. Penetration overturns the purpose of the appearance; it conflicts with the words of Christ: "I am not a spirit," etc.; and in both miracles the body of Christ was in its own place, it changed place, it was not at once inside and outside. 4. Jerome to Pammachius: "Would not the creature yield to the Creator?"

units.la: II. De fructibus resurrectio-nis Christi.
units.tr: II. On the fruits of Christ's resurrection.

units.la: Christus non sibi sed nobis resurrexit.
units.tr: Christ rose again not for himself but for us.

units.la: Ratio: Quia non sibi sed nobis natus, passus, mortuus erat.
units.tr: Reason: Because he was born, suffered and died not for himself but for us.

units.la: Adversativa. Etsi plurimos Scriptura recitet tamen tres tantum nunc repetam fructus.
units.tr: Objection answered. Although Scripture recounts very many, I will now recall only three fruits.

units.la: 1. Liberatio a peccato, morte, diabolo: & justificatio coram Deo.
units.tr: 1. Deliverance from sin, death and the devil, and justification before God.

units.la: Ratio prioris: Quia mors fuit lucta[?] cum istis hostibus: Resurrectio victoria & triumphus, Rom.4. Mortuus propter peccata nostra, Hebr.2. Ut per mortem, &c. 1.Cor.15. Si Christus non est excitatus, inanis est fides vestra, de liberatione a peccato & morte per mortem ejus: & adhuc estis in-peccatis vestris.
units.tr: Reason for the first: Because death was a struggle with these enemies; the resurrection is victory and triumph. Rom. 4: He was delivered up for our sins. Heb. 2: That through death, etc. 1 Cor. 15: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain, concerning deliverance from sin and death through his death; and you are still in your sins.

units.la: Infer a contrario sensu. Atqui excitatus est: pri-mitiæ, &c. Ergo firma stat fides nostra de redem-tione per Christum & non amplius sumus in peccatis nostris: Absorpta est mors in victoria.
units.tr: Inferred from the contrary sense. But he has been raised: the firstfruits, etc. Therefore our faith stands firm concerning redemption through Christ, and we are no longer in our sins: Death is swallowed up in victory.

units.la: Ratio posterioris ex priore. Quia absoluti a rea-tu omni, justi sumus coram Deo. Psal.32: Beati quorum remissæ sunt. Rom.4. Resurrexit propter justitiam nostram. Rom.5. Justificati igitur sanguine ejus.
units.tr: Reason for the second, from the first. Because, once absolved from all guilt, we are righteous before God. Ps. 32: Blessed are those whose transgressions are forgiven. Rom. 4: He was raised for our justification. Rom. 5: Therefore, having been justified by his blood.

units.la: Objectio: justificatio hic morti ascribitur.
units.tr: Objection: here justification is ascribed to death.

units.la: Respond. Quia utriusq; eadem beneficia. Distin-guit tamen morti ἀπολυτρωσιν, resurrectioni δικαίω-[?]σιν ascribit Paulus, ut gradib. victoriæ gradus beneficiorum respondeant: & quia mortis perse-ctio à resurrectione pendebat.
units.tr: Answer. Because both have the same benefits. Paul nevertheless distinguishes: he ascribes redemption [ἀπολύτρωσιν] to death and justification [δικαίωσιν] to the resurrection, so that the degrees of benefits correspond to the degrees of victory; and because the completion of death depended on the resurrection.

units.la: Ratio 1. Nam satisfactio sine resurrectione non fuisset perfecta: quia mortem non vicisset. 2. oportuit eundem mereri & conferre beneficia: Ideò non tantùm mori sed & resurgere, 1. Cor. 15. per hominem.
units.tr: Reason: 1. For satisfaction without the resurrection would not have been complete, because it would not have conquered death. 2. It was necessary that the same one should both merit and confer the benefits. Therefore he not only died but also rose again, 1 Cor. 15: through a man.

units.la: 11. Mortificatio veteris & vivificatio novi hominis.
units.tr: 11. The mortification of the old man and the vivification of the new man.

units.la: Ratio: Quia mortuus est & resurrexit, non tantùm in se, sed etiam in membris. Ergo etiam in his abolet peccatum: & vitam novam incoat per Spiritum suum. Ab absurdo: vivo capiti mortua membra non conveniùt. Rom. 6. Sumus consepulti, &c. 2. Cor. 5. Vno mortuo omnes, &c. Col. 3. Sirefurrexistis cum Christo, &c. Hæc prima resurrectio. Apoc. 20. Hanc Spiritus S. operatur per verbum. Ioh. 5. 25. In omnib. membris Christi: Ioh. 15. Omnem palmitem, & c. 2. Cor. 5. Superinduemur si non, &c. Apoc. 20. Beatus qui habet partem.
units.tr: Reason: Because he died and rose again not only in himself but also in his members. Therefore he also abolishes sin in them and begins a new life through his Spirit. Argument from absurdity: dead members do not agree with a living head. Rom. 6: We are buried together, etc. 2 Cor. 5: One died for all, etc. Col. 3: If you have risen with Christ, etc. This is the first resurrection. Rev. 20. The Holy Spirit works this through the Word. John 5:25. In all the members of Christ. John 15: Every branch, etc. 2 Cor. 5: We shall be clothed, if not, etc. Rev. 20: Blessed is he who has a part.

units.la: 111. Suscitatio corporum ex morte & glorificatio æterna.
units.tr: III. The raising of bodies from death and eternal glorification.

units.la: Explica argumentum Pauli, 1. Cor. 15. Christus resurrexit. Ergo mortui resurgent. Ratio conseq. 1. Christi primitiæ, nos massa: ipse caput, Sacerdos, Rex; nos membra, populus, cives. 2. per hominem mors & resurrectio. 3. Christus secundus Adam. 4. Spiritus Christi in nobis. Ergo vivificabit corpora nostra, Rom. 8. 11.
units.tr: Explain Paul's argument, 1 Cor. 15: Christ has risen. Therefore the dead will rise. Reason for the consequence: 1. Christ is the firstfruits, we the lump; he the head, priest, king; we the members, people, citizens. 2. Through a man, death and resurrection. 3. Christ is the second Adam. 4. The Spirit of Christ is in us. Therefore he will quicken our bodies, Rom. 8:11.

units.la: Adde breviter alia duo argumenta Pauli v. 18. & 19. Perirent mortui in Christo: essemus miserrimi, si non resurgeremus potentia Christi.
units.tr: Add briefly two other arguments of Paul, vv. 18 and 19: those who have died in Christ would perish; we would be most wretched if we were not raised by the power of Christ.

units.la: III. Ad quos hi fructus pertineant.
units.tr: III. To whom these fruits pertain.

units.la: Fiat transitio: & ponatur propositio: pertinent ad omnes & solos credentes.
units.tr: Let there be a transition, and let the proposition be stated: they pertain to all and only believers.

units.la: Ratio quia hi soli eos percipiunt.
units.tr: Reason: because only these receive them.

units.la: Probetur minor per partes: Omnes & soli credentes.
units.tr: Let the minor be proved part by part: all and only believers.

units.la: 1. Liberatur, Ioh. 5. 24. & Ioh. 3. 18. 36. Act. 10. 43
units.tr: 1. They are delivered, John 5:24; John 3:18, 36; Acts 10:43.

units.la: 2. Reconciliantur Deo & justificantur. Rom. 3. 28. 30. Heb. 11. 6.
units.tr: 2. They are reconciled to God and justified, Rom. 3:28, 30; Heb. 11:6.

units.la: 3. Regenerantur & excitantur in novam vitam in Christo, Actor. 15. 9. fide purificans corda. Eph. 2. 8. 10. Ioh. 15. Sine me nihil potestis facere.
units.tr: 3. They are regenerated and raised up into new life in Christ, Acts 15:9, faith purifying the hearts; Eph. 2:8, 10; John 15: Without me you can do nothing.

units.la: 4. Resurgent a mortuis per Christum, & glorificabuntur, Ioh. 6. 39. 40. Ioh. 11. 26. Ioh. 17. 24.
units.tr: 4. They will rise from the dead through Christ and be glorified, John 6:39, 40; John 11:26; John 17:24.

units.la: Concludes. Ad solos igitur & omnes credentes pertinent.
units.tr: Conclusion. Therefore these pertain to only and all believers.

units.la: Amplifica a contrario: Impii sine fide neque in re neque ad rem jus habent istorum fructuum: quod est non pertinere. Ioh. 3: Qui non credit super eum manet ira Dei. Si non manseritis in sermone meo, non habetis vitam in vobis. Qui non habet spiritum Christi non est eius.
units.tr: Amplify from the contrary: The impious, without faith, have neither right in fact nor in principle to these fruits, which is to say they do not pertain to them. John 3: He who does not believe, the wrath of God remains on him. If you do not remain in my word, you do not have life in you. He who does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his.

units.la: A correlatis: Si infideles non pertinent ad Christum, seu non sunt Christi. Ergo neq; Christus ad infideles pertinet cum suis fructibus.
units.tr: From correlatives: If unbelievers do not pertain to Christ, or are not Christ's, then neither does Christ pertain to unbelievers with his fruits.

units.la: Obiectio. Christus pro omnibus est mortuus & resurrexit. Ergo ad omnes pertinent fructus.
units.tr: Objection. Christ died and rose for all. Therefore the fruits pertain to all.

units.la: Respond. pro omnibus dignitate & sufficientia Αὐτῶς: pro solis electis sive credentibus efficacia gacia & applicatione fructuum.
units.tr: Answer. He died for all in dignity and sufficiency; for the elect or believers only, in the efficacy of grace and the application of the fruits.

units.la: Clamant hic quidam : hanc esse Saracenicam blasphemiam, negare Christum pro omnibus mortuum.
units.tr: Some here cry out that this is Saracen blasphemy, to deny that Christ died for all.

units.la: Resp. Imò diabolica est calumnia, nos negare cum distinguimus sufficientiam ab efficacia: fideles ab infidelibus: electos a reprobis. Distinguimus autem:
units.tr: Reply. Rather, it is a diabolical calumny for us to deny this, when we distinguish sufficiency from efficacy, believers from unbelievers, the elect from the reprobate. We distinguish, however, as follows:

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia Scriptura distinguit. 1. Cum solis credentibus & electis Christum cum suis beneficiis vendicat, Ioh.10. Pono vitam meam pro ovibus. Ioh.17. Non oro pro mundo sed pro iis quos dedisti mihi. Ioh.3. ut omnis qui credit habeat vitam aeternam. 2. cum incredulis omnib. adimit fructus: Qui non credit: non habet vitam: ira Dei manet super eo.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because Scripture distinguishes. First, it claims Christ with his benefits for believers and the elect alone: John 10: I lay down my life for the sheep. John 17: I do not pray for the world but for those whom you have given me. John 3: that everyone who believes may have eternal life. Second, it denies the fruits to all unbelievers: He who does not believe does not have life; the wrath of God remains upon him.

units.la: Ratio II.[?] Quia tàm experientia quàm Scriptura clamat omnes incredulos ante & post mortem Christi damnatos & damnandos ab utero matris ad extremum usq; spiritum, fuisse & esse filios irae, subditos diaboli, peccati servos & damnari. Matt. 7. Nunquam novi vos. Eph.2. Sumus filii irae, sicut & caeteri: mortui in offensis: Princeps aeris est efficax in homines contumacia. Ergo non in gratia Dei & a peccato efficaciter liberati.
units.tr: Reason II. Because experience as much as Scripture cries out that all unbelievers, before and after Christ's death, have been and are condemned and will be condemned, from the womb of their mother to their last breath, that they have been and are children of wrath, subjects of the devil, servants of sin, and are damned. Matt. 7: I never knew you. Eph. 2: We were children of wrath, as also the rest; dead in trespasses; the prince of the power of the air is at work in the disobedient. Therefore they have not been effectively delivered from sin and placed in the grace of God.

units.la: Ratio III. Quia multi Orthodoxi patres sic distinguunt, Cyrillus, Augustinus, Prosper.
units.tr: Reason III. Because many orthodox Fathers distinguish thus: Cyril, Augustine, Prosper.

units.la: Ratio IV. Quia dogma contrarium repugnat Scripturae & est absurdum.
units.tr: Reason IV. Because the contrary dogma contradicts Scripture and is absurd.

units.la: Explica dogma: Christum pro omnib. mortuū etiam quo ad efficaciā, h.e, omnes tàm incredulos quàm fideles pariter, æque Iudæ ac Petrum morte sua recōciliasse Deo, liberasse ab omni peccato & condemnatione, ita ut omnes reipsa in gratiam, atque in sinum Dei sint recepti, inque eo manent donec incredulitate rursus excidant, & se liberatione ea privent.
units.tr: Explain the dogma: that Christ died for all, even as to efficacy; that is, that all alike, unbelievers and believers, Judas as much as Peter, have been reconciled to God by his death, delivered from all sin and condemnation, so that all are in fact received into favour and into the bosom of God, and remain there until they fall away again through unbelief and deprive themselves of that deliverance.

units.la: Proba quod repugnet Scripturæ[?]: quia secundum hanc soli credentes sint reconciliati, in gratia Dei: liberati a condemnatione, Ioh. 6: Hæc est voluntas eius. Rom. 5. Iustificati fide pacem habemus. Rom. 8. Nulla condemnatio his, &c. Incredduli absolute excluduntur gratia, Ioh. 3. qui non credit iam iudicatus est: super eo manet ira Dei.
units.tr: Prove that it contradicts Scripture: because according to Scripture only believers are reconciled and in the grace of God, delivered from condemnation. John 6: This is his will. Rom. 5: Justified by faith, we have peace. Rom. 8: There is no condemnation for those, etc. Unbelievers are absolutely excluded from grace. John 3: He who does not believe is already judged; the wrath of God remains on him.

units.la: Proba quod sit absurdum: quia
units.tr: Prove that it is absurd, because:

units.la: I. Tollit peccatum originis: Ratio quia statuit omnes homines in Ecclesia & extra eam nasci in gratia: & liberationem a peccato etiam extra promissionem: & sine fide. Contra illud: omnes natu-ra filii iræ.
units.tr: I. It abolishes original sin. Reason: because it holds that all men, both within the Church and outside it, are born in grace, and are delivered from sin even outside the promise and without faith. Against that: all are by nature children of wrath.

units.la: II. Vendicat reconciliationem, gratiam, sinu Dei, fructus mortis & resurrectionis Christi oib. etiam Turcarum, Ethnicorum infantib. morientibus ante actualem incredulitatem.
units.tr: II. It claims reconciliation, grace, the bosom of God, and the fruits of Christ's death and resurrection for all, even for the infants of Turks and heathens dying before actual unbelief.

units.la: III. Evertit iplorūmet dogma de infantib. fideliū extra gratiam & salutem ante Baptismum.
units.tr: III. It overturns the very dogma about the infants of believers, that they are outside grace and salvation before baptism.

units.la: IV. Statuit oēs mortuos sine fide & damnatos ante Christi mortem, Christi morte rursus liberatos, reconciliatos Deo, in gratiam & sinu Dei receptos esse: atque ita denuo vel servatos sine fide: vel damnatos sine incredulitate.
units.tr: IV. It asserts that all who died without faith and were condemned before Christ's death were, by Christ's death, delivered again, reconciled to God, and received into grace and the bosom of God; and thus either saved again without faith or condemned without unbelief.

units.la: V. Incredulitatem vel non esse peccatum, vel fortiorem esse efficacia Christi fingit.
units.tr: V. It feigns either that unbelief is not sin, or that it is stronger than the efficacy of Christ.

units.la: VI. Seipsum eludit: quia fingit infideles sine incredulitate, fideles sine fide, dum ponit, incredu-los nondum adultos (ut sunt omnes ethnicorum infantes) vel etiam adultos barbaros, qui morte Christi nunquam auditam etiam nunquam spreverunt actuali incredulitate, liberatos ab omni peccato (proinde etiam ab incredulitate) ac manere in gratia ac sinu Dei, tantisper dum incredulitate gratiam rursus abjiciant, atque eapropter denuo in aeternum pereant.
units.tr: VI.
