It mocks itself, because it imagines unbelievers without unbelief and believers without faith, while it posits that unbelievers not yet adult (as are all the infants of the heathen), or even adult barbarians, who never heard of Christ's death and so never rejected it by actual unbelief, are freed from all sin (and therefore also from unbelief) and remain in grace and the bosom of God for as long as they do not again cast away grace by unbelief, and for that reason perish again forever.

units.la: VII. Tribuit id incredulis, quod stante doctrina Scripturae, de naturali reatu, nullo unquā momento de iis praedicari possit; quod sint in gratia.
units.tr: VII. This attributes to unbelievers what, with the doctrine of Scripture standing, cannot at any moment be said of them concerning natural guilt: that they are in grace.

units.la: - Conclude: Esse igitur dogma falsum & absurdum: Omnes incredulos & damnatos morte Christi Deo efficaciter reconciliatos.
units.tr: - Conclusion: therefore the dogma is false and absurd: that all unbelievers and the damned have been effectively reconciled to God by the death of Christ.

units.la: Instantia: promissiones Evangelii sunt universales.
units.tr: Objection: the promises of the Gospel are universal.

units.la: Respond. credentib. & agentib. poenitentiam, Matt.11. Venite omnes qui laboratis, Ioh.3. Ut omnis qui credit non pereat. Gal.3. Ut promissio daretur credentibus.
units.tr: Answer: to believers and to those who repent (Matt. 11), "Come to me, all you who labour"; (John 3) "that whoever believes should not perish"; (Gal. 3) "that the promise might be given to believers."

units.la: Instantia: 1. Cor.15. Sicut in Adam omnes moriun-tur: sic in Christo omnes vivificabuntur.
units.tr: Objection: 1 Cor. 15: "As in Adam all die, so in Christ all shall be made alive."

units.la: Respond. In Adamo omnes, qui in eo vel ab eo sunt, moriuntur: naturali propagatione: in Christo etiam omnes, qui in eo sunt (nempe omnes credentes) vivificantur per gratiam.
units.tr: Answer: In Adam all die who are in him or are from him, by natural propagation; in Christ also all are made alive who are in him (namely all believers), through grace.

units.la: Ostende Apostolum ad hos restringere vivifi-cationem.
units.tr: Show that the Apostle restricts this making alive to these.

units.la: Occupatio: Non sequi Adamū fortiorem esse Christo, quia plures ille perdidit, quàm hic servat.
units.tr: Occupation: it does not follow that Adam is stronger than Christ because he destroyed more than Christ saves.

units.la: Ratio: Quia potentia utriusque spectatur, nō in multitudine eorum, qui moriuntur, vel vivificantur: Sed in modo, quo fit perditio vel vivificatio, & in magnitudine bonorum amissorum & reparatorum.
units.tr: Reason: because the power of each is judged not by the number of those who die or are made alive, but by the manner in which destruction or restoration takes place, and by the greatness of the goods lost and recovered.

units.la: Decl. 1. Facilius est multos perdere, quam unum servare, aut perditum restituere: quia illud etiam creaturæ possunt: hoc solus Deus.
units.tr: Declaration: (1) It is easier for many to be destroyed than for one to be saved, or for one who is lost to be restored; for the former even creatures can do, but the latter only God alone can do.

units.la: 2. Bona per Christum reparata sunt multò majora iis, quæ per Adamum amisimus. Prob. Quia Adam terrenus: Christus coelestis 1.Cor.15.49. Item: Adam ex terreno Paradiso nos ejecit: Christus in coelestem nos collocavit.
units.tr: (2) The goods restored through Christ are far greater than those we lost through Adam. Proof: because Adam was earthly, Christ is heavenly (1 Cor. 15:49). Likewise, Adam cast us out of the earthly Paradise; Christ has placed us in the heavenly one.

units.la: Conclusio habeat ἐπιδείξιν[?]: hic vela contrahenda.
units.tr: Conclusion: let him have a display [?]; here the sails are to be furled.

units.la: Repete breviter quæ dixisti: & πεῖσμα[?].
units.tr: Repeat briefly what you have said, and [?] (a cable/anchor).

units.la: 1. Cum Christus verè resurrexerit tertio die juxta Scr. firmiter teneamus fidem Christianam: hunc Iesum esse Messiam promissum: contra sarcasmos impiorum.
units.tr: (1) Since Christ truly rose on the third day according to the Scriptures, let us firmly hold the Christian faith: that this Jesus is the promised Messiah, against the sarcasms of the impious.

units.la: 2. Cùm propria potentia vicerit mortem: peccatum: Verus ergo Deus est: vindicabit ergo Ecclesiam ab hostib. ornabit beneficiis ꝓ meritis. Specifica: Hoc ergo vindice stabit Ecclesia contra furores omnes: Quia nunc est ad dextram, &c.
units.tr: (2) Since by his own power he has conquered death and sin, he is therefore true God; he will therefore defend the Church from its enemies and adorn it with benefits in return for his merits. Specification: therefore, with this defender, the Church will stand against all rages, "because now he is at the right hand," etc.

units.la: 3. Cùm tanta beneficia sint resurrectionis: & ea dett[?] tantùm fidelib. & gratias ipsi agentib: nos igitur gratis mentibus ea etiam agnoscamus: fide nobis applicemus: peccato moriamur: vitam i-psi placentem agamus.
units.tr: (3) Since the benefits of the resurrection are so great, and these are granted only to believers who also give thanks to him, let us therefore gladly acknowledge them in our minds, apply them to ourselves by faith, die to sin, and live a life pleasing to him.

units.la: Gratias ergo agamus æterno Filio D e i D.N. 1. Christo quod mortuus sit propter peccata nostra & stra & resurrexerit propter justitiam nostram, &c. Oremus ut donet nos vera fide,&c. Colligat & conservet sibi inter nos veram & aeternam Eccle-siam, quam justificet, vivificet, suscitet & glorificet: Conservet scholas & puram doctrinam: conservet nobis haec halcyonia: pios magistratus & doctores. Age etiam gratias illustrissimis Prin-cipibus: & caeteris pro more.
units.tr: Let us therefore give thanks to the eternal Son of God our Lord Jesus Christ: that he died for our sins and rose again for our justification, etc. Let us pray that he would grant us true faith, etc. May he gather and preserve for himself among us a true and eternal Church, which he may justify, quicken, raise up and glorify; may he preserve schools and pure doctrine; may he preserve for us these halcyon days, pious magistrates and teachers. Also give thanks to the most illustrious princes, and to the others, as is customary.

units.la: Exercitatio V.
units.tr: Exercitatio V.

units.la: .De causis & fructibus Mortis atq; Resurrectio-nis Christi: ex dicto: Nonne haec oportuit Christum pati, &c.
units.tr: On the causes and fruits of the death and resurrection of Christ, from the saying: "Ought not these things to have been suffered by Christ, etc.?"
Luke 24:26.

units.la: EXordium hortetur ad laetitiam, à tempore: quæ cras Pascha, quo Ecclesia Resurrectionem Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ex mortuis solenni laetitia recolit.
units.tr: The opening exhorts to joy, from the time: tomorrow is Easter, on which the Church solemnly recalls with festive joy the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead.

units.la: Exponantur causæ lætitiæ[?]. I.[?] causa à mirando resurrectionis opere & beneficiis; quia Christus resurgendo se Deum demonstravit, mundum servavit, probrum hostium clamantium, {?}Alios servavit, seipsum servare non potest, refutavit, diabolum vicit, nos ab ejus tyrannide li-beravit, mortem protrivit, vitam reparavit, peccatum abolevit, justitiam reduxit, inferos destruxit, ad superos transfivit, nosque una de morte in vitam transfire fecit. O pascha exspectatum, O transitum exoptatum.
units.tr: Let the causes of joy be set out. First, the cause is the wonderful work and benefits of the resurrection; for by rising Christ showed himself to be God, saved the world, and refuted the reproach of enemies who cried, "He saved others; himself he cannot save." He conquered the devil, freed us from his tyranny, crushed death, restored life, abolished sin, brought back righteousness, destroyed hell, passed over to the heavenly ones, and caused us to pass with him from death into life. O Passover long awaited, O passage much desired!

units.la: {?}Amplif. Angeli laetantur: elementa exultant, Sol clarior solito crastina luce exoriens in ejus re-surrectione gaudet, in cujus passione condoluit:
units.tr: Amplification: the angels rejoice, the elements exult, and the sun, rising with a brighter light than usual on the morrow, rejoices at his resurrection, at whose passion it grieved.

units.la: 2. causa cur nobis præcipue fit lætandum: à comparatione hujus & præteriti pafchatis: Tunc horrenda lues pestilentiæ lætitiam turbabat: Nunc beneficio Christi resurgentis & triumphantis eo terrore & metu liberati sumus.
units.tr: Second, the reason why we ought above all to rejoice is the comparison with the Passover of the past. Then a dreadful plague of pestilence disturbed our joy; now, by the benefit of Christ rising and triumphant, we have been freed from that terror and fear.

units.la: 3. causa: quia hoc pascha Serenissimi Electo-ris exspectatissimum conspectum nobis ex Bavaria reduxit: Breviter compara incommoda & lu-crum[?] publicum ex ejus absentia cum commodis & lætitia præsentiæ. Exclamatio per adverf. Sed o mirandam Dei sapientiam & bonitatem: Ideo Celsitudinem ejus abduxerat, ut in tuto præsta-ret: ideo nos orbaverat, ut diu nobis servaret, & nos diu gaudeamus ejus præsidio, &c. Adde votum pro ejus Celsitudinis incolumitate: & hortare ad gratitudinem & ad munera Deo offerenda in festo: ex dicto, Deut.16. Non comparebis va-cuus, &c. Sed an aurum, argentum? Ne angeli quidem sat digna offerre possunt. Quid ergo?
units.tr: Third, because this Passover has brought back to us the most eagerly awaited sight of the most serene Elector from Bavaria. Briefly compare the public disadvantages and gains from his absence with the blessings and joy of his presence. Exclamation by way of contrast: But oh, the wonderful wisdom and goodness of God! He had therefore taken away his Highness so that he might be kept safe; he had therefore bereaved us, so that he might preserve him for us a long time, and that we might long rejoice in his protection, etc. Add a prayer for the safety of his Highness, and exhort to gratitude and to offering gifts to God at the festival, from the saying in Deut. 16: "You shall not appear empty," etc. But are they gold and silver? Not even the angels can offer things worthy enough. What then?

units.la: 1. Nos ipsos Deo gratissimum [illegible, ~7 letters]. Rom.12.1: hostiam Deo acceptam. Phil.4.18.
units.tr: First, ourselves, most pleasing to God [illegible, about seven letters]. Rom. 12:1: a sacrifice acceptable to God. Phil. 4:18.

units.la: 2. Orationem & laudes, quibus præclarius nihil habemus.
units.tr: Second, prayer and praises, than which we have nothing more excellent.

units.la: Captatio benevolentiæ per occupat: Te fateri tuam infantiam: Interim non absterreri à conatu aliquid proferendi: 1. fretum benevolentia auditorum. 2. quia facias ab iis jussus, quibus obte-perare officium & pietas suaserit.
units.tr: Captatio benevolentiae by anticipation: confess that you are a child in this matter, yet do not be frightened from the attempt to put something forward: first, trusting in the goodwill of the hearers; second, because you are doing so at the command of those whom duty and piety have persuaded you to obey.

units.la: Transitio ad propositionem habens locum attentionis: Cum multi ante te repetiverint historiam[?] triumphi & modum resurrectionis Christi à mortuis: te dicturum aliquid de causis & fructibus tum passionis & mortis tu resurrect. ex dicto Christi redivivi ad discipulos Luc. 24. Nonne hæc oportuit Christum pati: & ingredi in glor. suam.
units.tr: Transition to the proposition, which has a place for attention: since many before you have repeated the history of the triumph and the manner of Christ's resurrection from the dead, you will say something about the causes and fruits both of his passion and death and of his resurrection, from the saying of the risen Christ to the disciples, Luke 24: "Ought not these things to have been suffered by Christ, and to enter into his glory?"

units.la: Ratio 1. quia passio & mors Christi sit plena offensionis & scandali, causis non intellectis.
units.tr: Reason 1: because the passion and death of Christ are full of offence and stumbling, the causes not being understood.

units.la: Ratio 2. quia ratio humana & mundus resurrectionem Christi non credit.
units.tr: Reason 2: because human reason and the world do not believe in the resurrection of Christ.

units.la: Ratio 3. quia consideratio causarum & fructuum veram consolationem afferat, fidem corroboret & materiam celebrationis nobis suppeditet.
units.tr: Reason 3: because the consideration of the causes and fruits brings true consolation, strengthens faith, and supplies us with matter for celebration.

units.la: Propositio: Dicam igitur.
units.tr: Proposition: I shall therefore speak.

units.la: 1. Quid & quare oportuerit Christum pati. 11. Quomodo & quare oportuerit in gloriam ingredi.
units.tr: (1) What and why it was necessary for Christ to suffer. (2) How and why it was necessary for him to enter into glory.

units.la: I. Quid & quare oportuerit Christum pati.
units.tr: I. What and why it was necessary for Christ to suffer.

units.la: Quid sit passus Christus, ostendatur occasione dicti: Nonne hæc oportuit Christum pati, &c. ex precedentibus: Quomodo eum tradiderunt, &c. quibus à Cleopha vehementer perturbato passio Christi indicatur: sed nec tota nec gravissima: Ratio 1. quia tota vita fuit perpetua passio. 2. multi martyres etiam sunt traditi, condemnati, crucifixi, mortui, &c.
units.tr: What Christ suffered is to be shown on the occasion of the saying, "Ought not these things to have been suffered by Christ, etc.?" from what precedes: "how the chief priests and rulers delivered him up, etc.," in which the passion of Christ is indicated by Cleophas, who was greatly troubled; yet it was neither the whole nor the most grievous. Reason 1: because his whole life was a continual passion. 2: many martyrs also were delivered up, condemned, crucified, killed, etc.

units.la: Subjiciat p adversus [illegible, ~6 letters] Christi, qb. abartic. nativit. usq; ad mortem anima & corpore fuit obnoxius: Vir dolorum, &c. Ego vermis & nō homo: Filius hom. nō habet, &c. Infinitæ injuriæ, insidiæ, blaspheblasphemiæ, vincula, verbera, sputa, contumeliæ, irrisiones, condemnatio, mors crucis, &c.
units.tr: Let it be added against [illegible, about six letters] that Christ, from his birth to his death, was subject in soul and body: "A man of sorrows," etc.; "I am a worm and not a man"; "The Son of man has nowhere to lay his head," etc. Countless injuries, snares, blasphemies, chains, stripes, spittings, insults, mockeries, condemnation, the death of the cross, etc.

units.la: Præcipuè vero sensus iræ Dei adversus peccata generis humani: lucta cum diabolo, inferno, desperatione, &c. Tristis est anima, &c. Sudor cruentus: Deus meus quid, &c. Obtulit deprecationes & supplicationes Deo cum clamore valido & lacrymis, Hebr.5.7.
units.tr: Especially, indeed, the sense of God's wrath against the sins of the human race; struggle with the devil, with hell, with despair, etc. "My soul is sorrowful even unto death"; "bloody sweat"; "My God, why...?" He offered prayers and supplications to God with strong crying and tears, Heb. 5:7.

units.la: Claudatur : Hæc gravior pars cruciatuum & passionum ea, quam Cleophas vidit, & quæ ejus fidem ac spem adeo turbavit, &c. Nos au-tem sperabamus, &c. quasi dicat, spes fefellit, &c. Hanc nulli martyres sunt passi: sed est passio pro-pria filii Dei.
units.tr: Let it be concluded: this is the heavier part of his torments and sufferings, the one Cleophas saw, and which so greatly disturbed his faith and hope, etc. "But we hoped, etc." as if to say: hope failed, etc. No martyrs have suffered this; it is the proper passion of the Son of God.

units.la: πάθημα[?]: Infirmitas humana ex passione & morte Christi nihil potest colligere nisi offendi-culum, incredulitatem, desperationem: quia videtur sequi: Est crucifixus, mortuus. Ergo non est Messias: non potest nos servare. Sic Judæi ob-jiciebant. Medice cura te ipsum. Seipsum servare non potest. Si est rex Israel, descendat de cruce. Sic Pa-gani, Turcæ offensi Christi passionibus & morte, &c. negant eum Messiam, Deum, &c.
units.tr: Suffering [?]: Human weakness can gather from the passion and death of Christ nothing but stumbling, unbelief, and despair, because it seems to follow: he was crucified, he died; therefore he is not the Messiah; he cannot save us. So the Jews objected: "Physician, heal yourself"; "He cannot save himself"; "If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from the cross." So the pagans and Turks, offended by the sufferings and death of Christ, etc., deny that he is the Messiah, God, etc.

units.la: Adversativa. Sed hæc dialectica carnis est summa stultitia: O stulti & tardi corde, &c. Nonne hæc oportuit Christum pati? Christus contrarium infert: in passione, morte, fidem & consolatione fundari ostendit: Quia hæc est passus: ideo est Christus: Ratio: quia Christum oportuit hæc pati.
units.tr: By contrast: but this reasoning of the flesh is the height of folly. "O foolish and slow of heart, etc. Ought not these things to have been suffered by Christ?" Christ draws the opposite conclusion: he shows that faith and consolation are grounded in the passion and death; because he has suffered these things, therefore he is Christ. Reason: because it was necessary for Christ to suffer these things.

units.la: Hinc transeatur ad causas, & primo removean-tur non causæ, quasi invitus, vel coactus, vel ex impotentia fit trucidatus. Contrarium doceatur ex dictis: Ego habeo potestatem ponendi animam, &c. Iudæi ante tempus frustra ei insidiabantur, &c. Ultro in horto se hostibus obtulit, verbo eosdem prostravit: An non possem xii legiones a patre petere, &c.
units.tr: Hence we pass to the causes, and first the non-causes are to be removed: that he was slain as though unwillingly, or under compulsion, or from weakness. The contrary is to be taught from the sayings: "I have power to lay down my life, etc." The Jews plotted against him in vain before the appointed time, etc. In the garden he offered himself of his own accord to his enemies and with a word overthrew them: "Do you think that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he will send me more than twelve legions of angels?"

units.la: Addatur ratio: quia debuit esse victima voluntaria ad expiandam nostram inobedientiam: Phil.2. Factus obediens, &c. Hebr.10. Adsum ut faciam voluntatem tuam, &c. Nec propter sua peccata, propter quæ constitutum est omnibus se-mel mori: quia iustus, innocens: Hebr.7.
units.tr: Add the reason: he was to be a voluntary victim to expiate our disobedience: Phil. 2, "Becoming obedient, etc."; Heb. 10, "Lo, I come to do your will, etc." Nor was it for his own sins, for which it is appointed to all men once to die, since he was just and innocent: Heb. 7.

units.la: Deinde causæ huius necessitatis exponantur.
units.tr: Next, the causes of this necessity are to be set out.

units.la: Quare igitur oportuit Christum hæc pati?
units.tr: Why then was it necessary for Christ to suffer these things?

units.la: 1. Propter oracula, quæ oportebat impleri: quia Spiritus Dei non potuit mentiri: Ostende ex verbis Christi: O tardi corde ad credendum, &c. Matth. 26. Quomodo implerentur Scripturæ quod oporteat sic fieri? Has exposuit Christus discipulis Luc.24.27. Exorsus a Mose, &c. Subiice breviter quædam oracula & typos: Mordebit ei calcaneum: Agnus mactatus: victimæ cæsæ: Serpens suspensus: Ionæ triduum in cœto: Isc.53.[?] Per-cussus à Deo: Dan.9. Messias excidetur, &c.
units.tr: (1) Because of the oracles, which had to be fulfilled, since the Spirit of God cannot lie. Show it from the words of Christ: "O slow of heart to believe, etc." Matt. 26: "How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must be so?" Christ expounded these to the disciples, Luke 24:27: "beginning from Moses, etc." Briefly add some oracles and types: "He shall bruise his heel"; "the lamb slain"; the sacrificed victims; "the serpent lifted up"; Jonah's three days in the whale; Isaiah 53; "smitten by God," Dan. 9: "the Messiah shall be cut off, etc."

units.la: 2. Propter immutabile Dei decretum. Actor.2. Hunc definito consilio, &c. Et clarius: Act.4. Coa-Eli[?] sunt vere, &c. ut facerent ea quæ manus tua, &c. Ideo dicitur, quod Deus miserit, ipse tradiderit; percusserit filium. Isc. 53. Dominus voluit eum ita conterere. Zach.13. Ego percutiam pastorem.
units.tr: (2) Because of the immutable decree of God. Acts 2: "Him, delivered up by the determinate counsel, etc." And more clearly, Acts 4: "They were truly gathered together... to do whatever your hand and counsel had determined to be done." Therefore it is said that God sent him, that he himself delivered him up, and smote his Son. Isaiah 53: "The Lord was pleased to bruise him thus." Zech. 13: "I will smite the shepherd."

units.la: Per occup. ostendatur, Iudam, Pilatum; Iudæos, quorum opera Deus in percutiendo filio est usus; non excusari. 1. quia Christum trucidarunt sine Dei mandato speciali. 2. contra generale man-datum: Non occides. 3. Finis eorum & Dei lon-ge diversus.
units.tr: By anticipation it is shown that Judas, Pilate, and the Jews, through whose work God made use in striking his Son, are not excused. First, because they slew Christ without a special command from God. Second, against the general command: "Thou shalt not kill." Third, their end was far different from God's.

units.la: 3. Propter nostra peccata. Ad hanc transeatur occupatione: Pater amat filium: quomodo igitur eum percussit? Resp. ex dicto: Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut filium unigenitum daret: Etiam amavit genus humanum perditum: Hoc amore & misericordia motus filiū dilectū praeordinavit redemtorem 1.Pet.1. 20. Ergo filiū oportuit luere culpā & poenas nostrorū peccatorū. Hucaccōmo dentur dicta: Vere languores nostros portavit. Traditus propter iniquitates nostras. Fecit eum peccatū pro nobis, &c. Passus iustus pro iniustis, &c.
units.tr: (3) Because of our sins. Pass to this by anticipation: the Father loves the Son; how then did he smite him? Answer from the saying: "God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son" (John 3:16). He also loved the lost human race; moved by this love and mercy he foreordained his beloved Son as Redeemer (1 Pet. 1:20). Therefore the Son had to bear the guilt and punishments of our sins. Here may be added the sayings: "Surely he has borne our griefs" (Isa. 53:4); "delivered up for our iniquities" (Rom. 4:25); "He made him to be sin for us" (2 Cor. 5:21); "The just for the unjust" (1 Pet. 3:18).

units.la: &Amplif. amor Dei immensus, quem testatus est filii traditione pro nobis, & petatur ratio ex praestantia & fine hominis creati ad imaginem & celebrationem Dei.
units.tr: &Amplif. The immense love of God, which he bore witness to by the delivering up of his Son for us; and the reason should be drawn from the excellence and the end of man, created in the image of God and for the celebration of God.

units.la: 4. Propter iustitiam Dei, cui aliter satisfieri non potuit nisi morte filii Dei pro nostris peccatis.
units.tr: 4. On account of the justice of God, to which satisfaction could not otherwise have been made except by the death of the Son of God for our sins.

units.la: Probetur, quod non nisi morte: quia Iustitia Dei postulat aeternam destructionem peccantis. Ratio: quia peccatum est laesio summi boni, quā expiari oportet summo supplicio, & ultima destructione naturae peccantis: juxta dicta: Morte morieris: Stipendium peccati mors, &c. At Christus induit nostram personam: Ies.53. Conieci in eum iniquitates omnium nostrum. Item: quod non nisi morte filii Dei: quia nullius creaturae ἀντίλυτρον[?] fuisset sufficiens & sat dignum ἀντάλλαγμα pro hominis peccato.
units.tr: Let it be proved that it could be made only by death: because the justice of God demands the eternal destruction of the sinner. The reason: because sin is an injury to the supreme good, which must be expiated by the supreme punishment and the final destruction of the sinning nature, according to the sayings: "Dying you shall die" and "The wages of sin is death," etc. But Christ put on our person: Isaiah 53: "I have laid on him the iniquities of us all." Likewise, that it could be made only by the death of the Son of God: because no creature's ransom [ἀντίλυτρον] would have been sufficient, nor a sufficiently worthy exchange [ἀντάλλαγμα] for the sin of man.

units.la: Note: the Greek word before "fuisset" is only partly legible; read as ἀντίλυτρον with [?].
units.tr: Note: the Greek word before "fuisset" is only partly legible; read as ἀντίλυτρον with [?].

units.la: Obiect. 1. Christi[?] mors & destructio non fuit æterna sed temporalis. Resp. Attamen æternæ æquivalens. 1. propter dignitatem personæ morientis: quia est verus Deus & homo purus. 2. propter gravitatem supplicii: quia non tantũ corpore patitur intolerabiles cruciatus & morte cruciis: sed & anima sustinet cruciatus inferni & iram Dei adversus peccata totius generis humani, &c.
units.tr: Objection 1. The death and destruction of Christ was not eternal but temporal. Answer: Nevertheless it was equivalent to eternal death: (1) on account of the dignity of the person dying, because he is true God and pure man; (2) on account of the severity of the punishment: because he suffers not only in body intolerable torments and death on the cross, but also in soul he endures the torments of hell and the wrath of God against the sins of the whole human race, etc.

units.la: Obiect. 2. Pugnat cum justitia Dei punire insontem pro sontibus.
units.tr: Objection 2. It is contrary to the justice of God to punish the innocent for the guilty.

units.la: Resp. Etsi hoc non fert ἀκρεῖ̈ο̈δίκαιον[?] legis: cuius vox est: Anima quæ peccaverit ea morietur, fert tamen ἀθανασία[?] Evangelio declarata: cuius vox est: Quod legi erat impossibile infirmata per carnem, hoc fecit Deus misso filio, &c.
units.tr: Answer: Although this does not accord with the [ἀκρεῖ̈ο̈δίκαιον?] of the law, whose voice is: "The soul that sins, it shall die," it does accord with the [ἀθανασία?] declared in the Gospel, whose voice is: "What was impossible for the law, weakened through the flesh, God did by sending his Son, etc."

units.la: Ratio 1. quia Christus innocens ultrò se obtulit ad satisfactionem pro nobis nocentibus.
units.tr: The reason: (1) because Christ, innocent, offered himself of his own accord to make satisfaction for us who are guilty.

units.la: 2. Ideo assumsit naturam humanam.
units.tr: (2) Therefore he assumed human nature.

units.la: 3. Plene satisfecit.
units.tr: (3) He made full satisfaction.

units.la: 4. Ipse in supplicio non periit, sed emersit.
units.tr: (4) He himself did not perish in the punishment, but rose out again.

units.la: 5. Efficit, ut sontes post satisfactionem ces- sent Deum offendere.
units.tr: (5) He brings it about that the guilty, after the satisfaction, cease to offend God.

units.la: His autem conditionibus positis non est in- justum, innocentem plectere pro nocenti- bus.
units.tr: With these conditions laid down, it is not unjust to punish the innocent for the guilty.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia ἀκρεῖ̈ο̈δίκαιον[?] non tollit vel prohibet ἀθανασία[?], ubi sunt probabiles causæ, ut hic sunt: Aristoteles Ethic.lib.5. cap.10. τὸ ἀθανατικὸν δικαιον ἐστι, καὶ ἐπανόρθωμα νομίμου δικαίου[?]. 2. quia lex sic postulat satisfactionem propriam pro pec- cato, ut nusquam tamen excludat vel prohibeat alienam: quam docet Evangelium.
units.tr: The reason: (1) because the [ἀκρεῖ̈ο̈δίκαιον?] does not remove or forbid the [ἀθανασία?] where there are probable grounds, as here there are: Aristotle, Ethics book 5, chapter 10: "The equitable justice is correction of the legal justice" [τὸ ἀθανατικὸν δικαιον ἐστι, καὶ ἐπανόρθωμα νομίμου δικαίου]. (2) Because the law so requires a satisfaction of one's own for sin, and yet nowhere excludes or forbids a satisfaction by another, which the Gospel teaches.

units.la: Obiect. 3. Justitia puniens peccata pendet a libera Dei voluntate. Ergo non fuit necessaria satisfactio pro hominis peccato: proinde nec se-quitur ex Dei justitia, Christum oportuisse justitiae Dei satisfacere pro nobis: quia Deus libere potuit de suo jure remittere.
units.tr: Objection 3. Justice punishing sins depends on the free will of God. Therefore satisfaction was not necessary for the sin of man; and it does not follow from the justice of God that Christ had to satisfy the justice of God for us, since God could freely remit his own right.

units.la: Resp. 1. Negetur, quod justitia aversans & destruens peccatum sit tantum divini arbitrii, & non etiam de natura Dei: Vult & diligit justitiam natura, & ita natura, non vult, odit, aversatur, destruit peccatum tanquam naturae suae inimicum: Psal. 5. ver. 5. Deus non volens iniquitatem tues: Perdes omnes loquentes mendaciū. Psal. 45. Dilexisti justitiam, odisti iniquitatem. Potest igitur remittere de suo jure: sed non de sua natura: quia non potest seipsum negare. 2. Tim. 2. 13: Necesse igitur fuit pro hominis peccato vel ab homine ipso, vel ab alio, justitiae Dei satisfieri:
units.tr: Reply. 1. Let it be denied that justice, which turns away from and destroys sin, belongs only to the will of God, and not also to the nature of God. By nature he wills and loves justice, and so by nature he does not will, hates, turns away from and destroys sin as the enemy of his nature. Psalm 5:5: "Thou art not a God that hath pleasure in wickedness... Thou shalt destroy them that speak leasing." Psalm 45:7: "Thou hast loved righteousness and hated iniquity." God therefore can remit from his right, but not from his nature, because he cannot deny himself. 2 Timothy 2:13: "If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful; he cannot deny himself." It was necessary, therefore, that satisfaction be made to the justice of God for the sin of man, either by man himself or by another.

units.la: 2. Etsi justitia puniens peccatum in Deo mere effet arbitraria, ut condere mundum, hominem, pluvias, &c. tamen fuit necessaria satisfactio pro peccato hominis, ex hypothesi comminationis: Morte morieris: Hinc transeatur ad quintam causam.
units.tr: 2. Even if the justice that punishes sin were, in God, purely arbitrary, as is his founding of the world, of man, of rains, and so on, nevertheless satisfaction for the sin of man was necessary, given the hypothesis of the threat: "In the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die." Hence we pass on to the fifth cause.

units.la: 5. causa: Propter veritatem Dei: quia dixerat: Morte morieris: Hanc comminationem oportuit impleri destructione peccantis. Ergo aut totum humanum genus in aeternum mori oportuit, aut alium pro eo, quia Deus non potuit mentiri. At non voluit Deus totum humanum genus perire: nec mori alius pro eo potuit praeter Chri-stum, stum, Ergo Christum pro nobis mori oportuit.
units.tr: 5. Cause: on account of the truth of God. Because he had said: "Thou shalt surely die," this threat had to be fulfilled by the destruction of the sinner. Therefore either the whole human race had to die for ever, or another had to die for it, since God cannot lie. But God did not will that the whole human race should perish, and no one else could die for it except Christ. Therefore Christ had to die for us.

units.la: Claudantur causæ: & breviter porismata dedu cantur.
units.tr: Let the causes be closed, and let the corollaries be briefly drawn.

units.la: 1. Si Christum oportuit hæc pati: Ergo mentiebatur Basilides Simonem Cyrenæum esse passum. Videatur eius opinio apud Epiphanium hæres. 24. & breviter subiiciatur ex eodem refutatio. 1. quia sic non per Christum, sed per Simonem esset perfecta salus nostra. Frustra igitur mũ dus crederet in Christum. 2. Filius Dei damnaretur sycophantiæ, qui alium pro se coactum in mortem tradidisset. 3. Christus volens & sponte se obtulit: ad passionem descendit: veni in mũdum, ut faciam voluntatem patris: Ecce ascendimus Ierosolymam. 4. Testimonium Petri, Pauli: Mortificatus carne, gustavit mortem pro omnibus, &c.
units.tr: 1. If Christ had to suffer these things, then Basilides was lying when he said that Simon of Cyrene suffered in his place. Let his opinion be seen in Epiphanius, Heresy 24, and let the refutation from the same be briefly added. (1) Because in that case our salvation would not be perfected through Christ but through Simon; the world would then believe in Christ in vain. (2) The Son of God would be condemned for trickery, having handed over another, compelled to death, in his own place. (3) Christ willingly and voluntarily offered himself, descended to the passion: "Lo, I have come into the world to do the will of the Father"; "Behold, we go up to Jerusalem." (4) The testimony of Peter and Paul: "Put to death in the flesh, he tasted death for all," etc.

units.la: 11. Si Christum oportuit pati pro nobis. Ergo atrocius peccatum est, quam ut ab angelis vel hominibus expiari potuerit. Ergo ne quæramus satisfactionem extra Christum. Act. 4. Non est datum aliud nomen, &c.
units.tr: 11. If Christ had to suffer for us, then sin is more atrocious than could have been expiated by angels or men. Therefore let us not seek satisfaction outside Christ. Acts 4: "There is no other name given, etc."

units.la: 111. Si Christus hæc passus pro nobis: Ergo satisfecit pro nobis: culpam expiavit: Deum placavit: meritus nobis pacem justitiam & vitam.
units.tr: 111. If Christ suffered these things for us, then he satisfied for us: he expiated the guilt, he appeased God, he merited for us peace, justice and life.

units.la: Is[?]. 53. (Castigatio pacis nostræ super eum & tumore eius sanati sumus. Rom.8. Quis condemnabit electos Dei? Christus est qui mortuus est, &c.
units.tr: Isaiah 53: "The chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his stripes we are healed." Romans 8: "Who shall condemn the elect of God? It is Christ who died, etc."

units.la: II. Quomodo & quare oportuerit Christum ingredi in gloriam.
units.tr: II. How and why it was necessary for Christ to enter into glory.

units.la: Transitio.non tantum oportuit Christum pa-ti, sed & introire in gloriam suam. Ante causas declaretur quomodo oportuerit introire quasi tribus gradibus.
units.tr: Transition. It was necessary not only for Christ to suffer, but also to enter into his glory. Before the reasons are set out, it is to be explained how it was necessary to enter, as it were by three steps.

units.la: I. Resurgendo. Sic ipse interpretatur Luc. 24. ver. 46. Ita oportuit Christum pati & resurgere a mortuis tertio die.
units.tr: I. By rising again. Luke 24:46 interprets this itself: Thus it was necessary for Christ to suffer and to rise again from the dead on the third day.

units.la: Offende qualis gloria in resurrectione: quia infirmitates deposuit, immortalitate induit, victor & triumphator mortis, vitae reparator, &c.
units.tr: Observe what glory there is in the resurrection: for he laid aside infirmities, put on immortality, became the victor and triumphant over death, the restorer of life, etc.

units.la: II. Ascendendo in coelum: quia in terris nondum fuit consummata gloria: Ioh.20. Nondum ascendi ad patrem meum. Heb. 2. 7. Conveniebat nobis pontifex, &c. sublimior coelis factus: Hebr. 9. Ingressus in sacrarium non manufactum, sed in ipsum coelum.
units.tr: II. By ascending into heaven: because on earth his glory was not yet complete. John 20:17: I have not yet ascended to my Father. Heb. 2:7: It became us to have such a high priest, etc., made higher than the heavens. Heb. 9:24: He entered into the holy place not made with hands, but into heaven itself.

units.la: III. Sedendo ad dextram Dei subiectis angelis & potestatibus. Haec gloriae fuit consummatio. 1.Pet.3.22. Heb.1.3.
units.tr: III. By sitting at the right hand of God, with angels and powers made subject to him. This was the completion of his glory. 1 Pet. 3:22; Heb. 1:3.

units.la: In hanc igitur gloriam Christum post passionem oportuit introire.
units.tr: It was therefore necessary for Christ to enter into this glory after his passion.

units.la: Subiiciantur causae, propter quas necesse fuit Christum resurgere a mortuis & introire in suam gloriam.
units.tr: Let the reasons be set out for which it was necessary for Christ to rise from the dead and enter into his glory.

units.la: I. Vaticinia prophetarum quae impleri oportuit. Luc.24.46. Ita scriptum est, & ita oportuit, &c. Si de passione : multo magis de resurrectione. Recitentur breviter nonnulla. Psal. 16. Non relinques animam, &c. Applicatio huius ad Christi resurrectionem est Act. 2. & 13, Isai. 53. Ex judicio & angustia ereptus est, &c. Signum Ionæ Matth. 12. & 16.
units.tr: I. The prophecies of the prophets, which had to be fulfilled. Luke 24:46: Thus it is written, and thus it was necessary, etc. If this holds of the passion, much more of the resurrection. Some passages may be briefly recited. Ps. 16: You will not leave my soul, etc. The application of this to Christ's resurrection is in Acts 2 and 13; Isa. 53: He was taken away from judgment and distress, etc. The sign of Jonah, Matt. 12 and 16.

units.la: 2. Prædictiones ipsius Christi de se. Matth. 20. 19. Marc. 10. 34. Luc. 18. 33.
units.tr: 2. Christ's own predictions about himself. Matt. 20:19; Mark 10:34; Luke 18:33.

units.la: Amplif. Christus vita & veritas.
units.tr: Amplification. Christ is the life and the truth.

units.la: 3. Dignitas personæ: propter quam impossibile fuit Christum detineri à morte. Act. 2. 24.
units.tr: 3. The dignity of the person, on account of which it was impossible for Christ to be held by death. Acts 2:24.

units.la: Ratio consequentiæ. 1. quia unigenitus & dilectus filius Dei: quem pater non potuit relinquere in morte Psal. 16. Prospiciebam Deum coram me semper, &c. Act. 13. 33. Paulus probat resurrectionem Christi ex dicto Filius meus es tu, &c.
units.tr: The reasoning of the consequence: (1) because he is the only-begotten and beloved Son of God, whom the Father could not leave in death. Ps. 16: I have set the Lord always before me, etc. Acts 13:33: Paul proves the resurrection of Christ from the word You are my Son, etc.

units.la: 2. quia ipse verus Deus & vita æterna 1. Ioh. 5. 20. Ioh. 5. Pater dedit filio vitam habere in semetipso, &c. Non potuit igitur à morte superari:
units.tr: (2) Because he is himself true God and eternal life, 1 John 5:20; John 5: The Father has given to the Son to have life in himself, etc. He therefore could not be overcome by death.

units.la: 3. quia homo justus & sanctus: In cuius ore non inventus dolus. Et licet peccata nostra in se derivarat:tamen ea moriendo expiavit. Hebr. 10. Una oblatione consecravit sanctos, &c. Abolito igitur peccato mors non potuit ei dominari.
units.tr: (3) Because he is a righteous and holy man: in whose mouth no deceit was found. And although our sins had been imputed to him, yet by dying he atoned for them. Heb. 10: By one offering he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified, etc. Sin having therefore been abolished, death could not have dominion over him.

units.la: 4. Sacerdotium Christi: Debuit esse sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melch: propter juramentum Dei. Psal. 110. & Hebr. 7. 21. Ergo non tantum debuit sacrificare pro peccatis populi: quod fecit semel offerendo semetipsum in cruce: sed & intercedere perpetuo pro nobis: Rom. 8. 34. Heb. 9. 24. Ergo oportuit eum resurgere ex morte.
units.tr: (4) The priesthood of Christ: he was to be a priest for ever according to the order of Melchizedek, on account of the oath of God. Ps. 110; Heb. 7:21. Therefore he was not only to offer sacrifice for the sins of the people, which he did once for all by offering himself on the cross, but also to intercede for us continually: Rom. 8:34; Heb. 9:24. Therefore it was necessary for him to rise from death.

units.la: 5. Regnum Christi: Debuit regnare in æter-num, juxta promissiones semini Davidis factas 2.Sam.7. Pf.45.& 89. Ezech.37. David erit princeps eius in seculum. Luc.1. Regni eius non erit finis. 1.Cor.15. Oportet eum regnare. Declara quod regnare sit colligere tueri glorificare Ecclesiam. At hoc non potuisset manens in morte,&c.
units.tr: (5) The kingdom of Christ: he was to reign for ever, according to the promises made to the seed of David: 2 Sam. 7; Ps. 45 and 89; Ezek. 37: David shall be their prince for ever. Luke 1: Of his kingdom there shall be no end. 1 Cor. 15: He must reign. Explain that to reign is to gather, protect and glorify the Church. But he could not have done this while remaining in death, etc.

units.la: 6. Beneficia, quæ mediator Ecclesiæ non tantum mereri sed etiam conferre & applicare debuit. Ratio: quia nos mortui in peccatis: non po-teramus amplecti[?] nisi ipso nos vivificante Ioh.15. Sine me nihil potestis facere, &c. Breviter exponan-tur præcipua, quæ non poterat conferre nisi in-troiret in gloriam: & quæ nunc Ecclesiæ efficaci-ter confert.
units.tr: (6) The benefits which the mediator was to not only merit but also confer and apply to the Church. The reason: since we were dead in sins, we could not embrace them unless he quickened us. John 15: Without me you can do nothing, etc. The principal benefits, which he could not confer unless he entered into glory, and which he now effectively confers on the Church, are to be briefly expounded.

units.la: 1. Iustificatio seu remissio peccatorum Luc. 24.47. Prædicari oportuit in nomine eius resipiscen-tiam & remissionem peccatorum apud omnes gentes. Rom.4. Resurrexit propter iustificationem nostram. Rom.8. Quis accusabit electos Dei? Christus est qui mortuus est, qui resurrexit, &c.
units.tr: 1. Justification, or the remission of sins. Luke 24:47: Repentance and remission of sins were to be preached in his name among all nations. Rom. 4: He was raised for our justification. Rom. 8: Who shall accuse the elect of God? It is Christ who died, who rose again, etc.

units.la: 2. Vivificatio per Spiritum Sanctum. 1.Cor.15. In Christo omnes vivificantur. Eph.2. Vivificavit nos una cum Christo: Rom.6.5. Nam si cum eo plā-tati. 1.Pet.1. Regenuit nos in spem vivam per resur-rectionem Christi.
units.tr: 2. Quickening through the Holy Spirit. 1 Cor. 15: In Christ all shall be made alive. Eph. 2: He made us alive together with Christ; Rom. 6:5: For if we have been planted together with him. 1 Pet. 1: He has begotten us again to a living hope through the resurrection of Christ.

units.la: 3. Unio nostri cum Christi massa humana, ut ab ea gestemur, vivificemur & regamur, sicut me-bra à capite, palmites à vite Ioh.15. Eph.4.&5. Ergo oportuit massam Christi humanam emer-gere ex morte.
units.tr: 3. The union of ourselves with the human mass of Christ, so that we are carried by it, quickened and ruled, as the members by the head and the branches by the vine. John 15; Eph. 4 and 5. Therefore it was necessary for the human mass of Christ to rise out of death.

units.la: 4. Pax conscientiæ. Rom.5. Iustificati fide pacem habemus.[?] Item. Reconciliati per mortem filij multo magis servabimur ab ira.
units.tr: 4. Peace of conscience. Rom. 5: Being justified by faith, we have peace. Likewise: Having been reconciled through the death of the Son, much more shall we be saved from wrath.

units.la: 5. Resuscitatio ex morte & glorificatio: Ioh. 6. Hæc est voluntas eius qui misit me. Ioh. 10. Ego vitam æternam do eis: Resuscitabo eum novissimo die. 1. Thess. 4. Si credimus quod Iesus mortuus est & resurrexit: sic Deus eos qui obdormierunt per Iesum adducet cum eo. Phil. 3. Conformabit mortalia corpora nostra, &c.
units.tr: 5. Resurrection from death and glorification: John 6: This is the will of him who sent me. John 10: I give them eternal life: I will raise him up at the last day. 1 Thess. 4: If we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep through Jesus. Phil. 3: He will conform our mortal bodies, etc.

units.la: Per occupationem ostende 1. Hæc beneficia Christum non tantum debuisse mereri moriendo: sed etiam resurgendo efficaciter conferre: & eadem quidem esse beneficia mortis & resurrectionis: Sed illam sine hac non fuisse profutura.
units.tr: By way of occupation, show: (1) that Christ not only had to merit these benefits by dying, but also by rising to confer them effectively; and that indeed the benefits of death and resurrection are the same, but that the former would not have profited without the latter.

units.la: 2. Potuisse quidem Christum vi suæ Deitatis ea nobis conferre: sed & oportuisse peccatum & mortem vinci & aboleri in carne mediatoris. Quia per hominem mors & per hominem resurrectio 1.Cor.15.
units.tr: (2) That Christ could indeed have conferred these benefits upon us by the power of his Deity, but it was also necessary that sin and death be conquered and abolished in the flesh of the Mediator: For since by man came death, by man also came the resurrection; 1 Cor. 15.

units.la: 3. Etiam ante mortem & resurrectionem Christi hæc beneficia contigisse quidem fidelibus: sed respectu & vigore futuræ mortis & resurrectionis Mediatoris in natura humana assumta gloriose regnantis. Heb. 13. Iesus Christus heri, hodie & in secula. Ioh.13. Nisi ego te lavero, non habes par-tem, &c.
units.tr: (3) That even before the death and resurrection of Christ these benefits did indeed fall to the faithful, but in regard to and by the power of the future death and resurrection of the Mediator, who now reigns gloriously in the assumed human nature. Heb. 13: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and for ever. John 13: Unless I wash you, you have no part, etc.

units.la: Claudantur causæ: & breviter inferantur ἐισμάτα[?].
units.tr: Let the reasons be closed, and briefly drawn into conclusions.

units.la: 1. Cum Christum non tantum pati, sed & introire in gloriam oportuerit: non igitur esse, cur passionib. Christi offendamur, sed scandalis mundi gloriam eius opponamus.
units.tr: 1. Since it was necessary for Christ not only to suffer but also to enter into glory, there is therefore no reason for us to be offended by the sufferings of Christ, but we should set his glory against the scandals of the world.

units.la: II. Cum oportuerit introire in gloriam,&c. Ergo fides nostra stat immota, de Christi resurre-ctione: contra dubitationes carnis & sarcasmos impiorum, quod credimus in hominem crucifixum.
units.tr: II. Since it was necessary for him to enter into glory, etc., therefore our faith stands firm regarding the resurrection of Christ, against the doubts of the flesh and the mockeries of the impious, that we believe in a man crucified.

units.la: III. Cum certo resurrexerit secundum scri-pturas: Ergo certò est Messias ille promissus:&c. & certo beneficia justitiæ & salutis æternæ non tantum meruit, sed etiam donat & confert & ser-vabit in æternum.
units.tr: III. Since he certainly rose again according to the Scriptures, therefore certainly he is that promised Messiah, etc., and certainly he has not only merited the benefits of righteousness and eternal salvation, but also bestows and confers them and will preserve them for ever.

units.la: IV. Cum oportuerit Christum pati, & sic introire in gloriam: Ergo & nos cum eo patiamur, peccato moriamur, ut cum eo in gloriam introeamus: Rom.8. 29. prædestinavit ut conformes fiant imagini. 2. Tim.2. 11. Si cum eo mortui sumus cum eo vivemus, &c.
units.tr: IV. Since it was necessary for Christ to suffer, and so to enter into glory, therefore we too should suffer with him, die to sin, so that we may enter into glory with him: Rom. 8:29: He predestined that they should be conformed to the image [of his Son]. 2 Tim. 2:11: If we have died with him, we shall also live with him, etc.

units.la: Conclusio repetit breviter propositionem & hortare breviter ad fiduciam & gratitudinem.
units.tr: Conclusion, briefly repeating the proposition and briefly exhorting to confidence and gratitude.

units.la: I. Ad fiduciam: quod propter nos passus, mortuus, resurrexit, introivit in gloriam: Proinde fiduciam in eo habeamus: Si peccatum, si mundus, si passiones, si mors terret: Christi passiones, mortem, resurrectionem, gloriam opponamus: quia nostra est victoria per fidem 1. Cor. 15. v. 52. 1. Ioh. 5. 5. Ioh. 17. Volo ut ubi ego sum: etiam sint, quos dedisti mihi.
units.tr: I. To confidence: because he suffered, died, rose again and entered into glory on account of us; therefore let us have confidence in him. If sin, if the world, if sufferings, if death terrify us, let us set against them the passion, death, resurrection and glory of Christ, because the victory is ours through faith. 1 Cor. 15:52; 1 John 5:5; John 17: Father, I desire that where I am, there also may be those whom you have given me.

units.la: II. Ad gratitudinem pro tatis[?] beneficiis, quæ nō dantur infidelibus, ingratis, ignavis, aut mollibus: sed vera fide & obedientia Christo adhæ-rentibus: fortiter contra peccatum & mundum pugnantibus, & constantiam in cruce præstanti-bus. Claude voto & gratiarum actiuncula.
units.tr: II. To gratitude for such benefits, which are not given to the unbelieving, the ungrateful, the slothful, or the soft, but to those who cleave to Christ with true faith and obedience, who fight bravely against sin and the world, and who show constancy in the cross. Let us close with a vow and a short thanksgiving.

units.la: Exercitatio VI.
units.tr: Exercitatio VI.

units.la: De morte & resurrectione Christi: conferens oraculum Iesaiae 53. cum historia Evangelica.
units.tr: On the death and resurrection of Christ: comparing the oracle of Isaiah 53 with the Gospel history.

units.la: Exordium. Laudabili more quotannis in Ecclesia celebrari beneficia mortis & resurrectionis Christi.
units.tr: Exordium. It is a praiseworthy custom that the benefits of the death and resurrection of Christ are celebrated every year in the Church.

units.la: Ratio. Quia publica horum repetitio sit vtilis.
units.tr: Reason. Because this public repetition is useful.

units.la: I. Ut fides nostra corroboretur: Iesum crucifixum, mortuum & resuscitatum esse Christum,
units.tr: I. That our faith may be strengthened: that Jesus, crucified, dead and raised up, is the Christ;

units.la: II. Ut crescat consolatio adversus peccatum, diabolum, mortem, mundum: quos hostes Christus moriendo vicit, resurgendo contrivit.
units.tr: II. That consolation may grow against sin, the devil, death and the world, whose enemies Christ conquered by dying and crushed by rising.

units.la: III. Ut Christo victori publice gratias agamus.
units.tr: III. That we may publicly give thanks to Christ the victor.

units.la: Amplif. à minori: Si vetus Ecclesia liberationem ex Ægypto anniversaria solennitate celebravit: multo magis nos beneficium liberationis ex servitute peccati & mortis per Christum quotannis celebrare debemus.
units.tr: Amplification from the lesser: If the ancient Church celebrated the liberation from Egypt with an annual solemnity, then much more ought we to celebrate every year the benefit of our liberation through Christ from the bondage of sin and death.

units.la: Ratio I. quia hic sunt maiora beneficia. 2. quia typi impletio magis celebranda, quàm typus.
units.tr: Reasons: 1. because the benefits here are greater; 2. because the fulfilment of the type is to be celebrated more than the type itself.

units.la: Obiect. Non habemus mandatum certi temporis, ut illi.
units.tr: Objection. We do not have a command of a fixed time, as they had.

units.la: Resp. I. habemus mandatum perpetui Paschatis. 1. Cor. 5. 2. Ecclesia pro sua libertate iâ olim certũ tempus meditationi resurrectionis tribui voluit:non ut effet cultus singularis, neque quod aliis temporibus meditatio fieri non deberet:Sed his de causis: 1. Ut perpetua recordatio spiritualis liberationis solenniter excitetur & celebra-tio in mundi oculis sit conspectior. 2. Ut do-ctrina de Christi persona & beneficiis publice ex verbo Dei repetatur, & pura conservetur. 3. Ut impletio typi & oraculorum solenniter ostendatur, & Ecclesia Christiana à Iudaica separe-tur.
units.tr: Answer. I. We have a command of perpetual Passover: 1 Cor. 5. 2. The Church, in its freedom, long ago wished that a certain time be given to meditation on the resurrection, not so that it would be a special worship, nor because meditation ought not to take place at other times, but for these reasons: 1. so that the perpetual remembrance of spiritual liberation is solemnly stirred up and the celebration is more conspicuous in the eyes of the world; 2. so that the doctrine of Christ's person and benefits is publicly repeated from the Word of God and kept pure; 3. so that the fulfilment of the type and the oracles is solemnly displayed, and the Christian Church is separated from the Jewish.

units.la: Conclusio. Ergo tam laudabilis & utilis consuetudo nobis etiam retinenda.
units.tr: Conclusion. Therefore so praiseworthy and useful a custom is to be retained by us as well.

units.la: Locus benevolentiæ & docilitatis: Tequidem veniam petere debere: & percelli celebritate augustissimi confessus, ac loci insolentia, in quo antea nunquam steteris.
units.tr: Locus of goodwill and teachableness: indeed you ought to ask pardon, and be shaken by the solemnity of this most august assembly, and by the unfamiliarity of the place in which you have never stood before.

units.la: Adverf. Sed te erigi. 1. Conscientia officii, quia fis iussus dicere. 2. Ipsorum benevolentia, quod scientes, se non Demosthenem vel Ciceronem aliquem graviter perorantem, sed adolescentem balbutientem audituros, tamen frequentes accesserint. 3. Æquitate, quod scias, eos in his exercitiis non tam spectare facultatem, quam conatum dicentium, nec tam requirere ut bene & ornate dicant, quàm ut annitendo mediocriter dicere discant. 4. Qualitate argumenti, quod speres eos libenter audituros: quia sis collaturus celeberrimam illam prophetiam Iesaiæ cap. 53. de humilitate, exaltatione, & beneficiis Messiæ cum historia Evangelica.
units.tr: Against this: but you should take heart. 1. from the consciousness of your duty, since you have been ordered to speak; 2. from the goodwill of the audience, since, knowing they will hear not a Demosthenes or some Cicero delivering a weighty oration, but a stammering young man, they nevertheless came in large numbers; 3. from fairness, since you know that in these exercises they look less to skill than to the effort of the speakers, and require less that they speak well and elegantly than that, by striving, they learn to speak moderately well; 4. from the nature of the subject, since you hope they will listen gladly, because you are about to set beside the Gospel history that most celebrated prophecy of Isaiah, chapter 53, concerning the humiliation, exaltation and benefits of the Messiah.

units.la: Narratio sit brevis expositio præcipuorum capitum eius prophetiæ.
units.tr: Narration shall be a brief exposition of the principal heads of that prophecy.

units.la: Consolatur Deus captivos promissione gratuitæ liberationis. Tandem exponens, per quem & quo modo liberaturus esset.
units.tr: God comforts the captives with the promise of free liberation, and finally sets out through whom and in what manner he would liberate them.

units.la: I. Promittit Messiam seruum suum, humilem quidem, sed exaltandum valde: Ecce seruus meus prosperabitur:
units.tr: I. He promises the Messiah, his servant, humble indeed, but to be greatly exalted: Behold, my servant shall prosper:

units.la: II. Queritur propheta de cæcitate & scanda-lo Iudæorum: Quis credit auditui,&c.
units.tr: II. The prophet laments the blindness and the offence of the Jews: Who has believed our report, etc.

units.la: III. Exponit causam scandali: quia æstima-bunt Messiam exaspectu seu forma externa abiectissima: Assurgit ut planta,&c.
units.tr: III. He sets out the cause of the offence: because they will judge the Messiah by his outward appearance and form, most abject: He shall grow up like a plant, etc.

units.la: IV. Recitat historiam passionis, mortis, & resurrectionis Christi eiusque causas & fructus: opponens scandalo triplex remedium:
units.tr: IV. He recounts the history of Christ's passion, death and resurrection, its causes and fruits, opposing to the offence a threefold remedy:

units.la: 1. Reatum & expiationem peccatorum non suorum sed nostrorum per eius humilitatem & mortem: verè languores nostros,&c.
units.tr: 1. The guilt and the expiation of sins, not his own but ours, through his humiliation and death: Surely he has borne our griefs, etc.

units.la: 2. Beneplacitum Dei Patris conterentis Fi-lium propter peccata nostra: & imputantis satis-factionem eius credentibus. Iehova voluit,&c.
units.tr: 2. The good pleasure of God the Father, who crushed the Son on account of our sins, and imputes his satisfaction to believers: Jehovah was pleased, etc.

units.la: 3. Gloriosam resurrectionem, & regnum æ-ternum. Generationem eius, quis,&c.
units.tr: 3. The glorious resurrection and the eternal kingdom: Who shall declare his generation, etc.

units.la: Amplific. à tempore; & claritate prophetiæ. Hæc prædixit 8oo annis ante Christum exhibi-tum (reiiciatur numerus Epiphanii ann. 1600.) adeo aperte & ad historiam Evangelicam congruè: ut non prophetia, sed narratio rei gestæ videatur: & sit Evangelista potius, quam Prophe-ta: Hieronymus in Prologo.
units.tr: Amplification from time, and from the clarity of the prophecy. He foretold these things 800 years before Christ was revealed (let the number of Epiphanius, 1600 years, be rejected), so plainly and so congruently with the Gospel history that it seems not a prophecy but an account of things done, and he is more an Evangelist than a Prophet: Jerome in the Prologue.

units.la: Transitio ad Propos. Cum temporis angustia te singula persequi non sinat, delecturum te quædam præcipua. Propositio I. Quis sit ille servus Iehovæ, de quo Iesaias loquitur. II. Quid de eius humilitate & exaltatione dicat. III. Quid de causis & fructibus utriusque.
units.tr: Transition to the Propositions. Since the shortness of time does not allow me to pursue each point, I shall touch upon certain principal things. Proposition I. Who is that servant of Jehovah of whom Isaiah speaks. II. What he says of his humiliation and exaltation. III. What he says of the causes and fruits of both.

units.la: I. Quis sit ille servus Iehovæ apud Iesaiam.
units.tr: I. Who is that servant of Jehovah in Isaiah.

units.la: Expone recentiorum Iudæorum corruptelam: quod alij de populo Ifraelitico à Chaldæis & Romanis oppresso, alij de propheta, alij de Esra, alij de Iesu Pontifice exponant. Refuta, & ostende quod de Messia loquatur.
units.tr: Expose the corruption of the more recent Jews, who explain it variously: some of the people of Israel oppressed by the Chaldeans and Romans, others of the prophet, others of Ezra, others of Jesus the High Priest. Refute these, and show that it speaks of the Messiah.

units.la: Argumentum I. à scopo oraculi. Propheta consolatur populum promissione spiritualis & æternæ liberationis à peccato & morte: & reconciliationis cum Deo, & vitæ æternæ: At in solo Messia hæc promissio est rata. 2. Cor. 1.[?]
units.tr: Argument I. from the scope of the oracle. The prophet comforts the people with the promise of spiritual and eternal liberation from sin and death, and of reconciliation with God and eternal life. But this promise is valid only in the Messiah. 2 Cor. 1.[?]

units.la: II. Ab attributis, quæ soli Messiæ conveniunt: ut, peccata nostra portare, tollere & expiare sua morte: vibices nostras sanare: pacem cum Deo reddere: esse hominem ἀναμάρτητον[?]: notitia sui justificare multos, esse Pontificem & regem Ecclesiæ, intercedere: colligere & servare Ecclesiam, &c. Ioh.1.29. Hebr.9.28. Rom.8.34. &c.
units.tr: II. From the attributes that belong to the Messiah alone: that he bears, takes away and expiates our sins by his death; heals our wounds; restores peace with God; is a man without sin; by the knowledge of himself justifies many; is the High Priest and King of the Church, intercedes, gathers and preserves the Church, etc. John 1.29. Heb. 9.28. Rom. 8.34. etc.

units.la: III. A testimonio veterum Hebræorum ante & post Christum natum: Ionathanis, Chaldæi Paraphrastæ, Septuaginta interpretum.
units.tr: III. From the testimony of the ancient Hebrews before and after the birth of Christ: of Jonathan, of the Chaldee paraphrast, of the Septuagint, the Seventy.

units.la: IV. A testimonio Evangelistarum & Apostolorum, qui nobis Christianis sufficiunt. Adduc quædam loca, quibus in Christo Messia impleta prophetia dicitur: Phil.2. assumsit formam servi. Ioh.12.38. Rom.10.16. Quis credit, &c. Act. 8.31. de quo loquitur propheta? Matth.8.17. Ipse languores nostros portavit. 1.Pet.2.24.25. Livore eius: Eratis sicut oves, &c.
units.tr: IV. From the testimony of the Evangelists and Apostles, which is sufficient for us Christians. Let some passages be added, in which the prophecy is said to be fulfilled in Christ the Messiah: Phil. 2: he took the form of a servant. John 12.38. Rom. 10.16. Who has believed, etc. Acts 8.31: of whom does the prophet speak? Matt. 8.17: He himself bore our infirmities. 1 Pet. 2.24-25: By his stripes; you were like sheep, etc.

units.la: Obiectio. Iudaicus Populus vocatur Servus Iehovæ. Ies. 42. 19. Quis est cæcus nisi servus meus, &c.
units.tr: Objection. The Jewish people are called the Servant of Jehovah. Isa. 42.19: Who is blind but my servant, etc.

units.la: Respond. Negetur consequentia: si uno loco, quod ubiq;. Circumstantias id docere: quod ibi de populo, quia præcedit: Audite cæci: & sequitur: At ipse est populus direptus, &c. Hic non de populo sed de Messia: quia Servus Iehovæ discer-nitur à populo tanquam redemtor, justificator, à redimendis, justificandis. Illustra simili loco. Ies.42.1. Ecce servus meus quem sustento, &c. quem de Messia loqui patet ex collatione cum Ies. 11. v. 2.3.4. & ex interpretatione Spiritus Sancti Matt. 12.ver.18.
units.tr: Answer. The consequence is denied: what is said in one place is not to be applied everywhere. The context teaches that there it speaks of the people, because it is preceded by: Hear, you blind; and followed by: But this is a people plundered, etc. Here it speaks not of the people but of the Messiah, because the Servant of Jehovah is distinguished from the people as redeemer and justifier, from those to be redeemed and justified. Illustrate it by a similar passage: Isa. 42.1: Behold my servant, whom I uphold, etc., which clearly speaks of the Messiah from comparison with Isa. 11 vv. 2, 3, 4, and from the interpretation of the Holy Spirit, Matt. 12 v. 18.

units.la: Conclusio. Ergo oraculum de Messia loquitur & quidem uno primum humili deinde exaltan-do. Reiice figmentum veterum Hebræorum de duobus: uno humili mendico: altero glorioso monarcha. Ratio: quia tantum unus servus, u-nus Messias est promissus, unum semen mulieris: unus Emanuel: unus mediator Dei & hominum 1.Tim.2.
units.tr: Conclusion. Therefore the oracle speaks of the Messiah, and indeed first of him as humble, then as exalted. Reject the fiction of the ancient Hebrews about two: one a humble beggar, the other a glorious monarch. Reason: because only one servant, only one Messiah is promised, one seed of the woman, one Immanuel, one mediator between God and men: 1 Tim. 2.

units.la: II. De humilitate & exaltatione Messiæ.
units.tr: II. On the humility and exaltation of the Messiah.

units.la: Transitio: ut intelligamus, quis & qualis sit illefervus Ichovæ Messias: oraculum porrò cum impletione conferamus.
units.tr: Transition: so that we may understand who and what kind of man that servant of Jehovah, the Messiah, is; and then let us compare the prophecy with its fulfilment.

units.la: Cum circumstantię sint multæ,non est in singulis immorandum. Distinguein duo: Primum de humilitate: Deinde de glorificatione Messiæ vaticinatur.
units.tr: Since the circumstances are many, we need not dwell on each one. I distinguish two parts: first, he prophesies of the humility; then, of the glorification of the Messiah.

units.la: In singulis exponatur quid sit prædictum hic & alibi: postea ostendatur impletio ex historiâ Evangelicâ.
units.tr: In each case let it be explained what is foretold here and elsewhere; afterwards let the fulfilment be shown from the evangelical history.

units.la: De Humilitate.
units.tr: On the Humility.

units.la: I. Ascendit ut surculus & radix in terra solitaria:
units.tr: I. He shall grow up like a shoot and a root out of a dry ground:

units.la: Ostende de eodem surculo prophetam loqui hoc loco, & Ief. 11. 1. ex trunco succiso Isai, id est, familia Davidis quasi emortua. Terra solitaria generans radicem est virgo virum non passa: ex qua nihil nasci posse videbatur. Ief. 7. Ecce virgo concipiet, &c. Prædicit ergo nasciturum ex matre virgine, familia Davidis sed in summa miseriâ.
units.tr: Show that the prophet here speaks of the same shoot, Isa. 11:1, out of the cut-down stump of Jesse, that is, the family of David, as if it were dead. A dry ground bearing a root is a virgin who has not known a man; from her nothing seemed able to spring. Isa. 7: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, etc. He therefore foretells that he would be born of a virgin mother, of the family of David, but in the greatest misery.

units.la: Evangelista. Christus nascitur ex virgine Maria, quæ virum non cognovit. Luc.1.& 2. filia Davidis, Luc.3. sed paupercula. Bethlemi, sub censu, in stabulo, in præsepi, inter pecora fasciis involutus.
units.tr: The Evangelist: Christ is born of the virgin Mary, who had not known a man. Luke 1 and 2: a daughter of David; Luke 3: but a poor little woman. At Bethlehem, during the census, in a stable, in a manger, among the cattle, wrapped in swaddling clothes.

units.la: II. Non est forma ei, &c. vir dolorum, abjectissimus virorum, &c. Species erit humilis, contemta, conditio servilis, abiecta, misera, erit [illegible, ~8 letters] Psal.22. Vermis sum. Zach.9. Rex pauper.
units.tr: II. He has no form or comeliness, etc.; a man of sorrows, the most despised of men, etc. His appearance will be lowly and despised, his condition servile, abject, wretched; he will be [illegible, ~8 letters]. Ps. 22: I am a worm. Zech. 9: a poor king.

units.la: Evangelista: Christus puer quæritur ad nece, fugit: est positus in signum contradictionis. Luc.2. assumta servi forma: venit ministrare: non ha-bet quò bet quo reclinet caput : habetur pro fabro : pro dæmoniaco : pro helluone : pro impostore: est lapis reprobatus : equitat super asina, &c.
units.tr: The Evangelist: The child Christ is sought for slaughter, and flees; he is set for a sign of contradiction. Luke 2. He takes on the form of a servant; he came to minister; he has nowhere to lay his head; he is regarded as a carpenter, as one possessed by a demon, as a glutton, as an impostor; he is the rejected stone; he rides upon an ass, etc.

units.la: Obiectio. Cantic.1. Pulcher es dilecte mi: & Ni- cephorus formam ejus describit non inelegan-tem : ὡραῖος τῷ ὄψιν, &c.
units.tr: Objection. Song of Songs 1: Thou art beautiful, my beloved; and Nicephorus describes his appearance as not unlovely: beautiful in face, etc.

units.la: Resp. Non corporis & personæ, sed conditio-nis & Regni species contemta intelligitur: Sed coram mundo: ideo dicit: Coram eo: nempe in-fideli populo Iudaico: quia mundus imaginatur sibi Messiam magnificum, terrenum: fastidit vero Christi humilitatem & mortem.
units.tr: Answer. It is understood not of the body and person but of the condition and the kingdom, which is despised; but in the eyes of the world. Therefore he says: before him, namely before the unbelieving Jewish people, because the world imagines for itself a magnificent, earthly Messiah, but shrinks from the humility and death of Christ.

units.la: Transseatur[?] ad hujus narrationem, & ostenda-tur mirus circumstantiarum consensus cum hi-storia.
units.tr: Let us pass to the narration of this, and let the remarkable agreement of the circumstances with the history be shown.

units.la: III. Ex defectione populi mei plaga ei. Per defectionem intelligit apostasiam a Deo, impietatem, proditionem: Per populum suum, Iudæos: sicut Dan.9. Super populum tuum, h. e, ex quo tu natus, cujus tu es civis, propheta, &c. Ergo impietate & scelere Iudæorum prodetur, capietur & trucidabitur. Zach.9. Venditus est 30. argenteis.
units.tr: III. For the transgression of my people was he stricken. By transgression he understands apostasy from God, impiety, betrayal; by his people, the Jews, as in Dan. 9: upon thy people, that is, from whom you were born, whose citizen you are, prophet, etc. Therefore he will be betrayed, seized and slain through the impiety and crime of the Jews. Zech. 9: He was sold for thirty pieces of silver.

units.la: Evangelistæ: Tempore Christi regnabat apostasia: Pharisæi insidiantur Christo: pacisc[?]un-tur cum Iuda[?]: proditur 30. argenteis, capitur in horto[?], ut latro, &c.
units.tr: The Evangelists: In Christ's time apostasy reigned: the Pharisees lay in wait for Christ; they make a bargain with Judas; he is betrayed for thirty pieces of silver, seized in the garden like a robber, etc.

units.la: IV. Per coarctationem & judicium sublatus est. Alii. De angustia & judicio: quasi de resurrectio-ne loquatur Propheta, &c. Sed modus poenæ si-gnificatur: sistendum judicio: accusandum, con-spuendum, colaphis, contumeliis coarctandum: ac iudicis sententia damnandum, &c. Iel[?]. 50. v.6: Faciem meam non abscondi,&c. Judicium ergo erit tumultuarium,&c. Alii: sine carcere & sine judicio tolletur. h.e, violenter ad mortem rapietur: nec carceri includetur captivus, dū causa cognoscatur: sed mox damnatus judicio tolletur, &c.
units.tr: IV. He was taken away by restraint and judgment. Others: from distress and judgment, as if the prophet were speaking of the resurrection, etc. But the manner of punishment is signified: he will be brought before judgment, accused, spat upon, struck with fists, pressed with insults, and condemned by the sentence of the judge, etc. Isa. 50:6: I hid not my face, etc. The judgment therefore will be tumultuous, etc. Others: without prison and without judgment he shall be taken away, that is, he will be violently carried off to death; nor will he be shut up in prison as a captive while the case is examined, but he will be condemned at once and taken away by judgment, etc.

units.la: Evangelista: Christus vinctus sistitur Caiaphę, accusatur, creditur, damnatur. Quid videtur vobis? postridie à Pilato furiosæ plebis clamoribus damnatur ad crucem, illuditur, coronatur, crucifigitur.
units.tr: The Evangelist: Christ, bound, is brought before Caiaphas, accused, believed, condemned. What seems good to you? The next day, by the clamours of the raging mob, he is condemned by Pilate to the cross; he is mocked, crowned, and crucified.

units.la: v. Non aperiet os suum.
units.tr: V. He shall not open his mouth.

units.la: Evangelista: Christus silet, &c.
units.tr: The Evangelist: Christ is silent, etc.

units.la: v I. Ut ovis ducetur ad mactationem.
units.tr: VI. As a sheep he shall be led to the slaughter.

units.la: Evangelista. Christus bajulat crucem: extra urbem, in Golgotha, ad crucifixionem: Agnus Dei tollens peccata:
units.tr: The Evangelist: Christ bears the cross outside the city, to Golgotha, to crucifixion: the Lamb of God, taking away sins.

units.la: v I I. Crucifixus vulnerabitur, exscindetur de terra viventium. Dan. 9. Messias exscindetur. Psal.22. Perfoderunt manus: Diviserunt vestimenta: Psal.69. Potabitur fele.
units.tr: VII. Crucified, he will be wounded and cut off from the land of the living. Dan. 9: the Messiah shall be cut off. Ps. 22: they pierced my hands; they divided my garments. Ps. 69: they shall give me gall to drink.

units.la: Evangelista: Crucifixerunt cum, &c. Accurrens miles spongiam calamo imposuit, &c. Diviserunt vestimenta, &c.
units.tr: The Evangelist: They crucified him with others, etc. A soldier running up put a sponge on a reed, etc. They divided his garments, etc.

units.la: v I I I. Cum impiis reputabitur.
units.tr: VIII. He shall be reckoned among the wicked.

units.la: Evangelista: Componitur cum Barraba latrone: crucifigitur medius, inter duos latrones.
units.tr: The Evangelist: He is placed with Barabbas the robber; he is crucified in the middle, between two robbers.

units.la: I X. Pro transgressoribus oravit:
units.tr: IX. He prayed for the transgressors:

units.la: Evangelista: Pater dimitte eis, &c. Oravit pro Ecclesia, Ioh. 17. & interpellat pro nobis peccatoribus. Rom. 8.
units.tr: The Evangelist: Father, forgive them, etc. He prayed for the Church, John 17, and intercedes for us sinners, Rom. 8.

units.la: x. Populus meus dabit sepulcrum eius impiis: & diviti in mortibus eius. Aliqui μετὰ θάνατον[?] faciunt Morietur ut impius: sepelietur ut dives. Sed historia declarat. Impiis n. militib. sepulcrū ejus exposuit custodiēdum: in quod à divite Iosepho post mortem fuerat repositus.
units.tr: X. My people shall give his grave to the wicked, and to the rich in his death. Some make it: he shall die as the wicked, and be buried as the rich. But the history declares otherwise. For he placed his grave under the guard of wicked soldiers, into which, after death, he had been laid by the rich Joseph.

units.la: XII. Denique patietur & morietur Innocēs: Quia non fecit violentiam: nec est dolus. Psalm. 69. Quod non rapui, &c.
units.tr: XII. Finally, the innocent one will suffer and die: because he did no violence, nor was there any deceit. Ps. 69: which I did not steal, etc.

units.la: Evangelista: Ioh. 8. Quis ex vobis arguet me, &c. 1 Pet.1. Agnus immaculatus. 1. Pet.3. Passus justus pro iniustis. Damnatur à iudice innocēs. Cōgere breviter testimonia Innocētię. Pilatus quinquies innocente pronunciat. Vxor Pilati. Titulus crucis: Latro: Centurio: Epistola Pilati apud Ægef. Iosephus lib.18.c.4.
units.tr: The Evangelist: John 8: Which of you will convict me, etc. 1 Pet. 1: a lamb without blemish. 1 Pet. 3: the righteous suffered for the unrighteous. The innocent is condemned by the judge. Let the testimonies of his innocence be gathered briefly. Pilate pronounces him innocent five times. Pilate's wife. The title on the cross. The robber. The centurion. Pilate's letter, in Aegesippus. Josephus, book 18, chapter 4.

units.la: Transitio ad glorificationem.
units.tr: Transition to glorification.

units.la: I. Mortuus vincet mortem, resurget, vivet in æternum: Generationem eius quis enarrabit, &c. q.d,etsi per coarctationem & judicium tolletur: tamen revivisc et, & vivet in æternum. Videbit semen: quod non est mortuorum sed viventium: Prolongabit dies: post mortem: Exemtus molestia seipsum videbit. Ergo vivet: Ergo resurget. Partietur spolia cum iustis. Ergo eripiet spolia hostibus. Ergo vincet peccatum, mortem, diabolum. Ergo resurget. Psal.16: Non derelinques animam, &c.
units.tr: I. Having died, he will conquer death, rise again, and live forever: "Who will declare his generation?" etc. That is to say: even though he will be taken away by oppression and judgment, yet he will come back to life and live forever. "He shall see his seed," which belongs not to the dead but to the living. "He shall prolong his days": after death. "Freed from trouble, he shall see himself." Therefore he will live; therefore he will rise. "He shall divide the spoils with the righteous." Therefore he will snatch the spoils from his enemies; therefore he will conquer sin, death and the devil; therefore he will rise. Psalm 16: "You will not leave my soul," etc.

units.la: Evangelista: Resurgit tertia die, invitis hostib. apparet discipulis, mulieribus, videte. palpate, &c. Per mortem ademit potestatem. Heb.2. Triumphavit hostes per seipsum. Col.2. Nec moritur amplius. Rom.6.
units.tr: The Evangelist: He rises on the third day, appearing, against the wishes of his enemies, to the disciples and to the women: "See, touch," etc. "By his death he took away the power" (Heb. 2). "He triumphed over the enemies through himself" (Col. 2). "He dies no more" (Rom. 6).

units.la: II. Erit Rex & Sacerdos Ecclesiæ æternus. Servus meus exaltabitur valde: Delectatio Iehovæ in in manu ejus prosperabitur, &c. Justificabit multos, &c. & quidem evectus in coelum, dividet praedam, dabit dona hominibus. Psal. 68: Sedens ad dextram Dei dominabitur inimicis. Psal.110.
units.tr: II. He will be the eternal King and Priest of the Church. "My servant shall be exalted greatly; the good pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand," etc. "He shall justify many," etc. And indeed, carried up into heaven, he will divide the spoil and give gifts to men (Ps. 68). "Sitting at the right hand of God, he will rule over his enemies" (Ps. 110).

units.la: Evangelista: Ascendit die 40: sedet ad dextram Dei: caput Ecclesiae. Eph. 1. colligens ac regens Ecclesiam verbo & Spiritu: Euntes docete, &c. Ero vobiscum, &c. Justificans credentes, Rom 3.&5: mittens Spiritum S. Act. 2. dans dona hominibus. Eph. 4. & vitam aeternam. Joh. 3.
units.tr: The Evangelist: He ascended on the fortieth day, sits at the right hand of God, is the head of the Church (Eph. 1), gathering and ruling the Church by the Word and the Spirit: "Go and teach," etc. "I will be with you," etc. "Justifying those who believe" (Rom. 3 and 5), sending the Holy Spirit (Acts 2), giving gifts to men (Eph. 4), and eternal life (John 3).

units.la: Claudatur collatio & deducatur [illegible, ~9 letters] breviter.
units.tr: Let the comparison be closed and drawn together briefly.

units.la: 1. Contra Judaeos: Etsi non credant auditui non nostro:tamen Iesus est ille promissus servus Jehovae Messias: quia in eo solo omnia impleta.
units.tr: 1. Against the Jews: Even if they do not believe our hearing, yet Jesus is that promised servant of Jehovah, the Messiah, because in him alone all things have been fulfilled.

units.la: 2. Contra Marcionem: Eutychen: Vbiquitarios: Ergo verus homo nobis ὁμοούσιος excepto peccato. Hebr. 2. quia vere passus, mortuus:
units.tr: 2. Against Marcion, Eutyches, and the Ubiquitarians: Therefore he is a true man, homoousios with us, apart from sin (Heb. 2), because he truly suffered and died.

units.la: 3. Contra Arianos: Ergo & verus Deus. Jehovae opera facit propria potentia: remittit peccata: justificat multos: Deus est qui justificat. Rom. 8. seipsum excitat: Habeo potestatem, &c.
units.tr: 3. Against the Arians: Therefore also a true God. He does the works of Jehovah by his own power; he forgives sins; he justifies many; God is the one who justifies (Rom. 8). He raises himself up: "I have power," etc.

units.la: Obiectio. Est Servus Jehovae: Ergo non Jehova.
units.tr: Objection: He is the Servant of Jehovah; therefore he is not Jehovah.

units.la: Respon. Est utrumque diverso respectu. Jehova secundum Deitatem, quia facit opera Jehovae, & quidem ὁμοίως cum Patre. Joh. 5. Ierem. 32: Jehova justitia nostra. Jes. 25. Ecce Deus noster. 1. Cor. 2. Dominum gloriae crucifixerunt. Servus 1. Humanitate assumta. Phil. 2: assumsit formam servi. 2. Officio: quia opus Jehovae per manum eius prosperabitur. rabitur.Inæqualitas officii non tollit ęqualitatem naturæ.
units.tr: Answer: He is both, in different respects. He is Jehovah according to the Deity, because he performs the works of Jehovah, and indeed in the same way as the Father (John 5). "Jehovah is our righteousness" (Jer. 32). "Behold, our God" (Isa. 25). "They crucified the Lord of glory" (1 Cor. 2).
