He is Servant (1) in the assumed humanity: "he took the form of a servant" (Phil. 2); (2) in his office: because "the work of Jehovah shall prosper in his hand." The inequality of office does not remove the equality of nature.

units.la: 4. Contra Nestorianos. Ergo Deus & homo, idem: quia idem moritur, resurgit, justificat. Messias unus non duo, &c. Deus suo sanguine redemit Ecclesiam, &c. Act. 20.
units.tr: 4. Against the Nestorians: Therefore God and man are the same one: because the same one dies, rises again, justifies. The Messiah is one, not two, etc. "God redeemed the Church with his own blood" (Acts 20).

units.la: III. Causæ & fructus resurrectionis.
units.tr: III. The causes and fruits of the resurrection.

units.la: Transitio. Hæc scire parum prodesset, nisi causas & fructus tantæ humilitatis & subsecutæ gloriæ intelligeremus: exemplo Iudæorum &c.
units.tr: Transition. Knowing these things would profit us little, unless we also understood the causes and fruits both of so great a humiliation and of the glory that followed it: as in the example of the Jews, etc.

units.la: Expone duas causas, ex quibus fructus elician-tur.
units.tr: Set out the two causes from which the fruits are drawn.

units.la: Prima. Voluntas & consilium Dei. ver.10. Iehova delectatus est, &c. Zach.13. Percute pastorem, &c.
units.tr: First. The will and counsel of God. Ver. 10: Jehovah was pleased, etc. Zech. 13: Strike the shepherd, etc.

units.la: Confer Evangelica. Quia hoc consilium Dei oraculis fuit revelatum, & impleri oportuit: ideo Christus & Evangelistæ toties. Sic oportebat Christum pati, impleri Scripturas. Filius hominis vadit κατα το ωρισμένον. Luc.22. Act.2.&4.
units.tr: Compare the Gospels. Because this counsel of God was revealed in the oracles and had to be fulfilled, therefore Christ and the evangelists so often say: Thus it behooved Christ to suffer, that the Scriptures be fulfilled. The Son of man goes according to what has been determined [κατα το ωρισμένον]. Luke 22; Acts 2 and 4.

units.la: Illatio contrarii. Non ergo fortuito: nec rabie Iudæorum superatus ad dirissimam mortem pertractus est.
units.tr: Inference of the contrary. Therefore not by chance, nor was he overcome by the rage of the Jews and dragged to a most dreadful death.

units.la: Ad minori. Si ne pilus quidem absque Dei voluntate cadere potest, quomodo absque ea Filius Dei crucifixus?
units.tr: From the lesser. If not even a hair can fall without the will of God, how could the Son of God be crucified without it?

units.la: Occup. Non ideo excusati Iudæi, quia nec jussi, nec ut obtemperent Deo, Christum crucifigunt.
units.tr: Objection anticipated. The Jews are not excused on the ground that, in crucifying Christ, they neither were commanded nor acted to obey God.

units.la: Altera causa: Peccata nostra. Ad hanc transeatur per occupationem: An pater crudelis, qui Filium? lium ?an injustus,qui insontem? an [illegible, ~9 letters]-[illegible, ~3 letters] ,qui afflictum delectatus est conterere?
units.tr: Second cause: our sins. We pass to this by way of an objection: Is the Father cruel, who [delivered up] his Son? Is he unjust, who [was pleased] to crush the innocent, or the afflicted [illegible]?

units.la: Removeantur hæc ex secunda causa: Deus peccata nostra in eum conjecit v.6. & ipse in fe sponte suscepit, tradens animam suam sacrificium pro reatu, v.4.& 10.
units.tr: Let these be removed from the second cause: God laid our sins upon him (v. 6), and he himself took them up willingly, giving his soul as a sacrifice for guilt (vv. 4 and 10).

units.la: Quid peccata nostra ad ipsum? Resp. Fuit Meffias: debuit ergo satisfacere pro peccatis nostris, & liberare populum suum a morte: quod aliter, nisi luendo mortem peccatis nostris debitam fieri non potuit. Matt.1. Ideo Iesus dictus: Rom. 8. Qui filio proprio non pepercit, &c. Gal.1. Heb.9.
units.tr: What have our sins to do with him? Answer. He was the Messiah: he therefore had to make satisfaction for our sins and to free his people from death, which could not be done otherwise than by paying with death the penalty owed to our sins. Matt. 1. Therefore he was called Jesus. Rom. 8: He who did not spare his own Son, etc. Gal. 1; Heb. 9.

units.la: Tradidit semetipsum.
units.tr: He gave himself up.

units.la: Amplificetur a causis consilii Dei: cur per mortem Filii oportuerit fieri liberationem.
units.tr: Let it be enlarged from the causes of God's counsel: why the deliverance had to be effected through the death of the Son.

units.la: 1. Vt iustitiæ Dei fatisfieret.
units.tr: 1. So that the justice of God might be satisfied.

units.la: 2. Vt veritati comminationis: Morte morieris.
units.tr: 2. So that the truth of the threat might stand: You shall surely die.

units.la: 3. Vt Deus declararet immensam caritatem erga nos: tradendo filium unigenitum. Ioh.3. Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut filium suum daret, &c. Rom.5. In hoc commendat, &c.
units.tr: 3. So that God might declare his immense love toward us, by giving up his only-begotten Son. John 3: God so loved the world that he gave his Son, etc. Rom. 5: God commends his love, etc.

units.la: 4. Vt veritas responderet typis & oraculis: Victimæ cædebantur: Serpens æneus suspensus. Spiritus Christi in prophetis prædixerat. 1. Pet.1.
units.tr: 4. So that the truth might correspond to the types and oracles: victims were slain; the bronze serpent was lifted up. The Spirit of Christ had foretold it in the prophets. 1 Pet. 1.

units.la: Claude causas. Ergo Deus nō crudelis: injustus, [illegible, ~8 letters] : quia contrivit non ut Filium sed ut Meffiam: non ut innocentem: sed ut vadem: saluti nostræ consulens, &c.
units.tr: Let the causes be summed up. Therefore God is not cruel or unjust [illegible]: because he bruised not as a Son but as the Messiah, not as innocent but as a surety, consulting for our salvation, etc.

units.la: Eliciantur fructus breviter.
units.tr: Let the fruits be briefly drawn out.

units.la: 1. Reconciliatio nostri cum Deo. Deducatur ex prima causa: quia Deus ipse percussit: Ergo acceptat ejus [illegible, ~5 letters]. Castigatio pacis eius, &c. Rom.5. Reconciliati Deo per mortem, &c.
units.tr: 1. Reconciliation of us with God. This is deduced from the first cause: because God himself struck him; therefore he accepts his [illegible]. The chastisement of our peace is upon him, etc. Rom. 5: Reconciled to God through the death, etc.

units.la: 2. Remissio peccatorum seu Justificatio: quia peccatis abolitis sumus justi. Justificabit multos, &c. Rom 5. Justificati sanguine. Rom. 4. Mortuus propter peccata nostra.
units.tr: 2. Forgiveness of sins, or justification: because, with sins abolished, we are righteous. He shall justify many, etc. Rom. 5: Justified by his blood. Rom. 4: Dead for our sins.

units.la: 3. Regeneratio seu instauratio naturae per Spiritum S. Livore eius sanati: Explica metaphorā. Morsu diaboli perierat natura: Sanguine Christi sanatur morsus, Rom.6.2.Cor.5.Col.3.
units.tr: 3. Regeneration, or restoration of nature through the Holy Spirit. By his bruises we are healed: explain the metaphor. Nature had perished by the bite of the devil; by the blood of Christ the bite is healed. Rom. 6; 2 Cor. 5; Col. 3.

units.la: 4. Suscitatio corporum gloriosa. Videbit Semen: quia ipse caput, nos membra. Rom.8. Si spiritus eius, &c. 1.Cor.15. Sicut in Adamo omnes moriuntur, &c.
units.tr: 4. The raising of bodies in glory. He shall see his seed: because he is the head and we the members. Rom. 8: If his Spirit, etc. 1 Cor. 15: As in Adam all die, etc.

units.la: 5. Glorificatio Ecclesiae, ver. 11. Seipsum videns satiabitur. Ioh.17. volo:
units.tr: 5. The glorification of the Church, ver. 11: He shall see himself and be satisfied. John 17. I wish to add:

units.la: Ἀθροισμὸς per ἀποδίωξιν[?]. Beneficia Christi superare omnem eloquentiam: esse abyssum omnis consolationis: quia omnia fecit propter salutem nostram.
units.tr: Accumulation through a [turning away?]. The benefits of Christ surpass all eloquence: they are an abyss of all consolation, because he did everything for our salvation.

units.la: Percurre circunstantias & usum singularem.
units.tr: Run through the circumstances and the singular use.

units.la: Ideo ascendit ut surculus: ut nobis daret de ar-bore vitae. Apoc.2.7.
units.tr: Therefore he went up as a tender shoot: that he might give us to eat of the tree of life. Rev. 2:7.

units.la: Ideo pauper: ut nos ditaret.2.Cor.8.9.
units.tr: Therefore poor: that he might enrich us. 2 Cor. 8:9.

units.la: Abiectissimus virorum: ne abjiceremur a Deo,
units.tr: Most abject of men: lest we be cast off by God.

units.la: Vir dolorum: ut sanaret dolores nostros.
units.tr: A man of sorrows: that he might heal our sorrows.

units.la: A Deo percussus: ut iram Dei in se a nobis derivaret.
units.tr: Smitten by God: that he might turn the wrath of God from us upon himself.

units.la: Proditus: ut nos reciperemur in gratiam.
units.tr: Betrayed: that we might be received into favor.

units.la: Captus: ut nos in libertatem vindicaret.
units.tr: Taken captive: that he might vindicate us into liberty.

units.la: Per coarctationem & judicium sublatum: ne judicio Dei nos coarctaremur.
units.tr: Taken away by oppression and judgment: that we might not be oppressed by the judgment of God.

units.la: Os nō aperuit accusatus: non cōsentiēs[?] tacedo, sed despiciens non refellendo, ut gloriemur nos ejus patientia servatos.
units.tr: He did not open his mouth when accused: not consenting, but keeping silent, scorning to refute, so that we might glory that we were saved by his patience.

units.la: Ut ovis ad mactationem ductus: ut obedientia sua expiaret nostram contumaciam.
units.tr: Led as a sheep to the slaughter: that by his obedience he might expiate our stubbornness.

units.la: Opprobria pertulit: ut improperia detrahentium non moverent Electos.
units.tr: He bore reproaches: that the taunts of detractors might not move the elect.

units.la: Damnatus à judice: ut liberaret damnatos in judicio Dei.
units.tr: Condemned by the judge: that he might free the condemned in the judgment of God.

units.la: Eductus extra urbem: ut ex mundo nos in coelum duceret. Hebr.13.
units.tr: Led outside the city: that he might lead us out of the world into heaven. Heb. 13.

units.la: Deputatus inter impios: ut nos filios Dei faceret.
units.tr: Numbered among the wicked: that he might make us sons of God.

units.la: Crucifixus: ut maledictionem tolleret. Gal.3. & in cruce ostenderet veteris hominis nostri oc-casum: atque omnia ad se traheret.
units.tr: Crucified: that he might take away the curse. Gal. 3. And on the cross he showed the putting off of our old man, and drew all things to himself.

units.la: Vulneratus: ut sanaret & obligaret confractos.
units.tr: Wounded: that he might heal and bind up the broken.

units.la: Peccata nostra portavit in ligno: ut nos justifica-ret.
units.tr: He bore our sins on the tree: that he might justify us.

units.la: Innocens passus: ut esset victima: & Pontifex à peccatorib. separatus.
units.tr: Suffered as the innocent: that he might be the victim, and a high priest separated from sinners.

units.la: Clamavit in cruce : ut nos exaudiremur in morte.
units.tr: He cried out on the cross: that we might be heard in death.

units.la: Oravit pro transgressorib. ut nos clamemus Ab-ba pater.
units.tr: He prayed for transgressors: that we might cry, Abba, Father.

units.la: Mortuus est: ut mortuos vivificaret.
units.tr: He died: that he might quicken the dead.

units.la: Sepultus: ut sepulturam nobis sanctificaret.
units.tr: Buried: that he might sanctify the grave for us.

units.la: Resurrexit: ut victorem mortis, Diaboli, &c. se declararet.
units.tr: Rose again: that he might show himself the conqueror of death, of the devil, etc.

units.la: Accepit partem pro multis: ut cum justis præ-dam divideret.
units.tr: He received a portion among the many: that he might divide the spoil with the just.

units.la: Prolongat dies suos : ut opus Iehovæ per eum prosperetur, &c.
units.tr: He prolongs his days: that the work of Jehovah might prosper through him, etc.

units.la: Hinc deducātur breviter quædam κεφάλαια[?].
units.tr: From this let certain heads be briefly drawn.

units.la: 1. Cum simus Deo reconciliati: Ergo pacem habemus: nihil nos separabit, &c. qa sublatis peccatis Deus non habet causam nobis irascendi: Et gratia Dei immutabilis.
units.tr: 1. Since we are reconciled to God, we therefore have peace: nothing shall separate us, etc., because, with sins taken away, God has no cause to be angry with us, and the grace of God is unchangeable.

units.la: 2. Cum Filius peccata nostra portarit: Ergo in sola ejus satisfactione quaeramus justitiam & vitam. Act. 4. Non est aliud, &c.
units.tr: 2. Since the Son bore our sins, let us therefore seek righteousness and life in his satisfaction alone. Acts 4: There is no other, etc.

units.la: 3. Cum resurrexerit: Ergo vere devicit hostes, & nos ab eorum potestate liberavit. 1. Cor. 15.
units.tr: 3. Since he has risen, he has truly conquered our enemies and freed us from their power. 1 Cor. 15.

units.la: 4. Cum opus Iehovæ per eum prosperetur: Ergo perpetuo servabitur Eccl: licet premat. &c.
units.tr: 4. Since the work of Jehovah prospers through him, the Church will therefore be preserved forever, though it be pressed, etc.

units.la: 5. Cum generationem ejus nemo possit enarrare: Ergo nos glorificabit in aeternum: quia nos ejus <bl>{Greek: σῶμα}</bl>: membra: ossa.
units.tr: 5. Since no one can declare his generation, he will therefore glorify us forever, because we are his body [Greek: σῶμα], members, and bones.

units.la: Conclusio: Ista hoc tempore repetenda duxi.
units.tr: Conclusion: I have thought these things should be repeated at this time.

units.la: Sed oportet, ut nobis applicemus fide, & gratisimus,
units.tr: But we must apply them to ourselves by faith, and be most thankful.

units.la: Ratio: quia soli credentes & grati fruuntur hac consolatione: Servus meus justus cognitione sui justificabit multos. Ostende breviter, in quibus consistat salutaris cognitio Christi: de qua Ioh. 17: & rejice figmentum de redemtione generali etiam damnatorum: quia Evangelium requirit fidem: damnat infideles. Ioh. 3. Ut igitur ad nos pertineant beneficia.
units.tr: Reason: because only believers and the thankful enjoy this consolation: My righteous servant shall justify many by his knowledge. Briefly show in what the saving knowledge of Christ consists, concerning which John 17; and reject the fiction of a general redemption, even of the damned, because the Gospel requires faith and condemns unbelievers. John 3. So that the benefits may pertain to us:

units.la: 1. Fide amplectamur hunc servum Iehovae Iehovam: & in eo solo quaeramus remedia adversus omnes tentationes.
units.tr: 1. Let us embrace by faith this servant of Jehovah, Jehovah; and in him alone let us seek remedies against all temptations.

units.la: Si Iudaei blasphemant: Nos respiciamus consensum oraculi & historiae.
units.tr: If the Jews blaspheme: let us look to the agreement of the oracle and of history.

units.la: Si peccatorum conscientia nos urget: spectemus agnum hunc Dei, qui, &c.
units.tr: If the consciousness of sins presses us: let us look to this Lamb of God, who, etc.

units.la: Z v.
units.tr: Z v.

units.la: Si ira Dei terret: cogitemus contritum esse à Deo, ut nos livore. &c.
units.tr: If the wrath of God terrifies: let us consider that he was bruised by God so that we might be healed by his stripes, etc.

units.la: Si justitia deest: Servus Iehovæ cognoscentes ipsum justificat.
units.tr: If righteousness is lacking: the Servant of Jehovah, by being known, justifies.

units.la: Si peccatorum reliquiæ cruciant: sciamus hûc factum esse sacrificium pro reatu ; & nihil esse damnationis in iis qui:&c. Rom.8.
units.tr: If the remnants of sins torment: let us know that a sacrifice for guilt was made here, and that there is no condemnation for those who, etc. Rom. 8.

units.la: Si infirmitas & metus defectionis: Oravit pro transgressoribus: intercedit perpetuo ne deficiat fides nostra. Nemo rapiet,&c.
units.tr: If weakness and the fear of falling away: He prayed for transgressors: he intercedes perpetually that our faith may not fail. No one shall snatch, etc.

units.la: Si diabolus & Tyranni minantur tumultuan-tur: Sciamus per mortem ademisse potestatem: mundum vicisse: ridere conatus tyrannorum in cœlis: opus Domini prosperabitur.
units.tr: If the devil and tyrants threaten and rage: let us know that by death he has taken away power, has conquered the world, and laughs at the attempts of tyrants in the heavens; the work of the Lord shall prosper.

units.la: 2. Gratissimus. 1. Resurgendo cum Chri-sto.Rom.6.Col.2.
units.tr: 2. Thankfulness. 1. By rising with Christ. Rom. 6; Col. 2.

units.la: 2. Celebrando immensam[?] Dei φιλανθρωπίαν[?]: & Filii amorem,&c.
units.tr: 2. By celebrating the immense [?] philanthropy of God and the love of the Son, etc.

units.la: Gratias igitur tibi æterne Deus,&c. Oramus, ut nos confirmes: serves Ecclesiam, Scholas, Doctores, Principem, &c. compescas hostium furo-res: ut te in hac & æterna vita celebremus.
units.tr: Therefore we give thanks to you, eternal God, etc. We pray that you would confirm us, preserve the Church, the schools, the teachers, the prince, etc.; restrain the fury of enemies, so that we may celebrate you in this life and in eternal life.

units.la: Exercitatio VII.
units.tr: Exercitatio VII.

units.la: De persona Christi resurgentis: deque resurrectionis modo & fructibus.
units.tr: On the person of the risen Christ: and on the manner and fruits of the resurrection.

units.la: Exordii propositio: Suscipienti tibi hoc tempore dicendi munus, varia occurrere, quæ deterreant.
units.tr: Proposition of the exordium: As you take up the office of speaking at this time, various things present themselves which discourage you.

units.la: Αἰτιολογία per enumerationem difficultatum.
units.tr: Aetiology by enumeration of the difficulties.

units.la: 1. Argumenti tractandi magnitudo. 2. Tua infantia. 3. Gravitas judicii auditorum, cui satisfacere sit difficile. 4. Metus tædii, quod allaturus esse videaris auditorio eorundem repetitione, de quibus meminéris ex hoc loco non femelante hac dictum esse. Amplif. nova fere tantum delectare.
units.tr: 1. The greatness of the subject to be treated. 2. Your youth. 3. The weight of the judgment of the hearers, to which it is difficult to give satisfaction. 4. Fear of tedium, lest you seem likely to bore the audience by repeating what they will remember was said from this place, not once only, on the same matters. Amplification: new things alone delight almost everyone.

units.la: Adversativa: Sed non pauciora esse, quæ te in instituto confirmant.
units.tr: Adversative: But there are no fewer things which strengthen you in your undertaking.

units.la: 1. Authoritatem præceptorum.
units.tr: 1. The authority of your teachers.

units.la: 2. Academiæ laudabilem consuetudinem.
units.tr: 2. The commendable custom of the Academy.

units.la: 3. Ipsam temporis rationem, quæ solennem beneficiorum Christi repetitionem postulet.
units.tr: 3. The very reason of the time, which calls for the solemn repetition of the benefits of Christ.

units.la: 4. Exempla condiscipulorum, quos ante te patienter sæpe & attentè ex hoc loco dicentes audierint: res ipsas magis, quam ipsorum facultate spectantes, & sua æquanimitate approbationem exercitiorum ejusmodi testantes.
units.tr: 4. The examples of your fellow students, who before you have often heard others speaking from this place patiently and attentively, looking to the matters themselves rather than to the speakers' abilities, and by their equanimity testifying their approval of exercises of this kind.

units.la: 5. Iudicium Apostoli, qui non subinde nova, sed eadem de iisdem scripsit propter Ecclesiæ utilitatem. Phil. 3. 1. Hæc non singula singulis, sed omnia paucis periodis comprehendantur.
units.tr: 5. The judgment of the Apostle, who did not write new things from time to time, but the same things about the same matters, for the good of the Church. Phil. 3. 1. These things are to be comprehended not singly for each, but all together in a few periods.

units.la: Præcisio habens transitionem: His fretum te nō prolixius velle petere veniam: sed transfire ad rem ipsam.
units.tr: Transitional precision: Relying on these, you do not wish to ask pardon at greater length, but to pass over to the matter itself.

units.la: Propositio: Tria autem breviter repetiturum, quæ meminëris ab eo, qui anno superiore has partes agebat, tibi relicta fuisse.
units.tr: Proposition: You will, however, briefly repeat three things which you remember were left to you by the one who handled these parts in the previous year.

units.la: 1. Quis & qualis sit ille cujus resurrectionem hoc tempore celebrat Christiana Ecclesia.
units.tr: 1. Who and what kind of person is he whose resurrection the Christian Church celebrates at this time.

units.la: 2. Quis[?] quodus[?] resurrectionis tum externus, tum etiam internus fuerit.
units.tr: 2. What the resurrection was, both external and also internal.

units.la: 3. Additurum quædam de fructibus.
units.tr: 3. That he will add certain things concerning the fruits.

units.la: I. De persona Christi resurgentis.
units.tr: I. Of the person of the risen Christ.

units.la: Initio breviter ostendatur hujus partis necessitas, quod sit basis omnium eorum, quæ de resurrectione Christi Scriptura prædicat.
units.tr: First, the necessity of this part is briefly shown: that it is the basis of all those things which Scripture proclaims about the resurrection of Christ.

units.la: Ea comprehendantur duobus capitibus: 1. Certò ac verè Christum resurrexisse. 2. resurrexisse propter justitiam nostram.
units.tr: These are comprehended under two heads: 1. That Christ rose truly and certainly. 2. That he rose on account of our justification.

units.la: Horum neutrum vel extra Ecclesiam, vel ab hæreticis propter ignorationem Personæ & officii resurgentis credi posse, ostendatur ex eorum dilemmate: Aut creator aut creatura est ille resurgens. Si creator mori & resurgere non potuit: si creatura seu homo, nec resurgere sua vi, nec vitam parare nobis potuit.
units.tr: That neither of these can be believed outside the Church, or by heretics, on account of their ignorance of the person and office of the one rising, is shown from their dilemma: either the one rising is the Creator or a creature. If he is the Creator, he could not die and rise again; if a creature or man, he could neither rise by his own power nor procure life for us.

units.la: Subjiciatur per adversativam correctio seu tertium membrum: Nec Deum merum, nec hominem merum: sed utrunque esse: h. e, Deum, & hominem, & brevissimè declaratur unio personalis ex dictis. 1. Tim. 3. Deus manifestatus in carne: Heb. 2. Assumsit semen Abrahæ, ut per mortem, &c. & Rom. 1. Per resurrectionem declaratus est filius Dei. Ioh. 3. Rom. 8. 'Deus filium suum proprium dedit, ut omnis; & Act. 20. Deus proprio sanguine, &c. & hinc inferatur de officio: Quod hæc persona resurgens sit promissus servator, & Messias:
units.tr: A correction, or third member, is added by way of contrast: neither God alone nor man alone, but both: that is, God and man; and the personal union is briefly declared from the passages cited: 1 Tim. 3, God manifested in the flesh; Heb. 2, he took on the seed of Abraham, that through death, etc.; and Rom. 1, declared to be the Son of God by the resurrection. John 3; Rom. 8, God gave his own Son, that every one; and Acts 20, God with his own blood, etc. From this is inferred the office: that this risen person is the promised Saviour and Messiah.

units.la: Ratio Consequentiæ, seu convertibilitatis terminorum istorum: ἀναστάσιμον esse: & Messiam esse:
units.tr: The reasoning of the consequence, or the convertibility of these terms: to be risen again [ἀναστάσιμον] is to be the Messiah.

units.la: Ostendatur ex officio Mediatoris: quod nisi [ἀνθρώπῳ[?]] persona, & quidem unica (1. Tim. 2.) sustinere nemo potuit: quia & veri, ac justi hominis & Dei partes simul exequi debuit, &c.
units.tr: It is shown from the office of the Mediator: which no one could sustain unless the person were one, and indeed a single person (1 Tim. 2), since he had to fulfil at once the parts of a true and just man and of God, etc.

units.la: Colligatur hic breviter summa propositionis primæ de persona, & officio Christi: & exstruatur πρόθεσμα[?] de certitudine resurrectionis Christi.
units.tr: Here the sum of the first proposition about the person and office of Christ is briefly gathered, and a πρόθεσμα[?] about the certainty of the resurrection of Christ is constructed.

units.la: 1. Si filius Dei unigenitus; & dilectus: Non igitur pater eum derelinquere in morte potuit. Psal. 16. Est mihi à dextris, ne concutiar. Act. 13. 33. Paulus ex hoc argumento probat resurrectionem Christi.
units.tr: 1. If the Son of God is only-begotten and beloved, then the Father could not leave him in death. Psalm 16, He is at my right hand, that I may not be moved. Acts 13:33: Paul proves the resurrection of Christ by this argument.

units.la: 2. Si verus Deus: Ergo author, & dator vitæ, & à morte teneri non potuit.
units.tr: 2. If he is true God, then, as author and giver of life, he could not be held by death.

units.la: 3. Si verus & justus homo: Ergo mors ei dominari non potuit. Rom. 6. Stipendium peccati mors est.
units.tr: 3. If he is a true and just man, then death could not have dominion over him. Rom. 6, The wages of sin is death.

units.la: Occupatio: peccata quidem nostra, Deus in eâ rejecerat, sed moriendo jam expiaverat.
units.tr: Objection taken up: God indeed had cast our sins away in him, but by dying he had already made expiation for them.

units.la: 4. Si Messias: Ergo rex, & sacerdos Ecclesiæ: Ergo non tantum sacrificio suo pro peccatis nostris satisfacere: sed etiam deinceps perpetuò intercedere pro nobis: Ecclesiam liberare, regenerare, defendere, & glorificare tandem, ac proinde ex mortuis resurgere eum oportuit. 1. Cor. 15. Per hominem mors & resurrectio. Rom. 8. Quis est qui condemnet? &c.
units.tr: 4. If he is the Messiah, then he is king and priest of the Church. Therefore it was necessary that he not only satisfy God for our sins by his sacrifice, but also thereafter intercede for us perpetually, free, regenerate, defend and at last glorify the Church, and so rise from the dead. 1 Cor. 15, By man came death and resurrection. Rom. 8, Who is he that condemns? etc.

units.la: Concludatur: discendam igitur in Ecclesia, & puram retinendam esse doctrinam de persona & officio Christi: ut firma sit nobis, quam in resurrectione ejus ostendit scriptura, consolatio.
units.tr: Conclusion: Let it therefore be taught in the Church, and the pure doctrine of the person and office of Christ be retained, so that the consolation which Scripture shows in his resurrection may be firm for us.

units.la: II. Quis modus externus, & internus Resurrectionis.
units.tr: II. What is the external and internal manner of the resurrection.

units.la: Externum modum quid voces : ostende ex Circumstantiis historiæ ab evangelistis descriptę externis, seu extra personam resurgentis positis, & ad ipsum resurgendi actum non pertinentib.
units.tr: Tell what you mean by the external manner: show it from the external circumstances of the history described by the evangelists, which lie outside the person of the one rising and do not pertain to the act of rising itself.

units.la: 1. Mulieres valde mane ad sepulcrum veniunt, & his primum resurrectio Christi demonstratur.
units.tr: 1. The women come to the sepulchre very early in the morning, and to them the resurrection of Christ is first shown.

units.la: Breviter explica causas: 1. quia primæ mortem in mundum invexerunt. Primæ igitur resurrectionis nuncium accipiunt. 2. In morte vehementer doluerunt. Par igitur fuit, ut primò gaude[?]ret[?].
units.tr: Briefly explain the causes: 1. Because they first brought death into the world, they therefore first receive the news of the first resurrection. 2. They grieved greatly at the death; it was fitting therefore that they should first rejoice.

units.la: 3. Christum quærebant, inveniunt.
units.tr: 3. They seek Christ, and they find him.

units.la: Transfertur ad thesin: Zelus mulierum: Sed simul ostendatur earum inconsiderantia, quod sero demum de lapide revolvendo solicitæ sint.
units.tr: This is turned to the thesis: the zeal of the women. But at the same time their lack of consideration should be shown, in that they were anxious only late about rolling away the stone.

units.la: Thesis: Cum non ex fide agitur, multa sæpe imprudenter committitur[?]: & Deo dari, quod non requirit: Sic mulieres ferunt aromata, fidem non afferunt. Sic in Papatu dari Deo missas, ferias, vota, at fidem, & obedientiam non dari.
units.tr: Thesis: When matters are not handled from faith, much is often done imprudently, and what God does not require is given to him: thus the women bring spices but do not bring faith. Thus among the Papacy, masses, holy days and vows are given to God, but faith and obedience are not given.

units.la: II. Terræmotu facto angelus descendit de cœlo, & revolvit lapidem. Dic terræmotus & revolutionis non causam: Etsi probabile in terræmotu Christum resurrexisse: non tamen ideo angelus revolvit lapidem ut egrederetur. Hieroqua ipse voluit, & quae nulli mortalium est cognitu, indicasse, quod factum est.
units.tr: II. An earthquake having occurred, an angel descended from heaven and rolled away the stone. Say that the earthquake is not the cause of the rolling away: although it is probable that Christ rose during the earthquake, yet the angel did not therefore roll away the stone so that he might come out. What he himself willed, and what is known to no mortal, he has indicated; this is what happened.

units.la: Per ἀπολογίαν[?] subjice veram causam Angeli: ut testaretur de resurrectione: cum humani testes deessent: Terramotus: quia in resurrectione invertitur natura rerum, & oportuit hostes terreri.
units.tr: Through an apology, put forward the true cause of the angel: that he might bear witness to the resurrection, since human witnesses were lacking. The earthquake: because in the resurrection the order of nature is overturned, and it was fitting that the enemies should be terrified.

units.la: Obiect. Ergo per saxum penetravit corpore.
units.tr: Objection: Then he passed through the stone with his body.

units.la: Addatur de ingressu per januas clausas, & respondeatur ex Hieronymo ad Pammachium: 'Dic mihi (inquit de Johanne Episcopo Hierosol. transformante corpus Christi post resurrect. in phantasma) acutissime disputator: Quid est ma-jus, & c an creaturam cedere creatori?
units.tr: Add the entry through the closed doors, and answer from Jerome to Pammachius: "Tell me," he says (concerning John, Bishop of Jerusalem, who changed the body of Christ after the resurrection into a phantasm), "most acute disputant: what is greater, or what is it, for a creature to yield to the Creator?"

units.la: III. Mulieres conspectu angeli terrentur: Propter dissidium humanae & angelicae naturae ex peccato ortum:
units.tr: III. The women are terrified at the sight of the angel: on account of the discord between human and angelic nature, which arose from sin.

units.la: IV. Vigiles ut mortui facti sunt: Thesis: Sic tyranni volentes Christum retinere in sepulcro: Evangelium oppressum: Non est consilium contra dominum.
units.tr: IV. The guards became as dead men. Thesis: So tyrants, wishing to hold Christ in the sepulchre, oppress the Gospel: there is no counsel against the Lord.

units.la: V. Angeli solantur mulieres: non custodes: Nunciant & demonstrant resurrectionem: Surrexit, non est hic: praecedet, &c. Ergo non mansit in sepulcro: Nec fuit ubique corpus Christi.
units.tr: V. The angels comfort the women, not the guards: they announce and demonstrate the resurrection: He is risen, he is not here; he goes before, etc. Therefore the body did not remain in the sepulchre, nor was the body of Christ everywhere.

units.la: VI. Colligè[?] brevissimè apparitiones Christi factas Mariae: Petro: duobus Emauntinis: unde-cim discipulis: Thomae, quingentis fratribus in monte: Conversationem cum illis 40. diebus, usque ad ascensionem: Finis fuit: Veritatem re-surrectionis afferere. Claude: Ergo patet testimonio angelorum, mulierum: discipulorum, ipsiusqueredivivi Christi: resurrectionis veritas.
units.tr: VI. Gather very briefly the appearances of Christ made to Mary, to Peter, to the two on the way to Emmaus, to the eleven disciples, to Thomas, and to the five hundred brethren on the mountain; his conversation with them for forty days, up to the ascension. The purpose was to assert the truth of the resurrection. Conclude: therefore the truth of the resurrection is evident from the testimony of the angels, the women, the disciples, and of Christ himself, risen again.

units.la: INTERNO resurrectionis modo dicte notare conditiones ad ipsum resurgendi actum, & resurgentis personam pertinentes: quas non tam sensus, quam fides apprehendat in scriptura.
units.tr: Concerning the internal manner of the resurrection, note the conditions pertaining to the act of rising itself and to the person of the one rising, which faith, rather than the senses, apprehends in Scripture.

units.la: I. Christum vere a mortuis resurrexisse, h.e.: 1. animam vere a corpore per mortem avulsam fuisse. Emisit spiritum. 2. Eandem cum corpore mortuo denuo copulatam: vere illud vivificasse. Quid quaeritis viventem cum mortuis? 3. Vtrunque vere e sepulcro egressum. Surrexit, non est hic, &c.
units.tr: I. That Christ truly rose again from the dead, that is: 1. that his soul was truly torn from his body by death: "he gave up the spirit." 2. That the same soul was again joined to the dead body, and truly quickened it: "Why do you seek the living among the dead?" 3. That both truly came out of the sepulchre: "He is risen, he is not here," etc.

units.la: Π[illegible, ~5 letters] contra ubiquitarios. Ergo nec corpus, nec anima seorsum in divulsione, nec rursus eadem conjuncta simul ubique fuerunt: quia sic neque mori, neque egredi vere e sepulcro Christus potuisset.
units.tr: [Illegible, about five letters] against the ubiquitarians. Therefore neither the body nor the soul, separated in the divorce, nor the same again joined together, were everywhere at once: for in that way Christ could neither truly have died nor truly come out of the sepulchre.

units.la: Obiectio: Surrexit, non est hic: sc. modo naturali: qui modo majestatis erat ubique (Brentius de Majestate dicit, cum penderet corpus in cruce, etiam fuisse Romae: Athenis;) Resp. 1. Vrgeantur verba angeli: Non est hic: 2. Secundum eam distinctionem angeli verba vera fuissent, tantum modo physico: modo majestatis falsa. Sic de omnibus fidei articulis, &c.
units.tr: Objection: "He is risen, he is not here," namely in the natural mode, which in the mode of majesty was everywhere. (Brentius, in his work on the Majesty, says that while the body hung on the cross he was also at Rome and at Athens.) Answer: 1. Let the words of the angel be pressed: "He is not here." 2. According to that distinction, the words of the angel would have been true only in the physical mode, and false in the mode of majesty. So it is with all the articles of faith, etc.

units.la: II. Secundum naturam humanam, quae ciderat: quia quod λόγος assumsit, nunquam deponet. Destruite templum hoc, & reædifi[?]abo illud. Semen tritici moritur & revivescit. Christus sol justitiae occidens moriendo, oriens surgendo: Nostra natura debuit mori: Ergo & suscitari: Per hominem mors, & resurrectio. Ambrosius, & Hieronymus probant ex nota-tione vocis Resurgere.
units.tr: II. According to the human nature, which had fallen: because what the Word assumed, he will never lay aside. "Destroy this temple, and I will raise it up." "A grain of wheat dies and comes to life again." Christ, the sun of righteousness, setting in dying and rising in rising: our nature had to die, therefore also to be raised: "By man, death and resurrection." Ambrose and Jerome prove it from the signification of the word "to rise again."

units.la: III. Resurrexit corpus glorificatum: sed non deificatum, id est, quantum, finitum, visibile, & locale nihilominus manens. Luc.24. Videte, Palpate, &c.
units.tr: III. The body rose glorified, but not deified, that is, still remaining quantitative, finite, visible and local. Luke 24, "See, touch," etc.

units.la: Obiectio: Non fuit agnitus à Maria, discipulis, & evanuit. Ergo, &c. Et respondeatur ex Hieronymo ad Pammachium contra errores Ioh. Hier: Virtus Dei est non umbra, & phantasmatis: ubi Hieronymus has ubiquitarias phantasias de corpore non corpore ex professo refutat.
units.tr: Objection: He was not recognised by Mary or the disciples, and he vanished. Therefore, etc. And the answer is taken from Jerome to Pammachius against the errors of John of Jerusalem: The power of God is not a shadow and a phantasm; where Jerome professedly refutes these ubiquitarian fancies about a body that is not a body.

units.la: IV. Omnipotentia Deitatis non carnis: Ra-tio: Quia caro mortua non fuit simul viva. Proinde nec omnipotens, & tamen omnipotentia propria non aliena Christus resurrexit: Ego reae-dificabo illud. Ego vita & resurrectio: Ego suscitabo eum in novissimo die. Ergo multo magis suam carnem.
units.tr: IV. The omnipotence is of the Deity, not of the flesh. Reason: because dead flesh was not at once living. Therefore Christ, who was not omnipotent, rose nevertheless by his own, not another's, omnipotence: "I will raise it up. I am the resurrection and the life. I will raise him up at the last day." Therefore much more his own flesh.

units.la: Occupatio contra Arianos: Pater suscitavit filium 1. Massam mortuam filii sui: Sed per ipsum filium. Ioh.5. quia quae pater facit, filius facit ὁμοί-ως 1. Pet.3. Christus mortificatus carne, vivificatus spiritu, & Rom.1.
units.tr: Topic against the Arians: the Father raised the Son. 1. He raised the dead mass of his own Son, but through the Son himself: John 5, because whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise [ὁμοίως]. 1 Peter 3: Christ, put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit; and Romans 1.

units.la: Per ἀποδίωξιν attinge tantum σημεῖα[?]: 1. Christum esse verum Deum, cum resurgat propria potentia.
units.tr: By way of exclusion [ἀποδίωξις] he touches only on the signs [σημεῖα]: 1. that Christ is true God, since he rises by his own power.

units.la: 2. Verum hominem, ac fratrem nostrum, idque etiamnum in gloria pontificem esse, qui condolere possit. Hebr.2. & 4. Unde omnis nostra consolatio dependet.
units.tr: 2. That he is a true man and our brother, and that he is still now in glory a high priest who can sympathise with us: Hebrews 2 and 4. On this depends all our consolation.

units.la: Hinc transeatur ad tertiam partem.
units.tr: From here let us pass to the third part.

units.la: III. De fructibus resurrectionis Christi.
units.tr: III. On the fruits of the resurrection of Christ.

units.la: Hanc partem brevius persequere. ostede initio eius necessitatem: ex eo quod scriptura resurrectionem Christi facit basin universae religionis, fidei, consolationis, & salutis nostrae. 1.Cor.15.
units.tr: I shall pursue this part more briefly. Show first its necessity, from the fact that Scripture makes the resurrection of Christ the foundation of the whole religion, faith, comfort and salvation of ours. 1 Cor. 15.

units.la: Deinde expone effecta Resurrectionis. 1. in ipso Christo.
units.tr: Next, set out the effects of the Resurrection. (1) In Christ himself.

units.la: 1. Mutatio status humilitatis in statum glo-riae, quae breviter explicentur ex Phil. 2.
units.tr: (1) The change of his state from humiliation to glory, which is briefly to be explained from Phil. 2.

units.la: 2. Declaratus est filius Dei Rom. 1.
units.tr: (2) He was declared to be the Son of God, Rom. 1.

units.la: 3. Vicit mortem, diabolum, infernum, peccatum, quia cum his moriendo subierat certamen: Ergo mors tua o mors: Absorpta est mors in victoriam. Princeps mundi eiicietur foras. Filius Dei venit destruere opera diaboli
units.tr: (3) He conquered death, the devil, hell and sin, because by dying he had undergone the contest with all of these: "O death, where is thy sting? Death is swallowed up in victory." "The prince of this world shall be cast out." "The Son of God came to destroy the works of the devil."

units.la: 2. In nobis: Huc transfeatur applicatio istorum, quae de Christo dixisti ad nos a fine. Certavit & vicit, non sibi, sed nobis 1.Cor.15. Victoriam dedit nobis.
units.tr: (2) In us. Let the application of those things which you have said of Christ be transferred to us at the end. He fought and conquered, not for himself but for us, 1 Cor. 15. "He has given us the victory."

units.la: Ergo 1. Resurrectio nobis est testimonium devictorum omnium hostium, & justitiae, pacis, & vitae reparatae. Ostende ex dictis scripturae Rom. 6.ver.23. Rom.4.
units.tr: Therefore (1) the resurrection is for us a testimony that all enemies are overcome, and that righteousness, peace and restored life are ours. Show this from the sayings of Scripture, Rom. 6, verse 23; Rom. 4.

units.la: Occupatio: Morimur quidem etiam nos, sed non co modo, & fine quo Christus. Ostendatur diversitas,&c.
units.tr: Objection: We too indeed die, but not in the same way and to the same end as Christ. Let the difference be shown, etc.

units.la: 2. Pignus nostrae resurrectionis. Ostende co-secutionem testimoniis scripturae, & rationibus breviter. Occup. etiam impii resurgent, qui membra Christi non sunt: sed ex alio principio, & fine. Declaratur hoc: Pii in iudicium non venient. Ioh.5.
units.tr: (2) The pledge of our resurrection. Show the consequence from the testimonies of Scripture and briefly from reasons. Objection: The wicked too shall rise, who are not members of Christ, but from a different source and to a different end. This is made clear: the godly shall not come into judgment. John 5.

units.la: 3. Causa & exemplar caelestis vitae, quam suscitati a morte peccati cum ipso nunc incoemus. Rom. 6. Colos. 3. Hinc transeatur ad conclusionem quae 1. repetat nervos orationis. 2. Hortetur ad gratam considerationem tantorum beneficiorum, & gratitudinem. 3. Agat gratias Deo, Serenissimo Electori, Rectori, Auditorio, &c.
units.tr: (3) The cause and pattern of the heavenly life, which we, raised from the death of sin, now begin to live with him. Rom. 6; Col. 3. Hence pass to the conclusion, which (1) shall repeat the sinews of the discourse; (2) shall exhort to a grateful consideration of so great benefits, and to thankfulness; (3) shall give thanks to God, to the most serene Elector, to the Rector, to the audience, etc.

units.la: Dixi.
units.tr: I have spoken.

units.la: Exercitatio VIII.
units.tr: Exercitatio VIII.

units.la: De Missione Spiritus Sancti super Apostolos in Pentecoste Actor. 2.
units.tr: On the Sending of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles at Pentecost, Acts 2.

units.la: EXordium sit liberum, sed breve.
units.tr: The introduction may be free, but it should be brief.

units.la: Transitio ad propositum: Cum historia effusionis Spiritus Sancti sit nota in Ecclesia: te praetermissa narratione tres tantum circumstantias ex ea repetituram.
units.tr: Transition to the matter at hand: since the history of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit is well known in the Church, I will pass over the narrative and repeat from it only three circumstances.

units.la: 1. Quando effusio Spiritus Sancti sit facta. II. Quomodo facta. III. Quare facta.
units.tr: 1. When the outpouring of the Holy Spirit was made. II. How it was made. III. Why it was made.

units.la: I. Quando Spiritus Sanctus sit missus.
units.tr: I. When the Holy Spirit was sent.

units.la: In Pentecoste Act. 2. Cum advenisset, &c. h,e.
units.tr: At Pentecost, Acts 2: When the day had come, etc. That is,

units.la: quinquagesimo die à resurrectione, & undecimo ab ascensione: quod ostendatur ex Levit. 23. 16. Cito ergo Christus implevit promissionem: Si abiero rogabo patrem & mittet: Baptizabimini Spiritu Sancto post dies non multos. Act. 1.
units.tr: on the fiftieth day from the resurrection, and the eleventh from the ascension. This is shown from Leviticus 23:16. Christ therefore quickly fulfilled the promise: If I go away, I will ask the Father, and he will send him; you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days hence. Acts 1.

units.la: Triplex quaestio hic movetur, in quarum solutione remboveatur suspicio curiositatis.
units.tr: Here a threefold question arises, and in answering it the suspicion of curiosity is to be removed.

units.la: 1. Cur non illico à resurrectione miserit.
units.tr: 1. Why did he not send him immediately from the resurrection?

units.la: Resp. [illegible, ~6 letters] causarum.
units.tr: Answer: [illegible, ~6 letters] of causes.

units.la: 1. quia post ascensionem demum promiserat. Postquam abiero mittam, &c.
units.tr: 1. Because he had promised only after the ascension: After I have gone away, I will send, etc.

units.la: 2. quia praesente Christo nondum opus eo habebant.
units.tr: 2. Because while Christ was present they did not yet need him.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia pendebant ab eius praesentia. Matth. 9. Filii thalami non possunt lugere, &c.
units.tr: Reason 1: because they depended on his presence. Matthew 9: The sons of the bridegroom cannot mourn, etc.

units.la: Ratio 2. quia post ascensionem Evangelium ab eis promulgandum fuit: ideo iussi fuerant Hierosolymis exspectare. Act. 1.
units.tr: Reason 2: because after the ascension the Gospel was to be proclaimed by them; therefore they had been ordered to wait in Jerusalem. Acts 1.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia effusio Spiritus Sancti reservata erat glorificationi Messiae in coelis. Ioh. 7. nondum erat Spiritus Sanctus, quia Christus nondum glorificatus. Unde Petrus Act. 2. Exaltatus dextra Dei effudit hoc, &c.
units.tr: Reason 3: because the outpouring of the Holy Spirit was reserved for the glorification of the Messiah in heaven. John 7: The Holy Spirit was not yet, because Christ was not yet glorified. Hence Peter, Acts 2: Exalted at the right hand of God, he has poured out this, etc.

units.la: Addatur ratio ex Chrysostomo: Oportebat in coelo naturam nostram comparere, & intercessione eius perfectam reconciliationem fieri, actum venire Spiritum Sanctum ut purum merumq; gaudiu fieret.
units.tr: A reason from Chrysostom may be added: It was necessary that our nature appear in heaven, and that full reconciliation be made by his intercession, before the Holy Spirit came, so that the joy would be pure and unmixed.

units.la: 11. Cur non illico ab ascensione miserit.
units.tr: II. Why did he not send him immediately at the ascension?

units.la: Resp. 1. ut dilatio esset probatio fidei & obedientiae ipsorum: quia iussi erat manere Hierosolymis donec induerentur virtute ex alto. Luc. 24.
units.tr: Answer 1: so that the delay would be a test of their faith and obedience, since they had been ordered to remain in Jerusalem until they were clothed with power from on high. Luke 24.

units.la: 2. ut exerceretur ipsorum patientia.
units.tr: 2. So that their patience might be exercised.

units.la: 3. Vt excitaretur in eis ardentius desiderium & preces.
units.tr: 3. So that a more ardent desire and prayers might be stirred up in them.

units.la: 4. Vt beneficium expectatum tanto esset gratius & gaudium maius, iuxta Chrysost: Diebus aliquot interiectis differt missionem Spiritus Sancti, ut paulisper afflicti & in necessitate constituti mox solido puroque gaudio fruerentur.
units.tr: 4. So that the benefit awaited would be all the more welcome and the joy greater, according to Chrysostom: After some days had intervened, he deferred the sending of the Holy Spirit, so that those who had been afflicted for a little while and placed in need might presently enjoy solid and pure joy.

units.la: Correctio: Non tamen diu differt, sed mittit undecimo die post in Pentecoste iuxta promissionem. Act.1. Baptizabimini Spiritu Sancto non multis post diebus.
units.tr: Correction: Yet he does not delay for long, but sends him on the eleventh day after, at Pentecost, according to the promise. Acts 1: You shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days hence.

units.la: Thesis: Sic Deus aliquando differt promissiones sed non diu: ut patientiam & fidem exerceat: obedientiam probet: preces excitet: & opportunitas temporis opera eius in nobis conspectiora reddat.
units.tr: Thesis: So God sometimes defers promises, but not for long: in order to exercise patience and faith, to test obedience, to stir up prayers, and so that the fitness of the time makes his works more conspicuous in us.

units.la: III. Aduersus. Sed rursum quaeri: Cur in pen tecoste miserit? Responsio figuretur occupatiuncula: Te saltem indicaturum quid probabile videatur. Ratio: quia causas definire velle fit prohibita curiositas. Act. 1. ver. 7. Non est vestrum nosse,&c.
units.tr: III. Objection. But again it may be asked: Why did he send him at Pentecost? Answer: Let a small conjecture be put forward: I will at least indicate what seems probable. Reason: because to wish to define causes is forbidden curiosity. Acts 1:7: It is not yours to know, etc.

units.la: Subiciantur causae seu coniecturae tres.
units.tr: Let there be put forward three causes, or conjectures.

units.la: I. Vt caelesti miraculo & memorabili beneficio novam Pentecosten Ecclesiae novae sanciret.
units.tr: I. That by a heavenly miracle and a memorable benefit he might consecrate a new Pentecost for the new Church.

units.la: II. Vt miraculi celebritas & vtilitas in festo maior quam alio tempore esset.
units.tr: II. That the celebrity and usefulness of the miracle might be greater at the festival than at another time.

units.la: Ostendatur ex fine festi: quia tunc conveniebatur ad considerationem operum divinorum. Magis ergo omnes ad miraculum attenti futuri erant. Item: quia tunc maxime erat hominum confluxus, ex omni gente sub cœlo. Act.2. Tunc igitur miraculi fama latius spargi & pluribus innotescere potuit.
units.tr: Let it be shown from the purpose of the festival: since at that time people assembled for the consideration of the works of God, all would therefore be more attentive to the miracle. Likewise: because at that time there was the greatest concourse of people from every nation under heaven. Acts 2. Then therefore the report of the miracle could be spread more widely and become known to more people.

units.la: Amplificetur conjectura à fine miraculi seu visibilis missionis, quæ ideo fiebat, ne lateret, sed ut mundo innotesceret & prodesset. Item ab exemplis Christi & Pauli qui sæpe protecti leguntur Hierosol. ad festum, ut in hominum frequentia doctrinæ & miraculorum fructus esset uberior.
units.tr: Let the conjecture be amplified from the end of the miracle, or visible sending, which was made therefore not to remain hidden, but so that it might be known to the world and profit it. Likewise from the examples of Christ and Paul, who are often read to have gone up to Jerusalem for the festival, so that in the throng of people the fruit of the teaching and the miracles might be more abundant.

units.la: III. Vt promulgatio Evangelii per Spiritum Sanctum 50 die à resurrectione Christi veri paschatis facta, promulgationi Legis in Sinai temporis circunstantia responderet.
units.tr: III. That the proclamation of the Gospel through the Holy Spirit, made on the fiftieth day after the resurrection of Christ, the true Passover, might correspond to the circumstance of time in which the Law was proclaimed at Sinai.

units.la: Afferatur authoritate Augustini existimantis hanc anagogen à Christo etiam spectatam fuisse: & ostendatur coniecturæ probabilitas ex 2.Cor.3. Vbi Apostolus modum promulgatæ Legis & Evangelii quasi typum & rem significatam inter se comparare videtur. ver.3.
units.tr: Let it be supported by the authority of Augustine, who thought that this anagogy was also contemplated by Christ; and let the probability of the conjecture be shown from 2 Corinthians 3, where the Apostle seems to compare the manner of the proclaimed Law and Gospel with each other, as type and thing signified. Verse 3.

units.la: Claudatur adversativa[?]: Etsi tutissimum sit credere, Christum tunc misisse: quia tunc placuit: tamen hæc temporis consideratio non fuit nimis curiosa.
units.tr: Let an adversative be inserted [?]: Although it is safest to believe that Christ sent him then, because it pleased him then, yet this consideration of the time is not overly curious.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia etiam à summis Theologis Augustino Chrysostomo, &c. olim suscepta fuit.
units.tr: Reason 1: because it was long ago taken up even by the highest theologians, Augustine, Chrysostom, etc.

units.la: 2. quia ad illustrationem & confirmationem beneficii Ecclesiæ exhibiti pertinet.
units.tr: 2. because it pertains to the illustration and confirmation of the benefit exhibited to the Church.

units.la: Solvantur hic breviter duæ obiectiones:
units.tr: Let two objections be briefly solved here:

units.la: 1. Atqui etiam olim missus fuerat Patribus. 1.Pet.1.&2.Pet.1.
units.tr: 1. Yet he had also been sent to the Fathers before. 1 Peter 1 and 2 Peter 1.

units.la: Resp. 1. Sed non miraculose nec visibiliter, ut Apostolis : 2. Non ita copiose ut tempore Novi Testamenti. 3. Idque propter futuram Christi intercessionem & glorificationem.
units.tr: Answer 1: But not miraculously nor visibly, as to the Apostles; 2. Not so abundantly as in the time of the New Testament; 3. And this on account of Christ's future intercession and glorification.

units.la: II. Datus fuerat Apostolis etiam ante ascensionem per afflatum. Ioh. 20. Accipite Spiritum Sanctum, &c.
units.tr: II. He had been given to the Apostles even before the ascension, by breathing. John 20: Receive the Holy Spirit, etc.

units.la: Resp. Etsi Chrysostomus putet, Christum per enallagen temporis dicere: Accipite, pro accipietis: tamen rectius ab eodem dici eos iam tum accepisse primitus, quibus idoneos reddidit accipiendo postea complementum.
units.tr: Answer. Although Chrysostom thinks that Christ spoke by an enallage of tense, "Receive" for "you will receive," yet it is more correctly said by the same writer that they had already received him at the first, to whom he rendered them fit by giving the fulfilment afterwards on receiving.

units.la: II. Quomodo Spiritus Sanctus sit missus.
units.tr: II. How the Holy Spirit was sent.

units.la: Occup. Cum Spiritus Sanctus sit Deus immensus, quomodo potest mitti, effundi, &c. Resp. Mitti dicitur, non motu locali: Sed 1. Patefactione per novam operationem in animis hominum: Effundi, propter copiosam donorum collationem, phrasi prophetica: loc. 2. Metaphora ab aquis, quibus Spiritus passim comparatur. II. Patefactione externa per Symbola praesentiae Spiritus Sancti in Apostolis, quae qualia fuerint ostendatur:
units.tr: Objection. Since the Holy Spirit is an immeasurable God, how can he be sent, poured out, etc.? Answer. He is said to be sent not by local motion, but (1) by manifestation, through a new operation in the minds of men; he is said to be poured out, by a prophetic figure of speech, because of the abundant bestowal of gifts; (2) by a metaphor from waters, to which the Spirit is everywhere compared. (II) By external manifestation, through the signs of the presence of the Holy Spirit in the Apostles; let it be shown what these were:

units.la: Sonitus repentinus e coelo tanquam ruentis flatus: linguae dissectae seu dispertitae, igneae, &c.
units.tr: A sudden sound from heaven, as of a rushing wind; tongues divided or parted, fiery, etc.

units.la: Probetur haec fuisse symbola praesentis Spiritus Sancti: Repleti sunt omnes Spiritu Sancto. Item ex effectu: Caperunt[?] loqui linguis pro ut Spiritus dabat, &c. Item testimonio Petri: Hoc est illud, quod dictum est per Joelem: Item: Jesus evectus ad dextram, effudit hoc quod videtis, &c.
units.tr: Let it be proved that these were the signs of the present Holy Spirit: They were all filled with the Holy Spirit. Likewise from the effect: They began to speak with tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance, etc. Likewise from the testimony of Peter: This is that which was spoken by Joel; likewise: Jesus, exalted to the right hand, has poured out this which you see, etc.

units.la: Explicetur cur Symbola adhibuerit:
units.tr: Let it be explained why he used the signs:

units.la: I. Vt testaretur suam praesentiam & promissionis implectionem[?] Apostolis & spectatoribus.
units.tr: I. That he might attest to the Apostles and to the onlookers his presence and the fulfilment of the promise.

units.la: II. Vt docueret de natura & effectibus seu beneficiis collatis. Declaretur ex analogia Symbolorum & effectuum Spiritus Sancti.
units.tr: II. That he might teach about the nature and effects, or the benefits conferred. This is shown from the analogy between the signs and the effects of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: I. VENTUS in domum irruens. Sic Ezech.1, Joh. 2o. flatus: quia ut ventus omnia penetrat: impediri nequit: spirat ubi vult; aërem perpurgat: æstum refrigerat. &c. Sic Spiritus Sanctus praedicatione Apostolorum ubique penetravit: frustra obnitente Diabolo, mūdo, Tyrannis, &c. purificat corda electorum per fidem, restinguit æstum pravarum cupiditatum: reficit languentia corda consolatione, &c.
units.tr: I. THE WIND rushing into the house. So in Ezekiel 1 and John 2 the breath: because, like the wind, it penetrates everything; it cannot be hindered; it blows where it wills; it purifies the air; it cools the heat, etc. So the Holy Spirit, by the preaching of the Apostles, has penetrated everywhere, the Devil, the world, tyrants, etc. striving against it in vain; he purifies the hearts of the elect through faith, quenches the heat of wicked desires, and refreshes fainting hearts with consolation, etc.

units.la: II. LINGUÆ DISPERTITÆ: Hoc symbolo testatur apostolis collationem doni linguarum ad propagationem Evangelii in toto orbe.
units.tr: II. DIVIDED TONGUES: By this sign he attests to the Apostles the bestowal of the gift of tongues for the propagation of the Gospel throughout the whole world.

units.la: Ostende doni necessitatem: figuretur administratione[?] sapientiæ & bonitatis Dei convertentis poenam in organum salutis Ecclesiæ: quod explicetur collatione miraculi huius cum origine linguarum. Gen.11.
units.tr: Show the necessity of the gift: let it be pictured in the administration of the wisdom and goodness of God, who turns the punishment into an instrument of salvation for the Church; this is to be explained by comparing this miracle with the origin of languages, Genesis 11.

units.la: III. LINGUÆ IGNEÆ. Hoc symbolo 1. impletur promissio: Baptizabimini Spiritu Sancto & igni.
units.tr: III. FIERY TONGUES. By this sign 1. the promise is fulfilled: You shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

units.la: II. Docetur officium Spiritus Saneti[?]: Ignis lucet: calefacit:comburit stipulam & vstilia: purgat aurum & metalla. Sic Spiritus Sã-ctus illustrat mentes: Doctor veritatis: accen-dit amorem Dei & proximi: Diffusa est charitas Rom. 5. Convincit conscientias: electos convertens & purgans: reprobos inexcusabiles reddens: Arguet mundum,&c.
units.tr: II. The office of the Holy Spirit is taught: fire gives light, warms, burns up stubble and combustible things, purifies gold and metals. So the Holy Spirit illumines minds, is the Teacher of truth, kindles the love of God and of neighbour: The love of God has been poured out (Romans 5). He convicts consciences, converting and purifying the elect, and rendering the reprobate inexcusable: He will convict the world, etc.

units.la: Eliciantur breviter doctrinæ seu μερίσματα[?].
units.tr: Let the doctrines, or divisions, be briefly drawn out.

units.la: 1. Cum sit ventus libere spirans: ergo Tyranni frustra se opponunt Evangelio.
units.tr: 1. Since the wind blows freely, therefore tyrants oppose the Gospel in vain.

units.la: II. Cum sit ignis: Non ergo Evangelium est litera mortua. Sed efficax organum Spiritus Sancti, contra Schwenckfeldium. Rom. 1. Evangelium potentia Dei. Jerem. 6. Faciam verba tua ignem,&c.
units.tr: II. Since it is fire, the Gospel is therefore not a dead letter, but an effective instrument of the Holy Spirit, against Schwenckfeld. Romans 1: the Gospel is the power of God. Jeremiah 5 [6]: I will make your words fire, etc.

units.la: III. Cum his symbolis vere sit collatus Spiritus Sanctus: Deus ergo non ludit Ecclesiam symbolis,&c.
units.tr: III. Since with these signs the Holy Spirit was truly bestowed, God therefore does not mock the Church with signs, etc.

units.la: Explicetur de Baptismo & Cœna: Vere abluit fideles suo sanguine & spiritu: pascit suo corpore & sanguine juxta analogiam & promissionem symbolis annexam.
units.tr: Let it be explained concerning Baptism and the Supper: he truly washes the faithful with his blood and Spirit, and feeds them with his body and blood, according to the analogy and promise attached to the signs.

units.la: Refutetur calumnia de inanibus signis: Item, figmentum de conversione symbolorum, & latentia rerum in illis: per collationem locutionum Sacramentalium cum ista: Spiritus Sanctus sedit super unumquenque: Est ignis: columba: non cōversione:sed significatione Sacramentali.
units.tr: Let the calumny concerning empty signs be refuted; likewise the fiction concerning a conversion of the signs and a hiding of the things within them, by comparing sacramental expressions with this one: the Holy Spirit sat upon each one of them. He is fire; he is a dove: not by conversion, but by sacramental signification.

units.la: Obiectio: Fuit essentialiter præsens in Symbolis: Ergo & corpus Christi substantialiter in pane: propter locutionum Sacramentalium similitudinem. Resp. 1. fall. non causæ. Antecedens est verum non propter locutionem Sacramentalem : Sed propter immensitatem essentiæ Spiritus Sancti, quæ necessario extra & in symbolis fuit: quod de Christi corpore finito, & nunc in cœlis existente dici nequit.
units.tr: Objection: He was essentially present in the signs; therefore also the body of Christ is substantially in the bread, on account of the similarity of the sacramental expressions. Answer. 1. By denying the consequent, not the cause. The antecedent is true, not because of a sacramental expression, but because of the immensity of the essence of the Holy Spirit, which necessarily was both outside and in the signs; which cannot be said of the finite body of Christ, which now exists in heaven.

units.la: 2. Negatione antecedentis. Præsentia.n. ca, q̄ symbolis testatur, non est repletiva illa generalis, sed specialis gratiæ, quase præsentem & efficacem velle esse declarat nō in columba vel igne, Sed in Christo & Apostolis. Sic præsentia corporis Christi non est ubiquitas, sed præsentia gratiæ in fidelibus.
units.tr: 2. By denying the antecedent. For the presence which the signs attest is not that general, filling presence, but a special presence of grace; it declares that he wishes to be present and effective not in the dove or the fire, but in Christ and the Apostles. So the presence of the body of Christ is not ubiquity, but the presence of grace in the faithful.

units.la: 1 v. Ventus & ignis ruunt de cœlo repente, discipulis congregatis, precantibus & meditantibus promissiones, &c. Sic Spiritus Sanctus datur non hominum sed Dei arbitrio: dona communicans, quibus, quando, quatenus vult, &c. servatibus conversationem in Ecclesia, precantibus, discentibus, & meditantibus doctrinam, &c.
units.tr: 1 v. The wind and fire rush suddenly from heaven, the disciples being gathered together, praying and meditating upon the promises, etc. So the Holy Spirit is given at the will not of men but of God, communicating gifts to whom, when and so far as he wills, etc., to those who keep their conduct in the Church, who pray, learn, and meditate upon the doctrine, etc.

units.la: III. Ad quid Spiritus Sanctus sit missus Apostolis.
units.tr: III. What the Holy Spirit was sent to the Apostles for.

units.la: Effunditur Spiritus Sanctus in Apostolos: ut ipsos & Ecclesiam impleat donis. Ioel. 2. Effundam, &c. iuxta promissionem: Ducet vos in omnem veritatem. Manebit vobiscum, &c. Eph. 4. Ascendit ut impleret omnia.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit is poured out upon the Apostles, to fill them and the Church with gifts. Joel 2. I will pour out, etc., according to the promise: He will lead you into all truth. He will remain with you, etc. Eph. 4. He ascended that he might fill all things.

units.la: Explica dona Apostolis collata: & distingue in externa & interna. Externa: facultas intelligendi, loquendi, scri-bendi, dicendi linguas. Cæperunt loqui variis lin-guis, prout Spiritus dabat, &c.
units.tr: Explain the gifts conferred upon the Apostles, and distinguish them into external and internal. External: the faculty of understanding, speaking, writing and declaring tongues. They began to speak with various tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance, etc.

units.la: Astrue veritatem doni. i. quia linguæ diffe-ctæ[?] apparuerunt in Apostolis non in auditori-bus.
units.tr: Establish the truth of the gift, that is: because the tongues appeared in the Apostles, not in the hearers.

units.la: ii. Testimonio advenarum: Audimus lo-quentes nostris linguis.
units.tr: ii. From the testimony of the foreigners: We hear them speaking in our own tongues.

units.la: iii. Donum linguarum diu duravit in Ec-clesia. 1.Cor.12.&13.&14.
units.tr: iii. The gift of tongues lasted a long time in the Church. 1 Cor. 12, 13 and 14.

units.la: iv. Apostoli græcè scripserunt; & linguam non didicerant.
units.tr: iv. The Apostles wrote in Greek, and they had not learned the language.

units.la: Interna: de quibus Lucas: Et impleti sunt Spi-ritu Sancto: sine quibus externa parum profuis-sent, cum etiam hæc hypocritis contigerint. Matthæi 7.
units.tr: Internal: of which Luke speaks: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit; without which the external gifts would have profited little, since these too have fallen to hypocrites. Matt. 7.

units.la: Enumerentur & confirmentur collatione pro-missionis Christi & eventus.
units.tr: These are enumerated and confirmed by comparing the promise of Christ with the outcome.

units.la: i. Perfecta lux & cognitio doctrinæ Christi: Promissio; Ducet vos in omnem: Docebit vos omnia.
units.tr: i. Perfect light and knowledge of the doctrine of Christ. Promise: He will lead you into all; He will teach you all things.

units.la: Eventus: Loquuntur magnalia Dei: concio Petri de miraculi authore Christo: vero Messia, mortuo, suscitato, & ad dextram Dei evecto: Doctrina salutis perfecta deinceps tradita & relicta Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Outcome: They spoke the mighty works of God: Peter's sermon, that Christ was the author of the miracle, the true Messiah, who died, was raised, and was exalted to the right hand of God. The perfect doctrine of salvation was thenceforth delivered and left to the Church.

units.la: ii. Fides in Christum verum Deum & Messiam.
units.tr: ii. Faith in Christ as true God and Messiah.

units.la: Promissio: Ille testabitur de me: Adhuc pau-lum, & mundus non conspiciet me: Vos autem con-spicietis me: & cognoscetis me esse in Patre.
units.tr: Promise: He will bear witness of me. Yet a little while and the world will not see me; but you will see me, and you will know that I am in the Father.

units.la: Eventus: Certò sciat tota domus Israël, hunc esse factum à Deo Dominum & Christum. Hic est ille lapis, lapis, &c. Nec est in alio salus, &c. Huic testimonium dant omnes prophetæ. Credimus nos per gratiam Domini nostri Iesu Christi servatum iri, sicut & illi.
units.tr: Outcome: Let all the house of Israel know assuredly that God has made this Jesus Lord and Christ. This is the stone, the stone, etc. Neither is there salvation in any other, etc. To him all the prophets bear witness. We believe that we shall be saved through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, just as they also are.

units.la: III. Fortitudo in adeundis & tolerandis periculis:
units.tr: III. Courage in facing and enduring dangers:

units.la: Promissio: Et vos testabimini de me: Dabo vo-bis os,cui non poterunt: Arguet mundum de peccato, &c.
units.tr: Promise: And you also will bear witness of me. I will give you a mouth which none of your adversaries will be able to resist. He will convict the world of sin, etc.

units.la: Eventus: παῤῥησία[?] Petri: Notum sit toti domui Israël. Stans autem Petrus: Successus prædicationis in toto mundo: constantia in martyriis, &c.
units.tr: Outcome: Peter's boldness: Let all the house of Israel know. But Peter standing up: the success of preaching throughout the whole world, constancy in martyrdoms, etc.

units.la: IV. Consolatio in adversis & in morte.
units.tr: IV. Comfort in adversity and in death.

units.la: Promissio: Consolatorem alium mittet vobis. Manebit vobiscum, &c. Gaudium vestrum nemo tollet, &c.
units.tr: Promise: He will send you another Comforter. He will remain with you, etc. Your joy no one will take away, etc.

units.la: Eventus: Prius fugiebant: latebant: nunc prodeunt: lætantur in passione propter cōfessionem. Actor.5. Rom.8. Spiritus sublevat infirmitates nostras: Quis nos separabit a dilectione Dei, &c.
units.tr: Outcome: Before they fled and hid themselves; now they come forward and rejoice in suffering for the confession. Acts 5. Rom. 8. The Spirit helps our infirmities. Who shall separate us from the love of God, etc.

units.la: Obiectio: Hæc bona sunt apostolorum: Ergo nihil nos consolantur.
units.tr: Objection: These good things belonged to the Apostles. Therefore they do not console us at all.

units.la: Resp. maxime: quia Apostolis collata sunt propter nos. Probetur ex promissione: Manebit vobiscum in æternum. Ergo non est mortuus cum Apostolis: Et ex historia: Replevit totam domum. Et Eph.4. Dedit dona hominibus: ut impleret omnia: donec omnes, &c.
units.tr: Reply: chiefly because the gifts were conferred upon the Apostles on account of us. This is proved from the promise: He will remain with you forever. Therefore he has not died with the Apostles. And from the history: He filled the whole house. And Eph. 4: He gave gifts to men, that he might fill all things, until all, etc.

units.la: Instantia: Nihil cernitur in Ecclesia simile.
units.tr: Instance: Nothing similar is seen in the Church.

units.la: Respond. distinctione donorum.
units.tr: Reply: by a distinction of the gifts.

units.la: 1. Miraculosis non est opus post confirma-tam satis doctrinam: sed fuerunt hæc propria Ecclesiæ Apostolicæ. 1.Cor.12. Ut convinceretur mu-dus: [?]ibus: Generatio prava signum quærit: Non creditur nisi signa, &c.
units.tr: 1. Miraculous gifts are no longer needed once the doctrine has been sufficiently confirmed, but these were proper to the Apostolic Church. 1 Cor. 12. That the world might be convinced: [?]. An evil generation seeks a sign: it is not believed unless there are signs, etc.

units.la: II. Dona vocationis singulis adhuc dantur necessaria: Cognitio scripturæ, artium, linguarum, facundiæ, sapientiæ, &c. ad ædificationem. 1.Cor.12. Eph. 4. Etsi non miraculose, ut Apostolis: sed per media: laborem & preces.
units.tr: II. Gifts of calling are still given to individuals as needed: knowledge of Scripture, the arts, languages, eloquence, wisdom, etc., for edification. 1 Cor. 12. Eph. 4. Although not miraculously, as to the Apostles, but through means: labour and prayers.

units.la: III. Salutis dona eadem dantur omnibus Electis, quæ Apostolis, pro mensura donationis Christi. Eph.4. Gal. 4. Rom. 8. Qui non habet Spiritum eius, &c. Nemo potest Iesum appellare Dominum, nisi per Spiritum Sanctum. Iuxta oraculum: Effundam super omnem carnem: Et historiam: Replevit totam domum.
units.tr: III. The gifts of salvation are given to all the elect in the same way as to the Apostles, according to the measure of the gift of Christ. Eph. 4. Gal. 4. Rom. 8. Whoever does not have his Spirit, etc. No one can call Jesus Lord, except by the Holy Spirit. In accordance with the oracle: I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh; and the history: He filled the whole house.

units.la: Dantur hæc dona petentibus. Luc.11.
units.tr: These gifts are given to those who ask. Luke 11.

units.la: Accipiuntur fide per Evangelium Gal.3.
units.tr: They are received by faith through the Gospel. Gal. 3.

units.la: Manent & crescunt in fidelibus precatibus[?], & bonam conscientiam cum fide retinere studentibus.
units.tr: They remain and grow in the faithful, who strive to keep a good conscience together with faith.

units.la: Conclusio transferat doctrinam ad usum.
units.tr: Conclusion: let the doctrine be carried over into practice.

units.la: I. Ad confirmationem fidei.
units.tr: I. For the confirmation of faith.

units.la: 1. De Spiritus Sancti subsistentia & vera Deitate contra hæreticos: quia gestat visibiles formas: dat Apostolis eloqui: Sedens super unumquemque, implens totam domum & Apostolos donis. Est Spiritus Iehovæ: Effundam de Spiritu meo.
units.tr: 1. On the subsistence and true Deity of the Holy Spirit, against the heretics: because he bore visible forms; he gave the Apostles to speak; sitting upon each one, filling the whole house and the Apostles with gifts. He is the Spirit of Jehovah: I will pour out my Spirit.

units.la: 2. De Christi vera ascensione in cælum. Misit enim è cælo promissum Spiritum, Act.2.33. Effudit hoc, quod videtis. Ergo est in cælis apud Patrem: Orans pro nobis juxta promissionem: Vbi abiero, mittam: Orabo patrem: & alium paracletum mittet vobis.
units.tr: 2. On the true ascension of Christ into heaven. For he sent the promised Spirit from heaven, Acts 2:33. He has poured out this which you see. Therefore he is in heaven with the Father, interceding for us according to the promise: Where I go, I will send; I will pray the Father, and he will send you another Paraclete.

units.la: Ambrosius serm. 61. Credendum est, Christum revera sedere ad dextram, quia cernimus Spiritum Sanctum missum.
units.tr: Ambrose, sermon 61: It must be believed that Christ truly sits at the right hand, because we see the Holy Spirit sent.

units.la: πόλησις: Ergo coelum nobis patet: quia ibi est, ubi parat nobis locum Ioh. 14. & 17.
units.tr: Intercession: Therefore heaven is open to us, because he is there where he prepares a place for us. John 14 and 17.

units.la: 3. De regno Christi, quod non sit mundanum, sed spirituale, quia coelitus mittit, non auri talenta, sed Spiritus dona coelestes thesauros, &c Spiritum veritatis, consolatorem, qui in Ecclesia manet in aeternum. Hos ergo thesauros in hoc regno quaeramus & magnificiamus.
units.tr: 3. On the kingdom of Christ, that it is not worldly but spiritual, because from heaven he sends not talents of gold but the gifts of the Spirit, heavenly treasures, etc., the Spirit of truth, the Comforter, who remains in the Church forever. Let us therefore seek and magnify these treasures in this kingdom.

units.la: II. Ad gratitudinem.
units.tr: II. On gratitude.

units.la: Cum Spiritum Sanctum promissum dederit Doctorem veritatis, consolatorem Ecclesiae, pro tanto dono grati simus: nosque huic Doctori soli docendos, regendos tradamus:
units.tr: Since the Holy Spirit, promised, has been given as the Teacher of truth and the Comforter of the Church, let us be thankful for so great a gift, and let us hand ourselves over to this Teacher alone, to be taught and governed by him.

units.la: Cum detur petentibus: cum a Deo ardentibus votis petamus, ut nos quoque regat, confirmet, &c.
units.tr: He is given to those who ask; with burning prayers let us ask God that he may also rule and strengthen us, and so on.

units.la: Cum mundus eum non possit accipere: fugiamus mundum & concupiscentias eius, ne hospitem tam pretiosum turbemus Eph. 4.
units.tr: Since the world cannot receive him, let us flee the world and its lusts, lest we disturb so precious a guest (Eph. 4).

units.la: Addatur brevis gratiarum actio: & precatio pro conservatione donorum, doctorum, Ecclesiae, principum & hospitiorum: ut in hac vita ipsum celebremus, & in vita aeterna simus templa Spiritus Sancti cum Patre & Filio.
units.tr: Let there be added a brief thanksgiving and a prayer for the preservation of the gifts, the teachers, the Church, the princes and the hospitality shown to him, so that in this life we may celebrate him, and in eternal life be temples of the Holy Spirit together with the Father and the Son.

units.la: Amen.
units.tr: Amen.

units.la: Exercitatio IX.
units.tr: Exercitatio IX.

units.la: De causis & fructibus effusionis Spiritus Sanctis super Ecclesiam in Pentecoste. Act. 2.
units.tr: On the causes and fruits of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the Church at Pentecost. Acts 2.

units.la: EXordium ab ἀπολογία cur hoc tempore Ecclesia repetat memoriam miraculosæ effusionis Spiritus Sancti: cum beneficia Dei, maxime autem insigniora, quovis tempore sint recolenda.
units.tr: An introduction from apology: why the Church at this time repeats the memory of the miraculous outpouring of the Holy Spirit, since the benefits of God, and especially the more remarkable ones, ought to be recalled at every time.

units.la: Ratio I. quia hoc tempore effusus est Spiritus Sanctus super Apostolos & super omnem carnem iuxta prophetiam Ioelis.
units.tr: Reason I. Because at this time the Holy Spirit was poured out upon the Apostles and upon all flesh, according to the prophecy of Joel.

units.la: Illustretur & confirmetur exemplo Dei, qui olim quoque præcipua sua opera anniversarie circa id tempus, quo evenerant, recoli & celebrari voluit.
units.tr: Let it be illustrated and confirmed by the example of God, who in former times also wished his outstanding works to be recalled and celebrated annually around the same season in which they had occurred.

units.la: Item à minori: Tempus malorum quæ aliquando passi sumus memoriam efficacius reducit. Ergo multo magis bonorum.
units.tr: Likewise from the lesser to the greater: the time of the evils we have at some point suffered brings back the memory more effectively. Therefore much more so that of the good.

units.la: Ratio II. quia magis movent, & hærent in memoria iuventutis & populi, quæ solenniter anniversarie simul ab omnibus & uno consensu fiunt, quam quæ alias ab aliis privatim vel seorsum.
units.tr: Reason II. Because those things which are solemnly observed every year by all together and with one consent move us more and cling more to the memory of the young and of the people than those which are kept by individuals privately or separately.

units.la: Conclusio. Nos igitur cum Ecclesia vota nostra recte coniungimus.
units.tr: Conclusion. Therefore we rightly join our prayers with the Church.

units.la: Amplificatio: explicatio doctrinæ de patefactionibus & de beneficiis Dei & eorum celebratio cum primis ad nostrum ordinem pertinet. I. quia Scholæ Theologicæ sunt φυλακτικὰ doctrinæ cœlestis contra fraudes & depravationes hæretihæreticorum. 2. quia sine diligenti & frequenti meditatione doctrinæ & operum Dei non possumus nos præparare ad alios docendos aliquando & invitandos ad eorum agnitionem & celebrationem.
units.tr: Amplification: the explanation of the doctrine of God's revelations and of his benefits, and the celebration of them, belongs above all to our office. 1. Because theological schools are guardians [φυλακτικὰ] of the heavenly doctrine against the frauds and corruptions of heretics. 2.
