Because without diligent and frequent meditation upon the doctrine and works of God we cannot prepare ourselves to teach others at any time, and to invite them to the knowledge and celebration of these things.

units.la: Locus benevolentiæ: Etsi scio me non esse parem tractandæ rei: spero tamen vos benigne audituros.
units.tr: Appeal for goodwill: although I know that I am not equal to the handling of this matter, I hope nevertheless that you will listen kindly.

units.la: 1. quia non dicam ut vos doceam, sed ut res prius & melius quàm mihi cognitas, vobis in memoriam revocem, & plura atque maiora meditandi occasionem præbeam.
units.tr: 1. Because I do not say this to teach you, but to recall to your memory things known to you earlier and better than to me, and to give you occasion to meditate on more and greater things.

units.la: II. quia non repetam totam doctrinam de persona & de officio Spiritus Sancti, de quibus sæpe ante me alii dixerunt. Sed aliquam partem deligam.
units.tr: II. Because I shall not repeat the whole doctrine of the person and office of the Holy Spirit, of which others have often spoken before me. But I shall choose some part of it.

units.la: Propositio 1. De causis, propter quas missio Spiritus Sancti fuerit necessaria.
units.tr: Proposition 1. Concerning the causes for which the mission of the Holy Spirit was necessary.

units.la: II. De fructibus, quos inde Ecclesia percepit.
units.tr: II. Concerning the fruits which the Church has received from it.

units.la: I. De causis missi Spiritus Sancti.
units.tr: I. On the causes of the sending of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Causæ considerandæ. 1. ut fides miraculi magis confirmetur. 2. ut fructus beneficii plenius intelligantur.
units.tr: Causes to be considered. 1. That the faith in the miracle may be more firmly confirmed. 2. That the fruit of the benefit may be more fully understood.

units.la: Causa 1. Oracula prophetarum de beneficio effusionis Spiritus Sancti super Apostolos & super universam Ecclesiam in regno Christi.
units.tr: Cause 1. The oracles of the prophets concerning the benefit of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles and upon the whole Church in the kingdom of Christ.

units.la: Maior. Hæc oportuit impleri non minus quam alia, de morte, resurrectione, glorificatione & beneficiis Messiae. Ratio: quia sine hoc beneficio alia nihil profuissent: 1. Cor. 12. Nemo potest, &c. Rom. 8. Qui non habet spiritum Christi non est ejus.
units.tr: Major premise. These things had to be fulfilled no less than the others, concerning the death, resurrection, glorification and benefits of the Messiah. Reason: because without this benefit the others would have profited nothing: 1 Cor. 12. No one can, etc. Rom. 8. He who does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his.

units.la: Minor sit recitatio aliquot praecipuorum oraculorum.
units.tr: The minor premise is the recitation of some of the principal oracles.

units.la: 1. Isc.44.3. Effundam aquas, &c. Rejiciatur modeste interpretatio de spiritu universalis gratiae, qua omnia vivificantur: de quo Psal. 104.30. Ostendatur quod sit promissio de Spiritus sancti copiosa missione: 1. ex scopo, quia est oraculum de gratia Novi Testamenti: 2. ex verbo: effundam. 3. quia per aquas etiam alibi Spiritus sanctus purgans & vegetans corda per fidem intelligitur: Isc.55. Ezech.43. Item ex interpretatione Christi. Ioh.7.38. Chrysost. hom. de Spiritu S. col.887. Quid procedit? Spiritus sanctus, sicut a fonte aqua: unde hoc quod Spiritus S. aqua vocetur? &c.
units.tr: 1. Isa. 44.3. I will pour out waters, etc. The interpretation of the universal Spirit of grace, by which all things are quickened, is modestly rejected; concerning which see Ps. 104.30. Let it be shown that this is a promise of the abundant sending of the Holy Spirit: 1. from the purpose, since it is an oracle concerning the grace of the New Testament; 2. from the word I will pour out; 3. because elsewhere the Holy Spirit, cleansing and quickening hearts through faith, is also understood by waters: Isa. 55; Ezek. 43. Likewise from the interpretation of Christ, John 7.38. Chrysostom, homily on the Holy Spirit, col. 887. What follows? The Holy Spirit is, as water from a fountain... whence is it that the Holy Spirit is called water? etc.

units.la: 2. Ezech.36.25. Effundam super vos aquam mũ-dam, quod sit promissio de Spiritu S. effundendo probetur ex scopo & textu & ex 2. Cor.3. quia Spiritus S. facit carnea corda, &c.
units.tr: 2. Ezek. 36.25. I will sprinkle clean water upon you, which is a promise of the pouring out of the Holy Spirit, is proved from the purpose and the text, and from 2 Cor. 3, since the Holy Spirit makes hearts of flesh, etc.

units.la: 3. Ezech.39.29. Non abscondam ultrà faciem meam, quia effudi Spiritum, &c. Hebr. Praeteritum pro futuro quia effunda. Est promissio de effusione Spiritus gratiae. Rejiciatur interpretatio Graecorum de Spiritu furoris ἐξέα θυμόν [?]: quia promittitur instauratio Ecclesiae perpetua, per fidem & resipiscentiam electorum. Sic Chald. Paraph. Non auferam amplius majestatem meam ab eis, quia effundam Spiritum sanctum meum super, &c.
units.tr: 3. Ezek. 39.29. I will not hide my face from them any longer, because I have poured out my Spirit, etc. In Hebrew, the past is used for the future, since I will pour out. It is a promise of the outpouring of the Spirit of grace. The Greek interpretation of a spirit of fury [ἐξέα θυμόν?] is to be rejected, since a perpetual restoration of the Church is promised, through the faith and repentance of the elect. So also the Chaldee paraphrast: I will no longer take away my majesty from them, because I will pour out my holy Spirit upon, etc.

units.la: 4. Ioel.2. Posthac effundam, &c. Laudetur claritas hujus oraculi, testimonio Petri, Act.2.
units.tr: 4. Joel 2. Afterward I will pour out, etc. The brightness of this oracle is to be praised, by the testimony of Peter, Acts 2.

units.la: 5. Zach.12.10. Effundam Spiritum gratia & precum, &c.
units.tr: 5. Zech. 12.10. I will pour out the Spirit of grace and of supplication, etc.

units.la: Applicetur ad missionem miraculosam: ex verbo effusionis, quod scriptura constanter de hoc beneficio usurpat: & ex scopo: quia est oraculum de gratia novi Testamenti.
units.tr: Let it be applied to the miraculous mission: from the word "outpouring," which Scripture constantly uses of this benefit; and from the purpose, since it is an oracle concerning the grace of the New Testament.

units.la: Breviter claudatur causa prima: prius vero additur oraculum Iohannis Baptistae, Matth.3. Ipse vos baptizabit Spiritu sancto & igni.
units.tr: The first cause is briefly concluded; but first is added the oracle of John the Baptist, Matt. 3. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

units.la: Occupatio: Tribuit Christo internas partes Baptismi, videlicet sanctificationem Spiritus. Respond. Sed simul visibilem & miraculosam missionem Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: Objection: He attributes to Christ the inner part of Baptism, namely the sanctification of the Spirit. Answer: But at the same time also the visible and miraculous mission of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia Christus utriusque beneficii author. 2. quia utrunq; in Ecclesia apostolica per baptismum piis conferebatur & obsignabatur. 3. quia visibilis missio erat signum invisibilis, cujus Sacramentum est Baptismus. 4. Respicit ad oracula de effusione. Eadem ergo Metaphora missionem visibilem Spiritus sanctus vocat baptismum, qua Deus vocavit effusionem.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because Christ is the author of both benefits. 2. Because in the apostolic Church both were conferred upon and sealed to the godly through baptism. 3. Because the visible mission was a sign of the invisible, of which Baptism is the sacrament. 4. It looks back to the oracles about the outpouring. Therefore the Holy Spirit, by the same metaphor by which God called the outpouring, calls the visible mission of the Spirit a baptism.

units.la: Causa II. Promissio Christi. Recitentur & applicentur breviter praecipua loca quibus discipulis promisit Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: Cause II. The promise of Christ. Let the principal passages in which he promised the Holy Spirit to the disciples be briefly recited and applied.

units.la: Ioh.14.16. Mittam eum, &c.
units.tr: John 14.16. I will send him, etc.

units.la: Amplificetur ex asseveratione addita: Ego veritatem dico vobis, &c.
units.tr: Let it be amplified by the added assertion: I tell you the truth, etc.

units.la: Act.1.4. Baptizabimini Spiritu sancto ipsius non multis diebus post.
units.tr: Acts 1.4. You shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days after this.

units.la: Causa III. Glorificatio Messiæ exaltati.
units.tr: Cause III. The glorification of the exalted Messiah.

units.la: Glorificato Messia oportuit Spiritum sanctum effundi in Ecclesiam.
units.tr: Once the Messiah was glorified, it was fitting that the Holy Spirit should be poured out upon the Church.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia beneficium tam gloriosum erat magna pars gloriæ Messiæ, qua declaravit se esse evectum ad dextram Dei, & à Deo principem ac seruatorem constitutum: Actor. capite secundo & quinto. Item Ioh. 16. Ille me glorificabit, &c.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because so glorious a benefit was a great part of the glory of the Messiah, by which he showed that he had been raised to the right hand of God and appointed by God as prince and savior: Acts, chapters two and five. Likewise John 16: "He will glorify me," etc.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia Deus reservaverat hoc beneficium glorificationi Messiæ, ut per eum impleret promissiones de effusione Spiritus & gratiæ suæ in novam Ecclesiam: & in regno Christi ubertas illa donorum, tanquam præcipuum decus floreret. Iohan. capite septimo, verf. trig. nono. Nondum erat Spiritus sanctus: quia Christus nondum erat glorificatus.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because God had reserved this benefit for the glorification of the Messiah, so that through him he might fulfil the promises concerning the outpouring of the Spirit and of his grace upon the new Church; and in the kingdom of Christ that abundance of gifts was to flourish as its chief ornament. John, chapter seven, verse thirty-nine: "The Holy Spirit was not yet, because Christ was not yet glorified."

units.la: Breviter refutentur ΠΝΕΥΜΑΤΟΜΑΧΟΙ, qui hinc negant æternitatem Spiritus sancti, cum Christus ipso Ioh. interprete de copiosis donis loquatur, quæ usitata metalepsi causæ pro effectu ipsi Spiritus sanctus appellantur.
units.tr: Briefly, let those be refuted who, the Pneumatomachi, deny from this the eternity of the Holy Spirit, since Christ, in John's own interpretation, is speaking of abundant gifts, which by a customary metalepsis of cause for effect are called the Holy Spirit himself.

units.la: Ratio 3. quia Christus glorificatus intercessione à Patre impetravit. Ioh. 14. Rogabo patrem: Ioh. 16. Vbi abiero.
units.tr: Reason 3. Because the glorified Christ obtained by intercession from the Father. John 14: "I will ask the Father"; John 16: "When I go away."

units.la: Minor: At in Pentecoste illa prima fuit exaltatus & glorificatus Christus. Ergo effundi S. S. oportuit.
units.tr: Minor premise: But on that first Pentecost Christ was exalted and glorified. Therefore it was fitting that the Holy Spirit should be poured out.

units.la: Causa IV. Personæ Spiritus sancti proprietas: quæ
units.tr: Cause IV. The property of the Person of the Holy Spirit, which is:

units.la: quæ est mittià patre per filium ad Ecclesiam in cordacredentium.Gal.4.6. Misit Deus Spiri-tum filii sui, &c.
units.tr: that he is sent from the Father through the Son to the Church, into the hearts of believers. Gal. 4:6: "God sent the Spirit of his Son," etc.

units.la: Explicetur missio non de motu locali aut aliqua mutatione in Deo: sed de patefactione Patris & Filii per immediatam operationem Spiri-tus sanctii in Ecclesia: Fulgent l.2.ad Mon. Missionis nomine opus intelligamus manifestationis indultæ:
units.tr: Let the sending be explained not as local motion or any change in God, but as the manifestation of the Father and the Son through the immediate operation of the Holy Spirit in the Church. Fulgentius, book 2, to Monimus: "By the name of mission let us understand the work of a granted manifestation."

units.la: Occup. Mittitur quidem & Filius, sed non sicut Spiritus sanctus.
units.tr: Objection: Indeed the Son is also sent, but not in the way the Holy Spirit is.

units.la: Ostendatur discrimen: Filius 1. tantum à patre: Gal.4.4. 2. in carnem. 3. ad opus redemptionis. Spiritus sanctus à patre & filio: Ioh.14.26. Pater mittet in nomine meo. Ioh.15.26. Ego mittam à patre: ad opus sanctificationis Ecclesiæ. 1.Pet.1.2. Tit.3.5.
units.tr: Let the difference be shown: the Son is sent (1) only by the Father, Gal. 4:4; (2) into the flesh; (3) for the work of redemption. The Holy Spirit is sent by the Father and the Son, John 14:26: "The Father will send in my name"; John 15:26: "I will send from the Father"; for the work of sanctifying the Church. 1 Pet. 1:2; Titus 3:5.

units.la: Amplific. Non tantum invisibiliter, sed etiam visibiliter oportuit mitti. 1. propter prædictiones & promissiones. 2. propter gloriam Messiæ. 3. propter consolationem Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Amplification. It was fitting that he be sent not only invisibly but also visibly: (1) on account of the predictions and promises; (2) on account of the glory of the Messiah; (3) on account of the consolation of the Church.

units.la: Causa v. Officium Spiritus sancti requirebat, ut copiosè effunderetur in Apostolos & in totam Ecclesiam.
units.tr: Cause V. The office of the Holy Spirit required that he be poured out abundantly upon the Apostles and upon the whole Church.

units.la: Declaratur per partes & distinguatur in publi-cum, quod exercet per ministerium verbi: & privatum, quod apostolis & singulis fidelibus præ-stat.
units.tr: This is declared part by part, and distinguished into the public work, which he exercises through the ministry of the Word, and the private work, which he performs for the apostles and for each of the faithful.

units.la: In utroque urgeatur, quod missionem copio-sam postulaverit.
units.tr: In both, it is to be stressed that he has sought an abundant mission.

units.la: Publicum declaretur præcipue ex duobus locis, Ioh.16. Vbi venerit arguet mundum de peccato: Ubi paucis ostendatur quid, quare & quomodo Spiritus sit facturus: & 2. Corin. 3. ubi apostolus propter praesentiam & efficaciam Spiritus Novum Testamentum varie extollit & veteri ante-ponit: Paucis attinge discrimina[?] tanquam causas dignitatis Evangelii, quae absque effusione Spiritus sancti nulla fuisset.
units.tr: The public work is to be set forth chiefly from two passages: John 16: "When he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin"; where, in a few words, it is shown what, why and how the Spirit is going to act; and 2 Cor. 3, where the apostle, on account of the presence and efficacy of the Spirit, extols the New Testament in various ways and sets it above the old. Touch briefly on the differences as causes of the dignity of the Gospel, which would not have existed without the outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Privatum in Apostolis & omnibus electis debuit efficere.
units.tr: The private work ought to have been effected in the Apostles and in all the elect.

units.la: 1. Ducere in omnem veritatem: Ioh.16. Declaretur sententia: & per occupationem ostendatur an non & Christus in omnem veritatem eos duxerit.
units.tr: 1. To lead into all truth: John 16. The sense is to be declared, and by way of an objection it is to be shown whether Christ did not also lead them into all truth.

units.la: 2. Testari de Christo non tantum per vocem ministerii: sed & in cordibus electorum, quod sit Messias, 1.Ioh.5.6.
units.tr: 2. To bear witness of Christ, not only through the voice of the ministry, but also in the hearts of the elect, that he is the Messiah: 1 John 5:6.

units.la: 3. Esse consolatorem seu advocatū. Ioh.14.&16. Ostende quo discrimine Christus, Ioh.14.16. 1.Ioh.2: & Spiritus sanctus dicatur paracletus. Rom.8.v.16.26.
units.tr: 3. To be the comforter or advocate. John 14 and 16. Show by what difference Christ is called a paraclete, John 14:16; 1 John 2; and the Holy Spirit is called a paraclete too. Rom. 8:16, 26.

units.la: 4. Esse arrham [illegible, ~6 letters] sanctificationis & salutis nostrae. Rom.8.2.Cor.1.Eph.1.&4.
units.tr: 4. To be the earnest [illegible, ~6 letters] of our sanctification and salvation. Rom. 8:2; 2 Cor. 1; Eph. 1 and 4.

units.la: 5. Manere nobiscum in aeternum. Ies. 59.21. Ioh.4.16.
units.tr: 5. To remain with us for ever. Isa. 59:21; John 4:16.

units.la: Conclusio: Ergo oportuit mitti, ut maneret, & electos transformaret in eandem Christi imaginem de gloria in gloriam. 2.Cor.3.
units.tr: Conclusion: therefore he had to be sent, in order that he might remain, and transform the elect into the same image of Christ, from glory to glory. 2 Cor. 3.

units.la: VI. Causa sit [illegible, ~5 letters] superioris: Salus Ecclesiae: quoniam hanc non tantum debuit implere suis donis, sed etiam Deo & Christo capiti unire, & omnium beneficiorum ejus participem facere. 1.Ioh.4. Ex hoc scimus, &c. 1.Cor.6. Scimus templum Dei quia Spiritus, &c. Chrysost. hom. de Spiritu sancto, c. 882. Spiritus sanctus ipse fidem facit quod nos à Deo in filios adoptati simus: ipse corda nostra Christo conglutinat: est copula unionis nostræ cum Christo, &c. Ideo est spiritus gratiæ. Zach.12.quia per fidem inserit Christo, & gratiæ ejus facit participes. Oportuit ergo mitti.
units.tr: VI. The cause is [illegible, ~5 letters] of the preceding: the salvation of the Church, since he was obliged not only to fulfil it with his gifts, but also to unite it to God and to Christ, its head, and to make it a sharer in all his benefits. 1 John 4: "By this we know," etc. 1 Cor. 6: "We know that the temple of God is the Spirit," etc. Chrysostom, homily on the Holy Spirit, c. 882: "The Holy Spirit himself makes us sure that we have been adopted by God as sons; he himself cements our hearts to Christ; he is the bond of our union with Christ," etc. Therefore he is the Spirit of grace. Zech. 12, because through faith he engrafts us into Christ and makes us sharers in his grace. It was therefore fitting that he be sent.

units.la: Objectio: Etiam antea Patres sanctificavit, gubernavit: Psal.51. Spiritum rectum innova: Spiritum sanctum ne auferas à me. Psal.142. Spiritus tuus bonus, &c. Ante Christi ascensionem descendit visibiliter in specie columbæ; & datus est apostolis Christi flatu.
units.tr: Objection: Even before, he sanctified and governed the Fathers. Ps. 51: "Renew a right spirit within me"; "Take not your Holy Spirit from me." Ps. 143: "Your good Spirit, etc." Before Christ's ascension he descended visibly in the form of a dove; and he was given to the apostles by Christ's breath.

units.la: Respon. 1. Missus fuit olim propter futuram illam missionem merito & intercessione Messiæ impetrandam Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Answer 1. He was sent of old on account of that future mission, which was to be obtained for the Church by the merit and intercession of the Messiah.

units.la: 2. Paucioribus & parcius, adeo ut dicatur anteeffusionem tandem factum non fuisse: quod ostende comparare esse intelligendum. Didym. l.1. de Spiritu sancto. Effusionis verbum significat largam & divitem muneris abundantiam. Itaque, cum unus quis alicubi aut duo Spiritus sancti accipiunt, non dicitur, effundam de Spiritu meo, sed tunc quando in universas gentes munus Spir. S. redundaverit.
units.tr: 2. In smaller measure and more sparingly, so much so that it is said that before the outpouring the thing had not really happened at all; which should be shown to be understood by way of comparison. Didymus, book 1, On the Holy Spirit: "The word 'outpouring' signifies a broad and rich abundance of the gift. Therefore, when one or two persons somewhere receive the Holy Spirit, it is not said, 'I will pour out of my Spirit,' but only when the gift of the Holy Spirit has overflowed upon all nations."

units.la: 3. Descendit visibiliter in Baptismo Christi non super omnem carnem: ut postea, sed super Christum: Ioh.1.v.32. cui Deus eum non admetitur, Ioh.3.4.
units.tr: 3. He descended visibly at the baptism of Christ, not upon all flesh, as afterwards, but upon Christ alone: John 1:32; to whom God gave him without measure, John 3:34.

units.la: 4. Apostoli primitias tantum acceperunt: postea complementum in totam Ecclesiam est diffusum.
units.tr: 4. The apostles received only the firstfruits; afterwards the fulness was poured out upon the whole Church.

units.la: II. De fructibus.
units.tr: II. On the fruits.

units.la: Transitio ad fructus, qui partim ex historia partim ex causis deducantur.
units.tr: Transition to the fruits, which are derived partly from history and partly from causes.

units.la: Præmittantur præcipuę circunstantię miracu-li: Ventus ruens replet totam domum.
units.tr: Let the chief circumstances of the miracle be set out first: a rushing wind fills the whole house.

units.la: Linguæ apostolorum dissectę igneę apparent.
units.tr: The tongues of the apostles appear, divided, like fire.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus sedet super unumquemque, dans illis eloqui variis linguis magnifica Dei, &c.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit sits upon each one, giving them to speak in various tongues the magnificent works of God, etc.

units.la: Subjiciantur fructus miraculi.
units.tr: Let the fruits of the miracle be added.

units.la: 1. Primum fructum percipiunt apostoli, accipientes Spiritum sanctum toties promissum (Repleti sunt omnes Spiritu sancto:) & cum eo dona non tantum promissa, sed & alia plura.
units.tr: 1. The apostles first receive the fruit, taking the Holy Spirit so often promised (they were all filled with the Holy Spirit), and with him gifts not only promised but also many others.

units.la: Ostende quæ dona promiserit Christus, & quod ea acceperint.
units.tr: Show what gifts Christ promised, and that they received them.

units.la: 1. Illuminationem: Ducet vos in omnem veritatem: Revelabit vobis omnia, &c.
units.tr: 1. Illumination: "He will lead you into all truth; he will reveal to you all things," etc.

units.la: 2. Παῤῥησίαν docendi & confitendi Christum: Vos testabimini de me: Eritis mihi testes in Ier. usq. ad, &c.
units.tr: 2. Boldness [παῤῥησία] in teaching and confessing Christ: "You will bear witness of me; you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, as far as," etc.

units.la: 3. Consolationem & lætitiam in cruce. Alium consolatorem dabit vobis: Manebit vobiscum: gaudebit cor vestrum.
units.tr: 3. Consolation and joy in the cross: "He will give you another Comforter; he will abide with you; your heart will rejoice."

units.la: 4. Preces & fiduciam exauditionis: Illo die in nomine meo, &c.
units.tr: 4. Prayers and confidence of being heard: "In that day, in my name," etc.

units.la: Hæc Spiritus sanctus eis præstitit in Pentecoste & deinceps. Plene intelligunt doctrinam Christi: Intrepide loquuntur magnifica Dei: Petrus stans cum undecim demonstrat Christum esse Messiam, authorem miraculi, in festo, in concilio & deinceps: gaudentes discedunt è consp-ectu concilii, quod digni essent habiti, qui pro nomine Iesu contumelia afficerentur: quotidie in templo & domi non cessantes docere & Evangelizare Iesum Christum, Act. 5. donec universum orbem adigant in fidem Christi: ardenter precantur contra minas hostium, petentes sibi ut loquantur sermonem μετὰ πάσης; παῤῥη-σίας.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit gave these to them at Pentecost and afterwards. They fully understand the teaching of Christ; they speak fearlessly the magnificent works of God. Peter, standing with the eleven, shows that Christ is the Messiah, the author of the miracle, at the feast, before the council, and afterwards. They depart from the sight of the council rejoicing, because they were held worthy to be treated with contumely for the name of Jesus; daily, in the temple and at home, they do not cease to teach and to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ (Acts 5), until they drive the whole world into the faith of Christ. They pray fervently against the threats of enemies, asking that they may speak the word [with all boldness, μετὰ πάσης παῤῥησίας].

units.la: Transitio ad dona non promissa per Thesin: Beneficentia Dei plerunque superat promissio-nes.
units.tr: Transition to gifts not promised, by way of thesis: God's benefaction usually exceeds his promises.

units.la: Hypoth. sic discipulis præter illa datur donum linguarum.
units.tr: Hypothesis: thus, besides those things, the gift of tongues was given to the disciples.

units.la: Explica quale, & quod verè in Apostolis fuerit.
units.tr: Explain what kind of gift it was, and that it truly existed in the apostles.

units.la: Ampl. certitudo & præstantia doni.
units.tr: Amplification: the certainty and excellence of the gift.

units.la: 1. à Symbolo linguarum igneârum distinctarum[?] in ipsis.
units.tr: 1. From the symbol of the distinct fiery tongues in them.

units.la: 2. ab admiratione auditorum.
units.tr: 2. From the amazement of the hearers.

units.la: 3. ab usu: quod hoc dono Evangelium est prædicatum omnibus linguis, & propagatum ad omnes gentes.
units.tr: 3. From its use: by this gift the gospel was preached in all tongues and spread to all nations.

units.la: Ampl. Etiam ad nos. Irenæus testatur jam suo tempore Ecclesias in Germania fundatas & fidem Apostolicam amplexas fuisse.
units.tr: Amplification: also for us. Irenaeus testifies that already in his time churches had been founded in Germany and had embraced the apostolic faith.

units.la: Occupat. 1. Varietas linguarum olim fuit pœna [illegible, ~7 letters]. Gen.11. Ergo non est donum.
units.tr: Objection: 1. The variety of tongues was once a punishment [illegible]. Gen. 11. Therefore it is not a gift.

units.la: Resp. Confusio linguarum seu divisio unius in multas non intellectas fuit pœna. Sed peritia multarum quæ a nobis & ab aliis intelliguntur est donum præclarum & utile.
units.tr: Answer: The confusion of tongues, that is, the division of one language into many unintelligible ones, was the punishment. But skill in many languages, which are understood by us and by others, is an excellent and useful gift.

units.la: Occup. 2. Donum desiit. Ergo nihil nobis prodest.
units.tr: Objection: 2. The gift has ceased. Therefore it profits us nothing.

units.la: * Resp. 1. Imo quod Christum agnoscimus, & in Ecclesia sumus, dono apostolis semel collato debetur. Ergo prodest.
units.tr: * Answer: 1. Indeed, that we acknowledge Christ and are in the Church is owed to the gift once conferred on the apostles. Therefore it profits us.

units.la: 2. Non donum, sed miraculum desiit, sicut alia, post doctrinam satis propagatam & confir-matam.
units.tr: 2. It is not the gift but the miracle that has ceased, as with other miracles, after the doctrine has been sufficiently spread and confirmed.

units.la: Prob. quia multis Ecclesiæ membris datur peritia variarum linguarum, Hebraicæ, Græcæ, Latinæ ad colligendam & docendam Ecclesiam ne-cessariarū: licet non miraculo, ut apostolis: sed institutione & studio.
units.tr: Proof: because to many members of the Church is given skill in various languages, Hebrew, Greek, Latin, which is necessary for gathering and teaching the Church; although not by miracle, as with the apostles, but by instruction and study.

units.la: Instantia: Etiam extra Ecclesiam est talis peritia linguarum.
units.tr: Instance: Such skill in languages exists also outside the Church.

units.la: Resp. Sed tantum in Ecclesia est donum Spiri-tus S. quia in Ecclesia Spiritus sanctus agnoscitur & invocatur. Extra Ecclesiam est donum Dei ex actione generali, quia sine vera agnitione Dei. Sic intelligentia doctrinæ, facundia, sapientia, &c.
units.tr: Answer: But the gift of the Holy Spirit is only in the Church, because in the Church the Holy Spirit is acknowledged and invoked. Outside the Church it is a gift of God from general operation, not from the true knowledge of God. So too understanding of doctrine, eloquence, wisdom, etc.

units.la: Ostendatur ex 1. Cor. 12. Alii dantur genera lin-guarum per eundem spiritum: Loquitur Apostolus de donis Ecclesiæ non tantum illorum sed o-mnium temporum: quia de necessariis ad colligendam & ædificandam Ecclesiam.
units.tr: Let it be shown from 1 Cor. 12: "To others are given kinds of tongues through the same Spirit." The Apostle speaks of the gifts of the Church, not only of those times but of all times, since they are necessary for gathering and building up the Church.

units.la: Clauditur primus fructus: Non modo eximium fuisse in Apostolis, sed in universam Ec-clesiam redundasse ad salutem.
units.tr: The first fruit is concluded: it was not only remarkable in the apostles, but overflowed into the whole Church for salvation.

units.la: II. Fructus: Confirmatio fidei, quod Spiri-tus S. sit verus Deus cum Patre & Filio, contra hæreticos & infideles.
units.tr: II. Fruit: the confirmation of faith, that the Holy Spirit is true God with the Father and the Son, against heretics and unbelievers.

units.la: Probetur 1. quod sit ὑπόστασις[?] viva, intelligens, agens: non tantum motus vel operatio Dei.
units.tr: Let it be proved, first, that he is a living, intelligent, acting substance [ὑπόστασις], not merely a motion or operation of God.

units.la: 1. quia sustinet corpoream speciem ignis: itē columbæ.
units.tr: 1. Because he took the bodily form of fire, and likewise of a dove.

units.la: 2. quia dabat apostolis eloqui, &c. Item: est {*}effector χαρισμάτων[?] in Ecclesia, distribuens singulis prout vult. 1. Cor. 12.
units.tr: 2. Because he gave the apostles to speak, etc. Likewise: he is the effector of the gifts [χαρίσματα] in the Church, distributing to each one as he wills. 1 Cor. 12.

units.la: Occup. Etsi est donum: non tamen ideo non per se subsistens.
units.tr: Objection: Although he is a gift, he is nonetheless not for that reason not subsisting in himself.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia est donum & donans seu esse-ctor donorum, 1. Cor. 12.
units.tr: Reason: 1. Because he is a gift and the giver or effector of gifts, 1 Cor. 12.

units.la: 2. per instantiam. Etiam Filius est donum. Joh. 4.
units.tr: 2. By instance: the Son too is a gift. John 4.

units.la: Prob. 1 1. quod non creatura vel spiritus creatus, sed Deus: primum leviter ex historiæ circunstantiis: quia efficit Dei propria in apostolis: notitiam linguarum, doctrinæ & sapientiæ cœlestis: regens linguas, corda, &c. Item sedet super unumquemque, quod esse argumentum immensitatis Spiritus sancti: ostendatur ex Didymo, cujus argumenta pro Deitate Spiritus sancti hac occasione subjiciantur.
units.tr: Proof: 1. That he is not a creature or created spirit, but God. This is shown lightly from the circumstances of the history: because he effects in the apostles what belongs to God: knowledge of tongues, of doctrine and heavenly wisdom, governing tongues and hearts, etc. Likewise "he sat upon each one," which is an argument of the immensity of the Holy Spirit. It is shown from Didymus, whose arguments for the Deity of the Holy Spirit are set out on this occasion.

units.la: 1. Si Spiritus sanctus unus de creaturis esset, saltem circumscriptam haberet substantiam, sicut universa quæ facta sunt. Nam etsi non circumscribantur loco & finibus invisibiles creaturæ, tamen proprietate substantiæ finiuntur. Spiritus sanctus non habet circumscriptam substantiam: quia simul est in cœlo & in terra, & in pluribus sanctis. Prob. Effusus super omnem mnem[?] carnem, manet nihilominus in Deo: non discedens à Patre & Filio: Sedit super unumquemque apostolorum indivisus, licet divisum symbolum appareret: testificans, se esse in iis præsentem, & dona illa efficere, non tunc modo, cum Ierosolymæ essent congregati, sed & deinceps cum alii in alias essent nationes dispersi & longissimis spaciis in Asia, in Scythia, in India dis-juncti.
units.tr: 1. If the Holy Spirit were one of the creatures, he would at least have a circumscribed substance, like all things that have been made. For although invisible creatures are not circumscribed by place and limits, yet they are bounded by the property of their substance. The Holy Spirit does not have a circumscribed substance, because he is at once in heaven and on earth, and in many saints. Proof: poured out upon every flesh, he nevertheless remains in God, not departing from the Father and the Son. He sat upon each of the apostles undivided, although a divided symbol appeared, testifying that he is present in them and effects those gifts, not only then, when they were gathered at Jerusalem, but afterwards also, when others were dispersed into different nations and separated by very long distances: in Asia, in Scythia, in India.

units.la: II. Solius Dei est replere omnia substantia sua. Spiritus sanctus per naturam sanctifican-tem & implentem bonus universa bonus ipse subsistit: Nam de Apostolis dicitur: Repleti sunt omnes Spiritu sancto: ad omnes fideles, Ephes. 4. Implemini Spiritu sancto. De Stephano: cum esset plenus Spiritu sancto, &c. De Paulo: Actor.13. Saulus autem qui & Paulus repletus Spiritu sancto, &c. Nemo autem dicitur plenus creatura; Nec angeli præsentia sive alicujus alterius naturæ quæ facta est, implet mentem atque sensum: quia & ipsa aliunde completur. Quomodo enim ex plenitudine quis accipiens Salvatoris plenus efficitur sapientia & virtute & justitia & sermone Dei: Sic qui Spiritu sancto plenus est, statim universis donationibus Dei repletur, sapientia, scientia, fide cæterisque virtutibus. Qui igitur implet universas creaturas quæ tamen possunt virtutem & sapientiam capere, non est ex his quæ ipse complet. Ex quo concluditur Spiritum sanctum omnia replentem alterius esse sub-stantiæ. quam sunt omnes creaturæ.
units.tr: II. It belongs to God alone to fill all things with his substance. The Holy Spirit, by his sanctifying and filling nature, good, subsists as good over all things. For of the apostles it is said: "They were all filled with the Holy Spirit"; to all the faithful, Eph. 4: "Be filled with the Holy Spirit." Of Stephen: "when he was full of the Holy Spirit," etc. Of Paul, Acts 13: "But Saul, who is also Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit," etc. But no one is said to be full by a creature; nor does the presence of an angel or of any other nature that has been made fill the mind and sense, because it too is filled from elsewhere. For just as one who receives from the fullness of the Savior is made full of wisdom and virtue and justice and the word of God, so he who is full of the Holy Spirit is at once filled with all the gifts of God: wisdom, knowledge, faith and the other virtues. He therefore who fills all creatures, which nevertheless can receive virtue and wisdom, is not among those things which he himself fills. From this it is concluded that the Holy Spirit, who fills all things, is of a different substance from all creatures.

units.la: III. Ipsum quoque effusionis nomen increatam Spiritus sancti substantiam probat. Neque enim Deus, cum mittit angelum aut aliam creaturam, dicit: Effundam de angelo meo, aut principatu aut throno: In solis quippe his, quae ab aliis participantur, hic sermo consentit. De Spiritu autem sancto dicit. Effundam de Spiritu meo. Nomine autem effusionis largam attributionem Spiritus, & divitem muneris abundantiam significat: teste apostolo, Tit. 3. Quem effudit super nos abundanter. Neque enim cum unus aut duo Spiritum S. accipiunt, effusus dicitur Spiritus sanctus, sed tunc quando in universas gentes munus Spiritus S. redundaverit. Unde consequitur capabilem Spiritus sancti esse substantiā: & ex hoc increatā. Capabile vero substantiam vocat Didymus interprete Hieronymo quae capitur a pluribus, & eis sui consortium tribuit: capacem vero eā quae communicatione substantiae alterius implctur [?], & capiens aliud ipsa non capitur ab a-lio.
units.tr: III. The very name of "effusion" also proves the uncreated substance of the Holy Spirit. For God, when he sends an angel or another creature, does not say: "I will pour out of my angel, or of my principality or throne." Indeed, this language agrees only with those things which are shared by others. But of the Holy Spirit he says: "I will pour out of my Spirit" (Joel 2). By the name of effusion is signified a broad distribution of the Spirit and an abundance of rich gift, as the apostle witnesses, Titus 3: "which he poured out upon us abundantly." For when one or two receive the Holy Spirit, the Holy Spirit is not said to be poured out, but then when the gift of the Holy Spirit has overflowed into all nations. Whence it follows that the substance of the Holy Spirit is capable [of being received], and from this uncreated. Didymus, in Jerome's translation, calls "capable" a substance that is received by many and grants to them its fellowship; but "capacious" that which is filled by communication of another substance, and itself receives another, yet is not received by another.

units.la: I v. Si creatura est Spiritus S. vel corporea erit vel incorporalis. Non est corpus, quia a sensu & mente capitur, & sermonis, scientiae & sapientiae est effector. Nec incorporalis, quia nec anima nec angelus est, non anima, quia non suscipit sanctificationem & virtutes alias ut anima, sed effi-cit. Nec angelus, 1. quia non est Spiritus administratorius, ut sunt omnes angeli, Heb. 1. 2. An-geli non sunt ex propria substantia sancti, sed ex participatione Spiritus sancti, & inhabitatione Filii Dei, qui est sanctitas & communicatio Patris. At Spiritus sanctus natura proprietate est sanctus angelos & homines sanctificans.
units.tr: I. If the Holy Spirit is a creature, it will be either corporeal or incorporeal. It is not a body, because it is grasped by the senses and the mind, and it is the author of speech, knowledge and wisdom. Nor is it incorporeal, because it is neither a soul nor an angel: not a soul, because it does not receive sanctification and other virtues as a soul does, but effects them. Nor an angel, first, because it is not a ministering spirit, as all angels are (Heb. 1.2). Angels are not holy from their own substance, but through participation in the Holy Spirit and the indwelling of the Son of God, who is the holiness and communication of the Father. But the Holy Spirit is holy by its own nature, sanctifying angels and men.

units.la: His itaque argumentis alterius substantię ab omnibus creaturis Spiritus sanctus ostenditur. Si autem alterius est naturæ à creaturis, & in propria subsistit essentia, increatus & ineffectus proindeque Deus esse demonstratur.
units.tr: By these arguments, therefore, the Holy Spirit is shown to be of a substance different from all creatures. And if it is of a nature different from creatures, and subsists in its own essence, it is demonstrated to be uncreated and unmade, and therefore God.

units.la: Obiectio. Omnia per verbum facta sunt. Ergo etiam Spiritus S.
units.tr: Objection. All things were made through the Word. Therefore the Holy Spirit also.

units.la: Resp. Fall. divisionis: additur enim quæ facta sunt. At Spiritus S. non est ex omnibus quæ facta sunt, sed aliud extra omnia & ante omnia. Gen. 1. Spiritus incubabat aquis. Conditor cœli & terræ. Act. 4. Deus. Act. 5.
units.tr: Answer. A fallacy of division: for the words "which were made" are added. But the Holy Spirit is not one of all the things that were made, but something other than all things and before all things. (Gen. 1.) "The Spirit brooded over the waters." (Acts 4.) "Maker of heaven and earth." (Acts 5.) "God."

units.la: Prob. III. Quod sit ὁμοούσιον Patri & Filio.
units.tr: Proof. III. That it is homoousios with the Father and the Son.

units.la: 1. quia est Patris & Filii Spiritus: Effundam de Spiritu meo, hoc apud Ioelem dicit Iehova: Petrus de Christo interpretatur. Effudit quod videtis. Ergo est Patri & Filio coessentialis, quia in Deo non est accidens: & coæternus, quia Pater & Filius nunquam fuerunt sine suo spiritu.
units.tr: 1. Because it is the Spirit of the Father and of the Son: "I will pour out my Spirit" (Joel); Jehovah says this in Joel, and Peter interprets it of Christ: "He has poured out what you see" (Acts 2). Therefore it is coessential with the Father and the Son, because there is no accident in God; and coeternal, because the Father and the Son were never without their own Spirit.

units.la: πνεῦμα. Ab utroq; igitur procedit, i.e, cōmu-nicatam habet essentiam divinam ab utroq; sicut & ab utroq; mittitur. Qui à patre procedit. Pater mittet eum in nomine meo. Ego mittam eum à Patre.
units.tr: πνεῦμα [pneuma]. Therefore it proceeds from both, that is, it has the divine essence communicated from both, just as it is sent by both. "Who proceeds from the Father" (John 15); "The Father will send him in my name" (John 14); "I will send him from the Father" (John 15).

units.la: Breviter rejiciatur error Græcorum recentiorum, quod à solo Patre procedat. 1. quia sic non esset Spiritus Filii. 2. non posset mitti à Filio: 3. nō esset ὁμοούσιον utriq;: & sic error Græcorum est Samosatenianismus & Macedonianismus. 4. veteriores Græci contra sentiunt cum Scriptura.
units.tr: The error of the more recent Greeks, that it proceeds from the Father alone, is briefly refuted. First, because then it would not be the Spirit of the Son. Second, it could not be sent by the Son. Third, it would not be homoousios with both; and so the error of the Greeks is Samosatenianism and Macedonianism. Fourth, the older Greeks think otherwise, in agreement with Scripture.

units.la: Cyrillus de recta fide ad Theod.col.275. Athanasius in symb.fidei post medium libri. Didymus lib.2.
units.tr: Cyril, On the Right Faith, to Theodosius, col. 275. Athanasius, in the Creed, after the middle of the book. Didymus, book 2.

units.la: lib.2.de Spiritu sancto. Epiphan. hær. 69. contra Ariomanitas.& hæres 48.cont.Montanist.
units.tr: Book 2, On the Holy Spirit. Epiphanius, heresy 69, against the Ariomanites; and heresy 48, against the Montanists.

units.la: II. Est Jehova : quia quæ Jehovæ tribuun-tur in Scriptura : etiam Spiritui sancto conveniunt. Jef. 6. Jehova dixit: vade & dic populo huic,&c: Actor.28.Bene Spiritus sanctus locutus est per,&c.Psal.95.Heb.3. Sicut dicit Spiritus sanctus. Hodie si, &c. At Jehova gloriam suam alteri non dat.Jef.4.
units.tr: II. It is Jehovah: because what is attributed to Jehovah in Scripture also belongs to the Holy Spirit. (Isa. 6.) "Jehovah said: go and say to this people," etc. (Acts 28.) "Well has the Holy Spirit spoken through," etc. (Ps. 95; Heb. 3.) "As the Holy Spirit says: Today, if," etc. But Jehovah does not give his glory to another (Isa. 42).

units.la: III. Nec non & illud considerandum, quod in corde & sensu habitare non potest creatura, nisi Deus & sermo ejus in Spiritu sancto. De patre. Levit.26. Inhabitabo in illis. De Filio. Eph.3. De Spiritu S.1.Cor.6.&2.Cor.6.
units.tr: III. Nor is this also to be considered: that a creature cannot dwell in the heart and mind unless God and his Word dwell in it by the Holy Spirit. Of the Father: "I will dwell in them" (Lev. 26). Of the Son: (Eph. 3). Of the Holy Spirit: (1 Cor. 6; 2 Cor. 6).

units.la: IV. Una est fides in P.F.& Spiritu S. Eph.4.5.
units.tr: IV. There is one faith in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit (Eph. 4.5).

units.la: V. Unus & perfectus Baptismus est in nomine P.F.& S.S.Matt.28.Eph.4.
units.tr: V. There is one and perfect baptism in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit (Matt. 28; Eph. 4).

units.la: VI. Est verus Deus, qui non est nisi unus: Act.5. Non hominibus sed Deo mentitus es:1.Cor.6. Estis templum Dei: Act.4. Creator cœli & terræ: Hæretici inficiantes hoc, quocunque se fuco tegant, in alterutram ex his blasphemiis manifestissimis necessario incidunt, ut vel Deos & creatores plures constituant, vel à mundi creatione, veraque divinitate & æqualitate cum Patre & Filio Spir.S. removeant.
units.tr: VI. There is the true God, who is not other than one: (Acts 5) "You have lied not to men but to God"; (1 Cor. 6) "You are the temple of God"; (Acts 4) "Creator of heaven and earth." Heretics who deny this, however they cover it with whatever paint, necessarily fall into one of these most manifest blasphemies: either they set up several gods and creators, or they remove from the creation of the world, and from the true divinity and equality with the Father and the Son, the Holy Spirit.

units.la: VII[?]. Fructus: Spiritus S. effusus est super omnem carnem: Ergo & super nos. Breviter per-stringantur beneficia Sp.S.
units.tr: VII. Fruits: The Holy Spirit has been poured out upon all flesh; therefore also upon us. The benefits of the Holy Spirit are briefly set out.

units.la: I. Omnes prophetant, visiones, somnia videt: quibus phrasibus ostende illustrem Dei cognitionem significari, sub tropis veteri testamento convenientibus.
units.tr: I. All prophesy, see visions and dream dreams: by which phrases a clear knowledge of God is signified, under tropes suited to the Old Testament.

units.la: 2. Regeneratnos,quia est aqua: ignis expur-gans sordes. Tit.3.Salvosnosfecit,&c.
units.tr: 2. He regenerates us, because he is water, and fire that purges away filth (Titus 3): "He saved us," etc.

units.la: 3. Vnit cum Christo:quia est Spiritus Christi & habitat in nobis,Gal.4.1.Ioh.3.
units.tr: 3. He unites us with Christ, because he is the Spirit of Christ and dwells in us (Gal. 4; John 3).

units.la: 4. Consolatur & confirmat nos de salute. Roman.8. Contestatur Spiritui nostro: Ephef.1[?]. est arrhabo hæreditatis. Manet nobiscum in æternū secundum promissionem.
units.tr: 4. He comforts and confirms us concerning salvation (Rom. 8): "He bears witness to our spirit" (Eph. 1): "is the pledge of the inheritance"; "He remains with us forever according to the promise."

units.la: IV. Fructus: Consolatio: quod Christus ve-rein cœlis sit, intercedat: paret nobis locum, sedens ad dextram Dei defendat Ecclesiam: rediturus tandem & nos glorificaturus.
units.tr: IV. Fruit: Consolation: that Christ is truly in heaven, interceding, preparing a place for us, sitting at the right hand of God, defending the Church, and about to return and at last glorify us as well.

units.la: Ratio: quia promisit è cœlo se missurum Spiritum: Vocabo[?] patrem. Parabo vobis locum: non relinquam vos orphanos: Assumam[?] vos ad me: Vt videant gloriam meam. Ambros. ser. 61. de festo Pentecost. Credendum est Christum in Dei dextera considere, quia cernimus Spiritum S. sicut promisit Dominus in discipulis excitare. Aug. Tom.10.de tèp.ser.183. Credimus ad Patrem per-venisse filiū cum videmus ad apostolos pervenisse pa-racletum. Chrysost de S.S. Impletio oraculi loclus est fidelis confirmatio (Christi in cœlos assumti, ut absque hæsitatione credamus illum sedere in cœlis a dextris ob-lata nostra natura Patri, & in antidotum ac remu-neratione Sp.S. nobis demisso.
units.tr: Reason: because he promised to send the Spirit from heaven: "I will call the Father; I will prepare a place for you; I will not leave you orphans; I will take you to myself; that they may see my glory." Ambrose, sermon 61, on the feast of Pentecost: "We must believe that Christ sits at the right hand of God, because we see the Holy Spirit stirred up in the disciples, as the Lord promised." Augustine, vol. 10, On the Time, sermon 183: "We believe that the Son has reached the Father, when we see the Paraclete has reached the apostles." Chrysostom, On the Holy Spirit: "The fulfilment of the oracle is the faithful confirmation of Christ taken up into heaven, so that without hesitation we believe that our nature, offered to the Father, sits in heaven at his right hand, and that the Holy Spirit has been sent down to us as an antidote and reward."

units.la: Amplif. ab incommodis contrariis: Nisi cer-ti simus Christum in cœlis esse: nescimus ubi sit quærendus & inuocandus Christus: thesaurus noster. Vnde sit expectandus: ubi nostra sit su-tura mansio post hanc vitam,&c. Rejiciatur breviter error ubiquitariorum, de allegorica ascensione & disparitione, quo con-solatio & spes nostra convellitur.
units.tr: Amplification: from the contrary inconveniences: unless we are certain that Christ is in heaven, we do not know where Christ is to be sought and invoked, our treasure; whence he is to be expected; where our dwelling is to be after this life, etc. The error of the ubiquitarians is briefly refuted, concerning an allegorical ascension and disappearance, by which our consolation and hope are overthrown.

units.la: Conclusio: Hæc de causis & fructibus effusi Spiritus sancti in Pentecoste nunc repetenda duxi.
units.tr: Conclusion: I have thought it right to repeat these matters concerning the causes and fruits of the Holy Spirit poured out at Pentecost.

units.la: Hortatio ut sedulo meditemur, & grata mente amplectamur tanta beneficia: non tantum reti-neamus fidem veram de Spiritu sancto: propter hæreticos qui passim veteres blasphemias reno-vant: Sed etiam perpetua resipiscentia, modestia, reverentia superiorum, sedulitate, diligentia, & ardentibus votis dona ejus nobis collata conser-vare & augere studeamus: nec ingratitudine ef-fundamus: aut contristemus Spiritum sanctum, quo sumus obsignati. Gratias itaque agimus, &c.
units.tr: Exhortation: that we diligently meditate on, and embrace with a grateful mind, such great benefits; not only that we hold fast the true faith concerning the Holy Spirit, against the heretics who everywhere renew the old blasphemies; but also that, by perpetual repentance, modesty, reverence toward our superiors, earnestness, diligence and ardent prayers, we strive to preserve and increase the gifts conferred on us by him, and not pour them out in ingratitude, or grieve the Holy Spirit, by whom we are sealed. Therefore we give thanks, etc.

units.la: Exercitatio X. De vetere & nova Pentecoste; & de beneficiis Ecclesiæ in utraq; collatis.
units.tr: Exercitatio X. On the Old and the New Pentecost; and on the benefits conferred on the Church in both.

units.la: EXordium: Oratores in exordiis solere uti purgatione vel captatione benevolentiæ: qua vel ingenio suo, vel causæ, vel auditoribus diffi-dunt. Te neutrum nunc operose facturum non quod confidas ingenio, vel valeas dicendi aliqua vi aut usu: Ab utroque enim te imparatum: Sed. 1. quia obtemperes iis quibus debeas. 2. quia sciant hæc esse exercitia Tyronum, in quibus non solet requiri τ' ἀνεχέσ[?]εις[?], eaque se a-mare frequentia sua jam testentur. 3. quia antehac alios patienter audiverint.
units.tr: EXORDIUM: Orators are accustomed in their openings to make use of an apology or a winning of goodwill, by which they distrust either their own talent, their cause, or their hearers. That you will not now do either laboriously is not because you trust your ability, or because you have some power or practice in speaking; for you are unprepared in both respects. Rather: (1) because you should obey those to whom you owe obedience; (2) because they know these to be exercises of beginners, in which the forbearance (τ' ἀνεχέσ[?]εις) is not usually required, and by their numerous attendance they already show that they love them; (3) because previously they have listened patiently to others.

units.la: 4. quia argumentum sua dignitate sit illis non ingratum futurum: quippe conveniens tempori huic: quo tota Ecclesia celebrat solennitatem Pentecostes, in qua olim Deus legem promulgavit: tandem Spiritum Sanctum super Apostolos visibiliter effudit, unde Spiritus Sancti χαρίσματα[?] tanquam uberrima flumina viventis aquae in totam Ecclesiam dimanarunt.
units.tr: (4) Because the subject, by its own dignity, will not be unwelcome to them; for it is fitting for this time, when the whole Church celebrates the solemnity of Pentecost, on which God once promulgated the law, and at last poured out the Holy Spirit visibly upon the Apostles, whence the gifts (χαρίσματα) of the Holy Spirit flowed out into the whole Church like the most abundant rivers of living water.

units.la: Horum beneficiorum repetitionem debere nobis esse gratam, ut lætitiā & gratitudinem nostram pro iis cum tota Ecclesia publice declaremus. Item : quia maxime decet nostrum ordinem, qui aliquando enarrandis & celebrandis Dei beneficiis voce & exemplo nostro aliis praire[?] debemus.
units.tr: That the repetition of these benefits ought to be pleasing to us, so that we may publicly declare our joy and gratitude for them together with the whole Church. Likewise: because it especially befits our order, which must at some time go before others by voice and example in recounting and celebrating the benefits of God.

units.la: Transitio : Doctrinam de Spiritus Sancti persona, Divinitate & ὁμοουσίᾳ[?] cum æterno Patre & Filio te nunc non persecuturum. 1. quia sæpe de ea ab aliis sit dictum. 2. quia scias ipsorum mentibus & cordibus probe cognitam & confirmatam esse ex verbo Dei contra hæreticorum blasphemias. 3. quia diebus hisce festis in Ecclesia sint audituri.
units.tr: Transition: That you will not now pursue the doctrine of the person of the Holy Spirit, his Divinity and consubstantiality (ὁμοουσία) with the eternal Father and Son. (1) because it has often been spoken of by others; (2) because you know it to be well understood and confirmed in their minds and hearts from the Word of God, against the blasphemies of heretics; (3) because on these festal days they are going to hear it in the Church.

units.la: Propositio. Sed delegisse te hæc duo.
units.tr: Proposition. But you have chosen these two things:

units.la: 1. De Pentecoste veteri & nova.
units.tr: 1. Concerning the old and the new Pentecost.

units.la: II. De beneficiis Ecclesiæ in utraque à Deo exhibitis.
units.tr: II. Concerning the benefits given by God to the Church in both.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Præmittatur quæstionis ratio. 1. quia Lucas dicit, completo die Pentecostes effusum esse Spiritum Sanctum super Apostolos, de Pentecoste Iudæorum loquens. 2. quia çum Iudæorum festa sint abrogata, nihilominus Ecclesia Christiana celebrat Pentecosten.
units.tr: The reason of the question is set out first. (1) because Luke says that, when the day of Pentecost was complete, the Holy Spirit was poured out upon the Apostles, speaking of the Pentecost of the Jews; (2) because, although the festivals of the Jews have been abrogated, the Christian Church nevertheless celebrates Pentecost.

units.la: Ergo tenendum qualis vetus & nova Pentecoste.
units.tr: Therefore it must be held what the old and the new Pentecost were.

units.la: De veteri Pentecoste.
units.tr: On the Old Pentecost.

units.la: Erat unum ex tribus festis Iud. anniversariis. Petatur descriptio ex Levit.23 15. Num.28.v.26. Deut.16.9. & ordine exponatur.
units.tr: It was one of the three annual feasts of the Jews. Let the description be sought from Lev. 23:15, Num. 28:26, Deut. 16:9, and let it be explained in order.

units.la: 1. Quando celebrata. Resp. Septem septimanis expletis post initium messis triticæ Exod.34. ver.22. Deut.16.9. seu post oblatas primitias frugum. Num.28.26. seu post Pascha. Levit.23.15. Numerabis à postero die Sabbathi septem septimanas, seu quinquaginta dies. Inde dicta est [illegible, ~6 letters] festum hebdomadarum: & [illegible, ~8 letters] quinquagesima.
units.tr: 1. When it was celebrated. Answer. Seven weeks being completed after the beginning of the wheat harvest, Exod. 34:22, Deut. 16:9; or after the first fruits were offered, Num. 28:26; or after the Passover, Lev. 23:15: "You shall count from the morrow after the Sabbath seven weeks, or fifty days." Hence the feast was called the feast of weeks, and [illegible] the fiftieth.

units.la: Quæstio: à quo die Paschatis numerandus dies quinquagesimus. Resp. ab altero seu postero die Sabbathi Paschalis. Levit.23.15.
units.tr: Question: from which day of the Passover is the fiftieth day to be counted? Answer: from the second, that is, the morrow, of the Paschal Sabbath, Lev. 23:15.

units.la: Exponatur sententiarum diversitas: quod Alij posterum diem Sabbathi intelligant de feria prima, id est, die Dominica post Sabbathum proximum à Pascha te: Alij per Sabbathum intelligant totum festum Paschatis, & posterum diem Sabbathi feriam octavam post Pascha: Alij 2 diem azymorum, seu 16 Lunam. Hanc approba, & ostende ex textu. ver.12. 15. Numeratio iubetur fieri ab eo die, quo manipulus primitiarum offertur. Oblatio autem facta est 2 die festi seu 16 luna Ioseph.l.3.c.10. Bellarmini sententia reiiciatur tanquam ratione & authoritate carens: quod ordinarie quidem numeratio fit facta a secunda feria azymorum: sed si secunda esset Sabbathum, a tertia.
units.tr: Let the diversity of opinions be set out: some understand the morrow of the Sabbath as the first weekday, that is, the Sunday after the Sabbath nearest to the Passover; others understand by the Sabbath the whole feast of the Passover, and the morrow of the Sabbath as the eighth day after the Passover; others the second day of unleavened bread, or the 16th Moon. Approve this one and show it from the text, vv. 12, 15. The counting is commanded to be made from the day on which the sheaf of first fruits is offered. The offering, however, was made on the second day of the feast, or the 16th Moon, Josephus, bk. 3, ch. 10. The opinion of Bellarmine is to be rejected as lacking reason and authority, since the counting is ordinarily made from the second weekday of unleavened bread; but if the second were a Sabbath, from the third.

units.la: Quaestio alia: Cum septem septimanae sint dies tantum 49. cur dicantur quinquaginta. Respon. Proxime sequens erat Pentecoste Levit. 23. 16. Numerabitis usque ad posterum diem Sabbathi septimi, &c.
units.tr: Another question: since seven weeks are only 49 days, why are they said to be fifty? Answer: the nearest following day was Pentecost, Lev. 23:16: "You shall number until the morrow after the seventh Sabbath, etc."

units.la: II. Quomodo celebrata. Resp. 1. universali conventu. Deut.16. Ter in anno omnis mas, &c.
units.tr: II. How it was celebrated. Answer. 1. With a general assembly, Deut. 16: "Three times in the year every male, etc."

units.la: 2. Pari solennitate cum Paschate (cessatione a laboribus & epulis.) Sed uno tantum die: Reiiciatur eorum sententia, qui diebus septem continuatam volunt. Deut.16. 10. 3. Oblationibus Levit. 23. ver. 17. Num. 28. 12. Ioseph.lib.3. cap.10.
units.tr: 2. With the same solemnity as the Passover (cessation from labours and feasting). But only for one day; their opinion is to be rejected who want it to be continued for seven days, Deut. 16:10. 3. With offerings, Lev. 23:17, Num. 28:12, Josephus, bk. 3, ch. 10.

units.la: III. Quare. Exponantur causae institutae solennitatis. 1. Ut fieret gratiarum actio pro maturis frugibus agrorum & pro messe. Offerebant duos panes fermentatos ex primis frugibus, significantes ex Dei manu se accepisse. Ideo festum primitiarum & messis appellatum. Exod.23.16.
units.tr: III. Why. Let the causes of the instituted solemnity be set out. 1. That there might be a thanksgiving for the ripe fruits of the fields and for the harvest. They offered two leavened loaves from the first fruits, signifying that they had received them from the hand of God. Hence it was called the feast of first fruits and of harvest, Exod. 23:16.

units.la: Obiectio. Etiam secundo die azymorum offerebantur primitiae: & festo tabernaculorum pro frugibus agebatur gratiae. Quod ergo discrimen?
units.tr: Objection. On the second day of unleavened bread also first fruits were offered, and at the feast of tabernacles thanks were rendered for the fruits. What, then, is the difference?

units.la: Resp. In Paschate tantum manipulus spicarum triticearum maturescentium ante messem offerebatur. In Pentecoste messe peracta duo panes ex novis frugibus Deo consecrabantur. In festo tabernaculorum pro omnibus fructibus ex agris, vineis & hortis collectis fiebat gratiarum actio.
units.tr: Answer. At the Passover only a sheaf of ripening wheat ears was offered before the harvest. At Pentecost, when the harvest was finished, two loaves from the new fruits were consecrated to God. At the feast of tabernacles thanksgiving was made for all the fruits gathered from the fields, vineyards and gardens.

units.la: Ideo festum collectionis vocatur Exod. 23. ver. 16.
units.tr: Hence it is called the feast of ingathering, Exod. 23:16.

units.la: 11. Memoria introitus in terram promissam: quod tunc demum agros colere, serere & metere coepissent. Levit. 23.10.
units.tr: 11. Memorial of the entry into the promised land, because only then had they begun to till, sow and reap the fields, Lev. 23:10.

units.la: 111. Recordatio servitutis & liberationis Ægyptiæ Deut. 16. Memeto quod fueris servus, &c.
units.tr: 111. Remembrance of the servitude and liberation from Egypt, Deut. 16: "Remember that you were a servant, etc."

units.la: 1v. Gratiarum actio pro data lege in Sinai. Ratio: quia promulgatio legis die 50 ab exitu facta creditur.
units.tr: 1v. Thanksgiving for the law given at Sinai. Reason: because the promulgation of the law is believed to have been made on the 50th day from the exodus.

units.la: v. Fuit figura venturi in Pentecoste Spiritus Sancti super Apostolos & totam Ecclesiam. Ratio: quia omnia festa Iudæorum fuerunt typi beneficiorum spiritualium Messiæ. Hebr. 10. ver. 1. Et Paulus non obscure hanc figuram indicat. 2. Cor. 3. 3.
units.tr: v. It was a figure of the coming at Pentecost of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles and the whole Church. Reason: because all the festivals of the Jews were types of the spiritual benefits of the Messiah, Heb. 10:1. And Paul indicates this figure not obscurely, 2 Cor. 3:3.

units.la: Obiectio 1. Nusquam legitur promulgatæ legis causa fuisse institutam Pentecosten. Resp. 1. Implicite indicatur Deut. 16. 12. Facies festum septimanarum, & memento quod fueris servus, &c. hoc est, quod lege lata in Sinai liberatus fueris a servitute & legibus Ægyptiorum, & transieris in meam potestatem.
units.tr: Objection 1. Nowhere is it read that Pentecost was instituted on account of the promulgation of the law. Answer 1. It is implicitly indicated, Deut. 16:12: "You shall keep the feast of weeks, and remember that you were a servant, etc.," that is, that by the law given at Sinai you were freed from the servitude and laws of the Egyptians, and passed into my power.

units.la: Probetur a discrimine Paschatis & Pentecostes. Pascha simpliciter erat recordatio liberationis factæ ex Ægypto. Pentecoste simul renovabat memoriam de modo vindicationis, quod Deus lata sua lege in Pentecoste hunc populum sibi proprium vendicasset. 2. Est communis sententia veterum Patrum. Vide August. Ep. 119. c. 16. Isych. in Levit. 23. 3. Absurdum foret credere summi illius beneficii datæ legis, nullam a Deo institutam fuisse solennem memoriam.
units.tr: Let it be proved from the difference between the Passover and Pentecost. The Passover was simply a remembrance of the liberation made out of Egypt. Pentecost at the same time renewed the memory of the manner of deliverance, namely that God, by the law he had given at Pentecost, had claimed this people as his own. 2. It is the common opinion of the ancient Fathers. See Augustine, Ep. 119, ch. 16; Isychius on Leviticus 23. 3. It would be absurd to believe that, for so great a benefit as the giving of the law, God instituted no solemn memorial.

units.la: Obiectio 2. Lex non est lata die 50 sed 48 post exitum.
units.tr: Objection 2. The law was not given on the 50th day but on the 48th after the exodus.

units.la: Prob. ex Exod.19.v.1.11. Populus venit in desertum Sinai primo die tertii mensis Siuan, ab exitu: & tertio die post lata est lex. à die autem exitus, hoc est, à 15 die Nisan, usque ad 3 diem Siuan sunt dies tantum 48. Ergo promulgatio legis nō, videtur facta in Pentecoste.
units.tr: Proof from Exod. 19:1, 11: "The people came into the desert of Sinai on the first day of the third month, Sivan, from the exodus; and on the third day after, the law was given." From the day of the exodus, that is, from the 15th of Nisan, to the 3rd of Sivan there are only 48 days. Therefore the promulgation of the law seems not to have been made at Pentecost.

units.la: Resp. Neg. antecedens. 1. quia sic latio legis neque in Pentecosten neque in ullum aliud festum Iudæis incidisset: & nobis periret pulcerrima analogia latæ legis, & missi Spiritus Sancti in Pente-coste.
units.tr: Answer: I deny the antecedent. 1. Because in that case the giving of the law would not have fallen on Pentecost nor on any other feast of the Jews; and for us the most beautiful analogy of the law given and the Holy Spirit sent at Pentecost would be lost.

units.la: 2. quia locus Exod.19. 1. non evidenter pro-bat legem latam die tertio mensis tertii, sed tantum die tertio postquam venerunt in desertum Sinai. Quoto autem die eo venerint, non expri-mitur.
units.tr: 2. Because the passage Exod. 19:1 does not clearly prove that the law was given on the third day of the third month, but only on the third day after they came into the desert of Sinai. On what day of that month they came is not expressed.

units.la: Ostende ex textu & expone duplicem sensum; vel quod primo die, hoc est, in novilunio mensis tertii: (quia חדש[?] etiam novilunium significat) vel quod tertio die venerint: quia relativum in die hac, videtur referri ad numerum præcedentem mensis, hoc est, tertium: quasi dicat tertio mense & ea ipsa die, hoc est, tertia venerunt, &c.
units.tr: Show from the text and explain the twofold sense: either that they came on the first day, that is, at the new moon of the third month (since חדש also signifies new moon); or that they came on the third day, because the relative "on this day" seems to refer to the preceding number of the month, that is, the third, as if he said: in the third month and on that very day, that is, the third, they came, etc.

units.la: 3. quia etsi de die latæ Legis inter interpretes non conveniat, tamen convenit in hoc, latam esse in Pentecoste, hoc est, die 50: sed variant in numerationis termino à quo & ad quem.
units.tr: 3. For although the interpreters do not agree on the day on which the law was given, they do agree on this: that it was given at Pentecost, that is, on the fiftieth day; but they differ on the starting and ending points of the count.

units.la: Recensentur præcipuæ sententiæ.
units.tr: The principal opinions are listed.

units.la: 1. Augustinus numerat à 14 luna Nisan usque ad tertium diem tertii mensis inclusive, ex primo mensé dies 17, ex secundo, 30, ex tertio 3, qui conficiunt 50.
units.tr: 1. Augustine counts from the fourteenth day of the moon of Nisan up to and including the third day of the third month: from the first month 17 days, from the second 30, and from the third 3, which make 50.

units.la: Ostendatur error in termino à quo: quia non 14 sed 15 luna exiverunt. Item, quia non à 14. sed à 16. luna numerandum juxta legem Levit. 23.
units.tr: The error is shown in the starting point: for they went out not on the 14th but on the 15th day of the moon. Likewise, the count must begin not from the 14th but from the 16th day of the moon, according to the law in Leviticus 23.

units.la: 2. Rupertus Tuicensis abbas lib. 3. in Ex. cap. 23. & 41. numerat ab eadem 14 luna usque ad 4 lunam mensis tertii ponens legem etiam latam non tertio sed quarto die, quo est lecta à Mose coram populo, conjecturam faciens ex Exod. 24. & secundo mensi tribuens dies non 30. sed 29, pro ratione mensium Lunarium qui constant singuli 29 dieb. 12 hor. alterni dieb. 30 & 29, qualibus Hebraei nunc utuntur.
units.tr: 2. Rupert, abbot of Deutz, in book 3 on Exodus, chapters 23 and 41, counts from the same 14th day of the moon up to the 4th day of the moon of the third month. He holds that the law was given not on the third day but on the fourth day, when it was read by Moses before the people, conjecturing this from Exodus 24; and he assigns to the second month not 30 days but 29, following the reckoning of lunar months, each of which consists of 29 days and 12 hours, alternating between 30 and 29 days, such as the Hebrews use now.

units.la: Ostendatur error. 1. in termino à quo, ut prius.
units.tr: The error is shown: 1. in the starting point, as before.

units.la: 2. In termino ad quem: quia lex est lata à Deo in monte inter tonitrua: non infra montem à Mose: alioqui periret analogia miraculorum latæ legis veteris & novæ.
units.tr: 2. In the ending point: because the law was given by God on the mountain amid thunderings, not by Moses below the mountain; otherwise the analogy of the miracles of the giving of the old and new law would be lost.

units.la: 3. quia fierent non 50 sed 51 dies: quandoquidem Hebraei tunc non habuerint menses lunares sed solares, ut mox dicetur.
units.tr: 3. Because there would be not 50 but 51 days, since the Hebrews at that time did not have lunar months but solar ones, as will shortly be said.

units.la: 3. Lyra numerat à 16 luna Nisan usque ad 6 lunam Siuan, sumens ex Nisan 15. dies. ex Zif. 30. ex Siuan 6. qui sunt 50: quia Moses venerit in desertum Sinai die 3 tertii mensis: postridie dixerit: Estote parati die tertia: sexta lex lata, &c.
units.tr: 3. Lyra counts from the 16th day of the moon of Nisan up to the 6th day of the moon of Sivan, taking 15 days from Nisan, 30 from Iyyar, and 6 from Sivan, which make 50: because Moses came into the wilderness of Sinai on the third day of the third month; on the following day he said, "Be ready for the third day," and on the sixth the law was given, etc.

units.la: Approbetur sententia in termino à quo, juxta legem Levit. 23. Item in eo, quod venerint in desertum Sinai non primo sed tertio die Sivan Exod. 19. ver. 1. referens illud In die hac, sept. ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ ad numerum praecedentem mensis, hoc est tertium.
units.tr: The opinion is approved as to the starting point, according to the law in Leviticus 23. Likewise as to this, that they came into the wilderness of Sinai not on the first but on the third day of Sivan (Exodus 19:1), referring the words "On this day" (Greek ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ) to the preceding number of the month, that is, the third.

units.la: Ratio: quia de primo die Sivan non posse accipi ostensum est.
units.tr: The reason: because it has been shown that the first day of Sivan cannot be meant.

units.la: Obiect. ירח significat Novilunium. Resp. absolute positum, ut Psal.81.4. Clangite בחדש[?] in novilunio. 1.Sam.10.5. Cras est ירח novilunium, &c. Cum numero autem positum significat mensem: ut hoc loco.
units.tr: Objection: the word yerach signifies the new moon. Answer: it is so when used absolutely, as in Psalm 81:4, "Blow the trumpet at the new moon" (bachodesh, "at the new moon"); 1 Samuel 20:5, "Tomorrow is the new moon," etc. But when placed with a number it signifies the month, as in this passage.

units.la: Reprehendatur modeste dupliciter:
units.tr: The opinion is modestly rebuked in two ways:

units.la: 1. Quod Moses non tertio sed quarto die demum dixerit: Estote parati die tertia, &c. Probetur error ex textu: quia eodem die quo venerunt in desertum Sinai, etiam Moses mox ascendit in montem, & sanctificare coepit populum: & dixit, Estote parati in diem tertiam. ex collatione versus 10.11.&14.15.
units.tr: 1. That Moses did not say "Be ready for the third day" until the fourth day. The error is proved from the text: for on the same day on which they came into the wilderness of Sinai, Moses also immediately went up the mountain and began to sanctify the people, and said, "Be ready for the third day"; this is shown by comparing verses 10–11 and 14–15.

units.la: Obiectio: Videtur impossibile, omnia illa quae Exod.19. usque ad ver.15. habentur, uno die ter-tio facta, populum venisse, castra posuisse, Moses bis ascendisse montem, bis descendisse, bis con-cionatum esse populo, &c.
units.tr: Objection: it seems impossible that all those things which are recorded in Exodus 19 down to verse 15 were done on a single third day: that the people came, pitched camp, Moses went up the mountain twice, came down twice, preached to the people twice, etc.

units.la: Resp. non videtur, die praesertim longiore non procul à solstitio: quia potuerunt venire maturius, castra metantibus aliis Moses bis ascendere in montem vicinum aliquo usque, non in cacu-men, ut postea ver.20. bis referre paucis iussa Dei ad populum, vesperi eundem sanctificare, &c.
units.tr: Answer: it does not seem so, especially since the day was rather long and not far from the solstice: they could have come earlier, while others pitched camp, Moses could have gone up twice to a nearby mountain, not to its summit (as later in verse 20), twice reported God's commands briefly to the people, and in the evening sanctified them again, etc.

units.la: 11. Quod sexto die lata lex sit, quia à secunda die azymorum ad sextam Sivan inclusive, sunt dies 51. computatis diebus 15 ex primo, 30 ex secundo, 6 ex tertio mense.
units.tr: 11. That the law was given on the sixth day, because from the second day of unleavened bread to the sixth of Sivan inclusive there are 51 days, counting 15 days from the first month, 30 from the second, and 6 from the third month.

units.la: IV. Sententia probabilior, quod lex sit data die quinta Sivan.
units.tr: IV. The more probable opinion is that the law was given on the fifth day of Sivan.

units.la: Ratio 1. quia die quinta fuit expletum illud triduum, de quo ver. 15. Estote parati in diem ter-tiam, &c. nam tertio die venerunt in desertum, & eodem die Moses ascendit in montem, & vesperi coepit sanctificare populum: quarto laverunt vestimenta: quinto Deus descendit super montem inter tonitrua, &c.
units.tr: The reason 1: because on the fifth day that three-day period was completed, of which verse 15 speaks, "Be ready for the third day," etc.; for they came into the wilderness on the third day, and on the same day Moses went up the mountain, and in the evening began to sanctify the people; on the fourth they washed their garments; on the fifth God came down upon the mountain amid thunderings, etc.

units.la: 2. quia a secundo azymorum ad quintum Sivan praecise sunt dies 50: sumendo ex Nisan dies 15, ex Zif 30, ex Sivan quinque.
units.tr: 2. Because from the second of unleavened bread to the fifth of Sivan there are precisely 50 days, reckoning 15 days from Nisan, 30 from Iyyar, and five from Sivan.

units.la: Per occupatione ostendatur, quod secundo mensis 30 dies recte tribuantur: quia Hebraei tempore latae legis utebantur mensibus & annis non lunaribus inaequalibus, sed solaribus aequalibus Aegyptiis, usque ad aeram Alexandri M. per annos mundi 3449. Inde usque ad congestum Thalmud circa annum Christi 505 uti coeperunt lunaribus inaequalibus, quos tamen beneficio cycli Metonici reduxerunt ad Solares. A Thalmud congesto rursus aliam anni rationem, iuxta annos mundi habent in hunc usque diem.
units.tr: By the way, it is shown that 30 days are rightly assigned to the second month: because at the time of the giving of the law the Hebrews used months and years that were not lunar and unequal, but solar and equal, like the Egyptians, until the era of Alexander the Great, in the year of the world 3449. From then until the compiling of the Talmud, around the year of Christ 505, they began to use unequal lunar months, which they nevertheless brought back to solar ones by means of the Metonic cycle. Since the compiling of the Talmud they have again had another system of the year, reckoned by the years of the world, up to this day.

units.la: Author Christmannus Comment. in Alfrag. de Calendario Hebraeorum.
units.tr: The author is Christmann, in his commentary on the Alfraganus, concerning the Hebrew calendar.

units.la: Conclusio: Cum ergo sit certum, 50 die ab exitu legem esse latam: non est dubium a Deo in institutione Veteris Pentecostes anniversariam celebrationem tanti beneficii spectatam fuisse.
units.tr: Conclusion: since therefore it is certain that the law was given on the 50th day after the exodus, there is no doubt that God, in instituting the Old Pentecost, intended the annual celebration of so great a benefit.

units.la: Addatur aliquid de usu huius disputationis: quod faciat ad intelligentiam non paucorum Scripturae locorum: item historiae veteris Ecclesiae: item discriminis Iudaicæ & Christianæ Pentecos-tes: ad quam deinceps transfeatur.
units.tr: Something should be added about the use of this disputation: that it serves to the understanding of not a few passages of Scripture, likewise to the history of the early Church, and likewise to the difference between the Jewish and the Christian Pentecost, to which we shall then pass over.

units.la: De nova Pentecoste.
units.tr: On the New Pentecost.

units.la: Describatur initio, quod sit una ex anniversariis solemnitatibus Ecclesiæ Christianæ, qua quotannis quinquagesimo die à Dominica resurrectionis historia effusi Spiritus Sancti super Ecclesiam populo Christiano publicè recolenda proponitur, & tantum beneficium solenni voce Ecclesiæ celebratur.
units.tr: To begin with, let it be described that it is one of the annual solemnities of the Christian Church, by which, every year on the fiftieth day after the Lord's resurrection, the history of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the Church is publicly set before the Christian people to be commemorated, and so great a benefit is celebrated with the solemn voice of the Church.

units.la: Deinde ἀποστολικῶς[?] ex dicto Col. 2. Nemo vos iudicet in parte diei festi: Item Gal. 5. Ne rursus implicabimini servitutis iugo ostendatur, Christianos non Iudaizare, explicatis discriminibus utriusque Pentecostes.
units.tr: Next, from the apostolic word in Col. 2, "Let no one judge you in respect of a feast day," and likewise from Gal. 5, "Do not be entangled again with the yoke of bondage," let it be shown that Christians do not Judaize, the differences between the two Pentecosts being set out.

units.la: 1. Differunt observationis necessitate. Vetus fuit Iudæis à Deo præcepta tanquam pars cultus, & typus beneficiorum Messiæ: Unde eius omissio vel mutatio in Ecclesia Iudaica fuisset peccatum offendens Deum, &c.
units.tr: 1. They differ in the necessity of observance. The old feast was prescribed by God to the Jews as part of worship and as a type of the benefits of the Messiah. Hence its omission or alteration in the Jewish Church would have been a sin offending God, and so on.

units.la: Nova consuetudine libera Ecclesiæ est recepta in veteris locum, sine opinione necessitatis, aut cultus, aut typi: cum libertate omittendi vel mutandi, si Ecclesia necessarias, vel probabiles causas haberet.
units.tr: The new feast, by free custom of the Church, has been received in the place of the old, without any belief in its necessity, either as worship or as type, and with liberty to omit or change it if the Church had necessary or probable reasons.

units.la: Occupatio de Origine: videri nonnullis ab Apostolis institutam propter dicta 1. Cor. 16. 8. & Actor. 20. 16. Sed esse incertum. 1. quia ea loca possint de Pentecoste Iudæorum intelligi. 2. testimonio Socratis histor. Eccles. lib. 5. c. 21. quod neque Servator, neque Apostoli leges de festis praeceperint, vel iugum servitutis imposuerint: Sed festum (inquit) Paschatis aliaq; festa libero a-quoq; judicio eorum qui in illis diebus beneficia acce-perant, recolenda reliquerunt. Neque enim Apo-stolis propositum fuit, ut de celebrandis festis leges sancirent, sed ut rectae vivendi rationis & pietatis nobis authores essent.
units.tr: Concerning its origin: some think it was instituted by the Apostles, on account of the words in 1 Cor. 16:8 and Acts 20:16.
