"For if we have been made united with the likeness of his death," says Paul, "we shall certainly also be partakers of his resurrection, knowing this, that our old man was crucified together with him, so that the body of sin might be abolished."

units.la: Rom.6.3. — the first reference (Rom. 6:3) is printed in the right margin beside the italic quotation. mirum & resurrectionis participes erimus : illud sci-entes, quod vetus noster homo ; simul cum ipso cruci-fixus est, ut corpus peccati aboleretur. Ut enim fur-culus communem habet vitæ & mortis conditio-nem cum arbore, in quam insertus est : ita vitæ Christi non minus quàm mortis participes nos consentaneum est: id quod alibi Apostolus dicat, dum Christum dicit pro omnibus esse, ut qui vivunt, posthac non sibi vivis carnis desideriis indulgeant, sed pro omnibus mortuus est, & resurrexit, to-tos[?] ad eius voluntatem vitam suam componant. Item : Si consurrexistis cum Christo, quæ sursum sunt quaerite, non quæ supra terram : ac sanctus Apostolus diceret. Hæc sit tota vestra meditatio : huc ingenium, huc animum applica-te, ut mundo cum suis cupiditatibus renuncian-tes, vos totos Christo, qui nunc in cœlis ad dex-tram patris sedet & gloriosè regnat addicatis, pla-neque consecretis: quia nimirum cum Christo ex morte peccati resurrexistis. Hæc est prima illa resurrectio, quàm D. Iohannes in Apocalypsi prædicat. Hanc Christus per verbum & vocem Evangelii operatur in Electis, sicut inquit: Amen amen dico vobis, venit tempus & nunc est, cum mortui, (nempe in peccatis) audient vocem Filii Dei & qui audient vivent. Hanc omnes credentes in hac vita in se fieri sentiunt. Hi enim sunt palmites, qui manentes in vite, & purgati sanguine ac Spiritu eius fructum multum ferunt. Hi sunt, quos jure beatos prædicat Iohannes, siquidem partem in prima resurrectione habent. Hi denique sunt, qui, teste Apostolo, superinduen-tur, siquidem induti non nudi reperientur: sed Christi iustitia ornati, in Dei conspectu apparebunt. Hi tandem ubi Christus ad iudicandum vivos & mortuos est venturus, potétia eius ex mortuis suscitati speratā immortalitatis gloriam certò accepturi, nec non capiti suo glorioso conformes sunt futuri.
units.tr: Rom. 6:3. For just as the little graft shares the common condition of life and death with the tree into which it is grafted, so it is fitting that we share not less in the life of Christ than in his death. This the Apostle also says elsewhere, when he states that Christ died for all, so that those who live should no longer live to themselves in the desires of the flesh, but should arrange their whole life according to his will, since he died and rose for all. Likewise: "If you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, not those that are on the earth." And the holy Apostle says, as it were: let this be the whole of your meditation; apply your mind and your spirit to this, so that, renouncing the world with its desires, you may devote and wholly consecrate yourselves to Christ, who now sits in heaven at the right hand of the Father and reigns gloriously, since, of course, you have risen with Christ from the death of sin. This is that first resurrection which Saint John proclaims in the Apocalypse. Christ works this in the elect through the word and voice of the Gospel, as he says: "Verily, verily, I say to you, the hour is coming, and now is, when the dead (namely in sins) shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear shall live." All believers feel this happening within themselves in this life. For they are the branches which, abiding in the vine and cleansed by his blood and Spirit, bear much fruit. These are the ones whom John rightly pronounces blessed, since they have a part in the first resurrection. Finally, these are they who, as the Apostle testifies, are clothed upon, since, having been found clothed and not naked, they will appear adorned with the righteousness of Christ in the sight of God. And at last, when Christ comes to judge the living and the dead, they are to receive with certainty the hoped-for glory of immortality, raised from the dead by his power, and they are also to be made conformable to their glorious head.

units.la: Atque hic iam tertius resurrectionis dominicae est fructus, de quo pauca quaedam subiiciemus. Sanè quantum momentū resurrectio Christi habeat ad nostrorum corporū suscitationem, æternamque glorificationem adstruendam, vel ex unica Pauli argumentatione satis superque apparet. Cûm enim in Ecclesia Corinthiaca non deessent profana ingenia, quæ seu malitia seu humanæ philosophiæ ratiunculis fascinata resurrectionem carnis nostræ in dubium vocarent, atque ita non tam infirmos turbarent, quàm ipsam fidem Christianam à fundamentis everterent, ipse malo tàm pestilenti nullum efficacius remedium quàm Christi resurrectionem opponendum ratus, sic illos vanitatis convincebat. Christus resurrexit. Ergo mortui resurgent. Si enim, inquit, resurrectio mortuorum non est, Christus quoque non est excitatus. Atqui Christus est excitatus ex mortuis, primitiæ eorum, qui obdormiverunt factus: alioqui fatendum inanem esse Evangelii prædicationem, inanem fidem nostram: nos adhuc esse in peccatis nostris: quotquot in Christo obdormiverunt, periisse: nos in hac tantum vita sperare in Christum, atque ita omnium horminum miserrimos esse, quæ omnia multo ab-surdissima esse, quis non intelligit ? Hoc argumento quid, quæso, firmius? Si enim Christus primitiæ, nos massa sumus: an non ipsa ratio postulat, ut vis resurrectionis ipsius ad nos transfundatur? Si ipse caput nos membra sumus, quis non nisi summa cum iniuria membra à capite avellaret? Si ipse Sacerdos nos populus eius sumus: an non eos, quos unico sacrificio sui corporis redemit, atque in peculium sibi adscivit, plenè tandem liberatos ad se evehet,& gloria atque honore coronabit? Si denique rex, nos subditi sumus, an non æquissimum est, ut regni ipsius participes facti, tandem cum eo in æternum regnemus. Quid? An non Christus est secundus Adam? Sicut ergo in primo Adam omnes moriuntur: sic, inquit Apostolus, in Christo secundo Adamo omnes etiam vivificantur. Factus est enim prior homo Adam in animam viventem, posterior autem Adam factus est in Spiritum viventem. Vt ergo primus Adam, non sibi solum, sed nobis omnibus est mortuus, ita neque Christus, qui est antitypus, sibi soli resurrexit. Venit enim, ut quæ in Adamo pessundata erant, instauraret. Itaque si Spiritus eius, qui suscitavit Iesum ex mortuis, habitat in nobis: is qui suscitavit Christum ex mortuis, vivificabit etiam corpora nostra mortalia per Spiritum suum in nobis habitatem. Secus pro facto ex Apostoli sententia, oes qui in Christo sunt mortui perierint,& homine Christiano nemo stultior, qui vitam in morte quærat, nemo etiam miserior qui ob spem resurrectionis ac melioris vitæ, tot odia, pericula, ærumnas, denique mortem, Christi causa, adire & perferre non dubitat. At nos [illegible, ~6 letters] hanc spem cum Iobo in cordibus nostris firmiter[?] teneamus, redemtorem nostrum ex morte eluctatum vivere, nosque in novissimo die suscitaturum esse: ubi liberi à peccato, liberi à calamitatibus, liberi à lachrymis, à dolore, à periculis omnibus in cœlestem illam civitatem, quæ sursum est, adscribemur, & bonis, quæ nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec homo cogitatione comprehendit, in æternum utemur fruemur.
units.tr: Here is the third fruit of the Lord's resurrection, on which I will add a few points. Indeed, how great a weight Christ's resurrection has for establishing the raising of our bodies and their eternal glorification can be seen clearly enough and more than enough from Paul's argument alone. For when in the church at Corinth there were not lacking profane minds who, whether from malice or charmed by the petty reasonings of human philosophy, called into doubt the resurrection of our flesh, and so troubled not so much the weak as overturned the Christian faith itself from its foundations, Paul, thinking that no more effective remedy could be set against so pestilent an evil than Christ's resurrection, thus convinced them of their vanity. Christ has risen. Therefore the dead will rise. For, he says, "If there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised." But Christ has been raised from the dead, become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep; otherwise we must confess that the preaching of the Gospel is empty, our faith empty, that we are still in our sins, that all who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished, and that we who hope in Christ in this life only are of all men the most miserable. Who does not see that all these things are most absurd? What, I ask, is firmer than this argument? For if Christ is the firstfruits, we are the lump: does not reason itself demand that the power of his resurrection be poured into us? If he is the head, we are the members; who would not, with the greatest wrong, tear the members away from the head? If he is the Priest, we are his people: will he not at last raise to himself, fully freed, those whom he redeemed by the single sacrifice of his body and claimed for himself as his own possession, and crown them with glory and honour? If finally he is King, we are his subjects: is it not most just that, having been made partakers of his kingdom, we should at last reign with him for ever? What then? Is not Christ the second Adam? As therefore in the first Adam all die, so, says the Apostle, in Christ the second Adam all are also made alive. "For the first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit." Therefore, just as the first Adam died not for himself alone but for us all, so Christ, who is the antitype, did not rise for himself alone. For he came to restore what had been ruined in Adam. Therefore, if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in us, he who raised Christ from the dead will also quicken our mortal bodies through his Spirit dwelling in us. Otherwise, according to the Apostle's judgment, all who are dead in Christ have perished; no one is more foolish than a Christian who seeks life in death, and no one more wretched than he who, for the hope of resurrection and a better life, does not hesitate to face and endure so many hatreds, dangers, hardships and finally death for Christ's sake. But let us hold firmly in our hearts this hope, which Job held, that our Redeemer lives, having wrestled free from death, and that he will raise us up on the last day, when, free from sin, free from calamities, free from tears, from grief and from all dangers, we shall be enrolled in that heavenly city which is above, and shall enjoy and possess for ever the good things which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor the human mind comprehended.

units.la: Satis multa verba mihi fecisse videor de historia deque fructibus, qui inde tanquam ex perenni fonte promanant, & se se longe latéque diffundunt. Restat ut quod tertio loco instituimus, ad quosnam hi fructus pertineant, explicare pergamus.
units.tr: I seem to have said enough about the history and about the fruits which flow from it as from a perennial fountain and spread far and wide. It remains that we go on to explain, as the third point we proposed, to whom these fruits pertain.

units.la: Ad scripturam itaque sacram tanquam ad unicam dextrè judicandi Cynosuram cursum nostrum dirigentes, fructus hos tàm pretiosos ad omnes & solos credentes pertinere asserimus: impios verò omnesque incredulos ab illis procul arcemus. Etenim omnes & soli credentes fructuum illorum dulcedinem sentiunt, omnes & soli percipiunt, omnes & soli vera fide sibi applicant. Hi enim sunt qui sermonem Christi audiunt, credunt, vitamque æternam habent, nec in condemnationem veniunt: Hi sunt qui Deo reconciliatur & justificantur. Hi regenerantur, & in novam vitam cum Christo excitantur, quorum corda fide purificantur, quique ex gratia per fidem seruantur. Hi deniq; à mortuis per Christum resurgent, Quare ad eos à quibus percipiuntur, & quibus S. sacra proprios vendicat, hoc est, ad omnes & solos credentes, hos fructus pertinere, haud immerito statuimus. Quid enim, quaeso, impii viva & justificante fide destituti de his omnibus participarent, qui Deo non placent (sine fide.n. Deo placere est impossibile) qui ad Christum non pertinent: qui cùm non sint haeredes; neque in re, neque ad rem, quod dicitur, hic jus ullum habent: Quomodo ad eos pertineret Christus? Quomodo beneficia Christi? Quinimò isti omnes ipsius filii Dei voce ab his thesauris procul arcentur, & aeternae maledictioni adjudicantur. Sic enim ille in Evangelio: Qui non credit, jam judicatus est: & super eum manet ira Dei. Et Paulus: Qui non habet Spiritum Christi, non est eius. Quem Apostoli locum cumprimis huc facere arbitror. Si enim infideles ad Christum non pertinent, neque sunt Christi: à correlatis firmissimè concluditur, vicissim Christum cum suis beneficiis ad ipsos non pertinere: & sicut ipsi non sunt Christi: ita nec Christum ipsorum esse.
units.tr: Therefore, directing our course to Holy Scripture as to the one sure Cynosure for judging rightly, we affirm that these so precious fruits pertain to all and only believers, while we keep the impious and all unbelievers far away from them. For all and only believers feel the sweetness of those fruits, all and only receive them, all and only apply them to themselves by true faith. For these are they who hear the word of Christ, believe, have eternal life, and do not come into condemnation; these are they who are reconciled to God and justified. These are regenerated and raised up with Christ into a new life, whose hearts are purified by faith, and who are saved by grace through faith. These, finally, shall rise from the dead through Christ. Hence we have rightly determined that these fruits pertain to those by whom they are received, and to whom Holy Scripture assigns them as its own, that is, to all and only believers. For what, I ask, would the impious, destitute of living and justifying faith, have to do with all these things, since they do not please God (for without faith it is impossible to please God), since they do not belong to Christ, and since, not being heirs, they have, as the saying goes, neither right in the thing nor right to the thing? How would Christ pertain to them? How would the benefits of Christ? Nay, all of them are kept far away from these treasures by the voice of the Son of God himself, and are adjudged to eternal curse. For thus he says in the Gospel: "He who does not believe is already judged, and the wrath of God abides on him." And Paul: "He who does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his." I think this is the passage the Apostle has especially in view here. For if unbelievers do not pertain to Christ, and are not Christ's, it follows most firmly from the correlatives that, in turn, Christ with his benefits does not pertain to them; and just as they are not Christ's, so Christ is not theirs.

units.la: At inquis, Christus pro omnibus est mortuus. Pro omnibus ergo etiam resurrexit. Recte sane: Si λύτρως[?] & meriti eius sufficientiam spectes. De hac enim loquitur Iohannes: cnm dicit Christũ esse expiationem pro peccatis totius mundi. Et sane extra controversiam est, tantum pondus habere in judicio Dei mortem filii eius, ut sufficiat non unius tantùm mundi, sed millium peccatis expian-
units.tr: But you say: Christ died for all. Therefore he also rose again for all. Rightly indeed, if you look to the ransom and the sufficiency of his merit. For John speaks of this when he says that Christ is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world. And indeed it is beyond controversy that the death of the Son of God carries such weight in the judgment of God that it suffices to expiate the sins not of one world only, but of thousands

units.la: Hebr.11.6. expiandis, si modo hanc mortis medicinam om-nes fide acciperent. Sed de efficacia & actu ipso fructuum est quæstio, quem negamus incredulis juxta & credulis communem esse, nec dici potest eius respectu, Christū pariter pro omnibus mortuum esse.
units.tr: of worlds, if only all were to receive this medicine of death by faith. But the question concerns the efficacy and the actual enjoyment of the fruits, which we deny is common to unbelievers as well as believers; nor can it be said that, with respect to this, Christ died equally for all.

units.la: Hic vero malè feriati quidam homines, quasi parum controversiarum habeat Ecclesia, plenis buccis virus suum in nos despumant, indignissi-mè ferentes, nos cœlestes thesauros & margari-tas non æquo jure piis & impiis, fidelibus & infi-delibus, electis & reprobis, Christi membris & Diaboli servis, ovibus & porcis dividere. Clamat ergo nos negare Christū pro omnibus esse mor-tuum: hanc vero esse Saracenicam, Mahometi-cam & plus quàm Paganam blasphemiam, qua religio Christiana funditus evertatur.
units.tr: But here certain men, ill-occupied, as though the Church had too few controversies, foam out their venom against us with full cheeks, indignant that we divide the heavenly treasures and pearls not with equal right between the pious and the impious, the faithful and the unfaithful, the elect and the reprobate, the members of Christ and the servants of the Devil, sheep and swine. So they cry out that we deny that Christ died for all, and that this is Saracen, Mahometan and more than pagan blasphemy, by which the Christian religion is utterly overthrown.

units.la: Nobis vero auditores, cum talibus monstris non est propositum contendere. De calumnia tantum aliquid monendum est. Quid enim est putidissima calumnia alios gravare, si hoc non est? Hoccine est simpliciter negare Christum pro omnibus mortuum, cum sufficientiam ab efficacia distinguimus, & efficaciam ad solam fidelium universitatem ex Iudæis & gentibus collectam restringimus?
units.tr: But with such monsters, hearers, we have no intention of contending. Only a word must be said about the calumny. For what is the most foul calumny, if it is not this, to burden others with what they do not hold? Is this simply to deny that Christ died for all, when we distinguish sufficiency from efficacy, and restrict efficacy to the whole body of the faithful gathered from Jews and Gentiles alone?

units.la: Ceterum ut veritas magis elucescat, age pau-cis rationes gravissimas exponamus, quibus adducti hoc modo distinguamus. Ac primò quidem hoc non ex humani ingenii commentis sumus: Sed è scriptura ipsa hausimus, expressimus. Hæc enim passim solis credetibus & electis Chriftum cum suis beneficiis vendicat, dum eum vi-tam suam pro ovibus ponere affirmat. Hæc Christum non pro mundo, sed pro iis tantum, quii ipsi a patre dati erant, orasse testatur. Hæc denique incredulis omnibus fructus hosce adimit, dum eos vitam æternam habere negat: sed iram Dei super illis manere[?] constanter asseverat. Deinde nō tantum S.sacra clamat: sed & experientia sa-tis superque comprobat omnes incredulos per-petuò,tàm ante.quàm post Christi mortem dam-natos, vel adhuc damnandos, indè à matris lacte ad extremum usque halitum fuisse & esse, & fo-re filios iræ, hostes Dei, membra Satanæ, peccati servos & mancipia: nec partem habuisse vel ha-bere vel æternum habituros esse in regno Dei.
units.tr: Moreover, that the truth may shine more clearly, come, let us set out briefly the most weighty reasons by which we are led to distinguish in this way. And first, we have not drawn this from the inventions of human wit, but have drawn and expressed it from Scripture itself. For Scripture everywhere claims Christ with his benefits for believers and the elect alone, while it affirms that he laid down his life for the sheep. It attests that Christ prayed not for the world but only for those whom the Father had given him. Finally, it takes these fruits away from all unbelievers, while it denies that they have eternal life, and constantly asserts that the wrath of God abides on them. Second, Holy Scripture does not merely proclaim this, but experience also amply and more than sufficiently confirms that all unbelievers, condemned for ever both before and after Christ's death, or still to be condemned, from the mother's milk to the last breath have been and are, and will be, children of wrath, enemies of God, members of Satan, slaves and bondservants of sin; and that they have had no part, nor have, nor will ever have, in the kingdom of God.

units.la: Testatur hoc idem Apostolus, Eramus naturafi-lii iræ, sicut & reliqui: Et Christus de omnibus clamat: Nunquam novi vos, discedite à me omnes, qui operamini iniquitatem: Hósne efficaciter re-demtos & reconciliatos Deo Christi morte dice-mus, quos Christus nunquam pro suis agnovit? Aniflos[?] in gratia Dei esse, atque à peccato, mor-te & Diabolo efficaciter liberatos existimabimꝰ, quos Apostolus talibus titulis insignire non dubitat, qui Diabolis potius, quàm hominibus ad imaginem Dei conditis conveniunt, nunc filios iræ, nunc in offensis mortuos: nunc contumaces appellans: nunc principem aëris in eis efficacem esse affirmans, qui eos instar stolidi vel petulantis fesloris per invia rapit, per præcipitia devol-vit, ad contumaciam, ferociam, omnisque gene-ris sceleta instigat?
units.tr: The same Apostle testifies this too: "We were by nature children of wrath, even as the others." And Christ cries out concerning all: "I never knew you; depart from me, all you who work iniquity." Shall we say that these men were effectively redeemed and reconciled to God by the death of Christ, whom Christ never acknowledged as his own? Shall we think that they are in the grace of God, and effectively freed from sin, death and the Devil, those whom the Apostle does not hesitate to mark with such titles, who belong to the Devil rather than to men created in the image of God: now calling them children of wrath, now dead in their offences, now stubborn; and affirming that the prince of the air is active in them, who snatches them along impassable ways like a foolish or wanton horse, hurls them down precipices, and stirs them up to obstinacy, fierceness and every kind of wickedness?

units.la: Quod si orthodoxorum Patrum sententias producere animus esset, qui ita nobiscum distin-guunt, in amplissimum sane orationis campum vos deducerem. Audite Cyrillum, Christi verba. Non oro pro mundo: cum Iohannis dicto: Est propitiatio pro peccatis totius mundi: Sic conciliant m: Iohannes inquit, videtur discrepare a Salvatore. Salvator enim pro mundo hic rogare abnuit. Iohannes autem non pro nostris solum peccatis propitiationem & paracletum illum esse: sed pro universo affirmat mundo. Verum Beatus Iohannes, quoniam erat Iudaeus[?], ne pro Iudeis tantum paracletus esse Dominus apud patrem videretur, non autem etiam pro aliis gentibus, quae vocatae obsequuntur sunt, necessario pro toto mundo adduxit. Dominus autem Iesus suos a non suis separans, pro eis, inquit, TANTUM MODO, qui verba mea servant, & jugum meum acceperunt, rogo. Nam quorum mediator atq; pontifex est ipsis TANTUM MODO mediationis bonum non iniuria attribuit. Hactenus Cyrillus. Audite & Prosperum in responsionibus ad obiectiones Vicentinas, eodem modo distin-guentem. Quod ergo, inquit, ad magnitudinem & potentiam pretii, & quod ad unam pertinet causam generis humani: sanguis Christi redemptio est totius mundi. Sed qui hoc saeculum sine fide & sine regeneratio-nis sacramento pertransiunt: REDEMTIONIS ALIENI sunt. Cum itaq; propter unam omnium naturam, & unam omnium causam a Domino nostro in veritate susceptam, recte omnes aiicantur redemti, & tamen non omnes a captivitate sint eruti: redemtionis PROPRIETAS haud dubie penes illos est, de quibus princeps mundi missus est foras: & jam non vasa Diaboli, sed membra sunt Christi. Idem ad capitula Gallorum respondens, phrasin hanc, Christum tantum pro fidelibus esse mortuum, diserte approbat, quam isti ut Saracenicam damnant. Cum itaq; inquit, rectissime dicatur Salvator pro totius mundi redemtione crucifixus, propter veram naturæ humanæ susceptionem, & propter communem in primo homine perditionem: potest tamen dici pro his TANTUM crucifixus, quibus mors ipsius profuit. Dicit enim Evangelista, quia Iesus mortuus erat pro gente, nec tantum pro gente: sed etiam ut filios Dei dispersos congregaret in unum. Hactenus Prosper.
units.tr: If I meant to produce the opinions of the orthodox Fathers, who distinguish in the same way as we do, I would lead you into a very wide field of discourse indeed. Hear Cyril on the words of Christ: "I do not pray for the world," together with John's saying: "He is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world." He reconciles them thus: "John," he says, "seems to disagree with the Saviour. For the Saviour refuses to ask on behalf of the world here. But John affirms that he is the propitiation and the Paraclete not only for our sins, but for the whole world. Yet Blessed John, since he was a Jew, lest the Lord should seem to be a Paraclete with the Father only for the Jews, and not also for the other nations, who have been called and have obeyed, necessarily brought him forward for the whole world. But the Lord Jesus, separating his own from those who are not his, says: 'I pray for those ONLY who keep my words and have accepted my yoke.' For to those for whom he is mediator and high priest, he rightly attributes the benefit of the mediation ONLY." So far Cyril. Hear also Prosper, who distinguishes in the same way in his replies to the objections of the Vincentians: "Therefore," he says, "as regards the greatness and the power of the price, and as regards the one cause of the human race, the blood of Christ is the redemption of the whole world. But those who pass through this age without faith and without the sacrament of regeneration are OF ANOTHER REDEMPTION. Since, therefore, on account of the one nature of all, and the one cause of all, taken up in truth by our Lord, all are rightly said to be redeemed, and yet not all have been snatched from captivity, the OWNERSHIP of redemption undoubtedly belongs to those of whom the prince of the world has been sent out, and who are now not vessels of the Devil but members of Christ." Responding likewise to the chapters of the Gauls, he expressly approves the phrase that Christ died ONLY for believers, which those men condemn as Saracen. "Since, therefore," he says, "it is most rightly said that the Saviour was crucified for the redemption of the whole world, on account of the true assumption of human nature, and on account of the common ruin in the first man: yet it may be said that he was crucified ONLY for those to whom his death has profited. For the Evangelist says that Jesus 'was to die for the nation, and not for the nation only, but also that he might gather together into one the scattered children of God.'" So far Prosper.

units.la: Post orthodoxos Patres, Latinos præsertim, eandem doctrinam scholastici professi sunt: unâ duntaxat Thomæ sententiam recitabo. Meritum Christi, inquit, quatum ad SUFFICIENTIAM, æqualiter se habet ad omnes: non autem quantum ad EFFICACIAM: quod accidit, partim ex libero arbitrio, partim ex divina electione, per quam quibusdam misericorditer effectus meritorum Christi confertur: quibusdam verò justo Dei judicio subtrahitur. Hæc sunt Thomæ verba. Sed non addam plura, ne vidcamur humanis tantum autoritati-bus pugnare velle. Sunt aliæ rationes, quæ contra illorum morsus satis nos muniunt. Est enim dogma contrarium quod illi tuentur, non tantum S. sacræ è diametro repugnans, sed & instar agri vastati tribulos multos, h. e, absurda quàm plurima ex se procreat, & varie secum confli-git.
units.tr: After the orthodox Fathers, especially the Latin ones, the schoolmen also professed the same doctrine. I will recite the opinion of Thomas alone: "The merit of Christ," he says, "as regards SUFFICIENCY, stands equally related to all; but not as regards EFFICACY: which comes about partly from free will and partly from divine election, through which the effect of Christ's merits is conferred mercifully on some, but withheld from others by the just judgment of God." These are the words of Thomas. But I will add no more, lest we seem to wish to fight only with human authorities. There are other arguments which sufficiently fortify us against their attacks. For the opposing doctrine which they defend is not only flatly contrary to holy Scripture, but also, like a field laid waste, produces from itself many thorns, that is, very many absurdities, and conflicts with itself in various ways.

units.la: Contendunt, Christum pro omnibus etiam quoad efficaciam mortuum esse, hoc est, omnes & singulos tam incredulos quàm fideles, pariter & æquè Iudam ac Petrum, morte sua Deo reconciliasse, ab omni peccato & condemnatione liberasse: ita quidem ut omnes reipsa IN GRA-TIAM ET SINUM à Deo sint recepti, inque eo tantisper maneant, dum incredulitate rursus excidant, & se liberatione illa privent atque ita denuo, id est, bis pereant: non propter peccata, sed propter incredulitatem. Hoc ipsorum est dogma, & hæc ipsorum fere sunt verba, ne quis nos de calumnia suspectos habeat. Hoc inquam, dogma falsum & impium esse dicimus: quia Scripturæ sacræ repugnare manifestum est. Hæc enim solos, solos, inquam, credentes Deo Christi sanguine reconciliatos, justificatos, in sinu & gratia Dei constitutos, & ab æterna condemnatione liberatos esse constanter asserit. Quoties enim, quo-ties, quaso, Christus hoc clamat, & solis credentibus vitam æternam assignat? Hac est voluntas eius, qui misit me, ut omnis qui videt filium, & credit in eum, habeat vitam æternam: Id quod alibi iuramento affirmare non dubitat: Amen amen di-co vobis: qui sermonem meum audit, & credit in eum qui misit me, habet vitam æternam. Idem docet A-postolus: Justificati fide pacem habemus. Item: Nulla est condemnatio iis, qui sunt in Christo Iesu: Et Petrus in concione ad Cornelium. Huic om-nes prophetæ testimonium dant, remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen eius omnem qui credit in eum. De incredulis vero, quid pronunciet Scriptura jam ante audivistis: omnes nimirum exclu-dit à gratia & sinu Dei & à beneficiis Christi, atque æternæ morti adiudicat. Nam qui non credit, inquit Christus, jam condemnatus est, & ira Dei manet super eo, quia non credidit in nomen unigeniti filii Dei. Hæc fulgura non verba, si possunt sustineant, & concilient, cum suo impio thema-te, omnes omnes absque respectu fidei & infidelitatis à Deo IN GRATIAM ET SINUM receptos esse propter Christi mortem.
units.tr: They contend that Christ died for all even as regards efficacy, that is, that by his death he reconciled to God all and each, unbelievers as well as believers, Judas equally with Peter, and freed them from all sin and condemnation: so that indeed all are in fact received by God INTO GRACE AND HIS BOSOM, and remain there for a while, until by unbelief they fall away again and deprive themselves of that liberation, and so perish a second time, that is, twice: not because of sins, but because of unbelief. This is their doctrine, and these are nearly their own words, lest anyone think us guilty of calumny. This doctrine, I say, we declare to be false and impious, because it is manifestly opposed to holy Scripture. For Scripture constantly asserts that only, only, I say, those who believe are reconciled to God by the blood of Christ, justified, placed in the bosom and grace of God, and freed from eternal condemnation. For how often, I ask, does Christ proclaim this, and assign eternal life to believers alone? "This is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life." Which elsewhere he does not hesitate to affirm with an oath: "Amen, amen, I say to you: he who hears my word and believes in him who sent me has eternal life." The same is taught by the Apostle: "Justified by faith, we have peace." Likewise: "There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus." And Peter in his sermon to Cornelius: "To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him will receive forgiveness of sins through his name." But concerning unbelievers, what Scripture pronounces you have heard before: it certainly excludes them all from the grace and bosom of God and from the benefits of Christ, and adjudges them to eternal death. "For he who does not believe," says Christ, "is already condemned, and the wrath of God remains upon him, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God." These are not words but thunderbolts. Let them, if they can, sustain and reconcile with their impious thesis the claim that all, all without regard to faith or unbelief, have been received by God INTO GRACE AND HIS BOSOM on account of Christ's death.

units.la: Impium dixi: quia Scripturæ repugnat. Dico etiam absurdum: quia absurditatibus & contradictionibus scatet, seque ipsum elidit.
units.tr: I called it impious because it opposes Scripture. I also call it absurd, because it teems with absurdities and contradictions, and refutes itself.

units.la: Principio enim, omnia ea tollit & irrita facit, quæcunque vel Scriptura sacra vel orthodoxi Theologi de peccato & reatu originali tradunt, in quo omnes omnino homines concipiuntur & nascuntur. Cum enim Scriptura omnes natura filios iræ proclamet: illud contra OMNES IN GRATIA ET SINU DEI NASCI ET ESSE etiam antequam credant statuit, & liberationem à peccato & morte etiam sine fide incredulis largitur. Quid? quod reconciliationem, gratiam, li-num [?] Dei & omnes mortis & resurrectionis Christi fructus omnibus etiam Turcarum atque Eth-nicorum infantibus ante actualem incredulitatem morientibus vendicare cogitur, quo quid absurdius adstrui potest? Erit enim salus etiam extra Ecclesiam, & extra Christum: contra illud A-poftoli. Non est in alio quoquam salus: nec aliud nomen est sub cælo, quod datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos servari. Quod si infantes Turearum extra Ecclesiam in gratiam & in sinum Dei efficacia mortis Christi recepti sunt, & in eo nascuntur: quæ hæc est tam crudelis impudentia, infantes Christianorum ante Baptismum ex gratia & sinu illo Dei in Gehennam præcipitare? quod istos Briareos facere quis nescit? Quomodo igitur thesis ista aliud ipsorum dogma de infantibus fidelium extra gratiam nascentibus & ante Baptismum damnatis non evertit? Stante enim hoc ipsorum axiomate, omnes omninò homines in gratiam & sinum Dei etiam antequam credunt, receptos esse: cur infantes ante Baptismum ea gratia privant? Quod si per Baptismum demùm in gratiam & sinum Dei recipiuntur: quomodo morte Christi jam olim ante tot secula omnes & singulos in eam receptos esse profitentur?
units.tr: For first, it overturns and makes void everything that either holy Scripture or the orthodox theologians teach about sin and original guilt, in which all men without exception are conceived and born. For since Scripture proclaims that all are by nature children of wrath, this doctrine, on the contrary, establishes that ALL ARE BORN AND ARE IN GRACE AND THE BOSOM OF GOD even before they believe, and it grants freedom from sin and death even to unbelievers without faith. What then? It is forced to claim for the infants of the Turks and the heathen, who die before any actual unbelief, the reconciliation, the grace, the bosom of God, and all the fruits of Christ's death and resurrection: what could be asserted that is more absurd? For there will be salvation even outside the Church and outside Christ, contrary to the saying of the Apostle: "There is salvation in no other, nor is there any other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved." But if the infants of the Turks have been received outside the Church into grace and the bosom of God by the efficacy of Christ's death, and are born in it, what is this so cruel impudence, to hurl the infants of Christians, before baptism, out of that grace and bosom of God into Gehenna? Who does not know that these men are Briareus-like in doing so? How, then, does this thesis not overturn their other doctrine, about the infants of believers who are born outside grace and condemned before baptism? For if this axiom of theirs stands, that all men without exception are received into grace and the bosom of God even before they believe, why do they deprive infants of that grace before baptism? And if they are received into grace and the bosom of God only through baptism at last, how do they profess that all and each were received into it long ago, so many centuries before, by the death of Christ?

units.la: Statuit etiam hæc θέσις[?]: omnes ante Christū mortuos sine fide & damnatos, Christi morte rursus liberatos, Deo reconciliatos, in gratiam & sinum Dei receptos esse: atque ita denuò vel sine fide servatos vel sine incredulitate damnatos esse; quo quid absurdius? Fingit porrò incredulitatē vel non esse peccatum, vel certè efficaciā Christi fortiorem: quorum utrumque æquè est absurdū. Quid enim? an efficacia mortis Christi tàm impotens est, ut eos, quos semel (ut illis placet) in vitam asseruit, in eadem retinere nequeat? Hinc & absurdum aliud tanquam ex largo fonte ebullit, quo dogma hoc se ipsum elidit. Fingit enim nobis incredulos sine incredulitate, & fideles sine fide: dum ponit incredulos nondū adultos (qua[?]Iis sunt omnes ethnicorum infantes) vel etiam adultos barbaros, qui mortem Christi nunquam vel fando audiverunt, proinde nec actuali incredulitate spreverunt: ab omni peccato, etiam ab incredulitate (si modo incredulitatem peccatum esse sinunt) liberatos esse, ac tantisper in gratia & sinu Dei manere, dum incredulitate gratiam rursus abjiciant, atque ea propter denuo in æternum pereant.
units.tr: This thesis also holds that all who died before Christ without faith and were condemned were, by the death of Christ, afterwards freed, reconciled to God, and received into grace and the bosom of God; and so again they were saved without faith or condemned without unbelief. What could be more absurd? Moreover, he imagines that unbelief is either not a sin, or else that the efficacy of Christ is stronger than it; both of these are equally absurd. For what? Is the efficacy of Christ's death so weak that it cannot keep in life those whom, once (as they like to say), it has restored to life? From this there wells up another absurdity, as from a rich spring, by which this dogma destroys itself. For they make unbelievers without unbelief, and believers without faith: while they posit that unbelievers who are not yet adults (such are all the infants of the heathen), or even adult barbarians who have never heard of the death of Christ, and so have not actually scorned it in unbelief, are freed from every sin, even from unbelief (if indeed they allow that unbelief is a sin), and remain for a while in the grace and bosom of God, until by unbelief they cast grace away again, and on account of this perish anew for eternity.

units.la: Denique ne plura hujusmodi monstra enumerem, tribuit incredulis, quod, stante doctrina illa S.Sacræ de naturali reatu, nullo nunquam momento de iis prædicari possit, quod videlicet sint in gratia Dei. Nam ex sententia Scripturæ impii & increduli ab utero in sepulcrum usque, æternæ damnationis sunt rei: & ira Dei manet super eis: nec dari potest ullum temporis punctum, quo dici de iis queat, quod sint in gratia & sinu Dei. Mentiuntur ergo, qui contendunt omnes eos IN GRATIAM ET SINUM Dei receptos esse. Quis igitur nisi prorsus excæcatus non videt: dogma hoc, falsum, impium, absurdum, & ab Ecclesiæ limitibus procul arcendum atque exterminandum esse?
units.tr: Finally, not to list more monstrosities of this kind: they attribute to unbelievers what, given that doctrine of Holy Scripture concerning natural guilt, cannot at any moment be said of them, namely that they are in the grace of God. For according to the judgment of Scripture, the impious and unbelieving, from the womb to the grave, are liable to eternal damnation, and the wrath of God abides upon them; nor can any point of time be given at which it can be said of them that they are in the grace and bosom of God. Those therefore lie who contend that all of them have been received INTO THE GRACE AND BOSOM of God. Who then, unless he is utterly blinded, does not see that this dogma is false, impious, absurd, and to be kept far away from the bounds of the Church and driven out?

units.la: Sed videor hic mihi eos audire clamates: Promissionem[?] Evangelii esse universales: pertinere ad OMNES, OMNES: Nos vero toties eis regerimus: CREDENTES, CREDENTES. Sunt universales promissiones, sed respectu agentium pœnitentiam & credentium Evangelio. Atq; hic ad ipsam promissionum literam provocamus. Venite ad me o-MNES inquit Christus: sed addit, qui laboratis, & oneratis[?] tnerati[?] estis. Et alibi. Sic Deus dilexit mundum,ut Filium suum unigenitum daret, ut OMNIS qui CREDIT in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam. Sic Apostolus: Conclusit, inquit, Scriptura omnia sub peccatum, ut promissio ex fide Iesu Christi daretur CREDENTIBUS. Similis aliarum omnium promissionum Evangelii est ratio: Vel enim expressè, vel certè tacitè conditionem fidei ac poenitentiae annexam habent, nec possunt nisi de universitate fidelium citra blasphemiam intelligi.
units.tr: But I seem here to hear them crying out: the promises of the Gospel are universal; they pertain to ALL, ALL. We, however, repeat to them so often: BELIEVING, BELIEVING. There are universal promises, but with respect to those who repent and believe the Gospel. And here we appeal to the very letter of the promises. "Come to me, ALL," says Christ, "you who labour and are burdened." But he adds: "who labour and are burdened." And elsewhere: "God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, that ALL who BELIEVE in him should not perish, but have eternal life." So the Apostle: "Scripture," he says, "has concluded all things under sin, that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to THOSE WHO BELIEVE." The reasoning of all the other promises of the Gospel is similar: they either expressly, or certainly tacitly, have annexed to them the condition of faith and repentance, nor can they be understood, without blasphemy, of anything but the totality of believers.

units.la: Excipiunt: Sic statui promissiones particulares. Respondeat pro nobis author librorum de vocatione gentium sive is sit Ambrosius, cujus nomen praeferunt, sive Prosper quod nonnullis placere video. Habet, inquit, populus Dei plenitudinem suam, & quamvis magna pars hominum salvantis gratiam aut negligat aut repellat: in electis tamen & praescitis, atque ab omnium generalitate discretis SPECIALIS quaedam censetur UNIVERSITAS ut de toto mundo totus mundus liberatus, & de omnibus hominib. omnes homines videantur assumti.
units.tr: "They object": thus I establish particular promises. Let the author of the books on the calling of the Gentiles answer for us, whether he is Ambrose, whose name they bear, or Prosper, whom I see some are pleased with. "The people of God," he says, "has its fullness, and although a great part of men either neglect or reject the saving grace, yet among the elect and foreknown, and separated from the general mass of all, a certain SPECIAL UNIVERSALITY is reckoned, so that from the whole world the whole world is seen to be freed, and from all men all men seem to have been taken up."

units.la: Objiciunt deniq; ex Apostolo omnes in Christo vivificari: quemadmodum omnes in Adamo moriuntur. Atqui si absolutè omnes in Christo vivificari dicant, Scriptura & experientia eos refutabit. Hoc ergo dicit Apostolus, Christum omnibus suis conferre vitam, sicut Adam omnib. suis contulit mortem: Et ille quidem per gratiam, hic per naturalem propagationem. Atque hunc Pauli sensum esse, sequentia verba liquido probat. Cum n. omnes in Christo vivificari dixisset, statim subjungit: Unusquisque autem suo ordine: primitiæ Christus : postea qui sunt Christi, h. e, credentes, qui ipsi a patre dati sunt, & pro quibus patrem ardentissime oravit. Nec dissimiliter Au-gustinus interpretatur: ideo dictum esse, omnes in Christo vivificari, non quia omnes qui in Adamo moriuntur membra sint Christi: sed quia, sicut nemo corpore animali nisi in Adam moritur: ita nemo corpore spirituali, nisi in Christo vivificatur.
units.tr: Finally, they object from the Apostle that all are made alive in Christ, just as all die in Adam. But if they say absolutely that all are made alive in Christ, Scripture and experience will refute them. The Apostle therefore says this: that Christ bestows life on all his own, just as Adam bestowed death on all his own; and the former indeed through grace, the latter through natural propagation. And that this is the sense of Paul, the following words clearly prove. For when he had said that all are made alive in Christ, he at once adds: "But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, afterwards those who are Christ's", that is, the believers, who have been given to him by the Father, and for whom he most ardently prayed to the Father. Augustine interprets in no different way: it has been said that all are made alive in Christ, not because all who die in Adam are members of Christ, but because, just as no one dies in an animal body except in Adam, so no one is made alive in a spiritual body except in Christ.

units.la: Neque est, quod obstrepere pergant, hac ratione Adamum Christo fortiorem statui, si plures ille in exitium praecipitaverit, quàm hic servet, atque ex faucibus mortis eripiat. Potentia enim utriusque spectatur, non in numero eorum, qui moriuntur vel vivificantur: sed potius in modo, quo fit perditio & vivificatio: itemque in magnitudine bonorum amissorum & reparatorum spectatur. Citius enim atque facilius sexcentos homines perdas, de ponte praecipites, quam unum in integrum restituas: ex fluctib. & submersionis periculo liberes: illud Satanas, homines, bestiae; & res adversae omnes possunt: hoc in nullius creaturae quantumvis praestantis & excellentis potestate situm est: sed soli Deo rerum omnium creatori attribuendum. Fortior igitur mors Christi fuisset peccato Adami, si vel unicum hominem reparasset. Adde, quod bona illa, quae per Christum reparata sunt, tantùm praecellunt iis, quorum per Adamum jacturam fecimus, quantum terrenis & caducis rebus coelestia & aeterna praestant. Adam enim teste Paulo, est terrenus: Christus coelestis: ille animalis: hic spiritualis: ille ex terreno paradiso nos ejecit: hic in cœlestem collocavit, æternaq; felicitate donavit.
units.tr: Nor is there reason for them to keep clamouring that on this reasoning Adam is made stronger than Christ, if he has cast more into ruin than Christ saves and snatches from the jaws of death. For the power of each is judged not by the number of those who die or are made alive, but rather by the manner in which destruction and making alive take place, and likewise by the greatness of the goods lost and restored. For you can more quickly and more easily destroy six hundred men by throwing them headlong from a bridge than restore a single one entire, freeing him from the waves and the peril of drowning: the former Satan, men, beasts, and all adverse things can do; the latter lies in the power of no creature, however outstanding and excellent, but must be attributed to God alone, the Creator of all things. The death of Christ would therefore have been stronger than the sin of Adam, even if it had restored only a single man. Add that the good things which have been restored through Christ surpass by so much those things whose loss we suffered through Adam, as heavenly and eternal things surpass earthly and perishable ones. For Adam, according to the witness of Paul, is earthly; Christ is heavenly. The former is natural; the latter spiritual. The former cast us out of the earthly paradise; the latter has placed us in the heavenly one, and endowed us with eternal happiness.

units.la: Sed hîc jam vela contrahamus ac subsistamus. Longius enim quàm instituera[m] provecta est nostra oratio. Quapropter cum Christus verè tertia die ex morte resurrexerit, nec non omnia prophetarum oracula impleverit, nos fidem Christianam firmiter tenentes, hunc Iesum esse promissum Messiam & mundi Servatorem sciamus. Judæorum verò aliorumque hostium sarcasmos, ne unius assis æstimemus, risum Sardonium eos ridere certo certius statuentes. Cum propria potentia mortem superaverit, peccatum aboleverit, Diaboli imperium destruxerit: verum & omnipotentem Deum esse credamus. Mundus ergo, ut lubet tumultuetur, hostes fremant, tyranni in Ecclesiam sœviant: Christus iste rex hoster[?] ad dex-tram patris evectus dominatur in medio inimicorum suorum & gloriosè regnat. Hoc ergo vindice stabit Ecclesia contra mundi furores & inferorum portas: hanc ipse divina sua potentia armabit: hanc tandem ab omnibus hostibus vindicabit, hanc beneficiis promeritis, justitia sanctitate gloria & vita æterna ornabit. Cùm deniq; tanta sint beneficia resurrectionis ęaque dentur fidelibus tantùm & gratias Deo agentibus nos igitur gratis animis ea agnoscamus, fide nobis applicemus: peccato moriamur, in azymis sinceritatis & veritatis, h. e, in vero Dei timore, in vera dilectione Dei & proximi vivamus, atq; ita gloriosò capiti nostro Christo dignam, Decéque placentem vitam degamus. Æterno igitur Dei filio Domino nostro Jesu Christo toto pectore gratias agimus, quod propter peccata nostra tam diros cruciatus & terrores corpore & anima sustinuerit, seseque in tam contumeliosam mortem demiserit, ac propter justitiam nostram resurrexerit: in hujus conspectum nos supplices abjiciamus, huncardentibus votis & veris gemitibus oremus, ut nos vera & constanti fide donet, spiritu suo mentes nostras illuminet, corda regeneret, dirigat & confirmet ut in vita & in morte ipsum praedicare & celebrare nunquam desinamus: colligat & confervet sibi inter nos veram & aeternam Ecclesiam, quam justificet, vivificet, suscitet & glorificet: scholas foveat & puram Evangelii doctrinam indies magis ac magis accendat: confervet clementer haec halcyonia: pios magistratus & Doctores spiritu sapientiae & fortitudinis regat, gubernet & illuminet, ut sinceram doctrinam pro viribus tueantur, & ad posteros fideliter propagent ad laudem Sacrosancti nominis ipsius & multarum animarum salutem. Amen.
units.tr: But here let us now draw in our sails and stop. For our discourse has gone further than we intended. Therefore, since Christ truly rose from death on the third day, and also fulfilled all the oracles of the prophets, let us, firmly holding the Christian faith, know that this Jesus is the promised Messiah and Saviour of the world. As for the sneers of the Jews and of other enemies, let us not value them at a single farthing, being quite certain that they laugh a sardonic laugh. Since by his own power he has conquered death, abolished sin, and destroyed the empire of the Devil, let us believe him also to be true and almighty God. Let the world therefore rage as it pleases, let enemies roar, let tyrants rage against the Church: that Christ, the King, exalted to the right hand of the Father, rules in the midst of his enemies and reigns gloriously. Under this avenger therefore the Church will stand against the fury of the world and the gates of hell: he himself will arm her with his divine power; he will at last avenge her against all her enemies; he will adorn her with benefits won by merit, with righteousness, holiness, glory, and eternal life. Since then the benefits of the resurrection are so great, and are given only to believers and to those who give thanks to God, let us therefore acknowledge them with grateful minds, and apply them to ourselves by faith: let us die to sin, and live in the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, that is, in the true fear of God, in the true love of God and of neighbour; and thus let us lead a life worthy of our glorious head Christ and pleasing to God. To the eternal Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, therefore, we give thanks with all our heart, that for our sins he endured such dreadful torments and terrors in body and soul, and humbled himself to so shameful a death, and for our righteousness rose again. Let us cast ourselves as suppliants before his presence, and pray to him with ardent wishes and true groans, that he may grant us a true and steadfast faith, illumine our minds with his Spirit, regenerate, direct and strengthen our hearts, so that we may never cease to preach and celebrate him in life and in death; that he may gather and preserve for himself among us a true and eternal Church, which he may justify, quicken, raise up and glorify; that he may cherish the schools and kindle ever more and more daily the pure doctrine of the Gospel; that he may graciously preserve these halcyon days; that he may rule, govern and enlighten pious magistrates and Teachers with the Spirit of wisdom and strength, so that they may faithfully defend sound doctrine as far as they are able, and pass it on faithfully to posterity, to the praise of his most holy name and the salvation of many souls. Amen.

units.la: Gratias secundo loco quas possumus mentibus concipere, maximas agamus, illustrissimis Principibus ac Dominis: D. IOH. CASIMIRO Electoralis Palatinatus Tutori & Administratori prudentissimo & fortissimo: Domino item FRI-DERICO Electoralis Palatinatus haeredi dignissimo, Dominis ac Mœcenatibus nostris clementissimis; quod perturbatissimis hisce temporibus, quibus omnia nutare, adque interitum vergere videntur, quod, inquam illi inter tot tamq; graves Reipub.curas, inprimis tamen fidum Eccle-siarum & Scholarum patrocinium suscipiunt, eafquecontraRomani Antichristi furorem & tyrannidem variasque aliorum hostium machinationes CONSTANTER ET SINCERE defendunt; quodq; nullis omninò sumtib. parcentes fidelif-simos,omniq; disciplinarum genere instructiffi-mos Doctores, Professores & Præceptores libera liffimè fovent & sustentant, qui nos non tàm ad omnem pietatis cognitionem ac studiû excitent, quàm etiam ad varias hæreticorum præstigias & sophismata cavenda instruant ac muniant. Ora-mus toto pectore eúdem illum Iesum Christum, mortuum pro nobis ac resuscitatum ut hos nobis Patronos, laudatissimos Ecclesiæ nutritios diu salvos &incolumes clementer conservet,animos illorû indies magis ac magis amore doctrinæ cœ-lestis accendat, spiritu sap. & fortitudinis induat, Diaboli consilia irrita faciat, omnemq; potentiā sese adversus illos efferentem destruat, ut diu puram Evangelii doctrinam longè lateq; propaga-re & ad extremum usq; halitum oppuguare[?] quéant. Rogamus etiam eundem Dominum nostrû Iesum Christum,ut celeberrimam ACADEMIAM HEIDELBERGENSEM in tàm præstanti flore & honore, quo nunc eminet & conspicua est, quàm diutissimè conservare , piisque Doctô-ribus & Profesloribus[?] Spiritus sancti gratiam largiri dignetur , ut cunctis suis studiis , labo-ribus & consiliis sanctissimum ipsius nomen honoreac laudibus illustrent : & nos omnes ac singuli in cursu sanctæ vocationis magis ac magis proficiamus: donec aliquando tandem stadio hujus vitæ confecto ad beatam illam metam cœlestis gloriæ pertingamus. Gratias denique agimus Magn. D.Rectori, Generosis D.D.Baronib. Spectabili Decano cæterisque Professoribus clarissimis, & Præceptoribus nostris, reverendis & summa observantia colendis, nec non studiosis Juvenibus lectissimis, commilitonibus optimis, quòd partim gravissimis negotiis posthabitis partim studiis ardentissimis sepositis, huic nostræ balbutienti orationi interesse non fuerint dedi-gnati[?]: Nos vicissim omnibus ac singulis, quæcunque à nobis humanitatis officia proficisci queant polliceмur. Dixi.
units.tr: Secondly, we offer the greatest thanks we can conceive in our minds to the most illustrious princes and lords: to Lord JOHANN CASIMIR, guardian and most prudent and most brave administrator of the Electoral Palatinate; likewise to Lord FREDERICK, most worthy heir of the Electoral Palatinate, our lords and patrons most gracious. In these most troubled times, when all things seem to totter and tend towards ruin, they, I say, amid so many and so grave cares of the commonwealth, nevertheless take up above all the faithful patronage of the Churches and the schools, and defend them CONSTANTLY AND SINCERELY against the fury and tyranny of the Roman Antichrist and the various machinations of other enemies. Sparing no expense whatever, they most liberally cherish and support the most faithful teachers, professors and tutors, most well instructed in every kind of learning, who not only stir us up to all knowledge and zeal for piety, but also equip and fortify us to guard against the various deceits and sophisms of heretics. We pray with all our heart that the same Jesus Christ, who died for us and was raised again, would graciously preserve these our patrons, most praiseworthy nurturers of the Church, safe and sound for a long time; that he would kindle their minds more and more each day with love of heavenly doctrine, clothe them with the spirit of wisdom and courage, render the counsels of the Devil void, and destroy every power that raises itself against them, so that they may long be able to propagate the pure doctrine of the Gospel far and wide, and to defend it [oppuguare?] to the last breath. We also ask that the same our Lord Jesus Christ deign to preserve the most renowned UNIVERSITY OF HEIDELBERG in that excellent flower and honour with which it now stands out and is conspicuous, for as long as possible, and to grant the grace of the Holy Spirit to its pious teachers and professors, so that by all their studies, labours and counsels they may make his most holy name honoured and glorified; and that we all and each one of us may make more and more progress in the course of our holy calling, until at last, the race of this life being finished, we may reach that blessed goal of heavenly glory. Finally, we give thanks to the Magnificent Rector, the Noble Barons, the Respected Dean, and the other most distinguished Professors and our teachers, to be revered with the highest respect, and also to the most select young students and excellent fellow soldiers, that, having either set aside weightier business or laid aside their most eager studies, they have not disdained to attend this our stammering speech. In turn we promise to all and each one whatever acts of kindness may proceed from us. I have spoken.

units.la: ORATIO VIII. DE MORTE ET RESVR-RECTIONE CHRISTI, con-ferens oraculum Iesaiæ cap. 53. cum historia Evan-gelica,
units.tr: ORATION VIII. ON THE DEATH AND RESURRECTION OF CHRIST, comparing the oracle of Isaiah chapter 53 with the Gospel history,

units.la: Recitata ab ANDREA CELLARIO Pridie Paschatis, Anno 1592.
units.tr: Delivered by ANDREAS CELLARIUS, on the day before Easter, in the year 1592.

units.la: SOLENNEM beneficiorum mortis ac resur-rectionis Christi celebrationem in Ecclesia nostra & schola quotannis repetendam & con-servandam esse Auditores neminem equidem ex vobis dubitare existimo. Eam enim magno cum usu fructuque eximio nostro conjunctam esse, facile intelligunt omnes, qui & gloriam Servato-ris sui, & salutem propriam curæ habent. Augescit ac roboratur hinc fides nostra, qua indubi-tante assensione credimus, Iesum Nazarenum crucifixum ac mortuum propter peccata nostra, & suscitatum propter justificationem nostram, juxta Prophetarum oracula, verè Messiam illum esse, patribus à Deo promissum. Capit præterea[?] ex meditatione ista plurimum incrementi consolatio nostra : adversus peccatum, diabolum, mortem, ac mundum: quandoquidem hostes ipsos Christi morte devictos, resurrectione contritos esse, magno nostro commodo gaudioque recordamur.
units.tr: I do not think any of you, listeners, doubts that the solemn celebration of the benefits of Christ's death and resurrection is to be repeated and kept every year in our Church and school. For everyone who cares for the glory of his Saviour and for his own salvation readily understands that this celebration is joined to our great advantage and remarkable profit. Our faith is thereby increased and strengthened, by which we believe without any doubt that Jesus of Nazareth, crucified and dead for our sins and raised for our justification, according to the oracles of the Prophets, is truly that Messiah promised by God to the fathers. Moreover, our comfort gains very much from this meditation against sin, the devil, death and the world, since we remember with great benefit and joy that these enemies were overcome by Christ's death and crushed by his resurrection.

units.la: Porro quid suavius, quidve jucundius piis mentibus esse possit, quam cum Christo victore triumphum agere, ἐπινίκια[?] canere, spolia legere, trophæa statuere, denique eidem Christo victori pro parta salute gratias solennes agere? Quanta festivitate, quantoque gaudio, olim Ecclesia vetus memoriam liberationis suæ per Mosen ex servitute Ægypti anniversaria solennitate celebrârit, ex historia sacra notum est. Atqui tantò certè majori festivitate nobis celebranda esset recordatio liberationis per Christum, è servitute peccati & mortis, quantò majus & salutarius est hæc, quam illa fuit, beneficium: quantoque majorem laudem ac prædicationem meretur typi impletio, quam ipse umbratilis typus.
units.tr: Indeed, what could be sweeter or more pleasant to pious minds than to celebrate a triumph with Christ the victor, to sing songs of victory, to read the spoils, to set up trophies, and finally to offer solemn thanks to the same Christ, the victor, for the salvation won? From sacred history it is known with what festivity and what joy the ancient Church once celebrated, with a yearly solemnity, the memory of its liberation through Moses from slavery in Egypt. Yet surely we ought to celebrate the remembrance of liberation through Christ, from the slavery of sin and death, with much greater festivity, as much as this benefit is greater and more saving than that one was; and the fulfilment of the type deserves far greater praise and proclamation than the shadowy type itself.

units.la: Nec intercludere exultantem vocem debet, quod nobis non perinde ac Judæis certus ad effundendam hanc lætitiam dies imperatus & divino mandato constitutus est. Sequimur enim authoritatem mandati, quo divo Paulo referente, perpetua paschatis festivitas nobis Christianis indicitur. Sequimur etiam authoritatem Ecclesiæ Apostolicæ, quæ pro sua libertate jam olim certum tempus festivitati huic tribui voluit, & voluntatis hujus suæ causas gravissimas justissimasque habuit. Cultum quidem singularem in consuetudine ista ne-quaquam constituit, nec hoc spectavit, quasi aliis temporibus meditatio ista fieri non deberet: Sed potius ut recordatio spiritualis liberationis in nobis solenniter excitaretur, ut celebratio in mundi oculis esset conspectior, ut doctrina de Christi persona & beneficiis publice ex verbo Dei repeteretur & conservaretur, ut impletio typi & oraculorum solenniter ostenderetur, ut denique Ecclesia Christiana a Judaica sejungeretur: certo tempore Christianos omnes meditationibus illis publice occupari sanctissimo consilio decrevit. Hanc igi-tur consuetudinem quoniam origine probatissimam, usurpatione laudatissimam, moreque instituto majorum subnixam scimus, non abs re nos quoque ad locum hunc publicum frequentes confluximus, exemplo nostro ritum Ecclesiæ comprobaturi. Cæterum cum hucusque ea, quæ propter summam æquita-tem ex vobis probari, & mihi animum addere potuerint, confidenter & secure dixerim: jam vero huc mihi descendendum esse video, ut causam vobis reddam, cur ego vocem meam auditorio publico inferre ausus sim: vehementer equidem perturbor. Ita enim me hujus augustissimi concessus celebritas percellit, ita in solentia[?] loci amplissimi, in quo antea nunquam steti, confundit, ut an temeritatem deprecer, veniamque audaciæ petam: an tacitus de statione cedam, dubius & anxius hæream. Sed n.erigit[?] me trepidantem conscientia officii, quoniam non mea temeritate, sed eorum, quibus nec fas nec pium fuit refragari, authoritate huc locum conscendi. Vestra etiam me recreat benevolentia, qui scientes, vos non Demosthenem vel Ciceronem aliquem graviter perorantem, sed adolescentem balbutientem auditu-ros, frequentes tamen accessistis. Confirmat & æquanimitas vestra, quod in his exercitiis, non tam facultatem, quam conatum dicentium a vobis spectari, nec tam ut bene & ornate dicant, quam ut annitendo mediocriter dicere discant, requiri sciam. Deniq; in ipsa qualitate argumenti, quod libenter vos audituros spero, præsidium aliquod me habiturum confido. Collaturus enim sum celeberrimam illam Iesaiæ cap. 53. de humilitate, exaltatione, & beneficiis Messiæ prophetiam, cum historia Evangelica & rerum gestarum veritate. Concio est, ut scitis dulcissima, adeoque inter omnes alias non Iesaiæ tantum, sed reliquorum etiam prophetarum facile princeps. Eam Deus a propheta haberi voluit, ut populum in squalore exilii Babylonici miseræ se afflictantem consolaretur remissione gratuitæ & æternæ liberationis, expositio liberationis ejus authore ac modo. Promittit ergo Deus Messiam servum suum, quæ humile principio & abjectum futurum, sed mox ad summam gloriam evehendum, valdeq; exaltandum esse prædicit: Ecce, inquit, prosperabitur servus meus; extolletur & elevabitur & altus erit valde: & aspergent gentes multas: super eum claudent reges os suum, &c. Hic vero propheta eam populi cæcitatem fore conqueritur, ut oblatum salutis suæ authorem rem indignissimè abjecturi, divinorum vatum oraculis fidem derogaturi, & pro innata malitia gratiam salutarem in exitium sibi conversuri sint. Quis, inquit, credit auditui nostro: & brachium domini cui revelatum est? Mox tamen causam tanti stuporis exponens, ita eventurum ait, quia tantum ex aspectu & forma externa abjectissima Messiam æstimaturi, nec ad divinam, quam carne obvelatam gerit virtutem, divinaque beneficia per cum humano generi parata penetraturi sint. Ascender[?], inquit, ut surculus coram eo, & ut radix e terra deserta: Non forma ei, nec decor: Despectus & rejectus inter homines, vir dolorum, plenus infirmi-tatis: abscondimus faciem ab eo & nihil reputavimus eum. Tandem universam passionis, mortis, re-surrectionis, gloriæ ac regni Messiæ historiam, quasi in tabella vivis illustratam coloribus brevi-ter proponit. Ad causas etiam harum rerum nos deducit, & fructus ob oculos ponit, triplex scan-dalo remedium opponens: primum quod inno-cens ac sanctus ipse, nostrorum peccatorum rea-tum in se derivaturus, & nostrorum scelerum ex-piationi vitam suam impensurus sit mortemque oppetiturus. Sane, inquit, languores nostros ipse portavit: vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter peccata nostra: Castigatio pacis nostræ super eum: & in livore ejus sanatio nobis. Deinde quod ipse pater cœlestis, filium hoc modo sit contriturus propter peccata nostra: atque istam ejus pœnam in satisfactionem & justitiam impu-taturus credentibus, Jehova, inquit, sic voluit eum conterere: cumq; posuerit ille in sacrificium animam suam, videbit semen, prorogabit dies, & voluntas Domini in manu ejus prosperabitur: & notitia sui servus meus justus justificabit multos. Denique quod ex morte gloriosè sit resurrecturus Messias, Ecclesiam colleCturus, & regnum habiturus æternum. (Generationem ejus, inquit, quis enarrabit? & catera. Octingentis hæc annis ante Christum exhibitum (Nam quod Epiphanius 1600. annos inter hoc oraculum & Christi mortem numerat à veritate historiæ nimis remotum est) adeò aperte, & ad historiam Evangelicam congruè prædixit Iesaias, ut non prophetia sed rei gestæ narratio videatur, & verissimum sit illud, quod scriptum reliquit in prologo Hieronymus, evangelistam potius quam prophetam eum egisse. Cæterum quoniam in eam se amplitudinem luculentissima hæc prophetia diffundit ut temporis angustia persequi singula me non sinat, ex magno dicendorum acervo præcipua quædam, tempori huic & loco maxime accommodata deligam. Et principio quidem: quis sit ille servus Iehovæ, de quo Iesaias vaticinatur, ostendam. Tum quid de ejus humilitate & exaltatione dicat, expendam. Tandem ad causarum & fructuum utriusque considerationem descendens, nostræ singula quæ dixi utilitati accommodabo.
units.tr: Nor ought the rejoicing voice to be hindered by the fact that for us, unlike the Jews, no fixed day has been appointed by divine command for pouring out this joy. For we follow the authority of the command by which, as the divine Paul reports, a perpetual Passover festival is proclaimed to us Christians. We also follow the authority of the Apostolic Church, which for its own freedom long ago wished a set time to be assigned to this festival, and had most weighty and most just reasons for this its wish. Certainly it did not in this custom establish any special worship, nor did it look to this, as if this meditation ought not to be made at other times; but rather that the remembrance of spiritual liberation might be solemnly awakened in us, that the celebration might be more conspicuous in the eyes of the world, that the doctrine concerning the person and benefits of Christ might be publicly repeated and preserved from the Word of God, that the fulfilment of the type and of the oracles might be solemnly shown, and finally that the Christian Church might be separated from the Jewish; by a most holy counsel it decreed that at a set time all Christians should be publicly occupied with those meditations. Since we know this custom to be most approved in its origin, most praised in its practice, and supported by the institution handed down by our forebears, it is not without reason that we too have come together in large numbers to this public place, to confirm the rite of the Church by our example. However, since up to now I have been able to speak confidently and securely about those things which, by their great fairness, could be approved by you and could give me courage, now I see that I must come down to the point of giving you the reason why I have dared to bring my voice before this public audience: I am greatly disturbed. For the crowd of this most august assembly strikes me with such fear, and confuses me so much in the unfamiliar setting of this very large place, where I have never stood before, that I hang in doubt and anxiety whether I should beg pardon for my rashness and ask forgiveness for my boldness, or silently withdraw from my post. But the awareness of duty raises me up as I tremble, since I have climbed up here not by my own rashness, but by the authority of those whom it was neither right nor pious to oppose. Your goodwill also restores me, since you, knowing that you would hear not some Demosthenes or Cicero delivering a weighty oration, but a young man stammering, nevertheless came in large numbers. Your evenness of mind also strengthens me, since I know that in these exercises you look not so much at the skill of the speakers as at their effort, and require not so much that they speak well and elegantly as that by striving they learn to speak tolerably well. Finally, I trust that I shall have some support in the very nature of the subject, which I hope you will gladly hear. For I am about to compare that most famous prophecy of Isaiah chapter 53, concerning the humiliation, exaltation and benefits of the Messiah, with the Gospel history and the truth of the events. It is, as you know, a most sweet sermon, and therefore easily the foremost of all others, not only of Isaiah but of the other prophets as well. God willed it to be delivered through the prophet in order to console the people, who were miserably afflicted in the squalor of the Babylonian exile, with the promise of free and eternal liberation, and to set out the explanation of that liberation, its author and its manner. God therefore promises the Messiah, his servant, and foretells that he will be humble and abject at the beginning, but will soon be raised to the highest glory and greatly exalted: "Behold," he says, "my servant shall prosper; he shall be exalted and lifted up and shall be very high; and many nations shall be astonished at him; kings shall shut their mouths because of him," etc. Here, however, the prophet complains that such will be the blindness of the people that they will shamefully despise the author of salvation when he is offered, will withhold faith from the oracles of the divine seers, and, through their innate malice, will turn saving grace to their own destruction. "Who," he says, "has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?" Soon, however, setting out the cause of so great a wonder, he says that it will happen in this way: because they will judge the Messiah only from his outward appearance and most abject form, and will not penetrate to the divine power which he bears veiled in flesh, nor to the divine benefits prepared through him for the human race. "He shall grow up," he says, "like a sprout before him, and like a root out of dry ground; he has no form nor comeliness; he is despised and rejected among men, a man of sorrows, full of infirmity; we hid our faces from him, and we esteemed him as nothing." At last he briefly sets before us the whole history of the Messiah's passion, death, resurrection, glory and kingdom, as if illustrated with living colours on a tablet. He also leads us back to the causes of these things, and places the fruits before our eyes, setting against the stumbling-block a threefold remedy: first, that he himself, innocent and holy, will take upon himself the guilt of our sins and will devote his life to the expiation of our wickedness and will undergo death. "Surely," he says, "he has borne our sicknesses; he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins; the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his stripes we are healed." Second, that the heavenly Father himself will crush his Son in this way on account of our sins; and that he will reckon this punishment of his as satisfaction and righteousness to those who believe: "Jehovah," he says, "was pleased to crush him; and when he has made his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand; and my righteous servant, by his knowledge, shall justify many." Finally, that the Messiah will rise gloriously from death, will gather the Church, and will have an eternal kingdom: "Who shall declare his generation?" and the rest. Isaiah foretold these things eight hundred years before Christ was exhibited (for what Epiphanius counts as 1600 years between this oracle and the death of Christ is far too remote from the truth of history), so clearly and so agreeably with the Gospel history that the account seems to be not a prophecy but a narration of things done, and that saying of Jerome, written in his preface, is most true: that the evangelist rather than the prophet was at work there. Moreover, since this most brilliant prophecy spreads itself into such breadth that the shortness of time does not allow me to pursue each point, I shall choose from the great heap of things to be said certain outstanding ones, most suited to this time and place. And first, I shall show who that servant of Jehovah is of whom Isaiah prophesies. Then I shall weigh what he says about his humiliation and exaltation. Finally, descending to the consideration of the causes and fruits of both, I shall apply each of the things I have said to our own benefit.

units.la: Quem prophetain concione illa præclarif-sima servum Iehovæ intelligat, quoniam non est eadem omnium sententia, pedem nos in ipso li-mine figere oportet, & contra improbitatem recentiorum Iudæorum, fœdè oraculum corrum-pentium [?]pentium genuinum sensum tueri. Quidvis illi comminiscuntur, ut veritati quæ hac luce clarior est, tenebras offundant: Populum Israeliticum à Chaldæis & Romanis oppressum sunt qui intelligi velint: alii Prophetam de seipso verba fecisse autumant: quidem de Ezra nescio quid nugantur: nonnulli etiam Iesum Pontificem cujus in populo reduce celebris fuit authoritas & fama, nobis substituunt. Sed difficile est discernere, qui ex istis plus insaniant, omnes certe à manifesta veritate toto, quod ajunt, cœlo aberrant.
units.tr: Who the author takes the servant of Jehovah to be in that most famous discourse must be settled at the very start, since opinions on it are not all the same. We must stand firm on the threshold and defend the genuine sense of the oracle against the wickedness of recent Jews, who foully corrupt it. They invent all sorts of things to throw darkness over the truth, which is clearer than this light. Some want the servant to be the Israelite people oppressed by the Chaldeans and Romans; others claim the prophet spoke of himself; others babble some nonsense about Ezra; and some put in place of him Joshua the high priest, whose authority and fame among the people who returned was great. But it is hard to judge which of these is the more insane. All of them, at any rate, wander far, as they say, from the whole heaven of manifest truth.

units.la: De Messia enim summo Iehovæ servo: unico Servatore nostro, omnem illam prophetiam intelligi oportere, qui non plane infatuati sunt, libenter assentiuntur, qui negare audent, invictis rationibus validissime revincuntur. Primum nemini obscurum esse potest, qua occasione propheta in eum, quem habet, sermonem devenerit, quid in tota concione spectarit, quem ad scopum collimarit. Consolatur populum captivum spiritualis & æternæ liberationis promissione, liberationis inquam à peccato & à morte, spem facit reconciliationis cum Deo, justitiæ, & vitæ sempiternæ. Promissio ista totac tantorum beneficiorum, si quæra ex Iudæo, in quo rata sit, in quo fundamentum habeat: sit licet impudentissimus, & durissimi oris, nunquam certe Ezrâ, Iesum pontificem, aut alium hominem proferet sat scio, sed vel invitus fatebitur, Messiæ soli istud deferri, in quo solo omnes promissiones Dei sunt etiam & Amen. Deinde quo tandem pudore audent miseri & excæcati isti Judæi, nudi hominis nomen nobis obtrudere: cum attributa hujus servi Jehovę minime homini nudo, sed soli Messię θεανθρώπῳ[?] conveniant. Quis enim peccata nostra portare? morte sua expiare ac tollere? quis vibices nostras sanare? quis pacem cum Deo reddere, nisi solus Messias potuit? Quis vero hominum ab omni peccato & labe immunis fuit? quis notitia sui multos justificare valuit? Pontifex & rex Ecclesiæ vocari, intercedere & servare eandem potuit? Solus utiq; Messias potuit. Messiam ergo verum Deum verumq; hominem intelligit propheta servum Jehovæ, cui hæc omnia tribuit. Nec aliter sane veteres Hebraei, qui ætatem Christi brevi vel præcesserunt vel secuti sunt, prophetiam hanc intellexerunt, quorum testimonia recitare hic nil attinet: cum loco omnium nobis esse possit ac debeat Jonathan ille Vzielis filius, Hillelisque auditor, & Simeonis Justi, qui hunc servum Jehovæ, infantulum recens natum, ulnis excepit condiscipulus. Is inquam Jonathan in sua paraphrasi Chaldaica, expresse vocat hunc servum Jehovæ Messiam. Est autem hujus paraphrasis tanta apud Judæos omnes authoritas, ut ei non minus quam ipsi textui fidem adhibendam esse velint. Ac tamen etsi Evangelistarum & Apostolorum testimonium nullo loco Judæi habeant, apud nos tamen Christianos maximum meritissimo pondus obtinet, & vel solum aperiendo genuino prophetæ sensui potest sufficere. Quam ob rem de solo Christo oraculum accipimus, quoniam in eo solo, quæ prædixit Isaias, impleta fuisse, passim te-stantur. stantur sacri Novi Testamenti scriptores. Sic formam servi à Filio Dei assumptam scribit Paulus ad Phil. 2. Sic cur exiguus apud Iudæos tot tantorumque Christi miraculorum & doctrinæ fructus fuerit, cur credere in ipsum obstinati Iudæi noluerint, ex oraculo hoc aperit Iohannes in Evangelica historia cap. 12. & cur non omnes obediant Evangelio ad Rom. 10.
