Nunc cœlesti Spiritus Sancti robore armati, diversa faciunt omnia, nec abstistunt [?] prius, quam orbem universum, multis alioqui armis superabilem, igneo illo doctrinæ cœlestis flatu in fidem Christi adigant, quasique sub iugum mittant.
units.tr: Finally there is added, as it were, the protection (φυλακτήριον) of all, the confirmation and consolation of the saints. For since our Christian warfare is so full of very great calamities, of huge dangers and miseries, that it is by no means possible for us to hold our post without his help, he comforts us lest we succumb under the weight of evils; he strengthens the fearful, and so fortifies the timid and wavering that we not only boldly face whatever dangers there are in the world for the name of Christ, but also rejoice and triumph immensely even in tribulations themselves. For he is that sweet Paraclete promised to us, to remain with us for ever, not indeed idle (ἄχρεος), but pouring consolation into the souls of the faithful, surpassing all understanding, and very far removed from the masks of the world, which vanish at once in the struggle of temptations and leave embers instead of treasures to wretched men. Whereas, on the contrary, the pious, even when plunged into the very whirlpool of death, always enjoy true and solid consolation, exclaiming with the Apostle: "as dying, and behold we live; as chastened, and not killed; as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing all things." Do not believe these things, hearers, to be the boasting of a flatterer (Gnathonica μεγαλαυχία) nor some foolish paradox of the Stoics (Zenonicorum παραδοξολογία), but the unconquered strength of the saints breathed into them from heaven, by which they are crucified with the world and in turn crucify the world to themselves. For consider, I beg you, the apostles, who suddenly came forward with a new boldness (παρρησία) to teach, to defend the truth, and finally to suffer with the greatest eagerness and joy for the glory of Christ, they who before had been nothing more timid. They had fled at the mere sight of enemies, had denied Christ at the assault of a single weak woman, and for fear of the Jews had hidden themselves in the secret recesses of closed rooms. Now armed with the heavenly strength of the Holy Spirit, they do everything differently, nor do they desist until they bring the whole world, otherwise conquerable by many arms, under the faith of Christ by that fiery breath of heavenly doctrine, and, as it were, put it under the yoke.

units.la: Non denique, ut coronidis loco hoc addam, exiguum videri debet, quod tantam subito mentibus eorum πληροφορίαν [?] idem ille paracletus aspirat, ut abiecta omni hæsitatione, de Christi morte, suscitatione, gloria, universoque eius re[?]no,qua prius anxii & soliciti distinebantur, dubiiq; in omnes partes vacillabant, nunc in veritatis cognitione & professione stent plane ἀμετά-πτωτοι. Quid enim quaeso duorum illorum Emaunta proficiscentium querela: Sperabamus eum redempturum fuisse Israelem: aliud aiguit, quàm animum fluctuantem & dubitationibus miserè distractum? Huic verò opponentes gravissimam illam Petri apologeticam concionem, intelligemus sanctum illum paracletum esse, qui animis nostris quovis doctrinae vento, fluctuantibus dubitationes adimat, παρακλήτος[?] addat, denique quantum necesse est, nunquam non opituletur infirmitati nostrae, ut in fide radicati ac firmati, fiduciam & spem illam (ut cum Apostolo loquar) de qua gloriamur, ad finem usque firmam obti- neamus. Neque enim solis Apostolis à Domino fuit promissus, sed & nobis crediturisin ipsum, per verbum illorum. Alium paracletū dixit Christus, dabit vobis Pater, ut maneat vobiscum in aeternum. Gaudebit cor vestrum, & gaudium vestrum nemo tollet à vobis: Interpellat pro nobis, suspiriis inenarrabilibus: Est arrhabo etiā salutis nostrae, quo obsignavit nos Deus in cordibus nostris, dum in libertatem vindicemur, ad laudem gloriae ipsius. Quin igitur credimus, nos etiam ab eodem illo Spiritu veritatis duce, pro suo quoque modulo doceri, in homines novos regenerari, caelesti animorum robore fulciri & confirmari, ne unquam beata illa salutis spe excidamus. At cedo, nobis, inquiat aliquis, illam donorum caelestium Apostolicae Ecclesiae maiestatem, quae hodie nusquam apparet. Fateor:non esse nunc in nobis ita conspicuum, ut erat in illis Ecclesiæ primordiis. Quorsum verò nobis iam illa miraculosa dona, postquam nulla doctrinæ Evangelicæ, satis superque iam olim confirmatæ, inque omnes orbis partes divulga-tæ, nova obsignatione est opus? An ut dicatur nobis: Generatio hæc prava signum quærit? Miraculosis itaque donis utpote illius ætatis pro-priis, & quidem ad certum duntaxat temporis spatium tum duraturis, nobis hodie non est opus. Quæ verò singulorum vocationi sunt necessaria, ea non minus, quàm ipsis etiam Apostolis colla-ta semper fuisse, & hodie conferri à Deo: non modò omnium temporum experientia Ecclesiam docuit, sed Apostolus etiam prolixè cōfi:mavit[?]: hoc tantum discrimine accedente, quod non miraculo, ut olim, cœlitus illa in nos effundit Deus, sed studio, labore, institutione ac meditatione nostra comitante, Ecclesiæ ministros, doctores ac moderatores excitat, donis variis linguarum, interpretationis, prudentiæ, consolationis, facun-diæ, denique aliis alios exornat. Hæc inquam necessaria dona sunt in Ecclesia, sed non in omnibus eius membris. Non enim omnium eadem est vocatio, sed varia. Itaque pro diversitate functionum, varia etiam singulis dona distribuit, unus ille & idem Spiritus Dei, unicuique inquit Apostolus pro mensura donationis Christi, ad co-agmentationem Sanctorum, ad opus ministerii, ad ædificationem, inquam corporis Christi, do-nec evadamus omnes in unitatem fidei, & agni-tionis tionis filii Dei, in virum perfectum, ad mensuram adultæ ætatis Christi. Sunt denique alia etiam omnibus electis ad salutem necessaria dona, ut doceantur per vocem Evangelii, fide regenerentur, cum Christo capite in[?] corpus unum coalescant, ductu Spiritus gubernentur, consolatione firma in tentationibus suffulti confirmentur, ne deficiant, sed magis magisque in pietatis studio promoveant, ac pede inoffenso tandem salutis metam contingant. De his certissima promissio est apud Iacobum: Si cui deest sapientia, postulet à Deo, qui dat eam omnibus benignè, nec exprobrat, & dabitur ei: sed postulet cum fide nihil dissceptans. Et illa Christi promissio: Pater meus dabit Spiritum Sanctum petentibus: Minimè igitur cogitemus Auditores, nos ad ludos in vacuo theatro spectandos nunc convenisse, vel Penelopes historiam nobis recitari, dum illustria illa Spiritus Sancti dona in Apostolos miraculosè effusa grata memoria recolimus. Quin potius ex intimis cordis nostri penetralibus gratias agamus æterno Patri, cum Filio & Spiritu Sancto, pro summis & verè ineffabilibus beneficiis, quod præteritis toti in orbe gentibus ex mera sua misericordia se nobis patefecerit, & misso filio, suam de redemptione generis humani, voluntatem revelare nobis dignatus sit, & hanc sui suæque voluntatis revelationem, ad mirabili variorum donorum in Apostolos effusione, ceu arrhabone quodam confirmare & obsignare voluerit: Gratias, inquam, illi dies noctesque totis pectoribus agimus, pro infinita misericordia, & φιλανθρωπία[?], quod nos miseros peccatores, non dico terrae sed irae filios, fœdissimis peccatorum sordibus horribiliter defor-matos, non solum in gratiam receperit: verum etiam cum æterno Filio suo per Spiritum Sanctū tam arcte coniungit, ut perpetuo in nobis habitet, nosque membra Filii sui & templa Spiritus S. efficiat: cumque ingratitudine nostra vix unquam lacessere eum desinamus: tamen benignè semper ignoscat & opituletur infirmitati nostrae.
units.tr: Finally, so that I may add this as a crown to what has been said, it ought not to seem a small matter that the same Paraclete breathes into their minds such a sudden full assurance [πληροφορία], so that, having cast off all hesitation, they now stand firm and plainly unshakeable [ἀμετάπτωτοι] in the knowledge and confession of the truth concerning the death, resurrection and glory of Christ and His whole kingdom, whereas before they were anxious and troubled, distracted in every direction and wavering in doubt. For what, I ask, was the complaint of those two travelling to Emmaus: "We hoped that he would have redeemed Israel"? Does it say anything other than that their minds were fluctuating and miserably torn by doubts? Set against this, let us consider the very grave apologetic sermon of Peter, and we will understand that it is that holy Paraclete who removes doubts from our minds, which are tossed by every wind of doctrine, who adds encouragement [παράκλησις], and, as much as is needed, never ceases to come to the aid of our weakness, so that, rooted and established in faith, we may keep that confidence and hope (to speak with the Apostle) "of which we glory" firm to the end. For it was promised by the Lord not only to the Apostles but also to us, who are to believe in Him through their word. "Christ said: Another Paraclete, that the Father will give you, that He may abide with you for ever. Your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you." He intercedes for us "with groanings which cannot be uttered." He is also the pledge of our salvation, by which God has sealed us in our hearts while we are being set free, to the praise of His glory. Why then should we not believe that we too are taught by that same Spirit of truth as our leader, each in his own measure, that we are born anew as new men, and that we are strengthened and confirmed by the heavenly strength of our souls, so that we never fall away from that blessed hope of salvation? But, someone may say, "Show us that majesty of heavenly gifts which belonged to the Apostolic Church, which nowhere appears today." I admit that it is not so conspicuous in us now as it was in the first beginnings of the Church. But why do we now need those miraculous gifts, since there is no need of a new sealing of the Gospel doctrine, which was long ago confirmed more than sufficiently and has been spread into all parts of the world? Or is it so that someone may say to us: "This evil generation seeks a sign"? Miraculous gifts, therefore, being proper to that age, and indeed destined to last only for a certain span of time, are not needed by us today. But those gifts which are necessary for the calling of individuals have always been bestowed by God, no less than upon the Apostles themselves, and are bestowed today: not only has the experience of all ages taught the Church this, but the Apostle has also amply confirmed it. The only difference is that God does not pour these gifts from heaven upon us by a miracle, as formerly, but, accompanied by our zeal, labour, instruction and meditation, He raises up ministers, teachers and governors of the Church, and adorns some and others with various gifts: of tongues, of interpretation, of prudence, of consolation, of eloquence, and finally with other gifts. These, I say, are the gifts necessary in the Church, but not in all its members. For the calling of all is not the same, but varied. Therefore, according to the diversity of functions, the one and the same Spirit of God distributes various gifts to each one, as the Apostle says: "to each one according to the measure of the gift of Christ, for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ, until we all attain to the unity of faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ." There are also other gifts necessary for all the elect unto salvation: that they may be taught through the voice of the Gospel, be born again by faith, grow together into one body with Christ the head, be governed by the guidance of the Spirit, be upheld and confirmed by firm consolation in temptations, so that they do not fail, but advance more and more in the pursuit of godliness, and at last reach the goal of salvation with unhindered foot. Of these there is a most certain promise in James: "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it shall be given him; but let him ask in faith, with no doubting." And that promise of Christ: "My Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask." Therefore, hearers, let us by no means think that we have come together today to watch games in an empty theatre, or that the story of Penelope is being recited to us, while we gratefully recall the illustrious gifts of the Holy Spirit miraculously poured out upon the Apostles. Rather, from the inmost recesses of our hearts, let us give thanks to the eternal Father, with the Son and the Holy Spirit, for the highest and truly ineffable benefits: that, when all the nations of the world had been passed over, He revealed Himself to us out of His pure mercy, and, by sending His Son, was pleased to reveal to us His will concerning the redemption of mankind, and willed to confirm and seal this revelation of Himself and His will by the wonderful outpouring of various gifts upon the Apostles, as by a kind of pledge. Thanks, I say, we render with our whole hearts, day and night, for His infinite mercy and love of mankind, that He has not only received us wretched sinners, I will not say sons of the earth but sons of wrath, horribly deformed by the most foul filth of sins, into grace, but also joins us so closely to His eternal Son through the Holy Spirit that He dwells in us perpetually and makes us members of His Son and temples of the Holy Spirit; and although we scarcely ever cease to provoke Him by our ingratitude, yet He always pardons us kindly and comes to the aid of our weakness.

units.la: Oremus quoque supplices, ut Spiritus sui ductu & magisterio perpetuo nos regat, ne unquam tam ineffabilis beneficii oblivio nobis obrepat, sed grata memoria eius recordationem perpetuò foventes, ipsum celebremus, verisque gemitibus invocemus, ut pro sua bonitate non in nobis modò, tam saluti, quam singulorum vocationi necessaria dona Spiritus sui excitet, augeat & con-servet: Sed eadem effundat super omnem car-nem; hoc potissimum tristissimo seculo, ut multi ad agnitionem veritatis adducti, eandem perse-qui desinant. Hoc enim caput est hodie omnis mali in Ecclesia, quod vel Spiritus Sancti ductu procaciter fugiunt, quos maximè conveniebat hunc sequi: vel cruentissimos quosque carnis & livoris impetus, pro zelo gloriæ Dei venditant, qui scientes volentes per innocentum latera veritatem confodiunt, vel saltem ei tenebras offun-dere studeant, suum ipsi honorem quærentes, & sua idola adorantes. Petamus nos sanctificari in veritate, & robore Spiritus cœlestis sic confirmasi[?], ne impatientia victi, contra officium ruamus, neve spiritum, arrhabonem nostrum aliqua ratione contristemus: Ecclesiæ vulnera, concordiæ & pacis vinculo colligari: veritatis causa passim sub crucis mole suspirantium gemitus exaudiri: pios Ecclesiæ nutritios, Magistratus ac principes, & in his Illustrissimum nostrum Principem Dn. IOHANNEM CASIMIRUM, &c. veritatis cœlestis πνεύμαχον[?] constantem & syncerum Sancti Spiritus robore & consiliis patriæ ac Ecclesiæ salutaribus clementer instrui: ad laudem & gloriam æterni Dei, Patris, Filii & Spiritus Sancti, qui est unus verus & æternus Deus in secula, Amen.
units.tr: Let us also pray humbly that He would, by the perpetual guidance and teaching of His Spirit, rule us, so that the forgetting of so ineffable a benefit may never creep upon us, but that, constantly cherishing the grateful memory of it, we may celebrate Him and call upon Him with true groanings, that by His goodness He may stir up, increase and preserve in us not only the gifts of His Spirit necessary for salvation and for the calling of each one, but also pour the same out upon all flesh; this above all in this most sorrowful age, that many, being brought to the knowledge of the truth, may cease to persecute it. For this is today the head of all evil in the Church: that some boldly flee from the Spirit of the Holy Spirit whom they especially ought to follow, while others put forward the most bloody impulses of the flesh and of envy as zeal for the glory of God, who knowingly and willingly stab the truth through the sides of the innocent, or at least strive to cast darkness upon it, seeking their own honour and worshipping their own idols. Let us ask that we be sanctified in the truth and so strengthened by the power of the heavenly Spirit that, overcome by impatience, we do not rush against our duty, nor in any way grieve that Spirit, our pledge; that the wounds of the Church be bound together by the bond of concord and peace; that the groans of those everywhere sighing under the weight of the cross for the sake of the truth be heard; and that the godly nursing fathers of the Church, the magistrates and princes, and among them our most illustrious Prince, Lord John Casimir, etc., be mercifully instructed in the heavenly truth, constant and sincere, by the strength of the Holy Spirit and by counsels salutary to the fatherland and the Church: to the praise and glory of the eternal God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, who is one true and eternal God for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: ORATIO X. DE CAUSIS ET FRUCTIBUS MISSIONIS SPIRITUS Sancti in Pentecoste.
units.tr: ORATIO X. ON THE CAUSES AND FRUITS OF THE MISSION OF THE HOLY SPIRIT AT PENTECOST.

units.la: Recitata die Pentecostes anno 1594. Casparo Schallero Witebergensi.
units.tr: Delivered on the day of Pentecost in the year 1594. By Caspar Schaller of Wittenberg.

units.la: Tanta est operum ac beneficiorum Dei, cū-primis eorum, quibus sese illustrius & clarius generi humano patefecit, maiestas & amplitudo, ut meditationi eorum temporis & studii satis nunquam tribuere posse videamur, si vel maximè nos totos totiusque vitæ nostræ decursum huc impendamus, nedum si diem unum vel alterum in id incumbamus. Neque tamen ratione caret vetus illa, omniumque populorum, qui Christo nomen dederunt, observatione usuque comprobata consuetudo, ut tum statis temporibus certa quædam beneficia Dei anniversaria solennitate recolantur, tum verò dies hodiernus publicæ celebrationi miraculosæ effusionis Spiritus Sancti super Apostolos in Ecclesia tribuatur. Etenim hodie elapsis supra mille quingentis sexaginta annis & uno, Spiritus Sanctus instar venti ex alto ruentis, visibili linguarum dissectarum igneaignearum specie, non super paucos quosdam patriarchas & prophetas, nec modicè & obscurè ut olim sub veteri testamento: sed intimis cœli penetralibus reseratis & latissimè apertis, ingenti copia maximaque ubertate, illustri multisque testium myriadibus conspicuo miraculo, Ierolo-lymis Iudææ metropoli, prima Pentecostæ post Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum à mortuis suscitatum & ad cœlos evectum, super duodecim Apostolos totamque Apostolorum Ecclesiam, atque adeo super omnem carnem, iuxta Ioëlis prophetiam effusus prædicatur. Hoc tantum tâ-que incomparabile favoris atque clementiæ di-vinæ documentum, ne unquam animis nostris effluat, sed æternâ memoriâ inter nos vigeat, quotannis circa id tempus, quo olim à Deo edi-tum fuit, absque superstitione, bono ac laudabili instituto, eademque ratione in Ecclesia celebra-tur, qua ipse etiam Deus quondam certa quædam & præcipua beneficia sua certis quibusdam diebus festis anniversaria solennitate celebrari voluit. Ea quippe vis est temporis, ut eorum, quæ a-liquando secunda vel adversa nobis acciderunt memoriam efficacius reducat, & malorum quidé recordatione vulnus animi leviter curatum no-vo dolore & ægritudine plerumque renovet re-fricetque: bonorum verò consideratione quasi iterata fruitione pristinæ lætitiæ & voluptatis animos nostros suaviter perfundat. Illud verò etiam omni probatione certius & clarius est, magis per-cellere, fideliusq; & pertinacius in memoria præ-sertim iuventutis & populi hærere, quæ certis diebus bus festis, publicisque ac solennibus Ecclesiæ conventibus, uno omnium consensu celebrantur, quam quæ tacitis cogitationibus, privatisve sermonibus aliàs ab aliis seorsum ponderantur. Quæ cum ita sint, nostrum est, qui in scholis doctrinæ cœlestis versamur, cum votis Ecclesiæ vota nostra coniungere & una cum ea hunc diem repetendæ ac celebrandæ memoriæ Spiritus Sancti mirabiliter quondam effusi gratis mentibus lætisque vocibus impendere. In primis enim ad nostrum ordinem pertinet nostrisque studiis maximè consentanea est, diligens & assidua patefactionum Dei meditatio eiusque beneficiorum grata agnitio & prædictio: cum scholæ Theologorum sint esseque debeant φυλακτήρια mysteriorum Dei & eorundem fortissima propugnacula, oppositá fraudibus & machinis impiæ hæreticorum aliorumque malè feriatorum hominum turmæ, quæ in eo uno est tota, ut arcem cœlestis veritatis diruat, funditusque evertat. Hanc repellere, hanc spirituali gladio verbi Dei conficere eorum est, qui peculiariter cognitioni rerum divinarum consecrati sunt. Taceo iam quod fine accuratiore & frequentiore doctrinæ cœlestis consideratione ad alios quoque olim in saluberrimis religionis Christianæ dogmatibus instituendos nos præparare difficulter possumus. Recte enim Siracides: Antequam loquaris, disce, inquit. Et vulgare proverbium est: [illegible, ~20 letters]. Quæ duo nonnihil vereor ne & mihi huc loco concedere auso merito nunc obiici possint. Negare.n. nō polsū, qn mihi, si nō ante de his rebus, de qb[?] ex hoc loco dicere iussus sum, loquendū esset, q exacte eas perdidicissem, silentio perpetuo consenescendū foret. Caeterū benignitate & humanitate vestra fretus iudici orū aleam de me nō nimiū nunc pertimescā, sed veniam potius audaciæ mex[?], (si qua est) de vobis facilem mihi promitto. Neque.n. ideo ad dicendū prodeo authoritatem præceptorū meorū secutus, quò vos erudiā: quin potius res prius & melius vobis quā mihi cognitas folūmodo annitar ut in memoriam vobis revocē & plura atque maiora exinde meditandi occasione præbeam. Qua de causa nec totā doctrinā de persona & officio Spiritus S. quā sæpe ante me alii copiosiori ac politiori stylo tractarūt, repetā: sed duo tantū capita de miranda illa Spiritus S. missione explicabo. Vnū erit de causis propter quas Spiritū S. illustri miraculo in Ecclesia N.T. effundi necesse fuerit. Alterū maximos & dulcissimos fructus cōplectetur, q nō solū in Apostolos, sed in universā Ecclesiā inde ppetuo[?] redūdarūt.
units.tr: So great is the majesty and magnitude of God's works and benefits, especially of those by which he revealed himself to the human race more brightly and clearly, that we can never seem to devote enough time and study to their meditation, even if we were to give ourselves wholly, and the whole course of our life, to it, let alone if we only applied ourselves to it for a day or two. Yet that ancient custom, approved by the observance and practice of all peoples who have given their name to Christ, is not without reason: that certain benefits of God are commemorated each year with a solemn festival at fixed times, and that this present day is set aside for the public celebration of the wondrous outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles in the Church. For today, more than fifteen hundred and sixty-one years having passed, the Holy Spirit, like a wind rushing down from on high, in the visible form of tongues divided as of fire, was poured out, not upon a few patriarchs and prophets, nor sparingly and obscurely as of old under the Old Testament, but with the heavens' inmost recesses opened wide, in great abundance and the greatest plenty, in a famous miracle witnessed by many myriads of witnesses, at Jerusalem, the metropolis of Judea, on the first day of Pentecost after our Lord Jesus Christ had been raised from the dead and taken up to heaven: upon the twelve Apostles and the whole Church of the Apostles, and indeed upon all flesh, according to the prophecy of Joel. This so great and incomparable proof of divine favour and clemency must never slip from our minds, but must flourish among us in eternal memory. Each year, about the time when it was once done by God, it is celebrated in the Church, without superstition, as a good and laudable institution, and in the same manner in which God himself once wished certain of his particular benefits to be solemnly commemorated each year on certain festal days. Indeed, such is the power of time that it more effectively brings back to memory those things which at some time befell us, whether fortunate or adverse; and by recalling evils it often reopens and irritates a wound of the mind that had been lightly healed, with fresh pain and sorrow; but by considering good things, it gently bathes our minds, as if by a renewed enjoyment, in the former joy and delight. It is also more certain and clearer than any proof that those things which are celebrated on fixed festal days, in public and solemn assemblies of the Church with the common consent of all, penetrate more deeply and cling more faithfully and tenaciously in the memory, especially of youth and of the people, than those things which are otherwise weighed by each person apart in silent thoughts or private conversations. Since this is so, it is our task, who live among the schools of heavenly doctrine, to join our prayers to the prayers of the Church, and together with it to devote this day to the repeated and solemn remembrance of the Holy Spirit's wondrous outpouring, with grateful minds and joyful voices. For it belongs first of all to our calling, and is most in keeping with our studies, to meditate diligently and assiduously upon God's revelations, and to acknowledge and proclaim gratefully his benefits; since the schools of theologians are and ought to be the guardians of God's mysteries and their most stout bulwarks, set against the frauds and devices of the impious heretics and of the other ill-disposed men, whose whole aim lies in this one thing: to tear down and utterly overthrow the citadel of heavenly truth. To repel this, to overcome it with the spiritual sword of God's word, is the task of those who are especially consecrated to the knowledge of divine things. I say nothing yet of the fact that without a more careful and frequent consideration of heavenly doctrine we can hardly prepare ourselves to teach others in the most wholesome dogmas of the Christian religion. For Ben Sira rightly says: Before you speak, learn, he says. And there is a common proverb: [illegible, about twenty letters]. I fear somewhat that these two points may now rightly be raised against me, who have presumed to take this place. For I cannot deny that, if I had not first been ordered to speak of these matters, on which I am now ordered to speak from this place, I would have had to grow old in perpetual silence, unless I had learned them thoroughly. However, trusting in your kindness and humanity, I do not now greatly fear the hazard of your judgment concerning me; rather I promise myself an easy pardon from you for my boldness, if there is any. For I do not come forward to speak because I follow the authority of my teachers, in order to instruct you; rather I shall strive merely to recall to your memory things which are known to you earlier and better than to me, and from them to give you more and greater occasion for meditation. For this reason I shall not repeat the whole doctrine concerning the person and office of the Holy Spirit, which many others before me have often treated more fully and in a more polished style; rather I shall explain only two heads concerning that wondrous mission of the Holy Spirit. The first will be on the causes for which it was necessary that the Holy Spirit be poured out in the Church of the New Testament by a famous miracle. The second will embrace the greatest and sweetest fruits, which have flowed from it not only to the Apostles but to the whole Church, continually.

units.la: Neminē vero opinor esse, quin videat, quam non temerè cōsideretur, cur tam insueto planeq; admirādo modo Deus suis fidelibus initio Novi Testamenti Spiritū suū impertiri voluerit. Necesse [?]ariis.n. causis eventus ostēsis, demōstratur certitudo evētus. Vbi itaq; intellexerimus hoc divinū miraculū ob causas partim immutabiles, partim gravissimas non potuisse non fieri, utique & fides nostra tam immotis argumentis firmata magis confirmet. Idipsum vero ad fructus huius beneficii rectius & plenius intelligendos magnopere conducet, ut suo loco cum de his dicetur, patebit.
units.tr: Indeed, I think there is no one who does not see how carefully this must be considered: why God wished to impart his Spirit to his faithful at the beginning of the New Testament in such an unusual and altogether admirable manner. For when the causes of an event are shown, the certainty of the event is demonstrated. When we therefore understand that this divine miracle could not but happen, for causes partly unchangeable and partly most weighty, our faith, so strengthened by such firm arguments, will be confirmed all the more. This very thing will greatly help us to understand the fruits of this benefit more rightly and fully, as will become clear in its place when we speak of them.

units.la: Occurrunt autem inter causas primum oracu-la plurimis seculis ante per prophetas de Spiritus Sancti super Apostolos & universam Ecclesiam in regno Christi effusione, edita: Quæ non minus quam alia de morte, resurrectione, glorificatione & beneficiis Messiæ implenda fuisse extra controversiam esse debet. Sine hoc enim alia omnia divinæ gratiæ beneficia irrita sortita fuissent exitum nec quicquam Ecclesiæ profuissent, cum teste Apostolo nemo posset dicere Iesum dominum nisi per Spiritum Sanctum, neque quisquam fit Christi membrum qui Spiritum eius non habet. Audiamus ergo Iehovam apud Iesaiam sic loquentem: Ne timeas serve mi Iacob & ô rectè quem elegi: Quia effundam aquas super sitientem & fluenta super aridam: effundam Spiritum meum super semen tuum & benedictionem meam super germina tua. Hic Deum non de universali duntaxat gratia, qua omnia vivificantur, foventur & vegetantur; nec de vitali tantum Spiritu seu vigore, quem Deus omnibus creaturis ut conservari possint inspirat, & de quo Psal. 104. dicit psaltes; Emittes Spiritum tuum & creabuntur & renovabis faciem terræ: Sed de Spiritu gratiæ & copiosa eius effusione in regno Messiæ loqui, palam est. Est enim oraculum hoc promissio minime obscura de gratia Novi Testamenti, in quo Deus Ecclesiam magna donorum spiritualium affluentia ornaturus, eiusque vires iam pene deficientes illis, quarum propheta meminit, aquis refecturus atque ipsam omni cœlesti benedictione prosecuturus sit, id quod non so-lum ex lum ex scopo illius concionis est manifestum, sed etiam ex verbo effundendi liquet, quod non significat secreto quodam modo instillare sed notat evidentem copiam elargiri, ideoque frequentis-simè de futura illa Spiritus Sancti copiosa elargi-tione in Pentecoste à prophetis usurpatum occurrit. Quin etiam per aquas non semel alibi Spiritus Sanctus, instar aquæ purgans & vegetans corda nostra per fidem, intelligendus venit, ut in illo apud eundem prophetam: Omnes sitientes venite ad aquas, &c. Ubi invitat Deus omnes ad Spiritus sui gratiam accipiendam. Et apud Ezechielem per aquas è templo manantes similiter spiritualium donorum abundantia denotatur futura in nova Ecclesia, cuius typus erat templum. Accedit denique omni exceptione maior inter-pres ipse Christus, qui ad illud Iesaiæ & ad similia aliorum prophetarum oracula respiciens: Qui, inquit, credit in me, sicut scriptura dixit, flumina aquæ vivæ fluent ex ventre eius. Cuius dicti sensum Evangelista indicans, subiicit, hoc Christum dixisse de spiritu quem accepturi erant credentes in eum. Quare illustris est hæc de miraculosa Spiritus Sancti effusione, Esaiæ prophetia.
units.tr: Among the causes, the first that presents itself is the oracles, uttered many ages before by the prophets, concerning the outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles and the whole Church in the kingdom of Christ. These must be beyond controversy to have been fulfilled no less than the others concerning the death, resurrection, glorification and benefits of the Messiah. For without this, all the other benefits of divine grace would have come to nothing and profited the Church nothing, since, as the Apostle witnesses, no one can say that Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit, and no one becomes a member of Christ who does not have his Spirit. Let us therefore hear Jehovah speaking thus through Isaiah: Fear not, my servant Jacob, and you, Jeshurun whom I have chosen: For I will pour water upon the thirsty and streams upon the dry ground: I will pour out my Spirit upon your seed and my blessing upon your offspring. Here it is plain that God speaks not merely of the universal grace by which all things are quickened, cherished and invigorated, nor only of the vital Spirit or power which God breathes into all creatures that they may be preserved, and of which the psalmist says in Psalm 104: You send forth your Spirit, and they are created, and you renew the face of the earth; but of the Spirit of grace and his abundant outpouring in the kingdom of the Messiah. For this oracle is a promise by no means obscure concerning the grace of the New Testament, in which God, about to adorn the Church with a great abundance of spiritual gifts, and about to refresh its powers, now almost failing, with those waters of which the prophet speaks, will bless it with every heavenly benediction; and this is clear not only from the purpose of that passage, but also from the word to pour out, which does not signify to instil in some secret way but denotes the bestowing of an evident abundance; and therefore it is found very frequently in the prophets, used of that future copious bestowal of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost. Indeed, elsewhere too, not once, the Holy Spirit is to be understood under the figure of waters, cleansing and quickening our hearts through faith, as in that passage of the same prophet: All who thirst, come to the waters, etc. There God invites all to receive the grace of his Spirit. And in Ezekiel, the waters flowing from the temple likewise denote the abundance of spiritual gifts to come in the new Church, of which the temple was the type. Finally, Christ himself, the interpreter beyond all exception, adds his weight, looking back to that passage of Isaiah and to similar oracles of the other prophets: He who believes in me, he says, as the Scripture has said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. The Evangelist, indicating the sense of this saying, adds that Christ said this of the Spirit which those who believed in him were to receive. Therefore this prophecy of Isaiah concerning the miraculous outpouring of the Holy Spirit is clear and famous.

units.la: Huic accedit illud Ezechiel. 36. Effundam super vos aquam mundam & mundabimini: ab omnibus inquinamentis vestris & ab universis idolis vestris mundabo vos. Daboq; vobis cor novum & Spiritum novum dabo in medio vestri, & auferam cor lapideum è carne vestra, daboq; vobis cor carneum.
units.tr: To this is added that passage from Ezekiel 36: I will pour out clean water upon you, and you shall be clean: from all your filthiness and from all your idols I will cleanse you. And I will give you a new heart and a new spirit I will put within you, and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.

units.la: Promissio insignis de largiter effundendo Spiri-tu Sancto. Est enim totus iste locus Evangelica concio de regeneratione & instauratione Ecclesiae tempore novi Testamenti per singularem Spiritus Sancti efficaciam. Penes ipsum enim solum est mundare nos a sordibus peccatorum, & corda nostra lapidea in carnea convertere, teste Apostolo, ubi quasi huc alludens vocat Corinthios Epistolam Christi scriptam non atramento sed Spiritu Dei vivi in carneis tabulis cordis eorum.
units.tr: A remarkable promise of the copious outpouring of the Holy Spirit. For this whole passage is an evangelical proclamation of the regeneration and renewal of the Church in the time of the New Testament, through the singular efficacy of the Holy Spirit. For it lies in his power alone to cleanse us from the filth of sins and to change our stony hearts into fleshly ones, as the Apostle bears witness, where, as if alluding to this, he calls the Corinthians an epistle of Christ written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, on the fleshly tablets of their hearts.

units.la: Rursus Ezech.39. Non abscondam, inquit De’, ultra faciem meam ab eis, quia effudi Spiritum meum super domum Israel. Quin & hoc oraculum eodem spectet ac promissio fit de futura Spiritus Sancti effusione, dubitandi ratio non est. Effudi enim pro effundam notissimo Hebraismo dicitur. Per Spiritum vero haudquaquam Spiritum furoris seu θυμόν[?], ut Graeci interpretes reddiderunt, sed Spiritum gratiae intelligit. Nam erigit Deus eo loci fideles certa spe perpetuae conservationis & protectionis Ecclesiae, eiusque speciosae renovationis, magna multitudine electorum ad fidem & resipiscentiam potentiorem Spiritus Sancti adducta. Quod ipsum Chaldaeus Paraphrastes observans diserte addidit: Effundam Spiritum Sanctum meum.
units.tr: Again, Ezekiel 39: I will not hide my face from them any longer, says God, because I have poured out my Spirit upon the house of Israel. Indeed, there is no reason to doubt that this oracle also looks to the same thing as the promise of the future outpouring of the Holy Spirit. For I have poured out is said in place of I will pour out, by a very well-known Hebraism. But by the Spirit he does not mean at all the Spirit of wrath or θυμόν [?], as the Greek translators rendered it, but he means the Spirit of grace. For God there raises up the faithful with a sure hope of the perpetual preservation and protection of the Church, and of its splendid renewal, with a great multitude of the elect being brought to faith and repentance by the more powerful Spirit of the Holy Spirit. The Chaldee paraphrast, observing this very thing, expressly added: I will pour out my Holy Spirit.

units.la: Venio ad celebre illud vaticinium Ioelis, quo Deus, Posthac, inquit, erit: effundam Spiritum meum super omnem carnem & prophetabunt filii vestri & filiae vestrae: senes vestri somnia somniabunt, iuvenes vestri visiones videbunt. Quin & super servos meos & super ancillas effundam Spiritum meum. Hanc prophetiam evidentissimam, interque omnes huius generis alias instar clarissimi sideris fulgentem ipse Petrus Apostolus allegavit in Penteco-ste, eamque miraculo tum facto impletam esse ad versus calumnias improborum firmis argumen-tis demonstravit.
units.tr: I come to that famous prophecy of Joel, in which God says: Afterward, he says, it shall be: I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy; your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions. Moreover, upon my menservants and upon my maidservants I will pour out my Spirit. Peter the Apostle himself cited this most evident prophecy, shining among all others of this kind like the brightest star, on the day of Pentecost, and with firm arguments he showed against the slanders of the wicked that it was fulfilled by the miracle then performed.

units.la: Nec minus illustris est illa de eodem beneficio prophetia apud Zach. cap. 12. Effundam super domum David & super habitatores Jerusalaim[?] Spiri-tum gratiæ & precum. Argumentum pro applicatione huius oraculi ad effusionem Spiritus Sanc-ti in Pentecoste, ex eo petitur, quod constanter scriptura de larga illa donorum spiritualium in novam Ecclesiam collatione loquens, effusionis verbum usurpat. Miro enim consensu & Esaiam & Ezechielem & Ioëlem paulo ante & nunc Zachariam illo uti vidimus. Unde absurdum non est colligere quoties à Deo Spiritus effundendus promittitur, copiosam hanc in Apostolos & novam Ecclesiam Spiritus Sancti effusionem promitti. Idem ex scopo præsentis loci fit manifestum. Cum enim propheta in antecedentibus peccata populi sui graviter taxasset & pœnas non resipiscentibus denunciasset, subiicit tandem consolationem piorum: Quamvis ab hostibus Ecclesia sit affligenda, variisque calamitatibus exercenda: Deum tamen illorum conatibus tandem clausis atque ipsis iusto iudicio punitis, suos non modo conservaturum: sed etiam gratia copiosiore prosecuturum & Spiritus Sancti donis, præsertim vera resipiscentia & precum ardore quibus ira Dei & pœnæ procul arcentur, donaturum esse.
units.tr: No less remarkable is that prophecy of the same benefit in Zechariah 12: I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem the Spirit of grace and of supplications. The argument for applying this oracle to the outpouring of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost is drawn from the fact that Scripture, consistently speaking of that abundant bestowal of spiritual gifts upon the new Church, uses the word outpouring. For with remarkable agreement we have seen Isaiah and Ezekiel and Joel a little earlier, and now Zechariah, use this language. Hence it is not absurd to conclude that whenever God promises that the Spirit shall be poured out, this abundant outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles and the new Church is promised. The same becomes evident from the purpose of the present passage. For since the prophet, in the preceding verses, had sharply rebuked the sins of his people and announced punishments to those who did not repent, he finally adds the consolation of the godly: although the Church is to be afflicted by enemies and exercised by various calamities, God will not only preserve his own, when the efforts of those enemies have at last been checked and they themselves punished by his just judgment, but will also bless them with a more abundant grace and bestow on them the gifts of the Holy Spirit, especially true repentance and the fervour of prayer, by which the wrath of God and punishments are kept far away.

units.la: Atq; hæc sunt veterum prophetarum de hoc miraculo vaticinia, quibus quid vetat, quin ora-culum quoque Iohannis Baptistæ, qui ut veteres prophetias clausit, ita novi testamenti primus præco fuit, adiiciamus? Sic igitur ille: Ego quidem, inquit, baptizo vos aqua ad resipiscentiam: is vero qui pone me venit validior me est, cuius non sum dignus qui soleam portem, ipse vos baptizabit Spiritu Sancto & igni. Etsi autem Baptista hoc dicto inter suum & Christi in eodem baptismo conferendo officium proprie discernat, sibi quidem externam tantum administrationem aquæ relinquens: Christo vero internas partes sui baptismi ablu-tionem à peccatis & regenerationem per Spiritum Sanctum assignans: simul tamen quid Christus in cœlum exaltatus Ecclesiæ suæ collaturus esset in Pentecoste, prophetico spiritu indicat, visibilem & miraculosam Spiritus Sancti effusionem prænuncians. Est enim Christus utriusque beneficii author, utroque modo baptizans Ec-clesiam Spiritu Sancto, invisibiliter nimirum in baptismo aquæ & visibiliter in baptismo ignis. Neque est dubium utrumque in Ecclesia Apostolica piis collatum & obsignatum fuisse per baptismum. Hac ergo de causa Iohannes utrumque baptismum Spiritus appellavit & baptismum ignis addidit, proculdubio ad symbolum ignea-rum linguarum, quæ in Apostolis Spiritu Sancto copiose donatis, dissectæ visebantur, respiciens.
units.tr: And these are the prophecies of the ancient prophets concerning this miracle. What prevents us from adding also the oracle of John the Baptist, who, as he closed the ancient prophecies, so was the first herald of the New Testament? Thus he speaks: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance; but he who comes after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to bear; he himself will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire. Although the Baptist, in this saying, properly distinguishes his own office from that of Christ in administering the same baptism, leaving to himself only the external administration of water, but assigning to Christ the inward parts of his baptism, namely the washing away of sins and regeneration through the Holy Spirit, nevertheless at the same time, by prophetic spirit, he indicates what Christ, exalted into heaven, was going to bestow upon his Church at Pentecost, foretelling a visible and miraculous outpouring of the Holy Spirit. For Christ is the author of both benefits, baptizing the Church in both ways with the Holy Spirit: invisibly, of course, in the baptism of water, and visibly in the baptism of fire. Nor is there any doubt that both were bestowed upon and sealed to the pious in the Apostolic Church through baptism. For this reason John called both baptisms of the Spirit, and added the baptism of fire, undoubtedly looking to the symbol of the fiery tongues which were seen dividing themselves over the Apostles, who had been richly endowed with the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Hactenus oraculis variis prophetarum præ-nunciatam proindeque necessario tandem Ec-clesiæ præstitam esse largam Spiritus Sancti dona-tionem satis confirmatum esse puto. Ad oracula porrò prophetarum variæ de eodem beneficio ipsius Christi Servatoris promissiones accedunt, quarum veritatem eventu tandem comprobari non minus necesse fuit. Ego, inquit Christus ad Apostolos, patrem rogabo & alium consolatorem, dabit vobis ut maneat vobiscum in æternum. Quis vero est iste alius consolator, nisi Spiritus S. quo tandem eos donavit Christus in Pentecoste q.d.: Ego vobis a patre consolator fui datus, sed ad tempus: nunc defunctus cursu meo alium vobis dari petam, qui temporalis non sit, sed perpetuo apud vos maneat in terris & in Ecclesia. Alium autem a se nominat non juxta naturæ differentiam, sed juxta operationis diversitatem, ut loquitur Didymus. Neque vero semel tantum, sed sæpius hęc promissio Apostolis data & inculcata est a Servatore Christo. Ego, inquit, mittam vobis eum a patre, nempe consolatorem illum & spiritum illum veritatis, qui a patre procedit. Et postea, Ego veritatem dico vobis: expedit vobis ut abeam, nisi enim abiero consolator ille non veniet ad vos. Sin autem profectus fuero, mittam eum ad vos. Et iterum: vos baptizabimini Spiritu sancto istis non multis post diebus & recipietis virtutem Spiritus sancti, postquam superveneri in vos. In tot igitur tamque evidentibus promissionibus Filii Dei, qui mentiri non potuit, manifesta etiam causa est; qua missionem Spiritus Sancti miraculosam necessariam fuisse evincitur.
units.tr: So far I think it has been sufficiently confirmed that the abundant bestowal of the Holy Spirit was foretold by the various oracles of the prophets, and therefore was necessarily at last granted to the Church. To the oracles of the prophets are added the various promises of Christ the Saviour himself concerning the same benefit, whose truth it was no less necessary to have confirmed at last by the event. I, says Christ to the Apostles, will ask the Father, and he will give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever. Who, indeed, is that other Comforter, if not the Holy Spirit, whom Christ at last bestowed upon them at Pentecost? As if he said: I have been given to you as a Comforter by the Father, but only for a time; now, having finished my course, I will ask that another be given to you, who will not be temporary but will remain with you forever on earth and in the Church. He names him another, not according to difference of nature but according to diversity of operation, as Didymus says. And this promise was given and impressed upon the Apostles not once only but often by the Saviour Christ. I will send him to you from the Father, he says, that Comforter, that Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father. And afterward: I tell you the truth: it is expedient for you that I go away; for if I do not go away, that Comforter will not come to you. But if I depart, I will send him to you. And again: You shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days hence, and you shall receive the power of the Holy Spirit, after it has come upon you. Therefore, in so many and so clear promises of the Son of God, who could not lie, there is also a manifest cause by which the miraculous mission of the Holy Spirit is proved to have been necessary.

units.la: Post oracula prophetarum & promissiones Servatoris Christi, ejusdem beneficii causa statuenda est minime postrema: Glorificatio Mesfiæ in regno & sacerdotio suo exaltati. Glorifi-cato Messiæ oportuit demum tanta largitate effundi Spiritum sanctum in Ecclesiam. Primo enim beneficium tam gloriosum non exigua pars gloriæ Messiæ futurum erat: siquidem ipse eo declaravit, se evectum esse ad dextram Dei & à Deo principem & servatorem constitutum, ut docet Petrus, ex miraculoso illo & stupendo beneficio exaltationem seu evectionem Christi ad dextram Dei in cœlis demonstrans, cum inquit; Dextra Dei evectus & promissum Spiritum sanctum adeptus effudit hoc quod vos nunc spectatis & auditis. Et ali-bi, Hunc Deus dextra sua evectum constituit principem & servatorem ut det resipiscentiam Israeli. Quo pertinet, quod ipse Christus de spiritu venturo dicit; Ille me glorificabit, hoc est, copiose in Ecclesiam effusus glorificationis meæ testis erit. Accedit, quod Deus sapientissimo consilio tam illustre beneficium glorificationi Messiæ reservaverat, ut quoniam in eo omnes promissiones Dei sunt etiam & Amen, has quoque de effusio-ne Spiritus & gratiæ suæ in Novam Ecclesiam per eum compleret, atque [?]ic in regno Christi uber-tas illa donorum tan[?]quam præcipuum decus peculiariter conspiceretur. Confirmat hoc diserte Johannes, cum Christi humilitatem causam dicit fuisse, cur Spiritus S. tunc nondum esset. Non-dum, inquit, erat Spiritus S. quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus: Manifeste indicans tunc demum Spiritum sanctum copiose effundendum fuisse, postquam Christus e statu humilitatis egressus, in cœlis ad dextram Dei consedisset glorificatus. Neque; vero audiendi hic sunt πνευματομάχοι[?] hæretici, ex hoc dicto æternitatem Spiritus S. oppugnan-tes, cum luce meridiana sit clarius, non de persona Spiritus S. negari, quod fuerit humili adhuc Christo (in ipsa quippe rerum omnium creatione Spiritus S. incubabat aquis, molem indigestā futuri operis virtute sua sustentans scriptura teste) sed tantum de donis illis copiosis Spiritus S. quæ ante Messiam glorificatum non fuerunt, sed a glorificato demum effusa sunt in Ecclesiam. Sic enim ipse Iohannes verba Christi dicentis: Qui credit in me flumina aquæ vivæ fluent ex ventre eius, interpretatur, hoc eum dixisse de spiritu quem accepturi erant credentes in eum. Vsitata autem metalepsi causæ pro effectu, dona copiosa & visibilia Spiritus S. ipsum Spiritum S. appellat. Hæc nondum erant cum adhuc in terris humilis versaretur Christus, quia demum glorificatus sua intercessione a Patre ea impetrare debuit. Sic enim ipse: Ego rogabo, inquit, patrem & alium consolatorem dabit vobis. Et, ubi abiero, mittam eum ad vos. Quare certum est, glorificationem Messiæ inter præcipuas missionis Spiritus sancti causas numerandam esse.
units.tr: After the oracles of the prophets and the promises of the Saviour Christ, the cause of this benefit must be reckoned not least: the glorification of the Messiah, exalted in his kingdom and priesthood. It was fitting that the Holy Spirit should at last be poured out upon the Church in such abundance once the Messiah had been glorified. For, first, so glorious a benefit would be no small part of the glory of the Messiah: since by it he himself showed that he had been raised to the right hand of God and appointed by God as Prince and Saviour, as Peter teaches, pointing from that miraculous and astonishing benefit to the exaltation or elevation of Christ to the right hand of God in the heavens, when he says: Being exalted by the right hand of God, and having received the promised Holy Spirit, he has poured out this which you now see and hear. And elsewhere: God has exalted him with his right hand as Prince and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel. To this belongs what Christ himself says about the Spirit who is to come: He will glorify me; that is, having been copiously poured out upon the Church, he will be a witness of my glorification. In addition, God in his most wise counsel had reserved so illustrious a benefit for the glorification of the Messiah, so that, since in him all the promises of God are yea and amen, he might also fulfil through him these promises of the outpouring of his Spirit and grace upon the New Church, and so that in the kingdom of Christ that abundance of gifts might be seen especially as its chief glory. John expressly confirms this, when he says that the humility of Christ was the reason why the Holy Spirit was not yet present. The Spirit, he says, was not yet, because Jesus was not yet glorified. Clearly indicating that the copious outpouring of the Holy Spirit was to take place only after Christ, having emerged from the state of humility, had sat down glorified in heaven at the right hand of God. Nor are the heretics who fight against the Spirit to be heard here, who from this saying attack the eternity of the Holy Spirit, since it is clearer than the noonday light that what is denied is not the person of the Holy Spirit, who was present even while Christ was still in humility (for in the very creation of all things the Holy Spirit brooded over the waters, sustaining by his power the unformed mass of the future work, as Scripture testifies), but only those abundant gifts of the Holy Spirit which did not exist before the Messiah was glorified, but were poured out upon the Church by him once glorified. For John himself so interprets the words of Christ saying: He who believes in me, rivers of living water shall flow from his belly, that he said this of the Spirit whom those believing in him were about to receive. But by a common metalepsis of cause for effect, he calls the abundant and visible gifts of the Holy Spirit the Holy Spirit himself. These did not yet exist while Christ was still living in humility on earth, because only once glorified was he to obtain them from the Father by his intercession. For he himself says: I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Comforter. And when I have gone away, I will send him to you. Therefore it is certain that the glorification of the Messiah is to be counted among the chief causes of the mission of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: His porrò addenda est ea quæ ipsa proprietate personæ missæ nititur. Proprie enim Spiritui S. competit, quod est persona a Patre per Filium ad Ecclesiam in corda credentium missa, juxta illud Apostoli: Quoniam estis filii, emisit Deus spiritum filii sui in corda vestra, clamantem: Abba, pater. Missionis autem nomine haudquaquam intelligendus est motus localis aut a Patre & Filio discessio mutamutatióve aliqua in Deo; sed est Patris & Filii per immediatam operationem Spiritus sancti pa tefactio[?]. Mittitur quidem & Filius, sed non sicut Spiritus sanctus. Filius enim à solo Patre mittitur, & quidem ad naturam humanam assumen-dam, & ad opus redemtionis in carne peragendū. De quo Apostolus : Postquam, inquit, venit plenum tempus emisit Deus Filium suum factum ex muliere, factum legi obnoxium ut eos qui legi erant-obnoxii redimeret. At Spiritus S. non tantum à Patre sed & à Filio mittitur, quod docere volens Christus, dixit: Quem Pater mittet in nomine meo: Deinde verò: Quem ego mittam vobis à Patre: nec mittitur Spiritus S. quemadmodum Filius, ut vestit⁹ carne nostra peccata generis humani expiet, sed ad opus sanctificationis Ecclesiæ ablegatur: à quo opere tanquam sibi proprio, Spiritus S. & Spiritus sanctificationis atque renovationis appellatur. Neque verò satis fuit, eum ad hoc invisibiliter mitti in piorum corda: sed visibile quoque missionem tandem aliquando fieri necesse fuit, tum propter prædictiones illas propheta-rum & promissiones Christi, quæ sine ea inanes fuissent, tum verò maximè propter consolatic-nem & salutem Ecclesiæ de qua causa non multò post dicam, ubi prius necessitatem copiosæ effu-sionis Spiritus S. ex ejusdem officio insuper de-monstravero.
units.tr: To these things must be added also what rests on the very property of the person who is sent. For it belongs properly to the Holy Spirit that he is the person sent by the Father through the Son to the Church, into the hearts of believers, according to that saying of the Apostle: "Because you are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father." Now by the name of mission one must by no means understand a local movement, or a departure from the Father and the Son, or any change in God; rather it is a manifestation of the Father and the Son through the immediate operation of the Holy Spirit. The Son too is sent, but not in the same way as the Holy Spirit. For the Son is sent by the Father alone, and that indeed to assume human nature and to accomplish the work of redemption in the flesh. Of this the Apostle says: "When the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, that he might redeem those who were under the law." But the Holy Spirit is sent not only by the Father but also by the Son, which Christ, wishing to teach this, said: "Whom the Father will send in my name," and then again: "Whom I will send to you from the Father." Nor is the Holy Spirit sent as the Son was, that clothed in our flesh he might expiate the sins of the human race, but he is dispatched for the work of sanctifying the Church; from this work, as being his own, he is called the Spirit of sanctification and renewal. Nor was it enough that he be sent invisibly into the hearts of the godly for this; a visible mission also had at length to take place, both on account of those prophecies of the prophets and promises of Christ, which without it would have been empty, and above all on account of the consolation and salvation of the Church, for which cause I shall speak not long hence, after first having shown the necessity of the copious effusion of the Holy Spirit from his own office.

units.la: Ipsum enim quoque officium Spiritus S. requirebat ut copiosè effunderetur in Apostolos & in totam Ecclesiam. Nam sive publicum ejus munus (ut docendi causa sic distinguamus) quod per miniministerium verbi in Ecclesia exercet, sive privatum quod Apostolis & singulis fidelibus praestat, spectemus, utrunque certè copiosam ejus missionem postulavit. Publici enim officii ipsius partes tres praecipuas declarat Christus: Arguet, inquit, mundum (nempe per ministerium Evangelii) de peccato, quia non credunt in me: De iustitia, quia ad patrem vado: de iudicio, quia princeps mundi co-demnatus est. Mundum, inquit, arguet, quasi dicat, non Iudæos solum sed gentes, nationes & populos universos ad quos praeconesEvangelii pervenient, omnes, inquit, homines. Nec solum eos qui praedicationi Evangelii dociles aures adhibebunt, sed etiam eos, qui sermoni sibi annunciato contumaciter reluctabuntur. Arguet autem de peccato, hoc est, convincet de naturali pravitate, deque aeterna maledictione, donec Evangelii doctrinam amplexi in me credant & fide salutem quaerant. De iustitia vero convincet, unicam hac esse iustitiae verae & salutis aeternae viam, quam abitu meo ad patrem, hoc est, merito sacrificii mei & vigore intercessionis meae pro salute electorum in Evangelio patefactam consecravi. De iudicio denique convincet, hactenus quidem Satanae potentiam & regnum in maxima parte generis humani viguisse: At nunc mea potentia Satanam ipsum protritum & regnum ejus eversum esse, ut deinceps regnum Dei in cordibus electorum vigeat, totusque mundus quasi in ordinem coactus & renovatus deserto Satana ad Deum transeat & in obedientiam Evangelii concedat. Atqui per stultam praedicationem Evangelii & per homines[?] contemtos, quales fuerunt Apostoli & sunt, alii Ecclesiæ ministri, talia ac tanta gerere, haud-quaquam vulgarem efficaciam & præsentiam exigebat, sed prorsus singularem quę se in Pentecoste & deinceps in Nova Ecclesia exeruit. Quod, ipsum D. Paulus expendens variè Novum Testamentum Veteri anteponit: Vetus vocat literam occidentem, ministerium mortis & condemnationis, litteris informatum in saxis: novum verò Spiritum vivificantem, ministerium Spiritus justitiæ & vitæ scriptum in carneis tabulis cordium nostrorum & quæ alia plurima ibidem adfert, quibus dignitatem ministerii Evangelici longè supra œconomiam Mosis effert. Atqui excellentia ea Evangelii præ lege vix esse vel saltem sese exerere per ministerium vix poterat, nisi largissimus imber cœlestis gratiæ Ecclesiam tandem aliquando irrigasset, effuso Spiritu S. qui omnes nos retecta facie gloriam Domini ut in speculo intuentes, in eandem imaginem transformaret ex gloria in gloriam, ut Apostolus ibi præclarè loquitur.
units.tr: For the very office of the Holy Spirit also required that he be poured out abundantly upon the Apostles and upon the whole Church. For whether we consider his public function (to distinguish it thus for the sake of teaching), which he exercises in the Church through the ministry of the Word, or his private function, which he performs for the Apostles and for each of the faithful, either one certainly demanded his abundant mission. For Christ declares three principal parts of his public office: "He will convict the world (namely through the ministry of the Gospel) of sin, because they do not believe in me; of righteousness, because I go to the Father; of judgment, because the prince of this world has been condemned." He says "the world," as if to say not the Jews only but the Gentiles, nations and all peoples to whom the preachers of the Gospel will come: all men, he says. Not only those who will lend willing ears to the preaching of the Gospel, but also those who will stubbornly resist the message announced to them. He will convict of sin, that is, he will convince of natural depravity and of eternal damnation, until they embrace the doctrine of the Gospel, believe in me and seek salvation by faith. He will convict of righteousness, that there is one way of true righteousness and eternal salvation, which I have consecrated by my going to the Father, that is, by the merit of my sacrifice and the efficacy of my intercession for the salvation of the elect, now revealed in the Gospel. Finally he will convict of judgment: that hitherto indeed the power and kingdom of Satan has flourished in the greater part of the human race; but now by my power Satan himself has been crushed and his kingdom overthrown, so that henceforth the kingdom of God may flourish in the hearts of the elect, and the whole world, as if brought into order and renewed, may, Satan being forsaken, turn to God and yield to the obedience of the Gospel. Yet that such and so great things should be accomplished through the foolish preaching of the Gospel and through men held in contempt, such as the Apostles were and such as the other ministers of the Church are, required not an ordinary efficacy and presence, but a utterly singular one, which showed itself at Pentecost and thereafter in the New Church. St. Paul, weighing this very thing, variously sets the New Testament above the Old: he calls the Old the letter that kills, the ministry of death and condemnation, engraved with letters on stones; but the New the Spirit that gives life, the ministry of the Spirit of righteousness and life, written on the fleshly tablets of our hearts, and many other things he brings forward in the same place, by which he exalts the dignity of the Evangelical ministry far above the economy of Moses. Yet that excellence of the Gospel above the law could hardly exist, or at least could hardly show itself through the ministry, unless a most abundant rain of heavenly grace had at length watered the Church, the Spirit having been poured out, who, as we all behold the glory of the Lord with unveiled face as in a mirror, transforms us into the same image from glory to glory, as the Apostle speaks there most excellently.

units.la: Jam de privato Spiritus S. officio, quod dixi, eo tum in Apostolis tum in omnibus electis ita functurus erat, ut in omnem veritatem ipsos duceret, quemadmodum Christus de eo promiserat, hoc est, illorum mentibus magnum quoddam lumen infunderet, quod fulgore suo errorum caligine & nebulis dispulsis lucidissimam redderet semitam, qua ad doctrinæ cœlestis veram ac salutarem pervenitur cognitionem, & in hac semita peragranda ipse iis se fidelissimum ducem præberet, quem sequentes nunquam vel latum unguem in devia deflecterent. Duxerat quidem & Christus discipulos in omnem veritatem. Quomodo enim veritas a veritate vel minimum abduceret? Sed tamen quoad Christus in terris corporaliter versatus est & humana voce docuit, videmus ipsos Apostolos ne de aliis discipulis dicam, magna subinde ignorantia laborasse, & ad singula pene verba Christi tanquam ad obscurissima aenigmata quasi attonitos obstupuisse, nec quicquam fere ex concionibus Christi profecisse, eo quod opinione Iudaica de mundano Messiae regno imbuti essent. Debuit praeterea testari de Christo quod esset Messias promissus, non solum voce publici ministerii, sed & instinctu interno in cordibus electorum, dicente Christo: Ille testa-bitur de me. Et Iohanne Apostolo: Spiritus is est qui testificatur spiritum veritatem esse, hoc est, qui animos piorum certos reddit plenéque confirmat, hunc Iesum in Evangelio praedicatum promissum Messiam esse. Paracletus quoque, id est, consolator & advocatus piorum Spiritus S. esse debuit, sicut multoties Christus de eo erat pollicitus. Etsi enim de Christo etiam alicubi dicitur, quia nimirum in coelis apud patrem tanquam summus pontifex noster perpetuo pro nobis intercedit: tamen Spiritus S. alia ratione hoc nomine insignitur, quia videl. ut Apostolus loquitur, suspiriis inenarrabilibus pro nobis interpel-lat, hoc est, quia efficit in cordibus nostris summa angustia interdum constrictis abditos quosdam sed tamen divinae voluntati congruentes gemitus, licet ipsi quid & quomodo precemur nescia-mus. mus. Et hæc quidem singula præstare debuit longè efficacius Novæ Ecclesiæ, quam olim veteri præstiterat. Effundi ergo liberalius debuit. Idem arrha vioθεσίας, sanctificationis & salutis nostræ esse non potuisset, nisi nobis missus esset. Quæ officii ipsius pars valde à D. Paulo tanquam una ex præcipuis celebratur. Hinc cum vocat spiritum adoptionis per quem clamamus Abba, pater.
units.tr: Now concerning the private office of the Holy Spirit, which I mentioned, he was to function in this way both in the Apostles and in all the elect, that he would lead them into all truth, as Christ had promised concerning him; that is, he would pour a great light into their minds, which, by its brilliance dispelling the darkness and mists of errors, would render the path lucid, by which one arrives at the true and saving knowledge of heavenly doctrine; and in walking this path he himself would present himself to them as the most faithful guide, whom those following would never turn aside from by even the breadth of a fingernail into byways. Christ too had indeed led the disciples into all truth. For how could truth lead away from truth even slightly? But nevertheless, while Christ dwelt bodily on earth and taught with a human voice, we see that the Apostles themselves (not to mention the other disciples) often labored under great ignorance, and were astonished, as if at most obscure riddles, at nearly every word of Christ, and gained almost nothing from Christ's sermons, because they were imbued with the Jewish opinion about a worldly kingdom of the Messiah. Moreover, he had to bear witness concerning Christ that he was the promised Messiah, not only by the voice of the public ministry but also by inward impulse in the hearts of the elect, Christ saying: "He will bear witness of me." And the Apostle John: "It is the Spirit who testifies that the Spirit is truth," that is, the one who renders the minds of the godly certain and fully confirms them that this Jesus, preached in the Gospel, is the promised Messiah. The Holy Spirit also had to be the Paraclete, that is, the consoler and advocate of the godly, as Christ had often promised concerning him. For although of Christ too it is said somewhere, namely that he perpetually intercedes for us in heaven before the Father as our high priest: yet the Holy Spirit is designated by this name for another reason, namely because, as the Apostle says, he intercedes for us with unutterable groanings, that is, because he produces in our hearts, at times constricted by the greatest distress, certain hidden groanings which nevertheless agree with the divine will, although we do not know what or how we should pray. And indeed he had to accomplish each of these things far more efficaciously for the New Church than he had formerly done for the old. He therefore had to be poured out more liberally. The same could not have been the earnest of our adoption, sanctification and salvation, unless he had been sent to us. This part of his office is greatly celebrated by St. Paul as one of the principal ones. Hence when he calls him the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, Abba, Father.

units.la: Hinc alibi inquit, nos obsignatos esse Spiritu illo promissionis sancto qui sit arrhabo hæreditatis nostræ & graviter monet ne tristitia afficiamus Spiritum illum sanctum Dei per quem summus obsignati in diem redemtionis. Denique manere nobiscum in æternum qui potuit si nunquam ad nos venisset? Atqui præclara jam olim data fuit promissio de perpetua Spiritus Dei illustri præsentia in Ecclesia. Sic enim Deus per Iesaiam:
units.tr: Hence he says elsewhere that we have been sealed by that Spirit of the holy promise, who is the earnest of our inheritance, and he seriously warns us not to grieve that Holy Spirit of God by whom we have been sealed unto the day of redemption. Finally, could he who had never come to us have remained with us forever? Indeed, a splendid promise concerning the perpetual illustrious presence of the Spirit of God in the Church was given long ago. For thus God speaks through Isaiah:

units.la: Hoc pactum meum quod ego pangam cum eis dixit Jehova, Spiritus meus qui est super te & verba mea quæ posui in ore tuo non recedent de ore tuo, & de ore seminis tui, & de ore seminis seminis tui, dixit Jehova, ex hoc tempore & usque in seculum. Et nota est Servatoris promissio: Ego rogabo patrem & alium consolatorem dabit vobis ut maneat vobiscum in æternum.
units.tr: "This is my covenant that I will make with them," said the LORD: "My Spirit that is upon you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed, says the LORD, from this time and for ever." And the Saviour's promise is well known: "I will pray the Father, and he will give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever."

units.la: Quare ut munere suo publicè privatimque defungeretur illustrius in nova Ecclesia quam olim, illustrior ejus patefactio atque effusio requirebatur.
units.tr: Therefore, that he might discharge his office more illustriously in the new Church than of old, both publicly and privately, a more illustrious manifestation and outpouring of him was required.

units.la: Postrema causa est ipsa salus Ecclesiæ. Hanc enim non solum præclaris suis donis benignè implere, sed etiam Deo & Christo capiti unire atque omnium ejus beneficiorum participem facere. gere debuit Spiritus S.qui unus id potest. Ex Spi-ritu enim Dei quem dedit nobis cognoscimus quod Deum habitantem in nobis habeamus. Per Spiritum Domino agglutinari nos necesse est ut simus unum corpus & unus Spiritus cum eo. Nec aliter templa Dei sumus, nisi cum Spiri-tus S.est in nobis quem habemus à Deo ut testa-tur Apostolus. Ipse denique est copula unionis nostræ cum Christo, ipse corda agglutinat, & fi-dem facit quod à Deo in filios adoptati simus ut verbis Chrysost.loquar. Etsi itaque Christi me-rito salus Ecclesiæ acquisita fuit, tamen acceptari à nobis non poterat nisi per fidem. Fides verò Spiritus sancti effectum est proprium, quod non impetrant nisi illud serió à Deo petentes. Non petunt autem nisi in quibus Spiritus sanctus pre-ces accendit. Vnde Spiritus gratiæ & precum à Zacharia vocatur. Quia electos per fidem & pre-ces Christo inserit & ad gratiæ ipsius communio-nem adducit. Quod ut præstaret, mittendus o-mnino fuit. Sanctificavit quidem & gubernavit patres quoque Vet. Testamenti. Orat enim Da-vid: Cor mundum crea mihi & Spiritum tuum re-ctum innova in visceribus meis. Et, Spiritum sanctū tuum ne auferas à me. Alibi, Spiritus, inquit, tuus bonus deducat me in terra recta. Sic in baptismo Christi cœlis apertis descendit Spiritus Dei vi-sibili specie columbæ super Christum: datus quo-que fuit Apostolis flatu Christi non multò post resurrectionem ejus. Vnde constat Spiritum S. non demum in Pentecoste & deinceps Ecclesiæ esse missum. Verum hæc missio, quæ olim facta nullo modo fieri potuisset nisi copiosa ista missio, aliquando futura fuisset, merito & intercessione Messiæ impetrata Ecclesiæ. Hujus ergo vi illa veteribus contigit: sicut & alia omnia ad salutem necessaria beneficia propter Messiam ea suis electis acquisituram ipsis collata fuerunt. Interim nec hoc negari potest, multò paucioribus multoque parcius Spiritum sanctum sua dona impertivisse ante, quam solenni isto modo mitteretur, adeo ut dicatur prius non fuisse. Nondum erat Spiritus sanctus, inquit Iohannes, quia Christus nondum erat glorificatus. Quod comparatè intelligendum esse de largitate & latiori communione munerum ipsius quæ in Pentecoste initium sumens, deinceps in Nova Ecclesia viguit, supra est ostensum, ut sit sensus: Nondum erat Spiritus sanctus, nempe miraculosè effusus, &c. In Christi baptismo descendit quidem Spiritus, sed super solum Christum non super omnem carnem. Apostoli vero à Christo afflati, acceperunt Spiritus sancti tantum primitias, cujus complementum postea in totam Ecclesiam est diffusum. Atque hæc de primo orationis capite, quo causas copiosæ effusionis Spiritus S. ostendimus, dixisse satis sit; nunc de fructibus dicendum restat.
units.tr: The last cause is the salvation of the Church itself. For the Holy Spirit, who alone can do it, ought not only to fulfil this salvation kindly with his excellent gifts, but also to unite the Church to God and to Christ its head, and to make it a sharer in all his benefits. For it is from the Spirit of God, whom he has given us, that we know that we have God dwelling in us. It is necessary that we be joined to the Lord through the Spirit, so that we may be one body and one spirit with him. Nor are we otherwise the temples of God, unless the Holy Spirit is in us, whom we have from God, as the Apostle testifies. Finally, he is the bond of our union with Christ; he joins hearts together and makes it certain that we are adopted by God as sons, to use the words of Chrysostom. Although, therefore, the salvation of the Church was obtained by the merit of Christ, yet it could not be accepted by us except through faith. But faith is the proper effect of the Holy Spirit, which is obtained only by those who ask earnestly of God. Yet they do not ask unless the Holy Spirit kindles their prayers in them. Hence he is called by Zechariah the Spirit of grace and of prayer, because he joins the elect to Christ through faith and prayer and brings them into communion with his grace. In order to bring this about, he had altogether to be sent. He indeed sanctified and governed the fathers of the Old Testament too. For David prays: "Create in me a clean heart, and renew a right spirit within my bowels," and "Take not your Holy Spirit from me." Elsewhere he says: "Your good Spirit will lead me into the land of uprightness." So at the baptism of Christ, the heavens being opened, the Spirit of God descended in the visible form of a dove upon Christ; and he was given to the apostles by the breath of Christ not long after his resurrection. Hence it is clear that the Holy Spirit was not sent for the first time at Pentecost and thereafter to the Church. Yet this mission, which, though made of old, could in no way have been made without that abundant mission, would at some time be in the future, obtained for the Church by the merit and intercession of the Messiah. By his power, therefore, this was granted to the men of old, just as all the other benefits necessary for salvation were conferred upon them, to be acquired for his elect by the Messiah. Meanwhile, it cannot be denied that the Holy Spirit bestowed his gifts before this solemn mode of sending, both to far fewer people and far more sparingly, so much so that it can be said that he had not been given before. "The Holy Spirit was not yet," says John, "because Christ was not yet glorified." This must be understood comparatively, of the largeness and wider communion of his gifts, which, beginning at Pentecost, flourished thereafter in the New Church; as has been shown above, so that the sense is: "The Holy Spirit was not yet," namely, miraculously poured out, etc. At the baptism of Christ the Spirit indeed descended, but upon Christ alone, not upon all flesh. The apostles, however, breathed upon by Christ, received only the first-fruits of the Holy Spirit, whose fullness was afterwards diffused over the whole Church. And let this suffice concerning the first head of the oration, in which we have shown the causes of the abundant outpouring of the Holy Spirit; now it remains to speak of its fruits.

units.la: Primum vero miraculi fructum ipsi Apostoli sibi decerpunt, accipientes toties à Domino promissum Spiritum sanctum, quo ut scribit Lucas continuò tum repleti sunt omnes. Accipiunt autem cum eo tum ea quæ promiserat Christus, tum alia etiam plane admiranda dona. Repentes[?] nova luce cognitionis doctrinę cœlestis perfun- duntur & à Spiritu sancto juxta promissionem in omnem veritatem ducuntur: Repente abje- cto metu ex abdito prodeunt & magna cum πνεύ- ματος ἐνεργείᾳ[?] de Christo à mortuis suscitato & ad dextrā Dei evecto, testificantur; Iesum Nazarenum esse promissum Messiā, & miraculi ejus ꝑ Judęi audiebāt & spectabāt in Pentecoste authore fortissimè demonstrantes: læti pro nomine Jesu cō-tumelias perferunt: injurias pro Christi gloria cum gaudio suscipiunt: Plusquam Herculeo la-bore universum orbem peragrant & in fidem Christi adigunt: precum ardore & vehementia ipsum solum & locum, quo erant conjuncti, cō-movent: Deniq; omnes repleti Spiritu S. sermo-nem Dei liberè & intrepidè loquuntur, dissemi-nant, defendunt. Has tantas tamque inæstimabi-les virtutes ex promissionibus Christi Spiritus S. effecit in Apostolis.
units.tr: The first fruit of the miracle the apostles themselves gather for themselves, receiving the Holy Spirit so often promised by the Lord, with whom, as Luke writes, they were at once all filled. Yet with him they receive both the things Christ had promised and other gifts truly admirable. Being at once illuminated with the new light of heavenly doctrine, and led by the Holy Spirit, according to the promise, into all truth; suddenly, with fear cast off, they come forth from hiding, and with great energy of the Spirit testify concerning Christ raised from the dead and exalted to the right hand of God, that Jesus of Nazareth is the promised Messiah, most strongly demonstrating his miracle, which the Jews heard and saw on Pentecost. They bear reproaches joyfully for the name of Jesus; they accept injuries with joy for the glory of Christ; they travel over the whole world with more than Herculean labour and bring it to the faith of Christ; by the ardour and vehemence of their prayers they move the very place where they were gathered; finally, all filled with the Holy Spirit, they speak, spread abroad and defend the word of God freely and fearlessly.
